summary: Liu–Tian–Xiao–Zhang–Zhu prove cases of the Beilinson–Bloch–Kato conjecture for Rankin–Selberg motives ρ_{Π₀,λ} ⊗ ρ_{Π₁,λ}(n) of relevant cuspidal representations of GL_n × GL_{n+1} over a CM field: if L(1/2, Π₀ × Π₁) ≠ 0 the Bloch–Kato Selmer group vanishes for admissible λ, and if the diagonal Abel–Jacobi class is nonzero it has rank one (Theorems 1.1.5, 1.1.9, with the symmetric-power case 1.1.1 and the Steinberg case 1.1.7). The method is arithmetic level raising on unitary Shimura varieties at inert primes, via the special fibres of smooth and almost self-dual integral models (§§4–5, Appendix A), two geometric and two explicit reciprocity laws (§§4.6, 5.11, 7) and a Kolyvagin-type pairing argument (§§2.6, 8). The atlas plans the Selmer, Galois-representation, PEL, Satake, trace-comparison and vanishing-cycle foundations (twelve source routes); it lacks the unitary integral models and their basic loci, the unitary level-raising types and Hecke relations, the rigid R = T theorem, Liu's potential maps, Gan–Gross–Prasad periods and the level-raising Selmer argument itself (five Part II routes and one new roadmap). 126 mistakes are recorded (75 misprints, 30 gaps, 21 errors). The most serious: Lemma 2.6.4 and Propositions 2.6.6–2.6.7 are false when [F:F⁺] = 2, and the proofs of the main theorems choose the auxiliary Frobenius without regard to the 𝔠-eigenspace of the Selmer class, a gap in the base-change case; the unconditional theorems rest on the unpublished [37].

items.name: Theorem 1.1.1 — BBK in rank 0 for Sym^{n−1}A × Sym^n A′
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be a totally imaginary quadratic extension of a totally real number field. Let n ⩾ 2 be an integer. Let A and A′ be two modular elliptic curves over F⁺ such that End(A_{F̄}) = End(A′_{F̄}) = ℤ. Suppose that (a) A_{F̄} and A′_{F̄} are not isogenous to each other; (b) both Sym^{n−1}A and Sym^n A′ are modular; and (c) F⁺ ≠ ℚ. If the (central critical) L-value L(n, Sym^{n−1}A_F × Sym^n A′_F) does not vanish, then the Bloch–Kato Selmer group H¹_f(F, Sym^{n−1}H¹_ét(A_{F̄}, ℚ_ℓ) ⊗_{ℚ_ℓ} Sym^n H¹_ét(A′_{F̄}, ℚ_ℓ)(n)) vanishes for all but finitely many rational primes ℓ.
items.note: Stated as Corollary 8.2.3; deduced from Theorem 8.2.2 (= Theorem 1.1.5) once all but finitely many ℓ are admissible (Lemma 8.1.3, which uses Proposition 2.7.2 and Serre's open image theorem [68, Théorème 6]). H¹_f is Definition 2.4.1. Remark 1.1.2 says the excluded ℓ can be effectively bounded (not proved in the text). Here the Galois representation is restricted from F⁺, so R ≅ Rᶜ and H¹(F, R̄) splits into 𝔠-eigenspaces: a situation in which the obstruction of E1 (failure of Lemma 2.6.4 / Proposition 2.6.6 for [F:F⁺] = 2) is concretely live, so the proof as written has a gap; see E1 and the new issue on Proposition 2.7.2(3). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Remark 1.1.2 — role of the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1.1
items.statement: The finite set of rational primes ℓ excluded in Theorem 1.1.1 can be effectively bounded. (a) is necessary since otherwise (L3) and (L5) in Definition 8.1.1 fail for all rational primes ℓ. (b) is necessary since the approach only applies to Galois representations arising from automorphic representations (current knowledge on modularity of symmetric powers: Remark 8.2.4). (c) is necessary only for technical reasons: Hypothesis 3.2.10 (cohomology of unitary Shimura varieties) is not known for N ⩾ 4 if F⁺ = ℚ, and (an appropriate replacement for) Proposition D.1.3, a result generalizing [12], is not available when F⁺ = ℚ; with these results, (c) can be lifted.
items.note: Commentary; no proof given. The effective-bound claim is not substantiated in the text. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Definition 1.1.3 — relevant representation of GL_N(𝔸_F)
items.statement: Let F be a CM field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺ and 𝔠 ∈ Gal(F/F⁺) the complex conjugation. A complex representation Π of GL_N(𝔸_F) with N ⩾ 1 is relevant if (1) Π is an irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation; (2) Π ∘ 𝔠 ≃ Π^∨; and (3) for every archimedean place w of F, Π_w is isomorphic to the (irreducible) principal series representation induced by the characters (arg^{1−N}, arg^{3−N}, …, arg^{N−3}, arg^{N−1}), where arg: ℂ^× → ℂ^× is the argument character arg(z) := z/√(z z̄).
items.note: Serves for the whole article. Condition (3) fixes regular algebraic weight 0,…,N−1 and, via Remark 1.1.4, the parity (L(s,Π,As^{(−1)^N}) regular at s=1). Footnote 1 (p. 112) derives from (2) alone that the Satake parameter of Π_{1,𝔭} at an inert prime contains 1; that needs (3) as well (new issue). Planned: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.0 plans algebraic weights, fields of rationality and the normalization of relevant cuspidal representations.

items.name: Remark 1.1.4 — relevant implies regular algebraic; Asai regularity
items.statement: If Π is relevant (Definition 1.1.3), then Π is regular algebraic in the sense of [17, Définition 3.12]. Moreover, L(s, Π, As^{(−1)^N}) is regular at s = 1.
items.note: Cited, not proved: regular algebraicity from [17] (Clozel); the Asai statement is 'well known', see [28, §6.1] (Grobner–Harris–Lapid). For N odd this says As⁻ is regular, so As⁺ has the pole: Π is conjugate-orthogonal and descends to U(N). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Rankin–Selberg L-values in §1.1
items.statement: For relevant Π₀, Π₁ of GL_{n₀}(𝔸_F), GL_{n₁}(𝔸_F), L(s, Π₀ × Π₁) denotes the Rankin–Selberg L-function in the unitary normalization, with centre s = 1/2; L′(1/2, Π₀ × Π₁) is its derivative there, and the global epsilon factor of Π₀ × Π₁ is ±1. In Theorem 1.1.1 the motivic normalization is used: the central critical value is L(n, Sym^{n−1}A_F × Sym^n A′_F).
items.note: The paper does not say in §1 whether L is the finite or the completed L-function; the archimedean factors are finite and nonzero at s = 1/2 here, so the non-vanishing statements are insensitive to this. The rank-one discussion assumes ε(Π₀×Π₁) = −1. Planned: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.3 plans Rankin–Selberg L-functions.

items.name: Theorem 1.1.5 — rank 0: L(1/2) ≠ 0 ⇒ Selmer group vanishes at admissible λ
items.statement: Let n ⩾ 2 and let n₀, n₁ be the unique even and odd numbers in {n, n+1}. Let Π₀ and Π₁ be relevant representations of GL_{n₀}(𝔸_F) and GL_{n₁}(𝔸_F), respectively. Let E ⊆ ℂ be a strong coefficient field of both Π₀ and Π₁ (Definition 3.2.5). Suppose that F⁺ ≠ ℚ. If L(1/2, Π₀ × Π₁) ≠ 0, then for all admissible primes λ of E with respect to (Π₀, Π₁) (Definition 8.1.1), the Bloch–Kato Selmer group H¹_f(F, ρ_{Π₀,λ} ⊗_{E_λ} ρ_{Π₁,λ}(n)) vanishes, where ρ_{Π_α,λ} is the Galois representation of F with coefficients in E_λ attached to Π_α (Proposition 3.2.4 and Definition 3.2.5).
items.note: = Theorem 8.2.2. The proof (§8.2) uses Proposition 2.4.6, Lemmas 2.3.3–2.3.5, Lemma 2.7.1 and Proposition 2.6.6 with [F:F⁺] = 2, where Lemma 2.6.4/Proposition 2.6.6 are false as stated (E1); admissibility (L5-1) allows primes satisfying only Lemma 2.3.5(b), which is false when O_λ/λ ≠ 𝔽_ℓ (new issue). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Remark 1.1.6 — the conditions (L1)–(L7) defining admissible primes
items.statement: Admissible primes λ of E with respect to (Π₀, Π₁) are defined in Definition 8.1.1 by conditions (L1)–(L7). According to Remark 1.1.6: (L1),(L2) are elementary and exclude only finitely many λ; (L3) (absolute irreducibility of ρ_{Π₀,λ}⊗ρ_{Π₁,λ}) is expected to hold for every λ iff the conjectural automorphic product Π₀ ⊠ Π₁ on GL_{n(n+1)}(𝔸_F) is cuspidal; (L4) (residual absolute irreducibility of both) is expected for all but finitely many λ; (L5) says that under (L4) the image of (ρ̄_{Π₀,λ}, ρ̄_{Π₁,λ}) contains an element of a particular form, expected for all but finitely many λ if Π₀, Π₁ are not correlated (for n = 2, if Π₁ is not an automorphic twist of Sym²Π₀ after any base change); (L6) is only used in the R = T theorem of [51] and is expected for all but finitely many λ ([51, §4.2]); (L7) is a condition for vanishing of Hecke-localized cohomology off middle degree, and when F⁺ ≠ ℚ it holds for all but finitely many λ by Corollary D.1.4.
items.note: Only the (L7) claim is a proved statement (Corollary D.1.4). The precise conditions, including (L5-1) = 'one of the assumptions of Lemma 2.3.5' and (L5-2) = (GI¹_{F′,P}) of Lemma 2.7.1 with P = T²−1, are in Definition 8.1.1 (p. 303). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Theorem 1.1.7 — rank 0 for all but finitely many λ under local conditions
items.statement: Let Π₀, Π₁ and E be as in Theorem 1.1.5. Suppose that (a) there exists a very special inert prime 𝔭 of F⁺ (Definition 3.3.4) such that Π_{0,𝔭} is Steinberg, and Π_{1,𝔭} is unramified whose Satake parameter contains 1 exactly once; (b) for α = 0, 1, there exists a nonarchimedean place w_α of F such that Π_{α,w_α} is supercuspidal; and (c) F⁺ ≠ ℚ. If L(1/2, Π₀ × Π₁) ≠ 0, then for all but finitely many primes λ of E, the Bloch–Kato Selmer group H¹_f(F, ρ_{Π₀,λ} ⊗_{E_λ} ρ_{Π₁,λ}(n)) vanishes.
items.note: = Corollary 8.2.5, via Lemma 8.1.4 (all but finitely many λ admissible). Footnote 1: 'the Satake parameter of Π_{1,𝔭} has to contain 1 at least once by Definition 1.1.3(2)' — true for relevant Π₁ but needs Definition 1.1.3(3) (see new issue). Neither Theorem 1.1.7 nor Theorem 1.1.1 implies the other (p. 111). The (L5-1) verification in Lemma 8.1.4 goes through Lemma 2.3.5(b); the Jordan-block argument of Lemma 8.1.5(2) also gives the Frobenius-twisted condition needed to repair Lemma 2.3.5(b). Still subject to E1. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Remark 1.1.8 — very special inert primes when F is Galois or contains an imaginary quadratic field
items.statement: In (a) of Theorem 1.1.7, if the CM field F is Galois or contains an imaginary quadratic field, then a very special inert prime of F⁺ is simply a prime of F⁺ that is inert in F, of degree 1 over ℚ, whose underlying rational prime is odd and unramified in F.
items.note: Depends on Definition 3.3.4 (special/very special inert primes), outside these pages; not proved here. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: BBK prediction in the Rankin–Selberg setting and the class △_λ
items.statement: Let Π₀, Π₁ be relevant representations of GL_{n₀}(𝔸_F), GL_{n₁}(𝔸_F) and E ⊆ ℂ a strong coefficient field of both. The Beilinson–Bloch–Kato conjecture predicts: if L(1/2, Π₀ × Π₁) ≠ 0 then H¹_f(F, ρ_{Π₀,λ} ⊗_{E_λ} ρ_{Π₁,λ}(n)) = 0; and if the global epsilon factor of Π₀ × Π₁ is −1 and L′(1/2, Π₀ × Π₁) ≠ 0 then H¹_f(F, ρ_{Π₀,λ} ⊗_{E_λ} ρ_{Π₁,λ}(n)) has rank 1. For every prime λ of E the paper constructs (§8.3, (8.10)) an element △_λ of (the direct sum of finitely many copies of) H¹_f(F, ρ_{Π₀,λ} ⊗_{E_λ} ρ_{Π₁,λ}(n)) as the image under the Abel–Jacobi map of the diagonal cycle of the product unitary Shimura variety; by Conjecture 8.3.1 and Beilinson's conjecture on injectivity of the ℓ-adic Abel–Jacobi map, △_λ ≠ 0 is (conjecturally) equivalent to L′(1/2, Π₀ × Π₁) ≠ 0.
items.note: Conjectural statements, not proved; background refs [7] (Bloch–Kato) and [46]. The paper proves one half in each rank (Theorems 1.1.5, 1.1.9). Planned: PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.6 plans the Bloch–Kato conjecture interface.

items.name: Theorem 1.1.9 — rank 1: △_λ ≠ 0 ⇒ Selmer rank one
items.statement: Let Π₀ and Π₁ be relevant representations of GL_{n₀}(𝔸_F) and GL_{n₁}(𝔸_F), respectively. Let E ⊆ ℂ be a strong coefficient field of both Π₀ and Π₁ (Definition 3.2.5). Suppose that F⁺ ≠ ℚ. For all admissible primes λ of E with respect to (Π₀, Π₁), if △_λ ≠ 0, then H¹_f(F, ρ_{Π₀,λ} ⊗_{E_λ} ρ_{Π₁,λ}(n)) has dimension 1 over E_λ.
items.note: = Theorem 8.3.2. Proof uses Proposition 2.6.6 (r_S = 2) and the diagonal-basis claim of Proposition 2.6.7; both are affected (E1, E2). An analogue of Theorem 1.1.7 in rank one is mentioned but its statement is omitted (p. 112). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Remarks 1.1.2(c) and 1.1.10 — when F⁺ ≠ ℚ and (L6), (L7) can be dropped
items.statement: In both Theorems 1.1.5 and 1.1.9, the assumption F⁺ ≠ ℚ if n ⩾ 3 can be lifted once Hypothesis 3.2.10 is known for N ⩾ 4 when F⁺ = ℚ. When n = 2, a slightly different argument lifts the restriction F⁺ ≠ ℚ and the assumptions (L6) and (L7) of Definition 8.1.1 in all the results above. (Remark 1.1.2(c): the obstacles when F⁺ = ℚ are Hypothesis 3.2.10 for N ⩾ 4 and the lack of a replacement for Proposition D.1.3, which generalizes [12].)
items.note: Remarks only; the n = 2 argument is not given in §1. Hypothesis 3.2.10 is not proved in the paper and should not be marked as proved. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: (1.1) — GGP input: non-vanishing of the unitary period
items.statement: Road-map form (ad hoc notation): if L(1/2, Π₀ × Π₁) ≠ 0 there is a pair of hermitian spaces (V°_n, V°_{n+1}) over F (w.r.t. F/F⁺), V°_n totally positive definite of rank n and V°_{n+1} = V°_n ⊕ F·1 with 1 of norm 1, and cuspidal automorphic representations π₀, π₁ in the spaces of locally constant functions on Sh(V°_{n_α}) := U(V°_{n_α})(F⁺)\U(V°_{n_α})(𝔸^∞_{F⁺}) with BC(π₀) ≃ Π₀, BC(π₁) ≃ Π₁, such that 𝒫(f₀, f₁) := ∫_{Sh(V°_n)} f₀(h) f₁(h) dh ≠ 0 for some f₀ ∈ π₀ and f₁ ∈ π₁ valued in O_E.
items.note: Cited, not proved: the global Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture [25], proved by W. Zhang [77] under local restrictions and in general by Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu [6]. Precise version used: Lemma 8.2.1. The integral is over Sh(V°_n) with f for the rank-(n+1) space restricted. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §1.2 — strategy of proof (overview, ad hoc notation)
items.statement: Steps: (i) GGP gives (1.1); (ii) for a special inert prime 𝔭 of F⁺ with large residue characteristic p, attach to V°_{n_α} a strictly semistable scheme M_𝔭(V°_{n_α}) over Spec ℤ_{p²} of relative dimension n_α − 1 whose special fibre is M°_𝔭 ∪ M•_𝔭, M°_𝔭 a ℙ^{n_α−1}-fibration over Sh(V°_{n_α}) and the basic locus of M•_𝔭 fibred over Sh by Deligne–Lusztig varieties of dimension r_α = ⌊n_α/2⌋; (iii) study H¹(ℚ_{p²}, H^{n_α−1}_𝔗(M̄_𝔭(V°_{n_α}), RΨO_λ(r_α))_{𝔪_α}) (1.2); for a level-raising prime (ℓ ∤ p(p²−1), mod λ Satake parameter of Π_{0,𝔭} contains {p, p^{−1}} exactly once and not {−1,−1}) there is a canonical isomorphism H¹_sing(ℚ_{p²}, H^{n₀−1}_𝔗(M̄_𝔭(V°_{n₀}), RΨO_λ(r₀))/𝔪₀) ≃ O_λ[Sh(V°_{n₀})]/𝔪₀ (1.3), proved via an R = T theorem ([51]) comparing R^unr, R^ram, R^cong := R^unr ⊗_{R^mix} R^ram; (iv) the first explicit reciprocity law (§7.2) produces torsion classes whose singular localization at 𝔭 is controlled by 𝒫(f₀,f₁); (v) §8.2 bounds the Selmer group using §2.
items.note: The authors state that the notation here is ad hoc and obsolete after §1.2. Road map: §3 → §4 (A.1) → §5 (A.2, B, C.2) → §6 (B, C, D) ← §2; §§7.1–7.2 → §§8.1–8.2 (D.1) for rank 0; §4, §7.3 (C.3), §8.3 for rank 1. The mod-λ^m version of (1.3) is needed in practice. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §1.3 Generalities — conventions
items.statement: ℕ = {0,1,2,…}; √ is applied only to positive reals with positive values; 𝟙_S is the characteristic function of S; eigenvalues or generalized eigenvalues of a matrix over a field k are counted with multiplicity (a multi-subset of an algebraic extension of k); for each rational prime p an algebraic closure ℚ̄_p with residue field 𝔽̄_p is fixed, and ℚ_{p^r} ⊆ ℚ̄_p is the unramified extension of degree r, ℤ_{p^r} its ring of integers, 𝔽_{p^r} its residue field; for a nonarchimedean place v of a number field K, ‖v‖ is the cardinality of the residue field of K_v; all rings are commutative and unital, but 'algebra' is used in the general (non-commutative, non-unital) sense; an unspecified base ring of ⊗ is ℤ; for a ring L and a set S, L[S] is the L-module of finitely supported L-valued functions on S; Mod(A) is the category of left A-modules; ≃ denotes isomorphisms and a bold dash denotes a virtual object.
items.note: Conventions for the whole article including appendices. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §1.3 — coefficient rings for étale cohomology; n-coprime
items.statement: A coefficient ring (for étale cohomology) is either a finite ring, or a finite extension of ℚ_ℓ, or the ring of integers of a finite extension of ℚ_ℓ; in the latter two cases étale cohomology is understood as continuous étale cohomology. A coefficient ring L is n-coprime (n a positive integer) if n is invertible in L in the first case, and ℓ ∤ n in the latter two cases.
items.note: Also: for a number field K, a commutative group scheme G → S with O_K-action and an ideal 𝔞 ⊂ O_K, G[𝔞] is the maximal closed subgroup scheme annihilated by 𝔞. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §1.3 — scheme-theoretic conventions
items.statement: Sch (resp. Sch′) is the category of schemes (resp. locally Noetherian schemes), Sch_{/S}, Sch′_{/S} their slices; 𝒪_X the structure sheaf; X ⊗_R S or X_S := X ×_{Spec R} Spec S; σ is the absolute p-power Frobenius on a characteristic-p scheme and the canonical lift of Frobenius on W(κ) for κ perfect; 𝒯_{S/T} the relative tangent sheaf of a smooth S → T; for a locally free 𝒪_S-module 𝒱 of finite rank, ℙ(𝒱) → S is the moduli scheme of QUOTIENT line bundles of 𝒱 (the projective fibration); ℋom(ℱ,𝒢) the quasi-coherent sheaf of 𝒪_S-linear maps; M_{r,s} the ℤ-scheme of r × s matrices, M_r := M_{r,r}, GL_r ⊆ M_r; GL₁ = 𝐆_m := ℤ[T,T^{−1}] but the two are distinguished according to context.
items.note: The quotient-line-bundle convention for ℙ(𝒱) matters for the ℙ^{n−1}-fibrations of §§4–5. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §1.3 — group-theoretic conventions
items.statement: Let G, Γ̃ be groups, Γ ⊆ Γ̃ a subgroup and L a ring. Γ^{ab} is the maximal abelian quotient of Γ. For ρ: Γ → GL_r(L), the contragredient is ρ^∨(x) = ᵗρ(x)^{−1}. For ρ: Γ → G and γ ∈ Γ̃ normalizing Γ, ρ^γ(x) := ρ(γxγ^{−1}). ρ₁, ρ₂: Γ → G are conjugate if ρ₁ = g∘ρ₂∘g^{−1} for some g ∈ G. L[G] is the group algebra. For G locally compact totally disconnected and K ⊆ G open compact, L[K\G/K] (bi-K-invariant compactly supported L-valued functions) is an L-algebra under composition of cosets, with unit 𝟙_K.
items.note: The transpose-inverse convention for ρ^∨ is the one used in Notation 2.5.1 and Construction 2.5.4. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Notation 1.3.1 — q-binomials and the numbers d_{r,q}, d•_{r,q}
items.note: Used in §5 (intersection numbers, e.g. Proposition A.2.4(2) and (5.20)). Sanity values: d_{0,q} = 1, d•_{0,q} = 0; d_{1,q} = 1 − q − 2q², d•_{1,q} = −q. The printed '[0]_q = 1' conflicts with the formula for [n]_q (which gives 0); only [0]_q! = 1 is needed (misprint recorded). Missing: routed to a source of QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.0 (route 9).

items.name: §1.3 Ground fields — F, F⁺, Γ_F, embeddings, η, ε_ℓ
items.statement: 𝔠 ∈ Aut(ℂ/ℚ) is complex conjugation. F ⊆ ℂ is a fixed subfield, a number field stable under 𝔠, assumed CM except in §2; F⁺ ⊆ F is the maximal subfield on which 𝔠 acts trivially. F̄ is the algebraic closure of F in ℂ (printed 'Galois closure'), Γ_F := Gal(F̄/F), Γ_{F⁺} := Gal(F̄/F⁺). Σ_∞ (resp. Σ⁺_∞) is the set of complex embeddings of F (resp. F⁺) with default τ_∞ (resp. τ̲_∞); τ^𝔠 is the conjugate of τ ∈ Σ_∞. Σ⁺_p is the set of p-adic places of F⁺; Σ⁺_bad is the union of Σ⁺_p over p ramified in F. η_{F/F⁺}: Γ_{F⁺} → {±1} is the character of F/F⁺ and ε_ℓ: Γ_{F⁺} → ℤ_ℓ^× the ℓ-adic cyclotomic character.
items.note: 'Galois closure' is a misprint for 'algebraic closure' (new issue); Γ_F must be the absolute Galois group. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §1.3 — local fields, δ(v), decomposition groups, φ_w
items.statement: For a place v of F⁺: F_v := F ⊗_{F⁺} F⁺_v; δ(v) := 1 (resp. 2) if v splits (resp. does not split) in F; an algebraic closure F̄⁺_v containing F̄ is fixed and Γ_{F⁺_v} := Gal(F̄⁺_v/F⁺_v) ⊆ Γ_{F⁺}; for r a homomorphism from Γ_{F⁺}, r_v is its restriction to Γ_{F⁺_v}. For a nonarchimedean place w of F over v: Γ_{F_w} is identified with Γ_{F⁺_v} ∩ Γ_F (resp. 𝔠(Γ_{F⁺_v} ∩ Γ_F)𝔠) if the embedding F ↪ F̄⁺_v induces (resp. does not induce) w; I_{F_w} ⊆ Γ_{F_w} is the inertia subgroup; κ_w is the residue field of F_w and Γ_{κ_w} = Γ_{F_w}/I_{F_w}; φ_w ∈ Γ_{F_w} is a lift of the ARITHMETIC Frobenius of Γ_{κ_w}.
items.note: Arithmetic Frobenius throughout (so ε_ℓ(φ_w) = ‖w‖, cf. footnote 7). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Definition 1.3.2 — strongly disjoint sets of places
items.statement: Two subsets Σ⁺₁ and Σ⁺₂ of nonarchimedean places of F⁺ are strongly disjoint if there is no common rational prime underlying the places from both sets.
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §2 standing setup
items.statement: In §2, F ⊆ ℂ is a number field, not necessarily CM (so that the discussion also applies to an orthogonal case). ℓ is an odd rational prime unramified in F; E_λ/ℚ_ℓ is a finite extension with ring of integers O_λ and maximal ideal λ; 𝔹_cris is Fontaine's crystalline period ring for ℚ_ℓ; ε_ℓ is the ℓ-adic cyclotomic character. From Definition 2.4.4 on, complex conjugation 𝔠 is assumed to restrict to an automorphism of F (of order at most two) and F⁺ := F^{𝔠=1}.
items.note: Most of §2 generalizes [46] (Liu, HZ cycles) and [47]. When [F:F⁺] = 1 the setting is that of [46]; the case [F:F⁺] = 2 is new and is where Lemma 2.6.4 fails (E1). Missing: routed to a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 (route 1).

items.name: Continuous group cohomology (convention)
items.statement: For a topological group Γ and R ∈ Mod(Γ, L) (L a ℤ_ℓ-ring finite over ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ), Hⁱ(Γ, R) is continuous cohomology (continuous cochains modulo coboundaries; H¹ = continuous crossed homomorphisms modulo principal ones). For Γ ≅ ℤ̂ with topological generator γ one has H⁰ = R^Γ and H¹(Γ, R) = R_Γ = R/(γ−1)R. Global Galois cohomology is Hⁱ(F, R) := colim_Σ Hⁱ(Γ_{F,Σ}, R) (Notation 2.3.1).
items.locator: §1.3 (étale cohomology is continuous for ℓ-adic coefficient rings), p. 118; proof of Lemma 2.1.3, p. 121; Notation 2.3.1, p. 126
items.note: Implicit convention (the paper does not write out cochains). The identification H¹(ℤ̂, M) = M_Γ is used in the proof of Lemma 2.1.3(2). Library: TauCeti.ContCohomology.H1 at the pinned commits.

items.name: H¹ with trivial action is Hom
items.statement: If a profinite group Γ′ acts trivially on R, then H¹(Γ′, R) = Hom_cont(Γ′, R) = Hom(Γ′^{ab}, R). In (2.3): Γ_{F_ρ} acts trivially on R, so H¹(F_ρ, R)^G = Hom_G(Γ^{ab}_{F_ρ}, R) with G = Gal(F_ρ/F) acting on Γ^{ab}_{F_ρ} by conjugation and on R through ρ.
items.note: Standard; used without comment. Library: TauCeti.ContCohomology.H1EquivOfSmulEqSelf at the pinned commits.

items.name: Inflation–restriction exact sequence (as used)
items.statement: For a profinite group Γ, a closed normal subgroup Γ′ and a continuous Γ-module R, 0 → H¹(Γ/Γ′, R^{Γ′}) → H¹(Γ, R) → H¹(Γ′, R)^{Γ/Γ′} is exact, and it continues with → H²(Γ/Γ′, R^{Γ′}) (→ H²(Γ,R)) when R is discrete or the relevant lim¹ vanish.
items.locator: §2.2 after Definition 2.2.2 (citing [47, Lemma 2.6]), p. 124; proof of Lemma 2.3.5, p. 128; (2.3), p. 127
items.note: Standard; the paper cites [47, Lemma 2.6] for the local unramified case. Library: TauCeti.ContCohomology.explicitInfRes_exact at the pinned commits.

items.name: Notation 2.1.1 — Mod(Γ, L), Mod(Γ, L)_tor, Mod(Γ, L)_fr
items.statement: Let Γ be a topological group and L a ℤ_ℓ-ring that is finite over either ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ (every finitely generated L-module carries its natural ℓ-adic topology). Mod(Γ, L) is the category of finitely generated L-modules equipped with a continuous action of Γ; Mod(Γ, L)_tor (resp. Mod(Γ, L)_fr) is the full subcategory of objects whose underlying L-modules are torsion (resp. free).
items.note: Later notation: R_ℚ := R ⊗_{O_λ} E_λ and R̄^{(m)} := R ⊗_{O_λ} O_λ/λ^m (Notation 2.2.1). Planned: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0 plans integral and rational continuous cohomology.

items.name: Definition 2.1.2 — weakly semisimple
items.statement: An L[Γ]-module M is weakly semisimple if (1) M is an object of Mod(Γ, L); and (2) the natural map M^Γ → M_Γ is an isomorphism.
items.note: Only used for Γ ≅ ℤ̂ (Lemmas 2.1.3–2.1.5), e.g. for Frobenius acting on inertia invariants in §§6, 8. Missing: routed to a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 (route 1).

api.name: RankinSelberg.WeakSemisimplicity.compatibility

items.name: Lemma 2.1.3(1) — vanishing coinvariants force vanishing invariants
items.statement: Suppose Γ ≅ ℤ̂ and M ∈ Mod(Γ, L). If M_Γ = 0 then M^Γ = 0.
items.note: Proof: with a topological generator γ, 0 → M^Γ → M →(γ−1)→ M → M_Γ → 0 is exact; γ−1 surjective on the Noetherian module M is injective. Correct. Missing: routed to a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 (route 1).

items.name: Lemma 2.1.3(2) — surjective invariants→coinvariants implies weakly semisimple
items.statement: Suppose Γ ≅ ℤ̂ and M ∈ Mod(Γ, L). If the natural map M^Γ → M_Γ is surjective, then M is weakly semisimple.
items.note: Proof: the Γ-cohomology sequence of 0 → M^Γ → M → M/M^Γ → 0 gives (M/M^Γ)^Γ → M^Γ → M_Γ → (M/M^Γ)_Γ → 0 (using H¹(ℤ̂,−) = (−)_Γ); surjectivity gives (M/M^Γ)_Γ = 0, so (M/M^Γ)^Γ = 0 by (1), hence injectivity. Correct. Missing: routed to a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 (route 1).

items.name: Lemma 2.1.4(1) — direct sums of weakly semisimple modules
items.statement: Suppose Γ ≅ ℤ̂. A finite direct sum of weakly semisimple L[Γ]-modules is weakly semisimple.
items.note: 'Obvious' (invariants and coinvariants commute with finite sums). Missing: routed to a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 (route 1).

items.name: Lemma 2.1.4(2) — subquotients of weakly semisimple modules
items.statement: Suppose Γ ≅ ℤ̂. A subquotient L[Γ]-module of a weakly semisimple L[Γ]-module is weakly semisimple.
items.note: Proof via the diagram (2.1) for 0 → N → M → Q → 0: Q^Γ → Q_Γ surjective (so Q weakly semisimple by Lemma 2.1.3(2)), then M^Γ → Q^Γ surjective, so N_Γ → M_Γ injective and (2.1) is an isomorphism of exact sequences. Checked; correct. Missing: routed to a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 (route 1).

items.name: Lemma 2.1.5 — integral weak semisimplicity from the residual one
items.statement: Suppose Γ ≅ ℤ̂ and M ∈ Mod(Γ, O_λ)_fr. Suppose that M ⊗_{O_λ} O_λ/λ is weakly semisimple and dim_{E_λ}(M ⊗_{O_λ} E_λ)^Γ ⩾ dim_{O_λ/λ}(M ⊗_{O_λ} O_λ/λ)^Γ. Then M is weakly semisimple, and dim_{E_λ}(M ⊗_{O_λ} E_λ)^Γ = dim_{O_λ/λ}(M ⊗_{O_λ} O_λ/λ)^Γ.
items.note: Proof: M^Γ is saturated, so M^Γ ⊗ O_λ/λ ↪ (M ⊗ O_λ/λ)^Γ, an isomorphism by the dimension hypothesis; then Nakayama and Lemma 2.1.3(2). Correct. Used in §6 (Lemma 2.1.5 is cited at pp. 256, 287 of the published text). Missing: routed to a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 (route 1).

items.name: Definition 2.1.6 — exponent and order
items.statement: For an O_λ-module M and x ∈ M: exp_λ(x, M) := min{d ∈ ℤ_{⩾0} ∪ {∞} | λ^d x = 0} and ord_λ(x, M) := sup{d ∈ ℤ_{⩾0} | x ∈ λ^d M}.
items.note: Slightly generalizes [46, Definition 5.1]. Used in Proposition 2.6.7 and §8. Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: Notation 2.2.1 — local categories and functors
items.statement: Let w be a nonarchimedean place of F, L a ℤ_ℓ-ring finite over ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ, ? ∈ { , tor, fr}. (1) Mod(F_w, L)_? := Mod(Γ_{F_w}, L)_?; (2) –(j) is the j-th Tate twist (j ∈ ℤ); (3) –^∨: Mod(F_w, L)_?^{op} → Mod(F_w, L)_?, M ↦ Hom_L(M, L). Also –_ℚ: Mod(F_w, O_λ) → Mod(F_w, E_λ), M ↦ M ⊗_{O_λ} E_λ; –^*: Mod(F_w, O_λ)_tor^{op} → Mod(F_w, O_λ), M ↦ Hom_{O_λ}(M, E_λ/O_λ) (E_λ-Pontryagin dual); and for m, m′ ∈ {1, 2, …, ∞} with m′ ⩾ m the reduction functor –̄^{(m)} := – ⊗_{O_λ} O_λ/λ^m: Mod(F_w, O_λ/λ^{m′}) → Mod(F_w, O_λ/λ^m), R ↦ R̄^{(m)}, where O_λ/λ^∞ := O_λ; R̄ := R̄^{(1)}.
items.note: On torsion O_λ-modules –^∨ is only meaningful for L = O_λ/λ^m. Global analogues in Notation 2.3.1. Missing: routed to a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 (route 1).

items.name: (2.2) — local Tate pairing
items.statement: For R ∈ Mod(F_w, O_λ): ⟨ , ⟩_w: H¹(F_w, R) × H¹(F_w, R^*(1)) →(∪) H²(F_w, E_λ/O_λ(1)) ≃ E_λ/O_λ.
items.note: Cup product plus the invariant map of local class field theory. The submodule functor H¹_ns(F_w, −) is H¹_ur for ℓ ∤ w and H¹_f for ℓ | w. Planned: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L1 plans local and global duality (local Tate pairings and Euler characteristics imported from ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02).

items.name: Definition 2.2.2 — singular and nonsingular local cohomology (ℓ ∤ w)
items.statement: Let w ∤ ℓ. For R in Mod(F_w, E_λ) or Mod(F_w, O_λ): H¹_sing(F_w, R) := H¹(I_{F_w}, R)^{Γ_{κ_w}}, and H¹_ns(F_w, R) is the kernel of the canonical map ∂_w: H¹(F_w, R) → H¹_sing(F_w, R).
items.note: H¹_ns is the usual unramified subgroup H¹_ur. Planned: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L2 plans Selmer structures, unramified and relaxed local conditions.

items.name: After Definition 2.2.2 — ∂_w is surjective and H¹_ns = H¹(κ_w, R^{I})
items.statement: For w ∤ ℓ and R in Mod(F_w, E_λ) or Mod(F_w, O_λ), the map ∂_w: H¹(F_w, R) → H¹_sing(F_w, R) is surjective and H¹_ns(F_w, R) is canonically isomorphic to H¹(κ_w, R^{I_{F_w}}).
items.note: From inflation–restriction (cited [47, Lemma 2.6]) and H²(κ_w, R^{I_{F_w}}) = 0 (Γ_{κ_w} ≅ ℤ̂). Missing: routed to a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 (route 1).

items.name: Lemma 2.2.3 — unramified classes are mutually orthogonal
items.statement: Let w ∤ ℓ. For R ∈ Mod(F_w, O_λ)_tor, the restriction of the local Tate pairing ⟨ , ⟩_w (2.2) to H¹_ns(F_w, R) × H¹_ns(F_w, R^*(1)) vanishes.
items.note: Proof: the cup product factors through H²(κ_w, R^{I_{F_w}} ⊗ R^*(1)^{I_{F_w}}) = 0. Only vanishing is stated; exact-annihilator (perfectness) statements are NOT asserted here (an earlier version of this extraction's 'perfect pairing' was an addition). Planned: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L1 plans local and global duality (local Tate pairings and Euler characteristics imported from ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02).

items.name: Definition 2.2.4 — crystalline torsion and integral representations (ℓ | w)
items.statement: Let w | ℓ (so F_w/ℚ_ℓ is finite unramified), let –₀: Mod(F_w, O_λ) → Mod(F_w, ℤ_ℓ) be the forgetful functor, and let a ⩽ b be integers. (1) R ∈ Mod(F_w, ℤ_ℓ)_tor is crystalline (with Hodge–Tate weights in [a,b]) if R = R″/R′ where R′ ⊆ R″ are two Γ_{F_w}-stable ℤ_ℓ-lattices in a crystalline ℚ_ℓ-representation of Γ_{F_w} (with Hodge–Tate weights in [a,b]). (2) R ∈ Mod(F_w, ℤ_ℓ) is crystalline (with HT weights in [a,b]) if R/ℓ^m R is torsion crystalline (with HT weights in [a,b]) for every m ⩾ 1. (3) R ∈ Mod(F_w, O_λ) is crystalline (with HT weights in [a,b]) if R₀ is.
items.note: Convention: ℚ_ℓ(1) has Hodge–Tate weight −1. Footnote 5 claims that for a ⩽ 0 ⩽ b, b − a ⩽ ℓ − 2, R ∈ Mod(F_w, ℤ_ℓ)_fr is crystalline iff R_ℚ is, 'by Lemma 2.2.6'; the direction R_ℚ crystalline ⇒ R crystalline is immediate from (1)–(2) (take R″ = R, R′ = ℓ^m R) and is the only one used; the converse does not follow from Lemma 2.2.6 (new minor issue). Planned: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L4 plans finite Bloch–Kato local conditions; LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 plans crystalline and Fontaine–Laffaille local conditions.

items.name: Definition 2.2.5 — H¹_ns for w | ℓ (Nizioł)
items.statement: Let w | ℓ and let R ∈ Mod(F_w, O_λ) be crystalline. H¹_ns(F_w, R) is the subset of H¹(F_w, R) = H¹(F_w, R₀) consisting of the classes s represented by an extension 0 → R₀ → R_s → ℤ_ℓ → 0 in Mod(F_w, ℤ_ℓ) with R_s crystalline. It is an O_λ-submodule of H¹(F_w, R).
items.note: Following [59, §4] (Nizioł). The O_λ-module structure follows because torsion crystalline modules are closed under subquotients and finite sums (Baer sum and pushout). Footnote 6: if R is crystalline with HT weights in [a,b], a ⩽ 0 ⩽ b, then R_s is crystalline with HT weights in [a,b]. Missing: routed to a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 (route 1).

items.name: Lemma 2.2.6 — integral H¹_ns is the saturation of Bloch–Kato's H¹_f (Breuil)
items.statement: Let w | ℓ and let R ∈ Mod(F_w, O_λ)_fr be such that R_ℚ is crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights in [a, b] with a ⩽ 0 ⩽ b and b − a ⩽ ℓ − 2. Then H¹_ns(F_w, R) coincides with the preimage of ker(H¹(F_w, R_ℚ) → H¹(F_w, R_ℚ ⊗_{ℚ_ℓ} 𝔹_cris)) under the natural map H¹(F_w, R) → H¹(F_w, R_ℚ).
items.note: Cited, not proved: [9, Proposition 6] (Breuil 1999). Black box of Fontaine–Laffaille type; ℓ unramified in F is essential. Missing: routed to a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 (route 1).

items.name: Lemma 2.2.7 — crystalline local conditions are orthogonal up to the inverse different
items.statement: Let w | ℓ and let the integers a, b satisfy a < 0 ⩽ b and b − a ⩽ (ℓ−2)/2. Then for every R ∈ Mod(F_w, O_λ)_tor that is crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights in [a, b], the restriction of the local Tate pairing ⟨ , ⟩_w (2.2) to H¹_ns(F_w, R) × H¹_ns(F_w, R^*(1)) takes values in 𝔡_λ^{−1}/O_λ, where 𝔡_λ ⊆ O_λ is the different ideal of E_λ over ℚ_ℓ.
items.note: Proof: the trace Tr: (R^*)₀ → (R₀)^* maps H¹_ns(F_w, R^*(1)) into H¹_ns(F_w, (R₀)^*(1)); Tr_{E_λ/ℚ_ℓ}⟨x,y⟩_w = ⟨x, Tr(y)⟩_w = 0 by [59, Proposition 6.2]; O_λ-linearity then gives ⟨x,y⟩_w ∈ 𝔡_λ^{−1}/O_λ. Checked. Implicitly uses that R^*(1) is crystalline (weights in [−1−b, −1−a]). Missing: routed to a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 (route 1).

items.name: [59, Proposition 6.2] — orthogonality of torsion crystalline classes over ℤ_ℓ (as used)
items.statement: For w | ℓ with F_w/ℚ_ℓ unramified, integers a < 0 ⩽ b with b − a ⩽ (ℓ−2)/2, and a torsion ℤ_ℓ[Γ_{F_w}]-module R₀ crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights in [a, b], the local Tate pairing H¹_ns(F_w, R₀) × H¹_ns(F_w, (R₀)^*(1)) → ℚ_ℓ/ℤ_ℓ vanishes (H¹_ns as in Definition 2.2.5).
items.locator: Invoked in the proof of Lemma 2.2.7, published p. 125
items.note: Cited from Nizioł, Duke Math. J. 71 (1993), not proved here. Missing: routed to a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 (route 1).

items.name: Notation 2.3.1 — global categories, cohomology and localization
items.statement: For a finite set Σ of places of F, Γ_{F,Σ} is the Galois group of the maximal subextension of F̄/F unramified outside Σ. For L a ℤ_ℓ-ring finite over ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ and ? ∈ { , tor, fr}: Mod(F, L)_? := colim_Σ Mod(Γ_{F,Σ}, L)_? (inflation as transition functors), with functors –(j), –^∨, –_ℚ, –^*, –̄^{(m)} as in Notation 2.2.1; for R ∈ Mod(F, L), Hⁱ(F, R) := colim_Σ Hⁱ(Γ_{F,Σ}, R); for every place w of F there is the restriction functor Mod(F, L) → Mod(F_w, L) and loc_w: Hⁱ(F, R) → Hⁱ(F_w, R) is the localization map.
items.note: Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: Definition 2.3.2 — reducibility depth
items.statement: Let G be a profinite group and R ∈ Mod(G, O_λ)_tor. The reducibility depth of R is the smallest integer r_R ⩾ 0 such that (1) every G-stable O_λ-submodule R′ ⊆ R not contained in λR contains λ^{r_R}R; and (2) for every positive integer m, End_{O_λ[G]}(R̄^{(m)})/O_λ·id is annihilated by λ^{r_R}. If R/λR is absolutely irreducible, then r_R = 0.
items.note: From [46, Definition 5.1]. Checked the last sentence (absolute irreducibility of R/λR forces R free over its annihilator, Nakayama, Schur). Note the notation clash: in Lemma 2.3.3 and Definition 2.6.5, r_R for R ∈ Mod(F, O_λ) denotes a uniform upper bound, not a minimum. Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: Lemma 2.3.3 — uniform bound on reducibility depths
items.statement: Let R ∈ Mod(F, O_λ) be such that R_ℚ is absolutely irreducible. Then there exists an integer r_R depending on R only such that R̄^{(m)} has reducibility depth at most r_R for every positive integer m.
items.note: Proof: 'the same argument in [46, Lemma 5.2] applies … with ℤ/pⁿ replaced by O_λ/λ^m' (cited). r_R is not canonical; Definition 2.6.5 uses 'the' r_R of this lemma, so any admissible choice gives a (weaker or stronger) notion of abundance. Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: (2.3) — F_ρ, G, Res_ρ and the pairing [ , ]
items.statement: Fix m ⩾ 1 and R ∈ Mod(F, O_λ/λ^m)_fr with associated ρ: Γ_F → GL(R). F_ρ/F is the Galois extension fixed by ker ρ and G := Gal(F_ρ/F) ≅ im ρ. Res_ρ: H¹(F, R) → H¹(F_ρ, R)^G = Hom_G(Γ^{ab}_{F_ρ}, R), where Γ^{ab}_{F_ρ} := Gal(F^{ab}_ρ/F_ρ), F^{ab}_ρ ⊆ F̄ the maximal abelian extension of F_ρ, with G acting by conjugation. Res_ρ induces an O_λ-linear pairing [ , ]: H¹(F, R) × Γ^{ab}_{F_ρ} → R, compatible with the G-actions.
items.note: ker Res_ρ = H¹(G, R) by inflation–restriction. Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: (2.4) — the field F_S and the injection θ_S
items.statement: In the setting of (2.3), let S be a finitely generated O_λ/λ^m-submodule of H¹(F, R), and let F_S/F_ρ be the finite abelian extension such that Gal(F^{ab}_ρ/F_S) is the subgroup of Γ^{ab}_{F_ρ} of those γ with [s, γ] = 0 for every s ∈ S. The pairing induces an injective map θ_S: Gal(F_S/F_ρ) → Hom_{O_λ}(S, R) of abelian groups, compatible with the G-actions (G acting on Gal(F_S/F_ρ) by conjugation and on Hom(S, R) through R).
items.note: F_S is Galois over F; it need not be Galois over F⁺ (this matters in §2.6). θ_S(Gal) is only a ℤ_ℓ-submodule, not necessarily O_λ-stable. Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: The sequence 𝔣 (after (2.4))
items.note: As in [46, §5.1]. Equivalently 𝔣(0) = 𝔣(1) = 1 and 𝔣(r+1) = 2(𝔣(r)+1) for r ⩾ 1. Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: Lemma 2.3.4 — the image of θ_S is λ^{𝔣(r_S)r_R}-saturated
items.statement: In the setting of (2.3)–(2.4), suppose that Res_ρ is injective. If S is a free O_λ/λ^m-module of rank r_S (printed: 'for some positive integer m'), then the O_λ-submodule of Hom_{O_λ}(S, R) generated by the image of θ_S contains λ^{𝔣(r_S) r_R} Hom_{O_λ}(S, R), where r_R is the reducibility depth of R.
items.note: Proof by 'the same argument in [46, Lemma 5.4] … with ℤ/pⁿ replaced by O_λ/λ^m' (printed 'O_λ/λ^m p', misprint); uses only injectivity of Res_ρ. As applied (Proposition 2.6.6, §§8.2–8.3) S is free over O_λ/λ^{m−m₀} while R = R̄^{(m)}; arXiv v1/v2 stated the lemma for S free over O_λ/λ^{m−m′}, 0 ⩽ m′ ⩽ m, and the argument works in that generality (new minor issue). Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: Lemma 2.3.5(a) — a nontrivial residual scalar gives injectivity of Res_ρ
items.statement: In the setting of (2.3) (R ∈ Mod(F, O_λ/λ^m)_fr), suppose that the image of Γ_F in GL(R̄) contains a nontrivial scalar element. Then Res_ρ is injective.
items.note: Proof: G then contains a nontrivial scalar γ of order prime to ℓ (the prime-to-ℓ part of a lift is the Teichmüller scalar); H¹(G/⟨γ⟩, R^γ) = 0 since R^γ = 0 and H¹(⟨γ⟩, R) = 0, so H¹(G, R) = 0 ([29, Proposition 9.1]). Checked; correct. Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: Lemma 2.3.5(b) — small semisimple residual representation gives injectivity of Res_ρ (as printed; false if O_λ/λ ≠ 𝔽_ℓ)
items.statement: In the setting of (2.3), suppose that dim_{O_λ/λ} R̄ ⩽ min{(ℓ+1)/2, ℓ−3}, R̄ is a semisimple (O_λ/λ)[Γ_F]-module, and Hom_{(O_λ/λ)[Γ_F]}(End(R̄), R̄) = 0. Then Res_ρ is injective.
items.note: Proof: induction on H¹(G, R̄^{(i)}); H¹(G/G¹, R̄) = 0 by [30, Theorem A]; the step needs Hom_G(G^i/G^{i+1}, R̄) = 0 with G^i/G^{i+1} ⊆ End(R̄) an 𝔽_ℓ[G]-submodule, and uses End(R̄) ⊗_{𝔽_ℓ} (O_λ/λ) ≃ End(R̄)^d, which is false as (O_λ/λ)[G]-modules (it is ⊕_σ of Frobenius twists). The lemma is false when [O_λ/λ : 𝔽_ℓ] > 1 (counterexample in new issue); it is correct if the last hypothesis is strengthened to Hom_{𝔽_ℓ[Γ_F]}(End(R̄), R̄) = 0, and correct as printed when O_λ/λ = 𝔽_ℓ. Semisimplicity of End(R̄) from [69, Corollaire 1] (2 dim R̄ < ℓ + 2). Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: [29, Proposition 9.1] — scalar trick (as used)
items.statement: If a finite group G acting on a module R contains a central element γ of order prime to ℓ acting on R by a scalar z with z − 1 invertible, then H¹(G, R) = 0 (since H¹(⟨γ⟩, R) = 0 and R^γ = 0).
items.locator: Invoked in the proof of Lemma 2.3.5(a), published p. 128
items.note: Cited from Gross, 'Kolyvagin's work on modular elliptic curves'; elementary. Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: [30, Theorem A] — H¹ vanishing for small faithful semisimple modules (as used)
items.statement: As used: if a finite group H has no nontrivial normal ℓ-subgroup and V is a faithful semisimple k[H]-module (k of characteristic ℓ) with dim V ⩽ ℓ − 3, then H¹(H, V) = 0.
items.locator: Invoked in the proof of Lemma 2.3.5(b), published p. 128
items.note: Cited from Guralnick, 'Small representations are completely reducible', J. Algebra 220 (1999); the exact hypotheses of Theorem A there were not re-checked in this reading. Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: [69, Corollaire 1] — semisimplicity of tensor products (as used)
items.statement: If V₁, …, V_k are semisimple representations of a group over a field of characteristic ℓ with Σ (dim V_i − 1) < ℓ, then V₁ ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ V_k is semisimple. In particular End(R̄) = R̄ ⊗ R̄^∨ is semisimple when R̄ is semisimple and 2 dim R̄ < ℓ + 2.
items.locator: Invoked in the proof of Lemma 2.3.5(b), published p. 128 (and Lemma 8.1.5); also Cited in the proof of Lemma 8.1.5, published p. 305
items.note: Cited from Serre, Invent. Math. 116 (1994). Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: Definition 2.4.1 — Bloch–Kato Selmer group
items.statement: For R ∈ Mod(F, E_λ), H¹_f(F, R) is the E_λ-subspace of H¹(F, R) of classes s such that (1) loc_w(s) ∈ H¹_ns(F_w, R) (Definition 2.2.2) for every nonarchimedean place w of F not above ℓ; and (2) loc_w(s) ∈ ker(H¹(F_w, R) → H¹(F_w, R ⊗_{ℚ_ℓ} 𝔹_cris)) for every place w of F above ℓ.
items.note: From [7]. No condition at archimedean places (ℓ odd). Planned: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L2 plans Selmer structures, unramified and relaxed local conditions; SelmerIwasawaCohomology L4 plans finite Bloch–Kato local conditions.

items.name: Definition 2.4.2 — integral Selmer group and propagated reductions
items.statement: For R ∈ Mod(F, O_λ)_fr: (1) the (integral) Bloch–Kato Selmer group H¹_f(F, R) is the inverse image of H¹_f(F, R_ℚ) under H¹(F, R) → H¹(F, R_ℚ); (2) for m ∈ {1, 2, …, ∞}, H¹_{f,R}(F, R̄^{(m)}) is the image of H¹_f(F, R) under H¹(F, R) → H¹(F, R̄^{(m)}).
items.note: H¹_{f,R}(F, R̄^{(m)}) depends on the lattice R, not only on R̄^{(m)}. Missing: routed to a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 (route 1).

items.name: Lemma 2.4.3 — propagated classes satisfy the local conditions
items.statement: Let R ∈ Mod(F, O_λ)_fr and suppose either (1) w is a nonarchimedean place of F not above ℓ at which R is unramified, or (2) w is a place of F above ℓ at which R_ℚ is crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights in [a, b] with a ⩽ 0 ⩽ b and b − a ⩽ ℓ − 2. Then for every positive integer m, loc_w(H¹_{f,R}(F, R̄^{(m)})) ⊆ H¹_ns(F_w, R̄^{(m)}), where loc_w: H¹(F, R̄^{(m)}) → H¹(F_w, R̄^{(m)}).
items.note: Case (1): cited [65, Lemma 1.3.5 & Lemma 1.3.8] (Rubin). Case (2): Lemma 2.2.6 plus functoriality of Definition 2.2.5 under R → R̄^{(m)} (pushout of a crystalline extension; implicit). Checked. Missing: routed to a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 (route 1).

items.name: [65, Lemmas 1.3.5, 1.3.8] — unramified local conditions propagate (as used)
items.statement: If w ∤ ℓ and T is a free O_λ-module with continuous Γ_{F_w}-action unramified at w, then the preimage of H¹_ur(F_w, T ⊗ E_λ) in H¹(F_w, T) equals H¹_ur(F_w, T), and its image in H¹(F_w, T/λ^m T) lies in H¹_ur(F_w, T/λ^m T).
items.locator: Invoked in the proof of Lemma 2.4.3(1), published p. 129
items.note: Cited from Rubin, Euler Systems (2000). Missing: routed to a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 (route 1).

items.name: Definition 2.4.4 — purity of weight μ
items.statement: Let w ∤ ℓ be a nonarchimedean place of F and R ∈ Mod(F_w, E_λ), with attached Weil–Deligne representation WD(R) and graded pieces gr_n WD(R) of the monodromy filtration. For μ ∈ ℤ, R is pure of weight μ if gr_n WD(R) is strictly pure of weight μ + n for each n, i.e. all eigenvalues of φ_w on gr_n WD(R) are Weil ‖w‖^{−(μ+n)}-numbers.
items.note: With φ_w arithmetic Frobenius; E_λ(1) is (strictly) pure of weight −2. Missing: routed to a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 (route 1).

items.name: Lemma 2.4.5 — conjugation preserves Selmer groups
items.statement: Assume 𝔠 restricts to an automorphism of F and let –^𝔠: Mod(F, L) → Mod(F, L) be induced by conjugation by 𝔠. For every R ∈ Mod(F, E_λ), –^𝔠 induces an isomorphism H¹_f(F, R) ≃ H¹_f(F, R^𝔠).
items.note: Proof: apply –^𝔠 to extensions; the local conditions of Definition 2.4.1 are preserved. Correct. Missing: routed to a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 (route 1).

items.name: Proposition 2.4.6(1) — reductions of saturated free Selmer submodules stay free
items.statement: Let R ∈ Mod(F, O_λ)_fr and let S be a free O_λ-submodule of H¹_f(F, R) whose image in H¹_f(F, R)/H¹_f(F, R)_tor is saturated. For every positive integer m, the image S^{(m)} of S in H¹_{f,R}(F, R̄^{(m)}) is a free O_λ/λ^m-module of the same rank as S.
items.note: Proof: with T the image of H¹_f(F, R)_tor, the map (H¹_f/H¹_f,tor)/λ^m → H¹_{f,R}(F, R̄^{(m)})/T is injective (H¹_f(F,R) is saturated in H¹(F,R) and H¹(F,R)/λ^m ↪ H¹(F, R̄^{(m)})). Checked. No hypothesis H⁰ = 0 is needed (an earlier version of this extraction's 'when H⁰(F, R̄) = 0' is not in the paper). Missing: routed to a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 (route 1).

items.name: Proposition 2.4.6(2) — uniform annihilation of localizations at a finite set of places
items.statement: Let R ∈ Mod(F, O_λ)_fr satisfy R^𝔠_ℚ ≃ R^∨_ℚ(1), with R_ℚ pure of weight −1 at every nonarchimedean place w of F not above ℓ. For every finite set Σ of places of F there is a positive integer m_Σ, depending on R and Σ, such that for every S as in (1) and every integer m > m_Σ, loc_w(λ^{m_Σ} S^{(m)}) = 0 for every nonarchimedean place w ∈ Σ not above ℓ.
items.note: Proof: H⁰(F_w, R_ℚ) = 0 and H²(F_w, R_ℚ) ≃ H⁰(F_w, R^∨_ℚ(1))^∨ = 0 by purity, so H¹(F_w, R_ℚ) = 0 by the Euler characteristic formula (cf. [56, Proposition 4.2.2(1)]); if λ^{m_w} kills H¹(F_w, R) and H²(F_w, R)_tor then λ^{2m_w} kills H¹(F_w, R̄^{(m)}); m_Σ := max 2m_w. Checked (the conclusion holds for all m). Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: Local Tate duality and Euler characteristic for w ∤ ℓ (as used)
items.statement: For w ∤ ℓ and V ∈ Mod(F_w, E_λ): H²(F_w, V) ≃ H⁰(F_w, V^∨(1))^∨ and dim H⁰ − dim H¹ + dim H² = 0. Hence H¹(F_w, V) = 0 when V and V^∨(1) have no Γ_{F_w}-invariants (e.g. V pure of weight −1).
items.locator: Invoked in the proof of Proposition 2.4.6(2), published p. 131
items.note: Standard (Tate); the paper points to the proof of [56, Proposition 4.2.2(1)] (Nekovář). Planned: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L1 plans local and global duality (local Tate pairings and Euler characteristics imported from ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02).

items.name: Notation 2.5.1 — the group scheme 𝒢_N and ν
items.statement: When [F:F⁺] = 2: 𝒢_N := (GL_N × GL₁) ⋊ {1, 𝔠} with 𝔠² = 1 and 𝔠(g, μ)𝔠 = (μ·ᵗg^{−1}, μ) for (g, μ) ∈ GL_N × GL₁; ν: 𝒢_N → GL₁ is the homomorphism with ν|_{GL_N×GL₁} the projection to GL₁ and ν(𝔠) = −1. When [F:F⁺] = 1: 𝒢_N := GL_N × GL₁, 𝔠 is regarded as the identity, and ν is the projection to the second factor.
items.note: From [18, §1] (Clozel–Harris–Taylor). Useful identity: ((A, μ)𝔠)² = (μ A ᵗA^{−1}, μ²). Planned: GlobalGaloisDeformations G7 plans polarized dimension-n deformation problems for a CM extension, with the group 𝒢_n.

items.name: Notation 2.5.2 — r^♮
items.statement: For a topological ring R and a continuous homomorphism r: Γ_{F⁺} → 𝒢_N(R) with r(Γ_F) ⊆ GL_N(R) × R^×, r^♮: Γ_F → GL_N(R) is the composition of r|_{Γ_F} with the projection GL_N(R) × R^× → GL_N(R).

items.name: Definition 2.5.3 — j-polarization
items.statement: Let L be a ℤ_ℓ-ring finite over ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ, j an integer and R ∈ Mod(F, L). A j-polarization of R is an isomorphism Ξ: R^𝔠 ⥲ R^∨(j) in Mod(F, L) such that Ξ^{𝔠,∨}(j) = (−1)^{μ_Ξ + j + 1}·Ξ for some μ_Ξ ∈ ℤ/2ℤ. R is j-polarizable if a j-polarization exists.
items.note: After [18, §1]. For the Rankin–Selberg product (§2.7) j = 1; for R_α in §2.7, j = 1 − α. Missing: routed to a source of GlobalGaloisDeformations G7 (route 3).

items.name: Construction 2.5.4 — extension ρ₊ of a polarized ρ to Γ_{F⁺}
items.statement: Let R be a nonzero object of Mod(F, L)_fr with ρ: Γ_F → GL(R), equipped with a j-polarization Ξ, and fix R ≃ L^{⊕N}. (1) If [F:F⁺] = 1, ρ₊: Γ_{F⁺} → 𝒢_N(L) sends g ∈ Γ_{F⁺} = Γ_F to (ρ(g), ε_ℓ^j(g)). (2) If [F:F⁺] = 2, Ξ gives B ∈ GL_N(L) with ρ^𝔠 = B ∘ ε_ℓ^j ρ^∨ ∘ B^{−1} and B ᵗB^{−1} = (−1)^{μ_Ξ+j+1}; ρ₊: Γ_{F⁺} → 𝒢_N(L) is the continuous homomorphism with ρ₊|_{Γ_F} = (ρ, ε_ℓ^j|_{Γ_F}, 1) and ρ₊(𝔠) = (B, (−1)^{μ_Ξ+j+1}, 𝔠). ρ₊ is called an extension of ρ.
items.note: Checked: B = X^{−1} for the matrix X of Ξ, ᵗX = (−1)^{μ_Ξ+j+1}X gives the sign; ρ₊(𝔠)² = 1 and ρ₊(𝔠)ρ₊(g)ρ₊(𝔠)^{−1} = ρ₊(𝔠g𝔠); ν∘ρ₊ = ε_ℓ^j·η_{F/F⁺}^{μ_Ξ}. Missing: routed to a source of GlobalGaloisDeformations G7 (route 3).

items.name: Notation 2.6.1 — ρ̄^{(m)}, ρ̄₊^{(m)}, F^{(m)}, F₊^{(m)}
items.statement: Take a nonzero R ∈ Mod(F, O_λ)_fr with ρ: Γ_F → GL(R) and a j-polarization Ξ; fix R ≃ O_λ^{⊕N}; let ρ₊: Γ_{F⁺} → 𝒢_N(O_λ) be the extension of Construction 2.5.4. For m ⩾ 1, ρ̄^{(m)}: Γ_F → GL(R̄^{(m)}) ≃ GL_N(O_λ/λ^m) and ρ̄₊^{(m)}: Γ_{F⁺} → 𝒢_N(O_λ/λ^m) are the reductions (superscript omitted for m = 1). F^{(m)} := F_{ρ̄^{(m)}} and F₊^{(m)} are the subfields of F̄ fixed by ker ρ̄^{(m)} and ker ρ̄₊^{(m)}; F ⊆ F^{(m)} ⊆ F₊^{(m)} ⊆ F^{(m)}(ζ_{ℓ^m}).
items.note: Gal(F₊^{(m)}/F⁺) ≃ im ρ̄₊^{(m)}. If [F:F⁺] = 1 the polarization forces ker ρ̄^{(m)} ⊆ ker ε̄_ℓ^j, so F₊^{(m)} = F^{(m)}; if [F:F⁺] = 2, F₊^{(m)} ⊇ 𝔠(F^{(m)}) and F^{(m)} need not be Galois over F⁺. Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: Notation 2.6.2 — h_γ
items.statement: For m ⩾ 1 and γ ∈ (GL_N(O_λ/λ^m) × (O_λ/λ^m)^×, 𝔠) ⊆ 𝒢_N(O_λ/λ^m) (the 𝔠-coset), h_γ ∈ GL_N(O_λ/λ^m) is the first component of γ^{[F:F⁺]} ∈ GL_N(O_λ/λ^m) × (O_λ/λ^m)^×.
items.note: For γ = ρ̄₊^{(m)}(y) with y ∈ Γ_{F⁺} ∖ Γ_F: h_γ = ρ̄^{(m)}(y²) (checked from Construction 2.5.4); for [F:F⁺] = 1, h_γ is the GL_N-component of γ. Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: Definition 2.6.3 — γ-associated places
items.statement: Fix m ⩾ 1, a finitely generated O_λ-submodule S of H¹_{f,R}(F, R̄^{(m)}) (so F_S/F^{(m)} is the finite abelian extension of (2.4) for ρ = ρ̄^{(m)}), and γ as in Notation 2.6.2 lying in im ρ̄₊^{(m)}. A place w₊^{(m)} of F₊^{(m)} is γ-associated if: it is not above ∞ or ℓ; it is unramified over F⁺; its underlying place of F^{(m)} is unramified in F_S; and its arithmetic Frobenius substitution in Gal(F₊^{(m)}/F⁺) ≃ im ρ̄₊^{(m)} coincides with γ.
items.note: Essentially [46, Definition 5.6]. For [F:F⁺] = 2 the underlying place of F⁺ is inert in F (γ lies in the 𝔠-coset). Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).
