items.name: Ψ_{w^{(m)}} and the set G_{S,γ}
items.statement: For a γ-associated place w₊^{(m)} with underlying places w^{(m)} of F^{(m)} and w of F, Ψ_{w^{(m)}} ∈ Gal(F_S/F^{(m)}) is the arithmetic Frobenius of w^{(m)} (well defined since F_S/F^{(m)} is abelian). G_{S,γ} ⊆ Gal(F_S/F^{(m)}) is the set of Ψ_{w^{(m)}} for all γ-associated places w₊^{(m)}. θ_S: Gal(F_S/F^{(m)}) → Hom_{O_λ}(S, R̄^{(m)}) is the injection (2.4) for ρ = ρ̄^{(m)}, Gal(F^{(m)}/F)-equivariant.
items.note: Computation (used for E1): if σ ∈ Gal(L/F⁺) is a Frobenius above w₊^{(m)} in the Galois closure L of F_S F₊^{(m)} over F⁺, then Ψ_{w^{(m)}} = σ^{[F:F⁺]·g}|_{F_S} with g the order of h_γ. Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: Lemma 2.6.4 — Frobenius elements at γ-associated places (as printed; false for [F:F⁺] = 2)
items.statement: In the setting of Definition 2.6.3, suppose that the order of γ is coprime to ℓ. Then G_{S,γ} = θ_S^{−1} Hom_{O_λ}(S, (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ}).
items.note: The inclusion ⊆ is proved correctly. The converse rests on 'it is easy to see that there is γ̃ ∈ Gal(F̃_S/F⁺) lifting γ such that the image of γ̃^{[F:F⁺]} in Gal(F_S/F) coincides with (g^{−1}Ψ)h_γ', which fails when [F:F⁺] = 2. True statement: G_{S,γ} = q(N^α) with N = Gal(L/F₊^{(m)}), α = conjugation by an order-d lift of γ, q the restriction to F_S; equality with the printed right side holds when [F:F⁺] = 1. Counterexample and discussion: issue E1. Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: θ^r_{S,γ}
items.statement: By Lemma 2.6.4, for every r ∈ ℕ there is a map of abelian groups θ^r_{S,γ}: G^r_{S,γ} → Hom_{O_λ}(S, ((R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ})^{⊕r}) induced by θ_S ((Ψ₁,…,Ψ_r) ↦ (s ↦ (θ_S(Ψ_i)(s))_i)).
items.note: Only the inclusion part of Lemma 2.6.4 (which is correct) is needed to define it. G_{S,γ} is a set, not a priori a group; 'map of abelian groups' is loose. Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: Definition 2.6.5 — (S, γ)-abundant tuples
items.statement: Suppose S is a free O_λ/λ^{m−m₀}-module of rank r_S for some m₀ ∈ ℕ and r_S ∈ ℕ. An r_S-tuple (Ψ₁, …, Ψ_{r_S}) ∈ G^{r_S}_{S,γ} is (S, γ)-abundant if the image of the homomorphism θ^{r_S}_{S,γ}(Ψ₁, …, Ψ_{r_S}): S → ((R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ})^{⊕r_S} contains λ^{m₀ + 𝔣(r_S) r_R}((R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ})^{⊕r_S}, where r_R and 𝔣(r_S) are the integers of Lemmas 2.3.3 and 2.3.4.
items.note: If (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ} ≅ O_λ/λ^m, abundance says the r_S × r_S matrix (θ_S(Ψ_i)(s_j)) over O_λ/λ^{m−m₀} has image containing λ^{𝔣(r_S)r_R}; this does NOT make it diagonalizable by a change of basis of S (E2). Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: Proposition 2.6.6 — existence of abundant tuples (as printed; false for [F:F⁺] = 2)
items.statement: Suppose S is a free O_λ/λ^{m−m₀}-module of rank r_S for some m₀ ∈ ℕ and r_S ∈ ℕ, and that: R_ℚ is absolutely irreducible; either one of the two assumptions in Lemma 2.3.5 is satisfied; the order of γ is coprime to ℓ; and (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ} is free over O_λ/λ^m of rank 1. Then an (S, γ)-abundant r_S-tuple exists.
items.note: Proof: Res_{ρ̄^{(m)}} injective (Lemma 2.3.5), Lemmas 2.3.3–2.3.4, Hom(S,(R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ}) a direct summand, then Lemma 2.6.4. Given Lemma 2.6.4 the rest is fine (r_S generators of the O_λ-span can be chosen inside θ_S(G_{S,γ}) by Nakayama). Because Lemma 2.6.4 fails, the proposition fails: in the E1 example (R = ℤ₃(1), j = 2) all hypotheses hold and G_{S,γ} = {1} (new issue). Also Lemma 2.3.4 is applied with S free over O_λ/λ^{m−m₀}. Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: Proposition 2.6.7 (first part) — diagonal basis for an abundant tuple (as printed; not valid)
items.statement: Let the assumptions be as in Proposition 2.6.6 and put r := r_S. For every (S, γ)-abundant r-tuple (Ψ₁, …, Ψ_r), one can choose a basis {s₁, …, s_r} of S such that θ_S(Ψ_i)(s_j) = 0 if i ≠ j and exp_λ(θ_S(Ψ_j)(s_j), (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ}) ⩾ m − m₀ − 𝔣(r)r_R.
items.note: Proof: 'obvious from Definition 2.6.5' — invalid: a matrix over O_λ/λ^{m−m₀} whose image contains λ^c need not be diagonalizable by column operations (e.g. [[λ,1],[0,λ]]); see E2. Used with r = 2 in Theorem 8.3.2.

items.name: Proposition 2.6.7 (second part) — localizations at the associated places
items.statement: In the setting of Proposition 2.6.7, if Ψ_i = Ψ_{w_i^{(m)}} for γ-associated places w_i^{(m)} of F₊^{(m)} (1 ⩽ i ⩽ r) and w_i denotes the underlying place of F, then loc_{w_i}(s_j) = 0 if i ≠ j and exp_λ(loc_{w_i}(s_i), H¹_ns(F_{w_i}, R̄^{(m)})) ⩾ m − m₀ − 𝔣(r)r_R. Here loc_{w_i}(S) ⊆ H¹_ns(F_{w_i}, R̄^{(m)}) by Definition 2.6.3 and Lemma 2.4.3.
items.note: Proof: H¹_ns(F^{(m)}_{w_i^{(m)}}, R̄^{(m)}) ≃ R̄^{(m)} by evaluation at Ψ_i, and θ_S(Ψ_i) = S → H¹_ns(F_{w_i}, R̄^{(m)}) → H¹_ns(F^{(m)}_{w_i^{(m)}}, R̄^{(m)}) ≃ R̄^{(m)}. The vanishing loc_{w_i}(s_j) = 0 also needs injectivity of the middle restriction, which holds: it is the norm R̄/(h−1) → R̄^{h} for h of order g prime to ℓ. Correct given the first part (which is not valid). Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: §2.7 setup — Rankin–Selberg tensor product
items.statement: For α = 0, 1 take R_α ∈ Mod(F, O_λ)_fr of rank n_α > 0 with ρ_α: Γ_F → GL(R_α) and a (1−α)-polarization Ξ_α: R_α^𝔠 ⥲ R_α^∨(1−α); fix R_α ≃ O_λ^{⊕n_α}. Assume n₀ = 2r₀ is even and n₁ = 2r₁+1 is odd. Put R := R₀ ⊗_{O_λ} R₁, ρ := ρ₀ ⊗ ρ₁: Γ_F → GL(R), and Ξ := Ξ₀ ⊗ Ξ₁: R^𝔠 ⥲ R^∨(1), a 1-polarization of R. ρ_w is the restriction of ρ to Γ_{F_w}; ε̄_ℓ^{(m)}: Γ_{F⁺} → (O_λ/λ^m)^× is ε_ℓ mod λ^m and ε̄_ℓ := ε̄_ℓ^{(1)}.
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: (GI^m_{F′,𝒫}) — the image condition of Lemma 2.7.1
items.statement: Let F′/F⁺ be a totally real finite Galois extension contained in ℂ and 𝒫(T) ∈ ℤ[T]. For m ⩾ 1, (GI^m_{F′,𝒫}) is the statement: the image of the restriction to Gal(F̄/F′) of (ρ̄₀₊^{(m)}, ρ̄₁₊^{(m)}, ε̄_ℓ^{(m)}): Γ_{F⁺} → 𝒢_{n₀}(O_λ/λ^m) × 𝒢_{n₁}(O_λ/λ^m) × (O_λ/λ^m)^× contains an element (γ₀, γ₁, ξ) such that (a) 𝒫(ξ) is invertible in O_λ/λ^m; (b) for α = 0, 1, γ_α ∈ (GL_{n_α}(O_λ/λ^m) × (O_λ/λ^m)^×, 𝔠) with order coprime to ℓ; (c) the kernels of h_{γ₀} − 1, h_{γ₁} − 1 and h_{γ₀} ⊗ h_{γ₁} − 1 (Notation 2.6.2) are all free over O_λ/λ^m of rank 1; (d) if [F:F⁺] = 2, h_{γ₀} has no eigenvalue equal to −1 in O_λ/λ; (e) if [F:F⁺] = 2, h_{γ₁} has no eigenvalue equal to −ξ in O_λ/λ.
items.note: Used in Definition 8.1.1 (L5-2) with F′ = F⁺_rflx and 𝒫 = T² − 1. For 𝒫 = 0 the condition is unsatisfiable (E4). By (c), (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ} is free of rank one for the associated γ ∈ 𝒢_{n₀n₁}. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

api.name: RankinSelberg.RankinSelbergTensorAndGiCondition.data
api.statement: Keep all three coordinates in a single image, with every spectral exclusion.

api.name: RankinSelberg.RankinSelbergTensorAndGiCondition.characterisation
api.statement: P=T²−1 forces ξ²−1 to be a unit.

api.name: RankinSelberg.RankinSelbergTensorAndGiCondition.compatibility
api.statement: A common power of the entire triple remains in the same simultaneous image.

uses.how: Keep all three coordinates in a single image, with every spectral exclusion.

items.name: Lemma 2.7.1 — (GI¹) implies (GI^m)
items.statement: In the setting of §2.7, let F′/F⁺ be a totally real finite Galois extension contained in ℂ and 𝒫(T) ∈ ℤ[T]. Then (GI¹_{F′,𝒫}) implies (GI^m_{F′,𝒫}) for every m ⩾ 1.
items.note: True, but the printed proof raises γ′₀ and γ′₁ to different ℓ-powers and keeps ξ′, so the triple need not lie in the image; fix: raise a single Galois element to one ℓ-power (E3). Rank one of ker(h−1) over O_λ/λ^m (not just '1 is an eigenvalue') follows from the averaging idempotent of the prime-to-ℓ-order h. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §2.7 — the elliptic-curve lattices R_α
items.statement: Let A₀, A₁ be elliptic curves over F⁺ and ℓ odd and unramified in F. For α = 0, 1 put R_α := (Sym^{n_α−1}_{ℤ_ℓ} H¹_ét(A_{α F̄}, ℤ_ℓ))(r_α) as a ℤ_ℓ[Γ_F]-module (r_α = ⌊n_α/2⌋). The paper asserts R_α ∈ Mod(F, ℤ_ℓ)_fr has rank n_α and a canonical (1−α)-polarization Ξ_α: R_α^𝔠 ⥲ R_α^∨(1−α); R := R₀ ⊗_{ℤ_ℓ} R₁, Ξ := Ξ₀ ⊗ Ξ₁.
items.note: The polarization is induced by the Weil pairing and R_α^𝔠 ≃ R_α (defined over F⁺); the induced pairing on Sym^{n−1} of a rank-two lattice is perfect over ℤ_ℓ only for ℓ ⩾ n_α, so the assertion needs ℓ ⩾ n_α (harmless: only large ℓ are used; new minor issue). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proposition 2.7.2(1) — nontrivial scalar in the residual image
items.statement: Suppose A_{0F̄} and A_{1F̄} are not isogenous and End(A_{0F̄}) = End(A_{1F̄}) = ℤ; let F′/F⁺ be totally real finite Galois in ℂ and 𝒫(T) ∈ ℤ[T]. Then for sufficiently large ℓ, the image of ρ̄: Γ_F → GL(R ⊗ 𝔽_ℓ) contains a nontrivial scalar element.
items.note: Proof: by [68, Théorème 6], for ℓ ≫ 0 the image of (ρ̄_{A₀,ℓ}, ρ̄_{A₁,ℓ}, ε̄_ℓ) on Γ_F is {(g₀, g₁, ξ): det g₀ = det g₁ = ξ^{−1}}; g₀ = aI, g₁ = ±aI give the scalar a^{−1}. Checked. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proposition 2.7.2(2) — residual absolute irreducibility
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 2.7.2, for sufficiently large ℓ, all of ρ̄₀, ρ̄₁ and ρ̄₀ ⊗ ρ̄₁ are absolutely irreducible.
items.note: From the same image computation (Sym^{k} of SL₂(𝔽_ℓ) irreducible for k < ℓ; outer tensor product for SL₂ × SL₂). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proposition 2.7.2(3) — (GI¹_{F′,𝒫}) for large ℓ (as printed; needs 𝒫 ≠ 0)
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 2.7.2 (A_{0F̄}, A_{1F̄} non-isogenous, End(A_{αF̄}) = ℤ, F′/F⁺ totally real finite Galois in ℂ, 𝒫(T) ∈ ℤ[T]), for sufficiently large ℓ, (GI¹_{F′,𝒫}) from Lemma 2.7.1 holds (with the coefficient field E_λ = ℚ_ℓ).
items.note: False for 𝒫 = 0 (E4). The printed proof's list of conditions on (a, b) is miscomputed and the choice of g only up to conjugacy does not control h_γ (new issue); the statement is true for 𝒫 ≠ 0 with the corrected choice. Used for Theorem 1.1.1 via Lemma 8.1.3 with 𝒫 = T² − 1. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: [68, Théorème 6] — joint open image for two non-isogenous non-CM elliptic curves (as used)
items.statement: If A₀, A₁ are elliptic curves over a number field F with End(A_{αF̄}) = ℤ and A_{0F̄}, A_{1F̄} not isogenous, then for all sufficiently large ℓ the image of (ρ̄_{A₀,ℓ}, ρ̄_{A₁,ℓ}, ε̄_ℓ): Γ_F → GL₂(𝔽_ℓ) × GL₂(𝔽_ℓ) × 𝔽_ℓ^× is {(g₀, g₁, ξ): det g₀ = det g₁ = ξ^{−1}}.
items.locator: Invoked in the proofs of Proposition 2.7.2 (p. 137) and Lemma 8.1.3; also Cited in the proof of Lemma 8.1.3 (published p. 304) and Proposition 2.7.2
items.note: Cited from Serre, Invent. Math. 15 (1972). Uses that ℓ unramified in F (so ε̄_ℓ(Γ_F) = 𝔽_ℓ^×) and H¹ has determinant ε_ℓ^{−1}. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Definition 3.1.1 — coefficient field Q(Π)
items.statement: Let Π be an irreducible cuspidal automorphic (complex) representation of GL_N(𝔸_F). The coefficient field of Π, denoted Q(Π), is the smallest subfield of ℂ such that for every ρ ∈ Aut(ℂ/Q(Π)), Π^∞ and Π^∞ ⊗_{ℂ,ρ} ℂ are isomorphic.
items.note: Taken from Clozel [17, §3.1]. Throughout §3.1, Π denotes an irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_N(𝔸_F), with F the fixed CM field (F^+ its maximal totally real subfield). Missing: routed to a source of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII (route 5).

items.name: Satake parameter α(Π_w) and its field Q(Π_w)
items.statement: For a nonarchimedean place w of F such that Π_w is unramified, α(Π_w) := {α(Π_w)_1, …, α(Π_w)_N} ⊆ ℂ denotes the Satake parameter of Π_w, and Q(Π_w) ⊆ ℂ denotes the subfield generated by the coefficients of the polynomial ∏_{i=1}^{N} (T − α(Π_w)_i · √‖w‖^{N−1}) ∈ ℂ[T].
items.note: α(Π_w) is the unitarily normalised Satake parameter (for tempered Π_w all |α(Π_w)_i| = 1); the factor √‖w‖^{N−1} is the arithmetic normalisation, so that the coefficients are (up to powers of ‖w‖) the Hecke eigenvalues of Π_w and Q(Π_w) is the field of rationality of Π_w. ‖w‖ is the cardinality of the residue field of F_w. Missing: routed to a source of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII (route 5).

items.name: Lemma 3.1.2 — Q(Π) is a number field generated by the Q(Π_w)
items.statement: Suppose that Π is regular algebraic in the sense of [17, Définition 3.12]. Then the coefficient field Q(Π) is a number field, and is the composition of Q(Π_w) for all nonarchimedean places w of F such that Π_w is unramified.
items.note: Proof: Q(Π) is a number field by [17, Théorème 3.13]. Let Q(Π)′ be the composite of the Q(Π_w). For γ ∈ Aut(ℂ/Q(Π)′), Π_w and Π_w ⊗_{ℂ,γ} ℂ have the same Satake parameter for all unramified w; by [17, Théorème 3.13] there is a cuspidal ^γΠ with ^γΠ^∞ ≃ Π^∞ ⊗_{ℂ,γ} ℂ, and strong multiplicity one [60] gives ^γΠ ≃ Π, so Q(Π) ⊆ Q(Π)′. Conversely γ ∈ Aut(ℂ/Q(Π)) fixes each Q(Π_w) (the field of definition of the unramified Π_w), so Q(Π)′ ⊆ Q(Π). The last sentence of the proof misprints Q(Π)′ as Q(Π′) (see source issues). Clozel's theorem and strong multiplicity one are cited black boxes. Missing: routed to a source of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII (route 5).

items.name: Definition 3.1.3(1) — abstract Satake parameter at an inert place; unitarity
items.statement: Let L be a ring. For a multi-subset α := {α_1, …, α_N} ⊆ L put P_α(T) := ∏_{i=1}^{N} (T − α_i) ∈ L[T]. Let v be a nonarchimedean place of F^+ not in Σ^+_bad that is inert in F. An (abstract) Satake parameter in L at v of rank N is a multi-subset α ⊆ L of cardinality N. It is unitary if P_α(T) = (−T)^N · P_α(T^{−1}).
items.note: Σ^+_bad is the set of places of F^+ above rational primes ramified in F (§1.3). Unitarity is a polynomial identity in L[T, T^{−1}], not a statement about the multiset; over a field (or domain) it is equivalent to: the multiset α is stable under α ↦ α^{−1} and ∏α_i = 1. Over a general ring the two are not equivalent (source issue E5). Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

api.name: RankinSelberg.AbstractUnitarySatakeParameter.data
api.statement: Work with coefficient polynomials; do not assume global root pairing over arbitrary rings.

api.name: RankinSelberg.AbstractUnitarySatakeParameter.characterisation
api.statement: The product of the inert roots is one.

api.name: RankinSelberg.AbstractUnitarySatakeParameter.compatibility
api.statement: Tensor products of unitary parameters satisfy the corresponding reciprocal identity.

uses.how: Work with coefficient polynomials; do not assume global root pairing over arbitrary rings.

items.name: Definition 3.1.3(2) — abstract Satake parameter at a split place; unitarity
items.statement: Let L be a ring and v a nonarchimedean place of F^+ not in Σ^+_bad that splits in F into w_1, w_2. An (abstract) Satake parameter in L at v of rank N is a pair α := (α_1; α_2) of multi-subsets α_1, α_2 ⊆ L of cardinality N, indexed by the two places w_1, w_2 of F above v. It is unitary if P_{α_1}(T) = c · T^N · P_{α_2}(T^{−1}) for some constant c ∈ L^×.
items.note: Over a field, unitarity means α_1 = α_2^{−1} as multisets (then c = ∏_j(−α_{2,j})^{−1}). Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Tensor product of abstract Satake parameters
items.statement: For two Satake parameters α_0 and α_1 in L at v of rank n_0 and n_1 respectively, their tensor product α_0 ⊗ α_1 is the Satake parameter in L at v of rank n_0 n_1 formed 'in the obvious way': at an inert v, the multiset {a·b : a ∈ α_0, b ∈ α_1} (with multiplicities); at a split v, the pair (α_{0,1} ⊗ α_{1,1}; α_{0,2} ⊗ α_{1,2}) formed componentwise.
items.note: The paper only says 'in the obvious way'; the componentwise description is the evident reading. Used for the Rankin–Selberg parameter α(Π_{0,p}) ⊗ α(Π_{1,p}) in §§7–8 ((PI7)). Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Tensor product of unitary Satake parameters is unitary
items.statement: If α_0 and α_1 are both unitary Satake parameters in L at v (of ranks n_0, n_1), then α_0 ⊗ α_1 is unitary.
items.note: Stated without proof. It holds over every ring L: the coefficients of P_{α_0⊗α_1} are universal polynomials in the coefficients of P_{α_0}, P_{α_1}; unitarity is a set of linear relations among coefficients, so the universal coefficient ring is a polynomial ring over ℤ in which the identity can be checked on ℂ-points, where it is clear. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Notation 3.1.4 — Σ^+_Π and the Satake parameter α(Π_v)
items.statement: Σ^+_Π denotes the smallest (finite) set of nonarchimedean places of F^+ containing Σ^+_bad such that Π_w is unramified for every nonarchimedean place w of F not above Σ^+_Π. For a nonarchimedean place v of F^+ not in Σ^+_Π: (1) if v is inert in F, α(Π_v) := α(Π_w) for the unique place w of F above v; (2) if v splits in F into w_1 and w_2, α(Π_v) := (α(Π_{w_1}); α(Π_{w_2})). Thus α(Π_v) is a Satake parameter in ℂ at v of rank N.
items.note: Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Definition 3.1.5(1) — Tate generic
items.statement: Setting: v a nonarchimedean place of F^+ inert in F, L a ring in which ‖v‖ is invertible, and P ∈ L[T] a monic polynomial of degree N satisfying P(T) = (−T)^N · P(T^{−1}). When N is odd, P is Tate generic at v if P′(1) is invertible in L.
items.note: ‖v‖ is the norm (residue cardinality) of v in F^+. Applied to P = P_{α(Π_v)} mod λ (L = O_E/λ) in (P4), (PI4). Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

api.name: RankinSelberg.TateGenericParameter.data
api.statement: Extract the simple eigenvalue-one summand.

api.name: RankinSelberg.TateGenericParameter.characterisation
api.statement: Over a field this says the root 1 has multiplicity one.

api.name: RankinSelberg.TateGenericParameter.compatibility
api.statement: The simple-root idempotent is compatible with reduction if P′(1) stays a unit.

uses.how: Extract the simple eigenvalue-one summand.

items.name: Definition 3.1.5(2) — intertwining generic, N odd
items.statement: Setting: v a nonarchimedean place of F^+ inert in F, L a ring in which ‖v‖ is invertible, and P ∈ L[T] a monic polynomial of degree N satisfying P(T) = (−T)^N · P(T^{−1}). When N is odd, P is intertwining generic at v if P(−‖v‖) is invertible in L.
items.note: Used in (P5), (PI5). Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

api.name: RankinSelberg.IntertwiningGenericParameter.data
api.statement: Invert the appropriate Satake value of the composite intertwiner.

api.name: RankinSelberg.IntertwiningGenericParameter.characterisation
api.statement: In odd rank the pair {−q,−q^−1} is excluded over a field.

api.name: RankinSelberg.IntertwiningGenericParameter.compatibility
api.statement: In even rank a −1 root is excluded; genericity is preserved by local coefficient maps carrying units to units.

uses.how: Invert the appropriate Satake value of the composite intertwiner.

items.name: Definition 3.1.5(3) — level-raising special, N even
items.statement: Setting: v a nonarchimedean place of F^+ inert in F, L a ring in which ‖v‖ is invertible, and P ∈ L[T] a monic polynomial of degree N satisfying P(T) = (−T)^N · P(T^{−1}). When N is even, P is level-raising special at v if P(‖v‖) = 0 and P′(‖v‖) is invertible in L.
items.note: Applied with L = O_E/λ^m in (P4), (PI4), (PI7). In those applications (P2)/(PI2) (ℓ ∤ p(p²−1)) make ‖v‖² − 1 a unit, so ‖v‖ and ‖v‖^{−1} are distinct roots; this is not part of the definition. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

api.name: RankinSelberg.LevelRaisingSpecialParameter.data
api.statement: Separate equality modulo λ^m from residual simplicity.

api.name: RankinSelberg.LevelRaisingSpecialParameter.characterisation
api.statement: For q²−1 invertible, division by (T−q)(T−q^−1) leaves a polynomial invertible at q.

api.name: RankinSelberg.LevelRaisingSpecialParameter.compatibility
api.statement: The higher congruence P(q)=0 mod λ^m is not implied by the residual condition.

uses.how: Separate equality modulo λ^m from residual simplicity.

items.name: Definition 3.1.5(4) — intertwining generic, N even
items.statement: Setting: v a nonarchimedean place of F^+ inert in F, L a ring in which ‖v‖ is invertible, and P ∈ L[T] a monic polynomial of degree N satisfying P(T) = (−T)^N · P(T^{−1}). When N is even, P is intertwining generic at v if P(−1) is invertible in L.
items.note: Used in (P5), (PI5). Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Remark 3.1.6 — Definition 3.1.5 in terms of the Satake parameter (L a field)
items.statement: Suppose that L is a field in Definition 3.1.5 and P = P_α for a unitary Satake parameter α in L at v. Then: (1) P is Tate generic at v iff 1 appears exactly once in α; (2) (N odd) P is intertwining generic at v iff the pair {−‖v‖, −‖v‖^{−1}} does not appear in α; (3) P is level-raising special at v iff the pair {‖v‖, ‖v‖^{−1}} appears exactly once in α; (4) (N even) P is intertwining generic at v iff the pair {−1, −1} does not appear in α. Moreover, when N is odd, 1 appears in α and all other elements appear in pairs of the form {α, α^{−1}}; when N is even, the elements of α appear in pairs of the form {α, α^{−1}}.
items.note: Stated as 'easy to see'. (1) and (4) and the 'moreover' sentence are correct for every field; (2) fails if ‖v‖ = −1 in L and (3) fails if ‖v‖² = 1 in L (source issue). In all uses ‖v‖² ≠ 1 in L ((P2)/(PI2), or L = ℂ in Proposition C.2.5). Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Definition 3.1.7 — hermitian space over O_F ⊗ R and its unitary group
items.statement: Let R be an O_{F^+}[(Σ^+_bad)^{−1}]-ring. A hermitian space over O_F ⊗_{O_{F^+}} R of rank N is a projective O_F ⊗_{O_{F^+}} R-module V of rank N together with a perfect pairing ( , )_V: V × V → O_F ⊗_{O_{F^+}} R that is O_F ⊗_{O_{F^+}} R-linear in the first variable and (O_F ⊗_{O_{F^+}} R, c ⊗ id_R)-linear in the second variable, and satisfies (x, y)_V = (y, x)_V^c for x, y ∈ V. U(V) denotes the group of O_F ⊗_{O_{F^+}} R-linear isometries of V, which is a reductive group over R.
items.note: c is complex conjugation (the nontrivial automorphism of F/F^+). 'A hermitian space over F' means the case R = F^+. Reductivity over R uses that R is étale-locally split away from Σ^+_bad (F/F^+ unramified there). Planned: PELModuli M0 plans PEL linear algebra and reflex fields.

api.name: RankinSelberg.HermitianSpaceAndAdjoiningAUnitLine.data
api.statement: Use the inclusion V→V♯ and induced isometries.

api.name: RankinSelberg.HermitianSpaceAndAdjoiningAUnitLine.characterisation
api.statement: Pairing on the orthogonal direct sum has no cross terms.

api.name: RankinSelberg.HermitianSpaceAndAdjoiningAUnitLine.compatibility
api.statement: An isometry f extends to f⊕id on V♯.

uses.how: Use the inclusion V→V♯ and induced isometries.

items.name: The hermitian space V_♯ and the isometry f_♯
items.statement: For a hermitian space V over O_F ⊗_{O_{F^+}} R, V_♯ denotes the hermitian space V ⊕ O_F ⊗_{O_{F^+}} R · 1, where 1 has norm 1 (orthogonal direct sum). For an O_F ⊗_{O_{F^+}} R-linear isometry f: V → V′, f_♯: V_♯ → V′_♯ denotes the induced isometry (f on V, identity on the line spanned by 1).
items.note: V ↦ V_♯ is the rank-raising step (n → n+1) of the Gan–Gross–Prasad pair; U(V) ⊆ U(V_♯) via f ↦ f_♯. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: The local hermitian lattice Λ_{N,v} and the unitary group U_{N,v}
items.statement: Let v be a nonarchimedean place of F^+ not in Σ^+_bad. Λ_{N,v} denotes the unique up to isomorphism hermitian space over O_{F_v} = O_F ⊗_{O_{F^+}} O_{F^+_v} of rank N, and U_{N,v} its unitary group over O_{F^+_v}. Under a suitable basis, the hermitian form of Λ_{N,v} is given by the antidiagonal N×N matrix (1 in positions (i, N+1−i), 0 elsewhere).
items.note: Uniqueness is asserted (standard: self-dual hermitian O_{F_v}-lattices are unique up to isometry for v unramified in F or split). U_{N,v} is the reductive model over O_{F^+_v} used for the spherical Hecke algebra. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Local spherical Hecke algebra 𝕋_{N,v}; torus A_{N,v}
items.statement: For v ∉ Σ^+_bad, the local spherical Hecke algebra is 𝕋_{N,v} := ℤ[U_{N,v}(O_{F^+_v}) \ U_{N,v}(F^+_v) / U_{N,v}(O_{F^+_v})], whose unit element is the characteristic function 𝟙_{U_{N,v}(O_{F^+_v})}. A_{N,v} denotes the maximal split diagonal subtorus of U_{N,v} and X_*(A_{N,v}) its cocharacter group.
items.note: Convention (§1.3): Hecke algebras have ℤ-coefficients with unit the characteristic function of the level group. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Satake transform (3.1)
items.statement: There is a (well-known) Satake transform 𝕋_{N,v} → ℤ[‖v‖^{±δ(v)/2}][A_{N,v}(F^+_v)/A_{N,v}(O_{F^+_v})] ≃ ℤ[‖v‖^{±δ(v)/2}][X_*(A_{N,v})], which is a homomorphism of algebras; here δ(v) = 1 if v splits in F and δ(v) = 2 otherwise.
items.note: Cited as well known, not proved. It is the normalised (by δ_B^{1/2}) Satake transform; its image is the Weyl-group invariants, which is what makes φ_α in Construction 3.1.8 independent of the ordering. δ(v) is defined in §1.3 (p. 120); for inert v the coefficient ring is ℤ[‖v‖^{±1}], for split v it is ℤ[‖v‖^{±1/2}]. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Construction 3.1.8(1) — Hecke character φ_α at an inert place
items.statement: Let L be a ℤ[‖v‖^{±δ(v)/2}]-ring and α a unitary Satake parameter in L at v of rank N, with v inert in F; choose a uniformizer ϖ_v of F^+_v. A set of representatives of A_{N,v}(F^+_v)/A_{N,v}(O_{F^+_v}) is {diag(ϖ_v^{t_1}, …, ϖ_v^{t_N}) | t_1, …, t_N ∈ ℤ, t_i + t_{N+1−i} = 0 for all 1 ≤ i ≤ N}. Choose an ordering of α as (α_1, …, α_N) satisfying α_i α_{N+1−i} = 1; there is a unique homomorphism of ℤ[‖v‖^{±δ(v)/2}]-rings ℤ[‖v‖^{±δ(v)/2}][A_{N,v}(F^+_v)/A_{N,v}(O_{F^+_v})] → L sending the class of diag(ϖ_v^{t_1}, …, ϖ_v^{t_N}) to ∏_{i=1}^{⌊N/2⌋} α_i^{t_i}. Composing with the Satake transform (3.1) gives a ring homomorphism φ_α: 𝕋_{N,v} → L, which is independent of the choices of ϖ_v and of the ordering of α.
items.note: Over a general ring L an ordering with α_iα_{N+1−i} = 1 need not exist although α is unitary (source issue E5, counterexample in L = 𝔽_5 × 𝔽_5); it exists when L is an integral domain, and every use in the paper is over ℂ (Construction 3.1.10) or with an ordered tuple given (Notation B.2.5). When the ordering exists, independence holds because valid orderings give Weyl-conjugate characters and (3.1) lands in Weyl invariants. Planned: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 plans spherical representations and the Satake isomorphism.

api.name: RankinSelberg.SphericalHeckeEvaluation.characterisation
api.statement: Changing the uniformizer and Weyl-compatible ordering gives the same spherical character.

api.name: RankinSelberg.SphericalHeckeEvaluation.compatibility

items.name: Construction 3.1.8(2) — Hecke character φ_α at a split place
items.statement: Let L be a ℤ[‖v‖^{±δ(v)/2}]-ring and α = (α_1; α_2) a unitary Satake parameter in L at v of rank N, with v split in F into w_1 and w_2. A set of representatives of A_{N,v}(F^+_v)/A_{N,v}(O_{F^+_v}) is {(diag(ϖ_v^{t_1}, …, ϖ_v^{t_N}), diag(ϖ_v^{−t_N}, …, ϖ_v^{−t_1})) | t_1, …, t_N ∈ ℤ}, the first (resp. second) diagonal matrix regarded as an element of A_{N,v}(F_{w_1}) (resp. A_{N,v}(F_{w_2})). Choose orders (α_{1,1}, …, α_{1,N}) and (α_{2,1}, …, α_{2,N}) of α_1, α_2 satisfying α_{1,i} α_{2,N+1−i} = 1; there is a unique homomorphism of ℤ[‖v‖^{±δ(v)/2}]-rings ℤ[‖v‖^{±δ(v)/2}][A_{N,v}(F^+_v)/A_{N,v}(O_{F^+_v})] → L sending the class of (diag(ϖ_v^{t_1}, …, ϖ_v^{t_N}), diag(ϖ_v^{−t_N}, …, ϖ_v^{−t_1})) to ∏_{i=1}^{N} α_{1,i}^{t_i}. Composing with (3.1) gives a ring homomorphism φ_α: 𝕋_{N,v} → L, independent of ϖ_v, of the order of the two places of F above v, and of the orders in α_1 and α_2.
items.note: Same caveat as (1): over a non-domain L the required orders need not exist (see E5, split-case example). Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Definition 3.1.9 — abstract unitary Hecke algebra 𝕋_N^{Σ^+}
items.statement: For a finite set Σ^+ of nonarchimedean places of F^+ containing Σ^+_bad, the abstract unitary Hecke algebra away from Σ^+ is the restricted tensor product 𝕋_N^{Σ^+} := ⊗′_v 𝕋_{N,v} over all v ∉ Σ^+_∞ ∪ Σ^+, with respect to the unit elements. It is a ring.
items.note: Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Construction 3.1.10 — the Hecke character φ_Π: 𝕋_N^{Σ^+_Π} → ℂ
items.statement: Suppose that Π satisfies Π ∘ c ≃ Π^∨. For v ∉ Σ^+_Π, the Satake parameter α(Π_v) is (claimed to be) unitary; by Construction 3.1.8 one obtains the homomorphism φ_Π := ⊗_{v ∉ Σ^+_∞ ∪ Σ^+_Π} φ_{α(Π_v)}: 𝕋_N^{Σ^+_Π} → ℂ, where ℂ is regarded as a ℤ[‖v‖^{±δ(v)/2}]-ring by sending ‖v‖^{±δ(v)/2} to √‖v‖^{±δ(v)}.
items.note: The unitarity claim is false for general conjugate self-dual Π (e.g. N = 1, a Hecke character χ with χ|_{𝔸_{F^+}^×} = η_{F/F^+}: α(χ_v) = {−1} at inert v); it holds when the central character of Π is trivial on 𝔸_{F^+}^×, in particular for relevant Π (Definition 1.1.3(3) forces the archimedean central character to be trivial). Only relevant Π are used. See source issues. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: φ_Π is Q(Π)-valued, and O_{Q(Π)}-valued for relevant Π
items.statement: In Construction 3.1.10: if Π is regular algebraic, then φ_Π takes values in Q(Π) (by Lemma 3.1.2). Furthermore, when Π is relevant (Definition 1.1.3), φ_Π takes values in O_{Q(Π)}; in particular one obtains a homomorphism φ_Π: 𝕋_N^{Σ^+_Π} → O_{Q(Π)}.
items.note: Rationality: the values of φ_{α(Π_v)} are ℤ[‖v‖^{±1}]- (inert) or ℤ[‖v‖^{±1/2}]-combinations of symmetric functions of α(Π_v) whose normalisation matches Q(Π_w). Integrality is cited from Shin–Templier [73, Proposition 4.1 & Remark 4.2] (black box). φ_Π is the Hecke eigensystem used to define the maximal ideals 𝔪 in §§6–8. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Definition 3.1.11(1) — neat elements and neat subgroups
items.statement: Let V be a hermitian space over F of rank N and □ a finite set of nonarchimedean places of F^+. For a nonarchimedean place v of F^+ and g_v ∈ U(V)(F^+_v), let Γ(g_v) be the subgroup of (F̄^+_v)^× generated by the eigenvalues of g_v (regarded as an element of GL(V)(F_v)); its torsion subgroup Γ(g_v)_tors lies in ℚ̄^×. An element g = (g_v) ∈ U(V)(𝔸^{∞,□}_{F^+}) is neat if ⋂_{v ∉ □} Γ(g_v)_tors = {1}, and a subgroup K ⊆ U(V)(𝔸^{∞,□}_{F^+}) is neat if all its elements are neat.
items.note: The intersection makes sense because every F̄^+_v is fixed containing F̄ (§1.3), hence ℚ̄. When □ = ∅ the superscript is suppressed. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Definition 3.1.11(2) — the categories 𝔎(V)^□ and 𝔎′(V)^□
items.statement: 𝔎(V)^□ is the category whose objects are neat open compact subgroups K of U(V)(𝔸^{∞,□}_{F^+}), a morphism from K to K′ being an element g ∈ K\U(V)(𝔸^{∞,□}_{F^+})/K′ satisfying g^{−1}Kg ⊆ K′. 𝔎′(V)^□ denotes the subcategory of 𝔎(V)^□ that allows only identity double cosets as morphisms.
items.note: The condition g^{−1}Kg ⊆ K′ depends only on the double coset, and then KgK′ = gK′, so composition (KgK′)(K′g′K″) = Kgg′K″ is well defined. 𝔎′(V) has a morphism K → K′ iff K ⊆ K′. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 3.1.11(3) — the category 𝔎(V)^□_sp of pairs (K_♭, K_♯)
items.statement: 𝔎(V)^□_sp is the category whose objects are pairs K = (K_♭, K_♯) with K_♭ an object of 𝔎(V)^□ and K_♯ an object of 𝔎(V_♯)^□ such that K_♭ ⊆ K_♯ ∩ U(V)(𝔸^{∞,□}_{F^+}); a morphism from K = (K_♭, K_♯) to K′ = (K′_♭, K′_♯) is an element g ∈ K_♭\U(V)(𝔸^{∞,□}_{F^+})/K′_♭ such that g^{−1}K_♭g ⊆ K′_♭ and g^{−1}K_♯g ⊆ K′_♯. There are the obvious functors −_♭: 𝔎(V)^□_sp → 𝔎(V)^□ and −_♯: 𝔎(V)^□_sp → 𝔎(V_♯)^□ sending K to K_♭ and K_♯; 𝔎(V)^□_sp is a non-full subcategory of 𝔎(V)^□ × 𝔎(V_♯)^□.
items.note: U(V) ⊆ U(V_♯) via f ↦ f_♯. 'sp' refers to the special homomorphism (diagonal cycle) of Shimura varieties used in §§4.5, 5.10, 7. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 3.2.1(1) — standard definite hermitian space
items.statement: A hermitian space V over F of rank N is standard definite if it has signature (N, 0) at every place in Σ^+_∞.
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 3.2.1(2) — standard indefinite hermitian space
items.statement: A hermitian space V over F of rank N is standard indefinite if it has signature (N − 1, 1) at the default real place τ̲_∞ of F^+ and (N, 0) at the other places in Σ^+_∞.
items.note: τ̲_∞ is the restriction to F^+ of the default embedding τ_∞ of F (§1.3). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Unitary Shimura varieties Sh(V, K) for standard indefinite V
items.statement: For a standard indefinite hermitian space V over F of rank N there is a functor Sh(V, −): 𝔎(V) → Sch_{/F}, K ↦ Sh(V, K), of Shimura varieties associated to the reductive group Res_{F^+/ℚ} U(V) and the Deligne homomorphism h: Res_{ℂ/ℝ} 𝐆_m → (Res_{F^+/ℚ} U(V)) ⊗_ℚ ℝ = ∏_{τ̲ ∈ Σ^+_∞} U(V_τ̲), z ↦ ((1_{N−1}, z^c/z) [block-diagonal], 1_N, …, 1_N) ∈ U(V)(F^+_{τ̲_∞}) × ∏_{τ̲ ∈ Σ^+_∞, τ̲ ≠ τ̲_∞} U(V)(F^+_τ̲), where U(V)(F^+_{τ̲_∞}) is identified with a subgroup of GL_N(ℂ) via a complex basis of V ⊗_{F,τ_∞} ℂ under which the hermitian form is diag(1_{N−1}, −1).
items.note: Canonical models over F (reflex field contained in F via τ_∞). Footnote 10 (p. 146): this h is conjugate to the one in [48, §C.1], which is why ρ^c appears in Hypothesis 3.2.10. Existence of canonical models is standard Shimura-variety theory (Deligne), used as a black box. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Unitary Shimura sets Sh(V, K) for standard definite V
items.statement: For a standard definite hermitian space V over F of rank N there is a functor Sh(V, −): 𝔎(V) → Set, K ↦ Sh(V, K) := U(V)(F^+) \ U(V)(𝔸^∞_{F^+}) / K. (Remark 3.2.2: whether Sh(V, −) denotes schemes or sets depends on whether V is standard indefinite or standard definite; Sh(V, −) could be given a natural scheme structure in the definite case, but the paper does not take this point of view.)
items.note: Finite sets (U(V) is compact at every archimedean place). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 3.2.3 — automorphic base change BC(π)
items.statement: Let V be a hermitian space over F of rank N and π an irreducible admissible representation of U(V)(𝔸_{F^+}). An automorphic base change of π is an automorphic representation BC(π) of GL_N(𝔸_F) that is a finite isobaric sum of discrete automorphic representations such that BC(π)_v ≃ BC(π_v) for all but finitely many nonarchimedean places v of F^+ such that π_v is unramified.
items.note: BC(π_v) is the local unramified base change (a representation of GL_N(F_v), F_v = F ⊗_{F^+} F^+_v). Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Uniqueness of automorphic base change
items.statement: If BC(π) exists, then it is unique up to isomorphism.
items.note: By the strong multiplicity one property for GL_N, cited from [60] (Piatetski-Shapiro). For isobaric sums of discrete (non-cuspidal) representations this is the Jacquet–Shalika classification together with Mœglin–Waldspurger; the paper cites only [60]. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Proposition 3.2.4(1) — local temperedness of relevant Π
items.statement: Let Π be a relevant representation of GL_N(𝔸_F) (Definition 1.1.3). For every nonarchimedean place w of F, Π_w is tempered.
items.note: Cited from Caraiani [10, Theorem 1.2] (black box). Only nonarchimedean places are asserted. Planned: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.2 plans polarized cuspidal automorphic systems.

items.name: Proposition 3.2.4(2) — Galois representation ρ_{Π,ι_ℓ} of a relevant Π
items.statement: Let Π be relevant. For every rational prime ℓ and every isomorphism ι_ℓ: ℂ ⥲ ℚ̄_ℓ, there is a semisimple continuous homomorphism ρ_{Π,ι_ℓ}: Γ_F → GL_N(ℚ̄_ℓ), unique up to conjugation, such that for every nonarchimedean place w of F the Frobenius semisimplification of the Weil–Deligne representation associated to ρ_{Π,ι_ℓ}|_{Γ_{F_w}} corresponds to the irreducible admissible representation ι_ℓ Π_w |det|_w^{(1−N)/2} of GL_N(F_w) under the local Langlands correspondence. Moreover, ρ^c_{Π,ι_ℓ} and ρ^∨_{Π,ι_ℓ}(1 − N) are conjugate.
items.note: Construction cited from Chenevier–Harris [16, Theorem 3.2.3]; local–global compatibility at w ∤ ℓ from Caraiani [10, Theorem 1.1] and at w | ℓ from Caraiani [11, Theorem 1.1] (black boxes). The polarisation follows from local–global compatibility, Π∘c ≃ Π^∨, Chebotarev and semisimplicity. ρ^c(g) := ρ(cgc). Planned: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.5 plans local–global compatibility, including the Taylor–Yoshida and Caraiani purity upgrades; AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.6 plans coefficient-prime comparison and compatible systems.

items.name: Definition 3.2.5 — strong coefficient field
items.statement: Let Π be a relevant representation of GL_N(𝔸_F). A subfield E ⊆ ℂ is a strong coefficient field of Π if E is a number field containing Q(Π) (Definition 3.1.1), and for every prime λ of E there exists a continuous homomorphism ρ_{Π,λ}: Γ_F → GL_N(E_λ), necessarily unique up to conjugation, such that for every isomorphism ι_ℓ: ℂ ⥲ ℚ̄_ℓ inducing the prime λ, ρ_{Π,λ} ⊗_{E_λ} ℚ̄_ℓ and ρ_{Π,ι_ℓ} are conjugate, where ρ_{Π,ι_ℓ} is the homomorphism of Proposition 3.2.4(2).
items.note: Uniqueness over E_λ follows from Noether–Deuring. The main theorems take a strong coefficient field E as given. Planned: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.6 plans coefficient-prime comparison and compatible systems.

items.name: Remark 3.2.6 — existence of a strong coefficient field
items.statement: For Π relevant, a strong coefficient field of Π exists.
items.note: Cited from Chenevier–Harris [16, Proposition 3.2.5] (black box). Missing: routed to a source of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII (route 5).

items.name: Remark 3.2.6 — Q(Π) is a strong coefficient field (claimed, under Hypothesis 3.2.10)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 3.2.10, Q(Π) is already a strong coefficient field of Π if Π ≃ BC(π) for a standard pair (V, π) (Definition 3.2.7) in which V is standard indefinite.
items.note: Asserted without proof and never used later. Hypothesis 3.2.10 only applies when ρ_{BC(π),ι_ℓ} is irreducible, and descending ρ to Q(Π)_λ from the cohomology needs an argument (Brauer obstruction). See source issues. Missing: routed to a source of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII (route 5).

items.name: Definition 3.2.7 — standard pair (V, π)
items.statement: Consider a pair (V, π) where V is a hermitian space over F and π is a discrete automorphic representation of U(V)(𝔸_{F^+}). (V, π) is a standard pair if either (1) V is standard definite and π^∞ appears in lim_{→, K ∈ 𝔎′(V)} ℂ[Sh(V, K)]; or (2) V is standard indefinite and π^∞ appears in lim_{→, K ∈ 𝔎′(V)} ι_ℓ^{−1} H^i_ét(Sh(V, K)_{F̄}, ℚ̄_ℓ) for some isomorphism ι_ℓ: ℂ ⥲ ℚ̄_ℓ and some i ∈ ℤ.
items.note: Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Proposition 3.2.8 — base change exists for standard pairs
items.statement: Let (V, π) be a standard pair. Then BC(π) exists.
items.note: Cited from Shin [72, Theorem 1.1]; for V standard definite also Labesse [42, Corollaire 5.3] (preprint). Footnote 9: [72] treats unitary similitude groups and assumes F contains an imaginary quadratic field; the paper says the result in its setup follows 'by modifying the argument as in the proof of Proposition D.1.3' (not written out). Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Remark 3.2.9 — Galois representation for a standard pair
items.statement: For a standard pair (V, π), there is an associated Galois representation ρ_{BC(π),ι_ℓ} similar to the one in Proposition 3.2.4 (with N = dim_F V).
items.note: 'In view of [72, Theorem 1.1]'; BC(π) need not be cuspidal, so ρ_{BC(π),ι_ℓ} is the sum of the representations attached to its isobaric constituents. Black box. Missing: routed to a source of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII (route 5).

items.name: Hypothesis 3.2.10 — middle-degree cohomological realisation of ρ^c
items.statement: Consider an integer N ≥ 1. For every standard indefinite hermitian space V over F of rank N, every discrete automorphic representation π of U(V)(𝔸_{F^+}) such that BC(π) exists and is a relevant representation of GL_N(𝔸_F), and every isomorphism ι_ℓ: ℂ ⥲ ℚ̄_ℓ, if ρ_{BC(π),ι_ℓ} is irreducible, then W^{N−1}(π) := Hom_{ℚ̄_ℓ[U(V)(𝔸^∞_{F^+})]}(ι_ℓ π^∞, lim_{→, 𝔎′(V)} H^{N−1}_ét(Sh(V, K)_{F̄}, ℚ̄_ℓ)) is isomorphic to the underlying ℚ̄_ℓ[Γ_F]-module of ρ^c_{BC(π),ι_ℓ}.
items.note: An explicit hypothesis ('Hypothesis 3.2.10 for N') of Theorems 6.3.4, 8.2.2, 8.3.2 etc.; Proposition 3.2.11 says when it is known. The c-conjugate comes from the choice of Deligne homomorphism (footnote 10). Missing: routed to a source of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII (route 5).

items.name: Proposition 3.2.11 — cases where Hypothesis 3.2.10 holds
items.statement: Hypothesis 3.2.10 holds for N ≤ 3, and for N > 3 if F^+ ≠ ℚ.
items.note: Proof by citation: N = 1 from the definition of canonical models; N = 2 from [48, Theorem D.6(2)] (Liu, appendix by C. Li and Y. Zhu); N = 3, F^+ = ℚ from Rogawski [64]; N ≥ 3, F^+ ≠ ℚ 'will be proved in [37]', which the bibliography lists as Kisin–Shin–Zhu, 'Cohomology of certain Shimura varieties of abelian type (temporary title) (in preparation)'. So the case N ≥ 3, F^+ ≠ ℚ rests on unpublished work (source issue). It is invoked in the proof of Corollary 8.2.3 and underlies the unconditional form of the main theorems with F^+ ≠ ℚ (Remark 1.1.10). Missing: routed to a source of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII (route 5).

items.name: Definition 3.3.1 — generalized CM type, reflex field, CM type
items.statement: Let ℕ[Σ_∞] be the commutative monoid freely generated by the set Σ_∞ of complex embeddings of F, with its action of Aut(ℂ/ℚ) through Σ_∞. A generalized CM type of rank N is an element Ψ = Σ_{τ ∈ Σ_∞} r_τ τ ∈ ℕ[Σ_∞] satisfying r_τ + r_{τ^c} = N for every τ ∈ Σ_∞. Its reflex field F_Ψ ⊆ ℂ is the fixed subfield of the stabilizer of Ψ in Aut(ℂ/ℚ). A CM type is a generalized CM type of rank 1; a CM type Φ contains τ if its coefficient r_τ equals 1.
items.note: τ^c = c∘τ. Main example: Ψ = NΦ − τ_∞ + τ_∞^c (Lemma 4.2.1), the signature type of the moduli problem in §4. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Definition 3.3.2 — reflexive closure F_rflx
items.statement: The reflexive closure of F, denoted F_rflx, is the subfield of ℂ generated by F and the intersection of F_Φ for all CM types Φ of F. Put F^+_rflx := (F_rflx)^{c=1}.
items.note: The published definition uses the intersection ⋂_Φ F_Φ; arXiv v1–v3 instead used the composite of F and all F_Φ (which is the Galois closure of F). Galois-theoretically, with M the Galois closure of F and H ⊆ Gal(M/ℚ) the (normal) subgroup generated by the stabilizers of all CM types, F_rflx = M^{Gal(M/F) ∩ H}. Used only through 'very special inert' (Definition 3.3.4), (L5-2) of Definition 8.1.1 and Lemma 8.1.4; see source issues on footnote 11 and on the consequences of the change for §8. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Remark 3.3.3 — properties of F_rflx
items.statement: F_rflx is a CM field finite Galois over F; F^+_rflx is the maximal totally real subfield of F_rflx and is finite Galois over F^+. In many cases F_rflx = F and hence F^+_rflx = F^+, for example when F is Galois or contains an imaginary quadratic field.
items.note: 'It is clear'. Correct for the published definition: ⋂_Φ F_Φ is Galois over ℚ (the set of CM types is Aut(ℂ/ℚ)-stable) and is CM or totally real; if F is Galois every F_Φ ⊆ F; if F ⊇ K imaginary quadratic, the CM type induced from K has reflex field K ⊆ F. (With the v1–v3 definition the imaginary-quadratic case was false.) Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Definition 3.3.4 — special inert prime
items.statement: A prime 𝔭 of F^+ is special inert if (1) 𝔭 is inert in F; (2) the underlying rational prime p of 𝔭 is odd and is unramified in F; (3) 𝔭 is of degree one over ℚ, that is, F^+_𝔭 = ℚ_p. By abuse of notation, 𝔭 also denotes the induced prime of F.
items.note: Remark 3.3.5: condition (3) is imposed only to simplify the Dieudonné-module computations of §§4–5; the authors state (without proof) that those results should remain valid without it. Special inert primes are the level-raising primes of §§4–8. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Definition 3.3.4 — very special inert prime (with footnote 11)
items.statement: A special inert prime 𝔭 of F^+ is very special inert if it is special inert and splits completely in F^+_rflx. Footnote 11 asserts: this is equivalent to requiring that for every prime 𝔮 of F^+ above p that is inert in F, [F^+_𝔮 : ℚ_p] is odd.
items.note: The footnote's equivalence is false in both directions (source issue); the footnote's condition is instead equivalent to the existence of a CM type Φ containing τ_∞ with ℚ_p^Φ = ℚ_{p²} (condition (P3)/(PI3) of §§6–7). Very special inert primes appear in hypothesis (a) of Theorem 1.1.7 / Lemma 8.1.4, whose proof uses only that Frobenius at 𝔭 lies in Gal(F̄/F^+_rflx). v1–v3 phrase the definition as 'there exists a prime 𝔭′ of F^+_rflx above 𝔭 with (F^+_rflx)_{𝔭′} = F^+_𝔭 (= ℚ_p)', equivalent since F^+_rflx/F^+ is Galois. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Notation 3.3.6(1),(2) — unramified fields ℚ_p^τ and τ-parts ℱ_τ
items.statement: (1) For a finite unramified extension ℚ_p^? of ℚ_p introduced later, ℤ_p^? denotes its ring of integers and 𝔽_p^? := ℤ_p^?/pℤ_p^?. (2) For every τ ∈ Σ_∞, ℚ_p^τ ⊆ ℂ denotes the composite of τ(F) and ℚ_p, which is unramified over ℚ_p. For a scheme S ∈ Sch_{/ℤ_p^τ} and an 𝒪_S-module ℱ with an action O_F → End_{𝒪_S}(ℱ), ℱ_τ denotes the maximal 𝒪_S-submodule of ℱ on which O_F acts via the homomorphism τ: O_F → ℤ_p^τ → 𝒪_S.
items.note: Standing convention: p is a rational prime unramified in F, ι_p: ℂ ⥲ ℚ̄_p is fixed, Σ_∞ is regarded as the set of p-adic embeddings of F via ι_p, and ℚ_p ⊆ ℂ via ι_p^{−1} (p. 147). Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Notation 3.3.6(3) — ℚ_p^◇ and the Frobenius action on Σ_∞
items.statement: ℚ_p^◇ ⊆ ℂ denotes the composite of ℚ_p^τ for all τ ∈ Σ_∞, which is unramified over ℚ_p. Σ_∞ is identified with Hom(O_F, ℤ_p^◇) = Hom(O_F, 𝔽_p^◇); in particular the p-power Frobenius map σ acts on Σ_∞.
items.note: For 𝔭 special inert with ι_p∘τ̲_∞ inducing 𝔭, σ swaps τ_∞ and τ_∞^c. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Notation 3.3.6(4),(5) — ℚ_p^Ψ and fibre notation
items.statement: (4) For a generalized CM type Ψ of rank N, ℚ_p^Ψ ⊆ ℂ denotes the composite of ℚ_p, F and F_Ψ, which is contained in ℚ_p^◇. (5) For a (functor in) scheme over ℤ_p^? written like 𝐗_?(⋯), X_?(⋯) := 𝐗_?(⋯) ⊗_{ℤ_p^?} 𝔽_p^? and 𝐗^η_?(⋯) := 𝐗_?(⋯) ⊗_{ℤ_p^?} ℚ_p^?; for a (functor in) scheme over 𝔽_p^? written like X_?(⋯), X̄_?(⋯) := X_?(⋯) ⊗_{𝔽_p^?} 𝔽̄_p; similar conventions apply to morphisms.
items.note: Here F ⊆ ℂ is the default embedding τ_∞. For a special inert 𝔭 (with ι_p inducing 𝔭), ℚ_p^Φ = ℚ_{p²} iff σ² stabilizes Φ. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Notation 3.4.1 — dual, de Rham homology, Lie algebra, Hodge exact sequence
items.statement: Let A be an abelian scheme over a scheme S. A^∨ denotes the dual abelian scheme; H^dR_1(A/S), Lie_{A/S} and ω_{A/S} denote the relative de Rham homology, the Lie algebra and the dual Lie algebra of A/S, all regarded as locally free 𝒪_S-modules. There is the Hodge exact sequence 0 → ω_{A^∨/S} → H^dR_1(A/S) → Lie_{A/S} → 0 (3.2) of sheaves on S.
items.note: Covariant (homological) conventions throughout: the Hodge filtration of H^dR_1(A/S) is ω_{A^∨/S}. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Definition 3.4.2(1),(3) — O_F-abelian schemes and O_F-linear (quasi-)homomorphisms
items.statement: Fix a subring ℙ ⊆ ℚ and let S ∈ Sch_{/ℙ}. (1) An O_F-abelian scheme over S is a pair (A, i) with A an abelian scheme over S and i: O_F → End_S(A) ⊗ ℙ a homomorphism of algebras sending 1 to the identity. (3) For O_F-abelian schemes (A, i), (A′, i′) over S, a (quasi-)homomorphism from (A, i) to (A′, i′) is a (quasi-)homomorphism φ: A → A′ with φ ∘ i(a) = i′(a) ∘ φ for every a ∈ O_F (an O_F-linear (quasi-)homomorphism).
items.note: In §§3.4–5 ℙ = ℤ_(p). The action i is often suppressed. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Definition 3.4.2(2) — unitary O_F-abelian scheme
items.statement: (ℙ ⊆ ℚ, S ∈ Sch_{/ℙ}.) A unitary O_F-abelian scheme over S is a triple (A, i, λ) in which (A, i) is an O_F-abelian scheme over S and λ: A → A^∨ is a quasi-polarization such that i(a^c)^∨ ∘ λ = λ ∘ i(a) for every a ∈ O_F, and there exists c ∈ ℙ^× making cλ a polarization.
items.note: The Rosati involution of λ induces complex conjugation on O_F. With ℙ = ℤ_(p), λ is automatically a quasi-p-isogeny (p. 150). Planned: PELModuli M1 plans the PEL moduli functors.
