items.name: Definition 3.4.3 — signature type Ψ
items.statement: Let Ψ = Σ r_τ τ be a generalized CM type of rank N and S ∈ Sch_{/O_{F_Ψ} ⊗ ℙ}. An O_F-abelian scheme (A, i) over S has signature type Ψ if for every a ∈ O_F the characteristic polynomial of i(a) on Lie_{A/S} is ∏_{τ ∈ Σ_∞} (T − τ(a))^{r_τ} ∈ 𝒪_S[T].
items.note: The polynomial has coefficients in O_{F_Ψ} (they are fixed by Stab(Ψ)), which is why S is over O_{F_Ψ} ⊗ ℙ. An O_F-abelian scheme of signature type Ψ has dimension N·[F^+:ℚ]. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Construction 3.4.4 — hermitian space Hom^{λ_0,λ}(H_1^ét(A_0), H_1^ét(A))
items.statement: Let K be an O_{F_Ψ} ⊗ ℙ-ring that is an algebraically closed field. Given a unitary O_F-abelian scheme (A_0, i_0, λ_0) over K of signature type Φ, a CM type, and a unitary O_F-abelian scheme (A, i, λ) over K of signature type Ψ, for every set □ of places of ℚ containing ∞ and the characteristic of K (if nonzero) one constructs a hermitian space Hom^{λ_0,λ}_{F ⊗_ℚ 𝔸^□}(H^ét_1(A_0, 𝔸^□), H^ét_1(A, 𝔸^□)) over F ⊗_ℚ 𝔸^□ = F ⊗_{F^+} (F^+ ⊗_ℚ 𝔸^□), with underlying F ⊗_ℚ 𝔸^□-module Hom_{F ⊗_ℚ 𝔸^□}(H^ét_1(A_0, 𝔸^□), H^ét_1(A, 𝔸^□)) and pairing (x, y) := i_0^{−1}((λ_{0*})^{−1} ∘ y^∨ ∘ λ_* ∘ x) ∈ i_0^{−1} End_{F ⊗_ℚ 𝔸^□}(H^ét_1(A_0, 𝔸^□)) = F ⊗_ℚ 𝔸^□.
items.note: 𝔸^□ is the ring of adeles away from □. The pairing is linear in x and c-semilinear in y because λ_0 i_0(a) = i_0(a^c)^∨ λ_0; End(H^ét_1(A_0)) = F ⊗ 𝔸^□ since H^ét_1(A_0, 𝔸^□) is free of rank 1 over F ⊗ 𝔸^□. Used to compare the moduli spaces of §§4–5 with Sh(V, K). Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Definition 3.4.5 — quasi-p-homomorphisms, quasi-p-isogenies, p-principal quasi-polarizations
items.statement: Let p be a rational prime unramified in F, ℙ = ℤ_(p), and A, B abelian schemes over S ∈ Sch_{/ℤ_(p)}. A quasi-homomorphism (resp. quasi-isogeny) φ: A → B is a quasi-p-homomorphism (resp. quasi-p-isogeny) if there exists c ∈ ℤ_(p)^× such that cφ is a homomorphism (resp. isogeny). A quasi-isogeny φ is prime-to-p if both φ and φ^{−1} are quasi-p-isogenies. A quasi-polarization λ of A is p-principal if λ is a prime-to-p quasi-isogeny.
items.note: For a unitary O_F-abelian scheme (A, i, λ), λ is a quasi-p-isogeny (p. 150). Standing choice from p. 149: ι_p: ℂ ⥲ ℚ̄_p fixed and Notation 3.3.6 adopted. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Remark 3.4.6 — τ-part of the Hodge sequence and its ranks
items.statement: Let A be an O_F-abelian scheme of signature type Ψ over a scheme S ∈ Sch_{/ℤ_p^τ} for some τ ∈ Σ_∞. Then (3.2) induces a short exact sequence 0 → ω_{A^∨/S,τ} → H^dR_1(A/S)_τ → Lie_{A/S,τ} → 0 of locally free 𝒪_S-modules of ranks N − r_τ, N and r_τ, respectively.
items.note: Implicitly S must also be over O_{F_Ψ} ⊗ ℤ_(p) for 'signature type Ψ' to make sense (Definition 3.4.3); harmless. Uses that H^dR_1 is locally free over O_F ⊗ 𝒪_S (p unramified in F). Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Remark 3.4.6 — decomposition over ℤ_p^◇
items.statement: If S belongs to Sch_{/ℤ_p^◇}, then H^dR_1(A/S) = ⊕_{τ ∈ Σ_∞} H^dR_1(A/S)_τ, Lie_{A/S} = ⊕_{τ ∈ Σ_∞} Lie_{A/S,τ}, ω_{A/S} = ⊕_{τ ∈ Σ_∞} ω_{A/S,τ}, as locally free 𝒪_S-modules.
items.note: O_F ⊗ ℤ_p^◇ ≅ ∏_{τ} ℤ_p^◇ since p is unramified in F. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Notation 3.4.7 — the pairing ⟨ , ⟩_{λ,τ} and orthogonal complements
items.statement: Take τ ∈ Σ_∞ and a unitary O_F-abelian scheme (A, λ) of signature type Ψ over S ∈ Sch_{/ℤ_p^τ}. ⟨ , ⟩_{λ,τ}: H^dR_1(A/S)_τ × H^dR_1(A/S)_{τ^c} → 𝒪_S denotes the 𝒪_S-bilinear pairing induced by the quasi-polarization λ, which (as printed) is perfect if and only if λ is p-principal. For an 𝒪_S-submodule ℱ ⊆ H^dR_1(A/S)_τ, ℱ^⊥ ⊆ H^dR_1(A/S)_{τ^c} denotes its (right) orthogonal complement under this pairing.
items.note: 'If' is correct; 'only if' fails over bases on which p is invertible (minor source issue). v1/v2 said instead 'which might be degenerate'. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Deformation groupoids Def(S, Ŝ; A, λ) and Def′(S, Ŝ; A, λ)
items.statement: Let Ψ be a generalized CM type of rank N such that min{r_τ, r_{τ^c}} = 0 for every τ not above τ̲_∞. Let S ↪ Ŝ be a closed immersion in Sch_{/ℤ_p^Ψ} on which p is locally nilpotent, with ideal sheaf equipped with a PD structure, and (A, λ) a unitary O_F-abelian scheme of signature type Ψ over S. H^cris_1(A/Ŝ) is the evaluation of the first relative crystalline homology of A/S at the PD-thickening S ↪ Ŝ, a locally free 𝒪_Ŝ ⊗ O_F-module; λ induces a pairing ⟨ , ⟩^cris_{λ,τ_∞}: H^cris_1(A/Ŝ)_{τ_∞} × H^cris_1(A/Ŝ)_{τ_∞^c} → 𝒪_Ŝ (3.3). Def(S, Ŝ; A, λ) is the groupoid of unitary O_F-abelian schemes (Â, λ̂) of signature type Ψ over Ŝ lifting (A, λ). Def′(S, Ŝ; A, λ) is the groupoid of pairs (ω̂_{τ_∞}, ω̂_{τ_∞^c}) where, for τ ∈ {τ_∞, τ_∞^c}, ω̂_τ ⊆ H^cris_1(A/Ŝ)_τ is a subbundle lifting ω_{A^∨/S,τ} ⊆ H^dR_1(A/S)_τ, such that ⟨ω̂_{τ_∞}, ω̂_{τ_∞^c}⟩^cris_{λ,τ_∞} = 0.
items.note: Grothendieck–Messing theory is usually stated for nilpotent (or locally nilpotent) PD structures; the paper's 'p locally nilpotent + PD ideal' is the standard shorthand. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Proposition 3.4.8 — deformations of unitary O_F-abelian schemes ↔ isotropic Hodge lifts
items.statement: In the setting of the deformation groupoids above (Ψ of rank N with min{r_τ, r_{τ^c}} = 0 for every τ not above τ̲_∞; S ↪ Ŝ a PD closed immersion in Sch_{/ℤ_p^Ψ} with p locally nilpotent; (A, λ) unitary of signature type Ψ over S), the functor Def(S, Ŝ; A, λ) → Def′(S, Ŝ; A, λ) sending (Â, λ̂) to (ω_{Â^∨/Ŝ,τ_∞}, ω_{Â^∨/Ŝ,τ_∞^c}) is a natural equivalence.
items.note: Proof: by étale descent replace S ↪ Ŝ by its base change to ℤ_p^◇, where H^cris_1(A/Ŝ) = ⊕_τ H^cris_1(A/Ŝ)_τ; for τ ∉ {τ_∞, τ_∞^c} the subbundle ω_{A^∨/S,τ} (of rank 0 or N) has a unique lift (zero or everything), and these are automatically isotropic; the result then follows from Serre–Tate [34] and Grothendieck–Messing [52] theory (black boxes). The earlier item text about Dieudonné lattices of isogenies belongs to Lemma 3.4.12 (separate items below). Planned: PELModuli M2 plans representability and deformation theory at good level.

items.name: Serre–Tate and Grothendieck–Messing theorems (cited)
items.statement: (Serre–Tate) For S ↪ Ŝ a nilpotent thickening on which p is locally nilpotent, deforming an abelian scheme is equivalent to deforming its p-divisible group. (Grothendieck–Messing) For a PD thickening S ↪ Ŝ with (locally) nilpotent divided powers and p locally nilpotent, lifts of an abelian scheme A/S to Ŝ correspond to lifts of the Hodge filtration ω_{A^∨/S} ⊆ H^dR_1(A/S) to a subbundle of H^cris_1(A/Ŝ); a polarization (quasi-polarization) and endomorphisms lift iff the lifted filtration is isotropic, resp. stable.
items.locator: §3.4, before Proposition 3.4.8, p. 150 (cited: [34], [52]); also Used throughout the proofs of Theorems 5.2.5, 5.3.4, 5.4.4, 5.5.3, published pp. 191–210
items.note: Cited, not proved. Statement as used in the proof of Proposition 3.4.8 (and in §§4–5 deformation arguments). Planned: AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4 plans the Serre–Tate equivalence and Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory.

items.name: Notation 3.4.9 — Frobenius twist A^{(p)}, Frobenius and Verschiebung maps on H^dR_1
items.statement: Let A be an abelian scheme over S ∈ Sch_{/𝔽_p}, and A^{(p)} := A ×_{S,σ} S with σ the absolute Frobenius of S. Then: (1) there is a canonical isomorphism H^dR_1(A^{(p)}/S) ≃ σ^* H^dR_1(A/S) of 𝒪_S-modules; (2) the Frobenius homomorphism Fr_A: A → A^{(p)} induces the Verschiebung map 𝚅_A := (Fr_A)_*: H^dR_1(A/S) → H^dR_1(A^{(p)}/S); (3) the Verschiebung homomorphism Ver_A: A^{(p)} → A induces the Frobenius map 𝙵_A := (Ver_A)_*: H^dR_1(A^{(p)}/S) → H^dR_1(A/S). For a subbundle H of H^dR_1(A/S), H^{(p)} denotes the subbundle of H^dR_1(A^{(p)}/S) corresponding to σ^*H under (1).
items.note: Covariant conventions: Fr_A induces V and Ver_A induces F on homology. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Kernels and images of 𝙵 and 𝚅; Frobenius twist of τ-parts
items.statement: In Notation 3.4.9: ker 𝙵 = im 𝚅 = ω_{A^{(p)}/S} [as printed; the correct subbundle is ω_{(A^{(p)})^∨/S} = ω_{A^∨/S}^{(p)}, the Hodge filtration of H^dR_1(A^{(p)}/S)], and ker 𝚅 = im 𝙵. For τ ∈ Σ_∞, S ∈ Sch_{/𝔽_p^τ} and an O_F-abelian scheme A over S, (H^dR_1(A/S)_τ)^{(p)} = H^dR_1(A^{(p)}/S)_{στ} under Notations 3.3.6 and 3.4.9.
items.note: Stated without proof (standard, Oda). im 𝚅 ⊆ ker(H^dR_1(A^{(p)}) → Lie_{A^{(p)}}) because Lie(Fr_A) = 0; equality by ranks. Misprint recorded in source issues. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Notation 3.4.10(1) — semilinear 𝙵 and 𝚅 over a field
items.statement: Suppose S = Spec κ for a field κ of characteristic p, so H^dR_1(A^{(p)}/κ) ≃ H^dR_1(A/κ) ⊗_{κ,σ} κ canonically. By abuse of notation one has the (κ, σ)-linear Frobenius map 𝙵: H^dR_1(A/κ) → H^dR_1(A/κ) and, if κ is perfect, the (κ, σ^{−1})-linear Verschiebung map 𝚅: H^dR_1(A/κ) → H^dR_1(A/κ).
items.note: Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Notation 3.4.10(2),(3) — covariant Dieudonné module 𝒟(A) and its τ-parts
items.statement: (2) When κ is perfect, 𝒟(A) denotes the covariant Dieudonné module of the p-divisible group A[p^∞], a free W(κ)-module with 𝒟(A)/p𝒟(A) canonically isomorphic to H^dR_1(A/κ), with the (W(κ), σ)-linear Frobenius 𝙵: 𝒟(A) → 𝒟(A) and (W(κ), σ^{−1})-linear Verschiebung 𝚅: 𝒟(A) → 𝒟(A) lifting those of (1) and satisfying 𝙵∘𝚅 = 𝚅∘𝙵 = p. (3) When κ is perfect and contains 𝔽_p^τ for some τ ∈ Σ_∞, applying Notation 3.3.6 gives W(κ)-submodules 𝒟(A)_{σ^i τ} ⊆ 𝒟(A) (i ∈ ℤ), the (W(κ), σ)-linear 𝙵: 𝒟(A)_τ → 𝒟(A)_{στ} and (W(κ), σ^{−1})-linear 𝚅: 𝒟(A)_τ → 𝒟(A)_{σ^{−1}τ} by restriction, and canonical isomorphisms and inclusions 𝚅𝒟(A)_{στ}/p𝒟(A)_τ ≃ ω_{A^∨,τ} ⊆ 𝒟(A)_τ/p𝒟(A)_τ ≃ H^dR_1(A)_τ.
items.note: Standard covariant Dieudonné theory (black box). Consequently Lie_{A,τ} ≃ 𝒟(A)_τ/𝚅𝒟(A)_{στ}. Planned: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2 plans Dieudonné modules with Frobenius and Verschiebung.

items.name: Notation 3.4.11 — pairing on Dieudonné modules and duals
items.statement: Take τ ∈ Σ_∞ and a unitary O_F-abelian scheme (A, λ) of signature type Ψ over Spec κ, κ a perfect field containing 𝔽_p^τ. There is a pairing ⟨ , ⟩_{λ,τ}: 𝒟(A)_τ × 𝒟(A)_{τ^c} → W(κ) lifting the one of Notation 3.4.7. 𝒟(A)_τ^∨ denotes the W(κ)-dual of 𝒟(A)_τ, regarded as a submodule of 𝒟(A)_{τ^c} ⊗ ℚ via this pairing. Unless otherwise specified, duals are taken with respect to the default quasi-polarization.
items.note: Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Lemma 3.4.12(1) — exactness of α_* and β_* on the τ_∞, τ_∞^c parts
items.statement: Setting of Lemma 3.4.12: F^+ ⊆ ℚ_p via the embedding τ̲_∞: F^+ ↪ ℂ ≃ ℚ̄_p (printed 'τ'), with 𝔭 the induced p-adic prime; ϖ ∈ O_{F^+} with val_𝔭(ϖ) = 1; A and B are O_F-abelian schemes over S ∈ Sch_{/𝔽_{p²}}; α: A → B and β: B → A are O_F-linear quasi-p-isogenies (Definition 3.4.5) with β ∘ α = ϖ · id_A (hence α ∘ β = ϖ · id_B). [Tacitly, as in all applications (§§4–5, 𝔭 special inert), 𝔭 is inert in F; (2) is false if 𝔭 splits in F.] Then for τ ∈ {τ_∞, τ_∞^c}, the induced maps α_{*,τ}: H^dR_1(A/S)_τ → H^dR_1(B/S)_τ and β_{*,τ}: H^dR_1(B/S)_τ → H^dR_1(A/S)_τ satisfy ker α_{*,τ} = im β_{*,τ} and ker β_{*,τ} = im α_{*,τ}, and these kernels and images are locally free 𝒪_S-modules.
items.note: Proof: reduce to the 𝔭-parts H^dR_1 ⊗_{O_{F^+}} ℤ_p; with A[𝔭] of degree p^{2d} and ker α[𝔭] of degree p^r, it suffices that coker α_* and coker β_* are locally free of ranks r and 2d − r; following de Jong [23, Lemma 2.3], use the covariant Dieudonné crystals 𝒟(A[𝔭^∞]) ⊆ 𝒟(B[𝔭^∞]), the exact sequence (3.4) 0 → α_*𝒟(A)/ϖ𝒟(B) → 𝒟(B)/ϖ𝒟(B) → 𝒟(B)/α_*𝒟(A) → 0, the surjection (3.5) α_*: 𝒟(A)/β_*𝒟(B) → α_*𝒟(A)/ϖ𝒟(B), local freeness of 𝒟(B)/ϖ𝒟(B) of rank 2d [4, Proposition 4.3.1], and a count of generators at geometric points. Valid whether 𝔭 is inert or split in F. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Lemma 3.4.12(2) — change of Lie rank equals difference of kernel ranks
items.statement: Setting of Lemma 3.4.12: F^+ ⊆ ℚ_p via the embedding τ̲_∞: F^+ ↪ ℂ ≃ ℚ̄_p (printed 'τ'), with 𝔭 the induced p-adic prime; ϖ ∈ O_{F^+} with val_𝔭(ϖ) = 1; A and B are O_F-abelian schemes over S ∈ Sch_{/𝔽_{p²}}; α: A → B and β: B → A are O_F-linear quasi-p-isogenies (Definition 3.4.5) with β ∘ α = ϖ · id_A (hence α ∘ β = ϖ · id_B). [Tacitly, as in all applications (§§4–5, 𝔭 special inert), 𝔭 is inert in F; (2) is false if 𝔭 splits in F.] Then rank_{𝒪_S} Lie_{B/S,τ_∞} − rank_{𝒪_S} Lie_{A/S,τ_∞} = rank_{𝒪_S}(ker α_{*,τ_∞}) − rank_{𝒪_S}(ker α_{*,τ_∞^c}).
items.note: Proof: reduce to S = Spec κ, κ perfect ⊇ 𝔽_{p²}; with r = dim Lie_{A,τ_∞}, s = dim Lie_{B,τ_∞}, write s = dim ω_{B^∨,τ_∞^c} = dim 𝚅𝒟(B)_{τ_∞}/p𝒟(B)_{τ_∞^c} (and similarly r), then compare lengths via 𝒟(A) ⊆ 𝒟(B). The first equality needs σ^{−1}τ_∞^c = τ_∞ (𝔭 inert) and dim Lie_{τ_∞} + dim Lie_{τ_∞^c} = rank H^dR_1(B)_{τ_∞^c} (true for unitary schemes, not among the hypotheses); the conclusion nevertheless holds for 𝔭 inert by the direct count s − r = ℓ(𝒟(B)_{τ_∞}/𝒟(A)_{τ_∞}) − ℓ(𝒟(B)_{στ_∞}/𝒟(A)_{στ_∞}). See source issues. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Lemma 3.4.12(3) — total kernel rank for α^∨∘λ_B∘α = ϖλ_A
items.statement: Setting of Lemma 3.4.12: F^+ ⊆ ℚ_p via the embedding τ̲_∞: F^+ ↪ ℂ ≃ ℚ̄_p (printed 'τ'), with 𝔭 the induced p-adic prime; ϖ ∈ O_{F^+} with val_𝔭(ϖ) = 1; A and B are O_F-abelian schemes over S ∈ Sch_{/𝔽_{p²}}; α: A → B and β: B → A are O_F-linear quasi-p-isogenies (Definition 3.4.5) with β ∘ α = ϖ · id_A (hence α ∘ β = ϖ · id_B). [Tacitly, as in all applications (§§4–5, 𝔭 special inert), 𝔭 is inert in F; (2) is false if 𝔭 splits in F.] Let λ_A and λ_B be quasi-polarizations on A and B such that (A, λ_A) and (B, λ_B) are unitary O_F-abelian schemes of dimension N[F^+ : ℚ] for some integer N ≥ 1, and suppose α^∨ ∘ λ_B ∘ α = ϖλ_A. Then, writing ρ := rank_{𝒪_S}(ker α_{*,τ_∞}) + rank_{𝒪_S}(ker α_{*,τ_∞^c}): (a) if both λ_A and λ_B are p-principal, ρ = N; (b) if λ_A is p-principal and ker λ_B[𝔭^∞] is of rank p², ρ = N − 1; (c) if ker λ_A[𝔭^∞] is of rank p² and λ_B is p-principal, ρ = N + 1; (d) if both ker λ_A[𝔭^∞] and ker λ_B[𝔭^∞] are of rank p², ρ = N.
items.note: Proof: reduce to S = Spec κ, κ algebraically closed ⊇ 𝔽_{p²}; compare degrees of (α^∨∘λ_B∘α)[𝔭^∞] and (ϖλ_A)[𝔭^∞]: deg α[𝔭^∞] = deg α^∨[𝔭^∞] = p^ρ, so 2ρ + log_p deg λ_B[𝔭^∞] = 2N + log_p deg λ_A[𝔭^∞]; (a)–(d) follow (checked). 'Rank p²' means order p² as a finite flat group scheme. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Lemma 3.4.12(4) — total kernel rank for α^∨∘λ_B∘α = λ_A
items.statement: Setting of Lemma 3.4.12: F^+ ⊆ ℚ_p via the embedding τ̲_∞: F^+ ↪ ℂ ≃ ℚ̄_p (printed 'τ'), with 𝔭 the induced p-adic prime; ϖ ∈ O_{F^+} with val_𝔭(ϖ) = 1; A and B are O_F-abelian schemes over S ∈ Sch_{/𝔽_{p²}}; α: A → B and β: B → A are O_F-linear quasi-p-isogenies (Definition 3.4.5) with β ∘ α = ϖ · id_A (hence α ∘ β = ϖ · id_B). [Tacitly, as in all applications (§§4–5, 𝔭 special inert), 𝔭 is inert in F; (2) is false if 𝔭 splits in F.] Let λ_A, λ_B be quasi-polarizations making (A, λ_A), (B, λ_B) unitary O_F-abelian schemes of dimension N[F^+ : ℚ] for some N ≥ 1, and suppose α^∨ ∘ λ_B ∘ α = λ_A. If ker λ_A[𝔭^∞] is of rank p² and λ_B is p-principal, then rank_{𝒪_S}(ker α_{*,τ_∞}) + rank_{𝒪_S}(ker α_{*,τ_∞^c}) = 1.
items.note: 'Similar to (3)': 2ρ + 0 = 0 + 2 gives ρ = 1 (checked). Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Local freeness of Dieudonné crystals mod ϖ (cited)
items.statement: For a p-divisible group G = B[𝔭^∞] over S ∈ Sch_{/𝔽_p} of height 2d, the reduction 𝒟(G)/ϖ𝒟(G) of its covariant Dieudonné crystal on the big crystalline site (S/ℤ_p)_cris is a locally free 𝒪^cris_S/p𝒪^cris_S-module of rank 2d.
items.note: Black box from Berthelot–Breen–Messing (the Dieudonné crystal of a p-divisible group is locally free of rank equal to the height); ϖ = p·unit on the 𝔭-part since F^+_𝔭 = ℚ_p. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Definition 3.5.1(1) — rational skew-hermitian space
items.statement: Let R be a ℤ[(disc F)^{−1}]-ring. A rational skew-hermitian space over O_F ⊗ R of rank N is a free O_F ⊗ R-module W of rank N together with an R-bilinear skew-symmetric perfect pairing ⟨ , ⟩_W: W × W → R satisfying ⟨ax, y⟩_W = ⟨x, a^c y⟩_W for every a ∈ O_F ⊗ R and x, y ∈ W.
items.note: Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Definition 3.5.1(2)–(4) — similitudes, similarity, GU(W)
items.statement: (2) For rational skew-hermitian spaces W, W′ over O_F ⊗ R, a map f: W → W′ is a similitude if f is an O_F ⊗ R-linear isomorphism and there exists c(f) ∈ R^× with ⟨f(x), f(y)⟩_{W′} = c(f)⟨x, y⟩_W for all x, y ∈ W. (3) W and W′ are similar if there exists a similitude between them. (4) GU(W) denotes the group of similitudes of W, a reductive group over R: for every ring R′ over R, GU(W)(R′) is the set of self-similitudes of the rational skew-hermitian space W ⊗_R R′ over O_F ⊗ R′.
items.note: Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: The torus T_0
items.statement: T_0 ⊆ (Res_{O_F/ℤ} 𝐆_m) ⊗ ℤ[(disc F)^{−1}] is the subtorus such that for every ℤ[(disc F)^{−1}]-ring R, T_0(R) = {a ∈ O_F ⊗ R | Nm_{F/F^+} a ∈ R^×}.
items.note: Nm_{F/F^+} a = a a^c; the condition forces a to be a unit. T_0 is the similitude torus GU(1). Standing choice after this: p a rational prime unramified in F and ℙ = ℤ_(p). Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Remark 3.5.2 — GU(W_0) ≅ T_0; similarity classes and ker^1(T_0)
items.statement: Let W_0 be a rational skew-hermitian space over O_F ⊗ ℤ_(p) of rank 1. Then GU(W_0) is canonically isomorphic to T_0 ⊗_{ℤ[(disc F)^{−1}]} ℤ_(p). Moreover, the set of similarity classes of rational skew-hermitian spaces W′_0 over O_F ⊗ ℤ_(p) of rank 1 such that W′_0 ⊗_{ℤ_(p)} 𝔸 is similar to W_0 ⊗_{ℤ_(p)} 𝔸 is canonically isomorphic to ker^1(T_0) := ker(H^1(ℚ, T_0) → ∏_{v ≤ ∞} H^1(ℚ_v, T_0)), which is a finite abelian group.
items.note: Stated without proof (standard Galois-cohomological classification of forms; integrality at p is harmless because T_0 is smooth over ℤ_(p) with H^1(ℤ_p, T_0) = 0 by Lang). Finiteness of ker^1 of a torus is classical. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Definition 3.5.3 — rank-one skew-hermitian space of type Φ
items.statement: Let Φ be a CM type. A rational skew-hermitian space W_0 over O_F ⊗ ℤ_(p) of rank 1 has type Φ if for every x ∈ W_0 and every totally imaginary element a ∈ F^× satisfying Im τ(a) > 0 for all τ ∈ Φ, one has ⟨ax, x⟩_{W_0} ≥ 0.
items.note: A positivity (sign) condition at ∞ matching the Riemann form of a CM abelian variety of type Φ. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Definition 3.5.4 — the CM moduli presheaf 𝐓^1_p(W_0, K^p_0)
items.statement: For a rational skew-hermitian space W_0 over O_F ⊗ ℤ_(p) of rank 1 and type Φ and an open compact subgroup K^p_0 ⊆ T_0(𝔸^{∞,p}), 𝐓^1_p(W_0, K^p_0) is the presheaf on Sch′_{/O_{F_Φ} ⊗ ℤ_(p)} (locally noetherian schemes) such that, for S in it, 𝐓^1_p(W_0, K^p_0)(S) is the set of equivalence classes of triples (A_0, λ_0, η^p_0) where (A_0, λ_0) is a unitary O_F-abelian scheme of signature type Φ over S with λ_0 p-principal, and η^p_0 is a K^p_0-level structure, i.e. for a chosen geometric point s on every connected component of S, a π_1(S, s)-invariant K^p_0-orbit of similitudes η^p_0: W_0 ⊗_{ℤ_(p)} 𝔸^{∞,p} → H^ét_1(A_{0s}, 𝔸^{∞,p}) of rational skew-hermitian spaces over F ⊗_ℚ 𝔸^{∞,p}, H^ét_1(A_{0s}, 𝔸^{∞,p}) carrying the rational skew-hermitian form induced by λ_0. Two triples (A_0, λ_0, η^p_0) and (A′_0, λ′_0, η^{p′}_0) are equivalent if there is a prime-to-p O_F-linear quasi-isogeny φ_0: A_0 → A′_0 carrying (λ_0, η^p_0) to (cλ′_0, η^{p′}_0) for some c ∈ ℤ_(p)^×.
items.note: Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: The map w: 𝐓^1_p(W_0, K^p_0)(ℂ) → ker^1(T_0)
items.statement: For (A_0, λ_0, η^p_0) ∈ 𝐓^1_p(W_0, K^p_0)(ℂ), H_1(A_0(ℂ), ℤ_(p)) is a rational skew-hermitian space over O_F ⊗ ℤ_(p) induced by λ_0, of rank 1 and type Φ, and everywhere locally similar to W_0. By Remark 3.5.2 this gives a map w: 𝐓^1_p(W_0, K^p_0)(ℂ) → ker^1(T_0) sending (A_0, λ_0, η^p_0) to the similarity class of H_1(A_0(ℂ), ℤ_(p)).
items.note: Local similarity away from p comes from η^p_0, at p from p-principality (all self-dual rank-one forms over O_F ⊗ ℤ_p are similar), at ∞ from the type Φ; stated without further detail. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Representability of 𝐓^1_p(W_0, K^p_0) (cited as known)
items.statement: When K^p_0 is neat, 𝐓^1_p(W_0, K^p_0) is represented by a scheme finite and étale over O_{F_Φ} ⊗ ℤ_(p).
items.note: Introduced by 'It is known that'; no reference or proof (black box: CM abelian varieties have good reduction and rigid deformation theory for signature type Φ with p unramified). The previous item text ('§3.6', comparison with Sh(U(V)) × T, orbit trace) mixed this with Definition 3.5.8 and §4: there is no §3.6 in the published paper; the product comparison is in §4; the orbit-trace convention is Definition 3.5.8 (separate item). Planned: PELModuli M3 plans the complex and generic-fibre comparison; PELModuli M4 plans canonical models.

api.name: RankinSelberg.AuxiliaryCmTorusModel.data
api.statement: Use the finite étale CM object, component action and trace.

api.name: RankinSelberg.AuxiliaryCmTorusModel.characterisation
api.statement: The invariant cohomology identifies the unitary factor under the stated product comparison.

api.name: RankinSelberg.AuxiliaryCmTorusModel.compatibility
api.statement: Trace sums over free orbits are compatible with coefficient reduction.

uses.how: Use the finite étale CM object, component action and trace.

items.name: The CM moduli scheme 𝐓_p(W_0, K^p_0)
items.statement: 𝐓_p(W_0, K^p_0) is the minimal open and closed subscheme of 𝐓^1_p(W_0, K^p_0) containing w^{−1}(W_0) (the ℂ-points whose first homology is similar to W_0).
items.note: In §4.1 one puts 𝐓_𝔭 := 𝐓_p(W_0, K^p_0) ⊗_{O_{F_Φ} ⊗ ℤ_(p)} ℤ_p^Φ, with K^p_0 neat. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Action of T_0(𝔸^{∞,p}) on 𝐓_p(W_0, K^p_0); Galois structure
items.statement: T_0(𝔸^{∞,p}) acts on 𝐓_p(W_0, K^p_0) via a · (A_0, λ_0, η^p_0) = (A_0, λ_0, η^p_0 ∘ a), with stabilizer T_0(ℤ_(p))K^p_0. In fact, T_0(𝔸^{∞,p})/T_0(ℤ_(p))K^p_0 is the Galois group of the Galois morphism 𝐓_p(W_0, K^p_0) → Spec(O_{F_Φ} ⊗ ℤ_(p)).
items.note: Asserted without proof (CM theory: the ℂ-points of 𝐓_p(W_0, K^p_0) form a torsor under the finite group T_0(𝔸^{∞,p})/T_0(ℤ_(p))K^p_0; T_0(ℤ_(p)) acts trivially through i_0). The quotient is finite since it injects into T_0(ℚ)\T_0(𝔸^∞)/T_0(ℤ_p)K^p_0. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Definition 3.5.5 — the groupoid 𝔗
items.statement: 𝔗 denotes the groupoid of T_0(𝔸^{∞,p})/T_0(ℤ_(p))K^p_0, that is, the category with a single object ∗ and Hom(∗, ∗) = T_0(𝔸^{∞,p})/T_0(ℤ_(p))K^p_0.
items.note: Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Remark 3.5.6 — 𝐓_p(W_0, K^p_0) as a functor on 𝔗 (and on ℭ × 𝔗)
items.statement: As 𝐓_p(W_0, K^p_0) is an object of Sch_{/O_{F_Φ} ⊗ ℤ_(p)} with an action of T_0(𝔸^{∞,p})/T_0(ℤ_(p))K^p_0, it induces a functor 𝔗 → Sch_{/O_{F_Φ} ⊗ ℤ_(p)}, still denoted 𝐓_p(W_0, K^p_0). For another category ℭ, 𝐓_p(W_0, K^p_0) is regarded as a functor ℭ × 𝔗 → Sch_{/O_{F_Φ} ⊗ ℤ_(p)} by composing with the projection ℭ × 𝔗 → 𝔗.
items.note: Used with ℭ = 𝔎(V)^p, 𝔎(V)^p_sp in §§4–5. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Notation 3.5.7 — 𝔗-invariant cohomology
items.statement: For a functor X: 𝔗 → Sch and a coefficient ring L, H^i_𝔗(X, L(j)) ⊆ H^i_ét(X(∗), L(j)) and H^i_{𝔗,c}(X, L(j)) ⊆ H^i_{ét,c}(X(∗), L(j)) denote the maximal L-submodules on which T_0(𝔸^{∞,p})/T_0(ℤ_(p))K^p_0 acts trivially.
items.note: Invariants (not coinvariants, no averaging). This is how the auxiliary CM factor is removed from the cohomology of the product moduli spaces of §§4–5. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: Definition 3.5.8 — the 𝔗-trace map
items.statement: Let κ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p and L a p-coprime coefficient ring. For a functor X: 𝔗 → Sch_{/κ} such that X(∗) is smooth of finite type of dimension d and 𝔗 acts freely on the set of connected components of X(∗), the 𝔗-trace map ∫^𝔗_X: H^{2d}_{𝔗,c}(X(∗), L(d)) → L is the composite H^{2d}_{𝔗,c}(X(∗), L(d)) ↪ H^{2d}_c(X(∗), L(d)) → ⊕_Y H^{2d}_c(Y, L(d)) → L (the last map Σ tr_Y), where {Y} is a set of representatives of the 𝔗-orbits on the connected components of X(∗) and the second map is the natural projection. It does not depend on the choice of {Y}.
items.note: Independence: for a 𝔗-invariant class the traces on Y and gY agree. The trace sums over one representative per orbit only, so no division by the order of the (finite) group is needed in L. Missing: routed to a source of PELModuli M0–M4 (route 7).

items.name: §4.1 — initial data for the smooth case
items.statement: Fix a special inert prime 𝔭 of F⁺ (Definition 3.3.4: 𝔭 is inert in F, its underlying rational prime p is odd and unramified in F, and F⁺_𝔭 = Q_p) and take the prescribed subring P = Z_(p). Choose: a CM type Φ of F containing τ_∞; a rational skew-hermitian space W₀ over O_F ⊗ Z_(p) of rank 1 and type Φ (Definition 3.5.3); a neat open compact subgroup K₀^p ⊆ T₀(A^{∞,p}); an isomorphism ι_p: C ⥲ Q̄_p such that ι_p ∘ τ̲_∞: F⁺ ↪ Q̄_p induces the place 𝔭; an element ϖ ∈ O_{F⁺} that is totally positive with val_𝔭(ϖ) = 1 and val_𝔮(ϖ) = 0 for every prime 𝔮 ≠ 𝔭 of F⁺ above p. Adopt Notation 3.3.6 (so F_p^Φ ⊇ F_{p²}). Put T_𝔭 := T_p(W₀, K₀^p) ⊗_{O_{F_Φ} ⊗ Z_(p)} Z_p^Φ, where T_p(W₀, K₀^p) is the CM moduli scheme of Definition 3.5.4 (finite étale and Galois with group T₀(A^{∞,p})/T₀(Z_(p))K₀^p, viewed as a functor on the groupoid 𝔗 of that group, Definition 3.5.5/Remark 3.5.6). W₀ and K₀^p are suppressed from notation; 𝔭 is kept.
items.note: Setup only. Condition F⁺_𝔭 = Q_p is used to simplify Dieudonné-module computations (Remark 3.3.5). ϖ is used to twist polarizations (ϖλ₀, ϖλ) throughout §§4.3–4.6. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: §4.2 — the datum (V, {Λ_𝔮}) and the groups K_𝔮, K_p
items.statement: The moduli problems of §4 start from a datum (V, {Λ_𝔮}_{𝔮|p}) where V is a standard indefinite hermitian space over F of rank N ⩾ 1 (Definition 3.2.1: signature (N−1, 1) at τ̲_∞ and (N, 0) at the other archimedean places of F⁺), and Λ_𝔮 is a self-dual O_{F_𝔮}-lattice in V ⊗_F F_𝔮 for every prime 𝔮 of F⁺ above p. Let K_𝔮 be the stabilizer of Λ_𝔮 in U(V)(F⁺_𝔮) and K_p := ∏_{𝔮|p} K_𝔮. 𝔎(V)^p denotes the category of neat open compact subgroups K^p ⊆ U(V)(A^{∞,p}_{F⁺}) with morphisms g ∈ K^p\U(V)(A^{∞,p}_{F⁺})/K^{p′} satisfying g⁻¹K^p g ⊆ K^{p′} (Definition 3.1.11).
items.locator: §4.2 opening paragraph, p. 159; K_𝔮, K_p defined p. 161
items.note: Self-dual lattices exist at all 𝔮 | p because V is the base of the hyperspecial-level integral model; they are part of the datum. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 4.2.1 — Q_p^Φ contains the reflex field of NΦ − τ_∞ + τ_∞^c
items.statement: For every N ⩾ 1, Ψ := NΦ − τ_∞ + τ_∞^c is a generalized CM type of rank N (Definition 3.3.1), and the field Q_p^Φ contains its reflex field F_Ψ (the fixed field of the stabilizer of Ψ in Aut(C/Q)).
items.note: Proof: every ρ ∈ Aut(C/Q_p^Φ) ⊆ Aut(C/F) fixes Φ (as F_Φ ⊆ Q_p^Φ) and τ_∞, hence Ψ. Needed so that 'signature type Ψ' makes sense over Z_p^Φ-schemes (Definition 3.4.3 requires S over O_{F_Ψ} ⊗ P). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 4.2.2 — the smooth moduli functor M_𝔭(V, −)
items.statement: Let Sch′_{/Z_p^Φ} be the category of locally Noetherian Z_p^Φ-schemes and PSch′_{/Z_p^Φ} the category of presheaves on it. Define M_𝔭(V, −): 𝔎(V)^p × 𝔗 → PSch′_{/Z_p^Φ}, K^p ↦ M_𝔭(V, K^p), where for S ∈ Sch′_{/Z_p^Φ}, M_𝔭(V, K^p)(S) is the set of equivalence classes of sextuples (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A, λ, η^p) with: (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p) ∈ T_𝔭(S); (A, λ) a unitary O_F-abelian scheme over S of signature type NΦ − τ_∞ + τ_∞^c (Definitions 3.4.2, 3.4.3) with λ p-principal; η^p a K^p-level structure, i.e. for a chosen geometric point s on every connected component of S, a π₁(S, s)-invariant K^p-orbit of isomorphisms of hermitian spaces over F ⊗_Q A^{∞,p} = F ⊗_{F⁺} A^{∞,p}_{F⁺}, η^p: V ⊗_Q A^{∞,p} → Hom^{λ₀,λ}_{F⊗_Q A^{∞,p}}(H₁^ét(A_{0s}, A^{∞,p}), H₁^ét(A_s, A^{∞,p})) (hermitian form (x, y) = i₀⁻¹((λ_{0*})⁻¹ ∘ y^∨ ∘ λ_* ∘ x) of Construction 3.4.4 with □ = {∞, p}). Two sextuples are equivalent if there are prime-to-p O_F-linear quasi-isogenies φ₀: A₀ → A₀′ and φ: A → A′ such that φ₀ carries η₀^p to η₀^{p′}; there is c ∈ Z_(p)^× with φ₀^∨ ∘ λ₀′ ∘ φ₀ = cλ₀ and φ^∨ ∘ λ′ ∘ φ = cλ; and the K^p-orbit of v ↦ φ_* ∘ η^p(v) ∘ (φ_{0*})⁻¹ (v ∈ V ⊗_Q A^{∞,p}) coincides with η^{p′}. On morphisms: g ∈ K^p\U(V)(A^{∞,p}_{F⁺})/K^{p′} maps M_𝔭(V, K^p)(S) to M_𝔭(V, K^{p′})(S) by η^p ↦ η^p ∘ g; a morphism a of 𝔗 acts by η₀^p ↦ η₀^p ∘ a. There is the forgetful morphism M_𝔭(V, −) → T_𝔭 (4.1) in Fun(𝔎(V)^p × 𝔗, PSch′_{/Z_p^Φ}), T_𝔭 regarded as a constant-in-𝔎 functor as in Remark 3.5.6; its base change to F_p^Φ is written M_𝔭(V, −) → T_𝔭.
items.note: Notation (§4.1, Notation 3.3.6): 𝔭 is a special inert prime of F⁺ over the rational prime p; Q_p^Φ ⊆ C (via ι_p) is the composite of Q_p, F and the reflex field F_Φ, Z_p^Φ its ring of integers, F_p^Φ its residue field (⊇ F_{p²}); roman letters (M, S, B, T) denote special fibres over F_p^Φ, a bar denotes base change to F̄_p, a superscript η the base change to Q_p^Φ. The published text prints the double coset as K^p\U(V)(A_F^{∞,p})/K^{p′}; U(V) is a group over F⁺ and A^{∞,p}_{F⁺} is meant (source issue). Previous pass labelled this 'Definition 4.2.1' (no such definition; Lemma 4.2.1 is the reflex-field lemma; in arXiv v1/v2 this is Definition 4.1.2). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 4.2.3 (first and last assertions) — M_𝔭(V, −) is smooth quasi-projective of relative dimension N − 1
items.statement: The morphism (4.1) M_𝔭(V, −) → T_𝔭 is represented by a quasi-projective smooth scheme over T_𝔭 of relative dimension N − 1 (i.e. for every K^p ∈ 𝔎(V)^p, M_𝔭(V, K^p) is a quasi-projective smooth T_𝔭-scheme of relative dimension N − 1). Moreover, (4.1) is projective if and only if its base change to Q_p^Φ is.
items.note: Representability and quasi-projectivity are cited from [RSZ21, Theorem 4.4]; smoothness and separatedness by deformation theory using Proposition 3.4.8 (Serre–Tate + Grothendieck–Messing: deformations of (A, λ) ↔ lifts of (ω_{A^∨,τ_∞}, ω_{A^∨,τ_∞^c}) orthogonal under the crystalline pairing). The projectivity criterion is not addressed in the proof (source issue: gap, low impact). Since K₀^p and K^p are neat, the functor is an algebraic space. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 4.2.3 (tangent sheaf) — T_{M/T} ≃ Hom(ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞}, H₁^dR(𝒜)_{τ_∞}/ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞})
items.statement: For every K^p ∈ 𝔎(V)^p there is a canonical isomorphism of coherent sheaves on M_𝔭(V, K^p): T_{M_𝔭(V,K^p)/T_𝔭} ≃ ℋom(ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞}, H₁^dR(𝒜)_{τ_∞}/ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞}), where (𝒜₀, λ₀, η₀^p; 𝒜, λ, η^p) is the universal object over M_𝔭(V, K^p), T_{M/T} is the relative tangent sheaf, and 0 → ω_{𝒜^∨,τ} → H₁^dR(𝒜)_τ → Lie_{𝒜,τ} → 0 is the τ-component of the Hodge sequence (Remark 3.4.6). This sheaf is locally free of rank N − 1 (ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞} has rank 1 and the quotient has rank N − 1).
items.note: Proved by Grothendieck–Messing via Proposition 3.4.8: a lift is determined by a lift ω̂_{τ_∞} of the rank-1 subbundle ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞} (ω̂_{τ_∞^c} is then its orthogonal), so first-order deformations form a torsor under Hom(ω_{τ_∞}, H₁^dR_{τ_∞}/ω_{τ_∞}) ⊗ I. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: (4.2) — moduli interpretation of the generic fibre
items.statement: There is a canonical isomorphism M^η_𝔭(V, −) ⥲ Sh(V, −K_p) ×_{Spec F} T^η_𝔭 (4.2) in Fun(𝔎(V)^p × 𝔗, Sch_{/Q_p^Φ})_{/T^η_𝔭}, where M^η, T^η denote base change to Q_p^Φ (Notation 3.3.6(5)), Sh(V, K) is the unitary Shimura variety over F attached to Res_{F⁺/Q} U(V) (§3.2), K_p = ∏_{𝔮|p} K_𝔮, and 𝔗 acts on the right-hand side through the second factor.
items.note: Cited, not proved: 'As shown in [RSZ21, §3.3], there is a canonical moduli interpretation isomorphism'. Remark 4.2.5 describes it on C-points (item remark-4-2-5). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 4.2.4 — specialization isomorphisms for the smooth model
items.statement: Let L be a p-coprime coefficient ring. The two specialization maps H^i_{𝔗,c}(M_𝔭(V, −) ⊗_{Z_p^Φ} Q̄_p, L) → H^i_{𝔗,c}(M̄_𝔭(V, −), L) and H^i_𝔗(M_𝔭(V, −) ⊗_{Z_p^Φ} Q̄_p, L) → H^i_𝔗(M̄_𝔭(V, −), L) are isomorphisms (H^i_𝔗 = the maximal submodule on which T₀(A^{∞,p})/T₀(Z_(p))K₀^p acts trivially, Notation 3.5.7). In particular, (4.2) induces isomorphisms H^i_{ét,c}(Sh(V, −K_p)_{F̄}, L) ≃ H^i_{𝔗,c}(M̄_𝔭(V, −), L) and H^i_ét(Sh(V, −K_p)_{F̄}, L) ≃ H^i_𝔗(M̄_𝔭(V, −), L) in Fun(𝔎(V)^p, Mod(L[Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p^Φ)])) for every i ∈ Z, where Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p^Φ) is regarded as a subgroup of Gal(F̄/F) via ι_p.
items.note: Proof: smoothness (Theorem 4.2.3) gives L ≃ RΨL; if M_𝔭(V, −) is proper this is proper base change; otherwise it is [LS18, Corollary 5.20] (black box). Previous pass called this 'Proposition 4.2.4'. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Remark 4.2.5 — (4.2) on complex points
items.statement: For x = (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A, λ, η^p) ∈ M_𝔭(V, K^p)(C) the isomorphism (4.2) sends x to the class U(V)(F⁺)(η_rat(l_x), g_x K^p K_p) in Sh(V, K^p K_p)(C) = U(V)(F⁺)\(V(C)_−/C^× × U(V)(A^∞_{F⁺})/K^p K_p) (V(C)_−/C^× = negative definite complex lines in V ⊗_F C), where: V_x := Hom_F(H₁(A₀(C), Q), H₁(A(C), Q)) with the pairing of Construction 3.4.4 is a standard indefinite hermitian space of rank N; ρ: V_x ⊗_Q A^{∞,p} ⥲ Hom^{λ₀,λ}_{F⊗A^{∞,p}}(H₁^ét(A₀, A^{∞,p}), H₁^ét(A, A^{∞,p})) is the comparison isometry; Hom_{O_F⊗Z_p}(H₁^ét(A₀, Z_p), H₁^ét(A, Z_p)) = ⊕_{𝔮|p} Λ_{x,𝔮} with Λ_{x,𝔮} self-dual in V ⊗_F F_𝔮, so by the Hasse principle there is an isometry η_rat: V_x → V; g^p := η_rat ∘ ρ⁻¹ ∘ η^p ∈ U(V)(A^{∞,p}_{F⁺}); g_𝔮 ∈ U(V)(F⁺_𝔮) with g_𝔮Λ_𝔮 = η_ratΛ_{x,𝔮}; g_x := (g^p, (g_𝔮)_{𝔮|p}) ∈ U(V)(A^∞_{F⁺}); and l_x ⊆ V_x ⊗_{F,τ_∞} C is the Hodge line Hom(H₁^dR(A₀/C)_{τ_∞}, ω_{A^∨,τ_∞}) (printed as {α ∈ Hom_F(H₁^dR(A₀/C), H₁^dR(A/C)) | α(ω_{A₀^∨,τ_∞}) ⊆ ω_{A^∨,τ_∞}}), whose image under η_rat lies in V(C)_−/C^×. The class is independent of η_rat and invariant under 𝔗. This description determines (4.2) uniquely.
items.note: Stated for the readers' convenience; no proof. The printed definition of l_x is vacuous as written (ω_{A₀^∨,τ_∞} = 0 since A₀ has signature Φ ∋ τ_∞) — source issue (misprint); the statement above gives the evident intended line (Hodge type (1, −1)). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 4.3.1 — the source S_𝔭(V, −) of the basic correspondence
items.statement: Define S_𝔭(V, −): 𝔎(V)^p × 𝔗 → PSch′_{/F_p^Φ}, K^p ↦ S_𝔭(V, K^p), where for S ∈ Sch′_{/F_p^Φ}, S_𝔭(V, K^p)(S) is the set of equivalence classes of sextuples (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A^⋆, λ^⋆, η^{p⋆}) with: (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p) ∈ T_𝔭(S); (A^⋆, λ^⋆) a unitary O_F-abelian scheme over S of signature type NΦ such that ker λ^⋆[p^∞] is trivial if N is odd, and is contained in A^⋆[𝔭] and of rank p² if N is even; η^{p⋆} a π₁(S, s)-invariant K^p-orbit of isomorphisms of hermitian spaces over F ⊗_Q A^{∞,p}, η^{p⋆}: V ⊗_Q A^{∞,p} → Hom^{ϖλ₀,λ^⋆}_{F⊗_Q A^{∞,p}}(H₁^ét(A_{0s}, A^{∞,p}), H₁^ét(A^⋆_s, A^{∞,p})) (note ϖλ₀ in place of λ₀, footnote 12). Equivalence and the action of morphisms of 𝔎(V)^p × 𝔗 are as in Definition 4.2.2. There is the forgetful morphism S_𝔭(V, −) → T_𝔭 in Fun(𝔎(V)^p × 𝔗, PSch′_{/F_p^Φ}).
items.note: Notation (§4.1, Notation 3.3.6): 𝔭 is a special inert prime of F⁺ over the rational prime p; Q_p^Φ ⊆ C (via ι_p) is the composite of Q_p, F and the reflex field F_Φ, Z_p^Φ its ring of integers, F_p^Φ its residue field (⊇ F_{p²}); roman letters (M, S, B, T) denote special fibres over F_p^Φ, a bar denotes base change to F̄_p, a superscript η the base change to Q_p^Φ. For N odd λ^⋆ is p-principal. The condition 'contained in A^⋆[𝔭]' (fraktur 𝔭) forces the kernel to be concentrated at 𝔭. Previous pass bundled Definitions 4.3.1 and 4.3.3 as 'Definitions 4.3.1–4.3.2'; 4.3.2 is a Lemma. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).
