items.name: S_𝔭(V, −) → T_𝔭 is represented by finite étale schemes
items.statement: The forgetful morphism S_𝔭(V, −) → T_𝔭 in Fun(𝔎(V)^p × 𝔗, PSch′_{/F_p^Φ}) is represented by finite étale schemes (over T_𝔭). For a point s^⋆ = (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A^⋆, λ^⋆, η^{p⋆}) ∈ S_𝔭(V, K^p)(κ), κ ⊇ F_p^Φ a field, A^⋆[𝔭^∞] is a supersingular p-divisible group (by the signature condition and since 𝔭 is inert in F).
items.note: Representability cited from [RSZ21, Theorem 4.4] (black box). Supersingularity is asserted in the text (signature NΦ at the two embeddings above 𝔭). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: The Frobenius-twisted pairing { , }_{s⋆} on 𝒱_{s⋆} = H₁^dR(A^⋆/κ)_{τ_∞}
items.statement: For s^⋆ = (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A^⋆, λ^⋆, η^{p⋆}) ∈ S_𝔭(V, K^p)(κ) with κ a field containing F_p^Φ, let F: H₁^dR(A^⋆/κ)_{τ_∞} → H₁^dR(A^⋆/κ)_{στ_∞} = H₁^dR(A^⋆/κ)_{τ_∞^c} be the (κ, σ)-linear Frobenius (Notation 3.4.10). Define { , }_{s⋆}: H₁^dR(A^⋆/κ)_{τ_∞} × H₁^dR(A^⋆/κ)_{τ_∞} → κ by {x, y}_{s⋆} := ⟨Fx, y⟩_{λ^⋆,τ_∞^c}, where ⟨ , ⟩_{λ^⋆,τ}: H₁^dR(A^⋆)_τ × H₁^dR(A^⋆)_{τ^c} → κ is the pairing induced by λ^⋆ (Notation 3.4.7); it is (κ, σ)-linear in x and κ-linear in y. Put 𝒱_{s⋆} := H₁^dR(A^⋆/κ)_{τ_∞}.
items.note: The kernel of ⟨F·, ·⟩ has rank 0 (N odd) or 1 (N even) (proof of Lemma 4.3.2), since F: H₁^dR(A^⋆)_{τ_∞} → H₁^dR(A^⋆)_{τ_∞^c} is an isomorphism (signature NΦ) and ker λ^⋆ has rank 0 or p². Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 4.3.2 — (𝒱_{s⋆}, { , }_{s⋆}) is admissible; the Deligne–Lusztig variety DL_{s⋆}
items.statement: The pair (𝒱_{s⋆}, { , }_{s⋆}) is admissible of rank N (Definition A.1.1: there is an F_{p²}-linear subspace V₀ ⊆ 𝒱_{s⋆} ⊗_κ κ̄ with V₀ ⊗_{F_{p²}} κ̄ ⥲ 𝒱_{s⋆} ⊗_κ κ̄ and {x, y} = −{y, x}^σ for all x, y ∈ V₀), with dim_κ 𝒱_{s⋆}^⊣ = 0 if N is odd and 1 if N is even. In particular the Deligne–Lusztig variety DL_{s⋆} := DL(𝒱_{s⋆}, { , }_{s⋆}, ⌈(N+1)/2⌉) — the presheaf on Sch_{/κ} whose S-points are the subbundles H ⊆ (𝒱_{s⋆})_S of rank ⌈(N+1)/2⌉ with H^⊣ ⊆ H, H^⊣ being the right orthogonal complement of H under the unique extension of { , }_{s⋆} that is (O_S, σ)-linear in the first and O_S-linear in the second variable (Definition A.1.2) — is a geometrically irreducible projective smooth scheme in Sch_{/κ} of dimension ⌊(N−1)/2⌋, with a canonical isomorphism T_{DL_{s⋆}/κ} ≃ ℋom(ℋ/ℋ^⊣, (𝒱_{s⋆})_{DL_{s⋆}}/ℋ), ℋ ⊆ (𝒱_{s⋆})_{DL_{s⋆}} the universal subbundle.
items.note: Proof: over κ̄, F and the (κ̄, σ⁻¹)-linear V: H₁^dR(A^⋆)_{τ_∞} → H₁^dR(A^⋆)_{τ_∞^c} are isomorphisms; V₀ := fixed points of the σ²-linear V⁻¹F, and for x, y ∈ V₀: {x, y} = ⟨Fx, y⟩ = ⟨x, Vy⟩^σ = ⟨x, Fy⟩^σ = −⟨Fy, x⟩^σ = −{y, x}^σ. The proof's appeal to supersingularity/Dieudonné's classification for V₀ ⊗ κ̄ ≅ 𝒱 is more than needed (Lang's theorem for a σ²-linear bijection suffices). The cross-reference 'Definition 4.3.1(2)' refers to the second (unnumbered) bullet. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 4.3.3 — the correspondence space B_𝔭(V, −)
items.statement: Define B_𝔭(V, −): 𝔎(V)^p × 𝔗 → PSch′_{/F_p^Φ}, where for S ∈ Sch′_{/F_p^Φ}, B_𝔭(V, K^p)(S) is the set of equivalence classes of decuples (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A, λ, η^p; A^⋆, λ^⋆, η^{p⋆}; α) with: (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A, λ, η^p) ∈ M_𝔭(V, K^p)(S); (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A^⋆, λ^⋆, η^{p⋆}) ∈ S_𝔭(V, K^p)(S); α: A → A^⋆ an O_F-linear quasi-p-isogeny (Definition 3.4.5) such that (a) ker α[p^∞] is contained in A[𝔭]; (b) ϖ·λ = α^∨ ∘ λ^⋆ ∘ α; (c) the K^p-orbit of v ↦ α_* ∘ η^p(v) (v ∈ V ⊗_Q A^{∞,p}) coincides with η^{p⋆}. Two decuples are equivalent if there are prime-to-p O_F-linear quasi-isogenies φ₀: A₀ → A₀′, φ: A → A′, φ^⋆: A^⋆ → A^{⋆′} with φ₀ carrying η₀^p to η₀^{p′}; some c ∈ Z_(p)^× with φ₀^∨λ₀′φ₀ = cλ₀, φ^∨λ′φ = cλ, φ^{⋆∨}λ^{⋆′}φ^⋆ = cλ^⋆; the K^p-orbits of v ↦ φ_* ∘ η^p(v) ∘ (φ_{0*})⁻¹ and v ↦ φ^⋆_* ∘ η^{p⋆}(v) ∘ (φ_{0*})⁻¹ equal η^{p′} and η^{p⋆′}; and φ^⋆ ∘ α = α′ ∘ φ. A morphism g of 𝔎(V)^p changes η^p, η^{p⋆} to η^p ∘ g, η^{p⋆} ∘ g; a morphism a of 𝔗 changes η₀^p to η₀^p ∘ a.
items.note: Printed with two slips: the double coset is written in U(V)(A_F^{∞,p}) (for A^{∞,p}_{F⁺}), and the 𝔗-action is said to act 'on M_𝔭(V, K^p)(S)' (for B_𝔭(V, K^p)(S)) — source issues (misprints). The conditions imply that ᾰ := ϖα⁻¹: A^⋆ → A is a quasi-p-isogeny with ker ᾰ[p^∞] ⊆ A^⋆[𝔭], ϖλ^⋆ = ᾰ^∨λᾰ and the orbit of ϖ⁻¹ᾰ_*η^{p⋆} equal to η^p (proof of Theorem 4.3.5, (a′)–(c′)). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 4.3.4 — the basic correspondence (4.3)
items.statement: The forgetful maps give a correspondence S_𝔭(V, −) ←π− B_𝔭(V, −) −ι→ M_𝔭(V, −) (4.3) in Fun(𝔎(V)^p × 𝔗, PSch′_{/F_p^Φ})_{/T_𝔭}, where π forgets (A, λ, η^p; α) and ι forgets (A^⋆, λ^⋆, η^{p⋆}; α). (4.3) is called the basic correspondence on M_𝔭(V, −), and S_𝔭(V, −) its source.
items.note: Footnote 13: the image of ι is the basic locus of M_𝔭(V, −) (asserted, not proved here). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 4.3.5(1) — the fibres B_{s⋆} are smooth, with tangent bundle Hom(ω, ker α_*/ω)
items.statement: In (4.3), take s^⋆ = (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A^⋆, λ^⋆, η^{p⋆}) ∈ S_𝔭(V, K^p)(κ), κ a field containing F_p^Φ, put B_{s⋆} := π⁻¹(s^⋆), and let (𝒜, λ, η^p; α) be the universal object over B_{s⋆}. Then B_{s⋆} is a smooth scheme over κ, with a canonical isomorphism T_{B_{s⋆}/κ} ≃ ℋom(ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞}, ker α_{*,τ_∞}/ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞}), where α_{*,τ_∞}: H₁^dR(𝒜)_{τ_∞} → H₁^dR(A^⋆)_{τ_∞} (note ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞} ⊆ ker α_{*,τ_∞} because ω_{A^{⋆∨},τ_∞} = 0).
items.note: Proof via Serre–Tate/Grothendieck–Messing (Proposition 3.4.8): lifting x over a square-zero PD thickening is lifting α and ᾰ, i.e. lifting ω_{τ_∞} (rank 1) and ω_{τ_∞^c} (rank N − 1) subject to orthogonality and ᾰ_{*,τ_∞^c}H^cris(A^⋆)_{τ_∞^c} ⊆ ω̂_{τ_∞^c}; by (b′) this is equivalent to ω̂_{τ_∞} ⊆ ker α_{*,τ_∞}, giving a torsor under Hom(ω, (ker α_*/ω) ⊗ I). Rank of ker α_{*,τ_∞} is ⌈N/2⌉ (Lemma 3.4.12), so the tangent bundle has rank ⌊(N−1)/2⌋. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 4.3.5(2) — ι|B_{s⋆} is (locally) a closed immersion with normal bundle Hom(ω, im α_*)
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 4.3.5, the restriction of ι to B_{s⋆} is locally on B_{s⋆} a closed immersion, with a canonical isomorphism for its normal bundle N_{ι|B_{s⋆}} ≃ ℋom(ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞}, im α_{*,τ_∞}) (a bundle of rank ⌊N/2⌋, since ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞} has rank 1 and im α_{*,τ_∞} ≅ ker ᾰ_{*,τ_∞} has rank ⌊N/2⌋).
items.note: Proof: by Theorem 4.2.3, ι^*T_{M/κ}|_{B_{s⋆}} ≃ Hom(ω, H₁^dR(𝒜)_{τ_∞}/ω), and T_{B_{s⋆}} → ι^*T_M is the injection Hom(ω, ker α_*/ω) → Hom(ω, H₁^dR/ω) with cokernel Hom(ω, H₁^dR/ker α_*) ≅ Hom(ω, im α_*). This proves only that ι|B_{s⋆} is unramified (étale-locally a closed immersion). The Zariski-local reading (used in the proof of Proposition 4.5.5) is false whenever ι|B_{s⋆} is not injective on geometric points — e.g. for N = 3 whenever p + 1 exceeds |Sh(V^⋆, (iK^p)K^⋆_p)|, since the p + 1 components through a superspecial point then cannot come from p + 1 distinct points of S_𝔭 — because B_{s⋆} is irreducible and unibranch while its image is not (source issue). No later argument needs more than unramifiedness. For K^p small it is a closed immersion (Remark 4.3.6). Previous pass (G07) bundled (1) and (2); (1) is now thm-4-3-5-1. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 4.3.5(3) — B_{s⋆} ≅ DL_{s⋆}; dimension ⌊(N−1)/2⌋; ι of pure codimension ⌊N/2⌋
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 4.3.5, the assignment sending a point (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A, λ, η^p; A^⋆, λ^⋆, η^{p⋆}; α) ∈ B_{s⋆}(S), for S ∈ Sch′_{/κ}, to the subbundle H := (ᾰ_{*,τ_∞})⁻¹ ω_{A^∨/S,τ_∞} ⊆ H₁^dR(A^⋆/S)_{τ_∞} = H₁^dR(A^⋆/κ)_{τ_∞} ⊗_κ O_S = (𝒱_{s⋆})_S, where ᾰ: A^⋆ → A is the unique O_F-linear quasi-p-isogeny with ᾰ ∘ α = ϖ·id_A, induces an isomorphism ζ_{s⋆}: B_{s⋆} ⥲ DL_{s⋆} = DL(𝒱_{s⋆}, { , }_{s⋆}, ⌈(N+1)/2⌉). In particular B_{s⋆} is a geometrically irreducible projective smooth scheme in Sch_{/κ} of dimension ⌊(N−1)/2⌋ (by Lemma 4.3.2), and ι is of pure codimension ⌊N/2⌋.
items.note: Proof: Lemma 3.4.12(1,2,3) gives rank ker α_{*,τ_∞} = ⌈N/2⌉, rank ker ᾰ_{*,τ_∞} = ⌈(N−1)/2⌉, rank H = ⌈(N+1)/2⌉; F H^{(p)} = ker ᾰ_{*,τ_∞^c}; by Definition 4.3.3(b) ker ᾰ_{*,τ_∞} = im α_{*,τ_∞} ⊆ (ker ᾰ_{*,τ_∞^c})^⊥ = (FH^{(p)})^⊥ with equality by ranks (for N even this rank count uses ker λ^⋆_* ⊆ ker ᾰ_*, unstated), so H^⊣ = (FH^{(p)})^⊥ ⊆ H. Bijectivity on κ-points by the Dieudonné construction (item constr-dieudonne-inverse) and isomorphism on tangent spaces (H/(FH)^⊥ ≅ ω and H₁^dR(A^⋆)_{τ_∞}/H ≅ ker α_*/ω via ᾰ). Previous pass (G06) cited '(1,2)'; the content is part (3). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 4.3.5(3–1) — the Dieudonné lattice D_A attached to H ∈ DL_{s⋆}(κ)
items.statement: Let κ ⊇ F_p^Φ be perfect and y ∈ DL_{s⋆}(κ) given by H ⊆ 𝒱_{s⋆} = H₁^dR(A^⋆/κ)_{τ_∞} with (FH)^⊥ ⊆ H (F, V the sesquilinear maps of Notation 3.4.10). Let H̃ ⊆ 𝒟(A^⋆)_{τ_∞} be the preimage of H and H̃^c ⊆ 𝒟(A^⋆)_{τ_∞^c} the preimage of H^⊥ under 𝒟(A^⋆)_τ → 𝒟(A^⋆)_τ/p𝒟(A^⋆)_τ = H₁^dR(A^⋆)_τ. Put 𝒟_{A,τ} := 𝒟(A^⋆)_τ for τ ∉ {τ_∞, τ_∞^c}, 𝒟_{A,τ_∞} := V⁻¹H̃^c, 𝒟_{A,τ_∞^c} := FH̃, and 𝒟_A := ⊕_{τ∈Σ_∞} 𝒟_{A,τ}. Then 𝒟_A ⊆ 𝒟(A^⋆) is stable under F and V (FV⁻¹H̃^c ⊆ FH̃ as V⁻¹(H^⊥) = (FH)^⊥ ⊆ H; pFH̃ ⊆ H̃^c; H^⊥ ⊆ FH; pD ⊆ V⁻¹H̃^c), so there are an O_F-abelian variety A over κ with 𝒟(A)_τ = 𝒟_{A,τ} and an O_F-linear p-isogeny α: A → A^⋆ inducing 𝒟(A) ⊆ 𝒟(A^⋆), with ker α[p^∞] ⊆ A[𝔭] (as p𝒟(A^⋆) ⊆ 𝒟(A)); the quasi-polarization λ with ϖλ = α^∨ ∘ λ^⋆ ∘ α is p-principal (p⁻¹⟨ , ⟩_{λ^⋆,τ_∞} is perfect on 𝒟(A)_{τ_∞} × 𝒟(A)_{τ_∞^c}, since H̃ is W(κ)-dual to p⁻¹H̃^c and FH̃ is dual to p⁻¹V⁻¹H̃^c), A has signature type NΦ − τ_∞ + τ_∞^c (Lemma 3.4.12(2,3)), and with η^p forced by Definition 4.3.3(c) this gives the unique x ∈ B_{s⋆}(κ) with ζ_{s⋆}(x) = y.
items.note: Reused in the proof of Lemma 4.5.4 (p. 180: 'Under the notation in proof of Theorem 4.3.5'). For N even the pairing ⟨ , ⟩_{λ^⋆} is degenerate; the duality 'H̃ is W(κ)-dual to p⁻¹H̃^c' still holds because the kernel of the reduced pairing on the τ_∞ side lies in (FH)^⊥ ⊆ H (checked in this extraction). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Remark 4.3.6 — for small K^p, ι|B_{s⋆} is a closed immersion
items.statement: In Theorem 4.3.5, when K^p is sufficiently small, the restriction of ι to B_{s⋆} is a closed immersion for every point s^⋆ ∈ S_𝔭(V, K^p)(κ) and every field κ containing F_p^Φ.
items.note: No proof given. Since B_{s⋆} is projective and ι|B_{s⋆} unramified, this amounts to injectivity on geometric points; non-injectivity comes from self-quasi-isogenies of A^⋆ in the 𝔭-arithmetic group U(V^⋆)(F⁺) ∩ g^pK^p(g^p)⁻¹ moving the lattice 𝒟(A^⋆) to a neighbour, and shrinking K^p (for fixed p) excludes them. For fixed K^p and large p it does occur (see note to G07), so 'sufficiently small' depends on p. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 4.4.1 — definite uniformization datum (V^⋆, i, {Λ^⋆_𝔮}) for V at 𝔭
items.statement: A definite uniformization datum for V (at 𝔭) is a collection (V^⋆, i, {Λ^⋆_𝔮}_{𝔮|p}) where: V^⋆ is a standard definite hermitian space over F of rank N (signature (N, 0) at every archimedean place of F⁺); i: V ⊗_Q A^{∞,p} → V^⋆ ⊗_Q A^{∞,p} is an isometry; for every prime 𝔮 ≠ 𝔭 of F⁺ above p, Λ^⋆_𝔮 is a self-dual O_{F_𝔮}-lattice in V^⋆ ⊗_F F_𝔮; and Λ^⋆_𝔭 is an O_{F_𝔭}-lattice in V^⋆ ⊗_F F_𝔭 satisfying pΛ^⋆_𝔭 ⊆ (Λ^⋆_𝔭)^∨ with (Λ^⋆_𝔭)^∨/pΛ^⋆_𝔭 of length 0 if N is odd and of length 1 if N is even. By the Hasse principle for hermitian spaces such a datum exists; one is fixed. Let K^⋆_𝔮 be the stabilizer of Λ^⋆_𝔮 (𝔮 | p) and K^⋆_p := ∏_{𝔮|p} K^⋆_𝔮. The isometry i induces an equivalence of categories i: 𝔎(V)^p ⥲ 𝔎(V^⋆)^p.
items.note: Existence: V^⋆ must differ from V exactly at τ̲_∞ (signature) and at 𝔭 (the lattice type forces odd discriminant valuation, ε = −1, both for N odd — Λ^∨ = pΛ — and N even — [Λ^∨ : Λ] = 1 − N), an even number of places, so Landherr's theorem applies. For N odd K^⋆_𝔭 is hyperspecial (Λ^⋆_𝔭 self-dual for ϖ(,)); for N even U(V^⋆)_𝔭 is the non-quasi-split inner form and K^⋆_𝔭 is special maximal (Remark 4.4.8). Previous pass (G08) bundled this with Construction 4.4.2 (now constr-4-4-2). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

api.name: RankinSelberg.DefiniteUniformizationDatum.data
api.statement: Use the level-preserving finite Shimura-set identification.

api.name: RankinSelberg.DefiniteUniformizationDatum.characterisation
api.statement: The Galois action on the Shimura-set factor is trivial over the specified residue field.

api.name: RankinSelberg.DefiniteUniformizationDatum.compatibility
api.statement: Prime-to-p Hecke isogenies commute with this identification.

uses.how: Use the level-preserving finite Shimura-set identification.

items.name: Hasse principle for hermitian spaces (black box)
items.statement: Two hermitian spaces over the CM extension F/F⁺ of the same rank are isomorphic if and only if they are isomorphic at every place of F⁺; and a collection of local hermitian spaces (of fixed rank) is the localization of a global one if and only if almost all are the standard ones and the product of the local discriminant invariants is 1.
items.locator: used in Remark 4.2.5 (p. 162–163), Definition 4.4.1 (p. 171), Lemma 4.4.3 (p. 172); also §5.2, after Definition 5.2.6, published p. 192
items.note: Classical (Landherr); invoked without reference as 'the Hasse principle for hermitian spaces'. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Construction 4.4.2 — the uniformization map υ: S_𝔭(V, −)(F̄_p) → Sh(V^⋆, (i−)K^⋆_p) × T_𝔭(F̄_p)
items.statement: For s^⋆ = (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A^⋆, λ^⋆, η^{p⋆}) ∈ S_𝔭(V, K^p)(F̄_p) let V_{s⋆} := Hom_{O_F}(A₀, A^⋆) ⊗ Q with the pairing (x, y) := ϖ⁻¹ · λ₀⁻¹ ∘ y^∨ ∘ λ^⋆ ∘ x ∈ End_{O_F}(A₀) ⊗ Q = F (a hermitian space over F; note the factor ϖ⁻¹), and for 𝔮 | p let Λ_{s⋆,𝔮} := Hom_{O_F}(A₀[𝔮^∞], A^⋆[𝔮^∞]), an O_{F_𝔮}-lattice in (V_{s⋆})_𝔮 (A^⋆ is isogenous to A₀^N). Let ρ: V_{s⋆} ⊗_Q A^{∞,p} ⥲ Hom^{ϖλ₀,λ^⋆}_{F⊗A^{∞,p}}(H₁^ét(A₀, A^{∞,p}), H₁^ét(A^⋆, A^{∞,p})) be the natural isometry, choose an isometry η_rat: V_{s⋆} → V^⋆ (Lemma 4.4.3), put g^p := η_rat ∘ ρ⁻¹ ∘ η^{p⋆} ∘ i⁻¹ ∈ U(V^⋆)(A^{∞,p}_{F⁺}), choose g_𝔮 ∈ U(V^⋆)(F⁺_𝔮) with g_𝔮Λ^⋆_𝔮 = η_ratΛ_{s⋆,𝔮} for 𝔮 | p (Lemma 4.4.3(1,2)), and g_{s⋆} := (g^p, (g_𝔮)_{𝔮|p}) ∈ U(V^⋆)(A^∞_{F⁺}). The double coset U(V^⋆)(F⁺) g_{s⋆} (iK^p) K^⋆_p depends only on s^⋆, and υ(s^⋆) := (U(V^⋆)(F⁺) g_{s⋆} (iK^p) K^⋆_p, (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p)) ∈ Sh(V^⋆, (iK^p)K^⋆_p) × T_𝔭(F̄_p) (4.4), a morphism in Fun(𝔎(V)^p × 𝔗, Set)_{/T_𝔭(F̄_p)}. Here Sh(V^⋆, K) := U(V^⋆)(F⁺)\U(V^⋆)(A^∞_{F⁺})/K (§3.2).
items.note: Printed with U(V^⋆)(F) in place of U(V^⋆)(F⁺) (three times, pp. 172–173) and g in place of g_{s⋆} in the first double coset — source issue (misprint). The construction is non-canonical: it depends on the chosen definite uniformization datum. The script letter 𝒱_{s⋆} of §4.3 (a de Rham space) and the roman V_{s⋆} here (a rational hermitian space) are different objects. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 4.4.3 — V_{s⋆} ≅ V^⋆
items.statement: For s^⋆ ∈ S_𝔭(V, K^p)(F̄_p), the hermitian spaces V_{s⋆} (Construction 4.4.2) and V^⋆ are isomorphic.
items.note: Proof: by (1), (2) below and the Hasse principle it suffices that (i) V_{s⋆} is totally positive definite — 'the same argument as in [KR14, Lemma 2.7]' (black box, item kr-positivity) — and (ii) V_{s⋆} ⊗ A^{∞,p} ≅ V ⊗ A^{∞,p}: the natural map V_{s⋆} ⊗ A^{∞,p} → Hom^{ϖλ₀,λ^⋆}(H₁^ét(A₀), H₁^ét(A^⋆)) is injective between rank-N spaces and the target is isomorphic to V ⊗ A^{∞,p} via η^{p⋆}. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 4.4.3(1) — Λ_{s⋆,𝔮} is self-dual for 𝔮 ≠ 𝔭
items.statement: For every prime 𝔮 ≠ 𝔭 of F⁺ above p, the lattice Λ_{s⋆,𝔮} = Hom_{O_F}(A₀[𝔮^∞], A^⋆[𝔮^∞]) is self-dual (for the pairing (x, y) = ϖ⁻¹λ₀⁻¹y^∨λ^⋆x).
items.note: Proof: A^⋆[𝔮^∞] ≅ (A₀[𝔮^∞])^N with λ^⋆[𝔮^∞] principal, λ₀[𝔮^∞] principal and val_𝔮(ϖ) = 0. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 4.4.3(2) — the type of Λ_{s⋆,𝔭}
items.statement: The lattice Λ_{s⋆,𝔭} = Hom_{O_F}(A₀[𝔭^∞], A^⋆[𝔭^∞]) satisfies pΛ_{s⋆,𝔭} ⊆ (Λ_{s⋆,𝔭})^∨, and (Λ_{s⋆,𝔭})^∨/pΛ_{s⋆,𝔭} has length 0 if N is odd and length 1 if N is even (duals for the pairing (x, y) = ϖ⁻¹λ₀⁻¹y^∨λ^⋆x).
items.note: Proof: A^⋆[𝔭^∞] ≅ (A₀[𝔭^∞])^N with ker λ^⋆[𝔭^∞] trivial (N odd) or contained in A^⋆[𝔭] of rank p² (N even), λ₀[𝔭^∞] principal, val_𝔭(ϖ) = 1. So Λ_{s⋆,𝔮} has the same type as Λ^⋆_𝔮 of Definition 4.4.1. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: [KR14, Lemma 2.7] — positivity of Hom(A₀, A^⋆) ⊗ Q (black box)
items.statement: For s^⋆ ∈ S_𝔭(V, K^p)(F̄_p), the hermitian space V_{s⋆} = Hom_{O_F}(A₀, A^⋆) ⊗ Q with (x, y) = ϖ⁻¹λ₀⁻¹ y^∨ λ^⋆ x is totally positive definite.
items.note: Cited, not proved: 'it follows from the same argument in [KR14, Lemma 2.7]' (positivity of the Rosati involution; ϖ is totally positive). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proposition 4.4.4 (first assertion) — the uniformization map υ is bijective
items.statement: The uniformization map υ: S_𝔭(V, −)(F̄_p) → Sh(V^⋆, (i−)K^⋆_p) × T_𝔭(F̄_p) of (4.4) is an isomorphism in Fun(𝔎(V)^p × 𝔗, Set)_{/T_𝔭(F̄_p)}.
items.note: Proof: fibrewise over t = (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p) ∈ T_𝔭(F̄_p). Injectivity 'follows directly from the definition' (it uses the equivalence A^⋆ ↦ Hom_{O_F}(A₀, A^⋆) with O_F-hermitian lattices, inverse Λ ↦ A₀ ⊗_{O_F} Λ). Surjectivity: for g ∈ U(V^⋆)(A^{∞,p}_{F⁺}) take a lattice Λ^⋆ ⊆ V^⋆, A^⋆ := A₀ ⊗_{O_F} Λ^⋆ with the quasi-polarization making V^⋆ ⊗ A^{∞,p} ≃ Hom(H₁^ét(A₀), H₁^ét(A^⋆)) an isometry, and η^{p⋆} := (the identification) ∘ g ∘ i. The printed lattice condition 'Λ^⋆ ⊗_F F_𝔭 = Λ^⋆_𝔭' must be read as Λ^⋆ ⊗_{O_F} O_{F_𝔮} = Λ^⋆_𝔮 for all 𝔮 | p (source issue). Restricting to g with trivial p-component uses weak approximation for U(V^⋆) at the places above p (unstated). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proposition 4.4.4 (second assertion) — Galois acts through T_𝔭(F̄_p)
items.statement: The action of Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ) on the target Sh(V^⋆, (i−)K^⋆_p) × T_𝔭(F̄_p) of υ induced via the isomorphism υ factors through the projection Sh(V^⋆, (i−)K^⋆_p) × T_𝔭(F̄_p) → T_𝔭(F̄_p); i.e. it is trivial on the first factor.
items.note: Proof: for ς ∈ Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ), ςs^⋆ is the ς-twist (A₀^ς, …; A^{⋆ς}, …), V_{ςs⋆} = Hom(A₀^ς, A^{⋆ς}) ⊗ Q ≃ V_{s⋆} canonically and g_{s⋆} = g_{ςs⋆}. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Construction 4.4.5 — Hecke correspondences Hk_g on S_𝔭(V, −) at 𝔭
items.statement: For g ∈ K^⋆_𝔭\U(V^⋆)(F⁺_𝔭)/K^⋆_𝔭 define S_𝔭(V, −)_g: 𝔎(V)^p × 𝔗 → PSch′_{/F_p^Φ}, where S_𝔭(V, K^p)_g(S) is the set of equivalence classes of decuples (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A^⋆, λ^⋆, η^{p⋆}; A^⋆_g, λ^⋆_g, η_g^{p⋆}; φ^⋆) with (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A^⋆, λ^⋆, η^{p⋆}) and (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A^⋆_g, λ^⋆_g, η_g^{p⋆}) in S_𝔭(V, K^p)(S) and φ^⋆: A^⋆ → A^⋆_g an O_F-linear quasi-isogeny such that (a) φ^{⋆∨} ∘ λ^⋆_g ∘ φ^⋆ = λ^⋆; (b) φ^⋆[𝔭^∞]: A^⋆[𝔭^∞] → A^⋆_g[𝔭^∞] is a quasi-isogeny of height zero under which the lattices Hom_{O_F}(A_{0s}[𝔭^∞], A^⋆_s[𝔭^∞]) and Hom_{O_F}(A_{0s}[𝔭^∞], A^⋆_{g,s}[𝔭^∞]) are in the relative position determined by g, for every geometric point s of S; (c) φ^⋆[𝔮^∞] is an isomorphism for every prime 𝔮 ≠ 𝔭 of F⁺ above p; (d) the K^p-orbit of v ↦ φ^⋆_* ∘ η^{p⋆}(v) coincides with η_g^{p⋆}. Equivalences and morphisms as in Definition 4.3.3. The Hecke correspondence of g is Hk_g: S_𝔭(V, −)_g → S_𝔭(V, −) × S_𝔭(V, −) (4.5) in Fun(𝔎(V)^p × 𝔗, PSch′_{/F_p^Φ})_{/T_𝔭}, sending the decuple to the pair of sextuples; the product is taken over T_𝔭 (K^p ↦ S_𝔭(V, K^p) ×_{T_𝔭} S_𝔭(V, K^p), 𝔗 acting diagonally).
items.note: The relative position of two O_{F_𝔭}-lattices in the hermitian space V^⋆ ⊗ F_𝔭 is an element of K^⋆_𝔭\U(V^⋆)(F⁺_𝔭)/K^⋆_𝔭. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proposition 4.4.6(1) — Hk_g is finite étale
items.statement: For every g ∈ K^⋆_𝔭\U(V^⋆)(F⁺_𝔭)/K^⋆_𝔭, the morphism Hk_g (4.5) is finite étale; in particular it is a morphism in Fun(𝔎(V)^p × 𝔗, Sch_{/F_p^Φ})_{/T_𝔭}.
items.note: Proof: reduce to K^p sufficiently small; then Hk_g: S_𝔭(V, K^p)_g → S_𝔭(V, K^p) ×_{T_𝔭} S_𝔭(V, K^p) is closed, hence represented by a finite étale scheme (target finite étale over T_𝔭). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proposition 4.4.6(2) — υ intertwines Hk_g with the set-theoretic Hecke correspondence
items.statement: The uniformization map υ (4.4) lifts uniquely to an isomorphism S_𝔭(V, −)_g(F̄_p) ⥲ Sh(V^⋆, (i−)(gK^⋆_p g⁻¹ ∩ K^⋆_p)) × T_𝔭(F̄_p) making the square with left side Hk_g(F̄_p): S_𝔭(V, −)_g(F̄_p) → S_𝔭(V, −)(F̄_p) ×_{T_𝔭(F̄_p)} S_𝔭(V, −)(F̄_p), bottom υ × υ, and right side (the set-theoretic Hecke correspondence of g) Sh(V^⋆, (i−)(gK^⋆_p g⁻¹ ∩ K^⋆_p)) → Sh(V^⋆, (i−)K^⋆_p) × Sh(V^⋆, (i−)K^⋆_p) (times T_𝔭(F̄_p)) commute in Fun(𝔎(V)^p × 𝔗, Set)_{/T_𝔭(F̄_p)}.
items.note: 'Follows directly from the definition.' Here g ∈ U(V^⋆)(F⁺_𝔭) is placed in the 𝔭-component. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Remark 4.4.7 — Hk_g is a local isomorphism
items.statement: The proof of Proposition 4.4.6(1) together with Proposition 4.4.4 implies that Hk_g is a local isomorphism.
items.note: As printed; presumably each of the two projections S_𝔭(V, −)_g → S_𝔭(V, −) is finite étale (both sides finite étale over T_𝔭). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Remark 4.4.8 — the local Hecke algebra at 𝔭 on the definite side
items.statement: K^⋆_𝔭 is a special maximal open compact subgroup of U(V^⋆)(F⁺_𝔭), so Z[K^⋆_𝔭\U(V^⋆)(F⁺_𝔭)/K^⋆_𝔭] is commutative. When N is odd, Λ^⋆_𝔭 is self-dual for the pairing ϖ·( , )_{V^⋆}, hence Z[K^⋆_𝔭\U(V^⋆)(F⁺_𝔭)/K^⋆_𝔭] is canonically isomorphic to the spherical Hecke algebra T_{N,𝔭} = Z[U_{N,𝔭}(O_{F⁺_𝔭})\U_{N,𝔭}(F⁺_𝔭)/U_{N,𝔭}(O_{F⁺_𝔭})] of §3.1.
items.note: Printed as 'Λ_{s⋆,𝔭} is a self-dual lattice under ϖ·( , )_{V⋆}'; Λ^⋆_𝔭 is meant (source issue, misprint). Via Proposition 4.4.6, S_𝔭(V, −) and hence L[Sh(V^⋆, (i−)K^⋆_p)] carry actions of this algebra. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: L[Sh(V^⋆, (i−)K^⋆_p)] ≃ H⁰_𝔗(S̄_𝔭(V, −), L) = H⁰_𝔗(S_𝔭(V, −), L)
items.statement: Let L be a p-coprime coefficient ring. The uniformization map (4.4) induces an isomorphism L[Sh(V^⋆, (i−)K^⋆_p)] ≃ H⁰_𝔗(S̄_𝔭(V, −), L) = H⁰_𝔗(S_𝔭(V, −), L) in Fun(𝔎(V)^p, Mod(L[K^⋆_𝔭\U(V^⋆ ⊗_F F_𝔭)/K^⋆_𝔭])), the Hecke action on the right being through the correspondences Hk_g (Proposition 4.4.6).
items.note: From Propositions 4.4.4 and 4.4.6: T_𝔭(F̄_p) is a torsor under the group of 𝔗 and Galois acts through that factor, so 𝔗-invariant functions on S_𝔭(F̄_p) = Sh × T_𝔭(F̄_p) are functions on Sh and are Galois-invariant. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Construction 4.4.9 — the incidence maps inc^⋆_! and inc^*_⋆
items.statement: Put r := ⌊N/2⌋ ⩾ 0. Define, in Fun(𝔎(V)^p, Mod(L)), inc^⋆_!: L[Sh(V^⋆, (i−)K^⋆_p)] ⥲ H⁰_𝔗(S_𝔭(V, −), L) −π^*→ H⁰_𝔗(B_𝔭(V, −), L) −ι_!→ H^{2r}_𝔗(M_𝔭(V, −), L(r)), and inc^*_⋆: H^{2(N−r−1)}_𝔗(M_𝔭(V, −), L(N−r−1)) −ι^*→ H^{2(N−r−1)}_𝔗(B_𝔭(V, −), L(N−r−1)) −π_!→ H⁰_𝔗(S_𝔭(V, −), L) ⥲ L[Sh(V^⋆, (i−)K^⋆_p)], where ι_! is the Gysin map of ι (pure codimension r, Theorem 4.3.5(3)) and π_! is the trace map of the smooth proper π (fibres of dimension ⌊(N−1)/2⌋ = N − r − 1). The two maps are essentially Poincaré dual to each other.
items.note: M_𝔭 etc. are special fibres over F_p^Φ. Degrees: 2r + 2(N − r − 1) = 2(N − 1) = 2 dim M_𝔭; for N = 2r + 1 both are 2r, so inc^*_⋆ ∘ inc^⋆_! is defined. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

api.name: RankinSelberg.SmoothIncidenceMaps.data
api.statement: Use the pull–push maps between finite Shimura functions and cohomology.

api.name: RankinSelberg.SmoothIncidenceMaps.characterisation
api.statement: The two maps are adjoint under finite-function and Poincaré pairings.

api.name: RankinSelberg.SmoothIncidenceMaps.compatibility
api.statement: Hecke correspondences and level transitions commute with both maps.

uses.how: Use the pull–push maps between finite Shimura functions and cohomology.

items.name: The Hecke operator T^⋆_{N,𝔭} (N = 2r + 1) and the numbers d_{r,q}
items.statement: For N = 2r + 1 odd, T^⋆_{N,𝔭} := Σ_{δ=0}^{r} d_{r−δ,p} · T_{N,𝔭;δ} ∈ T_{N,𝔭}, where for s ⩾ 0 and q ∈ N, d_{s,q} := Σ_{δ=0}^{s} (−1)^δ (2δ + 1) q^{δ(δ+1)} [2s+1 choose s−δ]_{−q} (Gaussian binomial [n choose m]_q = [n]_q!/([n−m]_q! [m]_q!), [n]_q = (q^n − 1)/(q − 1), evaluated at −q) (Notation 1.3.1), and T_{N,𝔭;δ} ∈ T_{N,𝔭} is the characteristic function of K ϖ^{t_δ} K for t_δ = (1^δ, 0^{N−2δ}, (−1)^δ), K the hyperspecial stabilizer of the standard self-dual lattice (Notation B.2.1, written there T°_{N;δ}).
items.locator: §4.4, Theorem 4.4.10, p. 176 (with Notation 1.3.1, p. 119, and Notation B.2.1, p. 335)
items.note: Examples: d_{0,q} = 1; d_{1,q} = 1 − q − 2q². So T^⋆_{1,𝔭} = 1 and T^⋆_{3,𝔭} = T_{3,𝔭;1} + (1 − p − 2p²). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Theorem 4.4.10 — inc^*_⋆ ∘ inc^⋆_! = T^⋆_{N,𝔭} for N odd
items.statement: Suppose N = 2r + 1 is odd with r ⩾ 0. Then the composite map inc^*_⋆ ∘ inc^⋆_!: L[Sh(V^⋆, (i−)K^⋆_p)] → L[Sh(V^⋆, (i−)K^⋆_p)] is equal to the action of the Hecke operator T^⋆_{N,𝔭} = Σ_{δ=0}^{r} d_{r−δ,p} · T_{N,𝔭;δ} ∈ T_{N,𝔭} (item def-hecke-T-star), L[Sh(V^⋆, (i−)K^⋆_p)] being a T_{N,𝔭}-module by Remark 4.4.8.
items.note: Cited, not proved: 'This is [XZ, Theorem 9.3.5]' (Xiao–Zhu, preprint). Consistency check in this extraction for N = 3: the diagonal coefficient d_{1,p} = 1 − p − 2p² equals the self-intersection of a Deligne–Lusztig curve C = B_{s⋆} in the surface M_𝔭: by Theorem 4.3.5(2),(3) the normal bundle is Hom(ℋ/ℋ^⊣, ℋ^⊣) ≅ O(p−1)^∨ ⊗ O(−p) = O(1 − 2p) on the degree-(p+1) curve C ⊆ P², of degree (1 − 2p)(p + 1) = 1 − p − 2p². Previous pass called this 'Proposition 4.4.10'. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §4.5 — the data (V_n, V_{n+1}) and the category 𝔎(V_n)^p_sp
items.statement: Start from a datum (V_n, {Λ_{n,𝔮}}_{𝔮|p}) as in §4.2 with V_n standard indefinite of rank n ⩾ 1, and put (V_{n+1}, {Λ_{n+1,𝔮}}_{𝔮|p}) := ((V_n)_♯, {(Λ_{n,𝔮})_♯}_{𝔮|p}), of rank n + 1, where W_♯ := W ⊕ O_F·1 with (1, 1) = 1 (Definition 3.1.7). For N ∈ {n, n+1} let K_{N,𝔮} be the stabilizer of Λ_{N,𝔮} and K_{N,p} := ∏_{𝔮|p} K_{N,𝔮}. 𝔎(V_n)^p_sp (Definition 3.1.11(3)) is the category of pairs K = (K_♭, K_♯) with K_♭ ∈ 𝔎(V_n)^p, K_♯ ∈ 𝔎(V_{n+1})^p and K_♭ ⊆ K_♯ ∩ U(V_n)(A^{∞,p}_{F⁺}), a morphism K → K′ being g ∈ K_♭\U(V_n)(A^{∞,p}_{F⁺})/K′_♭ with g⁻¹K_♭g ⊆ K′_♭ and g⁻¹K_♯g ⊆ K′_♯; −_n := −_♭ and −_{n+1} := −_♯ are the two forgetful functors.
items.note: Five 'stages of functoriality' follow: Shimura varieties (4.6), smooth moduli (4.7)/(4.8), basic correspondences (4.9), Deligne–Lusztig fibres (Proposition 4.5.6), Shimura sets (Proposition 4.5.9). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: (4.6) — the special morphism of Shimura varieties sh_↑
items.statement: The canonical inclusions V_n ↪ V_{n+1} and Λ_{n,𝔮} ↪ Λ_{n+1,𝔮} (𝔮 | p) induce a morphism sh_↑: Sh(V_n, −_n K_{n,p}) → Sh(V_{n+1}, −_{n+1} K_{n+1,p}) (4.6) in Fun(𝔎(V_n)^p_sp, Sch_{/F}), called the special morphism.
items.note: Defined since K_♭K_{n,p} ⊆ K_♯K_{n+1,p} ∩ U(V_n)(A^∞_{F⁺}). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: (4.7)–(4.8) — the special morphism m_↑ of smooth moduli schemes, adjoining the CM factor
items.statement: There is a morphism m_↑: M_𝔭(V_n, −_n) → M_𝔭(V_{n+1}, −_{n+1}) (4.7) in Fun(𝔎(V_n)^p_sp × 𝔗, Sch_{/Z_p^Φ})_{/T_𝔭} sending (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A, λ, η^p) ∈ M_𝔭(V_n, K_n^p)(S) to (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A × A₀, λ × λ₀, η^p ⊕ (id_{A₀})_*) ∈ M_𝔭(V_{n+1}, K_{n+1}^p)(S), where η^p ⊕ (id_{A₀})_* sends the norm-one vector 1 to (id_{A₀})_*. Its generic fibre is compatible with sh_↑ under (4.2): the square with top (4.2): M^η_𝔭(V_{n+1}, −_{n+1}) → Sh(V_{n+1}, −_{n+1}K_{n+1,p}) ×_{Spec F} T^η_𝔭, bottom (4.2) for V_n, left m^η_↑ and right sh_↑ × id commutes (4.8) in Fun(𝔎(V_n)^p_sp × 𝔗, Sch_{/Q_p^Φ})_{/T^η_𝔭}.
items.note: Previous pass (G46) bundled this with Definitions 4.5.1/4.5.3, Lemma 4.5.4 and with §5.10 (Constructions 5.10.1–5.10.11, outside these pages); here G46 is restricted to (4.7)–(4.8); the others have their own items. λ × λ₀ is p-principal and A × A₀ has signature (n+1)Φ − τ_∞ + τ_∞^c, so m_↑ is well defined. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

api.name: RankinSelberg.SpecialMorphismsAdjoiningTheCmFactor.data
api.statement: Retain maps on all three strata and the auxiliary level object Ksp.

api.name: RankinSelberg.SpecialMorphismsAdjoiningTheCmFactor.characterisation
api.statement: The smooth basic square is Cartesian when n is even; the semistable ground square is Cartesian when n is odd.

api.name: RankinSelberg.SpecialMorphismsAdjoiningTheCmFactor.compatibility
api.statement: The other parity must use the stated special DL morphism and finite degree p+1, not a false Cartesian square.

uses.how: Retain maps on all three strata and the auxiliary level object Ksp.

items.name: Definition 4.5.1 — S_𝔭(V_n, −)_sp and the maps s_↓, s_↑
items.statement: Define S_𝔭(V_n, −)_sp: 𝔎(V_n)^p_sp × 𝔗 → PSch′_{/F_p^Φ}, where for S ∈ Sch′_{/F_p^Φ}, S_𝔭(V_n, K^p)_sp(S) is the set of equivalence classes of decuples (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A^⋆, λ^⋆, η^{p⋆}; A^⋆_♮, λ^⋆_♮, η_♮^{p⋆}; δ^⋆) with (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A^⋆, λ^⋆, η^{p⋆}) ∈ S_𝔭(V_n, K_n^p)(S), (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A^⋆_♮, λ^⋆_♮, η_♮^{p⋆}) ∈ S_𝔭(V_{n+1}, K^p_{n+1})(S), and δ^⋆: A^⋆ × A₀ → A^⋆_♮ an O_F-linear quasi-p-isogeny (Definition 3.4.5) such that (a) ker δ^⋆[p^∞] ⊆ (A^⋆ × A₀)[𝔭]; (b) λ^⋆ × ϖλ₀ = δ^{⋆∨} ∘ λ^⋆_♮ ∘ δ^⋆; (c) the K^p_{n+1}-orbit of v ↦ δ^⋆_* ∘ (η^{p⋆} ⊕ (id_{A₀})_*)(v), v ∈ V_{n+1} ⊗_Q A^{∞,p}, coincides with η_♮^{p⋆}. Equivalence and morphisms as in Definition 4.3.3. The forgetful morphism S_𝔭(V_n, −)_sp → T_𝔭 is represented by finite étale schemes, and there are forgetful morphisms s_↓: S_𝔭(V_n, −)_sp → S_𝔭(V_n, −_n) and s_↑: S_𝔭(V_n, −)_sp → S_𝔭(V_{n+1}, −_{n+1}) in Fun(𝔎(V_n)^p_sp × 𝔗, Sch_{/F_p^Φ})_{/T_𝔭}.
items.note: Here K_n^p = (K^p)_♭ and K_{n+1}^p = (K^p)_♯. Finite étaleness over T_𝔭 is asserted ('which is represented by finite and étale schemes'). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 4.5.2(1) — for n odd, s_↓ is an isomorphism and s_↑ ∘ s_↓⁻¹ adjoins (A₀, ϖλ₀)
items.statement: When n is odd, s_↓: S_𝔭(V_n, −)_sp → S_𝔭(V_n, −_n) is an isomorphism, and s_↑ ∘ s_↓⁻¹: S_𝔭(V_n, −_n) → S_𝔭(V_{n+1}, −_{n+1}) is given by (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A^⋆, λ^⋆, η^{p⋆}) ↦ (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A^⋆ × A₀, λ^⋆ × ϖλ₀, η^{p⋆} × (id_{A₀})_*).
items.note: Proof: the fibre of s_↓ over x consists of the single point with δ^⋆ = id: for n odd, λ^⋆ is p-principal, ker(ϖλ₀)[p^∞] = A₀[𝔭] has rank p² and λ^⋆_♮ has kernel of rank p² (n + 1 even), so the degree identity in Definition 4.5.1(b) forces δ^⋆ to be an isomorphism at p. The proof writes the level structure as 'η^{p⋆} × η₀^p' (twice) where η^{p⋆} ⊕ (id_{A₀})_* is meant (source issue, misprint). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 4.5.2(2) — for n even, s_↓ is finite étale of degree p + 1
items.statement: When n is even, s_↓: S_𝔭(V_n, −)_sp → S_𝔭(V_n, −_n) is finite étale of degree p + 1.
items.note: Proof: over a point x ∈ S_𝔭(V_n, K_n^p)(κ) (κ perfect), a point of the fibre is determined by δ^⋆, hence by a totally isotropic (O_F/𝔭)-subgroup of ker(λ^⋆ × ϖλ₀) of order p². With 𝒲_x := 𝒟(A^⋆ × A₀)^∨_{τ_∞^c}/𝒟(A^⋆ × A₀)_{τ_∞} (dual w.r.t. λ^⋆ × ϖλ₀; a 2-dimensional κ-space with non-degenerate induced hermitian pairing, admissible with 𝒲_{x,0} := 𝒲_x^{V⁻¹F=1}, a 2-dimensional F_{p²}-space), Dieudonné theory identifies such subgroups with isotropic F_{p²}-lines in 𝒲_{x,0}; there are p + 1 of them. Étaleness because both sides are finite étale over T_𝔭. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 4.5.3 — B_𝔭(V_n, −)_sp as a fibre product
items.statement: B_𝔭(V_n, −)_sp is defined by the Cartesian square B_𝔭(V_n, −)_sp = S_𝔭(V_n, −)_sp ×_{s_↓, S_𝔭(V_n, −_n), π_n} B_𝔭(V_n, −_n), with projections π_sp: B_𝔭(V_n, −)_sp → S_𝔭(V_n, −)_sp and b_↓: B_𝔭(V_n, −)_sp → B_𝔭(V_n, −_n), in Fun(𝔎(V_n)^p_sp × 𝔗, Sch_{/F_p^Φ})_{/T_𝔭}.
items.note: Its S-points are pairs of a decuple of B_𝔭(V_n, K_n^p)(S) and a decuple of S_𝔭(V_n, K^p)_sp(S) sharing (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A^⋆, λ^⋆, η^{p⋆}). b_↓ is finite étale (base change of s_↓). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 4.5.4 — the morphism b_↑: B_𝔭(V_n, −)_sp → B_𝔭(V_{n+1}, −_{n+1})
items.statement: The assignment sending an object ((A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A, λ, η^p; A^⋆, λ^⋆, η^{p⋆}; α), (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A^⋆, λ^⋆, η^{p⋆}; A^⋆_♮, λ^⋆_♮, η_♮^{p⋆}; δ^⋆)) of B_𝔭(V_n, K^p)_sp(S) to (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A × A₀, λ × λ₀, η^p ⊕ (id_{A₀})_*; A^⋆_♮, λ^⋆_♮, η_♮^{p⋆}; δ^⋆ ∘ (α × id_{A₀})) (4.10) defines a morphism b_↑: B_𝔭(V_n, −)_sp → B_𝔭(V_{n+1}, −_{n+1}) in Fun(𝔎(V_n)^p_sp × 𝔗, Sch_{/F_p^Φ})_{/T_𝔭}.
items.note: Only Definition 4.3.3(a) for α_♮ := δ^⋆ ∘ (α × id_{A₀}) is non-trivial ((b) holds as (α × id)^∨(λ^⋆ × ϖλ₀)(α × id) = ϖλ × ϖλ₀). On Dieudonné modules 𝒟(A^⋆_♮)_τ ⊆ 𝒟(A^⋆)^∨_{τ^c} ⊕ ϖ⁻¹𝒟(A₀)_τ, so it suffices that p𝒟(A^⋆)^∨_{τ^c} ⊆ 𝒟(A)_τ; for τ ∈ {τ_∞, τ_∞^c} this follows from (FH)^⊥ ⊆ H via the lattices H̃, H̃^c of the proof of Theorem 4.3.5 (constr-dieudonne-inverse). The printed 'p𝒟̃(A^⋆)^∨_{τ_∞}' has a stray tilde (source issue). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: (4.9) — compatibility of the basic correspondences for V_n and V_{n+1}
items.statement: Lemma 4.5.4 yields the commutative diagram (4.9) in Fun(𝔎(V_n)^p_sp × 𝔗, Sch_{/F_p^Φ})_{/T_𝔭}: top row S_𝔭(V_{n+1}, −_{n+1}) ←π_{n+1}− B_𝔭(V_{n+1}, −_{n+1}) −ι_{n+1}→ M_𝔭(V_{n+1}, −_{n+1}); middle row S_𝔭(V_n, −)_sp ←π_sp− B_𝔭(V_n, −)_sp; bottom row S_𝔭(V_n, −_n) ←π_n− B_𝔭(V_n, −_n) −ι_n→ M_𝔭(V_n, −_n); vertical maps s_↑, s_↓ (left), b_↑, b_↓ (middle) and m_↑: M_𝔭(V_n, −_n) → M_𝔭(V_{n+1}, −_{n+1}) (right); i.e. π_{n+1} ∘ b_↑ = s_↑ ∘ π_sp and ι_{n+1} ∘ b_↑ = m_↑ ∘ ι_n ∘ b_↓. The lower-left square is Cartesian (Definition 4.5.3); the lower and upper rows are the basic correspondences (Definition 4.3.4) for V_n and V_{n+1}.
items.locator: §4.5, (4.9) (p. 177) and 'By the above lemma, we obtain our desired diagram (4.9)' (p. 180)
items.note: Commutativity is immediate from the formulas (4.10) and (4.7). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proposition 4.5.5 — for n even, B_sp = B_𝔭(V_{n+1}) ×_{M_𝔭(V_{n+1})} M_𝔭(V_n)
items.statement: When n is even, the square with top ι_{n+1}: B_𝔭(V_{n+1}, −_{n+1}) → M_𝔭(V_{n+1}, −_{n+1}), bottom ι_n ∘ b_↓: B_𝔭(V_n, −)_sp → M_𝔭(V_n, −_n), left b_↑ and right m_↑, extracted from (4.9), is Cartesian; i.e. ι_sp: B_𝔭(V_n, −)_sp → B_𝔭(V_{n+1}, −_{n+1}) ×_{M_𝔭(V_{n+1}, −_{n+1})} M_𝔭(V_n, −_n) is an isomorphism. (The authors remark that this is not correct on the nose when n is odd and at least 3.)
items.note: Proof: (1) bijectivity on κ-points (κ algebraically closed) by constructing A^⋆ from a point (A; A^⋆_♮, α_♮) of the target via 𝒟_{A⋆,τ} := 𝒟(A^⋆_♮)_τ ∩ p⁻¹𝒟(A)_τ for τ ∈ {τ_∞, τ_∞^c} (and 𝒟(A)_τ otherwise), with auxiliary facts (1–3) surjectivity of 𝒟(A^⋆_♮)_τ → p⁻¹𝒟(A₀)_τ and (1–4) coker(𝒟(A^⋆)_τ ⊕ 𝒟(A₀)_τ ⊆ 𝒟(A^⋆_♮)_τ) ≅ κ, giving (1–1) signature nΦ and (1–2) ker λ^⋆[p^∞] ⊆ A^⋆[𝔭] of degree p²; (2) the tangent square (4.11) is Cartesian because ker α_{♮*,τ_∞} ∩ H₁^dR(A)_{τ_∞} = ker α_{*,τ_∞}. The opening reduction asserts that ι_sp is Zariski-locally a closed immersion 'such that both the source and the target are smooth'; only the source is known to be smooth, and Theorem 4.3.5(2) only gives unramifiedness (its Zariski reading fails in general) — the reduction nevertheless holds since an unramified morphism from a smooth scheme that is bijective on geometric points and on tangent spaces is an isomorphism (source issues). In (1–3) the step 'for both τ' uses M_{τ_∞^c} = F M_{τ_∞} (signature (n+1)Φ of A^⋆_♮), unstated; in (1–1) 'F: 𝒟(A^⋆)_τ → 𝒟(A^⋆)_{τ^c}' should read 𝒟(A^⋆)_{στ} and '(1.4)' should read (1–4) (source issue). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Fourth stage — the special morphism δ_{s⋆↑} of Deligne–Lusztig varieties
items.statement: Take s^⋆ = (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A^⋆, λ^⋆, η^{p⋆}; A^⋆_♮, λ^⋆_♮, η_♮^{p⋆}; δ^⋆) ∈ S_𝔭(V_n, K^p)_sp(κ), κ ⊇ F_p^Φ a field; put s^⋆_n := s_↓(s^⋆), s^⋆_{n+1} := s_↑(s^⋆), and let B_{s⋆}, B_{s⋆_n}, B_{s⋆_{n+1}} be the fibres of π_sp, π_n, π_{n+1} (4.9). With the admissible pairs (𝒱_{s⋆_n}, { , }_{s⋆_n}) and (𝒱_{s⋆_{n+1}}, { , }_{s⋆_{n+1}}) of Lemma 4.3.2, extend the first to 𝒱_{s⋆_n,♯} := 𝒱_{s⋆_n} ⊕ κ·1 with {1, 1}_♯ = 0 (Construction A.1.6). Then δ^⋆: A^⋆ × A₀ → A^⋆_♮ induces a κ-linear map δ_{s⋆}: 𝒱_{s⋆_n,♯} → 𝒱_{s⋆_{n+1}} (via H₁^dR(A^⋆ × A₀)_{τ_∞} = 𝒱_{s⋆_n} ⊕ H₁^dR(A₀)_{τ_∞}, 1 a basis of the rank-one second summand) with {δ_{s⋆}(x), δ_{s⋆}(y)}_{s⋆_{n+1}} = {x, y}_{s⋆_n,♯} for all x, y, and by Construction A.1.6 a morphism δ_{s⋆↑}: DL_{s⋆_n} = DL(𝒱_{s⋆_n}, { , }_{s⋆_n}, ⌈(n+1)/2⌉) → DL_{s⋆_{n+1}} = DL(𝒱_{s⋆_{n+1}}, { , }_{s⋆_{n+1}}, ⌈(n+2)/2⌉), H ↦ δ_{s⋆}(H ⊕ O_S·1).
items.note: Construction A.1.6 requires dim 𝒱^⊣ = n + 1 − 2⌊(n+1)/2⌋, dim 𝒱_♮^⊣ = n − 2⌊n/2⌋ and δ of corank dim 𝒱^⊣; these hold by Lemma 4.3.2 and Lemma 4.5.2 (δ^⋆ iso for n odd; kernel of rank 1 at τ_∞ for n even). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proposition 4.5.6 — b_↑ on fibres is the special morphism of DL varieties
items.statement: In the situation of item constr-delta-up, the diagram ζ_{s⋆_{n+1}} ∘ b_↑ = δ_{s⋆↑} ∘ (ζ_{s⋆_n} ∘ b_↓): B_{s⋆} → DL_{s⋆_{n+1}} commutes in Sch_{/κ}, where ζ_{s⋆_n}: B_{s⋆_n} ⥲ DL_{s⋆_n} and ζ_{s⋆_{n+1}}: B_{s⋆_{n+1}} ⥲ DL_{s⋆_{n+1}} are the isomorphisms of Theorem 4.3.5(3). In particular b_↑: B_{s⋆} → B_{s⋆_{n+1}} is an isomorphism if n is odd, and is a regular embedding of codimension one if n is even.
items.note: b_↓: B_{s⋆} → B_{s⋆_n} is an isomorphism (the paper cites Lemma 4.5.2; it is immediate from the Cartesian Definition 4.5.3). For n even the commutativity reduces to (4.12): δ^⋆_{*,τ_∞}((ᾰ_{*,τ_∞})⁻¹ω_{A^∨/S,τ_∞} ⊕ H₁^dR(A₀/S)_{τ_∞}) = (ᾰ_{♮*,τ_∞})⁻¹ω_{A^∨×A₀^∨/S,τ_∞}, proved from ᾰ_♮ ∘ δ^⋆ = ᾰ × ϖ·id_{A₀} and ϖ ≡ 0 on H₁^dR(A₀/S)_{τ_∞}; the asserted equality of ranks uses ker δ^⋆_{*,τ_∞} ⊆ ker ᾰ_{*,τ_∞} ⊕ H₁^dR(A₀)_{τ_∞} (unstated, true). The last claim then follows from Proposition A.1.7 and dimensions ⌊(n−1)/2⌋, ⌊n/2⌋. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Notation 4.5.7 — compatible definite uniformization data and K^⋆_{sp,p}
items.statement: Choose a definite uniformization datum (V^⋆_n, i_n, {Λ^⋆_{n,𝔮}}_{𝔮|p}) for V_n (Definition 4.4.1) and fix a definite uniformization datum (V^⋆_{n+1}, i_{n+1}, {Λ^⋆_{n+1,𝔮}}_{𝔮|p}) for V_{n+1} with V^⋆_{n+1} = (V^⋆_n)_♯, i_{n+1} = (i_n)_♯, Λ^⋆_{n+1,𝔮} = (Λ^⋆_{n,𝔮})_♯ for 𝔮 ≠ 𝔭, and (Λ^⋆_{n,𝔭})_♯ ⊆ Λ^⋆_{n+1,𝔭} ⊆ p⁻¹((Λ^⋆_{n,𝔭})^∨)_♯. Let K^⋆_{n+1,𝔮} be the stabilizer of Λ^⋆_{n+1,𝔮}, K^⋆_{n+1,p} := ∏_{𝔮|p} K^⋆_{n+1,𝔮}, K^⋆_{sp,𝔭} := K^⋆_{n,𝔭} ∩ K^⋆_{n+1,𝔭} (a subgroup of K^⋆_{n,𝔭}), and K^⋆_{sp,p} := K^⋆_{sp,𝔭} × ∏_{𝔮≠𝔭} K^⋆_{n,𝔮}.
items.note: Printed 'for V' where V_n is meant (source issue, trivial). Since 1 has norm 1, ((Λ)^∨)_♯ = ((Λ)_♯)^∨, so the upper bound is unambiguous. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Remark 4.5.8 (n odd) — Λ^⋆_{n+1,𝔭} = (Λ^⋆_{n,𝔭})_♯ and K^⋆_{sp,p} = K^⋆_{n,p}
items.statement: When n is odd, since (Λ^⋆_{n,𝔭})^∨ = pΛ^⋆_{n,𝔭}, necessarily Λ^⋆_{n+1,𝔭} = (Λ^⋆_{n,𝔭})_♯, hence K^⋆_{sp,p} = K^⋆_{n,p}.
items.note: Check: with Λ := Λ^⋆_{n,𝔭}, the admissible range is Λ ⊕ O1 ⊆ Λ′ ⊆ Λ ⊕ p⁻¹O1, and Λ ⊕ p⁻¹O1 violates pΛ′ ⊆ Λ′^∨. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Remark 4.5.8 (n even) — p + 1 choices of Λ^⋆_{n+1,𝔭}
items.statement: When n is even, the number of choices of Λ^⋆_{n+1,𝔭} in Notation 4.5.7 is p + 1.
items.note: No proof. Λ^⋆_{n+1,𝔭} corresponds to an isotropic line in the 2-dimensional non-degenerate hermitian F_{p²}-space ((Λ^⋆_{n,𝔭})^∨ ⊕ O1)/p(Λ^⋆_{n,𝔭} ⊕ O1) (hermitian curve in P¹ over F_{p²}: p + 1 points), matching Lemma 4.5.2(2). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: (4.13) — the uniformization map υ_sp
items.statement: Similarly to Construction 4.4.2 one constructs a uniformization map υ_sp: S_𝔭(V_n, −)_sp(F̄_p) → Sh(V^⋆_n, (i_n −_n)K^⋆_{sp,p}) × T_𝔭(F̄_p) (4.13) in Fun(𝔎(V_n)^p_sp × 𝔗, Set)_{/T_𝔭(F̄_p)}, which is an isomorphism.
items.note: 'Whose details we leave to the readers' (routine: the construction follows Construction 4.4.2 and Proposition 4.4.4). For n odd υ_sp = υ_n ∘ s_↓. For n even one attaches to (A^⋆, A^⋆_♮, δ^⋆) the pair (Λ_{s⋆,𝔭}, Λ_{s⋆_♮,𝔭}) with (Λ_{s⋆,𝔭})_♯ ⊆ Λ_{s⋆_♮,𝔭} via δ^⋆; the fibres of s_↓ (p + 1 points) match [K^⋆_{n,𝔭} : K^⋆_{sp,𝔭}] = p + 1 (K^⋆_{n,𝔭} acts on the p + 1 isotropic lines through its image U₁(F_p) of order p + 1, simply transitively). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proposition 4.5.9 — uniformization is compatible with s_↓, s_↑
items.statement: The diagram in Fun(𝔎(V_n)^p_sp × 𝔗, Set)_{/T_𝔭(F̄_p)} with rows υ_{n+1}: S_𝔭(V_{n+1}, −_{n+1})(F̄_p) → Sh(V^⋆_{n+1}, (i_{n+1}−_{n+1})K^⋆_{n+1,p}) × T_𝔭(F̄_p) (4.4), υ_sp (4.13), υ_n: S_𝔭(V_n, −_n)(F̄_p) → Sh(V^⋆_n, (i_n−_n)K^⋆_{n,p}) × T_𝔭(F̄_p) (4.4), left vertical maps s_↑(F̄_p), s_↓(F̄_p) and right vertical maps sh^⋆_↑ × id, sh^⋆_↓ × id commutes, where sh^⋆_↓: Sh(V^⋆_n, (i_n−_n)K^⋆_{sp,p}) → Sh(V^⋆_n, (i_n−_n)K^⋆_{n,p}) and sh^⋆_↑: Sh(V^⋆_n, (i_n−_n)K^⋆_{sp,p}) → Sh(V^⋆_{n+1}, (i_{n+1}−_{n+1})K^⋆_{n+1,p}) are the obvious maps of Shimura sets (induced by K^⋆_{sp,p} ⊆ K^⋆_{n,p} and U(V^⋆_n) ↪ U(V^⋆_{n+1}), K^⋆_{sp,p} ⊆ K^⋆_{n+1,p}). Moreover, the induced actions of Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ) on all terms on the right-hand side factor through the projection to T_𝔭(F̄_p).
items.note: 'The commutativity follows directly from definition' (of υ_sp, whose construction is left to the reader); the Galois claim as in Proposition 4.4.4. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: §4.6 — notation n₀, n₁, r₀, r₁ and X^?_{n_α}
items.statement: Keep §4.5, but let − = (−_n, −_{n+1}) be an object of 𝔎(V_n)^p × 𝔎(V_{n+1})^p. Let n₀ and n₁ be the unique even and odd numbers in {n, n+1}, and write n₀ = 2r₀, n₁ = 2r₁ + 1 (so n = r₀ + r₁; r₀ ⩾ 1, r₁ ⩾ 0 — printed 'r₀, r₁ ⩾ 1', which fails for n = 1). Let L be a p-coprime coefficient ring. For meaningful triples (X, ?, α) ∈ {M (bold), M, B, S} × {∅, η} × {0, 1} put X^?_{n_α} := X^?_𝔭(V_{n_α}, −_{n_α}); e.g. M_{n₀} = M_𝔭(V_{n₀}, −_{n₀}) (special fibre over F_p^Φ), B_{n₁}, S_{n₁}, with maps π_{n_α}: B_{n_α} → S_{n_α}, ι_{n_α}: B_{n_α} → M_{n_α}.
items.note: The definite data are those of Notation 4.5.7 (V^⋆_n, V^⋆_{n+1}), relabelled by n₀, n₁. Relative dimensions: dim M_{n_α} = n_α − 1, dim B_{n_α} fibres = ⌊(n_α − 1)/2⌋ (so r₀ − 1 and r₁), codim ι_{n_α} = ⌊n_α/2⌋ = r_α. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Construction 4.6.1(1) — the map loc′_𝔭
items.statement: For integers i, j define loc′_𝔭: H^i_ét(Sh(V_{n₀}, −_{n₀}K_{n₀,p}) ×_{Spec F} Sh(V_{n₁}, −_{n₁}K_{n₁,p}), L(j)) → H^i_𝔗(M_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} M_{n₁}, L(j)) as the composite of the localization map loc_𝔭: H^i_ét(Sh ×_F Sh, L(j)) → H^i_ét((Sh ×_F Sh) ⊗_F Q_p^Φ, L(j)), the pullback H^i_ét((Sh ×_F Sh) ⊗_F Q_p^Φ, L(j)) → H^i_𝔗(M^η_{n₀} ×_{T^η_𝔭} M^η_{n₁}, L(j)) induced by (4.2), and the isomorphism H^i_𝔗(M_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} M_{n₁}, RΨL(j)) ⥲ H^i_𝔗(M_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} M_{n₁}, L(j)) coming from L ≃ RΨL (smoothness, Theorem 4.2.3).
items.note: Source issue (gap): no map from the Q_p^Φ-cohomology H^i_𝔗(M^η_{n₀} × M^η_{n₁}) to the F_p^Φ-cohomology with RΨ-coefficients is specified, and over the non-closed fields Q_p^Φ, F_p^Φ the generic-fibre cohomology is H^i(X_s) ⊕ (residue part H^{i−1}(X_s)(−1)) rather than H^i(X_s); the map is canonical on classes unramified at 𝔭 (e.g. cycle classes of cycles with smooth closure), which covers Theorem 4.6.2. Used in §7.3 (Theorem 7.3.4). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Construction 4.6.1(2) — the map inc^{⋆,⋆}_!
items.statement: Analogously to Construction 4.4.9 define, in Fun(𝔎(V_n)^p × 𝔎(V_{n+1})^p, Mod(L)), inc^{⋆,⋆}_!: L[Sh(V^⋆_{n₀}, (i_{n₀}−_{n₀})K^⋆_{n₀,p})] ⊗_L L[Sh(V^⋆_{n₁}, (i_{n₁}−_{n₁})K^⋆_{n₁,p})] ⥲ H⁰_𝔗(S_{n₀}, L) ⊗_L H⁰_𝔗(S_{n₁}, L) = H⁰_𝔗(S_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} S_{n₁}, L) −(π_{n₀}×π_{n₁})^*→ H⁰_𝔗(B_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} B_{n₁}, L) −(ι_{n₀}×ι_{n₁})_!→ H^{2n}_𝔗(M_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} M_{n₁}, L(n)).
items.note: Codimension of ι_{n₀} × ι_{n₁} is r₀ + r₁ = n. The equality H⁰_𝔗(S_{n₀}) ⊗ H⁰_𝔗(S_{n₁}) = H⁰_𝔗(S_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} S_{n₁}) holds because T_𝔭(F̄_p) is a torsor for the group of 𝔗 (Proposition 4.4.4). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Construction 4.6.1(3) — the graph ΔSh(V_n, −_nK_{n,p}) and its class
items.statement: Suppose − is taken in 𝔎(V_n)^p_sp. ΔSh(V_n, −_nK_{n,p}) is the graph of sh_↑ (4.6), a closed subscheme of Sh(V_{n₀}, −_{n₀}K_{n₀,p}) ×_{Spec F} Sh(V_{n₁}, −_{n₁}K_{n₁,p}) (factors ordered by parity), with class [ΔSh(V_n, −_nK_{n,p})] ∈ H^{2n}_ét(Sh(V_{n₀}, −_{n₀}K_{n₀,p}) ×_{Spec F} Sh(V_{n₁}, −_{n₁}K_{n₁,p}), L(n)) given by the absolute cycle class map.
items.note: Codimension n = (2n − 1) − (n − 1). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Construction 4.6.1(4) — the graph ΔSh(V^⋆_n, (i_n−_n)K^⋆_{sp,p})
items.statement: ΔSh(V^⋆_n, (i_n−_n)K^⋆_{sp,p}) is the graph of the correspondence (sh^⋆_↓, sh^⋆_↑) (Proposition 4.5.9), a subset of Sh(V^⋆_{n₀}, (i_{n₀}−_{n₀})K^⋆_{n₀,p}) × Sh(V^⋆_{n₁}, (i_{n₁}−_{n₁})K^⋆_{n₁,p}); 1_{ΔSh(V^⋆_n, (i_n−_n)K^⋆_{sp,p})} denotes its characteristic function.
items.note: Source issue (error in the literal reading): for n even the map (sh^⋆_↓, sh^⋆_↑): Sh(V^⋆_n, (i_n−_n)K^⋆_{sp,p}) → Sh(V^⋆_{n₀}, …) × Sh(V^⋆_{n₁}, …) need not be injective (by pigeonhole it is not injective whenever p + 1 exceeds the number of points of Sh(V^⋆_{n+1}, (i_{n+1}−_{n+1})K^⋆_{n+1,p})), and the proof of Theorem 4.6.2 computes the pushforward (sh^⋆_↓, sh^⋆_↑)_*(1), not the characteristic function of the image subset. Theorem 7.3.4 (p. 300) explicitly regards the element as this pushforward. For n odd, sh^⋆_↓ = id and the two readings agree. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Theorem 4.6.2 — second geometric reciprocity law
items.statement: Suppose that − is taken in the subcategory 𝔎(V_n)^p_sp. Then T^⋆_{n₁,𝔭}.(id × π_{n₁})_!(id × ι_{n₁})^* loc′_𝔭([ΔSh(V_n, −_nK_{n,p})]) = (id × π_{n₁})_!(id × ι_{n₁})^* inc^{⋆,⋆}_!(1_{ΔSh(V^⋆_n, (i_n−_n)K^⋆_{sp,p})}) in H^{2r₀}_𝔗(M_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} S_{n₁}, L(r₀)), where (id × ι_{n₁})^*: H^{2n}_𝔗(M_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} M_{n₁}, L(n)) → H^{2n}_𝔗(M_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} B_{n₁}, L(n)), (id × π_{n₁})_! is the trace along the fibres of π_{n₁} (dimension r₁), and T^⋆_{n₁,𝔭} = Σ_{δ=0}^{r₁} d_{r₁−δ,p} T_{n₁,𝔭;δ} ∈ T_{n₁,𝔭} is the Hecke operator of Theorem 4.4.10, acting on H^{2r₀}_𝔗(M_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} S_{n₁}, L(r₀)) through S_{n₁} (Proposition 4.4.6, Remark 4.4.8).
items.note: Proof: (i) loc′_𝔭([ΔSh]) = m_{Δ!}[M_n] (item step-loc-graph); (ii) the square step-cartesian-4-6 is Cartesian and transversal, so (id × ι_{n₁})^*m_{Δ!}[M_n] = ((ι_{n₀} × id) ∘ b_Δ)_![B_sp] ('Proper Base Change'); (iii) (id × π_{n₁})_!((ι_{n₀} × id) ∘ b_Δ)_! = (ι_{n₀} × id)_!((id × π_{n₁}) ∘ b_Δ)_!; (iv) ((id × π_{n₁}) ∘ b_Δ)_![B_sp] = (π_{n₀} × id)^*(1_{ΔSh(V^⋆_n,…)}) (item step-bsp-pushforward); (v) Theorem 4.4.10 for n₁ applied in the second factor turns T^⋆_{n₁,𝔭}·1_{ΔSh} into (id × π_{n₁})_!(id × ι_{n₁})^*(id × ι_{n₁})_!(id × π_{n₁})^*1_{ΔSh}, and (ι_{n₀} × id)_!(π_{n₀} × id)^*(id × ι_{n₁})_!(id × π_{n₁})^* = inc^{⋆,⋆}_!. The theorem is meaningful with loc′_𝔭 read on unramified classes (source issue on Construction 4.6.1(1)), and it is correct with 1_{ΔSh(V^⋆_n,…)} read as the pushforward (sh^⋆_↓, sh^⋆_↑)_*(1) (source issue on Construction 4.6.1(4); for n even and p large the characteristic-function reading is false). Previous-pass statement was a paraphrase. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 4.6.2 — loc′_𝔭([ΔSh(V_n)]) = m_{Δ!}[M_n]
items.statement: Let m_Δ: M_n → M_n ×_{T_𝔭} M_{n+1} = M_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} M_{n₁} be the diagonal morphism of the correspondence (id, m_↑) (4.7), in Fun(𝔎(V_n)^p_sp × 𝔗, Sch_{/Z_p^Φ})_{/T_𝔭}. Then loc′_𝔭([ΔSh(V_n, −_nK_{n,p})]) = m_{Δ!}[M_n] ∈ H^{2n}_𝔗(M_n ×_{T_𝔭} M_{n+1}, L(n)).
items.note: 'By the commutative diagram (4.8)': the preimage of ΔSh under (4.2) is the generic fibre of m_Δ(M_n), whose closure m_Δ(M_n) is smooth over Z_p^Φ, so the cycle class specializes to the class of its special fibre. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 4.6.2 — the Cartesian square B_sp → M_{n₀} × B_{n₁} over M_n → M_{n₀} × M_{n₁}
items.statement: Put B_sp := B_𝔭(V_n, −)_sp and b_Δ := (b_↓, b_↑): B_sp → B_n ×_{T_𝔭} B_{n+1} = B_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} B_{n₁}. The commutative square with top (ι_{n₀} × id) ∘ b_Δ: B_sp → M_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} B_{n₁}, left ι_n ∘ b_↓: B_sp → M_n, right id × ι_{n₁}: M_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} B_{n₁} → M_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} M_{n₁} and bottom m_Δ: M_n → M_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} M_{n₁} is Cartesian.
items.note: By Proposition 4.5.5 when n = n₀ is even, and by Lemma 4.5.2(1) (b_↓ an isomorphism) with (4.9) when n = n₁ is odd. The fibre product has the expected dimension r₀ − 1 in both cases (checked in this extraction), so the intersection is transversal and base change of Gysin maps applies. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 4.6.2 — ((id × π_{n₁}) ∘ b_Δ)_![B_sp] = (π_{n₀} × id)^*(1_{ΔSh(V^⋆_n)})
items.statement: In H⁰_𝔗(B_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} S_{n₁}, L) one has ((id × π_{n₁}) ∘ b_Δ)_![B_sp] = (π_{n₀} × id)^*(1_{ΔSh(V^⋆_n, (i_n−_n)K^⋆_{sp,p})}), where 1_{ΔSh} ∈ L[Sh(V^⋆_{n₀}) × Sh(V^⋆_{n₁})] ≅ H⁰_𝔗(S_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} S_{n₁}, L) via uniformization.
items.note: 'By the definition of B_sp (Definition 4.5.3)' together with Proposition 4.5.9. For n even the map B_sp → B_n ×_{T_𝔭} S_{n+1} is the base change of (s_↓, s_↑): S_sp → S_n ×_{T_𝔭} S_{n+1} along π_n × id, so its pushforward counts multiplicities: the identity holds with 1_{ΔSh} = (sh^⋆_↓, sh^⋆_↑)_*(1), not with the characteristic function of the image when (s_↓, s_↑) is not injective (source issue). For n odd it additionally needs that b_↑ is an isomorphism on fibres (Proposition 4.5.6), not only Definition 4.5.3. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: [RSZ21, Theorem 4.4] — representability of the RSZ-type moduli problems (black box)
items.statement: The moduli functors M_𝔭(V, K^p) → T_𝔭 (Definition 4.2.2) and S_𝔭(V, K^p) → T_𝔭 (Definition 4.3.1) are representable, the former by a quasi-projective (smooth) scheme over T_𝔭 and the latter by a finite étale scheme over T_𝔭.
items.locator: used in the proof of Theorem 4.2.3 (p. 161) and after Definition 4.3.1 (p. 164); also Cited in Definitions 5.3.1 and 5.4.1, published pp. 194, 200 ([62, Theorem 4.4])
items.note: Cited, not proved. RSZ21 = Rapoport–Smithling–Zhang, On Shimura varieties for unitary groups. [RSZ21, §3.3] is also cited for the generic-fibre isomorphism (4.2) (item iso-4-2). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: §5.1 — initial setup for the semistable moduli
items.statement: Fix a special inert prime 𝔭 of F⁺ (Definition 3.3.4: 𝔭 is inert in F, the underlying rational prime p is odd and unramified in F, and F⁺_𝔭 = ℚ_p) with underlying rational prime p; take the prescribed subring ℙ of Definition 3.4.2 to be ℤ_(p). Choose: a CM type Φ containing τ_∞; a rational skew-hermitian space W₀ over O_F ⊗ ℤ_(p) of rank 1 and type Φ (Definition 3.5.3); a neat open compact subgroup K₀^p ⊆ T₀(𝔸^{∞,p}); an isomorphism ι_p: ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_p such that ι_p ∘ τ̲_∞: F⁺ ↪ ℚ̄_p induces the place 𝔭 of F⁺; and an element ϖ ∈ O_{F⁺} that is totally positive with val_𝔭(ϖ) = 1 and val_𝔮(ϖ) = 0 for every prime 𝔮 ≠ 𝔭 of F⁺ above p. Notation 3.3.6 is adopted; in particular 𝔽_p^Φ contains 𝔽_{p²}. Put 𝐓_𝔭 := 𝐓_p(W₀, K₀^p) ⊗_{O_{F_Φ} ⊗ ℤ_(p)} ℤ_p^Φ.
items.note: W₀ and K₀^p are suppressed from later notation; 𝔭 is kept because later several different special inert primes are used. Because F⁺_𝔭 = ℚ_p and 𝔭 is inert in F, exactly two embeddings in Σ_∞ induce the place above 𝔭 (τ_∞ and τ_∞^c), and the p-power Frobenius σ swaps them (σ⁻¹τ_∞ = τ_∞^c is used on pp. 195, 200). ϖ is used to twist polarizations in §§5.4–5.5 (e.g. ϖλ₀ in Definition 5.4.1). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 5.2.1 — the semistable moduli functor 𝐌_𝔭(V°, –)
items.statement: Datum: V° a standard definite hermitian space over F of rank N ⩾ 1 (Definition 3.2.1), and for every prime 𝔮 of F⁺ above p a self-dual O_{F_𝔮}-lattice Λ°_𝔮 in V° ⊗_F F_𝔮. Define 𝐌_𝔭(V°, –): 𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗 → PSch′_{/ℤ_p^Φ}, K^{p°} ↦ 𝐌_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}), where for S ∈ Sch′_{/ℤ_p^Φ}, 𝐌_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(S) is the set of equivalence classes of sextuples (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A, λ, η^p) with: (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p) ∈ 𝐓_𝔭(S); (A, λ) a unitary O_F-abelian scheme of signature type NΦ − τ_∞ + τ_∞^c over S (Definitions 3.4.2, 3.4.3) such that ker λ[p^∞] is contained in A[𝔭] and has rank p²; η^p a K^{p°}-level structure, i.e. for a chosen geometric point s on every connected component of S, a π₁(S, s)-invariant K^{p°}-orbit of isomorphisms η^p: V° ⊗_ℚ 𝔸^{∞,p} → Hom^{λ₀,λ}_{F⊗_ℚ𝔸^{∞,p}}(H₁^{ét}(A_{0s}, 𝔸^{∞,p}), H₁^{ét}(A_s, 𝔸^{∞,p})) of hermitian spaces over F ⊗_ℚ 𝔸^{∞,p} = F ⊗_{F⁺} 𝔸_{F⁺}^{∞,p} (Construction 3.4.4 with □ = {∞, p}). Equivalence and the action of morphisms of 𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗 are as in Definition 4.2.2.
items.note: Remark 5.2.2 (p. 189): the tame level is defined through the DEFINITE space V°, unlike the usual treatment; this makes the uniformization map (5.4) of the balloon source canonical, at the cost that the identification of the generic fibre with a unitary Shimura variety is non-canonical (it needs the datum of Definition 5.2.6). Lattices Λ°_𝔮 enter only via the uniformization maps (Constructions 5.3.6, 5.4.6, 5.5.5). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: (5.1) — forgetful morphism to 𝐓_𝔭 and special-fibre notation
items.statement: There is a forgetful morphism 𝐌_𝔭(V°, –) → 𝐓_𝔭 (5.1) in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗, PSch′_{/ℤ_p^Φ}), which is representable by quasi-projective schemes. Following Notation 3.3.6, M_𝔭(V°, –) → T_𝔭 denotes the base change of (5.1) to 𝔽_p^Φ, a morphism in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗, Sch_{/𝔽_p^Φ}).
items.note: Bold letters are schemes over ℤ_p^Φ, roman letters their special fibres over 𝔽_p^Φ; an overline (M̄) denotes base change to 𝔽̄_p, and a superscript η the generic fibre (Notation 3.3.6(5)). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 5.2.3 — balloon, ground and link strata
items.statement: For K^{p°} ∈ 𝔎(V°)^p let (𝒜₀, λ₀, η₀^p; 𝒜, λ, η^p) be the universal object over M_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}). (1) M°_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}) is the locus of M_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}) on which ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞} coincides with H₁^{dR}(𝒜)^⊥_{τ_∞^c} (balloon stratum); (2) M•_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}) is the locus on which H₁^{dR}(𝒜)^⊥_{τ_∞} is a line subbundle of ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c} (ground stratum); (3) M†_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}) := M°_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}) ∩ M•_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}) (link stratum). The inclusions are denoted m^{†°}: M†_𝔭(V°, –) → M°_𝔭(V°, –) and m^{†•}: M†_𝔭(V°, –) → M•_𝔭(V°, –).
items.note: Notation 3.4.7: for F ⊆ H₁^{dR}(A)_τ, F^⊥ ⊆ H₁^{dR}(A)_{τ^c} is its orthogonal under ⟨,⟩_{λ,τ}; thus H₁^{dR}(𝒜)^⊥_{τ_∞^c} ⊆ H₁^{dR}(𝒜)_{τ_∞} and H₁^{dR}(𝒜)^⊥_{τ_∞} ⊆ H₁^{dR}(𝒜)_{τ_∞^c} are the rank-1 radicals of the degenerate pairing (ker λ has rank p²). By Remark 3.4.6, ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞} has rank 1 and ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c} rank N−1. Footnote 14: 'balloon' is borrowed from an unpublished note of Kudla–Rapoport; footnote 15: the link stratum links balloons to the ground. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Remark 5.2.4 — N = 1
items.statement: When N = 1, the ground stratum M•_𝔭(V°, –) and the link stratum M†_𝔭(V°, –) are both empty.
items.note: For N = 1, H₁^{dR}(𝒜)^⊥_{τ_∞} is a line but ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c} = 0, so condition (2) of Definition 5.2.3 never holds. §§5.4–5.6 assume N ⩾ 2. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.2.5(1) — strict semistability
items.statement: For every K^{p°} ∈ 𝔎(V°)^p, the scheme 𝐌_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}) is quasi-projective and strictly semistable over 𝐓_𝔭 of relative dimension N − 1, and M_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}) = M°_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}) ∪ M•_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}). Moreover, (5.1) is projective if and only if its base change to ℚ_p^Φ is.
items.note: Proof (pp. 191–192): quasi-projectivity is 'well-known'; strict semistability follows from the four-case local computation (item local-model-5-2-5) together with smoothness of the generic fibre of dimension N − 1. The completed local ring W(κ)[[x₁,…,x_N]]/(x₁x_N − p) at link points is a proof ingredient, not part of the statement. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 5.2.5 — completed local rings
items.statement: Let x = (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A, λ, η^p) ∈ 𝐌_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(κ), κ a perfect field containing 𝔽_p^Φ, with completed local ring 𝒪_x. Choose D(A)_{τ_∞} ≅ W(κ)^{⊕N}, D(A)_{τ_∞^c} ≅ W(κ)^{⊕N} so that ⟨(x₁,…,x_N),(y₁,…,y_N)⟩_{λ,τ_∞} = p x₁y₁ + x₂y₂ + ⋯ + x_N y_N. By Proposition 3.4.8, Hom_{W(κ)}(𝒪_x, R) for Artinian quotients R is the set of pairs of R-subbundles M_{τ_∞} ⊆ D(A)_{τ_∞} ⊗ R, M_{τ_∞^c} ⊆ D(A)_{τ_∞^c} ⊗ R of ranks 1 and N−1 lifting ω_{A^∨/κ,τ_∞}, ω_{A^∨/κ,τ_∞^c}, with ⟨M_{τ_∞}, M_{τ_∞^c}⟩ = 0. (i) If ω_{A^∨/κ,τ_∞} is generated by (1,0,…,0) and ω_{A^∨/κ,τ_∞^c} contains (1,0,…,0), then (after changing coordinates) ω_{A^∨/κ,τ_∞^c} = {(y₁,…,y_{N−1},0)}, 𝒪_x ≅ W(κ)[[x₁,…,x_N]]/(x₁x_N − p), and x ∈ M†_𝔭. (ii) If ω_{A^∨/κ,τ_∞} is generated by (1,0,…,0) and ω_{A^∨/κ,τ_∞^c} ∌ (1,0,…,0), then ω_{A^∨/κ,τ_∞^c} = {(0,y₂,…,y_N)}, M_{τ_∞} is determined by M_{τ_∞^c}, and 𝒪_x ≅ W(κ)[[x₂,…,x_N]]. (iii) If ω_{A^∨/κ,τ_∞} is not generated by (1,0,…,0) and ω_{A^∨/κ,τ_∞^c} ∋ (1,0,…,0), then ω_{A^∨/κ,τ_∞} is generated by (0,…,0,1), M_{τ_∞^c} is determined by M_{τ_∞}, and 𝒪_x ≅ W(κ)[[x₁,…,x_{N−1}]]. (iv) The remaining case does not occur. M°_𝔭 is the locus of (i) or (ii); M•_𝔭 the locus of (i) or (iii).
items.note: Checked: in case (i), writing M_{τ_∞^c} as the graph of (a₁,…,a_{N−1}) and M_{τ_∞} = ⟨(1,b₂,…,b_N)⟩, orthogonality forces b_i = −a_i b_N (i ⩾ 2) and a₁b_N = −p, i.e. the stated local ring up to sign. Case (iv) cannot occur: if v ∉ κ·e₁ generates ω_{τ_∞}, then v^⊥ = ω_{τ_∞^c} (dimension N−1) and contains e₁. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.2.5(2) — smoothness of balloon and ground strata
items.statement: For every K^{p°} ∈ 𝔎(V°)^p, the loci M°_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}) and M•_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}) are both closed subsets of M_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}), smooth over T_𝔭 if endowed with the induced reduced scheme structure.
items.note: The statement does not state dimensions; relative dimension N − 1 of both strata follows from (3)–(4) (tangent sheaves of rank N − 1), and smoothness of M†_𝔭 of relative dimension N − 2 follows from the local model (case (i): the two branches x₁ = 0, x_N = 0 meet transversally) and from (5). An earlier version of this extraction's 'M† smooth of dimension N−2 when nonempty' is therefore a consequence, not a printed clause. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.2.5(3) — tangent sheaf of the balloon stratum
items.statement: For every K^{p°} ∈ 𝔎(V°)^p there is a canonical isomorphism 𝒯_{M°_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})/T_𝔭} ≃ ℋom(ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c}, Lie_{𝒜,τ_∞^c}) of coherent sheaves on M°_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}).
items.note: Proof (p. 192): by Proposition 3.4.8 (Serre–Tate/Grothendieck–Messing), liftings are pairs of orthogonal subbundles of crystalline homology; on the balloon ω̂_{τ_∞} is forced to be the orthogonal of H₁^{cris}(A/Ŝ)_{τ_∞^c}, so only ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c} is lifted freely (Remark 3.4.6). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.2.5(4) — tangent sequence of the ground stratum
items.statement: For every K^{p°} ∈ 𝔎(V°)^p, when N ⩾ 2 the relative tangent sheaf fits canonically into an exact sequence of coherent sheaves on M•_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}): 0 → ℋom(ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞}, ω^⊥_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c}/ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞}) → 𝒯_{M•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})/T_𝔭} → ℋom(ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c}/H₁^{dR}(𝒜)^⊥_{τ_∞}, Lie_{𝒜,τ_∞^c}) → 0.
items.note: ω^⊥_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c} ⊆ H₁^{dR}(𝒜)_{τ_∞} has rank 2 on M•, so the outer terms have ranks 1 and N − 2. Proof: first lift ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c} containing H₁^{cris}(A/Ŝ)^⊥_{τ_∞}, then lift ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞} orthogonally (Remark 3.4.6). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.2.5(5) — tangent sheaf of the link stratum
items.statement: For every K^{p°} ∈ 𝔎(V°)^p, when N ⩾ 2 the natural map 𝒯_{M†_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})/T_𝔭} → 𝒯_{M•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})/T_𝔭}|_{M†_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})} induces an isomorphism 𝒯_{M†_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})/T_𝔭} ≃ ℋom(ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c}/H₁^{dR}(𝒜)^⊥_{τ_∞}, Lie_{𝒜,τ_∞^c}) of coherent sheaves on M†_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}) under the exact sequence of (4). In particular, the exact sequence in (4) splits over M†_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}).
items.note: Hence the normal bundle of m^{†•} is the restriction of ℋom(ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞}, ω^⊥_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c}/ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞}); this is used in Corollary 5.3.5. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 5.2.6 — indefinite uniformization datum
items.statement: An indefinite uniformization datum for V° (at 𝔭) is a collection (V′, j, {Λ′_𝔮}_{𝔮|p}) where: V′ is a standard indefinite hermitian space over F of rank N; j: V° ⊗_ℚ 𝔸^{∞,p} → V′ ⊗_ℚ 𝔸^{∞,p} is an isometry; for every prime 𝔮 ≠ 𝔭 of F⁺ above p, Λ′_𝔮 is a self-dual O_{F_𝔮}-lattice in V′ ⊗_F F_𝔮; and Λ′_𝔭 is an O_{F_𝔭}-lattice in V′ ⊗_F F_𝔭 with Λ′_𝔭 ⊆ (Λ′_𝔭)^∨ and (Λ′_𝔭)^∨/Λ′_𝔭 of length 1.
items.note: Existence is asserted from the Hasse principle for hermitian spaces (item hasse-principle-hermitian); one datum is fixed. Consistency check: V′ differs from V° exactly at τ_∞ (signature) and at 𝔭 (parity of val det), an even number of places. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: (5.2) — moduli interpretation of the generic fibre
items.statement: Let K′_𝔮 be the stabilizer of Λ′_𝔮 for every 𝔮 | p and K′_p := ∏_{𝔮|p} K′_𝔮. The isometry j induces an equivalence j: 𝔎(V°)^p ≅ 𝔎(V′)^p. Similarly to Remark 4.2.5 there is a 'moduli interpretation' isomorphism 𝐌^η_𝔭(V°, –) ≅ Sh(V′, j–K′_p) ×_{Spec F} 𝐓^η_𝔭 (5.2) in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗, Sch_{/ℚ_p^Φ})_{/𝐓^η_𝔭}, where 𝔗 acts on Sh(V′, j–K′_p) ×_{Spec F} 𝐓^η_𝔭 via the second factor.
items.note: Non-canonical: depends on the chosen uniformization datum (Remark 5.2.2). Proof only by reference to Remark 4.2.5. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 5.2.7 — nearby-cycle comparison for 𝐌_𝔭(V°, –)
items.statement: Let L be a p-coprime coefficient ring. The two specialization maps H^i_{𝔗,c}(𝐌_𝔭(V°, –) ⊗_{ℤ_p^Φ} ℚ̄_p, L) → H^i_{𝔗,c}(M̄_𝔭(V°, –), RΨL) and H^i_𝔗(𝐌_𝔭(V°, –) ⊗_{ℤ_p^Φ} ℚ̄_p, L) → H^i_𝔗(M̄_𝔭(V°, –), RΨL) are both isomorphisms. In particular, (5.2) induces isomorphisms H^i_{ét,c}(Sh(V′, j–K′_p)_{F̄}, L) ≃ H^i_{𝔗,c}(M̄_𝔭(V°, –), RΨL) and H^i_{ét}(Sh(V′, j–K′_p)_{F̄}, L) ≃ H^i_𝔗(M̄_𝔭(V°, –), RΨL) in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p, Mod(L[Gal(ℚ̄_p/ℚ_p^Φ)])) for every i ∈ ℤ, where Gal(ℚ̄_p/ℚ_p^Φ) is regarded as a subgroup of Gal(F̄/F) via ι_p.
items.locator: §5.2, Lemma 5.2.7 (printed as a Lemma, not a Proposition), published p. 193
items.note: Proof: proper base change when 𝐌_𝔭 is proper (always the case if F⁺ ≠ ℚ, by Remark 5.2.8 and Theorem 5.2.5(1)); otherwise Lan–Stroh [43, Corollary 5.20] (item lan-stroh-cor-5-20). H_𝔗 denotes the maximal submodule on which T₀(𝔸^{∞,p})/T₀(ℤ_(p))K₀^p acts trivially (Notation 3.5.7). The earlier locator 'Lemma 5.11.2' is outside these pages. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lan–Stroh, Corollary 5.20 (black box)
items.statement: Used as: for the (possibly non-proper) integral model 𝐌_𝔭(V°, –) over ℤ_p^Φ and a p-coprime coefficient ring L, the specialization maps from (compactly supported) étale cohomology of the geometric generic fibre to (compactly supported) cohomology of the geometric special fibre with coefficients in the nearby-cycle complex RΨL are isomorphisms.
items.locator: Cited in proof of Lemma 5.2.7, published p. 193 ([43, Corollary 5.20]); also Cited in the proof of Lemma 5.11.2, published p. 251 (also Lemma 5.2.7, p. 193); also used in the proof of Lemma 4.2.4, p. 162
items.note: Cited, not proved. Its applicability to this semistable, non-principally-polarized PEL model (and to the 𝔗-equivariant setting) is asserted without further comment; only needed when F⁺ = ℚ. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Remark 5.2.8 — good reduction of Sh(V′) at other places above p
items.statement: Suppose F⁺ ≠ ℚ. Then Sh(V′, K^{p′}K′_p) is proper over F for K^{p′} ∈ 𝔎(V′)^p, and it has proper smooth reduction at every place w of F above Σ_p^+ ∖ {𝔭}. Explanation: take such w, a CM type Φ containing τ_∞ and ℂ ≃ ℚ̄_p inducing w; put 𝐓_w := 𝐓_p(W₀, K₀^p) ⊗_{O_{F_Φ}⊗ℤ_(p)} ℤ_p^Φ, and define 𝐌_w(V′, K^{p′}) on Sch′_{/ℤ_p^Φ} as equivalence classes of sextuples (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A, λ, η^p) with (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p) ∈ 𝐓_w(S), (A, λ) unitary of signature NΦ − τ_∞ + τ_∞^c with ker λ[p^∞] ⊆ A[𝔭] of rank p², and η^p a K^{p′}-level structure as in Definition 5.2.1. Then 𝐌_w(V′, K^{p′}) is represented by a projective scheme over ℤ_p^Φ, smooth of relative dimension N − 1, and 𝐌^η_w(V′, K^{p′}) ≃ Sh(V′, K^{p′}K′_p) ×_{Spec F} 𝐓^η_w over 𝐓^η_w; since 𝐓_w is finite étale over O_{F_w}, Sh(V′, K^{p′}K′_p) has proper smooth reduction at w.
items.note: Smoothness via 'an easy computation of the tangent sheaf as in Theorem 4.2.3': at 𝔭 the p-divisible group is rigid because τ_∞ no longer lies above 𝔭. The descent from ℤ_p^Φ to O_{F_w} is left implicit. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 5.3.1 — balloon source S°_𝔭(V°, –)
items.statement: Define S°_𝔭(V°, –): 𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗 → PSch′_{/𝔽_p^Φ}, K^{p°} ↦ S°_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}), where for S ∈ Sch′_{/𝔽_p^Φ}, S°_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(S) is the set of equivalence classes of sextuples (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A°, λ°, η^{p°}) with (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p) ∈ T_𝔭(S); (A°, λ°) a unitary O_F-abelian scheme of signature type NΦ over S with λ° p-principal; η^{p°}, for a chosen geometric point s on every connected component of S, a π₁(S, s)-invariant K^{p°}-orbit of isomorphisms η^{p°}: V° ⊗_ℚ 𝔸^{∞,p} → Hom^{λ₀,λ°}_{F⊗_ℚ𝔸^{∞,p}}(H₁^{ét}(A_{0s}, 𝔸^{∞,p}), H₁^{ét}(A°_s, 𝔸^{∞,p})) of hermitian spaces. Equivalence and morphisms as in Definition 4.2.2. The forgetful morphism S°_𝔭(V°, –) → T_𝔭 is represented by finite étale schemes [62, Theorem 4.4].
items.note: Finite étaleness is the black box item rsz-thm-4-4. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: §5.3 — the pairing {,}_{s°} and DL_{s°}
items.statement: Let s° = (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A°, λ°, η^{p°}) ∈ S°_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(κ), κ a perfect field containing 𝔽_p^Φ. Then A°_κ[𝔭^∞] is a supersingular p-divisible group, the (κ, σ⁻¹)-linear Verschiebung 𝕍: H₁^{dR}(A°/κ)_{τ_∞} → H₁^{dR}(A°/κ)_{σ⁻¹τ_∞} = H₁^{dR}(A°/κ)_{τ_∞^c} is an isomorphism, giving a (κ, σ)-linear isomorphism 𝕍⁻¹: H₁^{dR}(A°/κ)_{τ_∞^c} → H₁^{dR}(A°/κ)_{τ_∞}. Define the non-degenerate pairing {x, y}_{s°} := ⟨𝕍⁻¹x, y⟩_{λ°,τ_∞} on 𝒱_{s°} := H₁^{dR}(A°/κ)_{τ_∞^c}. Then (𝒱_{s°}, {,}_{s°}) is admissible (Definition A.1.1), and DL_{s°} := DL(𝒱_{s°}, {,}_{s°}, N − 1) (Definition A.1.2: rank-(N−1) subbundles H ⊆ 𝒱_S with H^⊣ ⊆ H, where H^⊣ is the right orthogonal under {,}).
items.note: Admissibility 'by the same proof as Lemma 4.3.2'. Admissible (Definition A.1.1, p. 321) means: there is an 𝔽_{p²}-subspace 𝒱₀ ⊆ 𝒱_{κ̄} with 𝒱₀ ⊗ κ̄ ≅ 𝒱_{κ̄} and {x,y} = −{y,x}^σ on 𝒱₀ — a GEOMETRIC 𝔽_{p²}-structure (relevant to E9 and to Lemma 5.6.2(3)). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 5.3.2 — balloon correspondence space B°_𝔭(V°, –)
items.statement: Define B°_𝔭(V°, –): 𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗 → PSch′_{/𝔽_p^Φ}, where for S ∈ Sch′_{/𝔽_p^Φ}, B°_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(S) is the set of equivalence classes of decuples (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A, λ, η^p; A°, λ°, η^{p°}; β) with (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A, λ, η^p) ∈ M°_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(S), (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A°, λ°, η^{p°}) ∈ S°_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(S), and β: A → A° an O_F-linear quasi-p-isogeny (Definition 3.4.5) such that (a) ker β[p^∞] ⊆ A[𝔭]; (b) λ = β^∨ ∘ λ° ∘ β; (c) the K^{p°}-orbit of v ↦ β_* ∘ η^p(v), v ∈ V° ⊗_ℚ 𝔸^{∞,p}, coincides with η^{p°}. Equivalence and morphisms as in Definition 4.3.3.
items.note: Degree count: λ has p-part of degree p² and λ° is p-principal, so deg β = p; ker β_{*,τ_∞} has rank 1 and β_{*,τ_∞^c} is an isomorphism (proof of Theorem 5.3.4). The isomorphism B° ≅ M° is Theorem 5.3.4 (item G16). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

api.name: RankinSelberg.BalloonIsogenyResolution.data
api.statement: Use the universal isogeny and projective quotient of de Rham data.

api.name: RankinSelberg.BalloonIsogenyResolution.characterisation
api.statement: ι° is an isomorphism.

api.name: RankinSelberg.BalloonIsogenyResolution.compatibility
api.statement: The fibre π°^−1(s) is P^(N−1) in the paper’s quotient convention.

uses.how: Use the universal isogeny and projective quotient of de Rham data.

items.name: (5.3) and Definition 5.3.3 — basic correspondence on the balloon stratum
items.statement: The obvious forgetful maps give a correspondence S°_𝔭(V°, –) ←π°— B°_𝔭(V°, –) —ι°→ M°_𝔭(V°, –) (5.3) in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗, PSch′_{/𝔽_p^Φ})_{/T_𝔭}; it is called the basic correspondence on the balloon stratum, with S°_𝔭(V°, –) its source.
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.3.4 — ι° is an isomorphism; balloon fibres are projective spaces
items.statement: In the diagram (5.3), ι°: B°_𝔭(V°, –) → M°_𝔭(V°, –) is an isomorphism. Moreover, for every point s° = (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A°, λ°, η^{p°}) ∈ S°_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(κ), κ a perfect field containing 𝔽_p^Φ, put B°_{s°} := π°⁻¹(s°); then the assignment sending (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A, λ, η^p; A°, λ°, η^{p°}; β) ∈ B°_{s°}(S) to the subbundle H := β_{*,τ_∞^c} ω_{A^∨/S,τ_∞^c} ⊆ H₁^{dR}(A°/S)_{τ_∞^c} = H₁^{dR}(A°/κ)_{τ_∞^c} ⊗_κ 𝒪_S = (𝒱_{s°})_S induces an isomorphism ζ°_{s°}: B°_{s°} ≅ ℙ(𝒱_{s°}) (ℙ(𝒱) parametrizing rank-(N−1) subbundles).
items.note: Proof (pp. 196–197): ι° is étale by Grothendieck–Messing, and bijective on κ′-points via Dieudonné theory: given x ∈ M°(κ), D(A)^∨_{τ_∞^c} = p⁻¹ω̃_{A^∨,τ_∞} (balloon condition), and one sets D_{A°,τ} := D(A)_τ (τ ≠ τ_∞), D_{A°,τ_∞} := p⁻¹ω̃_{A^∨,τ_∞}; A° has signature NΦ by Lemma 3.4.12(2,4), λ° is p-principal. ζ°_{s°} is well defined because rank ker β_{*,τ_∞} = 1, β_{*,τ_∞^c} is an isomorphism; it is an isomorphism by comparing tangent sheaves (Theorem 5.2.5(3)) and inverting on points via D_{A,τ_∞} := 𝕍⁻¹H̃. Proof checked; no problem found apart from issue on part (2). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.3.4(1) — the link in a balloon fibre is a Fermat hypersurface
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 5.3.4, ζ°_{s°} restricts to an isomorphism ζ°_{s°}: B°_{s°} ∩ ι°⁻¹M†_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}) ≅ DL_{s°} = DL(𝒱_{s°}, {,}_{s°}, N − 1). In particular, B°_{s°} ∩ ι°⁻¹M†_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}) is a Fermat hypersurface in B°_{s°} ≃ ℙ(𝒱_{s°}).
items.locator: §5.3, Theorem 5.3.4(1) and final sentence, published p. 196
items.note: Proof (p. 198): the link condition H₁^{dR}(A/S)^⊥_{τ_∞} ⊆ ω_{A^∨/S,τ_∞^c} becomes (𝕍⁻¹H^{(p)})^⊥ ⊆ H, i.e. H^⊣ ⊆ H. Degree p + 1 of the hypersurface is Lemma A.1.4(1); for N = 2 it is p + 1 points of ℙ¹. Checked. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.3.4(2) — normal line of the link on a balloon fibre
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 5.3.4, ℋom(ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞}, ω^⊥_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c}/ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞}) ≃ (ζ°_{s°})^* 𝒪_{ℙ(𝒱_{s°})}(−(p + 1)).
items.note: Printed without saying where the isomorphism lives; it holds on B°_{s°} ∩ ι°⁻¹M†_𝔭 (the Fermat hypersurface), where ω^⊥_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c}/ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞} is a line bundle; off the link that quotient is zero (see source issue). Proof: ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞} = ker β_{*,τ_∞} ≃ ζ*𝒪(p) (valid on all of B°_{s°}) and ω^⊥/ω ≃ H^⊥ ≃ ζ*𝒪(−1) (valid on the link). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Corollary 5.3.5 — normal bundle of the link in the ground stratum
items.statement: When N ⩾ 2, the normal bundle of the closed immersion m^{†•}: M†_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}) → M•_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}) is isomorphic to (m^{†°})^* 𝒪_{M°_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})}(−(p + 1)).
items.note: 𝒪_{M°}(1) means the tautological quotient line bundle transported from B° ≅ M° (fibrewise ζ°*𝒪_{ℙ(𝒱_{s°})}(1); cf. ξ in Definition 5.6.3). Proof: by Theorem 5.2.5(4,5) the normal bundle is ℋom(ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞}, ω^⊥_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c}/ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞}) restricted to M†; apply Theorem 5.3.4(2). Alternatively it is dual to the normal bundle of m^{†°}, which is 𝒪(p + 1) (hypersurface of degree p + 1). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Construction 5.3.6 — canonical uniformization of the balloon source
items.statement: Let K°_𝔮 be the stabilizer of Λ°_𝔮 for every 𝔮 | p and K°_p := ∏_{𝔮|p} K°_𝔮. Similarly to Construction 4.4.2 there is a canonical uniformization map υ°: S°_𝔭(V°, –)(𝔽̄_p) ≅ Sh(V°, –K°_p) × T_𝔭(𝔽̄_p) (5.4) in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗, Set)_{/T_𝔭(𝔽̄_p)}, which is an isomorphism, under which the induced action of Gal(𝔽̄_p/𝔽_p^Φ) on the target is trivial on Sh(V°, –K°_p).
items.note: Canonical because the tame level is defined through V° itself (Remark 5.2.2). Proof only by analogy with Construction 4.4.2. The Galois-triviality is an input to Lemma 5.6.2(3). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Construction 5.3.6 — Hecke correspondences on S°_𝔭
items.statement: Similarly to Construction 4.4.5 and Proposition 4.4.6, for every g ∈ K°_𝔭 \ U(V°)(F⁺_𝔭) / K°_𝔭 there is a Hecke correspondence Hk_g: S°_𝔭(V°, –)_g → S°_𝔭(V°, –) × S°_𝔭(V°, –), a morphism in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗, Sch_{/𝔽_p^Φ})_{/T_𝔭} that is finite étale and compatible with the uniformization map (5.4).
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 5.4.1 — ground source S•_𝔭(V°, –)
items.statement: Assume N ⩾ 2. Define S•_𝔭(V°, –): 𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗 → PSch′_{/𝔽_p^Φ}, where for S ∈ Sch′_{/𝔽_p^Φ}, S•_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(S) is the set of equivalence classes of sextuples (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A•, λ•, η^{p•}) with (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p) ∈ T_𝔭(S); (A•, λ•) a unitary O_F-abelian scheme of signature type NΦ over S such that ker λ•[p^∞] is trivial if N is even, resp. contained in A•[𝔭] of rank p² if N is odd; η^{p•}, for a chosen geometric point s on every connected component of S, a π₁(S, s)-invariant K^{p°}-orbit of isomorphisms η^{p•}: V° ⊗_ℚ 𝔸^{∞,p} → Hom^{ϖλ₀,λ•}_{F⊗_ℚ𝔸^{∞,p}}(H₁^{ét}(A_{0s}, 𝔸^{∞,p}), H₁^{ét}(A•_s, 𝔸^{∞,p})) of hermitian spaces. Equivalence and morphisms as in Definition 4.2.2. The forgetful morphism S•_𝔭(V°, –) → T_𝔭 is represented by finite étale schemes ([62, Theorem 4.4] and footnote 17).
items.note: Printed 'K^{p•}-orbit' is a misprint for K^{p°}-orbit (source issue). Footnote 16: ϖλ₀ (not λ₀) is used for compatibility with the polarization condition ϖ·λ = γ^∨∘λ•∘γ of Definition 5.4.2. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).
