items.name: §5.4 — the pairing {,}_{s•} and DL•_{s•}
items.statement: Let s• = (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A•, λ•, η^{p•}) ∈ S•_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(κ), κ perfect containing 𝔽_p^Φ. Then A•_κ[𝔭^∞] is supersingular, 𝕍: H₁^{dR}(A•/κ)_{τ_∞} → H₁^{dR}(A•/κ)_{τ_∞^c} is an isomorphism, and one defines {x, y}_{s•} := ⟨𝕍⁻¹x, y⟩_{λ•,τ_∞} on 𝒱_{s•} := H₁^{dR}(A•/κ)_{τ_∞^c}. The pair (𝒱_{s•}, {,}_{s•}) is admissible, DL•_{s•} := DL•(𝒱_{s•}, {,}_{s•}) (Definition A.2.1: pairs (H₁, H₂) of subbundles of ranks ⌈N/2⌉, ⌈N/2⌉ − 1 with 𝒱_S^⊣ ⊆ H₂ ⊆ H₁ ⊆ H₂^⊣, H₂ ⊆ H₁^⊣ ⊆ H₂^⊣), and dim_κ 𝒱_{s•}^⊥ equals 0 if N is even and 1 if N is odd.
items.note: Admissibility 'by the same proof as Lemma 4.3.2'. The radical 𝒱_{s•}^⊥ (written ^⊣ in Appendix A) is H₁^{dR}(A•/κ)^⊥_{τ_∞}, of dimension N − 2⌊N/2⌋. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 5.4.2 — ground correspondence space B•_𝔭(V°, –)
items.statement: Define B•_𝔭(V°, –): 𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗 → PSch′_{/𝔽_p^Φ}, where for S ∈ Sch′_{/𝔽_p^Φ}, B•_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(S) is the set of equivalence classes of decuples (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A, λ, η^p; A•, λ•, η^{p•}; γ) with (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A, λ, η^p) ∈ M•_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(S), (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A•, λ•, η^{p•}) ∈ S•_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(S), and γ: A → A• an O_F-linear quasi-p-isogeny such that (a) ker γ[p^∞] ⊆ A[𝔭]; (b) (ker γ_{*,τ_∞})^⊥ ⊆ ω_{A^∨/S,τ_∞^c}; (c) ker γ_{*,τ_∞} ⊇ H₁^{dR}(A/S)^⊥_{τ_∞^c}; (d) ϖ·λ = γ^∨ ∘ λ• ∘ γ; (e) the K^{p°}-orbit of v ↦ γ_* ∘ η^p(v), v ∈ V° ⊗_ℚ 𝔸^{∞,p}, coincides with η^{p•}. Equivalence and morphisms as in Definition 4.3.3.
items.note: Footnote 18: condition (c) is implied by the others when N is even (checked: with λ• perfect, (d) forces the radical of λ on the τ_∞ side into ker γ_{*,τ_∞}). (a) gives a unique quasi-p-isogeny γ̌: A• → A with γ̌∘γ = ϖ·id_A, γ∘γ̌ = ϖ·id_{A•}. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: (5.5) and Definition 5.4.3 — basic correspondence on the ground stratum
items.statement: The forgetful maps give S•_𝔭(V°, –) ←π•— B•_𝔭(V°, –) —ι•→ M•_𝔭(V°, –) (5.5) in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗, PSch′_{/𝔽_p^Φ})_{/T_𝔭}, called the basic correspondence on the ground stratum, with source S•_𝔭(V°, –).
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.4.4(1) — ground fibres are smooth; tangent sequence
items.statement: In (5.5), take s• ∈ S•_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(κ), κ perfect containing 𝔽_p^Φ, put B•_{s•} := π•⁻¹(s•) with universal object (𝒜, λ, η^p; γ). Then B•_{s•} is a smooth scheme over κ whose tangent sheaf fits canonically into an exact sequence 0 → ℋom(ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞}, ω^⊥_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c}/ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞}) → 𝒯_{B•_{s•}/κ} → ℋom(ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c}/(ker γ_{*,τ_∞})^⊥, Lie_{𝒜,τ_∞^c}) → 0 (printed with Lie_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c}, which the proof identifies with H₁^{dR}(𝒜)_{τ_∞^c}/ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c} = Lie_{𝒜,τ_∞^c}).
items.note: The paper prints Lie_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c} in the last term; from the proof (p. 206: 'Lie_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c} ≃ H₁^{dR}(𝒜)_{τ_∞^c}/ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c}') it means H₁^{dR}(𝒜)_{τ_∞^c}/ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c} = Lie_{𝒜,τ_∞^c} (Remark 3.4.6) — source issue. Ranks 1 and ⌊N/2⌋ − 1. Proof: lifting x amounts to lifting ω_{τ_∞^c} containing (ker γ_{*,τ_∞})^⊥ and then ω_{τ_∞} inside ω̂^⊥_{τ_∞^c} (conditions (a″)–(c″), p. 203). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.4.4(2) — ι• on a ground fibre and its normal sheaf
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 5.4.4, the restriction of ι•_κ to B•_{s•} is locally on B•_{s•} a closed immersion, with a canonical isomorphism for its normal sheaf 𝒩_{ι•_κ|B•_{s•}} ≃ ℋom((ker γ_{*,τ_∞})^⊥/H₁^{dR}(𝒜)^⊥_{τ_∞}, Lie_{𝒜,τ_∞^c}) ≃ (im γ_{*,τ_∞}) ⊗_{𝒪_{B•_{s•}}} Lie_{𝒜,τ_∞^c}. (Printed with Lie_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c} in both places; meaning H₁^{dR}(𝒜)_{τ_∞^c}/ω_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c} = Lie_{𝒜,τ_∞^c}.)
items.note: Printed with Lie_{𝒜^∨,τ_∞^c} (misprint, see (1)). Rank of the normal sheaf ⌈N/2⌉ − 1 = (N − 1) − ⌊N/2⌋. Proof (pp. 203–204) computes the tangent map via Theorem 5.2.5(4) and shows it is injective, with cokernel ℋom((im γ_{*,τ_∞})^∨, Lie); the 'locally a closed immersion' part is not argued beyond unramifiedness (see source issue). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.4.4(3) — image of the orthogonal of ker γ
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 5.4.4, γ_{*,τ_∞^c}((ker γ_{*,τ_∞})^⊥) = H₁^{dR}(A•/S)^⊥_{τ_∞}.
items.note: Proof (p. 204): λ∘γ̌ = γ^∨∘λ• gives (5.7) (ker γ_{*,τ_∞})^⊥ = γ_{*,τ_∞^c}⁻¹(H₁^{dR}(A•/S)^⊥_{τ_∞}); it remains that H₁^{dR}(A•/S)^⊥_{τ_∞} ⊆ im γ_{*,τ_∞^c} = ker γ̌_{*,τ_∞^c}, shown by a rank count using 5.4.2(c). Checked. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.4.4(4) — ground fibres are Deligne–Lusztig varieties DL•
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 5.4.4, the assignment sending (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A, λ, η^p; A•, λ•, η^{p•}; γ) ∈ B•_{s•}(S) to the subbundles H₁ := ((γ̌_{*,τ_∞})⁻¹ω_{A^∨/S,τ_∞})^⊥ ⊆ H₁^{dR}(A•/S)_{τ_∞^c} = (𝒱_{s•})_S and H₂ := γ_{*,τ_∞^c} ω_{A^∨/S,τ_∞^c} ⊆ (𝒱_{s•})_S, where γ̌: A• → A is the unique O_F-linear quasi-p-isogeny with γ̌∘γ = ϖ·id_A, induces an isomorphism ζ•_{s•}: B•_{s•} ≅ DL•_{s•} = DL•(𝒱_{s•}, {,}_{s•}). In particular, B•_{s•} is a geometrically irreducible projective smooth scheme in Sch_{/κ} of dimension ⌊N/2⌋.
items.note: Proof (pp. 204–207): ranks rank H₁ = ⌈N/2⌉, rank H₂ = ⌈N/2⌉ − 1; the inclusions of Definition A.2.1 (using (5.8)); bijectivity on points by reconstructing D_{A,τ_∞} := 𝕍⁻¹H̃₂, D_{A,τ_∞^c} := 𝔽H̃₁^c and checking F-, V-stability, kernel and polarization lengths; tangent isomorphism by the five lemma with Proposition A.2.2. Irreducibility and dimension from Proposition A.2.2(3) with d = N − 2⌊N/2⌋. Rank checks and lattice-length counts (2⌊N/2⌋+1, N+1, N−2⌊N/2⌋) verified. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.4.4(5) — the Lie line on a ground fibre
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 5.4.4, if (ℋ_{s•1}, ℋ_{s•2}) denotes the universal object over DL•_{s•}, there is a canonical isomorphism ζ•*_{s•}(ℋ^⊣_{s•1}/ℋ_{s•2}) ≃ ι•* Lie_{𝒜,τ_∞^c} of line bundles on B•_{s•}.
items.note: Proof: consequence of (5.8), im γ_{*,τ_∞^c} = H₁^⊣, via γ_{*,τ_∞^c}: H₁^{dR}(A)_{τ_∞^c}/ω_{A^∨,τ_∞^c} ≅ H₁^⊣/H₂. Here the paper writes Lie_{𝒜,τ_∞^c} (consistently with Remark 3.4.6). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: (5.6) — ranks of the kernels of γ_*
items.statement: For an S-point of B•_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}): rank_{𝒪_S}(ker γ_{*,τ_∞}) + rank_{𝒪_S}(ker γ_{*,τ_∞^c}) = 2⌊N/2⌋ + 1 and rank(ker γ_{*,τ_∞}) − rank(ker γ_{*,τ_∞^c}) = 1, hence rank(ker γ_{*,τ_∞}) = ⌈(N+1)/2⌉ and rank(ker γ_{*,τ_∞^c}) = ⌈(N−1)/2⌉. Under Definition 5.4.2(a,b,d), condition 5.4.2(c) is equivalent to (ker γ_{*,τ_∞})^⊥ being a subbundle of H₁^{dR}(A/S)_{τ_∞^c} of rank ⌈N/2⌉.
items.locator: §5.4, proof of Theorem 5.4.4, display (5.6), published p. 202
items.note: From Lemma 3.4.12(2,3) and Definition 5.4.2 (degree of γ from ϖλ = γ^∨λ•γ: p^{N+1} for N even, p^N for N odd). Verified. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: (5.7) and (5.8) — orthogonality identities on B•
items.statement: For an S-point of B•_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}): (5.7) (ker γ_{*,τ_∞})^⊥ = γ_{*,τ_∞^c}⁻¹(H₁^{dR}(A•/S)^⊥_{τ_∞}); and (5.8) im γ_{*,τ_∞^c} = H₁^⊣, where H₁ := ((γ̌_{*,τ_∞})⁻¹ω_{A^∨/S,τ_∞})^⊥ and ^⊣ is the right orthogonal for {,}_{s•}. Also im γ_{*,τ_∞^c} = ker γ̌_{*,τ_∞^c} and γ̌_{*,τ_∞}H₁^{dR}(A•)_{τ_∞} = ker γ_{*,τ_∞}.
items.locator: §5.4, proof of Theorem 5.4.4, displays (5.7), (5.8), published pp. 203–204
items.note: Used again in the proof of Theorem 5.5.3 and in §5.7. (5.8): im γ_{*,τ_∞^c} ⊆ 𝔽((H₁^{(p)})^⊥) ⇒ im γ_{*,τ_∞^c} ⊆ H₁^⊣, equality by ranks. Verified with Dieudonné lattices (for A• of signature NΦ, 𝔽 and 𝕍 map D(A•)_{τ_∞} bijectively onto D(A•)_{τ_∞^c} mod p). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Remark 5.4.5(1) — closed immersion for small level
items.statement: When K^{p°} is sufficiently small, the restriction of ι•_κ to B•_{s•} is a closed immersion for every point s• ∈ S•_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(κ) and every perfect field κ containing 𝔽_p^Φ.
items.note: No proof given. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Remark 5.4.5(2) — basic locus of the ground stratum
items.statement: One can show that the union of M†_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}) and the image of ι•: B•_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}) → M•_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}) is exactly the basic locus of M•_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}). In particular, as long as N ⩾ 5, the basic locus of M•_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}) is not equidimensional.
items.note: Stated without proof ('one can show'). Dimension check: M†_𝔭 has dimension N − 2 and the ι•-images have dimension ⌊N/2⌋ and are not contained in M† (they meet it in the divisor of Remark 5.5.4(2)); N − 2 > ⌊N/2⌋ iff N ⩾ 5. The existing paraphrase ('union of the balloon/link and the image of the ground correspondence') is corrected: the paper speaks of the basic locus of the GROUND stratum. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Construction 5.4.6 — uniformization and Hecke correspondences for S•_𝔭
items.statement: Choose an O_{F_𝔭}-lattice Λ•_𝔭 in V° ⊗_F F_𝔭 with Λ°_𝔭 ⊆ Λ•_𝔭 ⊆ p⁻¹Λ°_𝔭 and pΛ•_𝔭 ⊆ (Λ•_𝔭)^∨ such that (Λ•_𝔭)^∨/pΛ•_𝔭 has length 0 (N even), resp. 1 (N odd). Let K•_𝔭 be the stabilizer of Λ•_𝔭 and K•_p := K•_𝔭 × ∏_{𝔮|p, 𝔮≠𝔭} K°_𝔮. Similarly to Construction 4.4.2 there is a uniformization map υ•: S•_𝔭(V°, –)(𝔽̄_p) ≅ Sh(V°, –K•_p) × T_𝔭(𝔽̄_p) (5.9) in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗, Set)_{/T_𝔭(𝔽̄_p)}, an isomorphism under which Gal(𝔽̄_p/𝔽_p^Φ) acts trivially on Sh(V°, –K•_p). For every g ∈ K•_𝔭 \ U(V°)(F⁺_𝔭) / K•_𝔭 there is a finite étale Hecke correspondence Hk_g: S•_𝔭(V°, –)_g → S•_𝔭(V°, –) × S•_𝔭(V°, –) in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗, Sch_{/𝔽_p^Φ})_{/T_𝔭}, compatible with the uniformization map.
items.note: Length check: [Λ•:Λ°] = a forces length((Λ•)^∨/pΛ•) = N − 2a, so a = ⌊N/2⌋. Proof by analogy with Constructions 4.4.2, 4.4.5, Proposition 4.4.6. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 5.5.1 — link source S†_𝔭(V°, –)
items.statement: Assume N ⩾ 2. Define S†_𝔭(V°, –): 𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗 → PSch′_{/𝔽_p^Φ}, where for S ∈ Sch′_{/𝔽_p^Φ}, S†_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(S) is the set of equivalence classes of decuples (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A°, λ°, η^{p°}; A•, λ•, η^{p•}; ψ) with (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A°, λ°, η^{p°}) ∈ S°_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(S), (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A•, λ•, η^{p•}) ∈ S•_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(S), and ψ: A° → A• an O_F-linear quasi-p-isogeny such that (a) ker ψ[p^∞] ⊆ A°[𝔭]; (b) ϖ·λ° = ψ^∨ ∘ λ• ∘ ψ; (c) the K^{p°}-orbit of v ↦ ψ_* ∘ η^{p°}(v), v ∈ V° ⊗_ℚ 𝔸^{∞,p}, coincides with η^{p•}. Equivalence and morphisms as in Definition 4.3.3. The forgetful morphism S†_𝔭(V°, –) → T_𝔭 is represented by finite étale schemes, and there are forgetful morphisms s^{†°}: S†_𝔭(V°, –) → S°_𝔭(V°, –) and s^{†•}: S†_𝔭(V°, –) → S•_𝔭(V°, –) in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗, Sch_{/𝔽_p^Φ})_{/T_𝔭}.
items.note: Existing G22 bundled Definitions 5.5.1–5.5.2, Theorem 5.5.3 and Construction 5.5.5; split into G22, def-5-5-2, thm-5-5-3-1, thm-5-5-3-2, rem-5-5-4, constr-5-5-5. Finite étaleness is asserted without reference. Degree check: deg ψ = p^{2⌊N/2⌋}, and ker ψ_{*,τ_∞}, ker ψ_{*,τ_∞^c} both have rank ⌊N/2⌋. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

api.name: RankinSelberg.LinkCorrespondenceAndUniformization.data
api.statement: Use the factorization diagram and its universal property.

api.name: RankinSelberg.LinkCorrespondenceAndUniformization.characterisation
api.statement: Every geometric fibre over S† is P^(floor(N/2)−1).

api.name: RankinSelberg.LinkCorrespondenceAndUniformization.compatibility
api.statement: The map to the balloon fibre is a linear embedding and to the ground fibre is a regular divisor.

uses.how: Use the factorization diagram and its universal property.

items.name: Definition 5.5.2 and (5.10) — link correspondence space B†_𝔭(V°, –)
items.statement: B†_𝔭(V°, –) is the limit, in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗, Sch_{/𝔽_p^Φ})_{/T_𝔭}, of the diagram formed by S°_𝔭 ←π°— B°_𝔭 —ι°→ M°_𝔭, S•_𝔭 ←π•— B•_𝔭 —ι•→ M•_𝔭, s^{†°}, s^{†•}: S†_𝔭 → S°_𝔭, S•_𝔭 and m^{†°}, m^{†•}: M†_𝔭 → M°_𝔭, M•_𝔭. It comes with morphisms π†: B†_𝔭 → S†_𝔭, ι†: B†_𝔭 → M†_𝔭, b^{†°}: B†_𝔭 → B°_𝔭, b^{†•}: B†_𝔭 → B•_𝔭 making the oblique diagram (5.10) commute.
items.locator: §5.5, Definition 5.5.2 (a Definition, not a Construction) and display (5.10), published p. 209
items.note: Concretely (proof of Theorem 5.5.3) an S-point is a pair ((…; A°, λ°, η^{p°}; β), (…; A•, λ•, η^{p•}; γ)) over the same (A, λ, η^p) ∈ M†, with γ = ψ∘β. The reason for the oblique drawing is explained in §5.10. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.5.3(1) — the link square is Cartesian
items.statement: In the diagram (5.10), the square with B†_𝔭(V°, –) —ι†→ M†_𝔭(V°, –), b^{†•}: B†_𝔭 → B•_𝔭, m^{†•}: M†_𝔭 → M•_𝔭 and B•_𝔭(V°, –) —ι•→ M•_𝔭(V°, –) is Cartesian.
items.note: Proof (p. 210): for a point of M†(S) ×_{M•(S)} B•(S) = B°(S) ×_{M(S)} B•(S), ψ := γ∘β⁻¹ is a quasi-p-isogeny because ker β_{*,τ_∞} = ω_{A^∨,τ_∞} ⊆ ker γ (as ω_{A•^∨,τ_∞} = 0) and β_{*,τ_∞^c} is an isomorphism. Condition (a) of Definition 5.5.1 follows from ψ̌ψ = ϖ (not spelled out). Checked. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.5.3(2) — link fibres are projective spaces
items.statement: Take s† = (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A°, λ°, η^{p°}; A•, λ•, η^{p•}; ψ) ∈ S†_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(κ), κ perfect containing 𝔽_p^Φ. Put B†_{s†} := π†⁻¹(s†) and 𝒱_{s†} := (im ψ_{*,τ_∞^c})/H₁^{dR}(A•/κ)^⊥_{τ_∞}, which has dimension ⌊N/2⌋. Then the assignment sending ((A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A, λ, η^p; A°, λ°, η^{p°}; β), (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A, λ, η^p; A•, λ•, η^{p•}; γ)) ∈ B†_{s†}(S) (with γ = ψ∘β) to (γ_{*,τ_∞^c} ω_{A^∨/S,τ_∞^c})/H₁^{dR}(A•/S)^⊥_{τ_∞} induces an isomorphism ζ†_{s†}: B†_{s†} ≅ ℙ(𝒱_{s†}).
items.note: Proof: ι•(x•) ∈ M† iff H₁ = H₁^⊣ (using (5.8)); on B†_{s†}, H₁ = im ψ_{*,τ_∞^c} (rank ⌈N/2⌉ by Lemma 3.4.12(2,3)); combine with Theorem 5.4.4(4). So B†_{s†} is the locus of hyperplanes H₂/rad in the fixed space H₁/rad. dim 𝒱_{s†} = ⌈N/2⌉ − (N − 2⌊N/2⌋) = ⌊N/2⌋ checked. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Remark 5.5.4 — link fibres inside balloon and ground fibres
items.statement: For every s† ∈ S†_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(κ), with s° := s^{†°}(s†) and s• := s^{†•}(s†): (1) the morphism ζ°_{s°} ∘ b^{†°} ∘ (ζ†_{s†})⁻¹ identifies ℙ(𝒱_{s†}) with the closed subscheme of ℙ(𝒱_{s°}) induced by the obvious κ-linear surjection 𝒱_{s°} → 𝒱_{s†}; (2) the morphism ζ•_{s•} ∘ b^{†•} ∘ (ζ†_{s†})⁻¹ identifies ℙ(𝒱_{s†}) with the closed subscheme (of codimension one) of DL•(𝒱_{s•}, {,}_{s•}) defined by the condition H₁ = H₁^⊣.
items.note: Follows from the proof of Theorem 5.5.3. The surjection in (1) is ψ_{*,τ_∞^c} followed by the quotient by H₁^{dR}(A•)^⊥_{τ_∞}. ℙ(𝒱_{s†}) has dimension ⌊N/2⌋ − 1, so in (1) it is a maximal linear subspace of the Fermat hypersurface DL_{s°} when N is even. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Construction 5.5.5 — uniformization of the link source
items.statement: Put K†_p := K°_p ∩ K•_p. Similarly to Construction 4.4.2 there is a uniformization map υ†: S†_𝔭(V°, –)(𝔽̄_p) ≅ Sh(V°, –K†_p) × T_𝔭(𝔽̄_p) (5.11) in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗, Set)_{/T_𝔭(𝔽̄_p)}, an isomorphism under which Gal(𝔽̄_p/𝔽_p^Φ) acts trivially on Sh(V°, –K†_p).
items.note: K†_𝔭 is the stabilizer of the pair Λ°_𝔭 ⊆ Λ•_𝔭 of Construction 5.4.6. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: §5.6 — the principal congruence subgroup K°_{𝔭1}
items.statement: Assume N ⩾ 2. The natural action of K°_𝔭 = U(Λ°_𝔭)(O_{F⁺_𝔭}) on B°_𝔭(V°, –) (unlike on S°_𝔭(V°, –)) is nontrivial, and factors through the quotient U(Λ°_𝔭)(O_{F⁺_𝔭}) → U(Λ°_𝔭)(𝔽_p). K°_{𝔭1} denotes the kernel of the reduction map K°_𝔭 = U(Λ°_𝔭)(O_{F⁺_𝔭}) → U(Λ°_𝔭)(𝔽_p).
items.note: The factorization is justified only by the isomorphism of item constr-5-6-1-balloon ('as we will see'). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Construction 5.6.1 — level-𝔭 balloon source S°_{𝔭1}(V°, –) and its Hecke correspondences
items.statement: Define S°_{𝔭1}(V°, –): 𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗 → PSch′_{/𝔽_p^Φ}, K^{p°} ↦ S°_{𝔭1}(V°, K^{p°}), where for S ∈ Sch′_{/𝔽_p^Φ}, S°_{𝔭1}(V°, K^{p°})(S) is the set of equivalence classes of septuples (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A°, λ°, η^{p°}; η°_𝔭) with (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p; A°, λ°, η^{p°}) ∈ S°_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(S) and η°_𝔭, for a chosen geometric point s on every connected component of S, an isomorphism η°_𝔭: Λ°_𝔭 ⊗ 𝔽_p → Hom_{O_F}(A_{0s}[𝔭], A°_s[𝔭]) of hermitian spaces over O_{F_𝔭} ⊗ 𝔽_p, the target carrying the hermitian form constructed as in Construction 3.4.4 with respect to (λ₀, λ°). Equivalence and morphisms as in Definition 4.2.2. U(Λ°_𝔭)(𝔽_p) acts further on S°_{𝔭1}(V°, –), and, similarly to Construction 4.4.5 and Proposition 4.4.6, for every g ∈ K°_{𝔭1} \ U(V°)(F⁺_𝔭) / K°_{𝔭1} there is a finite étale Hecke correspondence Hk_g: S°_{𝔭1}(V°, –)_g → S°_{𝔭1}(V°, –) × S°_{𝔭1}(V°, –) (5.12) in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗, Sch_{/𝔽_p^Φ})_{/T_𝔭}.
items.note: The display prints K^{p°} ↦ S°_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}) for S°_{𝔭1}(V°, K^{p°}), and the π₁(S, s)-invariance of η°_𝔭 is not stated (source issue). The level structure η°_𝔭 provides a κ-rational 𝔽_{p²}-structure on balloon fibres, the natural input for Lemma 5.6.2(3). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Construction 5.6.1 — B°_𝔭 as an induced projective bundle; Hecke on B°_𝔭
items.statement: Theorem 5.3.4 gives a canonical isomorphism B°_𝔭(V°, –) ≃ S°_{𝔭1}(V°, –) ×^{U(Λ°_𝔭)(𝔽_p)} ℙ(Λ°_𝔭 ⊗ 𝔽_p) in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗, Sch_{/𝔽_p^Φ})_{/T_𝔭}. Consequently, for every g ∈ K°_{𝔭1} \ U(V°)(F⁺_𝔭) / K°_{𝔭1}, (5.12) induces a finite étale Hecke correspondence Hk_g: B°_𝔭(V°, –)_g → B°_𝔭(V°, –) × B°_𝔭(V°, –) in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗, Sch_{/𝔽_p^Φ})_{/T_𝔭}.
items.note: The identification of 𝒱_{s°} = H₁^{dR}(A°/κ)_{τ_∞^c} with (Λ°_𝔭 ⊗ 𝔽_p) ⊗_{𝔽_{p²}} κ (up to a line twist) via η°_𝔭 and Dieudonné theory of A°[𝔭] is left implicit. Under it the link becomes S°_{𝔭1} ×^{U} Iso(Λ̄°_𝔭), the Fermat hypersurface of Appendix C.2 (used in the proof of Proposition 5.6.4). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 5.6.2(1) — cohomology of the link away from the middle degree
items.statement: Let L be a p-coprime coefficient ring. If p + 1 is invertible in L, then the restriction map (m^{†°})^*: H^i_𝔗(M̄°_𝔭(V°, –), L) → H^i_𝔗(M̄†_𝔭(V°, –), L) is an isomorphism for every integer i ∉ {N − 2, 2N − 2}. In particular, H^i_𝔗(M̄°_𝔭(V°, –), L) and H^i_𝔗(M̄†_𝔭(V°, –), L) vanish if i is odd and different from N − 2.
items.note: Proof: by Theorem 5.3.4, over each s° ∈ S°_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(𝔽̄_p) the map is the restriction ℙ(𝒱) ⊇ DL(𝒱, {,}, N−1) of Lemma A.1.4, and (1) follows from Lemma A.1.4(2) (weak Lefschetz plus Gysin; cup with c₁(𝒪(p+1)) invertible since p+1 ∈ L^×). Checked, including N = 2. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 5.6.2(2) — freeness
items.statement: Let L be a p-coprime coefficient ring. For every i ∈ ℤ, both H^i_𝔗(M̄°_𝔭(V°, –), L) and H^i_𝔗(M̄†_𝔭(V°, –), L) are free L-modules.
items.note: No hypothesis that p + 1 ∈ L^× is made here, but the cited Lemma A.1.4(3) assumes it, and A.1.4(3) is called 'an immediate consequence of (2)', which does not cover the middle degree N − 2. The statement is nevertheless true: integral weak Lefschetz and Gysin, plus Poincaré duality for torsion (H^{N−2}_{tors} ≅ H^{N−1}_{tors} ≅ H^{N+1}(ℙ^{N−1}, ℤ_ℓ)_{tors} = 0), make H^*(Fermat, ℤ_ℓ) torsion-free for every ℓ ≠ p (source issue, gap). Freeness of 𝔗-invariants also uses the free 𝔗-action on components (implicit). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 5.6.2(3) — Galois action on middle link cohomology (N even)
items.statement: Let L be a p-coprime coefficient ring. When N is even, the action of Gal(𝔽̄_p/𝔽_p^Φ) on H^{N−2}_𝔗(M̄†_𝔭(V°, –), L((N−2)/2)) is trivial.
items.note: The paper states this for the actual link stratum, with no 𝔽_{p²}-model hypothesis and no assumption p + 1 ∈ L^×. Proof: 'follows from Lemma A.1.4(4) and Construction 5.3.6'. Lemma A.1.4(4) (p. 323) asserts triviality for EVERY pair (𝒱, {,}) over κ with 𝒱^⊣ = 0, which is false in general (E9: the 𝔽_{p²}-structure of an admissible pair is only defined over κ̄). An earlier version of this extraction's restatement ('for an actual split hermitian 𝔽_{p²}-model') is a repair, not the printed statement. For the Shimura fibres the needed descent is available through the level structure η°_𝔭 of Construction 5.6.1 once one knows that Frobenius fixes η°_𝔭 — see source issue (gap in the proof). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 5.6.3 — the tautological class ξ
items.statement: ξ ∈ H²_𝔗(B̄°_𝔭(V°, –), L(1)) is the first Chern class of the tautological quotient line bundle on B̄°_𝔭(V°, –); that is, in the situation of Theorem 5.3.4, the restriction of ξ to B°_{s°} is (the Chern class of) ζ°*_{s°}𝒪_{ℙ(𝒱_{s°})}(1) for every K^{p°} ∈ 𝔎(V°)^p and every s° ∈ S°_𝔭(V°, K^{p°})(𝔽̄_p).
items.note: ι°_!ξ ∈ H²_𝔗(M̄°_𝔭(V°, –), L(1)) is its transport along the isomorphism ι° (Theorem 5.3.4). The same ξ is used in §5.8 (incidence maps). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 5.6.3 — primitive cohomology of the link stratum
items.statement: For a coefficient ring L and i ∈ ℤ, the primitive cohomology H^prim(M̄†_𝔭(V°, –), L(i)) is the kernel of ∪(m^{†°*} ι°_! ξ): H^{N−2}_𝔗(M̄†_𝔭(V°, –), L(i)) → H^N_𝔗(M̄†_𝔭(V°, –), L(i + 1)), which is canonically a direct summand of H^{N−2}_𝔗(M̄†_𝔭(V°, –), L(i)).
items.note: Printed definition is the cup-product (hard-Lefschetz) kernel INSIDE the link. For N ⩾ 3 (and p + 1 ∈ L^× when N ⩾ 4) it equals the kernel of the Gysin map m^{†°}_!: H^{N−2}_𝔗(M̄†) → H^N_𝔗(M̄°)(1). For N = 2 (fibres = p + 1 points, H² = 0) the printed kernel is all of H⁰_𝔗(M̄†), which contains the constants; the intended object is the kernel of the trace/Gysin map (reduced H⁰). This is the §5.6 manifestation of E10 — see source issue. An earlier version of this extraction's statement (Gysin kernel) is the repair, not the printed definition. The 'canonically a direct summand' claim uses p + 1 ∈ L^× for the canonical splitting. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proposition 5.6.4 — primitive link cohomology as automorphic forms (5.13)
items.statement: Take K^{p°} ∈ 𝔎(V°)^p, a rational prime ℓ ≠ p and an isomorphism ι_ℓ: ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_ℓ. Then there is an isomorphism ι_ℓ⁻¹H^prim(M̄†_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}), ℚ̄_ℓ) ≃ Map_{K°_𝔭}(U(V°)(F⁺)\U(V°)(𝔸^∞_{F⁺})/K^{p°}∏_{𝔮|p,𝔮≠𝔭}K°_𝔮, Ω_N) (5.13) of ℂ[K^{p°}K°_{p1}\U(V°)(𝔸^∞_{F⁺})/K^{p°}K°_{p1}]-modules, where K°_{p1} := K°_{𝔭1} × ∏_{𝔮|p,𝔮≠𝔭} K°_𝔮 and Ω_N is the Tate–Thompson representation of K°_𝔭 (inflated from U(Λ°_𝔭)(𝔽_p) = K°_𝔭/K°_{𝔭1}) introduced in Appendix C.2.
items.locator: §5.6, Proposition 5.6.4 (a Proposition, not a Lemma), display (5.13), published p. 213
items.note: Proof (p. 213): H^{N−2}_𝔗(M̄†) is a module over the level-K°_{p1} Hecke algebra (Construction 5.6.1); for the base point s₀ ∈ S°_𝔭(𝔽̄_p) corresponding to the unit element in (5.4), H^prim_{s₀} := H^prim ∩ H^{N−2}(M̄† ∩ π°⁻¹(s₀)) is a U(Λ°_𝔭)(𝔽_p)-representation isomorphic to ι_ℓΩ_N. Appendix C.2 defines Ω_N as the unique irreducible representation isomorphic to the cup-kernel H^prim of the Fermat hypersurface (citing Tate–Thompson/[31]). For N = 2 this cup-kernel is the (p+1)-dimensional permutation representation, which is reducible, so (5.13) fails at N = 2 as printed (see source issue; E10). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Proposition 5.6.4 — local components of constituents of primitive link cohomology
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 5.6.4, let π^{∞,p} be an irreducible admissible representation of U(V°)(𝔸^{∞,p}_{F⁺}) such that (π^{∞,p})^{K^{p°}} is a constituent of ι_ℓ⁻¹H^prim(M̄†_𝔭(V°, K^{p°}), ℚ̄_ℓ). Then π^{∞,p} can be completed to an automorphic representation π = π^{∞,p} ⊗ π_∞ ⊗ ⊗_{𝔮|p} π_𝔮 of U(V°)(𝔸_{F⁺}) such that π_∞ is trivial, π_𝔮 is unramified for 𝔮 ≠ 𝔭, and (1) when N is even, π_𝔭 is a constituent of an unramified principal series; (2) when N is odd, BC(π_𝔭) is a constituent of an unramified principal series of GL_N(F_𝔭) whose Satake parameter contains {−p, −p⁻¹}.
items.note: Proof (p. 214): by (5.13) one gets π with π_𝔭|_{K°_𝔭} ⊇ Ω_N. (1) Ω_N has nonzero Borel-fixed vectors (Proposition C.2.1(2)), so π_𝔭 has Iwahori-fixed vectors. (2) N = 3: π_𝔭 = c-Ind_{K₃}^{U₃}Ω₃ by Proposition C.2.1(3) and [55, Theorem 6.11(2)], irreducible supercuspidal by [55, Proposition 6.6], equal to Rogawski's π^s(𝟏) [63, Proposition 13.1.3(d)], whose base change has Satake parameter {−p, 1, −p⁻¹} [63, Proposition 13.2.2(c)]; general N = 2r+1: by Proposition C.2.1(4) and [55, Theorem 6.11(2)], π_𝔭 is a constituent of the normalized parabolic induction of π^s(𝟏) ⊠ χ₁ ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ χ_{r−1} with unramified χ_i, then compatibility of base change with induction. Statement (1) remains true at N = 2 even with the printed cup-kernel (the extra trivial constituent is also spherical). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Moy–Prasad, Theorem 6.11(2) (black box)
items.statement: Used as: (N = 3) an irreducible smooth representation π_𝔭 of U(V°)(F⁺_𝔭) whose restriction to K°_𝔭 contains (the inflation of) the cuspidal unipotent representation Ω₃ of U₃(𝔽_p) is c-Ind_{K₃}^{U₃}Ω₃; (N = 2r + 1) if π_𝔭|_{K°_𝔭} contains Ω_N, which by Proposition C.2.1(4) is a constituent of a parabolic induction from a Levi with factor Ū₃ and cuspidal datum Ω₃ ⊠ 𝟏, then π_𝔭 is a constituent of the normalized parabolic induction of π^s(𝟏) ⊠ χ₁ ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ χ_{r−1} for some unramified characters χ_i.

items.name: Definition 5.7.1 — the functors S•_𝔭(V°,−)_j and the Hecke morphisms Hk_j
items.statement: Setting of §5 (§5.1, §5.4): 𝔭 is a special inert prime of F⁺ with underlying rational prime p (odd, unramified in F, F⁺_𝔭 = Q_p, 𝔭 inert in F); V° is a standard definite hermitian space over F of rank N ⩾ 2 with self-dual lattices Λ°_𝔮 (𝔮 | p); K^{p°} ∈ 𝔎(V°)^p; κ is a perfect field containing F_p^Φ. For every integer 0 ⩽ j ⩽ N define a functor S•_𝔭(V°,−)_j : 𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗 → PSch′_{/F_p^Φ}, K^{p°} ↦ S•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})_j, such that for every S ∈ Sch′_{/F_p^Φ}, S•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})_j(S) is the set of equivalence classes of decuples (A₀,λ₀,η₀^p; A•₁,λ•₁,η₁^{p•}; A•₂,λ•₂,η₂^{p•}; φ•) where: • (A₀,λ₀,η₀^p; A•_i,λ•_i,η_i^{p•}) ∈ S•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})(S) for i = 1,2 (Definition 5.4.1); and • φ• : A•₁ → A•₂ is an O_F-linear quasi-isogeny such that (a) pφ•∘λ•₁^{−1} is a quasi-p-isogeny, and ker(pφ•)[𝔭] has rank p^{2(N−j)}; (b) φ•[𝔮^∞] is an isomorphism for every prime 𝔮 ≠ 𝔭 of F⁺ above p; (c) φ•^∨∘λ•₂∘φ• = λ•₁; (d) the K^{p°}-orbit of the maps v ↦ φ•_*∘η₁^{p•}(v), v ∈ V°⊗_Q A^{∞,p}, coincides with η₂^{p•}. The equivalence relation and the action of morphisms in 𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗 are as in Definition 4.3.3. Finally Hk_j : S•_𝔭(V°,−)_j → S•_𝔭(V°,−) × S•_𝔭(V°,−) is the morphism in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p × 𝔗, Sch_{/F_p^Φ})_{/T_𝔭} sending (A₀,λ₀,η₀^p; A•₁,λ•₁,η₁^{p•}; A•₂,λ•₂,η₂^{p•}; φ•) to ((A₀,λ₀,η₀^p; A•₁,λ•₁,η₁^{p•}), (A₀,λ₀,η₀^p; A•₂,λ•₂,η₂^{p•})).
items.note: S•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°}) is the source of the basic correspondence on the ground stratum (Definition 5.4.1): (A•,λ•) unitary O_F-abelian scheme of signature type N with ker λ•[p^∞] trivial (N even) or contained in A•[𝔭] of rank p² (N odd). A quasi-p-isogeny is a quasi-isogeny φ with cφ an isogeny for some c ∈ Z_(p)^× (Definition 3.4.5). The index j is the relative position: s• ∈ S•_j corresponds, via Dieudonné theory, to lattices in relative position ϖ^{t_j}, t_j = (1^j, 0^{N−2j}, (−1)^j) (Notation B.2.1): pφ• has elementary divisors p², p, 1 with multiplicities j, N−2j, j, so ker(pφ•)[𝔭] has rank p^{2(N−j)}. The paper uses this identification of Hk_j with the Hecke operator T•_{N,𝔭;j} implicitly in Propositions 5.8.6, 5.8.8, 5.8.9. By Lemma 5.7.3, S•_j = ∅ for j > ⌊N/2⌋. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Remark 5.7.2 — Hk_j are closed immersions with disjoint images
items.statement: When K^{p°} is sufficiently small, the morphism Hk_j : S•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})_j → S•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°}) × S•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°}) is a closed immersion for every j, and the images of Hk_j for all j are mutually disjoint.
items.note: Stated without proof. Disjointness of the images is the uniqueness of j (the relative position of the two lattices); the closed-immersion claim needs K^{p°} neat enough that a pair (s•₁, s•₂) determines φ•. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Kernel of pφ• and image of pφ•^{−1} on de Rham homology
items.statement: Let s• = (A₀,λ₀,η₀^p; A•₁,λ•₁,η₁^{p•}; A•₂,λ•₂,η₂^{p•}; φ•) ∈ S•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})_j(κ). By Definition 5.7.1(c), (pφ•∘λ•₁^{−1})^∨ = pφ•^{−1}∘λ•₂^{−1}; thus pφ•^{−1}∘λ•₂^{−1}, hence pφ•^{−1}, are quasi-p-isogenies. For every τ ∈ Σ_∞ put ker(pφ•)_{*,τ} := ker((pφ•)_{*,τ} : H^dR_1(A•₁/κ)_τ → H^dR_1(A•₂/κ)_τ) and im(pφ•^{−1})_{*,τ} := im((pφ•^{−1})_{*,τ} : H^dR_1(A•₂/κ)_τ → H^dR_1(A•₁/κ)_τ).
items.note: For F ⊆ H^dR_1(A/κ)_τ, F^⊥ ⊆ H^dR_1(A/κ)_{τ^c} is the right orthogonal complement under the pairing ⟨ , ⟩_{λ,τ} : H^dR_1(A)_τ × H^dR_1(A)_{τ^c} → κ induced by λ (Notation 3.4.7); H^dR_1(A•₁/κ)^⊥_τ := (H^dR_1(A•₁/κ)_τ)^⊥ ⊆ H^dR_1(A•₁/κ)_{τ^c} is the radical, which is 0 if N is even (λ•₁ p-principal) and a line if N is odd. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 5.7.3(1),(2) — image inside kernel; dimension of the kernel
items.statement: For s• = (…; φ•) ∈ S•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})_j(κ) (κ perfect containing F_p^Φ): (1) im(pφ•^{−1})_{*,τ} ⊆ ker(pφ•)_{*,τ} for every τ ∈ Σ_∞; (2) dim_κ ker(pφ•)_{*,τ} = N − j for τ ∈ {τ_∞, τ_∞^c}.
items.note: (1) since (pφ•)∘(pφ•^{−1}) = p². (2): Definition 5.7.1(a) gives dim ker(pφ•)_{*,τ_∞} + dim ker(pφ•)_{*,τ_∞^c} = 2(N−j), and the Verschiebung isomorphisms V : H^dR_1(A•_i/κ)_{τ_∞} → H^dR_1(A•_i/κ)_{τ_∞^c} (i = 1,2), which commute with (pφ•)_*, make the two dimensions equal. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 5.7.3(3),(4) — the image meets the radical trivially and is orthogonal to the kernel
items.statement: For s• = (…; φ•) ∈ S•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})_j(κ): (3) im(pφ•^{−1})_{*,τ} ∩ H^dR_1(A•₁/κ)^⊥_{τ^c} = 0 for τ ∈ {τ_∞, τ_∞^c}; (4) (im(pφ•^{−1})_{*,τ})^⊥ = ker(pφ•)_{*,τ^c} for τ ∈ {τ_∞, τ_∞^c}, orthogonal complements taken with respect to λ•₁.
items.note: (3): reduce to τ = τ_∞ via V; regarding D(A•₂) ⊂ D(A•₁)_Q via φ•, one has pD(A•₂)_{τ_∞} ⊆ D(A•₁)_{τ_∞} ⊆ D(A•₂)^∨_{τ_∞^c}; a nonzero element of the intersection gives x ∈ D(A•₂)_{τ_∞} ∩ (D(A•₁)^∨_{τ_∞^c} ∖ D(A•₁)_{τ_∞}) with ⟨x, Vx⟩ both integral and non-integral. Trivial for N even. (4): λ•₁∘φ•^{−1} = φ•^∨∘λ•₂ gives (im(pφ•^{−1})_{*,τ})^⊥ = ((pφ•)_{*,τ^c})^{−1}H^dR_1(A•₂/κ)^⊥_τ, which equals ker(pφ•)_{*,τ^c} by (3) applied with the roles of A•₁, A•₂ exchanged (φ• replaced by φ•^{−1}); the paper just says 'by (3)'. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 5.7.3(5) — dimension of the image; emptiness of S•_j for j > ⌊N/2⌋
items.statement: For s• = (…; φ•) ∈ S•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})_j(κ): (5) dim_κ im(pφ•^{−1})_{*,τ} = j for τ ∈ {τ_∞, τ_∞^c}. In particular, S•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})_j is empty if j > ⌊N/2⌋.
items.locator: §5.7, Lemma 5.7.3(5) and final claim, published p. 216
items.note: (5) from (2),(3),(4); the last claim from (1),(2),(5): j ⩽ N − j. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: The hermitian space (𝒱_{s•}, { , }_{s•}) attached to s• ∈ S•_j(κ)
items.statement: For s• ∈ S•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})_j(κ) and τ ∈ {τ_∞, τ_∞^c} put H^dR_1(φ•)_τ := ker(pφ•)_{*,τ} / im(pφ•^{−1})_{*,τ} (well defined by Lemma 5.7.3(1,4)). ⟨ , ⟩_{λ•₁,τ_∞} induces a κ-bilinear pairing ⟨ , ⟩_{λ•₁,τ_∞} : H^dR_1(φ•)_{τ_∞} × H^dR_1(φ•)_{τ_∞^c} → κ. The (κ,σ^{−1})-linear Verschiebung V : H^dR_1(A•₁/κ)_{τ_∞} → H^dR_1(A•₁/κ)_{τ_∞^c} induces a (κ,σ^{−1})-linear isomorphism V : H^dR_1(φ•)_{τ_∞} → H^dR_1(φ•)_{τ_∞^c}. Define { , }_{s•} : H^dR_1(φ•)_{τ_∞^c} × H^dR_1(φ•)_{τ_∞^c} → κ by {x,y}_{s•} := ⟨V^{−1}x, y⟩_{λ•₁,τ_∞}, and put 𝒱_{s•} := H^dR_1(φ•)_{τ_∞^c}.
items.note: { , }_{s•} is (κ,σ)-linear in the first variable and κ-linear in the second (conventions of Appendix A.1). It is the subquotient of the pairing { , }_{s•₁} on 𝒱_{s•₁} = H^dR_1(A•₁/κ)_{τ_∞^c} of §5.4. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 5.7.4 — (𝒱_{s•}, { , }_{s•}) is admissible; DL•(𝒱_{s•}) irreducible of dimension ⌊N/2⌋ − j
items.statement: Let s• ∈ S•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})_j(κ) and suppose that j ⩽ ⌊N/2⌋ − 1. The pair (𝒱_{s•}, { , }_{s•}) is admissible of rank N − 2j (Definition A.1.1) satisfying dim_κ 𝒱_{s•}^⊣ = N − 2⌊N/2⌋. In particular, the Deligne–Lusztig variety DL•(𝒱_{s•}, { , }_{s•}) ∈ Sch_{/κ} (Definition A.2.1) is a geometrically irreducible smooth projective scheme of dimension ⌊N/2⌋ − j.
items.note: dim 𝒱_{s•} = N − 2j by Lemma 5.7.3(2,5); dim 𝒱^⊣ by Lemma 5.7.3(3,4); then Proposition A.2.2(2),(3) (N − 2j ⩾ 2 and d = (N−2j) − 2⌊(N−2j)/2⌋). The proof does not argue admissibility; it follows because ker(pφ•)_* and im(pφ•^{−1})_* are stable under the σ²-linear bijection V^{−1}F whose fixed points give the F_{p²}-structure of 𝒱_{s•₁} (proof of Lemma 4.3.2). DL•(𝒱,{,})(S) = pairs (H₁,H₂) of subbundles of ranks ⌈N′/2⌉, ⌈N′/2⌉ − 1 (N′ = dim 𝒱) with 𝒱^⊣_S ⊆ H₂ ⊆ H₁, H₂ ⊆ H₁^⊣, H₁ ⊆ H₂^⊣. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: The intersection B•_{s•₁,s•₂} of two ground-stratum fibres
items.statement: Given two (possibly equal) points s•₁, s•₂ ∈ S•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})(κ), put B•_{s•₁,s•₂} := B•_{s•₁} ×_{M•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})_κ} B•_{s•₂}, the (possibly empty) fibre product of ι•_κ|B•_{s•₁} and ι•_κ|B•_{s•₂}, where B•_{s•} = π•^{−1}(s•) is the fibre of the basic correspondence S•_𝔭 ←π•− B•_𝔭 −ι•→ M•_𝔭 (5.5). For a connected S ∈ Sch′_{/κ}, a point x ∈ B•_{s•₁,s•₂}(S) is represented by a quattuordecuple (A₀,λ₀,η₀^p; A,λ,η^p; A•₁,λ•₁,η₁^{p•}; γ₁; A•₂,λ•₂,η₂^{p•}; γ₂) with γ_i : A → A•_i as in Definition 5.4.2.
items.note: M•_𝔭 is the ground stratum of the strictly semistable model M_𝔭(V°,−) (Definition 5.2.3, Theorem 5.2.5); B•_{s•} ≃ DL•(𝒱_{s•},{,}_{s•}) via ζ•_{s•} (Theorem 5.4.4(4)), with universal subbundles H₁ := ((γ̆_{*,τ_∞})^{−1}ω_{A^∨/S,τ_∞})^⊥ and H₂ := γ_{*,τ_∞^c}ω_{A^∨/S,τ_∞^c} of H^dR_1(A•/S)_{τ_∞^c}. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 5.7.5 — relative position of a point of B•_{s•₁,s•₂} and the flag (5.14)
items.statement: Let S ∈ Sch′_{/κ} be connected and x ∈ B•_{s•₁,s•₂}(S) represented by (A₀,λ₀,η₀^p; A,λ,η^p; A•₁,λ•₁,η₁^{p•}; γ₁; A•₂,λ•₂,η₂^{p•}; γ₂). There exists a unique integer j with 0 ⩽ j ⩽ ⌊N/2⌋ − 1 such that s• := (A₀,λ₀,η₀^p; A•₁,λ•₁,η₁^{p•}; A•₂,λ•₂,η₂^{p•}; φ•) is an element of S•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})_j(S), where φ• := γ₂∘γ₁^{−1}. Moreover, im(pφ•^{−1})_{*,τ_∞^c} ⊆ H₂ ⊆ H₁ ⊆ ker(pφ•)_{*,τ_∞^c} (5.14), where H₂ ⊆ H₁ ⊆ H^dR_1(A•₁/S)_{τ_∞^c} are the subbundles of Theorem 5.4.4(4) for the image of x in B•_{s•₁}(S).
items.note: j is determined by the rank of ker(pφ•)[𝔭] = ker(γ₂∘γ̆₁)[𝔭] (γ̆₁∘γ₁ = ϖ); pφ•∘λ•₁^{−1} = γ₂∘γ̆₁∘λ•₁^{−1} is a quasi-p-isogeny by Theorem 5.4.4(4) and Definition 5.4.2(c); the bound j ⩽ ⌊N/2⌋ − 1 is proved by a rank count whose written form is wrong for N even (see source issue), though the bound holds; (5.14) from Lemma 5.7.3(4). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 5.7.6 — decomposition map and the components B•_{s•}
items.statement: By Lemma 5.7.5 there is a morphism B•_{s•₁,s•₂} → ⨆_{j=0}^{⌊N/2⌋−1} Hk_j^{−1}(s•₁,s•₂). For a point s• ∈ Hk_j^{−1}(s•₁,s•₂)(κ) with 0 ⩽ j ⩽ ⌊N/2⌋ − 1, denote by B•_{s•} the inverse image of s• under this morphism, an open and closed subscheme of B•_{s•₁,s•₂}.
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.7.7 — decomposition of the intersection of two ground fibres
items.statement: Let s•₁, s•₂ ∈ S•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})(κ) be two points for a perfect field κ containing F_p^Φ. Then B•_{s•₁,s•₂} = ⨆_{j=0}^{⌊N/2⌋−1} ⨆_{s• ∈ Hk_j^{−1}(s•₁,s•₂)(κ)} B•_{s•}.
items.note: Proof: from the definitions and the fact that Hk_j^{−1}(s•₁,s•₂) is a finite disjoint union of copies of Spec κ (asserted). Only j ⩽ ⌊N/2⌋ − 1 occurs (Lemma 5.7.5); j = ⌊N/2⌋ pairs do not meet. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.7.7(1) — each component B•_{s•} is the Deligne–Lusztig variety DL•(𝒱_{s•})
items.statement: Let s•₁, s•₂ ∈ S•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})(κ) and s• = (A₀,λ₀,η₀^p; A•₁,λ•₁,η₁^{p•}; A•₂,λ•₂,η₂^{p•}; φ•) ∈ Hk_j^{−1}(s•₁,s•₂)(κ) for some 0 ⩽ j ⩽ ⌊N/2⌋ − 1. Denote by H̄_i the image of H_i in H^dR_1(φ•)_{τ_∞^c} ⊗_κ O_S = (𝒱_{s•})_S for i = 1, 2 (H_i as in (5.14)). Then the assignment sending (A₀,λ₀,η₀^p; A,λ,η^p; A•₁,λ•₁,η₁^{p•}; γ₁; A•₂,λ•₂,η₂^{p•}; γ₂) ∈ B•_{s•}(S) to (H̄₁, H̄₂) induces an isomorphism ζ•_{s•} : B•_{s•} → DL•(𝒱_{s•}, { , }_{s•}) (Definition A.2.1) in Sch_{/κ}.
items.note: Proof: (H̄₁,H̄₂) ∈ DL• by Lemma 5.7.3; since the target is smooth (Lemma 5.7.4) and B•_{s•} ⊆ B•_{s•₁} is projective, it suffices to show bijectivity on κ′-points (inverse built from Theorem 5.4.4(4) and Dieudonné theory, checking Definition 5.4.2(a–e) for x₂) and isomorphism on tangent spaces (Theorem 5.4.4(1),(3),(5), Proposition A.2.2, the maps (5.15),(5.16) and the five lemma). Dimension ⌊N/2⌋ − j. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.7.7(2) — excess bundle of the intersection of two ground fibres
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 5.7.7(1), the cokernel of the map T_{B•_{s•₁}/κ}|_{B•_{s•}} ⊕ T_{B•_{s•₂}/κ}|_{B•_{s•}} → ι•*T_{M•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})/κ}|_{B•_{s•}} is canonically isomorphic to ζ•_{s•}*((σ*ℋ̄_{s•2}) ⊗_{O_{DL•(𝒱_{s•},{,}_{s•})}} (ℋ̄^⊣_{s•1}/ℋ̄_{s•2})), where (ℋ̄_{s•1}, ℋ̄_{s•2}) is the universal object over DL•(𝒱_{s•}, { , }_{s•}).
items.note: Rank of the excess bundle: ⌈(N−2j)/2⌉ − 1, i.e. r−j−1 for N = 2r and r−j for N = 2r+1, matching dim M• − dim B•_{s•₁} − dim B•_{s•₂} + dim B•_{s•}. σ*ℋ̄ is the Frobenius twist ℋ̄ ⊗_{O,σ} O. Proof: Theorem 5.4.4(2) identifies the cokernel with ℋom((ker γ₁*,τ_∞ + ker γ₂*,τ_∞)^⊥/H^dR_1(𝒜)^⊥_{τ_∞}, Lie_{𝒜,τ_∞^c}) (5.17) (printed with Lie_{𝒜^∨}; see source issue), then (5.18) and Theorem 5.4.4(5). Used with the excess intersection formula and Proposition A.2.4 in Propositions 5.8.6 and 5.8.9. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Link-stratum intersections B†_{s•}, S†_{s•} and the map π†_{s•}
items.statement: For s• ∈ Hk_j^{−1}(s•₁,s•₂)(κ) put B†_{s•} := B•_{s•} ×_{M•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})} M†_𝔭(V°,K^{p°}) and B†_{s•_i} := B•_{s•_i} ×_{M•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})} M†_𝔭(V°,K^{p°}) (i = 1,2); then B†_{s•} = B†_{s•₁} ×_{M†_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})} B†_{s•₂}. For S ∈ Sch_{/κ}, B†_{s•}(S) is the set of equivalence classes of unvigintuples (A₀,λ₀,η₀^p; A,λ,η^p; A°,λ°,η^{p°}; A•₁,λ•₁,η₁^{p•}; A•₂,λ•₂,η₂^{p•}; β, γ₁, γ₂, ψ₁, ψ₂, φ•) making the diagram with φ• : A•₁ → A•₂, γ_i : A → A•_i, β : A → A°, ψ_i : A° → A•_i commute (γ_i = ψ_i∘β, φ•∘γ₁ = γ₂, φ•∘ψ₁ = ψ₂). Put S†_{s•} := {s•} ×_{S•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})×S•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})} (S†_𝔭(V°,K^{p°}) × S†_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})) ×_{S°_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})×S°_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})} S°_𝔭(V°,K^{p°}), with S°_𝔭 → S°_𝔭 × S°_𝔭 the diagonal; π†_{s•} : B†_{s•} → S†_{s•} forgets (A,λ,η^p) and the related morphisms.
items.note: S†_𝔭, B†_𝔭 are the source and middle of the basic correspondence on the link stratum M†_𝔭 = M°_𝔭 ∩ M•_𝔭 (§5.5, Theorem 5.5.3). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.7.8 (first claim) — S†_{s•} is a finite set of rational points of explicit cardinality
items.statement: Let s•₁, s•₂ ∈ S•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})(κ) for a perfect field κ containing F_p^Φ, and s• ∈ Hk_j^{−1}(s•₁,s•₂)(κ) for some 0 ⩽ j ⩽ ⌊N/2⌋ − 1. Then S†_{s•} is a disjoint union of (p+1)(p³+1)···(p^{2⌊N/2⌋−2j−1}+1) copies of Spec κ.
items.note: Proof: t† ↦ im(ψ₁)_{*,τ_∞^c} is a bijection from S†_{s•}(S) to subbundles H ⊆ H^dR_1(A•₁/S)_{τ_∞^c} of rank ⌈N/2⌉ with im(pφ•^{−1})_{*,τ_∞^c} ⊗ O_S ⊆ H ⊆ ker(pφ•)_{*,τ_∞^c} ⊗ O_S and ⟨V^{−1}H, H⟩_{τ_∞^c} = 0, i.e. maximal isotropic F_{p²}-subspaces of the nondegenerate part (dimension 2(⌊N/2⌋ − j)) of 𝒱_{s•}; the count then uses the classical number of maximal isotropic subspaces of a hermitian space (item count-max-isotropic), not proved or cited in the paper. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Number of maximal isotropic subspaces of a split hermitian space over F_{q²}
items.statement: Let W be a nondegenerate hermitian (equivalently, skew-hermitian) space of dimension 2m over F_{q²}. The number of m-dimensional totally isotropic subspaces of W is ∏_{i=1}^{m} (q^{2i−1} + 1) = (q+1)(q³+1)···(q^{2m−1}+1).
items.locator: §5.7, proof of Theorem 5.7.8, published p. 224 (used implicitly)
items.note: Classical (e.g. counting points of the unitary Grassmannian / the finite-field Deligne–Lusztig variety DL(W, m) of dimension 0); used without proof or citation to count S†_{s•}. The same product appears as #S†_{s•} inside R•_{N,𝔭} (Proposition 5.8.8). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.7.8(1) — fibres of π†_{s•} are projective spaces
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 5.7.8, take a point t† = (A₀,λ₀,η₀^p; A°,λ°,η^{p°}; A•₁,λ•₁,η₁^{p•}; A•₂,λ•₂,η₂^{p•}; ψ₁, ψ₂, φ•) ∈ S†_{s•}(κ). The assignment sending (A₀,λ₀,η₀^p; A,λ,η^p; A°,λ°,η^{p°}; A•₁,λ•₁,η₁^{p•}; A•₂,λ•₂,η₂^{p•}; β, γ₁, γ₂, ψ₁, ψ₂, φ•) ∈ B†_{s•}(S) to H₂/(im(pφ•^{−1})_{*,τ_∞^c} + H^dR_1(A•₁/S)^⊥_{τ_∞}) induces an isomorphism ζ†_{t†} : (π†_{s•})^{−1}(t†) → P(𝒱_{t†}), where 𝒱_{t†} := im(ψ₁)_{*,τ_∞^c} / (im(pφ•^{−1})_{*,τ_∞^c} + H^dR_1(A•₁/κ)^⊥_{τ_∞}), which has dimension ⌊N/2⌋ − j.
items.note: P(𝒱) parametrizes subbundles of corank 1 (hyperplanes), as in Theorem 5.3.4, so dim P(𝒱_{t†}) = ⌊N/2⌋ − j − 1 and the tautological bundle ℋ_{t†} has rank ⌊N/2⌋ − j − 1. The paper writes H^dR_1(A•₁/S) inside 𝒱_{t†} although t† is a κ-point (misprint). Proof: a point of B†_{s•₁†} lies in B†_{s•} iff H₂ ⊇ im(pφ•^{−1})_{*,τ_∞^c} ⊗ O_S, then Theorem 5.5.3(2). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.7.8(2) — excess bundle of the intersection of two link fibres (valid for N even)
items.statement: Assume N is even (the printed statement has no parity hypothesis but is false for N odd; see source issues). In the situation of Theorem 5.7.8(1), the cokernel of the map T_{B†_{s•₁}/κ}|_{(π†_{s•})^{−1}(t†)} ⊕ T_{B†_{s•₂}/κ}|_{(π†_{s•})^{−1}(t†)} → ι•*T_{M†_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})/κ}|_{(π†_{s•})^{−1}(t†)} is canonically isomorphic to ζ†_{t†}*((σ*ℋ_{t†}) ⊗_{O_{P(𝒱_{t†})}} O_{P(𝒱_{t†})}(1)), where ℋ_{t†} is the universal object, namely the tautological (hyperplane) bundle on P(𝒱_{t†}).
items.note: Proof: Theorem 5.7.7(2) and (ℋ̄^⊣_{s•1}/ℋ̄_{s•2})|_{P(𝒱_{t†})} = (ℋ̄_{s•1}/ℋ̄_{s•2})|_{P(𝒱_{t†})} ≃ O_{P(𝒱_{t†})}(1); it also identifies ℋ̄_{s•2}|_{P(𝒱_{t†})} with ℋ_{t†}, which holds only when the radical 𝒱_{s•}^⊣ is 0, i.e. N even. For N = 2r+1 the cokernel has rank r − j, not r − j − 1. Used only in Proposition 5.8.8 (N even). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 5.8.1 — local Hecke algebras T°_{N,𝔭}, T•_{N,𝔭}, the operators T•°, T°• and the intertwining operator I°_{N,𝔭}
items.statement: Assume N ⩾ 2 and choose data as in Construction 5.4.6 (giving K•_𝔭); K°_𝔭 = ∏_{𝔮|p} K°_𝔮 with K°_𝔮 the stabilizer of Λ°_𝔮. Denote: T°_{N,𝔭} the Hecke algebra Z[K°_𝔭\U(V°)(F⁺_𝔭)/K°_𝔭]; T•_{N,𝔭} the Hecke algebra Z[K•_𝔭\U(V°)(F⁺_𝔭)/K•_𝔭]; T•°_{N,𝔭} ∈ Z[K•_𝔭\U(V°)(F⁺_𝔭)/K°_𝔭] the characteristic function of K•_𝔭K°_𝔭; T°•_{N,𝔭} ∈ Z[K°_𝔭\U(V°)(F⁺_𝔭)/K•_𝔭] the characteristic function of K°_𝔭K•_𝔭. The intertwining Hecke operator is I°_{N,𝔭} := T°•_{N,𝔭} ∘ T•°_{N,𝔭} ∈ T°_{N,𝔭}, the composition taken as composition of cosets.
items.note: Local copy of Definition B.2.3 (T•°_N, T°•_N, I°_N), whose explicit formula for I°_N is Lemma B.2.4. The Hecke operators T•_{N,𝔭;δ} (= T•_{N;δ} of Notation B.2.1, characteristic function of K•ϖ^{t_δ}K•, t_δ = (1^δ,0^{N−2δ},(−1)^δ)) enter Propositions 5.8.6, 5.8.8, 5.8.9. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Remark 5.8.2 — units of the two Hecke algebras and Haar measures
items.statement: By the convention of §1.3, the unit elements of Z[K°_𝔭\U(V°)(F⁺_𝔭)/K°_𝔭] and Z[K•_𝔭\U(V°)(F⁺_𝔭)/K•_𝔭] are 1_{K°_𝔭} and 1_{K•_𝔭}, respectively. When N is odd, K°_𝔭 and K•_𝔭 have different volumes under a common Haar measure on U(V°)(F⁺_𝔭); i.e. the convolution products on the two Hecke algebras are not induced by the same Haar measure.
items.note: Relevant for interpreting compositions such as T•°∘T°• and I° = T°•∘T•° as compositions of cosets. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Degree-0 cohomology of the sources as functions on Shimura sets
items.statement: Let L be a p-coprime coefficient ring. By Constructions 5.3.6 and 5.4.6 there are canonical isomorphisms L[Sh(V°, −K°_𝔭)] ≃ H⁰_𝔗(S̄°_𝔭(V°,−), L) and L[Sh(V°, −K•_𝔭)] ≃ H⁰_𝔗(S̄•_𝔭(V°,−), L), in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p, Mod(L[K°_𝔭\U(V°)(F⁺_𝔭)/K°_𝔭])) and in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p, Mod(L[K•_𝔭\U(V°)(F⁺_𝔭)/K•_𝔭])) respectively, induced by the uniformization maps υ° (5.4) and υ• (5.9).
items.note: Galois acts trivially on the Shimura-set factor of the uniformizations, used in Remark 5.9.5. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Construction 5.8.3 — balloon incidence pair inc°_!, inc°_*
items.statement: Recall ξ ∈ H²_𝔗(B̄°_𝔭(V°,−), L(1)), the first Chern class of the tautological quotient line bundle on B̄°_𝔭(V°,−) (Definition 5.6.3), and put r := ⌊N/2⌋ ⩾ 1. Define, in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p, Mod(L)): inc°_! : L[Sh(V°,−K°_𝔭)] ≃ H⁰_𝔗(S̄°_𝔭(V°,−),L) →(π°*) H⁰_𝔗(B̄°_𝔭(V°,−),L) →(∪ξ^{N−r−1}) H^{2(N−r−1)}_𝔗(B̄°_𝔭(V°,−),L(N−r−1)) →(ι°_!) H^{2(N−r−1)}_𝔗(M̄°_𝔭(V°,−),L(N−r−1)); and inc°_* : H^{2r}_𝔗(M̄°_𝔭(V°,−),L(r)) →(ι°*) H^{2r}_𝔗(B̄°_𝔭(V°,−),L(r)) →(∪ξ^{N−r−1}) H^{2(N−1)}_𝔗(B̄°_𝔭(V°,−),L(N−1)) →(π°_!) H⁰_𝔗(S̄°_𝔭(V°,−),L) ≃ L[Sh(V°,−K°_𝔭)].
items.note: ι° : B°_𝔭 → M°_𝔭 is an isomorphism and each fibre B°_{s°} ≃ P(𝒱_{s°}) ≃ P^{N−1} (Theorem 5.3.4), with ξ|_{B°_{s°}} = ζ°*c₁(O(1)). The paper says the two maps of each pair are 'essentially Poincaré dual'. inc°_* is written inc*_° in the paper. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Construction 5.8.3 — link incidence pair inc†_!, inc†_*
items.note: m†° : M†_𝔭 → M°_𝔭, m†• : M†_𝔭 → M•_𝔭 are the inclusions of the link stratum (a Fermat hypersurface of degree p+1 in each balloon P(𝒱_{s°}), Theorem 5.3.4). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Construction 5.8.3 — ground incidence pair inc•_!, inc•_*
items.note: B•_{s•} has dimension r in M•_𝔭 of dimension N−1, so ι•_! raises degree by 2(N−1−r); ι• is locally on B•_{s•} a closed immersion (Theorem 5.4.4(2)). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Definition 5.8.4 — incidence map on the ground stratum (N odd)
items.statement: Suppose N = 2r+1 is odd with r ⩾ 1. The incidence map (on the ground stratum) inc : L[Sh(V°,−K°_𝔭)] ⊕ L[Sh(V°,−K•_𝔭)] → L[Sh(V°,−K°_𝔭)] ⊕ L[Sh(V°,−K•_𝔭)] in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p, Mod(L)) is given by the matrix ( inc†_*∘inc†_! inc†_*∘inc•_! ; inc•_*∘inc†_! inc•_*∘inc•_! ), elements written in column form.
items.note: For N odd all maps meet in H^{2r}_𝔗(M̄•_𝔭, L(r)); Remark 5.8.5 encodes this in a diagram (valid for N odd only; degrees do not match for N even, whence Θ_ℒ in Definition 5.8.7). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proposition 5.8.6 — the odd-rank incidence matrix
items.statement: Suppose that N = 2r+1 is odd with r ⩾ 1. Then the incidence map inc of Definition 5.8.4 is given by the matrix ( −(p+1)² T°•_{N,𝔭} ; T•°_{N,𝔭} T•_{N,𝔭} ), where T•_{N,𝔭} := Σ_{δ=0}^{r−1} d•_{r−δ,p} · T•_{N,𝔭;δ}, in which the numbers d•_{r−δ,p} are those of Notation 1.3.1 and the Hecke operators T•_{N,𝔭;δ} are those of Notation B.2.1 (as T•_{N;δ}).
items.note: Notation 1.3.1: d_{r,q} := Σ_{δ=0}^r (−1)^δ(2δ+1)q^{δ(δ+1)} [2r+1 choose r−δ]_{−q}, d•_{r,q} := (1/(q+1))(d_{r,q} + ((−q)^{r+1}−1)/(q+1)·(q+1)(q³+1)···(q^{2r−1}+1)). Proof: inc†_*∘inc†_! = −(p+1)² since m†°*O(1) has degree p+1 and the normal bundle of M† in M• is m†°*O_{M°}(−(p+1)) (Corollary 5.3.5): ∫_X ξ^{r−1}·(−(p+1)ξ)·ξ^{r−1} = −(p+1)·deg X. Off-diagonal entries from Theorem 5.5.3 and Construction 5.5.5. inc•_*∘inc•_! = T•: by Theorem 5.7.7 the contribution of each component B•_{s•}, s• ∈ Hk_j^{−1}(s•₁,s•₂), is ∫ c_{r−j}(excess bundle) = d•_{r−j,p} by Theorem 5.7.7(2), Proposition A.2.4(1) (with r replaced by r−j) and the excess intersection formula; the identification of Σ over Hk_j with T•_{N,𝔭;j} is implicit. Checked: all entries consistent. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Definition 5.8.7 — Θ_ℒ and the ℒ-incidence map (N even)
items.statement: Now N = 2r is even with r ⩾ 2 (so M•_𝔭(V°,−) has dimension 2r−1 while B•_𝔭(V°,−) has dimension r). For every line bundle ℒ on M•_𝔭(V°,−) (a collection of line bundles ℒ(K^{p°}) on every M•_𝔭(V°,K^{p°}) compatible with pullbacks), denote by Θ_ℒ : H^{2r−2}_𝔗(M̄•_𝔭(V°,−),L(r−1)) → H^{2r}_𝔗(M̄•_𝔭(V°,−),L(r)) the map given by cup product with c₁(ℒ), and define the ℒ-incidence map (on the ground stratum) inc_ℒ : L[Sh(V°,−K°_𝔭)] ⊕ L[Sh(V°,−K•_𝔭)] → L[Sh(V°,−K°_𝔭)] ⊕ L[Sh(V°,−K•_𝔭)] in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p, Mod(L)) by the matrix ( inc†_*∘Θ_ℒ∘inc†_! inc†_*∘Θ_ℒ∘inc•_! ; inc•_*∘Θ_ℒ∘inc†_! inc•_*∘Θ_ℒ∘inc•_! ), elements in column form.
items.note: For N = 2r, inc†_! and inc•_! land in H^{2r−2}_𝔗(M̄•_𝔭, L(r−1)) while inc†_*, inc•_* start from H^{2r}_𝔗(M̄•_𝔭, L(r)); Θ_ℒ bridges the gap. Two choices are computed: ℒ = O(M†_𝔭(V°,−)) and ℒ = Lie_{𝒜,τ_∞^c}. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proposition 5.8.8 — incidence matrix for ℒ = O(M†)
items.statement: Suppose that N = 2r is even with r ⩾ 2. Let L be a p-coprime coefficient ring. For ℒ = O(M†_𝔭(V°,−)), the incidence map inc_ℒ is given by ( (p+1)³ −(p+1)T°•_{N,𝔭} ; −(p+1)T•°_{N,𝔭} R•_{N,𝔭} ), where R•_{N,𝔭} := Σ_{δ=0}^{r−1} ((1 − (−p)^{r−δ})/(p+1)) · (p+1)(p³+1)···(p^{2(r−δ)−1}+1) · T•_{N,𝔭;δ}, the Hecke operators T•_{N,𝔭;δ} being those of Notation B.2.1 (as T•_{N;δ}).
items.note: The paper prints the product as (p+1)(p+3)···(p^{2(r−δ)−1}+1) (misprint E6); the factors are p^{2i−1}+1, i = 1,…,r−δ (it is #S†_{s•}, Theorem 5.7.8). Proof: (p+1)³ = ∫_X ξ^{r−2}·(−(p+1)ξ)²·ξ^{r−2} = (p+1)²·deg X, X the Fermat hypersurface M† ∩ B°_{s°} of dimension 2r−2 and degree p+1 (Corollary 5.3.5); off-diagonal entries from Corollary 5.3.5, Theorem 5.5.3, Construction 5.5.5; the (2,2)-entry: [B•_{s•₁}]·[M†]·[B•_{s•₂}] is the intersection of B†_{s•₁} and B†_{s•₂} in M†, computed component by component via Theorem 5.7.8 and the excess intersection formula: #S†_{s•} · ∫_{P(𝒱_{t†})} c_{r−j−1}((σ*ℋ_{t†}) ⊗ O(1)) with the integral = (1−(−p)^{r−j})/(p+1) (item chern-exercise). Verified independently: all entries correct once the product is read with p³+1. (1−(−p)^k)/(p+1) is an integer. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: The 'simple exercise' in the proof of Proposition 5.8.8 — top Chern class of σ*ℋ ⊗ O(1) on a projective space
items.statement: Let 𝒱 be a κ-vector space of dimension n+1 (κ of characteristic p), P(𝒱) the projective space of hyperplanes with tautological hyperplane bundle ℋ (rank n) and 𝒱⊗O/ℋ ≃ O(1), and σ*ℋ its Frobenius twist. Then ∫_{P(𝒱)} c_n((σ*ℋ) ⊗ O_{P(𝒱)}(1)) = (1 − (−p)^{n+1})/(p+1). In the proof of Proposition 5.8.8 this is used with n = r−j−1: ∫_{P(𝒱_{t†})} c_{r−j−1}((σ*ℋ_{t†}) ⊗ O(1)) = (1−(−p)^{r−j})/(p+1) for every t† ∈ S†_{s•}(F̄_p).
items.note: Stated as 'a simple exercise'. Check: c(ℋ) = (1+h)^{−1}, so c_i(σ*ℋ) = (−p h)^i, and c_n(σ*ℋ ⊗ O(1)) = Σ_{i=0}^{n} c_i(σ*ℋ) h^{n−i} = h^n Σ_{i=0}^{n} (−p)^i; ∫ h^n = 1. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Excess intersection formula (black box)
items.statement: Let X be a smooth variety over a field κ and i_k : Y_k → X (k = 1,2) proper morphisms from smooth varieties which are locally closed immersions, such that Z := Y₁ ×_X Y₂ is smooth with connected components Z_α. Let E_α := coker(T_{Y₁}|_{Z_α} ⊕ T_{Y₂}|_{Z_α} → T_X|_{Z_α}) be the excess bundle, locally free of rank e_α = dim X + dim Z_α − dim Y₁ − dim Y₂. Then i₁*(i₂)_!(1) = Σ_α (j_α)_!(c_{e_α}(E_α)) with j_α : Z_α → Y₁; consequently, for a class θ on X, ∫_{Y₁} i₁*(θ ∪ (i₂)_!1) = Σ_α ∫_{Z_α} c_{e_α}(E_α) ∪ θ|_{Z_α}.
items.note: Invoked as 'the excess intersection formula' without reference (Fulton, Intersection Theory, Thm 6.3 / Prop. 6.3; for ℓ-adic cycle classes via the Gysin formalism). Applied to (Y₁,Y₂,X) = (B•_{s•₁}, B•_{s•₂}, M•) with excess bundles from Theorem 5.7.7(2), and to (B†_{s•₁}, B†_{s•₂}, M†) with excess bundles from Theorem 5.7.8(2). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: (5.19) — restriction of Lie_{𝒜,τ_∞^c} to the link stratum
items.statement: For K^{p°} ∈ 𝔎(V°)^p there is an isomorphism of line bundles on M†_𝔭(V°,K^{p°}): (m†•)*Lie_{𝒜,τ_∞^c} ≃ (m†°)*O_{M°_𝔭(V°,K^{p°})}(1), where 𝒜 is (part of) the universal object over M_𝔭(V°,K^{p°}) and O_{M°}(1) is the tautological quotient bundle transported by ζ° (Theorem 5.3.4).
items.note: Printed as ι•*Lie_{𝒜,τ_∞^c} ≃ m†°*O(1) 'of line bundles on M†'; ι• is the map B•_𝔭 → M•_𝔭, so the left side must be the restriction m†•* (misprint, see source issues). By Theorem 5.3.4, on each balloon Lie_{A,τ_∞^c} = H^dR_1(A)_{τ_∞^c}/ω_{A^∨,τ_∞^c} ≃ 𝒱_{s°}/H = O(1). Consequence used: Θ_{Lie}∘m†•_! = m†•_!(− ∪ ξ). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proposition 5.8.9 — incidence matrix for ℒ = Lie_{𝒜,τ_∞^c}
items.statement: Suppose that N = 2r is even with r ⩾ 2. Let L be a p-coprime coefficient ring. For ℒ = Lie_{𝒜,τ_∞^c}, the incidence map inc_ℒ is given by ( −(p+1)² T°•_{N,𝔭} ; T•°_{N,𝔭} T•_{N,𝔭} ), where T•_{N,𝔭} := Σ_{δ=0}^{r−1} d•_{r−δ,p} · T•_{N,𝔭;δ}, the numbers d•_{r−δ,p} being those of Notation 1.3.1 and T•_{N,𝔭;δ} those of Notation B.2.1 (as T•_{N;δ}).
items.note: Proof: (5.19), Corollary 5.3.5 and deg = p+1 give the (1,1)-entry; (5.19), Corollary 5.3.5, Theorem 5.5.3, Construction 5.5.5 give the off-diagonal entries; the (2,2)-entry reduces by Theorem 5.7.7 and the excess intersection formula to the identity (5.20) (item eq-5-20), which follows from Theorem 5.4.4(5) and Proposition A.2.4(2). Verified independently (e.g. r−j = 1: ∫_{P¹} c₁(ℋ₁^⊣) = −p = d•_{1,p}). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: (5.20) — excess contribution for the Lie incidence (corrected Chern index)
items.note: Printed with c_{r−1} in place of c_{r−j−1} (misprint E7): DL•(𝒱_{s•}) has dimension r−j and ℋ̄_{s•2} has rank r−j−1. Proof: (ζ•_{s•})_*Lie_{𝒜,τ_∞^c} ≃ ℋ̄^⊣_{s•1}/ℋ̄_{s•2} by Theorem 5.4.4(5), then Proposition A.2.4(2) for dim 𝒱_{s•} = 2(r−j), 𝒱^⊣ = 0. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Nearby-cycle cohomology H^i_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨL(r)) of the semistable model
items.statement: Setting of §5.9: N ⩾ 2, r := ⌊N/2⌋ ⩾ 1, L a p-coprime coefficient ring, X^?_N := X^?_𝔭(V°,−) for (X,?) ∈ {M, M, B, S} × { , °, •, †}; bars denote base change to F̄_p; H_𝔗 is the 𝔗-invariant part of étale cohomology (Notation 3.5.7). RΨL(r) denotes the complex of nearby cycles of the strictly semistable scheme M_𝔭(V°,−) over T_𝔭 (Theorem 5.2.5(1)) with coefficients L(r), on the geometric special fibre M̄_N; its cohomology H^i_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨL(r)) carries a continuous action of Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p^Φ), the inertia I_{Q_p^Φ} acting unipotently through its tame quotient (monodromy), and commuting Hecke actions; by Lemma 5.2.7 it is identified with H^i_{ét}(Sh(V′, j−K′_𝔭)_{F̄}, L(r)) for an indefinite uniformization datum.
items.locator: §5.9, published pp. 231–236 (identification with the generic fibre: §5.2, Lemma 5.2.7, p. 193)
items.note: The paper uses RΨ without re-defining it; nearby cycles, their monodromy filtration and weight spectral sequence are imported (Rapoport–Zink; Saito [66]). Hecke localization happens later (§6, §7), not in §5.9. Planned: LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.7 plans nearby cycles and the weight spectral sequence of a semistable family.

items.name: Construction 5.9.1 — the weight spectral sequence of M_𝔭(V°,−)
items.statement: Setting of §5.9: N ⩾ 2, r := ⌊N/2⌋ ⩾ 1, L a p-coprime coefficient ring, X^?_N := X^?_𝔭(V°,−) for (X,?) ∈ {M, M, B, S} × { , °, •, †}; bars denote base change to F̄_p; H_𝔗 is the 𝔗-invariant part of étale cohomology (Notation 3.5.7). By Theorem 5.2.5(1), there is the weight spectral sequence (E_s^{p,q}, d_s^{p,q}), with terms in the category of L[Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ)]-modules, abutting to the cohomology H^{p+q}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨL(r)). In particular E_1^{0,2d} = H^{2d}_𝔗(M̄°_N, L(r)) ⊕ H^{2d}_𝔗(M̄•_N, L(r)).
items.note: Standard form (not displayed in the paper): E_1^{p,q} = ⊕_{i ⩾ max(0,−p)} H^{q−2i}_𝔗(Y^{(p+2i)}, L(r−i)) with Y^{(0)} = M̄°_N ⊔ M̄•_N, Y^{(1)} = M̄†_N and Y^{(k)} = ∅ for k ⩾ 2, so only columns p ∈ {−1,0,1} occur; E_1^{p,q} ↔ gr^M_{−p} of the monodromy filtration. Explicit E_1 pages and differentials: Lemmas 5.9.2(1), 5.9.3(1). Missing: routed to a source of LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.7 (route 10).

items.name: Construction 5.9.1 — the six maps Inc°_!, Inc†_!, Inc•_!, Inc°_*, Inc†_*, Inc•_*
items.statement: The six maps of Construction 5.8.3 give rise to six maps in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p, Mod(L)): Inc°_! : L[Sh(V°,−K°_𝔭)] → E_1^{0,2(N−r−1)}(N−2r−1); Inc†_! : L[Sh(V°,−K°_𝔭)] → E_1^{0,2(N−r−1)}(N−2r−1); Inc•_! : L[Sh(V°,−K•_𝔭)] → E_1^{0,2(N−r−1)}(N−2r−1); Inc°_* : E_1^{0,2r} → L[Sh(V°,−K°_𝔭)]; Inc†_* : E_1^{0,2r} → L[Sh(V°,−K°_𝔭)]; Inc•_* : E_1^{0,2r} → L[Sh(V°,−K•_𝔭)].
items.note: Inc°_! = (inc°_!, 0) lands in the M̄° summand of E_1^{0,2(N−r−1)}(N−2r−1) = H^{2(N−r−1)}_𝔗(M̄°_N ⊔ M̄•_N, L(N−r−1)); Inc†_! = (0, inc†_!) and Inc•_! = (0, inc•_!) land in the M̄• summand; Inc°_* = inc°_* on the M̄° summand, Inc†_*, Inc•_* = inc†_*, inc•_* on the M̄• summand (zero on the other). The twist N−2r−1 is 0 (N odd) or −1 (N even). The text then announces the composites (Inc°_*,Inc†_*,Inc•_*)^T(Inc°_!,Inc†_!,Inc•_!) (N odd) and (Inc°_*,Inc†_*,Inc•_*)^T∘d_1^{−1,2r}∘d_1^{0,2r−2}(−1)∘(Inc°_!,Inc†_!,Inc•_!) (N even). Missing: routed to a source of LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.7 (route 10).

items.name: Lemma 5.9.2(1) — first page of the weight spectral sequence, N odd
items.statement: Suppose N = 2r+1 is odd with r ⩾ 1. The first page of E_s^{p,q} is: E_1^{−1,q} = H^{q−2}_𝔗(M̄†_N, L(r−1)), E_1^{0,q} = H^q_𝔗(M̄°_N, L(r)) ⊕ H^q_𝔗(M̄•_N, L(r)), E_1^{1,q} = H^q_𝔗(M̄†_N, L(r)) (displayed for q = 2r−1, 2r, 2r+1), with d_1^{−1,i} = (m†°_!, −m†•_!) and d_1^{0,i} = (m†°)* − (m†•)* for every i ∈ Z; and E_1^{p,q} = 0 if |p| > 1.
items.note: 'Immediate'. d_1∘d_1 = 0 because the normal bundles of M† in M° and M• are O(p+1) and O(−(p+1)) (Theorem 5.3.4, Corollary 5.3.5). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 5.9.2(2) — the 3×3 incidence matrix, N odd
items.statement: Suppose N = 2r+1 is odd with r ⩾ 1. Then (Inc°_*, Inc†_*, Inc•_*)^T ∘ (Inc°_! Inc†_! Inc•_!) = ( 1 0 0 ; 0 −(p+1)² T°•_{N,𝔭} ; 0 T•°_{N,𝔭} T•_{N,𝔭} ), with T•_{N,𝔭} as in Proposition 5.8.6.
items.note: Consequence of Proposition 5.8.6; the (1,1)-entry is ∫_{P^{2r}} ξ^r·ξ^r = 1, and the zeros hold because Inc°_! and Inc°_* live on the M° summand while the others live on the M• summand. Verified. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 5.9.2(3) — vanishing of the potential map on the image of d_1^{−1,2r}, N odd
items.statement: Suppose N = 2r+1 is odd with r ⩾ 1. Then (T•°_{N,𝔭} ∘ Inc†_* + (p+1)² Inc•_*) ∘ d_1^{−1,2r} = 0.
items.note: Proof: the composite i : L[Sh(V°,−K°_𝔭)] ≃ H⁰_𝔗(S̄°_N,L) →π°* H⁰_𝔗(B̄°_N,L) →∪ξ^{r−1} H^{2r−2}_𝔗(B̄°_N,L(r−1)) →ι°_! H^{2r−2}_𝔗(M̄°_N,L(r−1)) →m†°* H^{2r−2}_𝔗(M̄†_N,L(r−1)) = E_1^{−1,2r} is an isomorphism (weak Lefschetz for the Fermat hypersurface of dimension 2r−1, integral), and d_1^{−1,2r}∘i = (p+1)Inc°_! − Inc†_!; then (0, T•°, (p+1)²)·(matrix of (2))·(p+1, −1, 0)^T = 0. Verified. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Monodromy filtration and induced filtrations (N even)
items.statement: For N even there is an increasing monodromy filtration F_•RΨL(r) of RΨL(r). It induces a filtration F_•H^i_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨL(r)) of H^i_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨL(r)) and a corresponding filtration F_•H¹(I_{Q_p^Φ}, H^i_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨL(r))) of the quotient module H¹(I_{Q_p^Φ}, H^i_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨL(r))).
items.note: H¹(I, H) is a quotient of H(−1) (coinvariants of the tame inertia), whence 'quotient module'. With two components the monodromy operator N satisfies N² = 0 and the filtration has three steps F_{−1} ⊆ F_0 ⊆ F_1 in degree 2r−1 (Lemma 5.9.3(3)). Missing: routed to a source of LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.7 (route 10).

items.name: Lemma 5.9.3(1) — first page of the weight spectral sequence, N even
items.note: Proof: H^i_𝔗(M̄†_N, L) and H^i_𝔗(M̄°_N, L) vanish for i odd, citing Lemma 5.6.2(1) — whose hypothesis 'p+1 invertible in L' is not assumed here; the vanishing holds for every p-coprime L by weak Lefschetz (see source issues). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 5.9.3(2) — degeneration at E_2, N even
items.statement: Suppose N = 2r is even with r ⩾ 1. The spectral sequence E_s^{p,q} degenerates at the second page.
items.note: Only columns −1, 0, 1 are nonzero, so only d_2 : E_2^{−1,q} → E_2^{1,q−1} can be nonzero, and one of source and target lies in an odd row of the M† columns, which vanish by (1). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 5.9.3(3) — graded pieces of the three-step filtration on H^{2r−1}
items.statement: Suppose N = 2r is even with r ⩾ 1. In the (three-step) filtration F_•H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨL(r)) there are canonical isomorphisms F_{−1}H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N,RΨL(r)) ≃ E_2^{1,2r−2} = coker d_1^{0,2r−2}; F_0H^{2r−1}/F_{−1}H^{2r−1} ≃ E_2^{0,2r−1} = H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄•_N, L(r)); H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N,RΨL(r))/F_0H^{2r−1} ≃ E_2^{−1,2r} = ker d_1^{−1,2r}; in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p, Mod(L[Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ)])).
items.note: From (1),(2) and the identification of the weight filtration with the monodromy filtration [66, Corollary 2.8(2)] (no properness needed). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 5.9.3(4) — the monodromy operator on H^{2r−1}
items.statement: Suppose N = 2r is even with r ⩾ 1. The monodromy map on H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨL(r)) is trivial on F_0H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨL(r)) and is given by the composite E_2^{−1,2r} →μ E_2^{1,2r−2} ↪ H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨL(r)) in view of (3), where μ is the map induced from the identity map on H^{2r−2}_𝔗(M̄†_N, L(r−1)).
items.note: E_2^{−1,2r} ⊆ E_1^{−1,2r} = H^{2r−2}_𝔗(M̄†_N, L(r−1)) and E_2^{1,2r−2} is a quotient of E_1^{1,2r−2} = H^{2r−2}_𝔗(M̄†_N, L(r)); the identity is meant up to the Tate twist, i.e. μ : E_2^{−1,2r} → E_2^{1,2r−2}(−1) (monodromy N : H → H(−1)), a convention the paper suppresses. Source: [66, Corollary 2.8(2)]. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 5.9.3(5) — the lowest piece of H¹(I, H^{2r−1}) and its description by d_1
items.statement: Suppose N = 2r is even with r ⩾ 1. There is a canonical isomorphism F_{−1}H¹(I_{Q_p^Φ}, H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨL(r))) ≃ (E_2^{1,2r−2}/μE_2^{−1,2r})(−1) in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p, Mod(L[Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ)])); and the map d_1^{−1,2r} induces an isomorphism (E_2^{1,2r−2}/μE_2^{−1,2r})(−1) ≃ im d_1^{−1,2r} / im(d_1^{−1,2r} ∘ d_1^{0,2r−2}(−1)) in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p, Mod(L[Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ)])).
items.note: 'Follows from (1–4)': H¹(I,H) = coker(monodromy)(−1) and the monodromy has image in F_{−1}; for the second isomorphism note E_1^{1,2r−2}(−1) = E_1^{−1,2r} = H^{2r−2}_𝔗(M̄†_N, L(r−1)), so the left side is H^{2r−2}(M̄†,L(r−1))/(ker d_1^{−1,2r} + im d_1^{0,2r−2}(−1)). Verified. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 5.9.3(6) — the singular quotient H¹_sing (printed short exact sequence; right exactness unproven)
items.statement: Printed statement: suppose N = 2r is even with r ⩾ 1; if p² − 1 is invertible in L, then there is a canonical short exact sequence 0 → F_{−1}H¹(I_{Q_p^Φ}, H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨL(r))) → H¹_sing(Q_p^Φ, H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨL(r))) → H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄•_N, L(r−1))^{Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ)} → 0 in Fun(𝔎(V°)^p, Mod(L)). What the argument establishes: for every p-coprime L the natural map F_{−1}H¹(I_{Q_p^Φ}, H) → H¹_sing(Q_p^Φ, H) is injective (H := H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨL(r))); if moreover |F_p^Φ| − 1 is invertible in L (e.g. F_p^Φ = F_{p²} and p² − 1 invertible) there is an exact sequence 0 → F_{−1}H¹(I,H) → H¹_sing(Q_p^Φ,H) → H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄•_N, L(r−1))^{Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ)} →δ H¹(Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ), F_{−1}H¹(I,H)) ≃ F_{−1}H¹(I,H), and the printed short exact sequence holds iff δ = 0, e.g. when H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄•_N, L(r−1))^{Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ)} = 0.
items.note: H¹_sing(K, R) := H¹(I_K, R)^{Gal(k̄/k)} (Definition 2.2.2). The proof asserts H¹(Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ), F_{−1}H¹(I, H)) = 0 although it has just shown that Galois acts trivially on this module, for which H¹(Ẑ, M) = M (source issue E8); and it uses p² − 1 where |F_p^Φ| − 1 is needed (new issue). Downstream (Propositions 6.3.1(4), 6.4.1) only the injectivity is used, and §6 imposes Q_p^Φ = Q_{p²} (condition (P3)); the missing surjectivity is recovered there by a rank count. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 5.9.3(7) — the 3×3 potential-incidence matrix, N even
items.statement: Suppose N = 2r is even with r ⩾ 1. The composite map (Inc°_*, Inc†_*, Inc•_*)^T ∘ d_1^{−1,2r} ∘ d_1^{0,2r−2}(−1) ∘ (Inc°_! Inc†_! Inc•_!) coincides with ( p+1 (p+1)² −T°•_{N,𝔭} ; (p+1)² (p+1)³ −(p+1)T°•_{N,𝔭} ; −T•°_{N,𝔭} −(p+1)T•°_{N,𝔭} R•_{N,𝔭} ) when N ⩾ 4, and with ( p+1 0 −T°•_{N,𝔭} ; 0 0 0 ; −T•°_{N,𝔭} 0 R•_{N,𝔭} ) when N = 2, R•_{N,𝔭} being as in Proposition 5.8.8.
items.note: Proof: Theorem 5.3.4(2) and Proposition 5.8.8 for N ⩾ 4 (the entries ±T°•, ±T•° also use the computations behind Proposition 5.8.9/(5.19)); direct computation for N = 2. Verified entry by entry: with (a,b) ↦ c = a|_{M†} − b|_{M†} ↦ (m†°_!c, −m†•_!c), column 2 = (p+1)·column 1 and the (3,3)-entry is inc•_*∘Θ_{O(M†)}∘inc•_! = R•. For N = 2, R•_{2,𝔭} is given by the same formula (= (p+1)·1) though Proposition 5.8.8 assumes r ⩾ 2. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 5.9.3(8) — image of the level-raising potential map
items.statement: Suppose N = 2r is even with r ⩾ 1. The image of the map (T•°_{N,𝔭} ∘ Inc°_* + (p+1)Inc•_*) ∘ d_1^{−1,2r} ∘ d_1^{0,2r−2}(−1) ∘ (Inc°_! + Inc†_! + Inc•_!) : L[Sh(V°,−K°_𝔭)]^{⊕2} ⊕ L[Sh(V°,−K•_𝔭)] → L[Sh(V°,−K•_𝔭)] is exactly ((p+1)R•_{N,𝔭} − T•°_{N,𝔭} ∘ T°•_{N,𝔭}) L[Sh(V°,−K•_𝔭)], where R•_{N,𝔭} is introduced in Proposition 5.8.8.
items.note: From (7): (T•°, 0, p+1)·(matrix of (7)) = (0, 0, (p+1)R• − T•°∘T°•), for both N ⩾ 4 and N = 2. Verified. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Construction 5.9.4(1) — the map ∇¹ (N odd)
items.statement: When N = 2r+1 is odd, ∇¹ : E_2^{0,2r} → L[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)] is defined as the restriction of the map T•°_{N,𝔭} ∘ Inc†_* + (p+1)² Inc•_* : E_1^{0,2r} → L[Sh(V°_N, K•_N)] to ker d_1^{0,2r}, which factors through E_2^{0,2r} = ker d_1^{0,2r}/im d_1^{−1,2r} by Lemma 5.9.2(3), composed with T°•_{N,𝔭} : L[Sh(V°_N, K•_N)] → L[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)].
items.note: So ∇¹ = T°•∘(T•°∘Inc†_* + (p+1)²Inc•_*)|_{ker d_1^{0,2r}}. The notation Sh(V°_N, K°_N), Sh(V°_N, K•_N) anticipates §6; in §5 it means L[Sh(V°, −K°_𝔭)], L[Sh(V°, −K•_𝔭)]. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Construction 5.9.4(2) — the map ∇⁰ (N even)
items.statement: When N = 2r is even, ∇⁰ : ker d_1^{0,2r} → L[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)] is defined as the restriction of the map T•°_{N,𝔭} ∘ Inc°_* + (p+1)Inc•_* : E_1^{0,2r} → L[Sh(V°_N, K•_N)] of Lemma 5.9.3(8) to ker d_1^{0,2r}, composed with T°•_{N,𝔭} : L[Sh(V°_N, K•_N)] → L[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)].
items.note: So ∇⁰ = T°•∘(T•°∘Inc°_* + (p+1)Inc•_*)|_{ker d_1^{0,2r}}; by Lemma 5.9.3(8) its restriction to the image of d_1^{−1,2r}∘d_1^{0,2r−2}(−1)∘Inc_! is controlled by (p+1)R•_{N,𝔭} − T•°∘T°•. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).
