items.name: Remark 5.9.5 — ∇¹ factors through Galois coinvariants
items.statement: By the descriptions of the Galois actions in Constructions 5.3.6 and 5.4.6, the map ∇¹ factors through the quotient map E_2^{0,2r} → (E_2^{0,2r})_{Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ)}.
items.note: The maps Inc_* are Galois-equivariant and Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ) acts trivially on the Shimura-set factors under υ°, υ•. Used in §6 (p. 269). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 5.9.6 — compatibility of d_1^{0,2r} with the incidence maps
items.statement: Suppose N ⩾ 3. The diagram with top arrow (Inc°_*, Inc†_*, Inc•_*) : E_1^{0,2r} → L[Sh(V°,−K°_𝔭)]^{⊕2} ⊕ L[Sh(V°,−K•_𝔭)], left arrow d_1^{0,2r} : E_1^{0,2r} → E_1^{1,2r}, right arrow (p+1, −1, 0) : L[Sh(V°,−K°_𝔭)]^{⊕2} ⊕ L[Sh(V°,−K•_𝔭)] → L[Sh(V°,−K°_𝔭)], and bottom arrow the composite H^{2r}_𝔗(M̄†_𝔭(V°,−), L(r)) →m†°_! H^{2(r+1)}_𝔗(M̄°_𝔭(V°,−), L(r+1)) →ι°* H^{2(r+1)}_𝔗(B̄°_𝔭(V°,−), L(r+1)) →∪ξ^{N−r−2} H^{2(N−1)}_𝔗(B̄°_𝔭(V°,−), L(N−1)) →π°_! H⁰_𝔗(S̄°_𝔭(V°,−), L) ≃ L[Sh(V°,−K°_𝔭)], is commutative, and the bottom arrow is an isomorphism.
items.note: Proof: d_1^{0,2r} = (m†°)* − (m†•)* and M†_𝔭 is a hypersurface of degree p+1 in M°_𝔭 (Theorem 5.3.4, Lemma A.1.4(1)); the bottom arrow is an isomorphism 'by Lemma 5.6.2 and Poincaré duality' — it holds for every p-coprime L because the Gysin map H^{2r}(X) → H^{2r+2}(P^{N−1}) is an isomorphism for 2r > dim X = N−2 (weak Lefschetz), without p+1 invertible. Verified. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Saito's description of the monodromy on the weight spectral sequence (black box)
items.statement: For a strictly semistable scheme X over a henselian trait (not necessarily proper) and ℓ-adic or ℓ-torsion coefficients (ℓ invertible on the base), the weight spectral sequence E_1^{p,q} = ⊕_{i ⩾ max(0,−p)} H^{q−2i}(Y^{(p+2i)}, Λ(−i)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(X_{η̄}, Λ) is the spectral sequence of the monodromy filtration on RΨΛ, and the monodromy operator N is induced, on E_1^{p,q} → E_1^{p+2,q−2}(−1), by the identity maps on the summands H^{q−2i}(Y^{(p+2i)}) common to both.
items.locator: §5.9, proof of Lemma 5.9.3(2–4), published p. 235; cited as [66, Corollary 2.8(2)]
items.note: Cited, not proved. The paper stresses that properness is not needed. Only the case of two components (columns −1,0,1) is used here. Missing: routed to a source of LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.7 (route 10).

items.name: §5.10 setup — the rank-n datum and its ♯-extension
items.statement: Fix n ⩾ 2 and a datum (V°_n, {Λ°_{n,q}}_{q|p}) as at the beginning of §5.2: V°_n is a standard definite hermitian space over F of rank n and, for every prime q of F⁺ above p, Λ°_{n,q} is a self-dual O_{F_q}-lattice in V°_n ⊗_F F_q. Put (V°_{n+1}, {Λ°_{n+1,q}}_{q|p}) := ((V°_n)_♯, {(Λ°_{n,q})_♯}_{q|p}) (Definition 3.1.7: V_♯ = V ⊕ F·1 with the new vector of norm 1), a datum of rank n+1. For N ∈ {n, n+1} let K°_{N,q} be the stabilizer of Λ°_{N,q} and K°_{N,p} := ∏_{q|p} K°_{N,q}. On the category K(V°_n)^p_sp of Definition 3.1.11 write –_n := –_♭ and –_{n+1} := –_♯, so an object K^{p∘} gives K^{p∘}_n ∈ K(V°_n)^p and K^{p∘}_{n+1} ∈ K(V°_{n+1})^p.
items.note: The case n = 1 is Remark 5.10.15. Five 'stages of functoriality' follow (Shimura varieties; integral models; basic correspondences; Deligne–Lusztig fibres; Shimura sets), parallel to the smooth case §4.5. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Notation 5.10.1 — ♯-extension of an indefinite uniformization datum
items.statement: Choose an indefinite uniformization datum (V′_n, j_n, {Λ′_{n,q}}_{q|p}) for V°_n (Definition 5.2.6). Put V′_{n+1} := (V′_n)_♯, j_{n+1} := (j_n)_♯ and Λ′_{n+1,q} := (Λ′_{n,q})_♯. Then (V′_{n+1}, j_{n+1}, {Λ′_{n+1,q}}_{q|p}) is an indefinite uniformization datum for V°_{n+1}. For N ∈ {n, n+1}, K′_{N,q} denotes the stabilizer of Λ′_{N,q} and K′_{N,p} := ∏_{q|p} K′_{N,q}.
items.note: The claim that the ♯-datum is again an indefinite uniformization datum is stated without proof; it is immediate: ((Λ′_{n,𝔭})_♯)^∨/(Λ′_{n,𝔭})_♯ ≅ (Λ′_{n,𝔭})^∨/Λ′_{n,𝔭} has length 1, the lattices at q ≠ 𝔭 stay self-dual, and V′_{n+1} is standard indefinite. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Special morphism sh′↑ of the unitary Shimura varieties (first stage)
items.statement: There is a morphism sh′↑: Sh(V′_n, j_n –_n K′_{n,p}) → Sh(V′_{n+1}, j_{n+1} –_{n+1} K′_{n+1,p}) in Fun(K(V°_n)^p_sp, Sch/F), induced by V′_n ↪ V′_{n+1} = (V′_n)_♯.
items.note: Analogue of the special morphism sh↑ (4.6) of §4.5. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: (5.21) — special morphism m↑ of the semistable moduli schemes (second stage)
items.statement: m↑: M_p(V°_n, –_n) → M_p(V°_{n+1}, –_{n+1}) is the morphism in Fun(K(V°_n)^p_sp × T, Sch/Z_p^Φ)_{/T_p} sending an object (A0, λ0, η^p_0; A, λ, η^p) ∈ M_p(V°_n, K^{p∘}_n)(S) to (A0, λ0, η^p_0; A × A0, λ × λ0, η^p ⊕ (id_{A0})_*) ∈ M_p(V°_{n+1}, K^{p∘}_{n+1})(S).
items.note: M_p(V°, –) is the moduli functor of Definition 5.2.1 (unitary O_F-abelian schemes (A, λ) of signature type N − τ∞ + τ∞^c with ker λ[p^∞] ⊂ A[𝔭] of rank p², and a K^{p∘}-level structure modelled on V° ⊗ A^{∞,p}); (A0, λ0, η^p_0) is a point of the CM moduli T_p. ker(λ×λ0)[p^∞] = ker λ[p^∞] since λ0 is p-principal. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: (5.22) — m↑ preserves balloon, link and ground strata
items.statement: m↑ restricts to three morphisms m°↑: M°_p(V°_n, –_n) → M°_p(V°_{n+1}, –_{n+1}), m†↑: M†_p(V°_n, –_n) → M†_p(V°_{n+1}, –_{n+1}) and m•↑: M•_p(V°_n, –_n) → M•_p(V°_{n+1}, –_{n+1}) between the balloon, link and ground strata of Definition 5.2.3.
items.note: 'It is clear'. Check: ω_{A0^∨,τ∞} = 0, ω_{A0^∨,τ∞^c} = H^dR_1(A0)_{τ∞^c}, H^dR_1(A0)^⊥_{τ∞} = 0 and H^dR_1(A0)^⊥_{τ∞^c} = 0, so the balloon condition ω_{A^∨,τ∞} = H^dR_1(A)^⊥_{τ∞^c} and the ground condition (H^dR_1(A)^⊥_{τ∞} a line subbundle of ω_{A^∨,τ∞^c}) hold for A iff they hold for A × A0. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: (5.23) — compatibility of m↑ with sh′↑ on generic fibres
items.statement: The square with top row M^η_p(V°_{n+1}, –_{n+1}) → Sh(V′_{n+1}, j_{n+1}–_{n+1}K′_{n+1,p}) ×_{Spec F} T^η_p (the isomorphism (5.2)), bottom row M^η_p(V°_n, –_n) → Sh(V′_n, j_n–_nK′_{n,p}) ×_{Spec F} T^η_p ((5.2)), left arrow m^η↑ and right arrow sh′↑ × id commutes in Fun(K(V°_n)^p_sp × T, Sch/Q_p^Φ)_{/T^η_p}.
items.note: Stated without proof (immediate from the moduli interpretation (5.2)). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: (5.24) — the three-layer functoriality diagram of basic correspondences (third stage)
items.statement: A commutative diagram in Fun(K(V°_n)^p_sp × T, Sch/F_p^Φ)_{/T_p} whose bottom (resp. top) layer is the basic correspondence diagram (5.10) for M_p(V°_n, –_n) (resp. M_p(V°_{n+1}, –_{n+1})) — the sources S°, S†, S•, the correspondences B°, B†, B• and the strata M°, M†, M•, with the maps π, ι, s†°, s†•, b†°, b†•, m†°, m†• — and whose middle layer consists of S†_p(V°_n, –)_sp →(s†•_sp) S•_p(V°_n, –)_sp and B†_p(V°_n, –)_sp →(b†•_sp) B•_p(V°_n, –)_sp with π†_sp, π•_sp; the vertical maps are s°↑, b°↑, m°↑ (back layer), s†↓, s†↑, b†↓, b†↑, m†↑ (middle vertical layer) and s•↓, s•↑, b•↓, b•↑, m•↑ (front layer).
items.locator: §5.10, (5.24), published p. 239; completed after Definition 5.10.9, p. 245
items.note: The diagram is built in stages: back layer (s°↑, b°↑, p. 240), front layer (Definitions 5.10.3, 5.10.5), middle layer (Definitions 5.10.7, 5.10.9). The page is printed rotated. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Special morphism s°↑ of balloon sources
items.note: S°_p is the balloon source (Definition 5.3.1: (A°, λ°) of signature type N with λ° p-principal). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Remark 5.10.2 — sh°↑ and the balloon uniformization
items.statement: The canonical inclusions V°_n ↪ V°_{n+1} and Λ°_{n,q} ↪ Λ°_{n+1,q} (q | p) induce sh°↑: Sh(V°_n, –_n K°_{n,p}) → Sh(V°_{n+1}, –_{n+1} K°_{n+1,p}) in Fun(K(V°_n)^p_sp, Set), and υ°_{n+1} ∘ s°↑(F̄_p) = (sh°↑ × id_{T_p(F̄_p)}) ∘ υ°_n as maps S°_p(V°_n, –_n)(F̄_p) → Sh(V°_{n+1}, –_{n+1}K°_{n+1,p}) × T_p(F̄_p) in Fun(K(V°_n)^p_sp, Set)_{/T_p(F̄_p)}, where υ°_n, υ°_{n+1} are the uniformization maps of Construction 5.3.6.
items.note: 'It is clear.' Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Special morphism b°↑ of balloon correspondences
items.note: B°_p is Definition 5.3.2 (β: A → A° with ker β[p^∞] ⊂ A[𝔭], λ = β^∨λ°β). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 5.10.3 — the ground source S•_p(V°_n, –)_sp at special level
items.statement: S•_p(V°_n, –)_sp: K(V°_n)^p_sp × T → PSch′_{/F_p^Φ}, K^{p∘} ↦ S•_p(V°_n, K^{p∘})_sp, where for S ∈ Sch′_{/F_p^Φ} the set S•_p(V°_n, K^{p∘})_sp(S) consists of equivalence classes of decuples (A0, λ0, η^p_0; A•, λ•, η^{p•}; A•_♮, λ•_♮, η^{p•}_♮; δ•) such that (A0, λ0, η^p_0; A•, λ•, η^{p•}) ∈ S•_p(V°_n, K^{p∘}_n)(S), (A0, λ0, η^p_0; A•_♮, λ•_♮, η^{p•}_♮) ∈ S•_p(V°_{n+1}, K^{p∘}_{n+1})(S), and δ•: A• × A0 → A•_♮ is an O_F-linear quasi-p-isogeny (Definition 3.4.5) with (a) ker δ•[p^∞] ⊂ (A• × A0)[𝔭]; (b) λ• × ϖλ0 = δ•^∨ ∘ λ•_♮ ∘ δ•; (c) the K^{p∘}_{n+1}-orbit of the maps v ↦ δ•_* ∘ (η^{p•} ⊕ (id_{A0})_*)(v), v ∈ V°_{n+1} ⊗_Q A^{∞,p}, coincides with η^{p•}_♮. Equivalence and the action of K(V°_n)^p_sp × T are as in Definition 4.3.3.
items.note: (c) is printed with 'K^p_{n+1}-orbit' and 'v ∈ V°_♯ ⊗_Q A^{∞,p}' (copied from Definition 4.5.1); see source issue. S•_p is the ground source of Definition 5.4.1 (signature type N; ker λ•[p^∞] trivial if N even, contained in A•[𝔭] of rank p² if N odd; level structures use ϖλ0). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Forgetful maps from S•_p(V°_n, –)_sp
items.statement: The forgetful morphism S•_p(V°_n, –)_sp → T_p in Fun(K(V°_n)^p_sp × T, PSch′_{/F_p^Φ}) is represented by finite étale schemes, and there are forgetful morphisms s•↓: S•_p(V°_n, –)_sp → S•_p(V°_n, –_n) and s•↑: S•_p(V°_n, –)_sp → S•_p(V°_{n+1}, –_{n+1}) in Fun(K(V°_n)^p_sp × T, Sch/F_p^Φ)_{/T_p}.
items.note: Representability by finite étale schemes is asserted ('clearly'); it follows from that of S•_p(V°_N, –) ([62, Theorem 4.4], footnote 17) since δ• is determined by a finite subgroup scheme. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 5.10.4(1) — s•↓ is an isomorphism for n even
items.statement: If n is even, s•↓: S•_p(V°_n, –)_sp → S•_p(V°_n, –_n) is an isomorphism, and s•↑ ∘ (s•↓)^{-1}: S•_p(V°_n, –_n) → S•_p(V°_{n+1}, –_{n+1}) is given by (A0, λ0, η^p_0; A•, λ•, η^{p•}) ↦ (A0, λ0, η^p_0; A• × A0, λ• × ϖλ0, η^{p•} × (id_{A0})_*).
items.note: Proof 'very similar to Lemma 4.5.2', left to the reader. For n even λ• is p-principal, so deg(λ• × ϖλ0) = p² = deg λ•_♮ and (b) forces δ• to be an isomorphism. 'η^{p•} × (id_{A0})_*' means η^{p•} ⊕ (id_{A0})_*. The parities are swapped relative to Lemma 4.5.2. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 5.10.4(2) — s•↓ has degree p+1 for n odd
items.statement: If n is odd, s•↓: S•_p(V°_n, –)_sp → S•_p(V°_n, –_n) is finite étale of degree p + 1.
items.note: As in Lemma 4.5.2(2): the fibre is the set of totally isotropic (O_F/p)-subgroups of ker(λ• × ϖλ0) of order p², in bijection with the p+1 isotropic F_{p²}-lines of a 2-dimensional hermitian space over F_{p²}. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 5.10.5 — B•_p(V°_n, –)_sp and b•↑
items.statement: B•_p(V°_n, –)_sp := S•_p(V°_n, –)_sp ×_{s•↓, S•_p(V°_n, –_n), π•_n} B•_p(V°_n, –_n) in Fun(K(V°_n)^p_sp × T, Sch/F_p^Φ)_{/T_p}, with projections π•_sp and b•↓. The morphism b•↑: B•_p(V°_n, –)_sp → B•_p(V°_{n+1}, –_{n+1}) sends ((A0, λ0, η^p_0; A, λ, η^p; A•, λ•, η^{p•}; γ), (A0, λ0, η^p_0; A•, λ•, η^{p•}; A•_♮, λ•_♮, η^{p•}_♮; δ•)) ∈ B•_p(V°_n, K^{p∘})_sp(S) to (A0, λ0, η^p_0; A × A0, λ × λ0, η^p ⊕ (id_{A0})_*; A•_♮, λ•_♮, η^{p•}_♮; δ• ∘ (γ × id_{A0})), which is an object of B•_p(V°_{n+1}, K^{p∘}_{n+1})(S).
items.note: That the image satisfies Definition 5.4.2 is 'by a similar argument of Lemma 4.5.4' (not written out). Condition (d) is immediate: (γ × id)^∨(λ• × ϖλ0)(γ × id) = ϖ(λ × λ0). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proposition 5.10.6 — the ground square is Cartesian for n odd
items.statement: If n is odd, the square with top row B•_p(V°_{n+1}, –_{n+1}) →(ι•_{n+1}) M•_p(V°_{n+1}, –_{n+1}), bottom row B•_p(V°_n, –)_sp →(ι•_n ∘ b•↓) M•_p(V°_n, –_n), left arrow b•↑ and right arrow m•↑ (extracted from (5.24)) is Cartesian.
items.note: Proof 'very similar to Proposition 4.5.5', left to the reader. The parity is opposite to Proposition 4.5.5 because here s•↓ has degree p+1 exactly when n is odd. Used (with proper base change) in the proof of Theorem 5.11.5 for n odd and in Remark 5.10.10. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 5.10.7 — S†_p(V°_n, –)_sp and s†↑
items.statement: S†_p(V°_n, –)_sp := S†_p(V°_n, –_n) ×_{s†•_n, S•_p(V°_n, –_n), s•↓} S•_p(V°_n, –)_sp in Fun(K(V°_n)^p_sp × T, Sch/F_p^Φ)_{/T_p}, with projections s†↓ and s†•_sp; by Lemma 5.10.4, s†↓ is an isomorphism (resp. finite étale of degree p+1) when n is even (resp. odd). The morphism s†↑: S†_p(V°_n, –)_sp → S†_p(V°_{n+1}, –_{n+1}) sends ((A0, λ0, η^p_0; A°, λ°, η^{p∘}; A•, λ•, η^{p•}; ψ), (A0, λ0, η^p_0; A•, λ•, η^{p•}; A•_♮, λ•_♮, η^{p•}_♮; δ•)) ∈ S†_p(V°_n, K^{p∘})_sp(S) to (A0, λ0, η^p_0; A° × A0, λ° × λ0, η^{p∘} ⊕ (id_{A0})_*; A•_♮, λ•_♮, η^{p•}_♮; δ• ∘ (ψ × id_{A0})) ∈ S†_p(V°_{n+1}, K^{p∘}_{n+1})(S).
items.note: S†_p is the link source (Definition 5.5.1: ψ: A° → A• with ker ψ[p^∞] ⊂ A°[𝔭] and ϖλ° = ψ^∨λ•ψ). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 5.10.8(1) — link/ground square of sources is Cartesian for n even
items.statement: If n is even, the square with top row S†_p(V°_{n+1}, –_{n+1}) →(s†•_{n+1}) S•_p(V°_{n+1}, –_{n+1}), bottom row S†_p(V°_n, –)_sp →(s†•_sp) S•_p(V°_n, –)_sp and vertical arrows s†↑, s•↑ (extracted from (5.24)) is Cartesian.
items.note: Proof: both sides are étale over F_p^Φ, so it suffices to check bijectivity on κ-points (κ perfect). Using Lemma 5.10.4(1), a point of the fibre product is (A°_♮, λ°_♮; A• × A0, λ• × ϖλ0; ψ_♮); since λ°_♮ is p-principal and ϖλ°_♮ = ψ_♮^∨(λ• × ϖλ0)ψ_♮, the composite A°_♮ → A0 splits, A°_♮ ≅ A° × A0 with A° the quotient by the kernel of A°_♮ → A•, and λ° (ϖλ° = ψ^∨λ•ψ) is p-principal. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 5.10.8(2) — balloon/link square of sources is Cartesian for n odd
items.statement: If n is odd, the square with top row S°_p(V°_{n+1}, –_{n+1}) ←(s†°_{n+1}) S†_p(V°_{n+1}, –_{n+1}), bottom row S°_p(V°_n, –_n) ←(s†°_n ∘ s†↓) S†_p(V°_n, –)_sp and vertical arrows s°↑, s†↑ (extracted from (5.24)) is Cartesian.
items.note: Proof on κ-points: from ψ_♮: A° × A0 → A•_♮ one recovers A• (dual to the quotient of A•_♮^∨ by the kernel of A•_♮^∨ → A°^∨), ψ: A° → A•, δ•: A• × A0 → A•_♮, and λ• with ϖλ° = ψ^∨λ•ψ; ker λ•[p^∞] ⊂ A•[𝔭] of rank p² because λ•_♮ is p-principal. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition 5.10.9 — B†_p(V°_n, –)_sp, b†•_sp and b†↑
items.statement: B†_p(V°_n, –)_sp := B†_p(V°_n, –_n) ×_{π†_n, S†_p(V°_n, –_n), s†↓} S†_p(V°_n, –)_sp in Fun(K(V°_n)^p_sp × T, Sch/F_p^Φ)_{/T_p}, with projections b†↓ and π†_sp. By the universal property of Cartesian diagrams there is a unique morphism b†•_sp: B†_p(V°_n, –)_sp → B•_p(V°_n, –)_sp making the front lower-left cube of (5.24) commute, and there is a unique morphism b†↑: B†_p(V°_n, –)_sp → B†_p(V°_{n+1}, –_{n+1}) making the whole diagram (5.24) commute.
items.locator: §5.10, Definition 5.10.9 and following paragraph, published p. 245
items.note: b†↑ is asserted to follow from 'an easy diagram chasing': B†_p(V°_{n+1}, –_{n+1}) is the limit of Definition 5.5.2, and the compatible maps are b°↑∘b†°_n∘b†↓, b•↑∘b†•_sp, s†↑∘π†_sp and m†↑∘ι†_n∘b†↓. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Remark 5.10.10 — the link square is Cartesian for n odd
items.statement: If n is odd, the square with top row B†_p(V°_{n+1}, –_{n+1}) →(ι†_{n+1}) M†_p(V°_{n+1}, –_{n+1}), bottom row B†_p(V°_n, –)_sp →(ι†_n ∘ b†↓) M†_p(V°_n, –_n) and vertical arrows b†↑, m†↑ (extracted from (5.24)) is Cartesian.
items.note: Asserted to follow from Proposition 5.10.6 and Theorem 5.5.3(1) (B† = M† ×_{M•} B•). Check: M†_n ×_{M†_{n+1}} B†_{n+1} = M†_n ×_{M•_n} B•_sp = B†_n ×_{S•_n} S•_sp = B†_sp, using Definitions 5.10.5, 5.10.7, 5.10.9. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Remark 5.10.11 — the downward arrows are isomorphisms for n even
items.statement: If n is even, the four downward arrows s†↓, s•↓, b†↓, b•↓ of (5.24) are isomorphisms.
items.note: By Lemma 5.10.4(1) and Definitions 5.10.5, 5.10.7, 5.10.9 (base changes of s•↓). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Fourth-stage notation — fibres over a point s† of S†_p(V°_n, K^{p∘})_sp
items.statement: For a perfect field κ containing F_p^Φ and s† ∈ S†_p(V°_n, K^{p∘})_sp(κ), put s†_n := s†↓(s†), s†_{n+1} := s†↑(s†); s°_n := s†°_n(s†_n), s°_{n+1} := s†°_{n+1}(s†_{n+1}); s• := s†•_sp(s†), s•_n := s†•_n(s†_n), s•_{n+1} := s†•_{n+1}(s†_{n+1}). Denote by B†_{s†}, B†_{s†_n}, B†_{s†_{n+1}}, B°_{s°_n}, B°_{s°_{n+1}}, B•_{s•}, B•_{s•_n}, B•_{s•_{n+1}} their preimages under π†_sp, π†_n, π†_{n+1}, π°_n, π°_{n+1}, π•_sp, π•_n, π•_{n+1}, respectively.
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proposition 5.10.12 — special morphisms on Deligne–Lusztig fibres
items.statement: In Sch_κ the following diagram commutes. Its left face has vertices B°_{s°_n}, B°_{s°_{n+1}}, B†_{s†}, B†_{s†_{n+1}}, B•_{s•}, B•_{s•_{n+1}} with arrows b°↑: B°_{s°_n} → B°_{s°_{n+1}}, b†↑: B†_{s†} → B†_{s†_{n+1}}, b•↑: B•_{s•} → B•_{s•_{n+1}}, b†°_n∘b†↓: B†_{s†} → B°_{s°_n}, b†•_sp: B†_{s†} → B•_{s•}, b†°_{n+1}, b†•_{n+1}; its right face has vertices P(V_{s°_n}), P(V_{s°_{n+1}}), P(V_{s†_n}), P(V_{s†_{n+1}}), DL•_{s•_n}, DL•_{s•_{n+1}}; the horizontal arrows are ζ°_{s°_n}, ζ°_{s°_{n+1}} (isomorphisms of Theorem 5.3.4), ζ†_{s†_n}∘b†↓, ζ†_{s†_{n+1}} (isomorphisms of Theorem 5.5.3(2)), ζ•_{s•_n}∘b•↓, ζ•_{s•_{n+1}} (isomorphisms of Theorem 5.4.4(4)); and on the right: P(V_{s†_n}) → P(V_{s°_n}) and P(V_{s†_{n+1}}) → P(V_{s°_{n+1}}) are the closed embeddings of Remark 5.5.4(1); P(V_{s†_n}) → DL•_{s•_n} = DL•(V_{s•_n}, { , }_{s•_n}) and P(V_{s†_{n+1}}) → DL•_{s•_{n+1}} = DL•(V_{s•_{n+1}}, { , }_{s•_{n+1}}) are the closed embeddings of Remark 5.5.4(2); P(V_{s°_n}) → P(V_{s°_{n+1}}) is induced by the obvious surjective κ-linear map V_{s°_{n+1}} → V_{s°_n}; δ_{s•↑}: DL•_{s•_n} → DL•_{s•_{n+1}} is the morphism of Construction A.2.3 for the map δ_{s•}: V_{s•_n,♯} → V_{s•_{n+1}} induced by δ•: A• × A0 → A•_♮; and P(V_{s†_n}) → P(V_{s†_{n+1}}) is the restriction of δ_{s•↑} (in view of Remark 5.5.4(2)).
items.note: Proof 'very similar to Proposition 4.5.6', left to the reader. P(V) parametrises corank-one subspaces (rank-one quotients); V_{s°_{n+1}} = V_{s°_n} ⊕ H^dR_1(A0)_{τ∞^c} and b°↑ sends H to H ⊕ H^dR_1(A0)_{τ∞^c}. Construction A.2.3: δ_{s•} has corank dim V^⊣_{s•_n} = n − 2⌊n/2⌋ and δ_{s•↑}(H1, H2) = (δ(H1 ⊕ O·1), δ(H2 ⊕ O·1)) is a regular embedding. The earlier paraphrase cited a non-existent 'Proposition A.2.3'; the relevant result is Construction A.2.3. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proposition 5.10.12, last assertion — b•↑ on ground fibres is an isomorphism for n even
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 5.10.12, b•↑: B•_{s•} → B•_{s•_{n+1}} is an isomorphism when n is even.
items.note: Proof: b•↓: B•_{s•} → B•_{s•_n} is always an isomorphism (Definition 5.10.5 is a base change of π•_n), the ζ's are isomorphisms, and δ_{s•↑} is an isomorphism when n is even (δ_{s•} has corank 0). Used in the proof of Theorem 5.11.5 for n even. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Notation 5.10.13 — lattice chains and special level subgroups at p
items.statement: Choose lattice chains Λ°_{n,𝔭} ⊆ Λ•_{n,𝔭} ⊆ p^{-1}Λ°_{n,𝔭} in V°_n ⊗_F F_𝔭 and Λ°_{n+1,𝔭} ⊆ Λ•_{n+1,𝔭} ⊆ p^{-1}Λ°_{n+1,𝔭} in V°_{n+1} ⊗_F F_𝔭 satisfying the requirements of Construction 5.4.6 for N = n, n+1 (pΛ•_{N,𝔭} ⊆ (Λ•_{N,𝔭})^∨ with (Λ•_{N,𝔭})^∨/pΛ•_{N,𝔭} of length 0 if N is even and 1 if N is odd), such that (Λ•_{n,𝔭})_♯ ⊆ Λ•_{n+1,𝔭} ⊆ p^{-1}(Λ•_{n,𝔭})^∨_♯. For N ∈ {n, n+1} one has K°_{N,p} (Construction 5.3.6), K•_{N,p} (Construction 5.4.6) and K†_{N,p} = K°_{N,p} ∩ K•_{N,p} (Construction 5.5.5). Put K•_{sp,𝔭} := K•_{n,𝔭} ∩ K•_{n+1,𝔭} (as a subgroup of K•_{n,𝔭}), K•_{sp,p} := K•_{sp,𝔭} × ∏_{q|p, q≠𝔭} K°_{n,q}, and K†_{sp,p} := K•_{sp,p} ∩ K°_{n,p}.
items.note: 𝔭 is the special inert prime, p the rational prime below it; K•_{N,𝔭} is the stabilizer of Λ•_{N,𝔭} and K•_{N,p} := K•_{N,𝔭} × ∏_{q≠𝔭} K°_{N,q}. U(V°_n) ⊂ U(V°_{n+1}) via g ↦ g ⊕ 1. When n is even the chain condition forces Λ•_{n+1,𝔭} = (Λ•_{n,𝔭})_♯ (only two O-lattices lie between (Λ•_{n,𝔭})_♯ and p^{-1}(Λ•_{n,𝔭})^∨_♯ = Λ•_{n,𝔭} ⊕ p^{-1}O·1, and the larger violates the length condition), so K•_{sp,p} = K•_{n,p}, consistent with Lemma 5.10.4(1); when n is odd there are p+1 choices. (Reader's check, not stated in the paper; cf. Remark 4.5.8.) Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Natural maps of Shimura sets for §5.11 (after Notation 5.10.13)
items.note: The paper prints sh•↓ and sh†↓ with source and target interchanged (from the K_{n,p}-level to the K_{sp,p}-level), which is not a map since K•_{sp,p} ⊆ K•_{n,p} and K†_{sp,p} ⊆ K†_{n,p}; the directions given here are those of the diagram of Proposition 5.10.14 and of all later uses (proofs of Theorem 5.11.5 and Lemma 5.11.6, e.g. sh•_{↓!}). See source issue. All ten maps are induced by inclusions of level groups and V°_n ↪ V°_{n+1}. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: (5.25), (5.26) — uniformization of the special-level sources
items.statement: Similar to Construction 4.4.2 there are uniformization maps υ•_sp: S•_p(V°_n, –)_sp(F̄_p) → Sh(V°_n, –_nK•_{sp,p}) × T_p(F̄_p) (5.25) and υ†_sp: S†_p(V°_n, –)_sp(F̄_p) → Sh(V°_n, –_nK†_{sp,p}) × T_p(F̄_p) (5.26) in Fun(K(V°_n)^p_sp × T, Set)_{/T_p(F̄_p)}, which are isomorphisms.
items.note: Details left to the readers. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proposition 5.10.14 — uniformization is compatible with the special morphisms
items.statement: The diagram in Fun(K(V°_n)^p_sp × T, Set)_{/T_p(F̄_p)} formed by (i) the F̄_p-points of the source layer of (5.24): S°_p(V°_N, –_N)(F̄_p), S†_p(V°_N, –_N)(F̄_p), S•_p(V°_N, –_N)(F̄_p) (N = n, n+1), S†_p(V°_n, –)_sp(F̄_p), S•_p(V°_n, –)_sp(F̄_p), with the maps s°↑, s†↑, s†↓, s•↑, s•↓, s†°_N, s†•_N, s†•_sp; (ii) the sets Sh(V°_N, –_NK?_{N,p}) × T_p(F̄_p) (? = °, †, •) and Sh(V°_n, –_nK?_{sp,p}) × T_p(F̄_p) (? = †, •) with the maps sh × id of Notation 5.10.13 (sh†↓ × id and sh•↓ × id going from the sp-level to the n-level); and (iii) the uniformization maps υ°_N (5.4), υ†_N (5.11), υ•_N (5.9), υ†_sp (5.26), υ•_sp (5.25), commutes, and all uniformization maps are isomorphisms. Moreover, the induced actions of Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ) on all terms of the right-hand side factor through the projection to T_p(F̄_p).
items.note: Proof: 'This follows from Constructions 5.3.6, 5.4.6, and 5.5.5.' The page is printed rotated. The diagram settles the direction of sh•↓, sh†↓ (sp → n). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Remark 5.10.15 — the case n = 1
items.statement: When n = 1, the diagram (5.24) exists with all terms not in the top or back layers empty, and Propositions 5.10.12 and 5.10.14 can be modified in the obvious way.
items.note: For N = 1 the ground and link strata are empty (Remark 5.2.4). §5.11 needs n ⩾ 2 (r1 ⩾ 1). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: §5.11 setup — parities n0, n1 and abbreviations
items.statement: Keep the setup of §5.10 but allow – = (–_n, –_{n+1}) to be an object of K(V°_n)^p × K(V°_{n+1})^p. Let n0 and n1 be the unique even and odd numbers in {n, n+1}, and write n0 = 2r0, n1 = 2r1 + 1 with r0, r1 ⩾ 1, so n = r0 + r1. Let L be a p-coprime coefficient ring. Put X?_{nα} := X?_p(V°_{nα}, –_{nα}) for meaningful triples (X, ?, α) ∈ {𝐌, M, B, S} × { , η, °, •, †} × {0, 1}.
items.note: 𝐌 (bold) is the integral model over T_p, M its special fibre (Notation 3.3.6(5)); bars (M̄ etc.) denote base change to F̄_p. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Notation 5.11.1(1)–(3) — the product P and its blow-up Q along P^{°,°}
items.statement: (1) 𝐏 := 𝐌_{n0} ×_{T_p} 𝐌_{n1}. (2) For (?0, ?1) ∈ {°, •, †}², P^{?0,?1} := M^{?0}_{n0} ×_{T_p} M^{?1}_{n1}, a closed subscheme of P = 𝐏 ⊗ F_p^Φ. (3) σ: 𝐐 → 𝐏 is the blow-up along the subscheme P^{°,°}, a morphism in Fun(K(V°_n)^p × K(V°_{n+1})^p × T, Sch/Z_p^Φ)_{/T_p}.
items.note: P^{°,°} = M°_{n0} × M°_{n1} is a Weil divisor of 𝐏 that fails to be Cartier exactly along P^{†,†}; σ is an isomorphism outside P^{†,†} and a small resolution there (locally x0y0 = x1y1 = p; blowing up (x0, x1) gives u·x1·y0 = p). The cyclic ordering of components in the earlier paraphrase comes from footnote 21 (see item weight-ss-5-27). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

api.name: RankinSelberg.SemistableResolutionOfTheProduct.data
api.statement: Use the blowup map σ:Q→P and the ordered stratum inclusions.

api.name: RankinSelberg.SemistableResolutionOfTheProduct.characterisation
api.statement: Q is strictly semistable of relative dimension 2n−1.

api.name: RankinSelberg.SemistableResolutionOfTheProduct.compatibility
api.statement: The diagonal components are blowups along link×link; off-diagonal components are unchanged.

uses.how: Use the blowup map σ:Q→P and the ordered stratum inclusions.

items.name: Notation 5.11.1(4)–(5) — strata Q^{?0,?1} and the closed embeddings γ, δ
items.statement: (4) For (?0, ?1) ∈ {°, •, †}², Q^{?0,?1} is the strict transform of P^{?0,?1} under σ, a closed subscheme of Q. (5) γ^{?0,?1}_{?′0,?′1}: P^{?0,?1} → P^{?′0,?′1} is the closed embedding when P^{?0,?1} ⊂ P^{?′0,?′1}, and δ^{?0,?1}_{?′0,?′1}: Q^{?0,?1} → Q^{?′0,?′1} the closed embedding when Q^{?0,?1} ⊂ Q^{?′0,?′1}.
items.note: Read 'strict transform' as the closure of σ^{-1}(P^{?0,?1} ∖ P^{†,†}); for (†,†) this is empty, and the intended Q^{†,†} is σ^{-1}(P^{†,†}) = Q^{°,°} ∩ Q^{•,•} (the exceptional divisor), as Lemma 5.11.3 shows. See source issue. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Notation 5.11.1(6)–(8) — graph cycles P_△, P?_△, Q_△
items.statement: Suppose – is taken in K(V°_n)^p_sp. (6) 𝐏_△ is the graph of m↑: 𝐌_n → 𝐌_{n+1} (5.21) over T_p in Fun(K(V°_n)^p_sp × T, Sch/Z_p^Φ)_{/T_p}, a closed subscheme of 𝐏. (7) For ? = •, °, P?_△ is the graph of m?↑: M?_n → M?_{n+1} (5.22) over T_p in Fun(K(V°_n)^p_sp × T, Sch/F_p^Φ)_{/T_p}, a closed subscheme of P^{?,?}. (8) 𝐐_△ is the strict transform of 𝐏_△ under σ, a closed subscheme of 𝐐.
items.note: When n = n1 is odd, 𝐌_n × 𝐌_{n+1} is identified with 𝐌_{n0} × 𝐌_{n1} by swapping factors (implicit). 𝐏_△ ≅ 𝐌_n meets P^{°,°} in a Cartier divisor, so 𝐐_△ → 𝐏_△ is an isomorphism. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 5.11.2 — specialization isomorphisms for Q
items.statement: The two specialization maps H^i_{T,c}(𝐐 ⊗ Q̄_p, L) → H^i_{T,c}(Q̄, RΨL) and H^i_T(𝐐 ⊗ Q̄_p, L) → H^i_T(Q̄, RΨL) are isomorphisms.
items.note: Proof: proper base change when 𝐐 is proper (always if F⁺ ≠ Q, Remark 5.2.8); otherwise 'this again follows from [43, Corollary 5.20]'. The base is printed as ⊗_{Z_{p²}} instead of ⊗_{Z_p^Φ} (source issue). The non-proper case applies a result stated for Shimura-variety models to the blow-up 𝐐; this is harmless because σ is an isomorphism outside the proper subscheme P^{†,†}, so near the boundary 𝐐 = 𝐌_{n0} ×_{T_p} 𝐌_{n1}. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 5.11.3 (first sentence and (1)) — Q is strictly semistable; reduction graph
items.statement: The scheme 𝐐 (valued at any object of K(V°_n)^p_sp) is strictly semistable over Z_p^Φ of relative dimension 2n − 1. (1) Its reduction graph is the square with vertices Q^{•,°} (top left), Q^{°,°} (top right), Q^{•,•} (bottom left), Q^{°,•} (bottom right), edges Q^{†,°} (Q^{•,°}–Q^{°,°}), Q^{°,†} (Q^{°,°}–Q^{°,•}), Q^{†,•} (Q^{•,•}–Q^{°,•}), Q^{•,†} (Q^{•,°}–Q^{•,•}) and the diagonal Q^{†,†} (Q^{°,°}–Q^{•,•}), and 2-faces Q^{•,°} ∩ Q^{†,†} and Q^{°,•} ∩ Q^{†,†}; thus Q^{(0)} = Q^{°,°} ⊔ Q^{°,•} ⊔ Q^{•,•} ⊔ Q^{•,°}, Q^{(1)} = Q^{°,†} ⊔ Q^{†,•} ⊔ Q^{•,†} ⊔ Q^{†,°} ⊔ Q^{†,†}, Q^{(2)} = (Q^{•,°} ∩ Q^{†,†}) ⊔ (Q^{°,•} ∩ Q^{†,†}), and Q^{(c)} = ∅ for c ⩾ 3, where Q^{(c)} is the disjoint union of the strata of Q of codimension c.
items.note: Proof: 'a standard computation of blow-up'. Local check: near P^{†,†}, P is x0y0 = x1y1 (= p) with M°_{nα} = {xα = 0}; in the chart x0 = u·x1 of the blow-up of (x0, x1), y1 = u·y0 and p = u·x1·y0 with components {x1 = 0} = Q^{°,°}, {u = 0} = Q^{°,•}, {y0 = 0} = Q^{•,•}. The restriction to K(V°_n)^p_sp is unnecessary: §7.2 applies the lemma to objects of K(V°_n)^p × K(V°_{n+1})^p, and the proof is local. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 5.11.3(2), first bullet — σ is an isomorphism on off-diagonal strata
items.statement: For (?0, ?1) ∈ {°, •, †}² with ?0 ≠ ?1, the induced morphism σ: Q^{?0,?1} → P^{?0,?1} is an isomorphism.
items.note: Proof: standard blow-up computation (parts (1), (2) proved together). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 5.11.3(2), second bullet — the diagonal components are blow-ups along P^{†,†}
items.statement: For (?0, ?1) ∈ {(°,°), (•,•)}, the induced morphism σ: Q^{?0,?1} → P^{?0,?1} is the blow-up along P^{†,†}.
items.note: P^{†,†} = M†_{n0} ×_{T_p} M†_{n1} has codimension 2 in the smooth P^{°,°} and P^{•,•}; the exceptional divisor is Q^{†,†} = P(N_{P^{†,†}/P^{?,?}}). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 5.11.3(2), third bullet — the exceptional stratum Q^{†,†} over P^{†,†} (printed: trivial P¹-bundle)
items.statement: Printed statement: the induced morphism σ: Q^{†,†} → P^{†,†} is a trivial P¹-bundle. Correct statement: σ: Q^{†,†} → P^{†,†} is the P¹-bundle P(pr_0^*N_0 ⊕ pr_1^*N_1) over P^{†,†} = M†_{n0} ×_{T_p} M†_{n1}, where N_α := O_{M_{nα}}(−M°_{nα})|_{M†_{nα}} ≅ O(M•_{nα})|_{M†_{nα}} is the normal bundle of M†_{nα} in M°_{nα} (≅ O(p+1) on each Fermat fibre M†_{nα} ∩ B°_{s°}); it is Zariski-locally trivial, has the two disjoint sections Q^{•,°} ∩ Q^{†,†} and Q^{°,•} ∩ Q^{†,†}, and is not trivial on any connected component.
items.note: The printed triviality is false (see source issue): triviality would need pr_0^*N_0 ≅ pr_1^*N_1, and restricting to {z} × (Fermat hypersurface of dimension n1 − 2 ⩾ 1) would make O(p+1) trivial there. Nothing in the paper's later arguments that the first reading checked (Lemma 5.11.3(3)–(5), Lemma 7.2.5, proof of Theorem 7.2.8) needs more than a P¹-bundle with a section. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 5.11.3(2), fourth bullet — the codimension-2 strata are sections
items.statement: The induced morphisms σ: Q^{•,°} ∩ Q^{†,†} → P^{†,†} and σ: Q^{°,•} ∩ Q^{†,†} → P^{†,†} are both isomorphisms.
items.note: They are the two disjoint distinguished sections of the P¹-bundle Q^{†,†} → P^{†,†} (given by the two line-bundle summands). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 5.11.3(3) — pullback along σ on strata
items.statement: The natural map σ^*: H^i_T(P̄^{?0,?1}, O_λ) → H^i_T(Q̄^{?0,?1}, O_λ) is injective, and moreover an isomorphism if ?0 ≠ ?1.
items.note: 'Parts (3–5) follow from (2)': σ is a blow-up with smooth centre, a P¹-bundle, or an isomorphism. The coefficients switch from L to O_λ here without comment. Planned: EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.4 plans the projective-bundle and blow-up formulas.

items.name: Lemma 5.11.3(4) — blow-up formula for Q^{°,°} and Q^{•,•}
items.note: Standard blow-up formula for a codimension-2 smooth centre; here σ^* on the second summand is along σ: Q^{†,†} → P^{†,†}. Valid whatever the global structure of the P¹-bundle. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 5.11.3(5) — projective-bundle decomposition of H(Q^{†,†})
items.statement: If f ∈ H²_T(Q̄^{†,†}, O_λ(1)) denotes the cycle class of an arbitrary T-orbit of sections of the (printed: trivial) P¹-fibration σ̄: Q̄^{†,†} → P̄^{†,†}, then (f∪) ∘ σ^*: H^{i−2}_T(P̄^{†,†}, O_λ(−1)) → H^i_T(Q̄^{†,†}, O_λ) is injective and H^i_T(Q̄^{†,†}, O_λ) = σ^*H^i_T(P̄^{†,†}, O_λ) ⊕ f ∪ σ^*H^{i−2}_T(P̄^{†,†}, O_λ(−1)).
items.note: The conclusion holds for the non-trivial bundle too, by Leray–Hirsch, for f the class of any section, e.g. of the T-stable sections Q^{•,°} ∩ Q^{†,†} or Q^{°,•} ∩ Q^{†,†}; but the class depends on the section (the two differ by ±σ^*c1(pr_0^*N_0 ⊗ pr_1^*N_1^{-1})). arXiv v1–v3 say 'fibers' instead of 'sections'. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: (5.27) — weight spectral sequence of Q
items.statement: (E^{p,q}_s, d^{p,q}_s) is the weight spectral sequence abutting to H^{p+q}_T(Q̄, RΨO_λ(n)), whose first page is E^{p,q}_1 = 0 for |p| > 2, E^{−2,q}_1 = H^{q−4}_T(Q̄^{(2)}, O_λ(n−2)), E^{−1,q}_1 = H^{q−2}_T(Q̄^{(1)}, O_λ(n−1)), E^{0,q}_1 = H^q_T(Q̄^{(0)}, O_λ(n)) ⊕ H^{q−2}_T(Q̄^{(2)}, O_λ(n−1)), E^{1,q}_1 = H^q_T(Q̄^{(1)}, O_λ(n)), E^{2,q}_1 = H^q_T(Q̄^{(2)}, O_λ(n)), with differentials d^{p,q}_1: E^{p,q}_1 → E^{p+1,q}_1. The differentials depend on the ordering of the irreducible components of Q, chosen to be the clockwise order Q^{°,°} < Q^{°,•} < Q^{•,•} < Q^{•,°} (footnote 21).
items.note: Standard Rapoport–Zink/Saito weight spectral sequence for a strictly semistable scheme with Q^{(c)} = ∅ for c ⩾ 3. The table is printed rotated. Missing: routed to a source of LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.7 (route 10).

items.name: Construction 5.11.4 — tautological classes ξα
items.statement: For α = 0, 1, ξα ∈ H²_T(B̄°_{nα}, L(1)) is the first Chern class of the tautological quotient line bundle on B̄°_{nα} (Definition 5.6.3).
items.note: On a fibre B°_{s°} ≅ P(V_{s°}) ≅ P^{nα−1} it restricts to c1(O(1)). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Construction 5.11.4 — the pair inc^{°,†}_!, inc^*_{°,†}
items.note: External product of inc°_! (for n0) and inc†_! (for n1) of Construction 5.8.3. The identifications with Shimura sets are via υ° (5.4). 'The two maps in each pair are Poincaré dual to each other.' Degrees check: r0 + r1 = n; dim(B°_{n0} × B°_{n1}) = 2n − 1. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Construction 5.11.4 — the pair inc^{°,•}_!, inc^*_{°,•}
items.note: External product of inc°_! (n0) and inc•_! (n1). ι•_{n1} has codimension r1 (dim B•_{n1} = r1, dim M•_{n1} = 2r1), so the degrees are consistent; identifications via υ° (5.4) and υ• (5.9). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Construction 5.11.4 — the pair inc^{•,†}_!, inc^*_{•,†}
items.note: The first arrow of inc^{•,†}_! is printed '(π°_{n0} × π°_{n1})^*'; it must be (π•_{n0} × π°_{n1})^* (source issue). External product of inc•_! (n0) and inc†_! (n1). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Construction 5.11.4 — the pair inc^{•,•}_!, inc^*_{•,•}
items.note: Codimensions: ι•_{n0} has codimension r0 − 1, ι•_{n1} codimension r1, total n − 1. The duality claim is stated without proof. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.11.5(1) — first geometric reciprocity law, ground × link part
items.statement: Take an object K^{p∘} ∈ K(V°_n)^p_sp and the class cl(P•_△) ∈ H^{2n}_T(P̄^{•,•}, L(n)). For f ∈ L[Sh(V°_{n0}, K^{p∘}_{n0}K•_{n0,p})] ⊗_L L[Sh(V°_{n1}, K^{p∘}_{n1}K°_{n1,p})], ∫^T_{P̄^{•,•}} cl(P•_△) ∪ inc^{•,†}_!(f) = Σ_{s ∈ Sh(V°_n, K^{p∘}_nK•_{sp,p})} (T^{•∘}_{n1,p} f)(sh•↓(s), sh•↑(s)), where ∫^T_{P̄^{•,•}} is the T-trace map of Definition 3.5.8 and sh•↑, sh•↓ are the maps of Notation 5.10.13.
items.note: T^{•∘}_{N,p} = 1_{K•_pK°_p} (Definition 5.8.1) acts on the n1-variable. The pair (sh•↓(s), sh•↑(s)) is to be read with the Sh(V°_{n0})-entry first: when n = n1 is odd, sh•↑(s) is the n0-entry. Proof: n even — sh•↓ bijective (Lemma 5.10.4(1), Proposition 5.10.14), m•_{↑!}inc•_0(1_{s•_n}) = inc•_1(1_{s•_{n+1}}) by Proposition 5.10.12, then Proposition 5.8.6 (inc^*_• ∘ inc†_! = T^{•∘}_{n1,p}); n odd — m•↑^*inc•_0(1_{s•_{n+1}}) = inc•_1(sh•_{↓!}sh•↑^*1_{s•_{n+1}}) by Propositions 5.10.6, 5.10.12, 5.10.14 and base change, then Proposition 5.8.6. Earlier paraphrase bundled (1)–(3) and Lemma 5.11.6; (2), (3) and Lemma 5.11.6 are separate items. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.11.5(2) — first geometric reciprocity law, ground × ground part
items.note: T•_{n1,p} := Σ_{δ=0}^{r1−1} d•_{r1−δ,p}·T•_{n1,p;δ} (Proposition 5.8.6), acting on the n1-variable. Same proof as (1) using inc^*_• ∘ inc•_! = T•_{n1,p} (Proposition 5.8.6). In the n-odd case the proof ends 'Thus, (1) follows' where (2) is meant (source issue). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Theorem 5.11.5(3) — first geometric reciprocity law (the identity used in §7.2)
items.note: I°_{N,p} := T^{∘•}_{N,p} ∘ T^{•∘}_{N,p} (Definition 5.8.1). T°_{n1,p} is not defined in §5; it is Σ_{δ=0}^{r1} d_{r1−δ,p}·T°_{n1,p;δ}, the operator of Proposition B.4.3(2) / Theorem 4.4.10. Proof: by (1), (2) and Lemma B.4.4 — T^{•∘}_N ∘ T°_N = ((p+1)²T•_N + T^{•∘}_N ∘ T^{∘•}_N) ∘ T^{•∘}_N for N = n1, i.e. (p+1)²T•_{n1}T^{•∘}_{n1} = T^{•∘}_{n1}T°_{n1} − T^{•∘}_{n1}I°_{n1} — the left side equals Σ_{s∈Sh(K•_sp)} (T^{•∘}_{n0,p} ⊗ (T^{•∘}_{n1,p} ∘ T°_{n1,p}) f)(sh•↓(s), sh•↑(s)); then Lemma 5.11.6 applied to (T^{•∘}_{n0,p} ⊗ T°_{n1,p})f together with T^{∘•}_{n0,p}T^{•∘}_{n0,p} = I°_{n0,p}. This is 'the intersection number responsible for the first explicit reciprocity law' (Theorem 7.2.8). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Intersection formula for graphs (used in the proof of Theorem 5.11.5)
items.statement: For a finite morphism i: X → Y of smooth schemes over an algebraically closed field and proper smooth subschemes X′ ⊂ X, Y′ ⊂ Y (of complementary dimensions in Y), ⟨X_△, X′ × Y′⟩_{X×Y} = ⟨X′_△, X′ × Y′⟩_{X′×Y} = ⟨i_*X′, Y′⟩_Y, where X_△ and X′_△ are the graphs of i and i|X′.
items.note: Standard (transversality of X_△ with X′ × Y, and the projection formula along X′ × Y → Y). The dimension condition dim X′ + dim Y′ = dim Y is implicit. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Maps inc•_α, inc†_α with compactly supported targets (proof of Theorem 5.11.5)
items.statement: For α = 0, 1, the analogues of inc•_! and inc†_! of Construction 5.8.3 are taken with compactly supported target: inc•_α: L[Sh(V°_{nα}, K^{p∘}_{nα}K•_{nα,p})] → H^{2(rα+α−1)}_{T,c}(M̄•_{nα}, L(rα+α−1)) and inc†_α: L[Sh(V°_{nα}, K^{p∘}_{nα}K°_{nα,p})] → H^{2(rα+α−1)}_{T,c}(M̄•_{nα}, L(rα+α−1)).
items.note: inc^{•,†}_! = inc•_0 ⊠ inc†_1 and inc^{•,•}_! = inc•_0 ⊠ inc•_1 under Künneth. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma 5.11.6 — moving the special cycle from the ground level to the balloon level
items.note: Proof. n even: by Lemma 5.10.8(1) and Proposition 5.10.14 the left side equals Σ_{s∈Sh(K†_sp)} f(sh†•_n(sh†↓(s)), sh°↑(sh†°_n(sh†↓(s)))), and sh†↓ is bijective (Lemma 5.10.4(1), Definition 5.10.7). n odd: by Definition 5.10.7 and Proposition 5.10.14 it equals Σ_{s∈Sh(K†_sp)} f(sh†°_n(sh†↓(s)), sh†•_{n+1}(sh†↑(s))), then Lemma 5.10.8(2). Arguments of f are read with the n0-entry first. The first reading re-derived both chains using the Hecke correspondences T^{•∘} = (sh†•)_*(sh†°)^* and T^{∘•} = (sh†°)_*(sh†•)^*. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Construction 5.11.7 — the four maps Inc^*_{?,?} from H^{2n}(Q^{(0)})
items.note: σ: Q^{°,•} → P^{°,•} is an isomorphism and σ: Q^{•,•} → P^{•,•} a blow-up, so σ_! preserves degrees. The earlier paraphrase bundled these maps with ∇ (item construction-5-11-7-nabla). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

api.name: RankinSelberg.ProductIncidenceMapNabla.data

items.note: T^{∘•}_{N,p} = 1_{K°_pK•_p} converts K•-level functions to K°-level functions (Definition 5.8.1). items.name: Potential-map groups B^r(Q, L), B_r(Q, L) (after [47, §2.2])
items.note: Recalled from [47, §2.2]. Sign rule: for Q^{(1)}-stratum Q_i ∩ Q_j with Q_i < Q_j in the order of footnote 21, + for Q_j and − for Q_i; δ_{1!} has the same signs, so it is the Poincaré-dual adjoint of δ_0^*. The first reading checked all ten signs against the order Q^{°,°} < Q^{°,•} < Q^{•,•} < Q^{•,°}. Missing: routed to the Part II SemistablePotentialMaps (route 16).

items.name: B^r(Q, L)^0 and B_{2n−r−1}(Q, L)_0
items.statement: B^r(Q, L)^0 and B_{2n−r−1}(Q, L)_0 are the kernel and the cokernel of the tautological map B^r(Q, L) → B_{2n−r−1}(Q, L) (inclusion into H^{2r}_T(Q̄^{(0)}, L(r)) followed by the quotient map).
items.note: Both sides are built from H^{2r}_T(Q̄^{(0)}, L(r)). Missing: routed to the Part II SemistablePotentialMaps (route 16).

items.name: [47, Lemma 2.4] (cited) — δ_{1!}δ_0^* factors through B_{2n−r}(Q, L)_0 → B^r(Q, L)^0
items.statement: The composite H^{2(r−1)}_T(Q̄^{(0)}, L(r−1)) →(δ_0^*) H^{2(r−1)}_T(Q̄^{(1)}, L(r−1)) →(δ_{1!}) H^{2r}_T(Q̄^{(0)}, L(r)) factors through a unique map B_{2n−r}(Q, L)_0 → B^r(Q, L)^0 in Fun(K(V°_n)^p × K(V°_{n+1})^p, Mod(L[Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ)])).
items.note: Cited, not proved: [47, Lemma 2.4] (Liu, JEMS 2019), stated there for proper strictly semistable schemes; §7.2, footnote 29, asserts the relevant results hold for non-proper Q by Lemma 7.2.5(6). Missing: routed to the Part II SemistablePotentialMaps (route 16).

items.name: (5.28) — the potential map Δ^r
items.statement: C_r(Q, L) := B_r(Q, L)_0^{Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ)} (invariants) and C^r(Q, L) := B^r(Q, L)^0_{Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ)} (coinvariants); the map of [47, Lemma 2.4] induces the potential map Δ^r: C_{2n−r}(Q, L) → C^r(Q, L) (5.28) in Fun(K(V°_n)^p × K(V°_{n+1})^p, Mod(L)). The case of interest is r = n.
items.note: In [47], C^r(Q, L) and C_r(Q, L) are denoted A^r(Q, L)^0 and A_r(Q, L)_0 (footnote 22). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Remark 5.11.8 — ∇ factors through Galois coinvariants
items.statement: By the descriptions of the Galois actions in Constructions 5.3.6 and 5.4.6, the map ∇ of Construction 5.11.7 factors through the quotient map H^{2n}_T(Q̄^{(0)}, L(n)) → H^{2n}_T(Q̄^{(0)}, L(n))_{Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ)}, hence restricts to a map ∇: C^n(Q, L) → L[Sh(V°_{n0}, –_{n0}K°_{n0,p})] ⊗_L L[Sh(V°_{n1}, –_{n1}K°_{n1,p})] in Fun(K(V°_n)^p × K(V°_{n+1})^p, Mod(L)) via the canonical map C^n(Q, L) → H^{2n}_T(Q̄^{(0)}, L(n))_{Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ)}.
items.note: Used to define ∇ on C^n(Q, O_λ) in §7.2 (before Theorem 7.2.8). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: §6.1 data — Π, E, Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_lr, Σ⁺, λ, m, V°_N, Λ°_N, K°_N
items.statement: Let N ⩾ 2 and r := ⌊N/2⌋. One considers: a relevant representation Π of GL_N(A_F) (Definition 1.1.3); a strong coefficient field E ⊆ ℂ of Π (Definition 3.2.5); a finite set Σ⁺_min of nonarchimedean places of F⁺ containing Σ⁺_Π (Notation 3.1.4); a (possibly empty) finite set Σ⁺_lr of nonarchimedean places of F⁺ that are inert in F and strongly disjoint from Σ⁺_min (Definition 1.3.2); a finite set Σ⁺ of nonarchimedean places of F⁺ containing Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_lr. This gives φ_Π: T^{Σ⁺}_N → O_E (Construction 3.1.10) and, for every prime λ of E, a continuous ρ_{Π,λ}: Γ_F → GL_N(E_λ) (Proposition 3.2.4(2), Definition 3.2.5) with ρ^c_{Π,λ} and ρ^∨_{Π,λ}(1−N) conjugate. One then chooses: a prime λ of E whose underlying rational prime ℓ satisfies Σ⁺_min ∩ Σ⁺_ℓ = ∅ and ℓ ∤ ‖v‖(‖v‖²−1) for every v ∈ Σ⁺_lr; a positive integer m; a standard definite hermitian space V°_N of rank N over F with a self-dual ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_lr} O_{F_v}-lattice Λ°_N in V°_N ⊗_F A_F^{Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_lr}, such that (V°_N)_v is not split for v ∈ Σ⁺_lr when N is even; and K°_N ∈ 𝔎(V°_N) of the form K°_N = ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_lr} (K°_N)_v × ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_lr} U(Λ°_N)(O_{F⁺_v}), such that, when N is even, (K°_N)_v is a transferable open compact subgroup of U(V°_N)(F⁺_v) (Definition D.2.1) for v ∈ Σ⁺_min and a special maximal subgroup of U(V°_N)(F⁺_v) for v ∈ Σ⁺_lr.
items.note: Footnote 23: 'lr' stands for level-raising (printed 'standards for'). Footnote 24: by Lemma D.2.2(3) every sufficiently small (K°_N)_v is transferable. Only residual (mod λ) conditions are imposed at Σ⁺_lr here and in Definition 6.3.3; see the source issue on 𝔫 ∩ O_λ = λ^m O_λ. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §6.1 — the special inert prime 𝔭 and conditions (P1)–(P6)
items.statement: In the §6.1 setup one chooses a special inert prime 𝔭 of F⁺ (Definition 3.3.4: 𝔭 is inert in F, its underlying rational prime p is odd and unramified in F, and F⁺_𝔭 = ℚ_p) such that: (P1) Σ⁺ does not contain p-adic places; (P2) ℓ ∤ p(p²−1); (P3) there exists a CM type Φ containing τ_∞ as in the initial setup of §5 with ℚ_p^Φ = ℚ_{p²}; (P4) if N is even, P_{α(Π_𝔭)} mod λ^m is level-raising special at 𝔭, i.e. P(p) = 0 and P′(p) is invertible in O_λ/λ^m; if N is odd, P_{α(Π_𝔭)} mod λ is Tate generic at 𝔭, i.e. P′(1) is invertible in O_λ/λ (Definition 3.1.5); (P5) P_{α(Π_𝔭)} mod λ is intertwining generic at 𝔭, i.e. P(−p) (N odd), resp. P(−1) (N even), is invertible in O_λ/λ (Definition 3.1.5); (P6) if N is even, the natural map (O_E/λ^m)[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]/(T^{Σ⁺∪Σ⁺_p}_N ∩ ker φ_Π) → (O_E/λ^m)[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]/ker φ_Π is an isomorphism. Here P_α(T) = ∏_i (T − α_i) (Definition 3.1.3) and α(Π_𝔭) is the Satake parameter of Π at the place of F above 𝔭.
items.note: The setup of §5 is then applied to (V°_N, {Λ°_{N,𝔮}}_{𝔮|p}). By Remark 3.1.6 (over a field): Tate generic = 1 occurs exactly once in α; intertwining generic = {−p, −p⁻¹} (N odd), resp. {−1, −1} (N even), does not occur; level-raising special = {p, p⁻¹} occurs exactly once. (P4) for N even is imposed modulo λ^m, the rest modulo λ. In the proofs, (P4)+(P2) give ∏_i(α_i + α_i⁻¹ − p − p⁻¹) ≡ 0 mod λ^m and ∑_j∏_{i≠j}(α_i + α_i⁻¹ − p − p⁻¹) ≢ 0 mod λ (p. 273). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §6.1 — auxiliary data K•_𝔭, (V′_N, j_N), K•_N, strata X^?_N and the weight spectral sequence
items.statement: One further fixes the remaining data of §5.1 with ℚ_p^Φ = ℚ_{p²}; data as in Construction 5.4.6, giving the open compact subgroup K•_𝔭; and an indefinite uniformization datum (V′_N, j_N, {Λ′_{𝔮,N}}_{𝔮|p}) for V°_N as in Definition 5.2.6. Put K^{p∘}_N := (K°_N)^p and K•_N := K^{p∘}_N × K•_𝔭, and X^?_N := X^?_𝔭(V°_N, K^{p∘}_N) for meaningful pairs (X, ?) ∈ {M, M̄, B, S} × { , η, ∘, •, †}. (E^{p,q}_s, d^{p,q}_s) denotes the weight spectral sequence abutting to H^{p+q}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨO_λ(r)) from §5.9, and E^{p,q}_{s,𝔪} its localization at 𝔪.
items.note: The E_1 pages are displayed in Lemma 5.9.2(1) (N odd: E_1^{−1,q} = H^{q−2}_𝔗(M̄†_N, L(r−1)), E_1^{0,q} = H^q_𝔗(M̄°_N, L(r)) ⊕ H^q_𝔗(M̄•_N, L(r)), E_1^{1,q} = H^q_𝔗(M̄†_N, L(r))) and Lemma 5.9.3(1) (N even, same shape). The maps Inc^?_!, Inc*_? come from Construction 5.9.1, inc^?_!, inc*_? from Construction 5.8.3. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Remark 6.1.1 — P_{α(Π_𝔭)} is integral
items.statement: By Construction 3.1.10 and (P2) (namely ℓ ≠ p), P_{α(Π_𝔭)} is a polynomial with coefficients in O_λ.
items.note: Needed so that 'mod λ', 'mod λ^m' in (P4), (P5) make sense. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Remark 6.1.2 — for N = 2, (P2) and (P4) imply (P5)
items.statement: When N = 2, (P2) and (P4) together imply (P5).
items.note: Check: α(Π_𝔭) = {α, α⁻¹} with α ≡ p^{±1} mod λ by (P4); P(−1) = (1+α)(1+α⁻¹) ≡ (1+p)²/p, a unit by (P2). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Notation 6.1.3 — the ideals 𝔪 and 𝔫
items.statement: 𝔪 := T^{Σ⁺∪Σ⁺_p}_N ∩ ker(T^{Σ⁺}_N →(φ_Π) O_E → O_E/λ) and 𝔫 := T^{Σ⁺∪Σ⁺_p}_N ∩ ker(T^{Σ⁺}_N →(φ_Π) O_E → O_E/λ^m), ideals of T^{Σ⁺∪Σ⁺_p}_N.
items.note: 𝔪 and 𝔫 involve no Hecke operators at p. Formally they are ideals of the ℤ[‖v‖^{±1/2}]-algebra T; in (P6), Theorem 6.3.4(4)(5) and the proof of (5) ("𝔫 ∩ O_λ = λ^m O_λ") 𝔫 has to be read O_λ-linearly, as the kernel of O_λ ⊗ T^{Σ⁺∪Σ⁺_p}_N → O_λ/λ^m (see source issues). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Assumption 6.1.4 — localized nearby-cycle cohomology is concentrated in the middle degree and free
items.statement: H^i_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨO_λ)_𝔪 = 0 for i ≠ N−1, and H^{N−1}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨO_λ)_𝔪 is a finite free O_λ-module.
items.note: An earlier version of this extraction bundled Assumptions 6.1.4, 6.1.6 and Definition D.1.1; split into R02 (this), assumption-6-1-6 and remark-6-1-5. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Remark 6.1.5 — cohomological genericity implies Assumption 6.1.4
items.statement: Assumption 6.1.4 holds, for example, when the composite homomorphism T^{Σ⁺}_N →(φ_Π) O_E → O_E/λ is cohomologically generic (Definition D.1.1).
items.note: Proof: Lemma 5.2.7 (comparison of H_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨ) with the étale cohomology of Sh(V′_N, j_N K^{p∘}_N K′_{p,N})) and the universal coefficient theorem. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Assumption 6.1.6 — residual absolute irreducibility
items.statement: The Galois representation ρ_{Π,λ} is residually absolutely irreducible.
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Remark 6.1.7 — the residual representations ρ̄_{Π,λ} and ρ̄_{Π,λ,+}
items.statement: Under Assumption 6.1.6, the residual homomorphism of ρ_{Π,λ} gives ρ̄_{Π,λ}: Γ_F → GL_N(O_λ/λ), unique up to conjugation, absolutely irreducible and (1−N)-polarizable (Definition 2.5.3). Construction 2.5.4 gives an extension ρ̄_{Π,λ,+}: Γ_{F⁺} → 𝒢_N(O_λ/λ) of ρ̄_{Π,λ}.
items.note: ρ̄_{Π,λ,+} is the r̄ of §6.4, with similitude character ε_ℓ^{1−N} (N even). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Definition 6.1.8 — Π-congruent standard pair
items.statement: Fix ι_ℓ: ℂ ≅ Q̄_ℓ inducing the prime λ of E (for the rest of §6). A standard pair (V, π) (Definition 3.2.7) with dim_F V = N is Π-congruent (outside Σ⁺ ∪ Σ⁺_p) if for every nonarchimedean place v of F⁺ not in Σ⁺ ∪ Σ⁺_p ∪ Σ⁺_ℓ, π_v is unramified, and the two homomorphisms ι_ℓφ_{α(BC(π_v))} and ι_ℓφ_{α(Π_v)}: T_{N,v} → Q̄_ℓ, which take values in ℤ̄_ℓ, coincide in F̄_ℓ.
items.note: No condition at 𝔭 or at places above ℓ. The automorphic representations contributing to 𝔪-localized cohomology are Π-congruent. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 6.1.9 — the Hecke correspondences T•°_{N,𝔭}, T°•_{N,𝔭} are isomorphisms after localization at 𝔪
items.statement: The two maps T•°_{N,𝔭}: O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]_𝔪 → O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K•_N)]_𝔪 and T°•_{N,𝔭}: O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K•_N)]_𝔪 → O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]_𝔪 (Definition 5.8.1) are both isomorphisms.
items.note: Hypotheses: only the §6.1 setup (uses (P5); no Assumption 6.1.4/6.1.6). Printed with O_E[…]_𝔪 but treated as free O_λ-modules. Proof: by Proposition B.4.3(1) (N odd), resp. B.3.5(1) (N even), and (P5), I°_{N,𝔭} = T°•∘T•° acts invertibly on O_λ[Sh(V°_N,K°_N)]_𝔪; so it suffices to compare ranks, i.e. dimensions after ⊗Q̄_ℓ, both ≅ ⊕_π m(π)·π^{K} over π with (V°_N, ι_ℓ⁻¹π) Π-congruent (m(π) = 1 by Proposition C.3.1(2), not needed); since K•_𝔭 is special maximal, π_𝔭^{K•} has dimension ≤ 1 and the principal series I(α) has a unique constituent with K•-fixed vectors, and B.4.3(1)/B.3.5(1) show the unramified constituent π′_𝔭 has K•-fixed vectors, so π_𝔭 = π′_𝔭. The step 'α(π_𝔭) avoids {−1,−1} (resp. {−p,−p⁻¹}) by (P5)' needs an argument at 𝔭 (see source issue). An earlier version of this extraction's wording ('isomorphisms up to units') was inexact. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Lemma 6.1.10 — Π-congruent pairs have relevant, residually irreducible base change
items.statement: Let (V, π) be a Π-congruent standard pair. If Assumption 6.1.6 holds, then BC(π), which exists by Proposition 3.2.8, is a relevant representation of GL_N(A_F) (Definition 1.1.3); moreover ρ_{BC(π),ι_ℓ} is residually irreducible.
items.note: Proof: ρ_{BC(π),ι_ℓ} (Remark 3.2.9) admits by Chebotarev a lattice with residual representation ≅ ρ̄_{Π,λ} ⊗ F̄_ℓ, irreducible; if BC(π) were not cuspidal ρ_{BC(π),ι_ℓ} would be decomposable; cuspidality plus [72, Theorem 1.1(iii,iv)] gives relevance. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Lemma 6.1.11 — compactly supported and ordinary cohomology agree after localization at 𝔪
items.statement: Assume Assumption 6.1.6. Then the natural maps H^i_{ét,c}(Sh(V′_N, j_N K^{p∘}_N K′_{p,N})_{F̄}, O_λ)_𝔪 → H^i_ét(Sh(V′_N, j_N K^{p∘}_N K′_{p,N})_{F̄}, O_λ)_𝔪 and H^i_{𝔗,c}(M̄•_N, O_λ)_𝔪 → H^i_𝔗(M̄•_N, O_λ)_𝔪 are isomorphisms for every i ∈ ℤ.
items.note: Proof: by Lemma 5.2.7 and the weight spectral sequence (Lemmas 5.9.2, 5.9.3) it suffices to treat (6.1), the first map; trivial if the Shimura variety is proper. Otherwise V′_N has Witt index 1; unique toroidal compactification [2] (see [44] for N = 3), smooth over F; for neat level the boundary Z is geometrically a disjoint union of abelian varieties of dimension N−2, H^i_ét(Z_{F̄}, O_λ) is free, and every π′^∞ in H^i(Z_{F̄}) ⊗ ℂ extends to π′ which is a subquotient of a parabolic induction from the unique proper Levi, so BC(π′) is not cuspidal and the argument of Lemma 6.1.10 gives H^i(Z_{F̄}, O_λ)_𝔪 = 0. See source issue for the implicit steps. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: [72, Theorem 1.1] — cohomological base change for unitary groups (cited)
items.statement: For a standard pair (V, π) (Definition 3.2.7), the automorphic base change BC(π) to GL_N(A_F) exists (Proposition 3.2.8) and there is an associated Galois representation ρ_{BC(π),ι_ℓ} with the properties of Proposition 3.2.4 (Remark 3.2.9); by parts (iii), (iv), if BC(π) is cuspidal then it is a relevant representation of GL_N(A_F).
items.locator: cited in the proof of Lemma 6.1.10, published p. 267 (also Proposition 3.2.8, Remark 3.2.9)
items.note: Cited, not proved. Footnote 9 (p. 146): [72] treats unitary similitude groups with F containing an imaginary quadratic field; the authors adapt it as in Proposition D.1.3. Planned: EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.7a plans the unitary-to-GL base-change character identities.

items.name: [2] (with [44]) — toroidal compactification of the non-proper unitary Shimura variety (cited)
items.statement: If Sh(V′_N, j_N K^{p∘}_N K′_{p,N}) is not proper (so V′_N has Witt index 1), it has a unique toroidal compactification S̃h(V′_N, j_N K^{p∘}_N K′_{p,N}), since the relevant combinatorial data are unique; it is smooth over F; and, the level being neat, the boundary Z := S̃h \ Sh is geometrically isomorphic to a disjoint union of abelian varieties of dimension N−2.
items.locator: cited in the proof of Lemma 6.1.11, published p. 267
items.note: Cited from Ash–Mumford–Rapoport–Tai [2], with Larsen [44] for N = 3; not proved in the paper. Non-properness forces F⁺ = ℚ. Planned: ShimuraCompactifications C2 plans toroidal compactifications.

items.name: Lemma 6.2.1 — odd-degree cohomology of M̄†_N vanishes after localization (N odd)
items.statement: Let N = 2r+1 with r ⩾ 1. Then H^i_𝔗(M̄†_N, O_λ)_𝔪 = 0 for every odd integer i.
items.note: No Assumption 6.1.4/6.1.6. For i ≠ 2r−1 this is Lemma 5.6.2(1) (p+1 ∈ O_λ^× by (P2)). For i = 2r−1: a π^{∞,p} occurring is completed (Proposition 5.6.4) to π with (V°_N, π) Π-congruent and BC(π_𝔭) a constituent of an unramified principal series whose Satake parameter contains {−p, −p⁻¹}, excluded modulo λ by (P5); by Chebotarev the residual representations of ρ_{BC(π),ι_ℓ} and ρ_{Π,λ} ⊗ Q̄_ℓ have the same Frobenius eigenvalues at 𝔭, contradicting Proposition C.3.1(2) and Proposition 3.2.4(2). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 6.2.2(1)(2) — the localized E_1 page (N odd) is free and vanishes in odd rows
items.statement: Let N = 2r+1 (r ⩾ 1) and assume Assumption 6.1.4. Then (1) E^{p,q}_{1,𝔪} = 0 if q is odd; (2) E^{p,q}_{1,𝔪} is a free O_λ-module for every (p, q) ∈ ℤ².
items.note: (1) from Lemma 6.2.1 and Assumption 6.1.4 (the column p = 0 in an odd row survives to E_∞ and would contribute to H^q, q ≠ 2r); (2) 'immediate' from (1) and Assumption 6.1.4 (with Lemma 5.6.2(2) for the M̄°, M̄† terms, and the mod-λ version of (1) for M̄•). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 6.2.2(3)–(5) — the localized E_2 page (N odd) is concentrated at (0, 2r)
items.statement: Let N = 2r+1 (r ⩾ 1) and assume Assumption 6.1.4. Then (3) E^{p,q}_{2,𝔪} = 0 unless (p, q) = (0, 2r); (4) E^{0,2r}_{2,𝔪} is canonically isomorphic to H^{2r}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨO_λ(r))_𝔪, which is a free O_λ-module; (5) the spectral sequence E^{p,q}_{s,𝔪} degenerates at the second page.
items.note: (5) is printed 'E^{0,2r}_{s,𝔪} degenerates' (source issue). Proof of (3) as printed: 'd_1^{−1,2r} is injective and d_1^{0,2r} is surjective'; complete argument: odd rows vanish and there are only three columns, so d_s = 0 for s ⩾ 2, whence E_2 = E_∞, and Assumption 6.1.4 kills every E_2^{p,q} with p+q ≠ 2r. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Theorem 6.2.3 (first assertion) — surjectivity of ∇¹_𝔪 (N odd)
items.statement: Let N = 2r+1 with r ⩾ 1 (§6.1 setup, in particular (P2), (P4), (P5)). The map ∇¹_𝔪: E^{0,2r}_{2,𝔪} → O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]_𝔪 of Construction 5.9.4(1) — induced by T°•_{N,𝔭}∘(T•°_{N,𝔭}∘Inc*_† + (p+1)²Inc*_•) restricted to ker d_1^{0,2r} — is surjective. It always factors through the quotient E^{0,2r}_{2,𝔪} → (E^{0,2r}_{2,𝔪})_{Gal(F̄_p/F_{p²})} (Remark 5.9.5).
items.note: No Assumption 6.1.4/6.1.6 needed for surjectivity. Proof: the map (Inc^∘_!, Inc^†_!, Inc^•_!∘T•°_𝔭): O_λ[Sh(V°_N,K°_N)]^{⊕3} → E_1^{0,2r} sends ker(d_1^{0,2r}∘(…)) into ker d_1^{0,2r}; by Lemma 5.9.6 (N ⩾ 3) that kernel is the kernel of (p+1, −1, 0)·M with M the matrix of formula-6-2-3-matrix; since (p+1, −1, 0) and (0, I°, (p+1)²) are independent mod 𝔪 (2×2 minor (p+1)³, a unit by (P2)), Nakayama reduces surjectivity to nondegeneracy of that matrix mod 𝔪. An earlier version of this extraction bundled this with parts (1)–(3); split. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 6.2.3 — the incidence matrix and its determinant (N odd)
items.statement: For N = 2r+1: (Inc*_∘; Inc*_†; T°•_{N,𝔭}∘Inc*_•)∘(Inc^∘_!, Inc^†_!, Inc^•_!∘T•°_{N,𝔭}) = [[1, 0, 0], [0, −(p+1)², I°_{N,𝔭}], [0, I°_{N,𝔭}, T°•_{N,𝔭}∘T•_{N,𝔭}∘T•°_{N,𝔭}]] in T°_{N,𝔭}, and this matrix is nondegenerate modulo 𝔪.
items.note: The matrix follows from Lemma 5.9.2(2) by multiplying the third row by T°• and the third column by T•°. The paper cites Lemma B.4.4, Proposition B.4.3 and (P4, P5) for nondegeneracy. Reader's check: by Lemma B.4.4 (q = p), (p+1)²T°•T•T•° + (I°)² = T°•T•°T° = I°·T°, so det = −I°_{N,𝔭}·T°_N; by Proposition B.4.3, φ_α(I°) = p^{r²+r}∏_{i=1}^r(α_i + α_i⁻¹ + p + p⁻¹) (unit by (P5)) and φ_α(T°_N) = p^{r²+r}∏_{i=1}^r(α_i + α_i⁻¹ − 2) = ±p^{r²+r}P′(1) (unit by Tate genericity (P4)). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Theorem 6.2.3(1) — Frobenius eigenvalues on E^{0,2r}_{2,𝔪} mod λ (N odd)
items.statement: Let N = 2r+1 (r ⩾ 1) and assume Assumptions 6.1.4, 6.1.6 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for N. Then the generalized Frobenius eigenvalues of the (O_λ/λ)[Gal(F̄_p/F_{p²})]-module E^{0,2r}_{2,𝔪} ⊗_{O_λ} O_λ/λ are contained in the set of roots of P_{α(Π_𝔭)} mod λ in a finite extension of O_λ/λ.
items.note: Proof via formula-6-2-3-galois: E^{0,2r}_{2,𝔪} is a Γ_F-stable lattice in ⊕_{π′}ρ^c_{BC(π′)}(r)^{⊕d(π′)} whose residual representations are ρ̄^c_{Π,λ}(r); the arithmetic Frobenius eigenvalues of ρ^c_{Π,λ}(r)(φ_{p²}) are the α_i^{±1} (and 1). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Theorem 6.2.3(2) — weak semisimplicity of E^{0,2r}_{2,𝔪} (N odd)
items.statement: Let N = 2r+1 (r ⩾ 1) and assume Assumptions 6.1.4, 6.1.6 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for N. Then the O_λ[Gal(F̄_p/F_{p²})]-module E^{0,2r}_{2,𝔪} is weakly semisimple (Definition 2.1.2: the natural map M^Γ → M_Γ is an isomorphism).
items.note: Proof: by (P4) ρ̄^c_{Π,λ}(r) is weakly semisimple with 1-dimensional Frobenius invariants; each ρ^c_{BC(π′)}(r) has invariants of dimension ⩾ 1 (unitary parameter of odd rank contains 1), so Lemma 2.1.5 makes each lattice R^c_{BC(π′)} weakly semisimple with 1-dimensional invariants; then E^{0,2r}_{2,𝔪} ⊆ ⊕(R^c_{BC(π′)})^{⊕d(π′)} is weakly semisimple by Lemma 2.1.4 (printed '(1)' only; the submodule step is 2.1.4(2); source issue). An earlier version of this extraction's 'residue coinvariants' is Galois coinvariants; the iso is split off as thm-6-2-3-3. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Theorem 6.2.3(3) — ∇¹_𝔪 identifies Frobenius coinvariants with the Shimura set (N odd)
items.statement: Let N = 2r+1 (r ⩾ 1) and assume Assumptions 6.1.4, 6.1.6 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for N. Then ∇¹_𝔪 induces an isomorphism ∇¹_𝔪: (E^{0,2r}_{2,𝔪})_{Gal(F̄_p/F_{p²})} ≅ O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]_𝔪.
items.note: Proof: by (2) the coinvariants are free of rank ∑_{π′} d(π′); since ∇¹_𝔪 is surjective, it suffices that ∑_{π′} d(π′) ⩽ dim_{E_λ} O_λ[Sh(V°_N,K°_N)]_𝔪 ⊗ E_λ, which follows from Corollary C.3.3 and Lemma 6.1.9. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 6.2.3 — Galois decomposition of E^{0,2r}_{2,𝔪} (N odd)
items.statement: Let N = 2r+1 and assume Assumptions 6.1.4, 6.1.6 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for N. By Lemmas 5.2.7 and 6.2.2, E^{0,2r}_{2,𝔪} ≅ H^{2r}_ét(Sh(V′_N, j_N K^{p∘}_N K′_{p,N})_{F̄}, O_λ(r))_𝔪 as O_λ[Gal(Q̄_p/ℚ_{p²})]-modules; by Lemmas 6.1.10, 6.1.11, Proposition C.3.1(2) and Hypothesis 3.2.10, H^{2r}_ét(…)_𝔪 ⊗_{O_λ} Q̄_ℓ ≅ ⊕_{π′} ρ^c_{BC(π′),ι_ℓ}(r)^{⊕d(π′)} as Q̄_ℓ[Γ_F]-modules, with d(π′) := dim (π′^{∞,p})^{j_N K^{p∘}_N}, the sum over automorphic representations π′ of U(V′_N)(A_{F⁺}) such that (V′_N, π′) is a Π-congruent standard pair, π′_{τ_∞} is a holomorphic discrete series of U(V′_N)(F⁺_{τ_∞}) with Harish-Chandra parameter {−r, 1−r, …, r−1, r}, and π′_τ is trivial for every archimedean τ ≠ τ_∞. After enlarging E_λ, each ρ_{BC(π′),ι_ℓ}(r) has a Γ_F-stable O_λ-lattice R_{BC(π′)}, unique up to homothety, with reduction ≅ ρ̄_{Π,λ}(r), and E^{0,2r}_{2,𝔪} ⊆ ⊕_{π′}(R^c_{BC(π′)})^{⊕d(π′)} as O_λ[Gal(F̄_p/F_{p²})]-modules.
items.note: Printed with 'Sh(V′, …)' for Sh(V′_N, …). Only the holomorphic member of each archimedean packet is listed, each contributing the full N-dimensional ρ^c; this is a bookkeeping convention consistent with Hypothesis 3.2.10. The inclusion holds after rescaling (λ^k E ⊆ ⊕R^c). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proposition 6.3.1(1) — incidence maps onto E^{0,2r−2}_{1,𝔪}(−1) are isomorphisms (N even)
items.statement: Let N = 2r be even (r ⩾ 1) and assume Assumptions 6.1.4, 6.1.6 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for N. Then the map (Inc^∘_! + Inc^†_! + Inc^•_!)_𝔪: O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]^{⊕2}_𝔪 ⊕ O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K•_N)]_𝔪 → E^{0,2r−2}_{1,𝔪}(−1) when N ⩾ 4, resp. (Inc^∘_! + Inc^•_!)_𝔪: O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]_𝔪 ⊕ O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K•_N)]_𝔪 → E^{0,2r−2}_{1,𝔪}(−1) when N = 2 (maps from Construction 5.9.1), is an isomorphism.
items.note: Proved only for N ⩾ 4 ('leave the much easier case N = 2 to the readers'). Follows from claim-6-3-1-ground-iso and Lemma 6.1.9. An earlier version of this extraction bundled all four parts of Proposition 6.3.1 in garbled form; split into R07, prop-6-3-1-2, prop-6-3-1-3, prop-6-3-1-4. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proposition 6.3.1(2) — the restriction maps from E^{0,2r}_{1,𝔪} are surjective with kernel the torsion of H^{2r}(M̄•_N) (N even)
items.statement: Let N = 2r be even (r ⩾ 1) and assume Assumptions 6.1.4, 6.1.6 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for N. Then the map (Inc*_∘, Inc*_†, Inc*_•)_𝔪: E^{0,2r}_{1,𝔪} → O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]^{⊕2}_𝔪 ⊕ O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K•_N)]_𝔪 when N ⩾ 4, resp. (Inc*_∘, Inc*_•)_𝔪: E^{0,2r}_{1,𝔪} → O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]_𝔪 ⊕ O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K•_N)]_𝔪 when N = 2 (Construction 5.9.1), is surjective with kernel the O_λ-torsion of H^{2r}_𝔗(M̄•_N, O_λ(r))_𝔪.
items.note: Proof: from (1) by Poincaré duality on the (non-proper) M̄•_N, using Lemma 6.1.11 to replace H_c by H after localization. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proposition 6.3.1(3) — surjectivity of ∇⁰_𝔪 (N even)
items.statement: Let N = 2r be even (r ⩾ 1) and assume Assumptions 6.1.4, 6.1.6 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for N. Then the map ∇⁰_𝔪: ker d^{0,2r}_{1,𝔪} → O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]_𝔪 of Construction 5.9.4(2) — the restriction of T°•_{N,𝔭}∘(T•°_{N,𝔭}∘Inc*_∘ + (p+1)Inc*_•) — is surjective.
items.note: Proof: ∇⁰_𝔪 is the restriction of (1, 0, p+1)∘(T°•T•°Inc*_∘, Inc*_†, T°•Inc*_•)_𝔪, surjective by (2) and Lemma 6.1.9; the restriction of d_1^{0,2r} to H^{2r}_𝔗(M̄•_N, O_λ(r)) is inc*_† (Construction 5.8.3), surjective by (2) — jointly with Inc*_• — so ker d contains preimages of everything. The printed conclusion names the map 'Δ⁰_𝔪' (source issue). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proposition 6.3.1(4) — Tate classes in F_{−1}H¹ surject onto the level-raising quotient (N even)
items.statement: Let N = 2r be even (r ⩾ 1) and assume Assumptions 6.1.4, 6.1.6 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for N. Then ∇⁰_𝔪∘d^{−1,2r}_{1,𝔪} induces a map F_{−1}H¹(I_{ℚ_{p²}}, H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨO_λ(r))_𝔪) → O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]_𝔪/((p+1)R°_{N,𝔭} − I°_{N,𝔭}) which is surjective and whose kernel is canonically the O_λ-torsion of H^{2r}_𝔗(M̄•_N, O_λ(r))_𝔪.
items.note: R°_{N,𝔭}, I°_{N,𝔭}: Proposition B.3.5 with q = p. Proof (N ⩾ 4): identify (E^{0,2r}_{1,𝔪})_fr ≅ O_λ[K°]^{⊕2} ⊕ O_λ[K•] by (2); Lemma 5.9.6 identifies (ker d^{0,2r}_{1,𝔪})_fr with ker(p+1, −1, 0); Assumption 6.1.4 gives im d^{−1,2r} = ker d^{0,2r}, and Lemma 5.9.3(5) gives F_{−1}H¹ ≅ ker d^{0,2r}/im(d^{−1,2r}∘d^{0,2r−2}(−1)); Lemma 6.1.9 and Lemma 5.9.3(7) show (ker d)_fr ∩ ker ∇⁰ ⊆ im(d∘d); formula-6-3-1-image computes im(∇⁰∘d∘d). The kernel is tors/(tors ∩ im(d∘d)), and (6.2) tors ∩ im(d^{−1,2r}∘d^{0,2r−2}(−1)) = 0 follows from a rank count: each ρ_{Π′,ι_ℓ}(r) occurring in H^{2r−1}⊗Q̄_ℓ is pure of weight −1 at 𝔭 ([74, Lemma 1.4(3)], Proposition 3.2.4), so H¹(ℚ_{p²}, ρ_{Π′}(r)) = 0 ([56, Proposition 4.2.2(1)]) and F_{−1}H¹ ⊆ H¹_sing is torsion; hence rank im(d∘d) = rank ker d^{0,2r} = rank O_λ[K°]_𝔪 + rank O_λ[K•]_𝔪, equal to the rank of the free source E^{0,2r−2}_{1,𝔪}/im d^{−1,2r−2}_{1,𝔪} (this last equality uses rank H^{2r−4}(M̄†_N)_𝔪 = rank O_λ[K°]_𝔪, left implicit). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Proposition 6.3.1 — the ground-stratum incidence map in degree 2r−2 is an isomorphism (N ⩾ 4)
items.statement: Let N = 2r ⩾ 4 and assume Assumptions 6.1.4, 6.1.6 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for N. Then (inc^†_! + inc^•_!∘T•°_{N,𝔭})_𝔪: O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]^{⊕2}_𝔪 → H^{2r−2}_𝔗(M̄•_N, O_λ(r−1))_𝔪 is an isomorphism.
items.note: By Lemma 6.3.2 (rank of the target ⩽ 2·rank of the source, target free) it suffices to find a line bundle ℒ (Definition 5.8.7) with (inc_ℒ)_𝔪 surjective, where inc_ℒ := (inc*_†, T°•_{N,𝔭}∘inc*_•)∘Θ_ℒ∘(inc^†_! + inc^•_!∘T•°_{N,𝔭}); see formula-6-3-1-incL; then Nakayama. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Proposition 6.3.1 — matrix of inc_ℒ and its determinant mod 𝔪 (N ⩾ 4)
items.statement: Let N = 2r ⩾ 4 and ℒ = O(M†_N)^{⊗2} ⊗ (Lie_{𝒜,τ^c_∞})^{⊗(p+1)}. Then inc_ℒ := (inc*_†, T°•_{N,𝔭}∘inc*_•)∘Θ_ℒ∘(inc^†_! + inc^•_!∘T•°_{N,𝔭}) is given by the matrix [[(p+1)³, −(p+1)I°_{N,𝔭}], [−(p+1)I°_{N,𝔭}, T°•_{N,𝔭}∘(R•_{N,𝔭} + (R•_{N,𝔭} + (p+1)T•_{N,𝔭}))∘T•°_{N,𝔭}]] in T°_{N,𝔭}, and its determinant mod 𝔪 equals −p^{r²}∏_{i=1}^r(α_i + 1/α_i + 2)·((p+1)²p^{r²}∏_{i=1}^r(α_i + 1/α_i − p − 1/p) + (p+1)³(p^{r²+1} − p^{r²−1})∑_{j=1}^r∏_{i=1, i≠j}^r(α_i + 1/α_i − p − 1/p)), where {α_r, …, α_1, α_1⁻¹, …, α_r⁻¹} are the roots of P_{α(Π_𝔭)} mod λ in a finite extension of O_λ/λ. By (P2) p^{r²}(p+1)³(p^{r²+1} − p^{r²−1}) ≢ 0 mod λ; by (P4) ∏_i(α_i + 1/α_i − p − 1/p) ≡ 0 and ∑_j∏_{i≠j}(α_i + 1/α_i − p − 1/p) ≢ 0 mod λ; by (P5) ∏_i(α_i + 1/α_i + 2) ≢ 0 mod λ; hence inc_ℒ is nondegenerate modulo 𝔪.
items.note: From Propositions 5.8.8 (ℒ = O(M†)) and 5.8.9 (ℒ = Lie) by additivity of c_1, then Lemma B.3.6 and Proposition B.3.5(1)–(3) (q = p). Verified: det = (p+1)²I°[((p+1)R° − I°) + (p+1)(R° + (p+1)T°)], and B.3.5 gives φ(I°) = p^{r²}∏(α_i + α_i⁻¹ + 2), φ((p+1)R° − I°) = −p^{r²}∏(α_i + α_i⁻¹ − p − p⁻¹), φ(R° + (p+1)T°) = −(p^{r²+1} − p^{r²−1})∑_j∏_{i≠j}(…), reproducing the printed expression. Printed with 'P_{α(Π_{N,𝔭})}' and 'is given the matrix' (typos). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Proposition 6.3.1(4) — image of ∇⁰∘d∘d and the identity from Lemma B.3.6
items.note: Since I°_{N,𝔭} is invertible on the 𝔪-localization (Lemma 6.1.9), the quotient is O_λ[Sh(V°_N,K°_N)]_𝔪/((p+1)R°_{N,𝔭} − I°_{N,𝔭}). Verified from T•°∘R° = R•∘T•° and I° = T°•∘T•°. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 6.3.2 — H^{2r−2}(M̄•_N)_𝔪 is free of rank at most twice that of the Shimura set
items.statement: Suppose that N = 2r ⩾ 4. Assume Assumptions 6.1.4, 6.1.6 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for N. Then H^{2r−2}_𝔗(M̄•_N, O_λ)_𝔪 is a free O_λ-module, and its O_λ-rank is at most twice the rank of the (free) O_λ-module O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]_𝔪.
items.note: Proof: d_1^{0,2r−2} induces an injection H^{2r−2}(M̄•_N)_𝔪 ↪ H^{2r−2}(M̄†_N)_𝔪 ≅ O_λ[Sh(V°_N,K°_N)]_𝔪 ⊕ H^prim(M̄†_N, O_λ)_𝔪 (Assumption 6.1.4, Lemmas 5.9.3(2), 5.6.2(2); the injectivity also uses Lemma 5.6.2(1) and duality), so the source is free. For the rank, show (6.3) dim H^{2r−2}(M̄•_N, Q̄_ℓ)[ι_ℓπ^∞] ⩽ 2 dim Q̄_ℓ[Sh(V°_N,K°_N)][ι_ℓπ^∞] for each π completed via Proposition 5.6.4 (π_∞ trivial, π_𝔮 unramified for 𝔮 ≠ 𝔭, π_𝔭 a constituent of an unramified principal series, (V°_N, π) Π-congruent, BC(π) relevant by Lemma 6.1.10); by Chebotarev and Proposition 3.2.4(2), α(BC(π_𝔭)) avoids {−1,−1} (P5) and contains {p, p⁻¹} at most once (P4). Using (6.4) (Proposition 5.6.4: H^prim ≅ Map_{K°_{N,𝔭}}(…, Ω_N)) there are three cases: π_𝔭 unramified (multiplicity of Ω_N at most 1, Proposition C.2.1(2)); π_𝔭 ramified and ∉ 𝒮 (Lemma C.2.2(1): no Ω_N, both sides 0); π_𝔭 ∈ 𝒮 (Proposition C.2.5): Q̄_ℓ[Sh(K°)][π] = 0 and (6.5) embeds the left side into (π^{∞,p})^{K^{p∘}_N}, while nontrivial monodromy of ρ^c_{BC(π)} at 𝔭 (Lemma 6.1.11, Proposition C.3.1(2), Corollary C.3.2, Hypothesis 3.2.10, Proposition 3.2.4(2)) forces the cokernel of (6.5) to have full dimension, so the source vanishes. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Definition 6.3.3 — r̄ rigid for (Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_lr) (recalled from [51, §3.6])
items.statement: Let r̄: Γ_{F⁺} → 𝒢_N(O_λ/λ) be a continuous homomorphism with r̄⁻¹(GL_N(O_λ/λ) × (O_λ/λ)^×) = Γ_F and ν∘r̄ = η^N_{F/F⁺}ε_ℓ^{1−N}. r̄ is rigid for (Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_lr) if: (1) for v ∈ Σ⁺_min, every lifting of r̄_v is minimally ramified [51, Definition 3.4.8]; (2) for v ∈ Σ⁺_lr, the generalized eigenvalues of r̄^♮_v(φ_w) in F̄_ℓ contain the pair {‖v‖^{−N}, ‖v‖^{−N+2}} exactly once, where w is the unique place of F above v; (3) for v ∈ Σ⁺_ℓ, r̄^♮_v is regular Fontaine–Laffaille crystalline [51, Definition 3.2.4]; (4) for a nonarchimedean place v of F⁺ not in Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_lr ∪ Σ⁺_ℓ, r̄_v is unramified. All liftings are with respect to the similitude character η^N_{F/F⁺}ε_ℓ^{1−N}.
items.note: = [51, Definition 3.6.1] (checked against arXiv:2108.06998v1, p. 29). φ_w is an arithmetic Frobenius (§1.3 conventions); r̄^♮ is the restriction to Γ_F composed with the projection to GL_N (Notation 2.5.2). Condition (2) is only residual. An earlier version of this extraction's paraphrase ('exact special two-eigenvalue block', 'rigidity fixes the specified local lifting components') was inexact. Missing: routed to a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2/L7 (route 4).
