items.name: Theorem 6.3.4(1) — cohomology of the ground stratum M̄•_N is torsion free after localization
items.statement: Assume N = 2r even (r ⩾ 1), the §6.1 data with (P1)–(P6), Assumptions 6.1.4 and 6.1.6, Hypothesis 3.2.10 for N, and (a) ℓ ⩾ 2(N+1) and ℓ unramified in F; (b) ρ̄_{Π,λ,+} (Remark 6.1.7) is rigid for (Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_lr) (Definition 6.3.3) and ρ̄_{Π,λ}|_{Gal(F̄/F(ζ_ℓ))} is absolutely irreducible; (c) the composite T^{Σ⁺}_N →(φ_Π) O_E → O_E/λ is cohomologically generic (Definition D.1.1); (d) O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]_𝔪 is nonzero. Then H^i_𝔗(M̄•_N, O_λ)_𝔪 is a free O_λ-module for every i ∈ ℤ.
items.note: Key 'theorem-6-3-5' is historical (arXiv v3 numbered this Theorem 6.3.5); in the published version it is Theorem 6.3.4(1). Proof: Assumption 6.1.4, Lemma 5.6.2 and Lemma 5.9.3 give torsion-freeness for i ≠ 2r−1, 2r; Proposition 6.3.1(4) and Proposition 6.4.1 give it for i = 2r (the kernel in 6.3.1(4) is the torsion); Poincaré duality with Lemma 6.1.11 gives rank H^{2r} = rank H^{2r−2} and dim_{O_λ/λ} H^{2r}(M̄•, O_λ/λ)_𝔪 = dim H^{2r−2}(M̄•, O_λ/λ)_𝔪, whence H^{2r−1} is torsion free by universal coefficients. An earlier version of this extraction bundled (1) and (2); (2) is thm-6-3-4-2. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Theorem 6.3.4(2) — the localized E_2 page (N even) is free and supported on the three middle entries
items.statement: Assume N = 2r even (r ⩾ 1), the §6.1 data with (P1)–(P6), Assumptions 6.1.4 and 6.1.6, Hypothesis 3.2.10 for N, and (a) ℓ ⩾ 2(N+1) and ℓ unramified in F; (b) ρ̄_{Π,λ,+} (Remark 6.1.7) is rigid for (Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_lr) (Definition 6.3.3) and ρ̄_{Π,λ}|_{Gal(F̄/F(ζ_ℓ))} is absolutely irreducible; (c) the composite T^{Σ⁺}_N →(φ_Π) O_E → O_E/λ is cohomologically generic (Definition D.1.1); (d) O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]_𝔪 is nonzero. Then E^{p,q}_{2,𝔪} is a free O_λ-module, and vanishes if (p, q) ∉ {(−1, 2r), (0, 2r−1), (1, 2r−2)}.
items.note: Immediate from (1), Assumption 6.1.4, Lemma 5.6.2 and the spectral sequence of Lemma 5.9.3. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Theorem 6.3.4(3) — Frobenius eigenvalues on H^{2r−1}(M̄•_N) mod λ avoid 1 and p²
items.statement: Assume N = 2r even (r ⩾ 1), the §6.1 data with (P1)–(P6), Assumptions 6.1.4 and 6.1.6, Hypothesis 3.2.10 for N, and (a) ℓ ⩾ 2(N+1) and ℓ unramified in F; (b) ρ̄_{Π,λ,+} (Remark 6.1.7) is rigid for (Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_lr) (Definition 6.3.3) and ρ̄_{Π,λ}|_{Gal(F̄/F(ζ_ℓ))} is absolutely irreducible; (c) the composite T^{Σ⁺}_N →(φ_Π) O_E → O_E/λ is cohomologically generic (Definition D.1.1); (d) O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]_𝔪 is nonzero. Let {α_1^{±1}, …, α_r^{±1}} be the roots of P_{α(Π_𝔭)} mod λ in a finite extension of O_λ/λ. Then the generalized Frobenius eigenvalues of the (O_λ/λ)[Gal(F̄_p/F_{p²})]-module H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄•_N, O_λ(r))_𝔪 ⊗_{O_λ} O_λ/λ are contained in {pα_1^{±1}, …, pα_r^{±1}} \ {1, p²}.
items.note: An earlier version of this extraction stated only the exclusion of 1 and p². Proof as printed: consequence of (1) and (P4) via 'H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄•_N, O_λ(r)) ≃ H ⊗_{R^ram} R_1(r)' with R_1 undefined (source issue): R_1 should be the complement of the level-raising block span(v, v′) in (R^ram)^{⊕N}, on which r^♮_ram(φ_p²) has eigenvalues p^{1−2r}α_i^{±1} (i ≠ the level-raising index), twisted by ε_ℓ(φ_p²)^r = p^{2r}. The pair excluded, {p·p, p·p⁻¹} = {p², 1}, is where the level-raising pair lands. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Theorem 6.3.4(4) — arithmetic level-raising isomorphism modulo 𝔫
items.statement: Assume N = 2r even (r ⩾ 1), the §6.1 data with (P1)–(P6), Assumptions 6.1.4 and 6.1.6, Hypothesis 3.2.10 for N, and (a) ℓ ⩾ 2(N+1) and ℓ unramified in F; (b) ρ̄_{Π,λ,+} (Remark 6.1.7) is rigid for (Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_lr) (Definition 6.3.3) and ρ̄_{Π,λ}|_{Gal(F̄/F(ζ_ℓ))} is absolutely irreducible; (c) the composite T^{Σ⁺}_N →(φ_Π) O_E → O_E/λ is cohomologically generic (Definition D.1.1); (d) O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]_𝔪 is nonzero. Then the map of Proposition 6.3.1(4) factors through a map ∇⁰_{/𝔫}: F_{−1}H¹(I_{ℚ_{p²}}, H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨO_λ(r))/𝔫) → O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]/𝔫, which is an isomorphism, where 𝔫 is the ideal of Notation 6.1.3. The map from Lemma 5.9.3(6) induces a canonical isomorphism F_{−1}H¹(I_{ℚ_{p²}}, H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨO_λ(r))/𝔫) ≅ H¹_sing(ℚ_{p²}, H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨO_λ(r))/𝔫).
items.note: Proof: by Proposition 6.4.1 and (P6) (together with (P4) mod λ^m, which makes (p+1)R° − I° act by 0 on O_λ[Sh]/𝔫) it suffices that F_{−1}H¹(I, H_𝔪)/𝔫 → F_{−1}H¹(I, H/𝔫) and H¹_sing(ℚ_{p²}, H_𝔪)/𝔫 → H¹_sing(ℚ_{p²}, H/𝔫) are isomorphisms; the first because 0 → F_{−1}H¹(I,H_𝔪) → H¹(I,H_𝔪) → (H_𝔪/F_{−1}H_𝔪)(−1) → 0 splits by Frobenius eigenvalues and (3) (the '(−1)' is missing in print — source issue), the second because by (3) invariants can be replaced by coinvariants. An earlier version of this extraction bundled (4) and (5); (5) is thm-6-3-4-5. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Theorem 6.3.4(5) — the level-raised cohomology mod 𝔫 is a sum of copies of R̄^{(m)c}
items.statement: Assume N = 2r even (r ⩾ 1), the §6.1 data with (P1)–(P6), Assumptions 6.1.4 and 6.1.6, Hypothesis 3.2.10 for N, and (a) ℓ ⩾ 2(N+1) and ℓ unramified in F; (b) ρ̄_{Π,λ,+} (Remark 6.1.7) is rigid for (Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_lr) (Definition 6.3.3) and ρ̄_{Π,λ}|_{Gal(F̄/F(ζ_ℓ))} is absolutely irreducible; (c) the composite T^{Σ⁺}_N →(φ_Π) O_E → O_E/λ is cohomologically generic (Definition D.1.1); (d) O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]_𝔪 is nonzero. Then there exists a positive integer μ such that H^{2r−1}_ét(Sh(V′_N, j_N K^{p∘}_N K′_{p,N})_{F̄}, O_λ(r))/𝔫 ≃ (R̄^{(m)c})^{⊕μ} as O_λ[Γ_F]-modules, where R is the Γ_F-stable O_λ-lattice in ρ_{Π,λ}(r), unique up to homothety, and R̄^{(m)} = R ⊗ O_λ/λ^m.
items.note: Proof: H^{2r−1}_ét(…)/𝔫 ≅ H ⊗_{R^ram/𝔫} (R^ram/𝔫)^{⊕N}(r) by Lemma 5.2.7 (printed with ⊗ over R^ram/𝔫); claim O_λ/λ^m = R^ram/𝔫 'since 𝔫 ∩ O_λ = λ^m O_λ', then Chebotarev and Carayol [14, Théorème 1] identify (R^ram/𝔫)^{⊕N}(r) with R̄^{(m)c}; μ = d_ram. The equality O_λ/λ^m = R^ram/𝔫 is not justified by the stated hypotheses when Σ⁺_lr ≠ ∅ (source issue); it holds in the paper's applications. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Before Corollary 6.3.5 — the mod-ℓ Tate–Thompson map i
items.statement: Let N = 2r be even and suppose ℓ ∤ p∏_{i=1}^N(p^i − (−1)^i). Then the Tate–Thompson representation Ω_N of K°_{N,𝔭} (§C.2) has a model Ω_{N,F̄_ℓ} over F̄_ℓ, which is again an irreducible summand of Ind^{K°_{N,𝔭}}_{K°_{N,𝔭}∩K•_{N,𝔭}} F̄_ℓ. Hence a natural map of F̄_ℓ[T^{Σ⁺∪Σ⁺_p}_N]-modules i: F̄_ℓ[Sh(V°_N, K•_N)] → Map_{K°_{N,𝔭}}(U(V°_N)(F⁺)\U(V°_N)(A^∞_{F⁺})/K^{p∘}_N ∏_{𝔮|p, 𝔮≠𝔭} K°_{N,𝔮}, Ω_{N,F̄_ℓ}), defined as the composite of the inclusion F̄_ℓ[Sh(V°_N, K•_N)] → F̄_ℓ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N ∩ K•_N)], the tautological isomorphism F̄_ℓ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N ∩ K•_N)] ≅ Map_{K°_{N,𝔭}}(U(V°_N)(F⁺)\U(V°_N)(A^∞_{F⁺})/K^{p∘}_N ∏_{𝔮|p,𝔮≠𝔭} K°_{N,𝔮}, Ind^{K°_{N,𝔭}}_{K°_{N,𝔭}∩K•_{N,𝔭}} F̄_ℓ), and the projection Ind → Ω_{N,F̄_ℓ}.
items.note: ℓ ∤ p∏_{i=1}^N(p^i − (−1)^i) means ℓ ∤ |U_N(F_p)|, so mod-ℓ representation theory of U(Λ°_𝔭)(F_p) is semisimple. The paper calls the result an 'amazing corollary … which will not be used in this article'. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Corollary 6.3.5 — Ihara-type lemma for definite unitary Shimura sets
items.statement: Let N = 2r be even and let the setup be as in §6.1, but with (P4) replaced by the weaker condition that α(Π_𝔭) mod λ contains the pair {p, p⁻¹} at most once; suppose ℓ ∤ p∏_{i=1}^N(p^i − (−1)^i). Assume Assumptions 6.1.4, 6.1.6 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for N. Then i_𝔪 (the localization of the map i of tate-thompson-mod-l-map) is injective.
items.note: Published as Corollary 6.3.5 (not 'Theorem 6.3.5' as in an earlier version of this extraction; arXiv v3 stated it, unnumbered, inside Remark 6.3.3; absent from v1/v2). Not used later in the article. Proof given only for N ⩾ 4: with F̄_ℓ-coefficients (5.13) holds and i = (projection to H^prim)∘(m^{†•})*∘inc^•_!; by the injection H^{2r−2}(M̄•)_𝔪 ↪ H^{2r−2}(M̄†)_𝔪 it suffices that (inc^†_! + inc^•_!)_𝔪 on F̄_ℓ[Sh(K°)]_𝔪 ⊕ F̄_ℓ[Sh(K•)]_𝔪 is injective: by Proposition 6.3.1(1) if {p, p⁻¹} occurs, otherwise by injectivity of (inc_ℒ)_𝔪 for ℒ = O(M†_N), 'straightforward' from Proposition 5.8.8, Lemma 6.1.9, Proposition B.3.5(2), Lemma B.3.6 (determinant ∝ I°((p+1)R° − I°), a unit). The reduction steps are only sketched. An earlier version of this extraction's statement ('Tate–Thompson finite-type map', 'ℓ ∤ p∏(p^i − (−1)^i)') was imprecise. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: §6.4 — global deformation problems 𝒮^mix, 𝒮^unr, 𝒮^ram and the rings R^mix, R^unr, R^ram, R^cong
items.statement: (N = 2r even; hypotheses of Theorem 6.3.4.) Put r̄ := ρ̄_{Π,λ,+}: Γ_{F⁺} → 𝒢_N(O_λ/λ) and χ := ε_ℓ^{1−N} for the similitude character. Then r̄ is rigid for (Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_lr), and also for (Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_lr ∪ {𝔭}) by (P4). For ? ∈ {mix, unr, ram} let 𝒮^? := (r̄, χ, Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_lr ∪ {𝔭} ∪ Σ⁺_ℓ, {𝒟_v}_{v∈Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_lr∪{𝔭}∪Σ⁺_ℓ}) be the global deformation problem [51, Definition 3.1.6] with 𝒟_v = all liftings of r̄_v for v ∈ Σ⁺_min, 𝒟_v = 𝒟^ram for v ∈ Σ⁺_lr, 𝒟_𝔭 = 𝒟^? [51, Definition 3.5.1], and 𝒟_v = 𝒟^FL for v ∈ Σ⁺_ℓ [51, Definition 3.2.5]. Let R^? := R^univ_{𝒮^?} [51, Proposition 3.1.7]; there are canonical surjections R^mix → R^unr and R^mix → R^ram of O_λ-rings; put R^cong := R^unr ⊗_{R^mix} R^ram. A universal lifting r_mix: Γ_{F⁺} → 𝒢_N(R^mix) of r̄ induces r^♮_mix: Γ_F → GL_N(R^mix) by restriction (Notation 2.5.2), and by pushforward r_unr: Γ_{F⁺} → 𝒢_N(R^unr), r_ram: Γ_{F⁺} → 𝒢_N(R^ram).
items.note: The similitude character is printed 'η^μ_{F/F⁺}ε_ℓ^{1−N}' inside 𝒮^? ([51]'s notation η^μ, μ ∈ ℤ/2ℤ; here μ = 0 since N is even); source issue. An earlier version of this extraction merged this construction with the local relation (now local-model-6-4). Missing: routed to a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2/L7 (route 4).

items.name: §6.4 — local model at 𝔭: eigenvectors v, v′, eigenvalues s, s′, monodromy parameter x
items.statement: Let P_{F⁺_𝔭} ⊆ I_{F⁺_𝔭} ⊆ Γ_{F⁺_𝔭} be the maximal closed subgroup of the inertia subgroup of pro-order coprime to ℓ; then Γ_{F⁺_𝔭}/P_{F⁺_𝔭} ≃ t^{ℤ_ℓ} ⋊ φ_p^{ℤ̂} is a p-tame group [51, Definition 3.3.1] (φ_p t φ_p⁻¹ = t^p), and r^♮_mix is trivial on P_{F⁺_𝔭}. Let v̄, v̄′ ∈ (O_λ/λ)^{⊕N} be eigenvectors of r̄^♮(φ_p²) with eigenvalues p^{−2r} and p^{−2r+2}; by Hensel's lemma they lift to eigenvectors v, v′ ∈ (R^mix)^{⊕N} of r^♮_mix(φ_p²) with eigenvalues s, s′ ∈ R^mix lifting p^{−2r}, p^{−2r+2}. Let x ∈ R^mix be the unique element with r^♮_mix(t)v = v + xv′ (printed: r^♮_mix(t)v′ = xv + v′; see source issue). Then x(s − p^{−2r}) = 0, and by [51, Definition 3.5.1]: R^unr = R^mix/(x), R^ram = R^mix/(s − p^{−2r}), R^cong = R^mix/(s − p^{−2r}, x).
items.note: The relation x(s − p^{−2r}) = 0 and the three presentations are the content of [51, Proposition 3.5.2] (D^mix formally smooth over Spf O[[x_0, x_1]]/(x_0x_1), components D^unr = {x_0 = 0}, D^ram = {x_1 = 0}). With the printed direction of monodromy and φ_p t φ_p⁻¹ = t^p one would instead get x(s − p²s′) = 0 (source issue). Uses s′ = p^{−4r+2}s⁻¹ (polarization, cf. the characteristic polynomial below) and ℓ ∤ 2(p²−1). Missing: routed to a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2/L7 (route 4).

items.name: §6.4 — R^unr ≅ T^unr_𝔪 and freeness of the Shimura set module
items.statement: (Hypotheses of Theorem 6.3.4.) Let T^unr be the image of T^{Σ⁺}_N in End_{O_λ}(O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]). Then T^unr_𝔪 ≠ 0 by (d), and by [51, Theorem 3.6.3] there is a canonical isomorphism R^unr ≅ T^unr_𝔪 such that O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]_𝔪 is canonically a free R^unr-module of rank d_unr > 0.
items.note: Footnote 26: T^unr_𝔪 and O_λ[Sh(V°_N,K°_N)]_𝔪 do not change if 𝔪 is replaced by 𝔪 ∩ T^{Σ⁺∪Σ⁺_p∪Σ⁺_ℓ}_N (needed since [51] uses Hecke algebras away from ℓ). [51, Theorem 3.6.3] applies with the definite V°_N (d(V) = 0), hypotheses (D1) = (a), (D2) = (b), (D3) rigidity, (D4) = (c). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §6.4 — the level-raising quotient of the Shimura set is O_λ[Sh]_𝔪 ⊗_{R^unr} R^cong
items.statement: (Hypotheses of Theorem 6.3.4.) The characteristic polynomial of r^♮_unr(φ_p²) can be written (T − s)(T − p^{−4r+2}s⁻¹)Q(T) with Q(T) ∈ R^unr[T] whose reduction in (O_λ/λ)[T] has neither p^{−2r} nor p^{−2r+2} as a root. By Proposition B.3.5(2), ((p+1)R°_{N,𝔭} − I°_{N,𝔭})·O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]_𝔪 = (s − p^{−2r})·O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]_𝔪. In particular O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]_𝔪/((p+1)R°_{N,𝔭} − I°_{N,𝔭}) = O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]_𝔪 ⊗_{R^unr} R^cong, which is a free R^cong-module of rank d_unr.
items.note: Check: φ_α((p+1)R° − I°) = −p^{r²}∏_i(α_i + α_i⁻¹ − p − p⁻¹); for the level-raising index, with s = p^{1−2r}α⁻¹, the factor is (α − p)(α − p⁻¹)/α = unit·(s − p^{−2r}); the other factors are units because Q has no root ≡ p^{−2r}, p^{−2r+2}. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §6.4 — R^ram ≅ T^ram_𝔪, the multiplicity module H, and H^{2r−1}_𝔪 ≅ H ⊗ (R^ram)^{⊕N}
items.statement: (Hypotheses of Theorem 6.3.4.) Let T^ram be the image of T^{Σ⁺∪Σ⁺_p}_N (printed T^{Σ⁺∩Σ⁺_p}_N) in End_{O_λ}(H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨO_λ)). By Proposition 6.3.1(4) and Lemma 5.9.3(6), T^ram_𝔪 ≠ 0; by Lemma 5.2.7 and [51, Theorem 3.6.3] (with (Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_lr) replaced by (Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_lr ∪ {𝔭})) there is a canonical isomorphism R^ram ≅ T^ram_𝔪 such that H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨO_λ)_𝔪 is canonically a free R^ram-module. Put H := Hom_{Γ_F}((R^ram)^{⊕N}, H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨO_λ)_𝔪), where Γ_F acts on (R^ram)^{⊕N} via r^{♮,c}_ram. Then there is a canonical isomorphism H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨO_λ)_𝔪 ≅ H ⊗_{R^ram} (R^ram)^{⊕N} of R^ram[Γ_F]-modules, and H is a free R^ram-module, of rank d_ram say.
items.note: The tensor decomposition is 'by the same argument for [67, Theorem 5.6] (using Proposition C.3.1 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 here)'; H is free because R^ram is local. Footnote 27: T^ram_𝔪 and H^{2r−1}_𝔪 do not change if 𝔪 is replaced by 𝔪 ∩ T^{Σ⁺∪Σ⁺_p∪Σ⁺_ℓ}_N, a consequence of Theorem 6.3.4(c). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §6.4 — H¹_sing of the level-raised cohomology is H ⊗_{R^ram} R^cong
items.statement: (Hypotheses of Theorem 6.3.4.) H¹_sing(ℚ_{p²}, (R^ram)^{⊕N}(r)) ≅ R^ram/(x) = R^cong (printed as 'R^ram v/xv', see source issue on the local model; correctly the x-torsion line is spanned by the image of v′). Consequently H¹_sing(ℚ_{p²}, H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨO_λ(r))_𝔪) ≅ H ⊗_{R^ram} H¹_sing(ℚ_{p²}, (R^ram)^{⊕N}(r)) ≅ H ⊗_{R^ram} R^cong, a free R^cong-module of rank d_ram > 0.
items.note: An earlier version of this extraction described this as 'congruence comparison by finite cardinality … transport through the Hecke depth-m quotient', which mixes this computation with Proposition 6.4.1 and Theorem 6.3.4(4). Computation: H¹(I, M(r)) = M_I(r−1); in R^ram (s = p^{−2r}, s′ = p^{−2r+2}) φ_p² acts on the class of v′ by 1 and on the class of v by p^{−2}; the other eigenvalues are ≢ 1. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proposition 6.4.1 — d_unr = d_ram; the level-raising and singular-quotient maps are isomorphisms
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem 6.3.4, d_unr = d_ram. In particular the two canonical maps F_{−1}H¹(I_{ℚ_{p²}}, H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨO_λ(r))_𝔪) → O_λ[Sh(V°_N, K°_N)]_𝔪/((p+1)R°_{N,𝔭} − I°_{N,𝔭}) and F_{−1}H¹(I_{ℚ_{p²}}, H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨO_λ(r))_𝔪) → H¹_sing(ℚ_{p²}, H^{2r−1}_𝔗(M̄_N, RΨO_λ(r))_𝔪), from Proposition 6.3.1(4) and Lemma 5.9.3(6) respectively, are both isomorphisms.
items.note: Published numbering: Proposition 6.4.1 and Lemma 6.4.2 (the task description's 'Lemma 6.4.1, Proposition 6.4.2' is reversed). Proof: the first map is surjective (6.3.1(4)), the second injective (5.9.3(6)), so d_ram ⩾ d_unr > 0 (comparison of free R^cong-modules; R^cong has finite length). For equality take Q̄_ℓ-points η_1 of Spec R^unr in the support of O_λ[Sh(V°_N,K°_N)]_𝔪 and η_2 of Spec R^ram in the support of H^{2r−1}_𝔪, corresponding (Lemma 6.1.10) to relevant Π_1, Π_2 with ρ_{Π_i,ι_ℓ} residually ≅ ρ̄_{Π,λ} ⊗ F̄_ℓ: d_unr = dim Q̄_ℓ[Sh(V°_N,K°_N)][ι_ℓφ_{Π_1}], N·d_ram = dim H^{2r−1}_ét(Sh(V′_N, j_N K^{p∘}_N K′_{p,N})_{F̄}, Q̄_ℓ)[ι_ℓφ_{Π_2}] (Lemma 5.2.7); Proposition D.2.3 expresses both through ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min} tr(Π_v(φ_{K_v})∘A_{Π_v}) (and c_v = 1 at the level-raising places), and Lemma 6.4.2 makes the local factors for Π_1, Π_2 equal. An earlier version of this extraction bundled this with Lemma 6.4.2; split. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 6.4.2 — matching normalized intertwining operators at minimally ramified places
items.statement: Let Π_1 and Π_2 be relevant representations of GL_N(A_F) such that ρ_{Π_1,ι_ℓ} and ρ_{Π_2,ι_ℓ} are both residually isomorphic to ρ̄_{Π,λ} ⊗_{O_λ/λ} F̄_ℓ. For every v ∈ Σ⁺_min (so that every lifting of ρ̄_{Π,λ,+,v} is minimally ramified), if Π_{1,v} and Π_{2,v} are realized on vector spaces V_1 and V_2, then there exist normalized intertwining operators A_{Π_{1,v}}, A_{Π_{2,v}} for Π_{1,v}, Π_{2,v} [71, §4.1] and a GL_N(O_{F_v})-equivariant isomorphism i: V_1 ≅ V_2 with i∘A_{Π_{1,v}} = A_{Π_{2,v}}∘i.
items.note: Proof given for v nonsplit in F (split case 'left to the readers'). Π_{α,w} tempered (Proposition 3.2.4(1)), so Π_{α,w} = I^{GL_N(F_w)}_{P_α}(σ_{α,−t_α} ⊠ … ⊠ σ_{α,t_α}) with unitary discrete series σ_{α,−i} ≃ σ^{∨c}_{α,i}; by [51, Proposition 3.4.12(3)] and [3, Lemma 1.3.4(2)] ρ_{Π_1}|_{I_{F_w}} and ρ_{Π_2}|_{I_{F_w}} are conjugate, so by [76, Lemma 3.6] P_1 = P_2 = P, t_1 = t_2 = t and σ_{2,i} = σ_{1,i} ⊗ χ_i with unramified unitary χ_i, χ_{−i} ≃ χ_i⁻¹. With A_i: W_i → W_{−i} intertwining σ_{1,i} and σ^{∨c}_{1,−i}, A_{−i}∘A_i = id, A_σ = ⊗A_i, and w ∈ GL_N(F_w) with w = ᵗw^c reversing the blocks, (A_{Π_{1,w}}f)(g) = A_σ(f(w ᵗg^{−1,c})), same formula for Π_{2,w} (realized with the extra character χ); i(f) is the unique function in V_2 agreeing with f on GL_N(O_{F_w}). Implicitly w must be chosen in GL_N(O_{F_w}) (a block permutation matrix) for i to intertwine the A's. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: [51, Theorem 3.6.3] — an almost minimal R = T theorem for rigid r̄ (cited)
items.statement: Let ξ be a weight with ℓ ⩾ (b_ξ − a_ξ) + 2, ℓ odd and unramified in F; let Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_lr, Σ⁺_ℓ be mutually disjoint, Σ⁺_min ⊇ Σ⁺_bad, every v ∈ Σ⁺_lr inert in F with ℓ ∤ (‖v‖² − 1), and Σ⁺_lr = ∅ if N is odd. Let V be a hermitian space of rank N with V_v not split for v ∈ Σ⁺_lr, Λ a self-dual lattice away from Σ⁺_∞ ∪ Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_lr, K = ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_lr} K_v × ∏ U(Λ)(O_{F⁺_v}) neat with K_v special maximal for v ∈ Σ⁺_lr, Σ⁺ ⊇ Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_lr ∪ Σ⁺_ℓ, and 𝔪 the kernel of the homomorphism T^{Σ⁺}_N → k attached to r̄ (Hecke parameter α at inert v with {α_i‖v‖^{N−1}} the generalized eigenvalues of r̄^♮_v(φ_w⁻¹)). Assume (D1) ℓ ⩾ 2(N+1); (D2) r̄^♮|_{Gal(F̄/F(ζ_ℓ))} absolutely irreducible; (D3) r̄ rigid for (Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_lr); (D4) for all Σ⁺′ ⊇ Σ⁺ and K′ ⊆ K with K′_v = K_v for v ∉ Σ⁺′, H^d_ét(Sh(V, K′), L_ξ ⊗ k)_{T^{Σ⁺′}_N ∩ 𝔪} = 0 for d ≠ d(V). Let T be the image of T^{Σ⁺}_N in End_O(H^{d(V)}_ét(Sh(V, K), L_ξ)). If T_𝔪 ≠ 0 then (1) there is a canonical isomorphism R^univ_𝒮 ≅ T_𝔪 of local complete intersection rings over O, where 𝒮 = (r̄, η^μ ε_ℓ^{1−N}, Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_lr ∪ Σ⁺_ℓ, {all liftings, 𝒟^ram, 𝒟^FL}); (2) H^{d(V)}_ét(Sh(V, K), L_ξ)_𝔪 is a finite free T_𝔪-module; (3) μ ≡ N mod 2.
items.note: Cited, not proved here (companion paper, Taylor–Wiles–Kisin patching). Applied twice: to V°_N with (Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_lr) giving R^unr ≅ T^unr_𝔪, and to V′_N (via Lemma 5.2.7) with (Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_lr ∪ {𝔭}) giving R^ram ≅ T^ram_𝔪. Statement transcribed from arXiv:2108.06998v1 (the version cited). Missing: routed to the Part II PolarizedAutomorphyLifting (route 15).

items.name: [51, Definition 3.5.1, Proposition 3.5.2] — level-raising local deformation problems 𝒟^mix, 𝒟^unr, 𝒟^ram (cited)
items.statement: Let v be a place of F⁺ inert in F, not above ℓ, w the place of F above v, q = ‖v‖, with ℓ ⩾ N ⩾ 2, r̄ unramified at v, χ = η^μ_v ε_ℓ^{1−N}, ℓ ∤ (q² − 1), and the generalized eigenvalues of r̄^♮(φ_w) containing {q^{−N}, q^{−N+2}} exactly once. For every lifting r to R ∈ C_O there is a canonical r^♮(φ_w)-stable decomposition R^{⊕N} = M_0 ⊕ M_1 with the characteristic polynomial P_0 of r^♮(φ_w) on M_0 ≡ (T − q^{−N})(T − q^{−N+2}). 𝒟^mix classifies liftings with r^♮(I_{F_w}) preserving M_0 and acting trivially on M_1; 𝒟^unr ⊆ 𝒟^mix: I_{F_w} also acts trivially on M_0 (= 𝒟^min); 𝒟^ram ⊆ 𝒟^mix: P_0(T) = (T − q^{−N})(T − q^{−N+2}) in R[T]. Proposition 3.5.2: 𝒟^mix is formally smooth over Spf O[[x_0, x_1]]/(x_0x_1) of pure relative dimension N² − 1, with components {x_0 = 0} = 𝒟^unr and {x_1 = 0} = 𝒟^ram; 𝒟^ram is formally smooth of relative dimension N².
items.locator: cited in §6.4, published pp. 280–281; [51] §3.5, pp. 26–28 (Definition 3.5.1 and Proposition 3.5.2 on p. 27)
items.note: Cited, not proved here. In the proof of [51, Prop. 3.5.2] (N = 2), in the basis with r^♮(φ_q²) = diag(q^{−N}(1+x)(1+y)⁻¹, q^{−N+2}(1+y)(1+x)⁻¹), r^♮(t) = 1 + (0 0; x_0 0): the monodromy sends the q^{−N}-eigenvector to the q^{−N+2}-eigenvector; x_1 = x − y. Missing: routed to a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2/L7 (route 4).

items.name: [51, Definition 3.3.1] — the q-tame group (cited)
items.statement: For a positive integer q coprime to ℓ, the q-tame group T_q is the semidirect product t^{ℤ_ℓ} ⋊ φ_q^{ℤ̂} with φ_q t φ_q⁻¹ = t^q; for b ⩾ 1, T_{q^b} is identified with the subgroup topologically generated by t and φ_q^b.
items.note: For v = 𝔭 (q = p), Γ_{F⁺_𝔭}/P_{F⁺_𝔭} ≅ T_p and Γ_{F_𝔭}/P ≅ T_{p²}. Missing: routed to a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2/L7 (route 4).

items.name: [51, Definition 3.1.6, Proposition 3.1.7] — global deformation problems and universal rings (cited)
items.statement: A global deformation problem is a tuple 𝒮 = (r̄, χ, S, {𝒟_v}_{v∈S}) with (r̄, χ) as in [51, Notation 3.1.1] (r̄: Γ_{F⁺} → 𝒢_N(k), similitude character χ), S a finite set of nonarchimedean places of F⁺ containing all ℓ-adic places and all places where r̄ is ramified, and 𝒟_v a local deformation problem of r̄_v for v ∈ S; a lifting is of type 𝒮 if r_v ∈ 𝒟_v for v ∈ S and r is unramified outside S. If r̄|_{Γ_F} is absolutely irreducible, the functor of (T-framed) deformations of type 𝒮 is represented by a Noetherian ring; R^univ_𝒮 := R^{□∅}_𝒮.
items.note: Cited, not proved here. Missing: routed to the Part II PolarizedAutomorphyLifting (route 15).

items.name: [51, Proposition 3.4.12(3)] — minimally ramified liftings form a smooth component (cited)
items.statement: For v nonarchimedean not above ℓ, the local lifting ring R^loc_{r̄_v} is a reduced local complete intersection, flat of pure relative dimension N² over O, each irreducible component of Spf R^loc is a local deformation problem, and, when ℓ ⩾ N, 𝒟^min (minimally ramified liftings, [51, Definition 3.4.8]) is an irreducible component of Spf R^loc_{r̄_v}, formally smooth over Spf O of pure relative dimension N².
items.locator: cited in the proof of Lemma 6.4.2, published p. 284; [51] §3.4, p. 25
items.note: Used as: when every lifting of ρ̄_{Π,λ,+,v} is minimally ramified (rigidity at Σ⁺_min), all characteristic-0 lifts lie on the single smooth component, so (with [3, Lemma 1.3.4(2)]) their restrictions to inertia are conjugate. Missing: routed to a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2/L7 (route 4).

items.name: [3, Lemma 1.3.4(2)] — lifts on a common component have conjugate inertial restrictions (cited)
items.statement: (As used.) If two characteristic-0 liftings of r̄_v (v ∤ ℓ) lie on the same irreducible component of the local lifting ring, then their restrictions to the inertia group I_{F_w} are conjugate.
items.locator: cited in the proof of Lemma 6.4.2, published p. 284
items.note: Cited from Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty–Taylor, 'Potential automorphy and change of weight'; paraphrase of the use made here, not a transcription. Missing: routed to a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2/L7 (route 4).

items.name: [76, Lemma 3.6] — tempered representations with the same inertial type differ by unramified twists (cited)
items.statement: (As used.) If Π_{1,w}, Π_{2,w} are tempered, written as I^{GL_N(F_w)}_{P_α}(σ_{α,−t_α} ⊠ … ⊠ σ_{α,t_α}) (α = 1, 2), and the restrictions to I_{F_w} of the associated Weil–Deligne representations are conjugate, then P_1 = P_2, t_1 = t_2, and after reordering σ_{2,i} = σ_{1,i} ⊗ χ_i for unramified unitary characters χ_i of F_w^×, with χ_{−i} ≃ χ_i⁻¹ in the conjugate-self-dual situation.
items.locator: cited in the proof of Lemma 6.4.2, published p. 284
items.note: Cited from Z. Yao, 'The Breuil–Mézard conjecture for function fields' (arXiv:1808.09433); paraphrase of the use. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: [71, §4.1] — normalized intertwining operators for conjugate-self-dual representations (cited)
items.statement: For an irreducible admissible representation Π_w of GL_N(F_w) with Π_w ∘ θ ≅ Π_w (θ(g) = ᵗg^{−1,c}), a normalized intertwining operator is an operator A_{Π_w} on the space of Π_w with A_{Π_w}∘Π_w(g) = Π_w(θ(g))∘A_{Π_w}, normalized as in [71, §4.1] (here A² = 1).
items.locator: cited in Lemma 6.4.2 and Proposition D.2.3, published pp. 283–284
items.note: Cited from Shin, 'Galois representations arising from some compact Shimura varieties'; the traces tr(Π_v(φ_{K_v})∘A_{Π_v}) appear in Proposition D.2.3. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: [74, Lemma 1.4(3)] — purity of ρ_{Π′}(r) at 𝔭 (cited)
items.statement: (As used.) For a relevant representation Π′ of GL_N(A_F) (N = 2r), ρ_{Π′,ι_ℓ}(r) is pure of weight −1 at 𝔭 (Definition 2.4.4).
items.locator: cited in the proof of Proposition 6.3.1(4), published p. 275; also Cited in the proof of Lemma 8.1.6, published p. 306
items.note: Cited from Taylor–Yoshida, 'Compatibility of local and global Langlands correspondences', combined with Proposition 3.2.4 (temperedness, local–global compatibility). Planned: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.5 plans local–global compatibility, including the Taylor–Yoshida and Caraiani purity upgrades.

items.name: [56, Proposition 4.2.2(1)] — vanishing of local H¹ for weight −1 (cited)
items.statement: (As used.) If V is a finite-dimensional continuous ℓ-adic representation of Gal(Q̄_p/ℚ_{p²}) (ℓ ≠ p) that is pure of weight −1, then H¹(ℚ_{p²}, V) = 0.
items.locator: cited in the proof of Proposition 6.3.1(4), published p. 275
items.note: Cited from Nekovář, 'On the parity of ranks of Selmer groups III'. Consequence used: F_{−1}H¹(I_{ℚ_{p²}}, H^{2r−1}_𝔪) ⊆ H¹_sing(ℚ_{p²}, H^{2r−1}_𝔪) are torsion O_λ-modules. Missing: routed to a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 (route 1).

items.name: [67, Theorem 5.6] — argument giving H^{2r−1}_𝔪 ≅ H ⊗ (R^ram)^{⊕N} (cited)
items.statement: (As used.) If a finite free R^ram[Γ_F]-module M has, at every Q̄_ℓ-point of R^ram, fibre isomorphic to a sum of copies of the Galois representation r^{♮,c}_ram at that point (here guaranteed by Proposition C.3.1 and Hypothesis 3.2.10), then the evaluation map Hom_{Γ_F}((R^ram)^{⊕N}, M) ⊗_{R^ram} (R^ram)^{⊕N} → M is an isomorphism.
items.note: The paper says only 'by the same argument for [67, Theorem 5.6]' (Scholze, 'On the p-adic cohomology of the Lubin–Tate tower'); the statement here is a reconstruction of what is used (Carayol-type multiplicity-freeness argument with residually absolutely irreducible r̄). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: [14, Théorème 1] — liftings are determined by traces (cited)
items.statement: (As used.) Let A be a complete local Noetherian ring with finite residue field and ρ, ρ′: Γ → GL_N(A) continuous representations whose residual representation is absolutely irreducible. If tr ρ(g) = tr ρ′(g) for all g ∈ Γ, then ρ and ρ′ are conjugate.
items.locator: cited in the proof of Theorem 6.3.4(5), published p. 286
items.note: Cited from Carayol (Contemp. Math. 165, 1994). Combined with Chebotarev to identify (R^ram/𝔫)^{⊕N}(r) with R̄^{(m)c} over O_λ/λ^m. Missing: routed to a source of GlobalGaloisDeformations G7 (route 3).

items.name: §7.1 — the ranks n₀, n₁ and r₀, r₁
items.statement: Let n ⩾ 2 be an integer. Denote by n₀ and n₁ the unique even and the unique odd number in {n, n+1}, respectively, and write n₀ = 2r₀ and n₁ = 2r₁+1 for unique integers r₀, r₁ ⩾ 1. In particular n = r₀ + r₁.
items.note: Check: if n is even then n₀ = n, n₁ = n+1, r₀ = r₁ = n/2; if n is odd then n₁ = n, n₀ = n+1, r₀ = r₁+1. The same convention is used in §§4.6, 5.11 and 8. Throughout §7, objects indexed by n₀, n₁ are those indexed by n, n+1 in some order, so e.g. Sh(V_{n₀}) × Sh(V_{n₁}) is Sh(V_n) × Sh(V_{n+1}) up to swapping the factors. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §7.1 — the automorphic Rankin–Selberg data (Π₀, Π₁, E, Σ⁺_min, φ_{Π_α}, ρ_{Π_α,λ})
items.statement: In §§7–8 one considers, for α = 0, 1, a relevant representation Π_α of GL_{n_α}(𝔸_F) (Definition 1.1.3), and a strong coefficient field E ⊆ ℂ of both Π₀ and Π₁ (Definition 3.2.5). Put Σ⁺_min := Σ⁺_{Π₀} ∪ Σ⁺_{Π₁} (Notation 3.1.4). Then for α = 0, 1 there is a homomorphism φ_{Π_α}: 𝕋^{Σ⁺_min}_{n_α} → O_E, and for α = 0, 1 and every prime λ of E there is a continuous homomorphism ρ_{Π_α,λ}: Γ_F → GL_{n_α}(E_λ) (Proposition 3.2.4(2) and Definition 3.2.5) such that ρ^c_{Π_α,λ} and ρ^∨_{Π_α,λ}(1−n_α) are conjugate.
items.note: φ_{Π_α} is the Hecke character of Construction 3.1.10 (the spherical Hecke algebra away from Σ⁺_min acting on the Π_α-isotypic part). Setup data only; nothing is proved here. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Assumption 7.1.1 — residual absolute irreducibility of ρ_{Π₀,λ} and ρ_{Π₁,λ}
items.statement: For α = 0, 1, the Galois representation ρ_{Π_α,λ}: Γ_F → GL_{n_α}(E_λ) is residually absolutely irreducible.
items.note: Two propositions (α = 0 and α = 1). The prime λ is free in the printed assumption; it is the prime λ of E chosen at the start of §7.2 (resp. §7.3). Residual irreducibility makes the reduction ρ̄_{Π_α,λ} (and a Γ_F-stable lattice up to homothety) well defined; it reappears as condition (L4) of Definition 8.1.1. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

api.name: RankinSelberg.ResidualIrreducibilityForTheTwoFactors.1
api.statement: Project each factor’s residual irreducibility.

api.name: RankinSelberg.ResidualIrreducibilityForTheTwoFactors.2
api.statement: The conjunction is equivalent to the two separate factor statements.

api.name: RankinSelberg.ResidualIrreducibilityForTheTwoFactors.3
api.statement: Extending the residual coefficient field preserves absolute irreducibility.

items.name: §7.2 — auxiliary data for the first explicit reciprocity law (λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,I}, Σ⁺_I, V°_n, Λ°_n, K°)
items.statement: One chooses: • a prime λ of E whose underlying rational prime ℓ satisfies Σ⁺_min ∩ Σ⁺_ℓ = ∅, ℓ ⩾ 2(n₀+1), and ℓ unramified in F; • a positive integer m; • a (possibly empty) finite set Σ⁺_{lr,I} of nonarchimedean places of F⁺ that are inert in F, strongly disjoint from Σ⁺_min (Definition 1.3.2), satisfying ℓ ∤ ‖v‖(‖v‖²−1) for v ∈ Σ⁺_{lr,I}; • a finite set Σ⁺_I of nonarchimedean places of F⁺ containing Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_{lr,I}; • a standard definite hermitian space V°_n of rank n over F, together with a self-dual ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_{lr,I}} O_{F_v}-lattice Λ°_n in V°_n ⊗_F 𝔸_F^{Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_{lr,I}} (and put V°_{n+1} := (V°_n)_♯, Λ°_{n+1} := (Λ°_n)_♯), such that the hermitian space (V°_{n₀})_v is not split for v ∈ Σ⁺_{lr,I}; • objects K°_n ∈ 𝔎(V°_n) and (K°_sp, K°_{n+1}) ∈ 𝔎(V°_n)_sp of the forms K°_n = ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_{lr,I}} (K°_n)_v × ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_{lr,I}} U(Λ°_n)(O_{F⁺_v}), K°_sp = ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_{lr,I}} (K°_sp)_v × ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_{lr,I}} U(Λ°_n)(O_{F⁺_v}), K°_{n+1} = ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_{lr,I}} (K°_{n+1})_v × ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_{lr,I}} U(Λ°_{n+1})(O_{F⁺_v}), satisfying (K°_sp)_v = (K°_n)_v for v ∈ Σ⁺_min, (K°_sp)_v ⊆ (K°_n)_v for v ∈ Σ⁺_{lr,I}, and (K°_{n₀})_v is a transferable open compact subgroup (Definition D.2.1) of U(V°_{n₀})(F⁺_v) for v ∈ Σ⁺_min and a special maximal subgroup of U(V°_{n₀})(F⁺_v) for v ∈ Σ⁺_{lr,I}.
items.note: Setup data (first half of the list; the prime 𝔭 and (PI1)–(PI7) are item assumptions-7-2). Footnote 28: 'lr' = level-raising, 'I' = first. (V°_n)_♯ = V°_n ⊕ O·1 with ‖1‖ = 1 (Definition 3.1.7). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §7.2 — the special inert prime 𝔭 and conditions (PI1)–(PI7)
items.statement: In addition to the auxiliary data, one chooses a special inert prime 𝔭 of F⁺ (Definition 3.3.4), with underlying rational prime p, satisfying: (PI1) Σ⁺_I does not contain p-adic places; (PI2) ℓ does not divide p(p²−1); (PI3) there exists a CM type Φ containing τ_∞ as in the initial setup of §5 satisfying ℚ_p^Φ = ℚ_{p²}; (PI4) P_{α(Π_{0,𝔭})} mod λ^m is level-raising special at 𝔭, and P_{α(Π_{1,𝔭})} mod λ is Tate generic at 𝔭 (Definition 3.1.5); (PI5) P_{α(Π_{α,𝔭})} mod λ is intertwining generic at 𝔭 (Definition 3.1.5) for α = 0, 1; (PI6) for α = 0, 1 the natural map (O_E/λ^m)[Sh(V°_{n_α}, K°_{n_α})] / (𝕋^{Σ⁺_I∪Σ⁺_p}_{n_α} ∩ ker φ_{Π_α}) → (O_E/λ^m)[Sh(V°_{n_α}, K°_{n_α})] / (𝕋^{Σ⁺_I}_{n_α} ∩ ker φ_{Π_α}) is an isomorphism of nontrivial O_E/λ^m-modules; (PI7) P_{α(Π_{0,𝔭})⊗α(Π_{1,𝔭})} mod λ^m is level-raising special at 𝔭 (Definition 3.1.5). (So the setup of §5.10 applies to the datum (V°_n, {Λ°_{n,𝔮}}_{𝔮|p}).) One further fixes the remaining data of §5.1 with ℚ_p^Φ = ℚ_{p²}, and data as in Notation 5.10.13, which in particular give open compact subgroups K•_{n,p} and K•_{n+1,p}.
items.note: Definition 3.1.5 (for v inert, ‖v‖ invertible in L, P monic of degree N with P(T) = (−T)^N P(T⁻¹)): N odd — Tate generic iff P′(1) ∈ L^×, intertwining generic iff P(−‖v‖) ∈ L^×; N even — level-raising special iff P(‖v‖) = 0 and P′(‖v‖) ∈ L^×, intertwining generic iff P(−1) ∈ L^×. Here ‖𝔭‖ = p. In (PI6), 'M/(I)' means M/IM. (PI6) is what lets Hecke operators at 𝔭 act on (O_λ/λ^m)[Sh][𝔫_α] through φ_{Π_α} (used at the end of the proof of Theorem 7.2.8(3)). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §7.2 — level subgroups K^{p∘}, K•, schemes X^?_{n_α}, and the weight spectral sequences ^αE
items.statement: Put K^{p∘}_sp := (K°_sp)^p and K•_sp := K^{p∘}_sp × K•_{n₀,p} [as printed; see source issue]; put K^{p∘}_{n_α} := (K°_{n_α})^p and K•_{n_α} := K^{p∘}_{n_α} × K•_{n_α,p} for α = 0, 1. As in §5.11, put X^?_{n_α} := X^?_𝔭(V°_{n_α}, K^{p∘}_{n_α}) for meaningful triples (X, ?, α) ∈ {𝐌, M, B, S} × { , η, ∘, •, †} × {0, 1}. For α = 0, 1, let (^αE^{p,q}_s, ^αd^{p,q}_s) be the weight spectral sequence abutting to H^{p+q}_𝔗(M̄_{n_α}, RΨO_λ(r_α)) from §5.9.
items.locator: §7.2, paragraph after the data list, published p. 288
items.note: 𝐌 (bold) is the semistable integral model over ℤ_{p²}, M its special fibre, M̄ = M ⊗ F̄_p, X^η the generic fibre (Notation 3.3.6(5)); ∘, •, † are the two families of irreducible components of the special fibre and their intersection (§5). ^αE_1^{p,q} = ⊕_{i⩾max(0,−p)} H^{q−2i}(M̄^{(p+2i)}_{n_α}, O_λ(r_α−i)). K•_sp is not used again in §7. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Notation 7.2.1 — the ideals 𝔪_α and 𝔫_α
items.statement: For α = 0, 1 introduce the following ideals of 𝕋^{Σ⁺_I∪Σ⁺_p}_{n_α}: 𝔪_α := 𝕋^{Σ⁺_I∪Σ⁺_p}_{n_α} ∩ ker(𝕋^{Σ⁺}_{n_α} →^{φ_{Π_α}} O_E → O_E/λ), 𝔫_α := 𝕋^{Σ⁺_I∪Σ⁺_p}_{n_α} ∩ ker(𝕋^{Σ⁺}_{n_α} →^{φ_{Π_α}} O_E → O_E/λ^m). [𝕋^{Σ⁺}_{n_α} as printed; read 𝕋^{Σ⁺_min}_{n_α}, the domain of φ_{Π_α} — see source issue; the ideals are the same for any Σ⁺ with Σ⁺_min ⊆ Σ⁺ ⊆ Σ⁺_I.]
items.note: 𝔫_α ⊆ 𝔪_α; 𝔪_α is maximal and is the only maximal ideal containing 𝔫_α, so for any 𝕋-module M one has M/𝔫_α M = M_{𝔪_α}/𝔫_α M_{𝔪_α}. Subscript (𝔪₀,𝔪₁) means localization of a 𝕋^{Σ⁺_I∪Σ⁺_p}_{n₀} ⊗ 𝕋^{Σ⁺_I∪Σ⁺_p}_{n₁}-module at both ideals; '/(𝔫₀,𝔫₁)' the quotient by both. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Assumption 7.2.2 — rigidity of ρ̄_{Π₀,λ,+} and big image over F(ζ_ℓ)
items.statement: Under Assumption 7.1.1, the homomorphism ρ̄_{Π₀,λ,+} (Remark 6.1.7) is rigid for (Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_{lr,I}) (Definition 6.3.3); and ρ̄_{Π₀,λ}|_{Gal(F̄/F(ζ_ℓ))} is absolutely irreducible.
items.note: Used (via Theorem 6.3.4) for the even-rank factor n₀. arXiv v3 cites 'Definition 6.3.4' here; the published version correctly cites Definition 6.3.3. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Assumption 7.2.3 — localized nearby-cycle cohomology concentrated in the middle degree and free
items.statement: For α = 0, 1: H^i_𝔗(M̄_{n_α}, RΨO_λ)_{𝔪_α} = 0 for i ≠ n_α − 1, and H^{n_α−1}_𝔗(M̄_{n_α}, RΨO_λ)_{𝔪_α} is a finite free O_λ-module.
items.note: The analogue of Assumption 6.1.4 for both ranks. By Lemma 5.2.7 it is a statement about the étale cohomology of the indefinite unitary Shimura varieties Sh(V′_{n_α}, …)_{F̄} localized at 𝔪_α. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Assumption 7.2.4 — cohomological genericity for Π₀
items.statement: The composite homomorphism 𝕋^{Σ⁺_min}_{n₀} →^{φ_{Π₀}} O_E → O_E/λ is cohomologically generic (Definition D.1.1).
items.note: Only for the even-rank factor; the analogue of Assumption 6.1.6 needed for Theorem 6.3.4. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §7.2 — the product P, its blow-up σ: Q → P and the localized weight spectral sequence 𝔼_{s,(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)}
items.statement: Apply the constructions of §5.11 to the object (K^{p∘}_n, K^{p∘}_{n+1}) of 𝔎(V°_n)^p × 𝔎(V°_{n+1})^p: P := 𝐌_{n₀} ×_{𝐓_𝔭} 𝐌_{n₁}, P^{?₀,?₁} := M^{?₀}_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} M^{?₁}_{n₁} for (?₀,?₁) ∈ {∘,•,†}², σ: Q → P the blow-up along P^{∘,∘}, and Q^{?₀,?₁} the strict transform of P^{?₀,?₁} (Notation 5.11.1). Q is strictly semistable over ℤ_{p²} of relative dimension 2n−1 with Q^{(0)} = Q^{∘,∘} ⊔ Q^{∘,•} ⊔ Q^{•,•} ⊔ Q^{•,∘}, Q^{(1)} = Q^{∘,†} ⊔ Q^{†,•} ⊔ Q^{•,†} ⊔ Q^{†,∘} ⊔ Q^{†,†}, Q^{(2)} = (Q^{•,∘}∩Q^{†,†}) ⊔ (Q^{∘,•}∩Q^{†,†}), Q^{(c)} = ∅ for c ⩾ 3 (Lemma 5.11.3). (𝔼^{p,q}_{s,(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)}, d^{p,q}_{s,(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)}) is the localization at (𝔪₀,𝔪₁) of the weight spectral sequence (5.27) abutting to H^{p+q}_𝔗(Q̄, RΨO_λ(n)), with 𝔼^{p,q}_1 = ⊕_{i⩾max(0,−p)} H^{q−2i}_𝔗(Q̄^{(p+2i)}, O_λ(n−i)) and 𝔼^{p,q}_1 = 0 for |p| > 2.
items.locator: §7.2, paragraph before Lemma 7.2.5, published p. 288 (constructions from §5.11, pp. 250–253)
items.note: The differentials of (5.27) depend on the ordering Q^{∘,∘} < Q^{∘,•} < Q^{•,•} < Q^{•,∘} of components (footnote 21, p. 252). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 7.2.5(1) — Künneth decomposition of the localized cohomology of the strata P̄^{?₀,?₁}
items.statement: Assume Assumptions 7.1.1, 7.2.2, 7.2.3, 7.2.4 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for both n and n+1 (in the setup of §7.2: λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,I}, Σ⁺_I, V°_n, K°_n, (K°_sp, K°_{n+1}) and the special inert prime 𝔭 satisfying (PI1)–(PI7)). Then for (?₀,?₁) ∈ {∘,•,†}² and i ∈ ℤ there is a canonical isomorphism H^i_𝔗(P̄^{?₀,?₁}, O_λ)_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} ≃ ⊕_{i₀+i₁=i} H^{i₀}_𝔗(M̄^{?₀}_{n₀}, O_λ)_{𝔪₀} ⊗_{O_λ} H^{i₁}_𝔗(M̄^{?₁}_{n₁}, O_λ)_{𝔪₁} in Mod(Gal(F̄_p/F_{p²}), O_λ)_fr.
items.note: The published version labels this 'Lemma 7.2.5' (an earlier version of this extraction said 'Proposition 7.2.5'). Proof: each H^{i_α}_𝔗(M̄^{?_α}_{n_α}, O_λ)_{𝔪_α} is finitely generated free (Lemma 5.6.2, Lemma 6.2.2(2), Theorem 6.3.4(1)); then Lemma 6.1.11 and the Künneth formula. Mod(…)_fr = finite free O_λ-modules with continuous action. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 7.2.5(2) — shape of the localized product weight spectral sequence at E₂
items.statement: Assume Assumptions 7.1.1, 7.2.2, 7.2.3, 7.2.4 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for both n and n+1 (in the setup of §7.2: λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,I}, Σ⁺_I, V°_n, K°_n, (K°_sp, K°_{n+1}) and the special inert prime 𝔭 satisfying (PI1)–(PI7)). Then 𝔼^{p,q}_{2,(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} = 0 if (p,q) ∉ {(−1,2n), (0,2n−1), (1,2n−2)}, and there are canonical isomorphisms 𝔼^{−1,2n}_{2,(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} ≃ ⁰E^{−1,2r₀}_{2,𝔪₀} ⊗_{O_λ} ¹E^{0,2r₁}_{2,𝔪₁}, 𝔼^{0,2n−1}_{2,(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} ≃ ⁰E^{0,2r₀−1}_{2,𝔪₀} ⊗_{O_λ} ¹E^{0,2r₁}_{2,𝔪₁}, 𝔼^{1,2n−2}_{2,(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} ≃ ⁰E^{1,2r₀−2}_{2,𝔪₀} ⊗_{O_λ} ¹E^{0,2r₁}_{2,𝔪₁} in Mod(Gal(F̄_p/F_{p²}), O_λ)_fr.
items.note: Proof: first E₂-degeneration: d^{−2,q}_1 is injective (its composite with the projection to H^{q−2}(Q̄^{†,†}) ⊕ H^{q−2}(Q̄^{†,∘}) is injective by (1), Lemmas 5.11.3(2), 5.6.2, 6.2.1), dually 𝔼^{2,q}_2 = 0; d^{−1,q}_1 injective and d^{0,q}_1 surjective for q odd. Then σ induces σ*₂: ⊕ ⁰E^{p₀,q₀}_{2,𝔪₀} ⊗ ¹E^{p₁,q₁}_{2,𝔪₁} → 𝔼^{p,q}_{2,(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)}, an isomorphism because the abutments compare via Lemma 5.2.7, Lemma 5.11.2, Lemma 6.1.11 and Künneth; the positions follow from Lemma 6.2.2 (odd rank: only ¹E^{0,2r₁}_2 ≠ 0) and Theorem 6.3.4(2) (even rank: positions (−1,2r₀), (0,2r₀−1), (1,2r₀−2)). The vanishing pattern alone implies degeneration at E₂ (no d₂ can connect two nonzero positions), which is condition (N1) of [47, Definition 2.15]. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 7.2.5(3) — no Frobenius-fixed subquotients off the p = 1 column
items.statement: Assume Assumptions 7.1.1, 7.2.2, 7.2.3, 7.2.4 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for both n and n+1 (in the setup of §7.2: λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,I}, Σ⁺_I, V°_n, K°_n, (K°_sp, K°_{n+1}) and the special inert prime 𝔭 satisfying (PI1)–(PI7)). If 𝔼^{i,2n−1−i}_{2,(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)}(−1) has a nontrivial subquotient on which Gal(F̄_p/F_{p²}) acts trivially, then i = 1.
items.note: Proof: let {α^{±1}_{0,1},…,α^{±1}_{0,r₀}} and {α^{±1}_{1,1},…,α^{±1}_{1,r₁},1} be the roots of P_{α(Π_{0,𝔭})} mod λ and P_{α(Π_{1,𝔭})} mod λ; by (PI4) take α_{0,r₀} = p. By (2), Theorem 6.2.3(1) and Theorem 6.3.4(3), the generalized Frobenius eigenvalues of 𝔼^{−1,2n}_2(−1) ⊗ O_λ/λ lie in {p^{−2}α^{±1}_{1,1},…,p^{−2}α^{±1}_{1,r₁}, p^{−2}} and those of 𝔼^{0,2n−1}_2(−1) ⊗ O_λ/λ in {p^{−1}α^{±1}_{0,i₀}α^{±1}_{1,i₁}: i₀ < r₀} ∪ {p^{−1}α^{±1}_{0,i₀}: i₀ < r₀}. (PI2) gives p² ≠ 1; (PI7) gives α_{1,i₁} ∉ {p², p^{−2}} and α^{±1}_{0,i₀}α^{±1}_{1,i₁} ∉ {p, p^{−1}} for i₀ < r₀ (printed only for α_{0,i₀}α_{1,i₁}; all sign choices follow from (PI7) since the tensor parameter contains all products); (PI4) gives α_{0,i₀} ∉ {p, p^{−1}} for i₀ < r₀. So 1 is not an eigenvalue for i = −1, 0; other i vanish by (2). Checked: the eigenvalue sets agree with the arithmetic-Frobenius weights (−1-twist multiplies by p^{−2}). This is condition (N2) of [47, Definition 2.15]. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 7.2.5(4) — weak semisimplicity of even-degree cohomology of the strata
items.statement: Assume Assumptions 7.1.1, 7.2.2, 7.2.3, 7.2.4 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for both n and n+1 (in the setup of §7.2: λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,I}, Σ⁺_I, V°_n, K°_n, (K°_sp, K°_{n+1}) and the special inert prime 𝔭 satisfying (PI1)–(PI7)). For (?₀,?₁) ∈ {∘,•,†}² and i ∈ ℤ, both H^{2i}_𝔗(P̄^{?₀,?₁}, O_λ(i))_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} and H^{2i}_𝔗(Q̄^{?₀,?₁}, O_λ(i))_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} are weakly semisimple, i.e. objects of Mod(Gal(F̄_p/F_{p²}), O_λ) for which the natural map from invariants to coinvariants is an isomorphism (Definition 2.1.2).
items.note: Proof: reduce Q to P by Lemma 5.11.3(3–5) and Lemma 2.1.4(1); by (1) and Lemma 6.2.2(1) reduce to H^{2i₀}(M̄^{?₀}_{n₀}, O_λ(i₀))_{𝔪₀} ⊗ H^{2i₁}(M̄^{?₁}_{n₁}, O_λ(i₁))_{𝔪₁}; Galois acts trivially on the ∘ and † factors (Lemma 5.6.2), on the • factors unless i₀ ∈ {r₀−1, r₀} or i₁ = r₁ (Theorem 6.3.4(2), Lemma 6.2.2(3)), and also on H^{2r₀−2}(M̄•_{n₀}, O_λ(r₀−1))_{𝔪₀}, H^{2r₀}(M̄•_{n₀}, O_λ(r₀))_{𝔪₀} (Proposition 6.3.1(1,2), Theorem 6.3.4(1)); the remaining H^{2r₁}(M̄•_{n₁}, O_λ(r₁))_{𝔪₁} ≅ ¹E^{0,2r₁}_{2,𝔪₁} ⊕ H^{2r₁}(M̄†_{n₁}, O_λ(r₁))_{𝔪₁} is weakly semisimple by Theorem 6.2.3(2). With Lemma 2.1.4(2) this gives condition (N3) of [47, Definition 2.15]. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 7.2.5(5) — localized nearby-cycle cohomology of Q is concentrated in degree 2n−1
items.statement: Assume Assumptions 7.1.1, 7.2.2, 7.2.3, 7.2.4 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for both n and n+1 (in the setup of §7.2: λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,I}, Σ⁺_I, V°_n, K°_n, (K°_sp, K°_{n+1}) and the special inert prime 𝔭 satisfying (PI1)–(PI7)). Then H^i_𝔗(Q̄, RΨO_λ)_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} = 0 for i ≠ 2n−1.
items.note: Direct consequence of (2) (only p+q = 2n−1 survives). By Remark 7.2.6 it holds under Assumption 7.2.3 alone. It makes every codimension-n cycle on Q^η homologically trivial after localization, so AJ_Q is defined on all of Z^n_𝔗(Q^η). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 7.2.5(6) — compactly supported equals ordinary cohomology of the strata after localization
items.statement: Assume Assumptions 7.1.1, 7.2.2, 7.2.3, 7.2.4 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for both n and n+1 (in the setup of §7.2: λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,I}, Σ⁺_I, V°_n, K°_n, (K°_sp, K°_{n+1}) and the special inert prime 𝔭 satisfying (PI1)–(PI7)). Then the canonical map H^i_{𝔗,c}(Q̄^{(c)}, O_λ)_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} → H^i_𝔗(Q̄^{(c)}, O_λ)_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} is an isomorphism for all integers c and i.
items.note: Proof: (1), Lemma 6.1.11 and Lemma 5.11.3(3–5). By Remark 7.2.6 it holds under Assumption 7.1.1 alone. This is the input quoted in footnote 29 to justify applying [47] (stated for proper X) to the possibly non-proper Q. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Remark 7.2.6 (first half) — Lemma 7.2.5(5) needs only Assumption 7.2.3
items.statement: Lemma 7.2.5(5) (H^i_𝔗(Q̄, RΨO_λ)_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} = 0 for i ≠ 2n−1) holds under Assumption 7.2.3 only.
items.note: No proof is given. Plausible route: Lemma 5.11.2 identifies H(Q̄, RΨO_λ) with the cohomology of the geometric generic fibre of P, and Künneth plus Assumption 7.2.3 (concentration in degrees n_α−1) give concentration in degree n₀−1+n₁−1 = 2n−1. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Remark 7.2.6 (second half) — Lemma 7.2.5(6) needs only Assumption 7.1.1
items.statement: Lemma 7.2.5(6) (H^i_{𝔗,c}(Q̄^{(c)}, O_λ)_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} ≅ H^i_𝔗(Q̄^{(c)}, O_λ)_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} for all c, i) holds under Assumption 7.1.1 only.
items.note: No proof is given (residual irreducibility kills boundary contributions after localization, cf. Lemma 6.1.11). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §7.2 — the localized Abel–Jacobi map AJ_Q on Z^n_𝔗(Q^η)
items.statement: Lemma 7.2.5(5) induces a coboundary map AJ_Q: Z^n_𝔗(Q^η) → H¹(ℚ_{p²}, H^{2n−1}_𝔗(Q̄, RΨO_λ(n))_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)}).
items.note: Z^n_𝔗(Q^η): 𝔗-families of codimension-n cycles on the generic fibre. Since the localized H^{2n} of the geometric generic fibre vanishes (Lemma 7.2.5(5) with Lemma 5.11.2), the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence sends the localized absolute cycle class into H¹(ℚ_{p²}, H^{2n−1}(…)_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)}). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: (7.1) — the singular quotient map ∂
items.statement: ∂: H¹(ℚ_{p²}, H^{2n−1}_𝔗(Q̄, RΨO_λ(n))_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)}) → H¹_sing(ℚ_{p²}, H^{2n−1}_𝔗(Q̄, RΨO_λ(n))_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)}) is the singular quotient map from Definition 2.2.2, where for a module R over the local field K, H¹_sing(K, R) := H¹(I_K, R)^{Gal(k̄/k)} and ∂ is the restriction to inertia (surjective, with kernel H¹_ns(K,R) ≅ H¹(k, R^{I_K})).
items.note: The same symbol is used for the mod-(𝔫₀,𝔫₁) coefficients in Corollary 7.2.9 (∂_𝔭 there). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §7.2 — the cycles P_sp, Q_sp and the class cl(Q_sp) ∈ C^n(Q, L)
items.statement: By the choice of K°_n and (K°_sp, K°_{n+1}) there is a finite morphism 𝐌_𝔭(V°_n, K°_sp) → P. Denote by P_sp the corresponding cycle, and let Q_sp be the strict transform of P_sp under σ, which is a T_𝔭-invariant cycle of Q; Q^η_sp is its generic fibre. The main goal is to compute ∂AJ_Q(Q^η_sp) in H¹_sing(ℚ_{p²}, H^{2n−1}_𝔗(Q̄, RΨO_λ(n))/(𝔫₀,𝔫₁)). The cycle Q_sp gives rise to a class cl(Q_sp) ∈ C^n(Q, L), where C^n(Q, L) is the target of the potential map Δ^n (5.28).
items.note: Q_sp has codimension n in Q (relative dimensions n−1 and 2n−1). C^n(Q, L) = B^n(Q, L)^0_{Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ)} (§5.11; see P01). How cl(Q_sp) is formed is not spelled out; in [47, Theorem 2.18] the relevant class is e_z (the cycle class of the flat closure, restricted to Q̄^{(0)}), which by [47, Proposition 2.19] equals the geometric cycle class of Q_sp ×_Q Q̄^{(0)} when the singular locus has codimension ⩾ n+1 in each component of the special fibre; the proof of Theorem 7.2.8(3) uses the latter description (component on Q̄^{•,•}). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proposition 7.2.7 — singular part of the Abel–Jacobi class of Q^η_sp as the potential cokernel
items.statement: Assume Assumptions 7.1.1, 7.2.2, 7.2.3, 7.2.4 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for both n and n+1 (in the setup of §7.2: λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,I}, Σ⁺_I, V°_n, K°_n, (K°_sp, K°_{n+1}) and the special inert prime 𝔭 satisfying (PI1)–(PI7)). There is a canonical isomorphism H¹_sing(ℚ_{p²}, H^{2n−1}_𝔗(Q̄, RΨO_λ(n))_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)}) ≃ coker Δ^n_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)}, under which ∂AJ_Q(Q^η_sp) coincides with the image of cl(Q_sp) in coker Δ^n_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)}.
items.note: Proof: by [47, Theorem 2.16 and Theorem 2.18] it suffices that O_λ is a very nice coefficient ring for 𝔼^{p,q}_{s,(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} in the sense of [47, Definition 2.15]: (N1) by Lemma 7.2.5(2), (N2) by Lemma 7.2.5(3), (N3) by Lemma 7.2.5(4) and Lemma 2.1.4(2). Footnote 29: [47] assumes X proper, but 'the proof of relevant results works without change in our case even when Q is not proper in view of Lemma 7.2.5(6)'. [47, §2] is also stated only for Λ ∈ {ℚ_ℓ, ℤ/ℓ^ν}, and its A^r(·)^0 are G_κ-invariants where C^n uses coinvariants (they agree under (N3)); see source issue — a named proof obligation for a formalisation. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §7.2 — the map ∇: C^n(Q, O_λ) → O_λ[Sh(V°_{n₀},K°_{n₀})] ⊗ O_λ[Sh(V°_{n₁},K°_{n₁})]
items.statement: By Construction 5.11.7 and Remark 5.11.8 there is a map ∇: C^n(Q, O_λ) → O_λ[Sh(V°_{n₀}, K°_{n₀})] ⊗_{O_λ} O_λ[Sh(V°_{n₁}, K°_{n₁})]. On H^{2n}_𝔗(Q̄^{(0)}, L(n)) it is the sum (I°_{n₀,𝔭} ⊗ I°_{n₁,𝔭}) ∘ Inc*_{∘,†} + (p+1)²(I°_{n₀,𝔭} ⊗ T°•_{n₁,𝔭}) ∘ Inc*_{∘,•} + (p+1)(T°•_{n₀,𝔭} ⊗ I°_{n₁,𝔭}) ∘ Inc*_{•,†} + (p+1)³(T°•_{n₀,𝔭} ⊗ T°•_{n₁,𝔭}) ∘ Inc*_{•,•}, where Inc*_{∘,†}, Inc*_{∘,•} (resp. Inc*_{•,†}, Inc*_{•,•}) restrict to Q̄^{∘,•} (resp. Q̄^{•,•}), push forward by σ and apply inc* of Construction 5.11.4; it factors through Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ)-coinvariants and so restricts to C^n(Q, L) via C^n(Q, L) → H^{2n}_𝔗(Q̄^{(0)}, L(n))_{Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ)}.
items.locator: §7.2, display before Theorem 7.2.8, published p. 292 (Construction 5.11.7, p. 261; Remark 5.11.8, p. 263)
items.note: Here the level at p of Sh(V°_{n_α}, K°_{n_α}) is K°_{n_α,p}; ∇ lands in functions on the definite Shimura sets. I°, T°•, R° are Hecke operators at 𝔭 (Appendix B). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Theorem 7.2.8(1) — ∇ ∘ Δ^n lands in 𝔫₀
items.statement: Assume Assumptions 7.1.1, 7.2.2, 7.2.3, 7.2.4 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for both n and n+1 (in the setup of §7.2: λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,I}, Σ⁺_I, V°_n, K°_n, (K°_sp, K°_{n+1}) and the special inert prime 𝔭 satisfying (PI1)–(PI7)). Then the image of the composite map ∇_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} ∘ Δ^n_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} is contained in 𝔫₀·O_λ[Sh(V°_{n₀}, K°_{n₀})]_{𝔪₀} ⊗_{O_λ} O_λ[Sh(V°_{n₁}, K°_{n₁})]_{𝔪₁}.
items.locator: §7.2, Theorem 7.2.8(1) (First explicit reciprocity law), published pp. 292–295
items.note: Proof: by [47, Lemma 2.4] Δ^n is induced by δ_{1!} ∘ δ*₀ on H^{2(n−1)}(Q̄^{(0)}, O_λ(n−1)), which by Lemma 5.11.3(3,4) is ⊕_{(?₀,?₁)∈{∘,•}²} σ*H^{2(n−1)}(P̄^{?₀,?₁}) ⊕ (δ^{†,†}_{∘,∘})_!σ*H^{2(n−2)}(P̄^{†,†}) ⊕ (δ^{†,†}_{•,•})_!σ*H^{2(n−2)}(P̄^{†,†}). (1a) image of σ*H(P̄^{∘,•}) ⊕ σ*H(P̄^{•,•}) lies in 𝔫₀·(…) via a commutative diagram with (∇⁰ ∘ ⁰d^{−1,2r₀}_1 ∘ ⁰d^{0,2r₀−2}_1(−1))_{𝔪₀} ⊗ (I°_{n₁,𝔭}∘inc*_† + (p+1)²T°•_{n₁,𝔭}∘inc*_•)_{𝔪₁}, Proposition B.3.5(2), (PI4) (giving ((p+1)R°_{n₀,𝔭} − I°_{n₀,𝔭})·O_λ[Sh]_{𝔪₀} ⊆ 𝔫₀·O_λ[Sh]_{𝔪₀}), Proposition 6.3.1(4) and Lemma 5.11.3(3); (1b), (1c) images vanish by Lemma 7.2.5(1) and Lemma 5.9.2(3); (1d) follows from (1c) by [47, Lemma 2.4] (the two pushforwards from Q̄^{†,†} differ by an element of im δ_{1!}). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Theorem 7.2.8(2) — ∇ induces an isomorphism coker Δ^n/𝔫₀ ≅ O_λ[Sh]/𝔫₀ ⊗ O_λ[Sh]_{𝔪₁}
items.statement: Assume Assumptions 7.1.1, 7.2.2, 7.2.3, 7.2.4 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for both n and n+1 (in the setup of §7.2: λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,I}, Σ⁺_I, V°_n, K°_n, (K°_sp, K°_{n+1}) and the special inert prime 𝔭 satisfying (PI1)–(PI7)). In view of Theorem 7.2.8(1), the induced map ∇_{𝔪₁/𝔫₀}: coker Δ^n_{𝔪₁}/𝔫₀ → O_λ[Sh(V°_{n₀}, K°_{n₀})]/𝔫₀ ⊗_{O_λ} O_λ[Sh(V°_{n₁}, K°_{n₁})]_{𝔪₁} is an isomorphism.
items.note: coker Δ^n_{𝔪₁}/𝔫₀ = coker Δ^n_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)}/𝔫₀. Proof: ∇_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} is surjective (item thm-7-2-8-proof-nabla-surjective), and domain and target are finite of the same cardinality by (7.2) (item formula-7-2). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Theorem 7.2.8(3) — first explicit reciprocity law (pairing formula)
items.statement: Assume Assumptions 7.1.1, 7.2.2, 7.2.3, 7.2.4 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for both n and n+1 (in the setup of §7.2: λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,I}, Σ⁺_I, V°_n, K°_n, (K°_sp, K°_{n+1}) and the special inert prime 𝔭 satisfying (PI1)–(PI7)). Under the natural pairing O_λ[Sh(V°_{n₀}, K°_{n₀})]/𝔫₀ ⊗_{O_λ} O_λ[Sh(V°_{n₁}, K°_{n₁})]_{𝔪₁} × (O_λ/λ^m)[Sh(V°_{n₀}, K°_{n₀})][𝔫₀] ⊗_{O_λ} O_λ[Sh(V°_{n₁}, K°_{n₁})]_{𝔪₁} → O_λ/λ^m obtained by taking inner product, the pairing of ∇_{/(𝔫₀,𝔫₁)}(∂AJ_Q(Q^η_sp)) [printed Q^η_△; see source issue] and every function f ∈ (O_λ/λ^m)[Sh(V°_{n₀}, K°_{n₀})][𝔫₀] ⊗_{O_λ} (O_λ/λ^m)[Sh(V°_{n₁}, K°_{n₁})][𝔫₁] is equal to (p+1) · φ_{Π₀}(I°_{n₀,𝔭}) · φ_{Π₁}(T°_{n₁,𝔭}) · Σ_{s∈Sh(V°_n, K°_sp)} f(s, sh°_↑(s)). Here ∂AJ_Q(Q^η_sp) is regarded as an element of coker Δ^n_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} (hence of coker Δ^n_{𝔪₁}/𝔫₀) via the canonical isomorphism of Proposition 7.2.7.
items.note: [M][𝔫] = 𝔫-torsion. The sum over Sh(V°_n, K°_sp) means: s mapped to Sh(V°_n, K°_n) and sh°_↑(s) ∈ Sh(V°_{n+1}, K°_{n+1}) (Notation 5.10.13), with factors reordered when n is odd. Proof: since Q_sp does not meet Q^{∘,•}, ∇(cl(Q_sp)) only sees the Q̄^{•,•}-component, so ∇(cl(Q_sp)) = ((p+1)(T°•_{n₀,𝔭} ⊗ I°_{n₁,𝔭})∘inc*_{•,†} + (p+1)³(T°•_{n₀,𝔭} ⊗ T°•_{n₁,𝔭})∘inc*_{•,•})(cl(P•_sp)); applying Theorem 5.11.5(3) to (K°_sp, K°_{n+1}) ∈ 𝔎(V°_n)_sp and pushing forward gives the pairing (p+1)Σ_s (I°_{n₀,𝔭} ⊗ T°_{n₁,𝔭} f)(s, sh°_↑(s)), and (PI6) replaces the Hecke operators at 𝔭 by φ_{Π₀}(I°_{n₀,𝔭}), φ_{Π₁}(T°_{n₁,𝔭}) on f; conclude by Proposition 7.2.7. The (p+1) prefactor comes from ∇, the Hecke factors from Theorem 5.11.5(3). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 7.2.8(2), claim — ∇_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} is surjective
items.statement: Assume Assumptions 7.1.1, 7.2.2, 7.2.3, 7.2.4 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for both n and n+1 (in the setup of §7.2: λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,I}, Σ⁺_I, V°_n, K°_n, (K°_sp, K°_{n+1}) and the special inert prime 𝔭 satisfying (PI1)–(PI7)). The map ∇_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} with domain C^n(Q, O_λ)_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} is surjective. More precisely, ker ⁰d^{0,2r₀}_{1,𝔪₀} ⊗_{O_λ} ker ¹d^{0,2r₁}_{1,𝔪₁} ⊆ ⊕_{(?₀,?₁)∈{∘,•}²} H^{2n}_𝔗(P̄^{?₀,?₁}, O_λ(n))_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} [printed H^{2(n−1)}_𝔗(…, O_λ(n−1)); see source issue] by Lemma 7.2.5(1); σ*(ker ⁰d^{0,2r₀}_{1,𝔪₀} ⊗ ker ¹d^{0,2r₁}_{1,𝔪₁}) is contained in C^n(Q, O_λ)_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)}; and ∇_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} ∘ σ* on it coincides with ∇⁰_{𝔪₀} ⊗ ∇¹_{𝔪₁}, which is surjective by Proposition 6.3.1(3) and Theorem 6.2.3.
items.note: ∇⁰ (even rank, §6.3) and ∇¹ (odd rank, Construction 5.9.4 / Theorem 6.2.3) are the one-factor analogues of ∇. 'Contained in C^n' means: lies in B^n(Q,O_λ)^0 and is taken to its image in the coinvariants. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: (7.2) and the computation of coker Δ^n/𝔫₀ in the proof of Theorem 7.2.8(2)
items.statement: Assume Assumptions 7.1.1, 7.2.2, 7.2.3, 7.2.4 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for both n and n+1 (in the setup of §7.2: λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,I}, Σ⁺_I, V°_n, K°_n, (K°_sp, K°_{n+1}) and the special inert prime 𝔭 satisfying (PI1)–(PI7)). By Proposition 7.2.7 there is an isomorphism of O_λ/λ^m-modules (7.2): coker Δ^n_{𝔪₁}/𝔫₀ = coker Δ^n_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)}/𝔫₀ ≃ H¹_sing(ℚ_{p²}, H^{2n−1}_𝔗(Q̄, RΨO_λ(n))_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)})/𝔫₀. By Lemma 7.2.5(2,3) and Theorem 6.2.3(2), H¹_sing(ℚ_{p²}, H^{2n−1}_𝔗(Q̄, RΨO_λ(n))_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)}) ≃ H¹_sing(ℚ_{p²}, H^{2r₀−1}_𝔗(M̄_{n₀}, RΨO_λ(r₀))_{𝔪₀}) ⊗_{O_λ} (¹E^{0,2r₁}_{2,𝔪₁})^{Gal(F̄_p/F_{p²})}. Then by Theorems 6.2.3(3) and 6.3.4(4), (7.2) ≃ O_λ[Sh(V°_{n₀}, K°_{n₀})]/𝔫₀ ⊗_{O_λ} O_λ[Sh(V°_{n₁}, K°_{n₁})]_{𝔪₁}.
items.note: Theorem 6.3.4(4): arithmetic level raising, H¹_sing(ℚ_{p²}, H^{2r₀−1}(M̄_{n₀}, RΨO_λ(r₀))/𝔫₀) ≅ O_λ[Sh(V°_{n₀},K°_{n₀})]/𝔫₀; Theorem 6.2.3(3): (¹E^{0,2r₁}_{2,𝔪₁})^{Gal} ≅ O_λ[Sh(V°_{n₁},K°_{n₁})]_{𝔪₁} (via ∇¹). The second isomorphism uses that ⁰E^{−1,2r₀}_2 contributes the singular part and ¹E^{0,2r₁}_2 is free and weakly semisimple. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §7.2 — indefinite Shimura varieties Sh′_{n_α} and the localized Abel–Jacobi map AJ
items.statement: Choose an indefinite uniformization datum as in Notation 5.10.1 and put Sh′_{n_α} := Sh(V′_{n_α}, j_{n_α}K^{p∘}_{n_α}K′_{n_α,p}) for α = 0, 1. Assume Assumptions 7.1.1 and 7.2.3. By Lemma 6.1.11, Lemma 5.2.7 and the Künneth formula, H^i_ét((Sh′_{n₀} ×_{Spec F} Sh′_{n₁})_{F̄}, O_λ)_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} = 0 if i ≠ 2n−1. In particular one obtains the Abel–Jacobi map AJ: Z^n(Sh′_{n₀} ×_{Spec F} Sh′_{n₁}) → H¹(F, H^{2n−1}_ét((Sh′_{n₀} ×_{Spec F} Sh′_{n₁})_{F̄}, O_λ(n))/(𝔫₀,𝔫₁)).
items.note: AJ is defined on all codimension-n cycles because the localized degree-2n geometric cohomology vanishes (Hochschild–Serre). V′_{n_α} is the indefinite (signature (n_α−1,1) at τ_∞) hermitian space of the uniformization datum; Sh′_{n_α} ⊗ ℚ_{p²} is the generic fibre of 𝐌_{n_α} (isomorphism (5.2)). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §7.2 — the diagonal cycle Sh′_sp
items.statement: Let Sh′_sp be the cycle given by the finite morphism Sh(V′_n, j_nK^{p∘}_spK′_{n,p}) → Sh′_n ×_{Spec F} Sh′_{n+1}; it is an element of Z^n(Sh′_{n₀} ×_{Spec F} Sh′_{n₁}).
items.note: Conjecture 8.3.1 versus Theorem 8.3.2' refers mostly to §8.3 (outside these pages) and §7.1 contains no cycle. In §7.2 the diagonal cycle is Sh′_sp (the graph of the embedding Sh(V′_n) → Sh(V′_{n+1}) at level K_sp, pushed forward), with AJ(Sh′_sp) ∈ H¹(F, H^{2n−1}_ét(…)/(𝔫₀,𝔫₁)); its §7.3 counterpart is the absolute class [Sh(V_n, K_sp)] (item construction-7-3-cycle-class). Codimension check: dim Sh′_n + dim Sh′_{n+1} − dim Sh(V′_n) = (n−1) + n − (n−1) = n. Missing: routed to a source of MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.2 (route 11).

items.name: Corollary 7.2.9 — exponent of the singular part of the Abel–Jacobi class of Sh′_sp
items.statement: Assume Assumptions 7.1.1, 7.2.2, 7.2.3, 7.2.4 and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for both n and n+1 (in the setup of §7.2: λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,I}, Σ⁺_I, V°_n, K°_n, (K°_sp, K°_{n+1}) and the special inert prime 𝔭 satisfying (PI1)–(PI7)). Then exp_λ(∂_𝔭 loc_𝔭 AJ(Sh′_sp), H¹_sing(F_𝔭, H^{2n−1}_ét((Sh′_{n₀} ×_{Spec F} Sh′_{n₁})_{F̄}, O_λ(n))/(𝔫₀,𝔫₁))) = exp_λ(𝟙_{Sh(V°_n, K°_sp)}, O_λ[Sh(V°_{n₀}, K°_{n₀}) × Sh(V°_{n₁}, K°_{n₁})]/(𝔫₀,𝔫₁)), where exp_λ(x, M) := min{d ∈ ℤ_{⩾0} ∪ {∞} | λ^d x = 0} (Definition 2.1.6), and 𝟙_{Sh(V°_n, K°_sp)} is regarded as the pushforward of the characteristic function along Sh(V°_n, K°_sp) → Sh(V°_n, K°_n) × Sh(V°_{n+1}, K°_{n+1}).
items.note: Proof: (5.2) induces H^{2n−1}_ét((Sh′_{n₀}×Sh′_{n₁})_{F̄}, O_λ(n))_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} → H^{2n−1}_𝔗(Q̄, RΨO_λ(n))_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)}, an isomorphism of O_λ[Gal(ℚ̄_p/ℚ_{p²})]-modules by Lemma 5.11.2; with diagram (5.23) the left side equals exp_λ(∂AJ_Q(Q^η_sp), H¹_sing(ℚ_{p²}, H^{2n−1}_𝔗(Q̄, RΨO_λ(n))/(𝔫₀,𝔫₁))); Theorem 7.2.8 turns this into exp_λ((p+1)φ_{Π₀}(I°_{n₀,𝔭})φ_{Π₁}(T°_{n₁,𝔭})𝟙_{Sh(V°_n,K°_sp)}, O_λ[Sh(V°_{n₀},K°_{n₀})]/𝔫₀ ⊗ O_λ[Sh(V°_{n₁},K°_{n₁})]/𝔫₁); the three factors are units: p+1 by (PI2), φ_{Π₀}(I°_{n₀,𝔭}) by (PI5) and Proposition B.3.5(1), φ_{Π₁}(T°_{n₁,𝔭}) by (PI4) and Proposition B.4.3(2). The step from Theorem 7.2.8 (which concerns H¹_sing(…_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)})/(𝔫₀,𝔫₁)) to H¹_sing of the mod-(𝔫₀,𝔫₁) module is not argued; see source issue. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §7.3 — data for the second explicit reciprocity law (λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,II}, Σ⁺_II, V_n, K, 𝔭 with (PII1)–(PII4), (PII7))
items.statement: One chooses: • a prime λ of E whose underlying rational prime ℓ satisfies Σ⁺_min ∩ Σ⁺_ℓ = ∅; • a positive integer m; • a (possibly empty) finite set Σ⁺_{lr,II} of nonarchimedean places of F⁺ that are inert in F, strongly disjoint from Σ⁺_min (Definition 1.3.2), satisfying ℓ ∤ ‖v‖(‖v‖²−1) for v ∈ Σ⁺_{lr,II}; • a finite set Σ⁺_II of nonarchimedean places of F⁺ containing Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_{lr,II}; • a standard indefinite hermitian space V_n of rank n over F, together with a self-dual ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_{lr,II}} O_{F_v}-lattice Λ_n in V_n ⊗_F 𝔸_F^{Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_{lr,II}} (and put V_{n+1} := (V_n)_♯, Λ_{n+1} := (Λ_n)_♯), such that (V_{n₀})_v is not split for v ∈ Σ⁺_{lr,II}; • objects K_n ∈ 𝔎(V_n) and (K_sp, K_{n+1}) ∈ 𝔎(V_n)_sp of the forms K_n = ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_{lr,II}} (K_n)_v × ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_{lr,II}} U(Λ_n)(O_{F⁺_v}), K_sp = ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_{lr,II}} (K_sp)_v × ∏_{v∉…} U(Λ_n)(O_{F⁺_v}), K_{n+1} = ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_{lr,II}} (K_{n+1})_v × ∏_{v∉…} U(Λ_{n+1})(O_{F⁺_v}), satisfying (K_sp)_v = (K_n)_v for v ∈ Σ⁺_min, (K_sp)_v ⊆ (K_n)_v for v ∈ Σ⁺_{lr,II}, and (K_{n₀})_v is a transferable open compact subgroup (Definition D.2.1) of U(V_{n₀})(F⁺_v) for v ∈ Σ⁺_min and a special maximal subgroup of U(V_{n₀})(F⁺_v) for v ∈ Σ⁺_{lr,II}; • a special inert prime 𝔭 of F⁺ (Definition 3.3.4), with underlying rational prime p, satisfying (PII1) Σ⁺_II does not contain p-adic places; (PII2) ℓ does not divide p(p²−1); (PII3) there exists a CM type Φ containing τ_∞ as in the initial setup of §5 satisfying ℚ_p^Φ = ℚ_{p²}; (PII4) P_{α(Π_{0,𝔭})} mod λ^m is level-raising special at 𝔭 and P_{α(Π_{1,𝔭})} mod λ is Tate generic at 𝔭 (Definition 3.1.5); (PII7) P_{α(Π_{0,𝔭})⊗α(Π_{1,𝔭})} mod λ^m is level-raising special at 𝔭 (Definition 3.1.5) (so the setup of §4.5 applies to (V_n, {Λ_{n,𝔮}}_{𝔮|p})); • the remaining data in §4.1 with ℚ_p^Φ = ℚ_{p²}; and • a definite uniformization datum as in Notation 4.5.7, which in particular gives open compact subgroups K*_{n,p}, K*_{n+1,p} and K*_{sp,p}. (Footnote 30: 𝔭 is also regarded as the unique place of F above 𝔭.)
items.note: The numbering deliberately skips (PII5), (PII6) (parallel with (PI1)–(PI7)): there is no intertwining-genericity or Hecke-quotient condition, and no requirement ℓ ⩾ 2(n₀+1) or ℓ unramified in F. Here V_n is indefinite and 𝔭 gives good (smooth) reduction: the §4 models 𝐌_𝔭(V_n, ·) are smooth over ℤ_{p²} (hyperspecial level at p), and the basic locus B_{n₁} → S_{n₁} is used, not a semistable model. items.name: §7.3 — the level subgroups K*_sp, K*_{n_α}, K*_{sp,sp}, K*_{n,sp} and the schemes X^?_{n_α}
items.statement: Put K*_sp := (i_nK^p_sp) × K*_{n,p}, and K*_{n_α} := (i_{n_α}K^p_{n_α}) × K*_{n_α,p} for α = 0, 1. Put K*_{sp,sp} := (i_nK^p_sp) × K*_{sp,p} and K*_{n,sp} := (i_nK^p_n) × K*_{sp,p}. As in §4.6, put X^?_{n_α} := X^?_𝔭(V_{n_α}, K^p_{n_α}) for meaningful triples (X, ?, α) ∈ {𝐌, M, B, S} × { , η} × {0, 1}.
items.locator: §7.3, paragraph after the data list, published p. 298
items.note: K^p_? := (K_?)^p is implicit (not defined in §7.3; cf. K^{p∘} in §7.2). i_{n_α} is the identification V_{n_α} ⊗ 𝔸^{∞,p} ≅ V*_{n_α} ⊗ 𝔸^{∞,p} of the definite uniformization datum (V*_{n_α} the definite 'nearby' hermitian space). B_{n₁} is the basic locus of M_{n₁} with projection π_{n₁}: B_{n₁} → S_{n₁} and inclusion ι_{n₁}: B_{n₁} → M_{n₁} (§4.4); S_{n₁} is the Shimura set of V*_{n₁}. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Notation 7.3.1 — the ideals 𝔪_α, 𝔫_α for the second law
items.statement: For α = 0, 1, the ideals 𝔪_α and 𝔫_α of 𝕋^{Σ⁺_II∪Σ⁺_p}_{n_α} are introduced in the same way as in Notation 7.2.1 but replacing Σ⁺_I with Σ⁺_II: 𝔪_α := 𝕋^{Σ⁺_II∪Σ⁺_p}_{n_α} ∩ ker(𝕋^{Σ⁺_min}_{n_α} →^{φ_{Π_α}} O_E → O_E/λ), 𝔫_α := 𝕋^{Σ⁺_II∪Σ⁺_p}_{n_α} ∩ ker(𝕋^{Σ⁺_min}_{n_α} →^{φ_{Π_α}} O_E → O_E/λ^m).
items.note: Inherits from Notation 7.2.1 the undefined 𝕋^{Σ⁺} (read 𝕋^{Σ⁺_min}; harmless). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Assumption 7.3.2 — localized cohomology of the smooth special fibres concentrated in the middle degree and free
items.statement: For α = 0, 1: H^i_𝔗(M̄_{n_α}, O_λ)_{𝔪_α} = 0 for i ≠ n_α − 1, and H^{n_α−1}_𝔗(M̄_{n_α}, O_λ)_{𝔪_α} is a finite free O_λ-module.
items.note: Counterpart of Assumption 7.2.3 in the good-reduction setting (no nearby cycles needed since RΨO_λ ≅ O_λ, Theorem 4.2.3). By Lemma 4.2.4 it is equivalent to the same statement for Sh(V_{n_α}, K_{n_α})_{F̄}. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 7.3.3(1) — weak semisimplicity of the middle cohomology of the odd-rank smooth fibre
items.statement: Assume Assumptions 7.1.1, 7.3.2, and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for n₁ (in the setup of §7.3). Then the O_λ[Gal(F̄_p/F_{p²})]-module H^{2r₁}_𝔗(M̄_{n₁}, O_λ(r₁))_{𝔪₁} is weakly semisimple (Definition 2.1.2).
items.note: The published version labels this 'Lemma 7.3.3' (an earlier version of this extraction says 'Proposition 7.3.3'). Proof (same as Theorem 6.2.3): H^{2r₁}_𝔗(M̄_{n₁}, O_λ(r₁))_{𝔪₁} ≃ H^{2r₁}_ét(Sh(V_{n₁}, K_{n₁})_{F̄}, O_λ(r₁))_{𝔪₁} (Lemma 4.2.4); after ⊗ ℚ̄_ℓ it is ⊕_{π₁} ρ^c_{BC(π₁),ι_ℓ}(r₁)^{⊕d(π₁)} (Lemmas 6.1.10, 6.1.11, Proposition C.3.1(2), Hypothesis 3.2.10), d(π₁) := dim (π₁^{∞,p})^{K^p_{n₁}}, sum over automorphic π₁ of U(V_{n₁})(𝔸_{F⁺}) with (V_{n₁}, π₁) a Π₁-congruent standard pair (Definition 6.1.8 with Σ⁺ = Σ⁺_II), π_{1,τ_∞} holomorphic discrete series with Harish-Chandra parameter {−r₁, 1−r₁, …, r₁−1, r₁}, π_{1,τ} trivial for archimedean τ ≠ τ_∞; after enlarging E_λ, each ρ_{BC(π₁),ι_ℓ}(r₁) has a Γ_F-stable lattice R_{BC(π₁)}, unique up to homothety, with reduction ≅ ρ̄_{Π₁,λ}(r₁), and H embeds into ⊕(R^c_{BC(π₁)})^{⊕d(π₁)}; by (PII4) ρ̄^c_{Π₁,λ}(r₁) is weakly semisimple with 1-dimensional Frobenius invariants, dim_{E_λ} ρ^c_{BC(π₁),ι_ℓ}(r₁)^{Gal} ⩾ 1, so Lemma 2.1.5 makes each R^c weakly semisimple; conclude by Lemma 2.1.4 (the printed citation is Lemma 2.1.4(1); the submodule step also needs Lemma 2.1.4(2)). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 7.3.3(2) — Frobenius coinvariants of the odd-rank middle cohomology are the Shimura-set functions
items.statement: Assume Assumptions 7.1.1, 7.3.2, and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for n₁ (in the setup of §7.3). Then the map π_{n₁!} ∘ ι*_{n₁}: (H^{2r₁}_𝔗(M̄_{n₁}, O_λ(r₁))_{𝔪₁})_{Gal(F̄_p/F_{p²})} → H⁰_𝔗(S̄_{n₁}, O_λ)_{𝔪₁} is an isomorphism.
items.note: Proof: the proof of (1) shows the coinvariants are free of rank Σ_{π₁} d(π₁) (Lemma 2.1.5 gives dim ρ^{Gal} = 1); π_{n₁!} ∘ ι*_{n₁} is surjective by Theorem 4.4.10, Proposition B.4.3(2) and (PII4); and Σ_{π₁} d(π₁) ⩽ dim_{E_λ} H⁰_𝔗(S̄_{n₁}, O_λ)_{𝔪₁} ⊗ E_λ by Proposition 4.4.4 and Corollary C.3.3. A surjection between free O_λ-modules with rank(source) ⩽ rank(target) is an isomorphism. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: §7.3 — the absolute cycle class [Sh(V_n, K_sp)]
items.statement: The finite morphism Sh(V_n, K_sp) → Sh(V_n, K_n) ×_{Spec F} Sh(V_{n+1}, K_{n+1}) gives rise, by the absolute cycle class map, to a class [Sh(V_n, K_sp)] ∈ H^{2n}_ét(Sh(V_{n₀}, K_{n₀}) ×_{Spec F} Sh(V_{n₁}, K_{n₁}), O_λ(n)).
items.note: Absolute (not geometric) étale cohomology over F; loc_𝔭 restricts it to F_𝔭 = ℚ_{p²}. It is the pushforward along K_sp → K_n of the graph class [△Sh(V_n, K_n·K_{n,p})] of Construction 4.6.1(3). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Theorem 7.3.4 — second explicit reciprocity law (exponent bound)
items.statement: Assume Assumptions 7.1.1, 7.3.2, and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for both n and n+1 (in the setup of §7.3: λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,II}, Σ⁺_II, V_n, K_n, (K_sp, K_{n+1}), the special inert prime 𝔭 satisfying (PII1)–(PII4), (PII7), and a definite uniformization datum). Then exp_λ(loc_𝔭([Sh(V_n, K_sp)]), H^{2n}_ét((Sh(V_{n₀}, K_{n₀}) ×_{Spec F} Sh(V_{n₁}, K_{n₁}))_{F_𝔭}, O_λ(n))/(𝔫₀,𝔫₁)) ⩽ exp_λ(𝟙_{Sh(V*_n, K*_{sp,sp})}, O_λ[Sh(V*_{n₀}, K*_{n₀}) × Sh(V*_{n₁}, K*_{n₁})]/(𝔫₀,𝔫₁)), where loc_𝔭 is the localization map of Construction 4.6.1, exp_λ(x, M) := min{d ∈ ℤ_{⩾0} ∪ {∞} | λ^d x = 0} (Definition 2.1.6), and 𝟙_{Sh(V*_n, K*_{sp,sp})} is regarded as the pushforward of the characteristic function along Sh(V*_n, K*_{sp,sp}) → Sh(V*_n, K*_n) × Sh(V*_{n+1}, K*_{n+1}).
items.note: An inequality, not an equality. Proof: take a uniformizer λ₀ and suppose λ₀^e𝟙 = 0 in O_λ[Sh*×Sh*]/(𝔫₀,𝔫₁); Theorem 4.6.2 on (K_sp, K_{n+1}) ∈ 𝔎(V_n)_sp and pushforward give λ₀^e T*_{n₁,𝔭}·(id×π_{n₁})_!(id×ι_{n₁})* loc′_𝔭([Sh(V_n,K_sp)]) = 0 in H^{2r₀}_𝔗(M_{n₀}×_{T_𝔭}S_{n₁}, O_λ(r₀))/(𝔫₀,𝔫₁) [printed H^{2n}(…, O_λ(n)); see source issue]; claims (1) and (2) (items thm-7-3-4-claim-1, -2) give λ₀^e loc′_𝔭([Sh(V_n,K_sp)]) = 0 in H^{2n}_𝔗(M_{n₀}×_{T_𝔭}M_{n₁}, O_λ(n))/(𝔫₀,𝔫₁); hence λ₀^e loc_𝔭([Sh(V_n,K_sp)]) = 0 because H^{2n}_ét((Sh×Sh)_{F_𝔭}, O_λ(n)) → H^{2n}_𝔗(M_{n₀}×_{T_𝔭}M_{n₁}, O_λ(n)) is an isomorphism (true after localization at (𝔪₀,𝔪₁); see source issue). By Remark 7.3.5 the class lies in H¹_ur, the counterpart of H¹_sing in Corollary 7.2.9. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 7.3.4, claim (1) — T*_{n₁,𝔭} acts invertibly
items.statement: Assume Assumptions 7.1.1, 7.3.2, and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for both n and n+1 (in the setup of §7.3: λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,II}, Σ⁺_II, V_n, K_n, (K_sp, K_{n+1}), the special inert prime 𝔭 satisfying (PII1)–(PII4), (PII7), and a definite uniformization datum). Then the action of T*_{n₁,𝔭} on H^{2r₀}_𝔗(M_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} S_{n₁}, O_λ(r₀))_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} is invertible.
items.locator: §7.3, proof of Theorem 7.3.4, claim (1), published pp. 300, 302
items.note: Proof: the 𝕋_{n₁,𝔭}-action factors through the second factor of (7.4); by Proposition B.4.3(2) and (PII4), T*_{n₁,𝔭} acts invertibly on H⁰_𝔗(S̄_{n₁}, O_λ)_{𝔪₁}. T*_{n₁,𝔭} ∈ 𝕋_{n₁,𝔭} is the Hecke operator of Theorem 4.4.10. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 7.3.4, claim (2) — restriction to the basic locus is an isomorphism on localized absolute cohomology
items.statement: Assume Assumptions 7.1.1, 7.3.2, and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for both n and n+1 (in the setup of §7.3: λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,II}, Σ⁺_II, V_n, K_n, (K_sp, K_{n+1}), the special inert prime 𝔭 satisfying (PII1)–(PII4), (PII7), and a definite uniformization datum). Then the composite map (id × π_{n₁})_! ∘ (id × ι_{n₁})*: H^{2n}_𝔗(M_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} M_{n₁}, O_λ(n))_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} → H^{2r₀}_𝔗(M_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} S_{n₁}, O_λ(r₀))_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} is an isomorphism.
items.locator: §7.3, proof of Theorem 7.3.4, claim (2), published pp. 300, 302
items.note: Proof: by (PII7) and the argument of Lemma 7.2.5(3), H^{2r₀−1}_𝔗(M̄_{n₀}, O_λ(r₀))_{𝔪₀} ⊗ ker(H^{2r₁}_𝔗(M̄_{n₁}, O_λ(r₁))_{𝔪₁} → (H^{2r₁}_𝔗(M̄_{n₁}, O_λ(r₁))_{𝔪₁})_{Gal(F̄_p/F_{p²})}) has zero Gal(F̄_p/F_{p²})-coinvariants (checked: its Frobenius eigenvalues mod λ are pα^{±1}_{0,i₀}α^{±1}_{1,i₁}, never 1 by (PII4), (PII7)); with (7.3) and Lemma 7.3.3 this gives H^{2n}_𝔗(M_{n₀}×_{T_𝔭}M_{n₁}, O_λ(n))_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} ≃ H¹(F_{p²}, H^{2r₀−1}_𝔗(M̄_{n₀}, O_λ(r₀))_{𝔪₀}) ⊗_{O_λ} (H^{2r₁}_𝔗(M̄_{n₁}, O_λ(r₁))_{𝔪₁})_{Gal(F̄_p/F_{p²})}, under which the composite becomes id ⊗ (π_{n₁!} ∘ ι*_{n₁}), an isomorphism by Lemma 7.3.3(2) and (7.4). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: (7.3) — localized absolute cohomology of M_{n₀} × M_{n₁} in degree 2n
items.statement: Assume Assumptions 7.1.1, 7.3.2, and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for both n and n+1 (in the setup of §7.3: λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,II}, Σ⁺_II, V_n, K_n, (K_sp, K_{n+1}), the special inert prime 𝔭 satisfying (PII1)–(PII4), (PII7), and a definite uniformization datum). By the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence there is a short exact sequence of O_λ-modules 0 → H¹(F_{p²}, H^{2n−1}_𝔗(M̄_{n₀} ×_{T̄_𝔭} M̄_{n₁}, O_λ(n))_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)}) → H^{2n}_𝔗(M_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} M_{n₁}, O_λ(n))_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} → H^{2n}_𝔗(M̄_{n₀} ×_{T̄_𝔭} M̄_{n₁}, O_λ(n))^{Gal(F̄_p/F_{p²})}_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} → 0. By the Künneth formula and (an analogue of) Lemma 6.1.11, H^i_𝔗(M̄_{n₀} ×_{T̄_𝔭} M̄_{n₁}, O_λ)_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} ≃ ⊕_{i₀+i₁=i} H^{i₀}_𝔗(M̄_{n₀}, O_λ)_{𝔪₀} ⊗_{O_λ} H^{i₁}_𝔗(M̄_{n₁}, O_λ)_{𝔪₁} [localizations omitted in print; see source issue] for every i; hence H^{2n}_𝔗(M̄_{n₀} ×_{T̄_𝔭} M̄_{n₁}, O_λ(n))_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} = 0, H^{2n−1}_𝔗(M̄_{n₀} ×_{T̄_𝔭} M̄_{n₁}, O_λ(n))_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} ≃ H^{2r₀−1}_𝔗(M̄_{n₀}, O_λ(r₀))_{𝔪₀} ⊗_{O_λ} H^{2r₁}_𝔗(M̄_{n₁}, O_λ(r₁))_{𝔪₁}, and (7.3): H^{2n}_𝔗(M_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} M_{n₁}, O_λ(n))_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} ≃ H¹(F_{p²}, H^{2r₀−1}_𝔗(M̄_{n₀}, O_λ(r₀))_{𝔪₀} ⊗_{O_λ} H^{2r₁}_𝔗(M̄_{n₁}, O_λ(r₁))_{𝔪₁}).
items.note: Degree check: by Assumption 7.3.2 only (i₀, i₁) = (2r₀−1, 2r₁) = (n₀−1, n₁−1) survives, total 2n−1. Here M_{n_α} (roman) is the special fibre over T_𝔭 = Spec F_{p²} and H_𝔗 of it is absolute cohomology over F_{p²} (Notation 3.3.6(5)). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: (7.4) — localized absolute cohomology of M_{n₀} × S_{n₁}
items.statement: Assume Assumptions 7.1.1, 7.3.2, and Hypothesis 3.2.10 for both n and n+1 (in the setup of §7.3: λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,II}, Σ⁺_II, V_n, K_n, (K_sp, K_{n+1}), the special inert prime 𝔭 satisfying (PII1)–(PII4), (PII7), and a definite uniformization datum). Similarly, H^{2r₀}_𝔗(M_{n₀} ×_{T_𝔭} S_{n₁}, O_λ(r₀))_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} ≃ H¹(F_{p²}, H^{2r₀−1}_𝔗(M̄_{n₀}, O_λ(r₀))_{𝔪₀} ⊗_{O_λ} H⁰_𝔗(S̄_{n₁}, O_λ)_{𝔪₁}) = H¹(F_{p²}, H^{2r₀−1}_𝔗(M̄_{n₀}, O_λ(r₀))_{𝔪₀}) ⊗_{O_λ} H⁰_𝔗(S̄_{n₁}, O_λ)_{𝔪₁}.
items.note: The last equality uses that Gal(F̄_p/F_{p²}) acts trivially on the free module H⁰_𝔗(S̄_{n₁}, O_λ)_{𝔪₁} (Proposition 4.4.4). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Remark 7.3.5 — the second law lives in the unramified part
items.statement: In Theorem 7.3.4, the element loc_𝔭([Sh(V_n, K_sp)]) belongs to the O_λ-submodule H¹_ur(F_𝔭, H^{2n−1}_ét((Sh(V_{n₀}, K_{n₀}) ×_{Spec F} Sh(V_{n₁}, K_{n₁}))_{F̄_𝔭}, O_λ(n))/(𝔫₀,𝔫₁)) [printed H^{2n}_ét; see E14], which can be viewed as the counterpart of H¹_sing in the first reciprocity law. Then Theorem 7.3.4 implies that the exponent of loc_𝔭([Sh(V_n, K_sp)]) in this submodule is bounded above by the exponent of the diagonal distribution 𝟙_{Sh(V*_n, K*_{sp,sp})} in O_λ[Sh(V*_{n₀}, K*_{n₀}) × Sh(V*_{n₁}, K*_{n₁})]/(𝔫₀,𝔫₁).
items.note: No proof; it follows from (7.3) (the localized H^{2n} is H¹ of F_{p²} with coefficients in the geometric H^{2n−1}, i.e. unramified classes) and the localized comparison of generic and special fibres. The remark is new in the published version (absent from arXiv v1–v3). exp_λ(x, ·) depends only on x, so the exponent in the submodule equals the one in Theorem 7.3.4. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: [47, §2.2] — the potential map Δ^r (and its localized version), as used in (5.28)
items.statement: (Cited.) Let K be a henselian discretely valued field with residue field κ, ℓ a prime ≠ char κ, Λ = ℚ_ℓ or ℤ/ℓ^ν, and X a proper strictly semistable scheme over O_K purely of relative dimension d, with X^{(p)}_{κ̄} the disjoint union of the (p+1)-fold intersections of irreducible components of the special fibre and δ*_p, δ_{p*} the alternating sums of pullbacks and Gysin maps. Put B^j(X_κ, Λ) := ker[δ*₀: H^{2j}(X^{(0)}_{κ̄}, Λ(j)) → H^{2j}(X^{(1)}_{κ̄}, Λ(j))] and B_j(X_κ, Λ) := coker[δ_{1*}: H^{2(d−1−j)}(X^{(1)}_{κ̄}, Λ(d−1−j)) → H^{2(d−j)}(X^{(0)}_{κ̄}, Λ(d−j))]; B^j(X_κ, Λ)^0 := ker[B^j(X_κ, Λ) → ^jE^{0,2j}_2] (weight spectral sequence), and B_j(X_κ, Λ) → B_j(X_κ, Λ)_0 the quotient map dual to B^j(·)^0 ⊂ B^j(·). By [47, Lemma 2.4], δ_{1*} ∘ δ*₀ induces B_{d+1−r}(X_κ, Λ)_0 → B^r(X_κ, Λ)^0 (2.5). With A^j(X_κ, Λ)^? := (B^j(X_κ, Λ)^?)^{G_κ} and A_j(X_κ, Λ)_? := B_j(X_κ, Λ)_?^{G_κ} (? = ∅, 0), the potential map is Δ^r: A_{d+1−r}(X_κ, Λ)_0 → A^r(X_κ, Λ)^0 [47, Definition 2.5]. If a commutative monoid 𝕋 acts through étale correspondences and 𝔪 is a prime of Λ[𝕋], localizing gives Δ^r_𝔪: A_{d+1−r}(X_κ, Λ)^𝔪_0 → A^r(X_κ, Λ)^0_𝔪 [47, Definition 2.14]. In LTXZZ (§5.11, (5.28)), for X = Q (d = 2n−1): C_r(Q, L) := B_r(Q, L)_0^{Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ)}, C^r(Q, L) := B^r(Q, L)^0_{Gal(F̄_p/F_p^Φ)}, Δ^r: C_{2n−r}(Q, L) → C^r(Q, L).
items.locator: [47] §2.2, Definition 2.5 and (2.4)–(2.5); localized: §2.3, (2.14) and Definition 2.14 (arXiv v2 numbering); LTXZZ §5.11, (5.28), p. 262, footnote 22; used in §7.2 (Proposition 7.2.7, Theorem 7.2.8)
items.note: Cited, not proved in LTXZZ. Differences a formaliser must reconcile: (i) [47] takes G_κ-invariants for both A^r and A_r, while LTXZZ's C^r is the coinvariants of B^r(Q,L)^0 (footnote 22 identifies C^r with A^r(Q,L)^0); the canonical map invariants → coinvariants is an isomorphism under (N3) of [47, Definition 2.15], since B^r ⊆ H^{2r}(Q̄^{(0)}, L(r)) = ker μ^{1,2r−1}; (ii) LTXZZ define B^r(Q,L)^0 as ker(B^r → B_{2n−r−1}) = B^r ∩ im δ_{1!} rather than ker(B^r → ^rE^{0,2r}_2); one has [47]'s B^r_0 ⊆ B^r ∩ im δ_{1!} ⊆ B^r, and after localization at (𝔪₀,𝔪₁) with r = n all three agree because 𝔼^{0,2n}_{2,(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} = 0 (Lemma 7.2.5(2)); dually for the lower side; (iii) [47] requires X proper and Λ ∈ {ℚ_ℓ, ℤ/ℓ^ν}, LTXZZ use L = O_λ and a possibly non-proper Q (footnote 29). Missing: routed to the Part II SemistablePotentialMaps (route 16).
