items.name: [47, Lemma 2.4] — δ_{1*}∘δ*₀ lands in B^r(·)^0 and factors through B_{d+1−r}(·)_0
items.statement: (Cited.) In the setting of [47, §2.2] (X proper strictly semistable over O_K of relative dimension d, Λ = ℚ_ℓ or ℤ/ℓ^ν), consider the composite H^{2r−2}(X^{(0)}_{κ̄}, Λ(r−1)) →^{δ*₀} H^{2r−2}(X^{(1)}_{κ̄}, Λ(r−1)) →^{δ_{1*}} H^{2r}(X^{(0)}_{κ̄}, Λ(r)). Its image is contained in B^r(X_κ, Λ)^0 and it factorizes through B_{d+1−r}(X_κ, Λ)_0.
items.locator: [47] §2.2, Lemma 2.4; cited in LTXZZ §5.11 (p. 262) and in the proof of Theorem 7.2.8(1d), p. 295
items.note: Cited, not proved in LTXZZ. Proof in [47]: δ*₀δ_{1*} = −δ_{2*}δ*₁ and δ*₁δ*₀ = 0 give image ⊆ B^r; the restriction of d^{−1,2r}_1 to H^{2r−2}(X^{(1)}) is δ_{1*} + δ*₁ ([Saito 2003, Prop. 2.10]) gives image ⊆ im d^{−1,2r}_1; the factorization is dual. In (1d) of Theorem 7.2.8 it is used to see that the two pushforwards (δ^{†,†}_{∘,∘})_! and (δ^{†,†}_{•,•})_! from Q̄^{†,†} have the same image under δ_{1!}∘δ*₀ (they differ by an element of im δ_{1!}). Missing: routed to the Part II SemistablePotentialMaps (route 16).

items.name: [47, Definition 2.15] — nice and very nice coefficients (localized)
items.statement: (Cited.) In the setting of [47, §2.3] (X proper strictly semistable over O_K, a commutative monoid 𝕋 acting by étale correspondences, 𝔪 a prime of Λ[𝕋], ^rE_𝔪 = ^rE_{X,𝔪} the localized weight spectral sequence with ^rE^{p,q}_{𝔪,1} = ⊕_{i⩾max(0,−p)} H^{q−2i}(X^{(p+2i)}_{κ̄}, Λ(r−i))_𝔪 ⇒ H^{p+q}(X_{K̄}, Λ(r))_𝔪), Λ is a nice coefficient for ^rE_𝔪 if (N1) ^rE_𝔪, with coefficient Λ, degenerates at the second page; and (N2) if ^rE^{p,2r−1−p}_{𝔪,2}(−1) has a nontrivial subquotient on which G_κ acts trivially, then p = 1. Λ is a very nice coefficient if moreover (N3) for every subquotient Λ[G_κ]-module M of ker μ^{1,2r−1}_𝔪 ⊕ coker μ^{−1,2r−1}_𝔪(−1), the natural map M^{G_κ} → M_{G_κ} is an isomorphism. Here μ^{p,q}: ^rE^{p−1,q+1}_1 → ^rE^{p+1,q−1}_1 is the monodromy map of [Saito 2003, Cor. 2.8(2)] (tensor product with t₀(T) on the summands that appear in the target, zero otherwise).
items.locator: [47] §2.3, Definition 2.15 (unlocalized version: Definition 2.7), arXiv v2 numbering; cited in LTXZZ Proposition 7.2.7, p. 292
items.note: Cited, not proved. Concretely ker μ^{1,2r−1} = H^{2r}(X^{(0)}_{κ̄}, Λ(r)) and coker μ^{−1,2r−1}(−1) = H^{2r−2}(X^{(0)}_{κ̄}, Λ(r−1)), so (N3) is weak semisimplicity of all subquotients of these; in LTXZZ it is supplied by Lemma 7.2.5(4) with Lemma 2.1.4(2). (N1), (N2) are supplied by Lemma 7.2.5(2), (3) with r = n. Missing: routed to the Part II SemistablePotentialMaps (route 16).

items.name: [47, Theorem 2.16] — potential map and the singular/unramified local cohomology (localized)
items.statement: (Cited.) Let X be a proper strictly semistable scheme over O_K purely of relative dimension d, Λ = ℚ_ℓ or ℤ/ℓ^ν, 𝕋, 𝔪 as in [47, §2.3], and suppose Λ is a nice coefficient for ^rE_{X,𝔪}. (1) There is a canonical map η^r_𝔪: A^r(X_κ, Λ)^0_𝔪 → H¹_sing(K, H^{2r−1}(X_{K̄}, Λ(r))_𝔪). (2) If Λ is moreover very nice, there is a canonical exact sequence 0 → H¹_unr(K, H^{2r−1}(X_{K̄}, Λ(r))_𝔪) → A_{d+1−r}(X_κ, Λ)^𝔪_0 →^{Δ^r_𝔪} A^r(X_κ, Λ)^0_𝔪 →^{η^r_𝔪} H¹_sing(K, H^{2r−1}(X_{K̄}, Λ(r))_𝔪) → 0.
items.locator: [47] §2.3, Theorem 2.16 (localized version of Theorem 2.9), arXiv v2; used in LTXZZ Proposition 7.2.7, p. 292
items.note: Cited, not proved in LTXZZ. Applied with X = Q, d = 2n−1, r = n, 𝔪 = (𝔪₀,𝔪₁), K = ℚ_{p²}, Λ = O_λ: gives coker Δ^n_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)} ≅ H¹_sing(ℚ_{p²}, H^{2n−1}_𝔗(Q̄, RΨO_λ(n))_{(𝔪₀,𝔪₁)}) (Proposition 7.2.7). The application is outside the stated hypotheses in two respects (Q possibly non-proper — footnote 29; Λ = O_λ) — see source issue. H¹_sing(K, M) = H¹(I_K, M)^{G_κ} ([47, Lemma 2.6]); H¹_unr = H¹(G_κ, M^{I_K}). Missing: routed to the Part II SemistablePotentialMaps (route 16).

items.name: [47, Theorem 2.18] — the potential boundary of e_z equals the singular part of the Abel–Jacobi class
items.statement: (Cited.) Let X, Λ, 𝕋, 𝔪 be as in [47, §2.3] and suppose Λ is a nice coefficient for ^rE_𝔪 = ^rE_{X,𝔪} (Definition 2.15). Then for every algebraic cycle z on X_K of codimension r belonging to CH^r(X_K, Λ)^0_𝔪 (the localization of the kernel of the cycle class map to H^{2r}(X_{K̄}, Λ(r))), one has η^r_𝔪(e_z) = ∂(α_𝔪(z)) in H¹_sing(K, H^{2r−1}(X_{K̄}, Λ(r))_𝔪), where α_𝔪 is the localized Abel–Jacobi map, ∂ the singular quotient map, and e_z is the image of the cycle class [z♯] ∈ H^{2r}_Z(X, Λ(r)) of the unique codimension-r cycle z♯ on X supported on the Zariski closure Z of supp z and restricting to z, under H^{2r}_Z(X, Λ(r)) → H^{2r}(X, Λ(r)) → H^{2r}(X_κ, Λ(r)) → H^{2r}(X_{κ̄}, Λ(r))^{G_κ} → H^{2r}(X^{(0)}_{κ̄}, Λ(r))_𝔪, viewed in A^r(X_κ, Λ)^0_𝔪 (using ^rE^{0,2r}_{𝔪,2} = ^rE^{0,2r}_{𝔪,∞}).
items.locator: [47] §2.4, Theorem 2.18 (with Lemma 2.17), arXiv v2; used in LTXZZ Proposition 7.2.7, p. 292
items.note: Cited, not proved in LTXZZ. Applied to z = Q^η_sp (codimension n; homologically trivial after localization by Lemma 7.2.5(5)). LTXZZ write 'cl(Q_sp)' for e_z. Proposition 2.19 (bundled in the earlier item) is now cite-liu19-prop-2-19. Missing: routed to the Part II SemistablePotentialMaps (route 16).

items.name: [47, Proposition 2.19] — e_z restricted to X^{(0)} is the geometric cycle class of the specialized cycle
items.statement: (Cited.) Let z be an algebraic cycle on X_K of codimension r (X proper strictly semistable over O_K). Suppose that for every irreducible component Z_i of the Zariski closure Z, the codimension of the singular locus Z_i^sing of Z_i in each irreducible component X_j of X_κ is at least r+1. Then the image of e_z under the restriction map H^{2r}(X_{κ̄}, Λ(r)) → H^{2r}(X^{(0)}_{κ̄}, Λ(r)) coincides with the geometric cycle class of z♯ ×_X X^{(0)}_{κ̄}.
items.locator: [47] §2.4, Proposition 2.19, arXiv v2; implicit in LTXZZ §7.2 (definition of cl(Q_sp), p. 291, and proof of Theorem 7.2.8(3), p. 295)
items.note: Not cited by name in LTXZZ, but needed to identify [47]'s e_z with the geometric class cl(Q_sp) whose Q̄^{•,•}-component is computed in the proof of Theorem 7.2.8(3). The codimension hypothesis for Q_sp is not verified in the paper (plausible: Q_sp has dimension n, its singular locus lies over the †-stratum of 𝐌_𝔭(V°_n, K°_sp), of dimension ⩽ n−2, i.e. codimension ⩾ n+1 in the (2n−1)-dimensional components of Q_κ). Missing: routed to the Part II SemistablePotentialMaps (route 16).

items.name: Definition 8.1.1 — admissible prime λ of the coefficient field
items.statement: Setup of §7.1: n ⩾ 2; n0, n1 the even and odd elements of {n, n+1}, n0 = 2r0, n1 = 2r1+1 (r0, r1 ⩾ 1, n = r0+r1); Π_α a relevant representation of GL_{n_α}(𝔸_F) (α = 0,1); E ⊂ ℂ a strong coefficient field of both; Σ⁺_min := Σ⁺_{Π0} ∪ Σ⁺_{Π1} (Notation 3.1.4); φ_α = φ_{Π_α}: 𝕋^{Σ⁺_min}_{n_α} → O_E; ρ_{Π_α,λ}: Γ_F → GL_{n_α}(E_λ) with ρ^c_{Π_α,λ} ≅ ρ^∨_{Π_α,λ}(1−n_α). A prime λ of E, with underlying rational prime ℓ and ring of integers O_λ of E_λ, is admissible (with respect to (Π0, Π1)) if: (L1) ℓ > 4n and ℓ is unramified in F; (L2) Σ⁺_min contains no ℓ-adic places; (L3) ρ_{Π0,λ} ⊗_{E_λ} ρ_{Π1,λ} is absolutely irreducible; (L4) Assumption 7.1.1 holds, i.e. both ρ_{Π0,λ} and ρ_{Π1,λ} are residually absolutely irreducible; (L5) under (L4), for α = 0,1 there is a Γ_F-stable O_λ-lattice R_α in ρ_{Π_α,λ}(r_α), unique up to homothety, that is (1−α)-polarizable; one chooses a (1−α)-polarization Ξ_α: R_α^c ≅ R_α^∨(1−α) and an isomorphism R_α ≅ O_λ^{⊕n_α} of O_λ-modules; with the notation of §2.7 (R := R0 ⊗_{O_λ} R1, ρ := ρ0 ⊗ ρ1, Ξ := Ξ0 ⊗ Ξ1: R^c ≅ R^∨(1), a 1-polarization) one requires (L5-1) one of the two assumptions of Lemma 2.3.5 holds [(a) the image of Γ_F in GL(R̄) contains a nontrivial scalar; (b) dim_{O_λ/λ} R̄ ⩽ min{(ℓ+1)/2, ℓ−3}, R̄ is a semisimple (O_λ/λ)[Γ_F]-module and Hom_{(O_λ/λ)[Γ_F]}(End(R̄), R̄) = 0], and (L5-2) the statement (GI¹_{F′,𝒫}) of Lemma 2.7.1 holds with F′ = F⁺_rflx (Definition 3.3.2) and 𝒫(T) = T² − 1 (Remark 8.1.2); (L6) under (L4), ρ̄_{Π0,λ,+} (Remark 6.1.7) is rigid for (Σ⁺_min, ∅) (Definition 6.3.3), and ρ̄_{Π0,λ}|_{Gal(F̄/F(ζ_ℓ))} is absolutely irreducible; (L7) for α = 0,1 the composite 𝕋^{Σ⁺_min}_{n_α} →^{φ_{Π_α}} O_E → O_E/λ is cohomologically generic (Definition D.1.1).
items.note: Footnote 31: (L5) does not depend on the choices, since Ξ_α is unique up to O_λ^× and the basis up to GL_{n_α}(O_λ)-conjugation. The twist by r_α turns ρ^c ≅ ρ^∨(1−n_α) into R_α^c ≅ R_α^∨(1−α). Where each condition is used: (L1) gives b − a = 2n − 1 ⩽ (ℓ−2)/2 in Lemma 2.2.7 and ℓ ⩾ 2(N+1) in Theorem 6.3.4 and §7.2; (L2) gives crystallinity at ℓ and good reduction there; (L3) feeds Lemma 2.3.3 and Proposition 2.6.6; (L4) is Assumption 7.1.1 and forces H⁰(F, R̄) = 0 (n0 ≠ n1), so H¹(F, R) is torsion-free; (L5-1) makes Res injective (Lemma 2.3.5); (L5-2) produces γ (Lemma 2.7.1); (L6) is Assumption 7.2.2 and hypothesis (b) of Theorem 6.3.4; (L7) is Assumption 7.2.4, gives Assumptions 7.2.3/7.3.2 via Remark 6.1.5, and is a hypothesis of Lemma 8.1.7. In arXiv v1/v2 (L1)–(L5) defined 'weakly admissible' and (L1)–(L7) 'admissible'; v3 and the published version keep only 'admissible'. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Remark 8.1.2 — explicit form of (L5-2)
items.statement: In Definition 8.1.1, (L5-2) is equivalent to: the image of the restriction to Gal(F̄/F⁺_rflx) of (ρ̄_{0+}, ρ̄_{1+}, ϵ̄_ℓ): Γ_{F⁺} → 𝒢_{n0}(O_λ/λ) × 𝒢_{n1}(O_λ/λ) × (O_λ/λ)^× (Notation 2.6.1) contains an element (γ0, γ1, ξ) such that (a) ξ² − 1 ≠ 0; (b) for α = 0,1, γ_α lies in the component (GL_{n_α}(O_λ/λ) × (O_λ/λ)^×, 𝔠) and has order coprime to ℓ; (c) 1 appears among the eigenvalues of each of h_{γ0}, h_{γ1} and h_{γ0} ⊗ h_{γ1} (Notation 2.6.2: h_γ is the first component of γ^{[F:F⁺]}) with multiplicity one; (d) h_{γ0} has no eigenvalue equal to −1 in O_λ/λ; (e) h_{γ1} has no eigenvalue equal to −ξ in O_λ/λ.
items.note: Unwinding (GI¹_{F′,𝒫}) of Lemma 2.7.1 with m = 1, [F:F⁺] = 2, 𝒫 = T² − 1 (so 'P(ξ) invertible' is ξ² ≠ 1). 'Multiplicity one' in (c) matches 'ker(h − 1) free of rank 1' because h has order prime to ℓ, hence is semisimple. items.name: Lemma 8.1.3 — elliptic-curve examples: almost all ℓ are admissible
items.statement: Setup of §7.1: n ⩾ 2; n0, n1 the even and odd elements of {n, n+1}, n0 = 2r0, n1 = 2r1+1 (r0, r1 ⩾ 1, n = r0+r1); Π_α a relevant representation of GL_{n_α}(𝔸_F) (α = 0,1); E ⊂ ℂ a strong coefficient field of both; Σ⁺_min := Σ⁺_{Π0} ∪ Σ⁺_{Π1} (Notation 3.1.4); φ_α = φ_{Π_α}: 𝕋^{Σ⁺_min}_{n_α} → O_E; ρ_{Π_α,λ}: Γ_F → GL_{n_α}(E_λ) with ρ^c_{Π_α,λ} ≅ ρ^∨_{Π_α,λ}(1−n_α). Suppose that F⁺ ≠ ℚ, that E = ℚ, and that there are two elliptic curves A0 and A1 over F⁺ such that for every rational prime ℓ of E and α = 0,1, ρ_{Π_α,ℓ} ≅ Sym^{n_α−1} H¹_ét(A_{α,F̄}, ℚ_ℓ)|_{Γ_F}. If A_{0,F̄} and A_{1,F̄} are not isogenous to each other and End(A_{0,F̄}) = End(A_{1,F̄}) = ℤ, then all but finitely many rational primes ℓ are admissible (Definition 8.1.1).
items.note: Published numbering: Lemma 8.1.3 (an earlier version of this extraction called it 'Proposition 8.1.3'; in arXiv v1/v2 it was Proposition 8.1.5, which also claimed weak admissibility without F⁺ ≠ ℚ). Proof: by [68, Théorème 6] the mod-ℓ representations Γ_{F⁺} → GL(H¹_ét(A_{α,F̄}, 𝔽_ℓ)) ≅ GL2(𝔽_ℓ) are surjective for ℓ ≫ 0; (L1), (L2) are trivial; (L3), (L4), (L5) come from Proposition 2.7.2 (joint image, nontrivial scalar, (GI¹) for F′ = F⁺_rflx, 𝒫 = T²−1; E4's 𝒫 ≠ 0 is harmless here); for (L6), rigidity for (Σ⁺_min, ∅) excludes finitely many ℓ by [51, Corollary 4.1.2], and 'the remaining two conditions' (irreducibility on Gal(F̄/F(ζ_ℓ)), automatic for large ℓ from the open image, and the remaining clauses of Definition 6.3.3) exclude finitely many ℓ; (L7) comes from Corollary D.1.4, which requires F⁺ ≠ ℚ. The hypothesis F⁺ ≠ ℚ is used only for (L7), and Corollary 8.2.3 invokes this lemma without it when n = 2 (see source issue). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 8.1.4 — Steinberg/supercuspidal examples: almost all λ are admissible
items.statement: Keep the setup in §7.1. Suppose that (a) there is a very special inert prime 𝔭 of F⁺ (Definition 3.3.4: 𝔭 is inert in F, of degree one over ℚ, its rational prime p is odd and unramified in F, and 𝔭 splits completely in F⁺_rflx) such that Π_{0,𝔭} is Steinberg and Π_{1,𝔭} is unramified with Satake parameter containing 1 exactly once; (b) for α = 0,1 there is a nonarchimedean place w_α of F such that Π_{α,w_α} is supercuspidal; and (c) F⁺ ≠ ℚ. Then all but finitely many primes λ of E are admissible.
items.note: Proof: (L1), (L2) trivial; (L4) by [51, Proposition 4.2.3(1)] and (b); (L3) by Lemma 8.1.5 in characteristic 0, using (L4) and (a) (t in the inertia group at 𝔭, where ρ_{Π0} is regular unipotent and ρ_{Π1} trivial); (L6) by [51, Theorem 4.2.6] and (b); (L7) by Corollary D.1.4 and (c); (L5-1): for λ satisfying (L4), (L6) with ℓ ⩾ 2n(n+1)−1, Lemma 8.1.5(2) with k = O_λ/λ and Γ = Γ_F gives assumption (b) of Lemma 2.3.5 (dim R̄ = n(n+1) ⩽ (ℓ+1)/2 explains the bound). That ρ̄_{Π0,λ}(t) is still conjugate to 1 + J_{n0} mod λ is attributed to (a), but it needs (L6): 𝔭 ∈ Σ⁺_min and every lift of ρ̄_{Π0,λ,+,𝔭} is minimally ramified, so the Steinberg lift forces a regular unipotent reduction. (L5-2): take an arithmetic Frobenius φ_𝔭 ∈ Γ_{F⁺_𝔭} ⊂ Gal(F̄/F⁺_rflx); the Satake parameter of Π_{0,𝔭} is {p^{±1}, …, p^{±(2r0−1)}}, that of Π_{1,𝔭} is {1, α_1^{±1}, …, α_{r1}^{±1}} with α_i ≠ 1 algebraic, |α_i| = 1 (Proposition 3.2.4(1)); after enlarging E, for all but finitely many λ: {p, α_1, …, α_{r1}} ⊂ O_λ^×; p^{±1}, …, p^{±(2r0−1)} mod λ are distinct and ≠ −1; α_i mod λ ∉ {1, −p, −p^{−1}}; p^{±k}α_i mod λ ∉ {p, p^{−1}} (k = 1, 3, …, 2r0−1); for such λ with (L4), (ρ̄_{0+}, ρ̄_{1+}, ϵ̄_ℓ)(φ_𝔭) satisfies Remark 8.1.2(a)–(e). All four conditions hold for the algebraic numbers themselves, which is why only finitely many λ are lost. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Notation — standard nilpotent Jordan block J_m
items.statement: For every integer m ⩾ 1, J_m ∈ M_m is the standard upper-triangular nilpotent Jordan block of size m: (J_m)_{i,i+1} = 1 for 1 ⩽ i < m and all other entries 0.
items.note: Printed 'or size m' for 'of size m' (typographic). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 8.1.5(1) — regular-unipotent tensor irreducibility
items.statement: Let Γ be a group and k a field of characteristic either 0 or at least 2n(n+1) − 1. Let ρ0: Γ → GL_{n0}(k) and ρ1: Γ → GL_{n1}(k) be absolutely irreducible homomorphisms. Suppose there is t ∈ Γ with ρ0(t) = 1 + J_{n0} and ρ1(t) = 1. Then ρ0 ⊗ ρ1 is absolutely irreducible.
items.note: Proof: reduce to k algebraically closed; by [69, Corollaire 1] ρ0 ⊗ ρ1 and ad(ρ0 ⊗ ρ1) are semisimple; if e spans V0^t then (V0 ⊗ V1)^t = k·e ⊗ V1; for a nonzero direct summand W write W^t = k·e ⊗ V1′. The claim that V1′ is Γ-stable is only asserted ('it is easy to see'); it holds because ρ1 kills the normal closure H of t, V0|_H is semisimple (Clifford) and indecomposable (t is one Jordan block), hence absolutely irreducible, so every Γ-submodule of V0 ⊗ V1 is V0 ⊗ V1′ with V1′ Γ-stable (source issue). Then V1′ = V1 and, since a unipotent t has fixed vectors on any nonzero complement, W = V0 ⊗ V1. Only the characteristic bound 2n−1 < char k is needed for (1). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 8.1.5(2) — the tensor product is not a subquotient of its adjoint
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 8.1.5 (Γ a group, k of characteristic 0 or ⩾ 2n(n+1) − 1, ρ0: Γ → GL_{n0}(k), ρ1: Γ → GL_{n1}(k) absolutely irreducible, t ∈ Γ with ρ0(t) = 1 + J_{n0}, ρ1(t) = 1), ρ0 ⊗ ρ1 is not a subquotient of ad(ρ0 ⊗ ρ1).
items.note: Proof: (ρ0 ⊗ ρ1)(t) is conjugate to (1 + J_{n0})^{⊕n1}, while ad(ρ0 ⊗ ρ1)(t) is conjugate to ⊕_{i=1}^{n0}(1 + J_{2i−1})^{⊕n1²} (the Jordan type of the adjoint of a regular unipotent, valid in characteristic 0 or ⩾ 2n0 − 1); n0 is even and all blocks of ad are odd, and ad(ρ0 ⊗ ρ1) is semisimple ([69, Corollaire 1]; here the bound 2(n(n+1) − 1) < char k is what forces 2n(n+1) − 1), so a subquotient would be a direct summand whose Jordan blocks are among those of ad. Used to verify Lemma 2.3.5(b), Hom(End R̄, R̄) = 0. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 8.1.6 — purity of weight −1
items.statement: In the setup of §7.1, the representation ρ_{Π0,λ} ⊗_{E_λ} ρ_{Π1,λ}(n) is pure of weight −1 (Definition 2.4.4: each graded piece Gr_k of the monodromy filtration of the attached Weil–Deligne representation is strictly pure of weight −1 + k, i.e. all eigenvalues of φ_w on it are Weil ‖w‖^{−(−1+k)}-numbers; E_λ(1) has weight −2) at every nonarchimedean place w of F not above ℓ.
items.note: Proof: it suffices that each ρ_{Π_α,λ}|_{Γ_{F_w}} is pure of some weight; by [74, Lemma 1.4(3)] and local–global compatibility (Proposition 3.2.4(2)) this follows from temperedness of Π_{α,w} (Proposition 3.2.4(1)). That the weight of the tensor product is exactly −1 is then forced by R^c ≅ R^∨(1) (μ ↦ −μ − 2), not stated. Used to apply Proposition 2.4.6(2) in both main proofs and to place the Abel–Jacobi class in H¹_f in Theorem 8.3.2. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 8.1.7 — independence of the special maximal level at level-raising primes (integral)
items.statement: Keep the setup of §7.1 and assume Hypothesis 3.2.10 for n1. Let V_{n1} be a standard indefinite hermitian space of rank n1 over F, Λ_{n1} a self-dual ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min} O_{F_v}-lattice in V_{n1} ⊗_F 𝔸_F^{Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min}, and λ a prime of E. Let 𝔓 be a finite set of special inert primes of F⁺ (Definition 3.3.4) whose underlying rational primes are distinct and coprime to Σ⁺_min, and K_{n1} ∈ 𝔎(V_{n1}) of the form (K_{n1})_{Σ⁺_min} × ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min} U(Λ_{n1})(O_{F⁺_v}). Put 𝔪1 := 𝕋^{Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_𝔓}_{n1} ∩ ker(𝕋^{Σ⁺_min}_{n1} →^{φ_{Π1}} O_E → O_E/λ), where Σ⁺_𝔓 is the union of Σ⁺_p over the underlying rational primes p of 𝔓. Suppose that P_{α(Π_{1,𝔭})} mod λ is intertwining generic at 𝔭 (Definition 3.1.5: P(−‖𝔭‖) = P(−p) is invertible, i.e. the pair {−p, −p^{−1}} does not occur in the Satake parameter mod λ) for every 𝔭 ∈ 𝔓, and that 𝕋^{Σ⁺_min}_{n1} →^{φ_{Π1}} O_E → O_E/λ is cohomologically generic (Definition D.1.1). Then for every special maximal subgroup K′_{n1,𝔓} of ∏_{𝔭∈𝔓} U(V_{n1})(F⁺_𝔭) and every i ∈ ℤ there is an isomorphism H^i_ét(Sh(V_{n1}, K_{n1})_{F̄}, O_λ)_{𝔪1} ≅ H^i_ét(Sh(V_{n1}, K^𝔓_{n1}K′_{n1,𝔓})_{F̄}, O_λ)_{𝔪1} of O_λ[Γ_F]-modules.
items.note: Proof as printed: for each 𝔭 ∈ 𝔓, U(V_{n1})(F⁺_𝔭) has two conjugacy classes of special maximal subgroups, exactly one hyperspecial, so one changes one prime at a time from hyperspecial K° to non-hyperspecial K•. Cohomological genericity gives H^i(…, O_E/λ)_{𝔪1} = 0 for i ≠ 2r1, hence all H^i(…, O_λ)_{𝔪1} are torsion-free; the paper then reduces to a rational isomorphism (8.1) and proves it via the local step (lemma-8-1-7-local-step). The reduction 'torsion-free ⇒ rational isomorphism suffices' is invalid (E13); the statement is recovered by showing that T^{•∘}_{n1,𝔭} itself is an integral isomorphism (both composites have unit determinant). The application in (8.7) also needs the isomorphism to be 𝕋^{Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_𝔓}_{n1}-linear, which the statement omits (source issue); T^{•∘} provides this. Called 'Proposition 8.1.7' by an earlier version of this extraction; Lemma 8.1.4 in arXiv v1/v2. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Lemma 8.1.7 — local intertwining maps are isomorphisms (8.1), (8.2)
items.statement: In the setting of Lemma 8.1.7, fix 𝔭 ∈ 𝔓 (rational prime p), a special maximal K′^𝔭_{n1,𝔓} of ∏_{𝔭′∈𝔓∖{𝔭}} U(V_{n1})(F⁺_{𝔭′}), a hyperspecial K°_{n1,𝔭} and a non-hyperspecial special maximal K•_{n1,𝔭} of U(V_{n1})(F⁺_𝔭); without loss of generality K°_{n1,𝔭}, K•_{n1,𝔭} are the stabilizers of lattices Λ°_{n1,𝔭} ⊆ Λ•_{n1,𝔭} with Λ°_{n1,𝔭} self-dual and (Λ•_{n1,𝔭})^∨/𝔭Λ•_{n1,𝔭} ≅ 𝔽_{p²}. For every (necessarily cuspidal) automorphic representation π1 of U(V_{n1})(𝔸_{F⁺}) occurring in either side of (8.1), the intertwining Hecke operators T^{•∘}_{n1,𝔭}: π_{1,𝔭}^{K°_{n1,𝔭}} → π_{1,𝔭}^{K•_{n1,𝔭}} and T^{∘•}_{n1,𝔭}: π_{1,𝔭}^{K•_{n1,𝔭}} → π_{1,𝔭}^{K°_{n1,𝔭}} (Definition 5.8.1) are isomorphisms (8.2); consequently H^i_ét(Sh(V_{n1}, K^𝔓_{n1}K′^𝔭_{n1,𝔓}K°_{n1,𝔭})_{F̄}, O_λ)_{𝔪1} ⊗_{O_λ} ℚ̄_ℓ ≅ H^i_ét(Sh(V_{n1}, K^𝔓_{n1}K′^𝔭_{n1,𝔓}K•_{n1,𝔭})_{F̄}, O_λ)_{𝔪1} ⊗_{O_λ} ℚ̄_ℓ as ℚ̄_ℓ[Γ_F]-modules for every i (8.1).
items.note: Fix ι_ℓ: ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_ℓ inducing λ. By Chebotarev, ρ_{BC(π1),ι_ℓ} and ρ_{Π1,λ} ⊗ ℚ̄_ℓ have isomorphic residual representations, so the Satake parameter {α_1^{±1}, …, α_{r1}^{±1}, 1} of BC(π1)_𝔭 avoids {−p, −p^{−1}} mod λ (Proposition 3.2.4(2) and intertwining genericity). For an unramified principal series π̃ containing π_{1,𝔭}, Proposition B.4.3(1) gives that I°_{n1,𝔭} := T^{∘•} ∘ T^{•∘} acts on the line π̃^{K°} by p^{r1²+r1}∏_{i=1}^{r1}(α_i + α_i^{−1} + p + p^{−1}) = p^{r1²+r1}∏(α_i+p)(α_i+p^{−1})/α_i ≠ 0; K°, K• special ⇒ π̃^{K°}, π̃^{K•} are lines and the same constituent carries both. The printed argument only uses that this scalar is nonzero; the same formula shows it is a λ-adic unit (p is invertible mod λ, as Definition 3.1.5 presupposes, and α_i ≢ −p^{±1} mod λ), which is what the integral repair of E13 needs. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Lemma 8.2.1 — nonvanishing central value gives a nonzero definite diagonal period
items.statement: Keep the setup in §7.1. If L(1/2, Π0 × Π1) ≠ 0, then there exist (i) a standard definite hermitian space V°_n of rank n over F with a self-dual ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min} O_{F_v}-lattice Λ°_n in V°_n ⊗_F 𝔸_F^{Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min} (put V°_{n+1} := (V°_n)_♯, Λ°_{n+1} := (Λ°_n)_♯), and (ii) an object (K°_n, K°_{n+1}) ∈ 𝔎(V°_n)_sp with K°_{n_α} = ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min}(K°_{n_α})_v × ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min} U(Λ°_{n_α})(O_{F⁺_v}) for α = 0,1, such that Σ_{s∈Sh(V°_n,K°_n)} f(s, sh_↑(s)) ≠ 0 for some f ∈ O_E[Sh(V°_{n0},K°_{n0})][ker φ_{Π0}] ⊗_{O_E} O_E[Sh(V°_{n1},K°_{n1})][ker φ_{Π1}].
items.note: Cited, not proved: by Remark 1.1.4 (a relevant Π is regular algebraic and L(s, Π, As^{(−1)^N}) is regular at s = 1) it is the direction (1)⇒(2) of [6, Theorem 1.8] together with [6, Remark 4.17]; since Π0, Π1 are relevant, both hermitian spaces in [6, Theorem 1.8(2)] must be standard definite. V_♯ = V ⊕ O_F·1 with 1 of norm 1 (Definition 3.1.7); sh_↑: Sh(V°_n,K°_n) → Sh(V°_{n+1},K°_{n+1}); O_E[X][ker φ] is the module of O_E-valued φ-eigenfunctions, and f(s, sh_↑(s)) implicitly orders the two factors as (n0, n1). This is essentially the Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture for Π0 × Π1 (BPLZZ). Missing: routed to the new roadmap GanGrossPrasadConjecturesForClassicalGroups (route 17).

items.name: Theorem 8.2.2 — Selmer rank 0 (Bloch–Kato for L(1/2) ≠ 0)
items.statement: Keep the setup in §7.1. Assume Hypothesis 3.2.10 for both n and n+1. If L(1/2, Π0 × Π1) ≠ 0, then for every admissible prime λ of E (Definition 8.1.1), H¹_f(F, ρ_{Π0,λ} ⊗_{E_λ} ρ_{Π1,λ}(n)) = 0.
items.note: Stated as Theorem 1.1.5 in the introduction (there with F⁺ ≠ ℚ in place of Hypothesis 3.2.10, via Proposition 3.2.11). Proof by contradiction: Kolyvagin-type argument with the first explicit reciprocity law (Corollary 7.2.9) at one level-raising prime 𝔭, the pairing computation being bound-by-annihilators; constants m_per, m_lat, m_Σ, 𝔯_R, m_dif are independent of m. The proof as printed depends on E1 (via Proposition 2.6.6; see the sign-obstruction source issue), on E13 (Lemma 8.1.7) and on the ℓ-adic case of (8.5); none of these threatens the statement in the non-base-change case, and repairs are indicated in the source issues. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.2.2 (1) — the period exponent m_per
items.statement: Fix V°_n, Λ°_n, (K°_n, K°_{n+1}) as in Lemma 8.2.1, shrunk at Σ⁺_min (Lemma D.2.2(3)) so that (K°_{n0})_v is transferable (Definition D.2.1) for v ∈ Σ⁺_min. For a prime λ of E, m_per is the largest nonnegative integer such that Σ_{s∈Sh(V°_n,K°_n)} f(s, sh_↑(s)) ∈ λ^{m_per}O_E for every f ∈ O_E[Sh(V°_{n0},K°_{n0})][ker φ_{Π0}] ⊗_{O_E} O_E[Sh(V°_{n1},K°_{n1})][ker φ_{Π1}].
items.note: Finite because some period is nonzero (Lemma 8.2.1); shrinking the level multiplies periods by nonzero indices. Independent of m. The setup of §2.7 is taken with the initial data of Definition 8.1.1. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.2.2 (2) — auxiliary indefinite space V_{n1} and the lattice exponent m_lat
items.statement: Choose a standard indefinite hermitian space V_{n1} of rank n1 over F and an identification U((V°_{n1})^∞) ≅ U(V_{n1}^∞) of reductive groups over 𝔸^∞_{F⁺}; this gives the Shimura variety Sh(V_{n1}, K°_{n1}). By Hypothesis 3.2.10 there is an isomorphism H^{2r1}_ét(Sh(V_{n1},K°_{n1})_{F̄}, E_λ(r1))/ker φ_{Π1} ≅ (R1^c ⊗_{O_λ} E_λ)^{⊕μ1} of E_λ[Γ_F]-modules for some integer μ1 > 0. Fix an O_λ[Γ_F]-map H^{2r1}_ét(Sh(V_{n1},K°_{n1})_{F̄}, O_λ(r1))/ker φ_{Π1} → (R1^c)^{⊕μ1} whose kernel and cokernel are O_λ-torsion; m_lat is the smallest nonnegative integer such that λ^{m_lat} annihilates both.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 8.2.2, (2) and footnote 32, published p. 309
items.note: Footnote 32: there are many choices of V_{n1} and of the identification; one is fixed to control the discrepancy between the integral cohomology of Shimura varieties and the Galois lattice. μ1 > 0 also needs that the π with BC(π) = Π1 seen on V°_{n1} occur on V_{n1} (multiplicity formula for stable parameters), which is implicit. m_lat is independent of m and of the level-raising prime; transporting it to the level-raised variety is what Lemma 8.1.7 is for (hence E13 matters). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.2.2 — the rank-one Selmer submodule S and its Kummer map θ_S
items.statement: Let λ be admissible and suppose, for contradiction, dim_{E_λ} H¹_f(F, ρ_{Π0,λ} ⊗ ρ_{Π1,λ}(n)) ⩾ 1; let m be large. By Lemma 8.1.6, Proposition 2.4.6 applies with Σ the set of places of F above Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_ℓ, giving a submodule S ⊂ H¹_{f,R}(F, R̄^{(m)}) free of rank 1 over O_λ/λ^{m−m_Σ} with loc_w|_S = 0 for every nonarchimedean w ∈ Σ not above ℓ. By (L5-1) and Lemma 2.3.4 the injective map θ_S: Gal(F_S/F_{ρ̄^{(m)}}) → Hom_{O_λ}(S, R̄^{(m)}) has image generating an O_λ-submodule containing λ^{𝔯_{R̄^{(m)}}}Hom_{O_λ}(S, R̄^{(m)}), which contains λ^{𝔯_R}Hom_{O_λ}(S, R̄^{(m)}) by Lemma 2.3.3 and (L3).
items.note: Concretely S = λ^{m_Σ}S^{(m)} with S^{(m)} the image of a saturated rank-one S0 ⊂ H¹_f(F, R). Lemma 2.3.4 is stated for S free over O_λ/λ^m; it applies here through S^{(m)} since θ_S is the restriction of θ_{S^{(m)}} and Hom(S^{(m)}, R̄^{(m)}) → Hom(S, R̄^{(m)}) is onto. 𝔣(1) = 1. m_Σ is the integer of Proposition 2.4.6(2), independent of m. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proofs of Theorems 8.2.2 and 8.3.2 — the element γ from (L5-2)
items.statement: By (L5-2) and Lemma 2.7.1 ((GI¹) ⇒ (GI^m)), choose (γ0, γ1, ξ) in the image of (ρ̄^{(m)}_{0+}, ρ̄^{(m)}_{1+}, ϵ̄^{(m)}_ℓ)|_{Gal(F̄/F⁺_rflx)} satisfying Lemma 2.7.1(a)–(e): (a) ξ² − 1 ∈ (O_λ/λ^m)^×; (b) γ_α ∈ (GL_{n_α}(O_λ/λ^m) × (O_λ/λ^m)^×, 𝔠) has order coprime to ℓ; (c) ker(h_{γ0} − 1), ker(h_{γ1} − 1), ker(h_{γ0} ⊗ h_{γ1} − 1) are free of rank 1 over O_λ/λ^m; (d) h_{γ0} has no eigenvalue −1 in O_λ/λ; (e) h_{γ1} has no eigenvalue −ξ in O_λ/λ. It gives γ ∈ (GL_{n0n1}(O_λ/λ^m) × (O_λ/λ^m)^×, 𝔠) in the image of ρ̄^{(m)}_+ (Notation 2.6.2), of order prime to ℓ, with (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ} free of rank 1 over O_λ/λ^m.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 8.2.2, published p. 310; proof of Theorem 8.3.2, published p. 317
items.note: Printed as '(γ1, γ2, ξ) in the image of (ρ̄^{(m)}_{1+}, ρ̄^{(m)}_{2+}, ϵ̄^{(m)}_ℓ)' — index misprint (source issue). γ is chosen independently of S; when F_S is Galois over F⁺ the Frobenii at γ-associated places can miss S entirely (sign obstruction, source issue downstream of E1). E3 concerns the proof of Lemma 2.7.1. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.2.2 — an (S,γ)-abundant Frobenius Ψ
items.statement: By Proposition 2.6.6 with m0 = m_Σ and r_S = 1, fix an (S,γ)-abundant element Ψ ∈ G_{S,γ} (Definition 2.6.5): Ψ is the Frobenius Ψ_{w^{(m)}} ∈ Gal(F_S/F^{(m)}) of some γ-associated place and the image of θ_S(Ψ): S → (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ} contains λ^{m_Σ+𝔯_R}(R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ}.
items.note: Hypotheses of Proposition 2.6.6: R_ℚ absolutely irreducible ((L3)), Lemma 2.3.5 ((L5-1)), γ of order prime to ℓ, (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ} free of rank 1. Proposition 2.6.6 rests on Lemma 2.6.4, which fails in general (E1); see the sign-obstruction source issue for what this means here. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.2.2 — the level-raising prime 𝔭 and the data of §7.2
items.statement: Apply §7.2 with λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,I} = ∅, Σ⁺_I = Σ⁺_min, (V°_n, Λ°_n), K°_n and (K°_sp, K°_{n+1}) = (K°_n, K°_{n+1}). By the Chebotarev density theorem choose a γ-associated place w_+^{(m)} of F_+^{(m)} (Definition 2.6.3) with Ψ_{w^{(m)}} = Ψ whose underlying prime 𝔭 of F⁺ (rational prime p) is special inert and satisfies (PI1)–(PI7) of §7.2 and (PI8): the natural map H^i_ét(Sh(V_{n1},K°_{n1})_{F̄}, O_λ(r1))/(𝕋^{Σ⁺_I∪Σ⁺_p}_{n1} ∩ ker φ_{Π1}) → H^i_ét(Sh(V_{n1},K°_{n1})_{F̄}, O_λ(r1))/ker φ_{Π1} is an isomorphism for every i. Choose the remaining data of §5.1 with ℚ_p^Φ = ℚ_{p²}, data as in Notation 5.10.13, and an indefinite uniformization datum (Notation 5.10.1); put Sh′_{n_α} := Sh(V′_{n_α}, j_{n_α}K^{p∘}_{n_α}K′_{n_α,p}).
items.note: (PI1) Σ⁺_I has no p-adic places; (PI2) ℓ ∤ p(p² − 1); (PI3) a CM type Φ ∋ τ_∞ with ℚ_p^Φ = ℚ_{p²}; (PI4) P_{α(Π_{0,𝔭})} mod λ^m level-raising special and P_{α(Π_{1,𝔭})} mod λ Tate generic; (PI5) both intertwining generic mod λ; (PI6) (O_E/λ^m)[Sh(V°_{n_α},K°_{n_α})]/(𝕋^{Σ⁺_I∪Σ⁺_p} ∩ ker φ) → …/(𝕋^{Σ⁺_I} ∩ ker φ) an isomorphism of nontrivial modules; (PI7) P_{α(Π_{0,𝔭})⊗α(Π_{1,𝔭})} mod λ^m level-raising special. The Frobenius conditions come from γ and Lemma 2.7.1(a)–(e); (PI6), (PI8) exclude only finitely many 𝔭 (the Hecke image on a fixed finitely generated module is generated by finitely many T_v and φ factors through it), which the paper leaves implicit. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.2.2 — (8.3), the definite period bound
items.statement: exp_λ(𝟙_{Sh(V°_n,K°_sp)}, O_E[Sh(V°_{n0},K°_{n0}) × Sh(V°_{n1},K°_{n1})]/(𝔫0, 𝔫1)) ⩾ m − m_per (8.3), where 𝔫_α = 𝕋^{Σ⁺_I∪Σ⁺_p}_{n_α} ∩ ker(𝕋^{Σ⁺_min}_{n_α} →^{φ_{Π_α}} O_E → O_E/λ^m) for α = 0,1, K°_sp = K°_n, and 𝟙_{Sh(V°_n,K°_sp)} is the characteristic function of the graph △Sh(V°_n,K°_n) of Sh(V°_n,K°_n) → Sh(V°_{n+1},K°_{n+1}).
items.note: 'By the definition of m_per': 𝔫_α contains λ^m and 𝕋^{Σ⁺_I∪Σ⁺_p} ∩ ker φ_{Π_α}, and every t ∈ 𝔫_α acts as (t − φ(t)) + φ(t) with φ(t) ∈ λ^mO_E, so by (PI6) the quotient is (O_E[X]/(ker φ_{Π0}, ker φ_{Π1})) ⊗ O_E/λ^m, whose O_E-linear dual is spanned by the eigenfunctions f in the definition of m_per; hence the image of the graph in its torsion-free quotient is λ^{m_per} times a primitive vector. exp_λ(x, M) = min{d : λ^d x = 0} (Definition 2.1.6). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.2.2 — claim (8.4)–(8.5): the level-raised annihilating class c1
items.statement: There is c1 ∈ H¹(F, R̄^{(m)c}) such that (8.4) exp_λ(∂_𝔭 loc_𝔭(c1), H¹_sing(F_𝔭, R̄^{(m)c})) ⩾ m − m_per − m_lat, and (8.5) loc_w(c1) ∈ H¹_ns(F_w, R̄^{(m)c}) for every nonarchimedean place w of F not above Σ⁺ ∪ {𝔭}.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 8.2.2, claim (8.4)–(8.5), published p. 311; proved on pp. 312–313
items.note: Σ⁺ is not defined in §8; it must be read as Σ⁺_min (= Σ⁺_I here), and ℓ-adic w are included (H¹_ns there is the Fontaine–Laffaille subgroup of Definition 2.2.5), since the ℓ-adic pairing bullet uses (8.5). c1 is one of the classes c_i of constr-Upsilon-c-i attaining the maximum in (8.9). (8.5) is justified by 'both Sh′_n and Sh′_{n+1} have smooth models over O_{F_w} for which (an analogue of) Lemma 4.2.4 holds' — adequate for w ∤ ℓ, not argued for w | ℓ (source issue). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.2.2 — (8.6), the even-rank level-raised cohomology
items.statement: By Remark 6.1.5, Assumption 7.2.3 holds (Lemma 5.2.7 and (L7)). By (L4), (L6) and Theorem 6.3.4(5) there is an isomorphism H^{2r0−1}_ét(Sh(V′_{n0}, j_{n0}K^{p∘}_{n0}K′_{n0,p})_{F̄}, O_λ(r0))/𝔫0 ≅ (R̄_0^{(m)c})^{⊕μ0} of O_λ[Γ_F]-modules, for some positive integer μ0 (8.6).
items.note: Theorem 6.3.4 (N = n0, Σ⁺_lr = ∅) needs ℓ ⩾ 2(n0+1) and ℓ unramified in F ((L1)), rigidity for (Σ⁺_min, ∅) and irreducibility on Gal(F̄/F(ζ_ℓ)) ((L6)), cohomological genericity ((L7)) and nontriviality of O_λ[Sh(V°_{n0},K°_{n0})]_𝔪 ((PI6)). In particular the left side is unramified at 𝔭. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.2.2 — (8.7), the odd-rank level-raised cohomology up to λ^{m_lat}
items.statement: By Lemma 8.1.7, H^i_ét(Sh(V_{n1},K°_{n1})_{F̄}, O_λ)_{𝔪1} ≅ H^i_ét(Sh(V′_{n1}, j_{n1}K^{p∘}_{n1}K′_{n1,p})_{F̄}, O_λ)_{𝔪1} as O_λ[Γ_F]-modules. By (PI8) one fixes an O_λ[Γ_F]-map H^{2r1}_ét(Sh(V′_{n1}, j_{n1}K^{p∘}_{n1}K′_{n1,p})_{F̄}, O_λ(r1))/(𝕋^{Σ⁺_I∪Σ⁺_p}_{n1} ∩ ker φ_{Π1}) → (R1^c)^{⊕μ1} whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by λ^{m_lat}; reducing modulo λ^m gives an O_λ[Γ_F]-map H^{2r1}_ét(Sh(V′_{n1}, j_{n1}K^{p∘}_{n1}K′_{n1,p})_{F̄}, O_λ(r1))/𝔫1 → (R̄_1^{(m)c})^{⊕μ1} (8.7) whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by λ^{m_lat}.
items.note: Implicit steps: V′_{n1} is identified with V_{n1} (odd rank, same signatures, so the unitary groups agree and K′_{n1,p} is a special maximal subgroup of U(V_{n1})(F⁺_𝔭)); the transfer of the m_lat map needs Lemma 8.1.7 to be integral (E13) and 𝕋^{Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_p}-linear (source issue). Reduction mod λ^m keeps the bound λ^{m_lat} on the kernel because the target is torsion-free (the map kills the torsion of the source and is injective with cokernel killed by λ^{m_lat} on a free complement). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.2.2 — (8.8) the comparison Υ and the classes c_i
items.statement: With Sh′_{n_α} := Sh(V′_{n_α}, j_{n_α}K^{p∘}_{n_α}K′_{n_α,p}), Lemma 6.1.11 and the Künneth formula combine (8.6) and (8.7) into an O_λ[Γ_F]-map Υ: H^{2n−1}_ét((Sh′_{n0} ×_{Spec F} Sh′_{n1})_{F̄}, O_λ(n))/(𝔫0, 𝔫1) → (R̄^{(m)c})^{⊕μ0μ1} (8.8) whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by λ^{m_lat}. For 1 ⩽ i ⩽ μ0μ1 let Υ_i be Υ followed by the i-th projection and c_i := H¹(F, Υ_i)(AJ(Sh′_sp)) ∈ H¹(F, R̄^{(m)c}), where AJ(Sh′_sp) ∈ H¹(F, H^{2n−1}_ét((Sh′_{n0} ×_{Spec F} Sh′_{n1})_{F̄}, O_λ(n))/(𝔫0, 𝔫1)) is the Abel–Jacobi class of the cycle Sh′_sp, the graph of Sh′_n → Sh′_{n+1}.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 8.2.2, (8.8) and definition of c_i, published pp. 312–313
items.note: Only the (2r0−1, 2r1) Künneth summand survives after localization; tensoring the isomorphism (8.6) (free target) with (8.7) keeps the λ^{m_lat} bounds. AJ is the map of §7.2 before Corollary 7.2.9 (defined because H^i of the product localized at (𝔪0,𝔪1) vanishes for i ≠ 2n − 1). items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.2.2 — (8.9) and the bound for max_i ∂_𝔭 loc_𝔭(c_i)
items.statement: By Corollary 7.2.9 and (8.3), exp_λ(∂_𝔭 loc_𝔭 AJ(Sh′_sp), H¹_sing(F_𝔭, H^{2n−1}_ét((Sh′_{n0} ×_{Spec F} Sh′_{n1})_{F̄}, O_λ(n))/(𝔫0,𝔫1))) ⩾ m − m_per (8.9). Consequently max_{1⩽i⩽μ0μ1} exp_λ(∂_𝔭 loc_𝔭(c_i), H¹_sing(F_𝔭, R̄^{(m)c})) ⩾ m − m_per − m_lat, which gives (8.4) for c1 := c_i with i attaining the maximum.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 8.2.2, (8.9) and following lines, published p. 313
items.note: Corollary 7.2.9 is an equality of exponents with 𝟙_{Sh(V°_n,K°_sp)}. The loss of a single m_lat is correct but needs the unstated fact that the source of Υ is unramified at 𝔭 ((8.6), and (8.7) via Lemma 8.1.7 to hyperspecial level): then H¹_sing(F_𝔭, M) = M(−1)^{Frob_𝔭 = 1} is left exact and only ker Υ can lower the exponent; for ramified modules the cokernel would cost another m_lat. items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.2.2 — the rank-zero pairing computation
items.statement: Let s1 be the image in H¹(F, R̄^{(m)}) of a generator of S, identify R̄^{(m)c} with (R̄^{(m)})^*(1) via Ξ, and consider the local Tate pairings ⟨s1, c1⟩_w (2.2) for nonarchimedean w of F. (i) w above Σ⁺_min: loc_w(s1) = 0 by the choice of S, so ⟨s1,c1⟩_w = 0. (ii) w above Σ⁺_ℓ: by (L2) R_ℚ is crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights in [−n, n−1], so loc_w(s1) ∈ H¹_ns(F_w, R̄^{(m)}) (Lemma 2.4.3(2), (L1)); by (8.5), Lemma 2.2.7 and (L1), λ^{m_dif}⟨s1,c1⟩_w = 0, where 𝔡_λ = λ^{m_dif} ⊆ O_λ is the different of E_λ/ℚ_ℓ. (iii) w not above Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_ℓ ∪ {𝔭}: R is unramified, loc_w(s1) ∈ H¹_ns (Lemma 2.4.3(1)), and (8.5) with Lemma 2.2.3 gives ⟨s1,c1⟩_w = 0. (iv) w the place above 𝔭: exp_λ(loc_w(s1), H¹_ns(F_w, R̄^{(m)})) ⩾ m − m_Σ − 𝔯_R (Proposition 2.6.7), hence with (8.4) exp_λ(⟨s1,c1⟩_w, O_λ/λ^m) ⩾ m − m_per − m_lat − m_Σ − 𝔯_R. If m > m_per + m_lat + m_Σ + 𝔯_R + m_dif this contradicts Σ_w ⟨s1,c1⟩_w = 0.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 8.2.2, pairing computation, published pp. 311–312
items.note: Checked line by line. The printed identification is 'with (R̄^{(m)})^*' (the twist (1) is missing, misprint). Step (iv) uses Proposition 2.6.7 with r = 1, which is correct (E2 only concerns r ⩾ 2): the abundant Ψ gives a generator with θ_S(Ψ)(s1) of valuation ⩽ m_Σ + 𝔯_R, and H¹_ns(F_w, R̄^{(m)}) ≅ (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ} by evaluation at Ψ (injective since h_γ has order prime to ℓ). The exponent inequality in (iv) is not a consequence of Lemma 2.2.3 alone: it uses that H¹_ns(F_w, R̄^{(m)}) and H¹_sing(F_w, R̄^{(m)*}(1)) are free of rank one and perfectly paired (local Tate duality, std-local-tate-duality), whence exp⟨x,y⟩ ⩾ exp x + exp y − m. The contradiction uses global reciprocity (std-global-reciprocity). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Corollary 8.2.3 — symmetric powers of two elliptic curves, rank 0
items.statement: Let n ⩾ 2 be an integer and n0, n1 the even and odd elements of {n, n+1}. Let A0 and A1 be modular elliptic curves over F⁺ with End(A_{0,F̄}) = End(A_{1,F̄}) = ℤ. Suppose that (a) A_{0,F̄} and A_{1,F̄} are not isogenous to each other; (b) both Sym^{n0−1}A0 and Sym^{n1−1}A1 are modular; and (c) F⁺ ≠ ℚ if n ⩾ 3. If the (central critical) L-value L(n, Sym^{n0−1}A_{0,F} × Sym^{n1−1}A_{1,F}) does not vanish, then H¹_f(F, Sym^{n0−1}H¹_ét(A_{0,F̄}, ℚ_ℓ) ⊗_{ℚ_ℓ} Sym^{n1−1}H¹_ét(A_{1,F̄}, ℚ_ℓ)(n)) = 0 for all but finitely many rational primes ℓ.
items.note: Proof: by (b) and [1] the base changes Sym^{n_α−1}A_{α,F} are modular; Π_α is the associated cuspidal (relevant) representation of GL_{n_α}(𝔸_F), L(n+s, Sym^{n0−1}A_{0F} × Sym^{n1−1}A_{1F}) = L(1/2+s, Π0 × Π1) and ρ_{Π_α,ℓ} ≅ Sym^{n_α−1}H¹_ét(A_{α,F̄},ℚ_ℓ); Hypothesis 3.2.10 holds by Proposition 3.2.11 and (c) (N = 2 by [48]; N = 3 with F⁺ = ℚ by [64]; N ⩾ 3 with F⁺ ≠ ℚ by [37], 'in preparation' at publication); then Theorem 8.2.2 and Lemma 8.1.3 with E = ℚ. Gap: Lemma 8.1.3 requires F⁺ ≠ ℚ for all n, so the case n = 2, F⁺ = ℚ allowed by (c) is not proved (source issue); the introduction's version (Theorem 1.1.1, with A = A0, A′ = A1) assumes F⁺ ≠ ℚ outright. In arXiv v1/v2 this was Corollary 8.2.5. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Remark 8.2.4 — known modularity of symmetric powers (inputs for Corollary 8.2.3(b))
items.statement: Let A be a modular elliptic curve over F⁺ with End(A_{F̄}) = ℤ. Then Sym²A is modular [26]; Sym³A is modular [36]; Sym⁴A is modular [35]; Sym⁵A and Sym⁶A are modular if F⁺ is linearly disjoint from ℚ(ζ5) over ℚ; Sym⁷A is modular if F⁺ is linearly disjoint from ℚ(ζ35) over ℚ; Sym⁸A is modular if F⁺ is linearly disjoint from ℚ(ζ7) over ℚ (the last three by Clozel–Thorne [19–21]). By Newton–Thorne [57, 58] all symmetric powers of non-CM elliptic curves over ℚ are modular; in particular Sym^n A is modular if F⁺/ℚ is solvable and A is the base change of an elliptic curve over ℚ.
items.note: Cited results, not proved. The remark says it summarizes 'condition (a) in Corollary 8.2.3'; modularity is condition (b) (misprint, source issue). The Newton–Thorne consequence over solvable F⁺ uses solvable base change [1]. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Corollary 8.2.5 — Steinberg/supercuspidal family, rank 0
items.statement: Keep the setup in §7.1. Suppose that (a) there is a very special inert prime 𝔭 of F⁺ (Definition 3.3.4) such that Π_{0,𝔭} is Steinberg and Π_{1,𝔭} is unramified with Satake parameter containing 1 exactly once; (b) for α = 0,1 there is a nonarchimedean place w_α of F with Π_{α,w_α} supercuspidal; and (c) F⁺ ≠ ℚ if n ⩾ 3. If L(1/2, Π0 × Π1) ≠ 0, then H¹_f(F, ρ_{Π0,λ} ⊗_{E_λ} ρ_{Π1,λ}(n)) = 0 for all but finitely many primes λ of E.
items.note: Proof: 'This follows from Theorem 8.2.2 and Lemma 8.1.4' (Hypothesis 3.2.10 for n, n+1 comes tacitly from Proposition 3.2.11 and (c)). Lemma 8.1.4 needs F⁺ ≠ ℚ, so n = 2 with F⁺ = ℚ is not covered (source issue); the introduction's Theorem 1.1.7 assumes F⁺ ≠ ℚ. In arXiv v1/v2 this was Corollary 8.2.3. The paper remarks (end of §8.3) that a rank-one analogue is left to the reader. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Conjecture 8.3.1 — weak arithmetic Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture
items.statement: Keep the setup in §7.1. Suppose that L(1/2, Π0 × Π1) = 0 but L′(1/2, Π0 × Π1) ≠ 0. Then there exist (i) a standard indefinite hermitian space V_n of rank n over F with a self-dual ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min} O_{F_v}-lattice Λ_n in V_n ⊗_F 𝔸_F^{Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min} (put V_{n+1} := (V_n)_♯, Λ_{n+1} := (Λ_n)_♯), and (ii) an object (K_n, K_{n+1}) ∈ 𝔎(V_n)_sp with K_{n_α} = ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min}(K_{n_α})_v × ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min} U(Λ_{n_α})(O_{F⁺_v}) for α = 0,1, such that [printed: for every prime λ of E] the graph △Sh(V_n,K_n) of sh_↑: Sh(V_n,K_n) → Sh(V_{n+1},K_{n+1}) (4.6) is nonvanishing in the quotient Chow group CH^n(Sh(V_{n0},K_{n0}) ×_{Spec F} Sh(V_{n1},K_{n1}))_E/(ker φ_{Π0}, ker φ_{Π1}).
items.note: A conjecture, assumed nowhere in the proofs. The quantifier 'for every prime λ of E' is vacuous (the conclusion does not involve λ; source issue). Together with Beilinson's injectivity conjecture for the ℓ-adic Abel–Jacobi map it would give (8.10) for all λ (introduction). Theorem 8.3.2 additionally needs (K_{n0})_v transferable at Σ⁺_min, obtainable by shrinking the level. Missing: routed to the new roadmap GanGrossPrasadConjecturesForClassicalGroups (route 17).

items.name: §8.3 — the Π-isotypic Abel–Jacobi map AJ_λ^{Π0,Π1}
items.statement: In the situation of Conjecture 8.3.1 (Π0, Π1 cuspidal), H^i_ét((Sh(V_{n0},K_{n0}) ×_{Spec F} Sh(V_{n1},K_{n1}))_{F̄}, E_λ)/(ker φ_{Π0}, ker φ_{Π1}) = 0 for i ≠ 2n − 1, so the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence yields a coboundary map AJ_λ^{Π0,Π1}: Z^n(Sh(V_{n0},K_{n0}) ×_{Spec F} Sh(V_{n1},K_{n1})) → H¹(F, H^{2n−1}_ét((Sh(V_{n0},K_{n0}) ×_{Spec F} Sh(V_{n1},K_{n1}))_{F̄}, E_λ(n))/(ker φ_{Π0}, ker φ_{Π1})).
items.note: The vanishing off degree 2n − 1 is asserted 'since both Π0 and Π1 are cuspidal' (tempered cuspidal contributions of regular weight live in middle degree; with Künneth, dimension (n0−1)+(n1−1) = 2n−1). Because the Π-part of H^{2n} over F̄ vanishes, the map is defined on all codimension-n cycles, not only homologically trivial ones. △_λ in the introduction is AJ_λ^{Π0,Π1}(△Sh(V_n,K_n)). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Theorem 8.3.2 — Selmer rank 1 from a nonzero diagonal Abel–Jacobi class
items.statement: Keep the setup in §7.1. Assume Hypothesis 3.2.10 for both n and n+1. Let λ be a prime of E for which there exist a standard indefinite hermitian space V_n of rank n over F with a self-dual ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min} O_{F_v}-lattice Λ_n in V_n ⊗_F 𝔸_F^{Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min} (V_{n+1} := (V_n)_♯, Λ_{n+1} := (Λ_n)_♯) and an object (K_n, K_{n+1}) ∈ 𝔎(V_n)_sp with K_{n_α} = ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min}(K_{n_α})_v × ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min} U(Λ_{n_α})(O_{F⁺_v}) (α = 0,1), such that (K_{n0})_v is a transferable open compact subgroup (Definition D.2.1) of U(V_{n0})(F⁺_v) [printed U(V°_{n0})(F⁺_v)] for v ∈ Σ⁺_min, and such that AJ_λ^{Π0,Π1}(△Sh(V_n,K_n)) ≠ 0 (8.10). If λ is admissible, then dim_{E_λ} H¹_f(F, ρ_{Π0,λ} ⊗_{E_λ} ρ_{Π1,λ}(n)) = 1.
items.note: Theorem 1.1.9 of the introduction (with F⁺ ≠ ℚ instead of Hypothesis 3.2.10). Nonvanishing of L′ alone is not a hypothesis: (8.10) is. Proof: dim ⩾ 1 from the AJ class; assuming dim ⩾ 2, a rank-two S, an abundant pair (Ψ1, Ψ2), the second reciprocity law (Theorem 7.3.4) at 𝔭1 and the first (Corollary 7.2.9) at 𝔭2 produce c2 whose pairing with s2 is too large (pairing-rank1). The diagonal-basis step (8.11) relies on Proposition 2.6.7 (E2) but only its one-sided consequence is used, which holds with the same constant 4𝔯_R (source issue); E1, E13 and the ℓ-adic (8.14) affect it as in Theorem 8.2.2. The paper leaves the rank-one analogue of Corollary 8.2.5 to the reader. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Remark 8.3.3 — (8.10) forces root number −1
items.statement: In Theorem 8.3.2, condition (8.10) (AJ_λ^{Π0,Π1}(△Sh(V_n,K_n)) ≠ 0) already implies that the global epsilon factor of Π0 × Π1 is −1.
items.note: Stated without proof and not used later; presumably via local Gan–Gross–Prasad (the Π-component of the diagonal cycle can be nonzero only if Π is distinguished by the incoherent collection underlying Sh(V_n), which forces ε(1/2, Π0 × Π1) = −1). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.3.2 — the diagonal Abel–Jacobi class is Bloch–Kato
items.statement: Lemma 8.1.6 and (L2) imply that AJ_λ^{Π0,Π1}(△Sh(V_n,K_n)) lies in H¹_f(F, H^{2n−1}_ét((Sh(V_{n0},K_{n0}) ×_{Spec F} Sh(V_{n1},K_{n1}))_{F̄}, E_λ(n))/(ker φ_{Π0}, ker φ_{Π1})), and hence (Definition 2.4.2) in the integral Bloch–Kato submodule H¹_f(F, H^{2n−1}_ét((Sh(V_{n0},K_{n0}) ×_{Spec F} Sh(V_{n1},K_{n1}))_{F̄}, O_λ(n))/(ker φ_{Π0}, ker φ_{Π1})).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 8.3.2, first paragraph, published p. 316
items.note: At w ∤ ℓ, purity of weight −1 (Lemma 8.1.6, via Hypothesis 3.2.10 identifying the module with copies of ρ^c_{Π0}⊗ρ^c_{Π1}(n)) gives H⁰ = 0 on both sides of local duality, so H¹_f = H¹ locally; at w | ℓ, (L2) and ℓ unramified in F give good reduction, so the AJ class is crystalline (standard comparison, not cited). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.3.2 (1) — the Selmer class s and m_per
items.statement: By Hypothesis 3.2.10 choose an O_λ[Γ_F]-map H^{2n−1}_ét((Sh(V_{n0},K_{n0}) ×_{Spec F} Sh(V_{n1},K_{n1}))_{F̄}, O_λ(n))/(ker φ_{Π0}, ker φ_{Π1}) → R^c such that the induced image s^c ∈ H¹_f(F, R^c) of AJ_λ^{Π0,Π1}(△Sh(V_n,K_n)) is non-torsion. Let s ∈ H¹_f(F, R) correspond to s^c under the conjugation isomorphism of Lemma 2.4.5, and m_per := ord_λ(s, H¹_f(F,R)/H¹_f(F,R)_tor) (Definition 2.1.6: sup{d ⩾ 0 : s ∈ λ^d(H¹_f/H¹_f,tor)}), a nonnegative integer. In particular s is a nonzero element of H¹_f(F,R)_ℚ = H¹_f(F, R_ℚ) = H¹_f(F, ρ_{Π0,λ} ⊗_{E_λ} ρ_{Π1,λ}(n)), so this space has dimension ⩾ 1.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 8.3.2, (1) and the following paragraph, published pp. 316–317
items.note: The notation of §2.7 is taken with the initial data of Definition 8.1.1 (R = R0 ⊗ R1, Ξ). Lemma 2.4.5 is stated for E_λ-coefficients; the same c-conjugation works integrally. Since H⁰(F, R̄) = 0 ((L4), n0 ≠ n1), H¹(F, R) is torsion-free, so H¹_f(F,R)_tor = 0 here. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.3.2 (2) — the lattice exponent m_lat
items.statement: By Hypothesis 3.2.10, H^{2r1}_ét(Sh(V_{n1},K_{n1})_{F̄}, E_λ(r1))/ker φ_{Π1} ≅ (R1^c ⊗_{O_λ} E_λ)^{⊕μ1} as E_λ[Γ_F]-modules for some integer μ1 > 0. Fix an O_λ[Γ_F]-map H^{2r1}_ét(Sh(V_{n1},K_{n1})_{F̄}, O_λ(r1))/ker φ_{Π1} → (R1^c)^{⊕μ1} whose kernel and cokernel are O_λ-torsion; m_lat is the smallest nonnegative integer such that λ^{m_lat} annihilates both.
items.note: Same role as def-m-lat-rank0, now with the indefinite space V_{n1} of the theorem itself. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.3.2 — the rank-two Selmer submodule S containing the AJ class
items.statement: Assume, for contradiction, dim_{E_λ} H¹_f(F, ρ_{Π0,λ} ⊗ ρ_{Π1,λ}(n)) ⩾ 2; take m large and a uniformizer λ0 of E_λ. By Lemma 8.1.6, Proposition 2.4.6 with Σ the places of F above Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_ℓ gives a submodule S ⊂ H¹_{f,R}(F, R̄^{(m)}), free of rank 2 over O_λ/λ^{m−m_Σ}, containing (the image of) λ0^{m_Σ−m_per}s as an element of order 0 (i.e. not in λS), with loc_w|_S = 0 for every nonarchimedean w ∈ Σ not above ℓ. Here (footnote 33) λ0^{−m_per}s is any element of H¹_f(F,R) with λ0^{m_per}(λ0^{−m_per}s) = s. By (L5-1) and Lemma 2.3.4, θ_S: Gal(F_S/F_{ρ̄^{(m)}}) → Hom_{O_λ}(S, R̄^{(m)}) is injective with image generating an O_λ-submodule containing λ^{4𝔯_{R̄^{(m)}}}Hom_{O_λ}(S, R̄^{(m)}) ⊇ λ^{4𝔯_R}Hom_{O_λ}(S, R̄^{(m)}) (Lemma 2.3.3, (L3)).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 8.3.2 and footnote 33, published p. 317
items.note: S = λ^{m_Σ}S^{(m)} with S^{(m)} the image of a saturated rank-2 S0 ⊂ H¹_f(F,R) containing the primitive element λ0^{−m_per}s. Footnote 33 needs s ∈ λ^{m_per}H¹_f(F,R), not just modulo torsion; this holds because H¹(F,R) is torsion-free (def-m-per-rank1). 𝔣(2) = 4. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.3.2 — abundant pair (Ψ1, Ψ2) and the localization bounds (8.11)
items.statement: With γ as in constr-gamma, Proposition 2.6.6 (m0 = m_Σ, r_S = 2) gives an (S,γ)-abundant pair (Ψ1, Ψ2) ∈ G²_{S,γ}. As printed: by Proposition 2.6.7 there is a basis {s1, s2} of S with θ_S(Ψ1)(s2) = θ_S(Ψ2)(s1) = 0 and exp_λ(θ_S(Ψ_j)(s_j), (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ}) ⩾ m − m_Σ − 4𝔯_R for j = 1,2 (8.11); and without loss of generality λ0^{m_Σ−m_per}s = a1s1 + a2s2 with a1 ∈ O_λ^×. What is actually used, and follows from abundance alone: after possibly interchanging Ψ1 and Ψ2, (i) exp_λ(θ_S(Ψ1)(λ0^{m_Σ−m_per}s), (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ}) ⩾ m − m_Σ − 4𝔯_R, and (ii) there is a primitive t ∈ S (playing the role of s2) with θ_S(Ψ1)(t) = 0 and exp_λ(θ_S(Ψ2)(t), (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ}) ⩾ m − m_Σ − 4𝔯_R.
items.note: Proposition 2.6.7's diagonal basis is not implied by abundance for r = 2 (E2); e.g. rows λ^{m_Σ}(λ, 1), λ^{m_Σ}(0, λ) are abundant when 4𝔯_R ⩾ 2 but no basis diagonalizes them. Proof of (i)–(ii): write A for the 2×2 matrix (θ_S(Ψ_i)(e_j)) = λ^{m_Σ}A′, A′ over O_λ/λ^{m−m_Σ}; abundance means the elementary divisors of A′ have valuation ⩽ 4𝔯_R; hence for every primitive v ∈ S some coordinate of A′v has valuation ⩽ 4𝔯_R (swap so it is the first, for v = λ0^{m_Σ−m_per}s); the first row of A′ is λ^a·u with u unimodular, a ⩽ 4𝔯_R, and a primitive t spanning ker u satisfies θ_S(Ψ1)(t) = 0 while A′t, hence θ_S(Ψ2)(t), has valuation ⩽ 4𝔯_R. This is the repair S25-consumer, recorded by an earlier version of this extraction which is correct. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.3.2 — the first auxiliary prime 𝔭1 (second reciprocity law)
items.statement: Apply §7.3 with λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,II} = ∅, Σ⁺_II = Σ⁺_min, (V_n, Λ_n), K_n and (K_sp, K_{n+1}) = (K_n, K_{n+1}). By Chebotarev choose a γ-associated place w_{1+}^{(m)} of F_+^{(m)} with Ψ_{w_1^{(m)}} = Ψ1 whose underlying prime 𝔭1 of F⁺ (rational prime p1) is special inert and satisfies (PII1)–(PII7) of §7.3 and (PII8): H^i_ét(Sh(V_{n1},K_{n1})_{F̄}, O_λ(r1))/(𝕋^{Σ⁺_II∪Σ⁺_{p1}}_{n1} ∩ ker φ_{Π1}) → H^i_ét(Sh(V_{n1},K_{n1})_{F̄}, O_λ(r1))/ker φ_{Π1} is an isomorphism for every i. Choose the remaining data of §4.1 with ℚ_{p1}^Φ = ℚ_{p1²} and a definite uniformization datum (V*_{n_α}, i_{n_α}, {Λ*_{n_α,𝔮}}_{𝔮|p1}) for α = 0,1 (Notation 4.5.7).
items.note: (PII1) Σ⁺_II has no p1-adic places; (PII2) ℓ ∤ p1(p1² − 1); (PII3) ℚ_{p1}^Φ = ℚ_{p1²}; (PII4) P_{α(Π_{0,𝔭1})} mod λ^m level-raising special, P_{α(Π_{1,𝔭1})} mod λ Tate generic; (PII7) P_{α(Π_{0,𝔭1})⊗α(Π_{1,𝔭1})} mod λ^m level-raising special (there is no (PII5), (PII6)). With 𝔫_α := 𝕋^{Σ⁺_II∪Σ⁺_{p1}}_{n_α} ∩ ker(𝕋^{Σ⁺_min}_{n_α} → O_E → O_E/λ^m). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.3.2 — localization of s and of the diagonal cycle at 𝔭1
items.statement: By (8.11) and the choice of S, exp_λ(loc_{w1}(s), H¹_ns(F_{w1}, R̄^{(m)})) ⩾ m − m_per − 4𝔯_R, which implies exp_λ(loc_{𝔭1}([△Sh(V_n,K_n)]), H^{2n}_ét((Sh(V_{n0},K_{n0}) ×_{Spec F} Sh(V_{n1},K_{n1}))_{F_{𝔭1}}, O_λ(n))/(𝔫0, 𝔫1)) ⩾ m − m_per − 4𝔯_R [coefficients printed 'L(n)'].
items.note: First inequality: λ0^{m_Σ}(λ0^{−m_per}s) = a1s1 + a2s2 with θ_S(Ψ1)(s2) = 0 (or (i) of basis-8-11) gives exp loc_{w1}(λ0^{−m_per}s) ⩾ m − 4𝔯_R, and exp(λ^a x) = max(exp x − a, 0). Second: [△Sh(V_n,K_n)] = [Sh(V_n,K_sp)] with K_sp = K_n. Since 𝔫_α ⊆ ker(𝕋^{Σ⁺_min}_{n_α} → O_E/λ^m), the map of (1) reduced mod λ^m induces H/(𝔫0,𝔫1) ↠ H/(ker φ_{Π0}, ker φ_{Π1}, λ^m) → R̄^{(m)c}; via Hochschild–Serre it sends loc_{𝔭1}[△Sh(V_n,K_n)] to loc_{w1}(s̄^c), which corresponds to loc_{w1}(s̄) under c-conjugation (𝔭1 is inert, so w1^c = w1); exponents do not increase under homomorphisms. H^{2n} is correct here because the variety is over F_{𝔭1}, not F̄_{𝔭1} (contrast E14 in Remark 7.3.5). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.3.2 — (8.12), transfer to the definite side at 𝔭1
items.statement: Similarly to Remark 6.1.5, Assumption 7.3.2 holds by Lemma 4.2.4 and (L7), so Theorem 7.3.4 applies and gives exp_λ(𝟙_{Sh(V*_n, K*_{sp,sp})}, O_E[Sh(V*_{n0},K*_{n0}) × Sh(V*_{n1},K*_{n1})]/(𝔫0, 𝔫1)) ⩾ m − m_per − 4𝔯_R (8.12) [printed with K*_sp].
items.note: Theorem 7.3.4 (second explicit reciprocity law) bounds exp_λ(loc_𝔭[Sh(V_n,K_sp)]) above by exp_λ(𝟙_{Sh(V*_n,K*_{sp,sp})}) with K*_{sp,sp} := (i_nK^p_sp) × K*_{sp,p}; for n even K*_{sp,p} = K*_{n,p} ∩ K*_{n+1,p} is smaller than K*_{n,p} (Remark 4.5.8), so the printed K*_sp = (i_nK^p_sp) × K*_{n,p} is a misprint (source issue). O_E[…]/(𝔫0,𝔫1) = O_λ[…]/(𝔫0,𝔫1) since λ^m ∈ 𝔫_α. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.3.2 — the second auxiliary prime 𝔭2 (first reciprocity law on the definite side)
items.statement: Apply §7.2 with λ, m, Σ⁺_{lr,I} = {𝔭1}, Σ⁺_I = Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_{p1}, V°_n = V*_n, K°_n = K*_n and (K°_sp, K°_{n+1}) = (K*_{sp,sp}, K*_{n+1}) [printed (K*_sp, K*_{n+1})]. By Chebotarev choose a γ-associated place w_{2+}^{(m)} of F_+^{(m)} with Ψ_{w_2^{(m)}} = Ψ2 whose underlying prime 𝔭2 (rational prime p2 ≠ p1) is special inert and satisfies (PI1)–(PI7) and (PI8): H^{2r1}_ét(Sh(V_{n1},K_{n1})_{F̄}, O_λ(r1))/(𝕋^{Σ⁺_I∪Σ⁺_{p2}}_{n1} ∩ ker φ_{Π1}) → H^{2r1}_ét(Sh(V_{n1},K_{n1})_{F̄}, O_λ(r1))/ker φ_{Π1} is an isomorphism.
items.note: §7.2's conditions at Σ⁺_{lr,I} = {𝔭1}: ℓ ∤ p1(p1²−1) ((PII2)), (V*_{n0})_{𝔭1} non-split and (K*_{n0})_{𝔭1} special maximal (definite uniformization datum), (K°_sp)_{𝔭1} ⊆ (K°_n)_{𝔭1}. The (PI6) nontriviality comes from (8.12). Here 𝔫_α := 𝕋^{Σ⁺_I∪Σ⁺_{p2}}_{n_α} ∩ ker(… → O_E/λ^m) is smaller than in (8.12), so (8.12) persists for the new quotient. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.3.2 — claim (8.13)–(8.14): the class c2
items.statement: There is c2 ∈ H¹(F, R̄^{(m)c}) such that (8.13) exp_λ(∂_{𝔭2} loc_{𝔭2}(c2), H¹_sing(F_{𝔭2}, R̄^{(m)c})) ⩾ m − m_per − 4𝔯_R − m_lat, and (8.14) loc_w(c2) ∈ H¹_ns(F_w, R̄^{(m)c}) for every nonarchimedean place w of F not above Σ⁺ ∪ {𝔭1, 𝔭2}.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 8.3.2, (8.13)–(8.14) and footnote 34, published p. 319
items.note: Proof: by Remarks 4.4.8 and 4.5.8 there is an isomorphism U((V°_{n1})^∞) ≅ U(V_{n1}^∞) sending K°_{n1} = K*_{n1} to K_{n1} (n1 odd: K*_{n1,𝔭1} stabilizes a p1-modular lattice and corresponds to the hyperspecial K_{n1,𝔭1}), so the argument for c1 (Theorem 8.2.2) applies with (8.12) replacing (8.3), m_lat of def-m-lat-rank1, and the fact that ρ̄_{Π0,λ,+} is rigid for (Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_{lr,I}) = (Σ⁺_min, {𝔭1}) — which follows from (L6) together with (PII4) (Definition 6.3.3(2) at 𝔭1), not spelled out. Footnote 34: when F⁺ ≠ ℚ, Sh′_{n0}, Sh′_{n1} have proper smooth reduction at every place above Σ⁺_{p1} ∖ {𝔭1} (Remark 5.2.8); this is needed for (8.14) there, so Σ⁺ must mean Σ⁺_min. The ℓ-adic case of (8.14) has the same justification gap as (8.5). Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 8.3.2 — the rank-one pairing computation
items.statement: Replace s2 by its image in H¹(F, R̄^{(m)}) [printed H¹_f(F, R̄^{(m)})] and identify R̄^{(m)c} with (R̄^{(m)})^*(1) via Ξ. For the local Tate pairings ⟨s2, c2⟩_w: (i) w above Σ⁺_min: loc_w(s2) = 0 by the choice of S, so ⟨s2,c2⟩_w = 0; (ii) w above Σ⁺_ℓ: R_ℚ is crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights in [−n, n−1] [printed [1−n, n], E15], loc_w(s2) ∈ H¹_ns(F_w, R̄^{(m)}) (Lemma 2.4.3(2), (L1)), and by (8.14), Lemma 2.2.7, (L1): λ^{m_dif}⟨s2,c2⟩_w = 0; (iii) w not above Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_ℓ ∪ {𝔭1, 𝔭2}: R unramified, loc_w(s2) ∈ H¹_ns (Lemma 2.4.3(1)), (8.14) and Lemma 2.2.3 give 0; (iv) w above 𝔭1: loc_w(s2) = 0 (Proposition 2.6.7), so 0; (v) w above 𝔭2: exp_λ(loc_w(s2), H¹_ns(F_w, R̄^{(m)})) ⩾ m − m_Σ − 4𝔯_R (Proposition 2.6.7), so by (8.13) exp_λ(⟨s2,c2⟩_w, O_λ/λ^m) ⩾ m − m_per − m_lat − m_Σ − 8𝔯_R. If m > m_per + m_lat + m_Σ + 8𝔯_R + m_dif this contradicts Σ_w ⟨s2,c2⟩_w = 0.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 8.3.2, pairing computation, published pp. 319–320
items.note: Checked line by line: (m − m_Σ − 4𝔯_R) + (m − m_per − 4𝔯_R − m_lat) − m = m − m_per − m_lat − m_Σ − 8𝔯_R. Steps (iv) and (v) need only the one-sided element t of basis-8-11 (loc_{w1}(t) = 0, exp loc_{w2}(t) ⩾ m − m_Σ − 4𝔯_R), so E2 does not change the threshold. As in rank 0, (v) uses perfectness of H¹_ns × H¹_sing at 𝔭2 (std-local-tate-duality), and the contradiction uses std-global-reciprocity. c2 may be ramified at 𝔭1 (level K*_{n,𝔭1}), which is why loc_{w1}(s2) = 0 is needed. Missing: routed to the Part II ArithmeticLevelRaisingAndBipartiteEulerSystems (route 18).

items.name: Global Gan–Gross–Prasad for U(n) × U(n+1) [6, Theorem 1.8, Remark 4.17] (as used)
items.statement: Let Π0, Π1 be relevant (conjugate self-dual, cuspidal, regular algebraic of the prescribed weights) representations of GL_{n0}(𝔸_F), GL_{n1}(𝔸_F). If L(1/2, Π0 × Π1) ≠ 0, then there are hermitian spaces V_n ⊂ V_{n+1} = (V_n)_♯ over F, lattices and open compact subgroups of the shape in Lemma 8.2.1 (hyperspecial outside Σ⁺_min), and a cuspidal automorphic representation π of U(V_n) × U(V_{n+1}) with BC(π) = Π0 ⊠ Π1 whose diagonal U(V_n)-period is nonzero on a vector fixed by that level; for relevant Π both spaces are standard definite, so the period is the finite sum of Lemma 8.2.1.
items.locator: Cited in the proof of Lemma 8.2.1, published p. 308
items.note: Cited, not proved (direction (1)⇒(2) of [6, Theorem 1.8]; [6, Remark 4.17] controls the level). The hypotheses are met by Remark 1.1.4. Missing: routed to the new roadmap GanGrossPrasadConjecturesForClassicalGroups (route 17).

items.name: Companion paper [51] (as used): rigidity and residual irreducibility for almost all λ
items.statement: (i) [51, Corollary 4.1.2]: in the situation of Lemma 8.1.3 (symmetric powers of a non-CM elliptic curve), ρ̄_{Π0,λ,+} is rigid for (Σ⁺_min, ∅) for all but finitely many ℓ. (ii) [51, Proposition 4.2.3(1)]: if Π_{α,w_α} is supercuspidal at some nonarchimedean w_α, then ρ_{Π_α,λ} is residually absolutely irreducible for all but finitely many λ. (iii) [51, Theorem 4.2.6]: if Π_{0,w_0} is supercuspidal at some nonarchimedean w_0, then (L6) holds for all but finitely many λ.
items.locator: Cited in the proofs of Lemmas 8.1.3 and 8.1.4, published p. 304
items.note: Cited black boxes from the companion paper Liu–Tian–Xiao–Zhang–Zhu, 'Deformation of rigid conjugate self-dual Galois representations' (arXiv:2108.06998v1); statements paraphrased from how they are used ('rigid' is Definition 6.3.3, taken from [51, §3.6], with minimally ramified lifts [51, Definition 3.4.8]). In arXiv v1 the corresponding results were Appendix E (Proposition E.5.12, Lemma E.8.3, Theorem E.8.4). Missing: routed to the Part II PolarizedAutomorphyLifting (route 15).

items.name: Arthur–Clozel base change [1] (as used in Corollary 8.2.3)
items.statement: For a cyclic (in particular quadratic) extension F/F⁺, a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_N(𝔸_{F⁺}) has an automorphic base change to GL_N(𝔸_F); in Corollary 8.2.3 this makes Sym^{n_α−1}A_{α,F} modular, and the base change is cuspidal because its Galois representation is irreducible.
items.locator: Cited in the proof of Corollary 8.2.3, published p. 313
items.note: Cited, not proved; also underlies the Newton–Thorne consequence over solvable F⁺ in Remark 8.2.4. Planned: EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.7a plans the unitary-to-GL base-change character identities.

items.name: Inputs for Hypothesis 3.2.10 via Proposition 3.2.11 (as used in Corollary 8.2.3)
items.statement: Hypothesis 3.2.10 (for standard indefinite V of rank N and π with BC(π) relevant and ρ_{BC(π)} irreducible, W^{N−1}(π) ≅ ρ^c_{BC(π),ι_ℓ}) holds for N = 1 (canonical models), N = 2 ([48, Theorem D.6(2)]), N = 3 when F⁺ = ℚ ([64]), and N ⩾ 3 when F⁺ ≠ ℚ ([37], announced as in preparation).
items.locator: Proposition 3.2.11 (published p. 146), invoked in the proof of Corollary 8.2.3, published p. 314
items.note: Cited black boxes. Corollary 8.2.3 (and hence Theorem 1.1.1) for F⁺ ≠ ℚ, including n = 2 (N = 3), depends on [37], listed in the bibliography as 'Kisin, Shin, Zhu: Cohomology of certain Shimura varieties of abelian type (temporary title) (in preparation)'. Missing: routed to a source of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII (route 5).

items.name: Local Tate duality for unramified classes (used implicitly)
items.statement: Let w be a nonarchimedean place of F not above ℓ and M a finite O_λ[Γ_{F_w}]-module unramified at w. Under the local Tate pairing ⟨ , ⟩_w: H¹(F_w, M) × H¹(F_w, M^*(1)) → E_λ/O_λ, H¹_ns(F_w, M) and H¹_ns(F_w, M^*(1)) are exact annihilators of each other, so ⟨ , ⟩_w induces a perfect pairing H¹_ns(F_w, M) × H¹_sing(F_w, M^*(1)) → E_λ/O_λ.
items.locator: Used (not cited) in the 𝔭-bullet of the proof of Theorem 8.2.2 (p. 311) and the 𝔭2-bullet of Theorem 8.3.2 (p. 320)
items.note: Standard. The paper cites only Lemma 2.2.3 (vanishing on H¹_ns × H¹_ns). With H¹_ns(F_w, R̄^{(m)}) ≅ (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ} and H¹_sing(F_w, R̄^{(m)*}(1)) its dual, both free of rank one over O_λ/λ^m, one gets exp⟨x, y⟩ ⩾ exp x + exp y − m, which is the displayed bound. Planned: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L1 plans local and global duality (local Tate pairings and Euler characteristics imported from ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02).

items.name: Global reciprocity for local Tate pairings (used implicitly)
items.statement: For a finite O_λ[Γ_F]-module M, s ∈ H¹(F, M) and c ∈ H¹(F, M^*(1)), Σ_w ⟨loc_w s, loc_w c⟩_w = 0, the sum over all places w of F (almost all terms vanish; archimedean terms vanish since F is totally imaginary).
items.locator: Used at the end of the proofs of Theorems 8.2.2 (p. 312) and 8.3.2 (p. 320)
items.note: Standard (reciprocity law for the Brauer group / Poitou–Tate), invoked as 'the relation Σ_w ⟨s1, c1⟩_w = 0'. Planned: ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4 plans Poitou–Tate duality with the local invariant maps and their sum.

items.name: Appendix A setup — σ-sesquilinear pairs and right orthogonal complements
items.statement: Fix a prime p and a field κ ⊇ F_{p²}; σ denotes the absolute p-power Frobenius (of κ and of κ-schemes). A pair (V, { , }) consists of a finite-dimensional κ-vector space V and a (not necessarily non-degenerate) pairing { , }: V × V → κ that is (κ,σ)-linear in the first variable ({ax, y} = a^p{x, y}) and κ-linear in the second. For a κ-scheme S put V_S := V ⊗_κ O_S; there is a unique pairing { , }_S: V_S × V_S → O_S extending { , } that is (O_S,σ)-linear in the first and O_S-linear in the second variable. For a subbundle H ⊆ V_S, H^⊣ ⊆ V_S denotes its right orthogonal complement {y : {H, y}_S = 0}; V^⊣ is the right radical. The left orthogonal complement {x : {x, H} = 0} is written H^⊢ (used from Proposition A.1.5 on; the pair of symbols (⊢,⊣) is formally introduced in the proof of Proposition A.2.4).
items.locator: Appendix A preamble and §A.1 before Definition A.1.1, published p. 321 (H^⊢: p. 323, p. 327)
items.note: Convention: σ-linear in the FIRST variable. H^⊣ is a subbundle only under rank conditions; for H ⊇ V^⊣ in an admissible pair, rank H^⊣ = N − rank H + d. In the non-degenerate case ⊢(H^⊣) = H, so H^⊣ ⊆ H ⟺ H^⊢ ⊆ H (checked; needed for the quotients H/H^⊢ in A.1.5 and A.2.4). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition A.1.1 — admissible pair
items.statement: A pair (V, { , }) is admissible if there exists an F_{p²}-linear subspace V_0 ⊆ V_κ̄ such that the induced map V_0 ⊗_{F_{p²}} κ̄ → V_κ̄ is an isomorphism, and {x, y} = −{y, x}^σ for every x, y ∈ V_0.
items.note: The condition forces {x,y} = {x,y}^{p²} ∈ F_{p²} on V_0, so { , }|V_0 is an F_{p²}/F_p skew-Hermitian form. By Lang's theorem (the map g ↦ σ(g)ᵗJ_0g is onto GL_N(κ̄)) every non-degenerate pair is admissible; admissibility constrains only the radical (left and right radicals correspond). The earlier paraphrase 'retain the radical dimension d' is not part of the definition (d := dim V^⊣ is introduced in Proposition A.1.3). V_0 need not be defined over κ: κ-forms of an admissible pair are twisted by U_N(F_p) (relevant for Source issue E9). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition A.1.2 — unitary Deligne–Lusztig variety DL(V,{ , },h)
items.statement: For a pair (V, { , }) and an integer h, DL(V, { , }, h) is the presheaf on Sch/κ such that, for every S ∈ Sch/κ, DL(V, { , }, h)(S) is the set of subbundles H ⊆ V_S of rank h such that H^⊣ ⊆ H. It is called the (unitary) Deligne–Lusztig variety attached to (V, { , }) of rank h.
items.note: A closed sub-presheaf of the Grassmannian Gr(V,h) (representability in Proposition A.1.3(2)). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proposition A.1.3(1) — emptiness of DL(V,{ , },h)
items.statement: Let (V, { , }) be an admissible pair, N := dim_κ V, d := dim_κ V^⊣. If 2h < N + d or h > N, then DL(V, { , }, h) is empty.
items.note: 'Obvious from the definitions': for H in DL, V^⊣ ⊆ H^⊣ ⊆ H and rank H^⊣ = N − h + d, so N − h + d ≤ h. Checked. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proposition A.1.3(2) — smoothness, dimension and tangent sheaf of DL(V,{ , },h)
items.statement: Let (V, { , }) be admissible, N := dim_κ V, d := dim_κ V^⊣. If N + d ≤ 2h ≤ 2N, then DL(V, { , }, h) is represented by a projective smooth scheme over κ of dimension (2h − N − d)(N − h), with a canonical isomorphism T_{DL(V,{ , },h)/κ} ≃ Hom(ℋ/ℋ^⊣, V_{DL(V,{ , },h)}/ℋ), where ℋ ⊆ V_{DL(V,{ , },h)} is the universal subbundle.
items.note: Proof: closed sub-presheaf of Gr(V,h); for a square-zero thickening S ⊆ Ŝ (ideal I, I² = 0, hence I^p = 0) Ĥ^⊣ depends only on H because σ kills I, so the lifts of H in DL form a torsor under Hom(H/H^⊣, (V_S/H) ⊗ I) ⊆ Hom(H, (V_S/H) ⊗ I). Rank (2h−N−d)(N−h) checked. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proposition A.1.3(3) — geometric irreducibility of DL(V,{ , },h)
items.statement: Let (V, { , }) be admissible, N := dim_κ V, d := dim_κ V^⊣. If N + d < 2h ≤ 2N, then DL(V, { , }, h) is geometrically irreducible.
items.note: Proof: reduce to κ = κ̄ and DL(V,{ , },h) ≃ DL(V_0,{ , }_0,h) ⊗_{F_{p²}} κ; for d = 0 cite [8, Theorem 1] (Bonnafé–Rouquier irreducibility criterion for Deligne–Lusztig varieties; the identification of DL(V_0,h) with (the closure of) a suitable fine DL variety is left implicit); for d > 0 pass to V_0' := V_0/V_0^⊣ via H ↦ H/V^⊣_{0S}. The printed target DL(V_0', { , }_0', h) should be DL(V_0', { , }_0', h − d) (Source issue E11). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma A.1.4(1) — DL(V,{ , },N−1) is a hypersurface of degree p+1
items.statement: Consider a pair (V, { , }) with dim_κ V = N ≥ 2 and dim_κ V^⊣ = 0, and a p-coprime coefficient ring L in which p + 1 is invertible. Then the subscheme DL(V, { , }, N − 1) is a hypersurface in P(V) (= Gr(V, N−1), hyperplanes) of degree p + 1.
items.note: Printed as 'Lemma' (an earlier version of this extraction called it Proposition A.1.4). Admissibility is not assumed in the statement but is automatic for non-degenerate pairs (Lang). In coordinates {x,y} = σ(x)ᵗJy and H = ker(a), the condition H^⊣ ⊆ H is aᵗJ^{-1}σ(a) = 0 (checked), a Hermitian (Fermat-type) hypersurface; the hypotheses on L are irrelevant for (1). A p-coprime coefficient ring is a finite ring with p invertible, a finite extension of Q_ℓ or its ring of integers with ℓ ≠ p (§1.3, p. 118). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma A.1.4(2) — cohomology of DL(V,{ , },N−1) away from the middle degree
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma A.1.4 (dim_κ V = N ≥ 2, V^⊣ = 0, L p-coprime with p + 1 ∈ L^×), the restriction map H^i_ét(P(V)_κ̄, L) → H^i_ét(DL(V, { , }, N − 1)_κ̄, L) induced by the inclusion DL(V, { , }, N − 1) → P(V) is an isomorphism for every i ∉ {N − 2, 2N − 2}.
items.note: Proof: for N ≥ 3, S := DL(V,{ , },N−1) is a geometrically connected smooth hypersurface (A.1.3); weak Lefschetz gives isomorphisms for 0 ≤ i ≤ N−3; the Gysin map H^i(S) → H^{i+2}(P(V))(1) is an isomorphism for N−1 ≤ i ≤ 2(N−2), and the composite restriction∘Gysin is cup product with c_1(O(p+1)), invertible for i ≠ 2N−2 since p+1 ∈ L^×. N = 2 is trivial for this part. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma A.1.4(3) — freeness of the cohomology of DL(V,{ , },N−1)
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma A.1.4, for every i ∈ Z, H^i_ét(DL(V, { , }, N − 1)_κ̄, L) is a free L-module.
items.note: 'Immediate consequence of (2)': for i ≠ N−2 from (2); for i = N−2 one also needs that the torsion of H^{N−2}(S, Z_ℓ) is dual to that of H^{N−1}(S, Z_ℓ) ≅ H^{N−1}(P, Z_ℓ) (free) and universal coefficients — not spelled out but standard. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Lemma A.1.4(4) — Galois action on the middle cohomology (as printed; false in this generality)
items.statement: As printed: under the hypotheses of Lemma A.1.4, when N is even, the action of Gal(κ̄/κ) on H^{N−2}_ét(DL(V, { , }, N − 1)_κ̄, L((N−2)/2)) is trivial. Valid form: this holds when the pair has an F_{p²}-structure defined over κ, i.e. V = V_0 ⊗_{F_{p²}} κ with {x,y} = −{y,x}^σ on V_0 (then H^{N−2} is spanned by Tate cycles defined over F_{p²} ⊆ κ); for general κ-forms (twisted by U_N(F_p)) it fails, already for N = 2 (Source issue E9).
items.note: Proof in the paper: reduce to L = Q_ℓ by (3), then 'it is well-known that H^{N−2} … is spanned by Tate cycles over κ (see, for example, [31])' (Hotta–Matsui). The N = 2 case is declared trivial but is exactly where the counterexample lives. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proposition A.1.5 — top Chern number on DL(V,{ , },r+1) for dim V = 2r+1 (cited)
items.statement: Suppose κ is algebraically closed. Let (V, { , }) be an admissible pair over κ with dim_κ V = 2r + 1 for some integer r ≥ 1 and dim_κ V^⊣ = 0, and let ℋ be the universal object over DL(V, { , }, r + 1). Then ∫_{DL(V,{ , },r+1)} c_r((σ*ℋ^⊢) ⊗_{O_{DL(V,{ , },r+1)}} (ℋ/ℋ^⊢)) = d_{r,p}, where d_{r,p} := Σ_{δ=0}^{r} (−1)^δ (2δ+1) p^{δ(δ+1)} [2r+1, r−δ]_{−p} (Notation 1.3.1).
items.note: Cited, not proved: 'This is [75, Proposition 9.3.10]' (Xiao–Zhu, Cycles on Shimura varieties via geometric Satake). DL(V,{ , },r+1) is smooth irreducible of dimension r; ℋ^⊢ ⊆ ℋ because ℋ^⊣ ⊆ ℋ. Sanity check r = 1 (Hermitian plane curve of degree p+1): c_1 = (p−1)c_1(ℋ^⊢) + c_1(ℋ) has degree −(p+1)(p−1) − p(p+1) = 1 − p − 2p² = d_{1,p}. Added in arXiv v3 (v1/v2 cite [XZ, Prop. 9.3.10] inside the proof of A.2.4). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Construction A.1.6 — special morphism δ↑ between DL varieties when the rank increases
items.statement: Let (V, { , }) be admissible with dim_κ V = n ≥ 1 and dim V^⊣ = n + 1 − 2⌊(n+1)/2⌋. Put V♯ := V ⊕ κ1 and extend { , } to a pairing { , }♯ on V♯ with {1, 1}♯ = 0 (orthogonal sum). Let (V♮, { , }♮) be another admissible pair with dim_κ V♮ = n + 1 and dim V♮^⊣ = n − 2⌊n/2⌋, together with a κ-linear map δ: V♯ → V♮ of corank dim V^⊣ such that {δ(x), δ(y)}♮ = {x, y}♯ for all x, y ∈ V♯. Define δ↑: DL(V, { , }, ⌈(n+1)/2⌉) → DL(V♮, { , }♮, ⌈(n+2)/2⌉) by H ↦ δ(H ⊕ O_S1). δ↑ is called a special morphism.
items.note: Numbered Construction A.1.5 in arXiv v1/v2. The orthogonality {V,1}♯ = 0 is implicit in 'extend'. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proposition A.1.7 — the special morphism is a regular embedding
items.statement: In Construction A.1.6, the morphism δ↑ is well defined and is a regular embedding; when n is odd, δ is an isomorphism and δ↑ is an isomorphism.
items.note: n even: δ has corank 1 and ker δ ⊆ V♯^⊣ = V^⊣ ⊕ κ1 ⊆ H ⊕ O_S1, so δ(H ⊕ O_S1) has rank ⌈(n+1)/2⌉ = ⌈(n+2)/2⌉; δ(H^⊣ ⊕ O_S1) ⊆ δ(H ⊕ O_S1)^⊣ with equality by rank n/2; the image is the closed locus (δκ1)_S ⊆ H♮ ⊆ (δV♯)_S, and δ↑ is a closed immersion of smooth schemes (A.1.3(2)). Checked. Typo 'well-defined an is'. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Definition A.2.1 — the variety DL•(V,{ , })
items.statement: For a pair (V, { , }) with dim_κ V = N, DL•(V, { , }) is the presheaf on Sch/κ such that DL•(V, { , })(S) is the set of pairs (H_1, H_2) of subbundles of V_S of ranks ⌈N/2⌉ and ⌈N/2⌉ − 1 respectively, satisfying V_S^⊣ ⊆ H_2 ⊆ H_1, H_2 ⊆ H_1^⊣, H_1 ⊆ H_2^⊣ (and hence H_1^⊣ ⊆ H_2^⊣).
items.note: The inclusions are given by a diamond diagram on p. 325. H_2 ⊆ H_1^⊣ is equivalent to H_1 ⊆ H_2^⊢. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).
