items.name: Proposition A.2.2(1) — emptiness of DL•
items.statement: Let (V, { , }) be admissible, N := dim_κ V, d := dim_κ V^⊣. If d ≥ ⌈N/2⌉, then DL•(V, { , }) is empty.
items.note: V^⊣ ⊆ H_2 of rank ⌈N/2⌉ − 1. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proposition A.2.2(2) — smoothness and tangent sequence of DL•
items.statement: Let (V, { , }) be admissible, N := dim_κ V, d := dim_κ V^⊣. If d ≤ ⌈N/2⌉ − 1, then DL•(V, { , }) is represented by a projective smooth scheme over κ whose tangent sheaf fits canonically into an exact sequence 0 → Hom(ℋ_1/ℋ_2, ℋ_2^⊣/ℋ_1) → T_{DL•(V,{ , })/κ} → Hom(ℋ_2/V^⊣_{DL•(V,{ , })}, ℋ_1^⊣/ℋ_2) → 0, where V^⊣_{DL•} ⊆ ℋ_2 ⊆ ℋ_1 ⊆ V_{DL•} are the universal subbundles.
items.note: Closed in Gr(V,⌈N/2⌉) × Gr(V,⌈N/2⌉−1); lifts of H_2 form a torsor under Hom(H_2/V^⊣, (H_1^⊣/H_2) ⊗ I) (Ĥ_1^⊣ depends only on H_1), then lifts of H_1 a torsor under Hom(H_1/H_2, (H_2^⊣/H_1) ⊗ I). Rank count (not stated in the paper): dim = (N − 2⌈N/2⌉ + 1 + d)(⌈N/2⌉ − d), i.e. r for (N,d) = (2r,0) or (2r+1,1), and 0 for (2r+1,0). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proposition A.2.2(3) — irreducibility and dimension of DL•
items.statement: Let (V, { , }) be admissible, N := dim_κ V, d := dim_κ V^⊣. If N ≥ 2 and d = N − 2⌊N/2⌋, then DL•(V, { , }) is geometrically irreducible of dimension ⌊N/2⌋.
items.note: Proof: as for A.1.3(3), reduce (via V/V^⊣) to N even, d = 0, then 'follows again by [8, Theorem 1]'. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Construction A.2.3 — special morphism δ↑ for DL•
items.statement: Let (V, { , }) be admissible with dim_κ V = n ≥ 2 and dim_κ V^⊣ = n − 2⌊n/2⌋. Put V♯ := V ⊕ κ1 and extend { , } to { , }♯ on V♯ with {1, 1}♯ = 0. Let (V♮, { , }♮) be admissible with dim_κ V♮ = n + 1 and dim V♮^⊣ = n + 1 − 2⌊(n+1)/2⌋, and δ: V♯ → V♮ a κ-linear map of corank dim V^⊣ with {δ(x), δ(y)}♮ = {x, y}♯ for all x, y ∈ V♯. Then there is a morphism δ↑: DL•(V, { , }) → DL•(V♮, { , }♮), (H_1, H_2) ↦ (δ(H_1 ⊕ O_S1), δ(H_2 ⊕ O_S1)), and it is a regular embedding.
items.note: 'Similar to Construction A.1.6 and Proposition A.1.7'; no separate proof. Rank bookkeeping checked for n even (δ an isomorphism) and n odd (corank 1, ker δ ⊆ V^⊣ ⊕ κ1 ⊆ H_2 ⊕ O_S1). Added in arXiv v3. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proposition A.2.4(1) — intersection number on DL• for dim V = 2r+1, dim V^⊣ = 1
items.statement: Suppose κ is algebraically closed, (V, { , }) is admissible over κ, and (ℋ_1, ℋ_2) is the universal object over DL•(V, { , }). If dim_κ V = 2r + 1 for some integer r ≥ 1 and dim_κ V^⊣ = 1, then ∫_{DL•(V,{ , })} c_r((σ*ℋ_2) ⊗_{O_{DL•(V,{ , })}} (ℋ_1^⊣/ℋ_2)) = d•_{r,p}, where d•_{r,p} := (1/(p+1)) (d_{r,p} + (((−p)^{r+1} − 1)/(p+1)) (p+1)(p³+1)⋯(p^{2r−1}+1)) and d_{r,p} is as in Proposition A.1.5 (Notation 1.3.1).
items.note: DL• is irreducible of dimension r (A.2.2). Proof: DL•(V) ≃ DL•(V̄) for V̄ := V/V^⊣ via (H_1,H_2) ↦ (H_1/V^⊣, H_2/V^⊣), and σ*ℋ_2 is an extension of σ*ℋ̄_2 by the trivial bundle σ*V^⊣, so c_r(σ*ℋ_2 ⊗ Q) = c_{r−1}(σ*ℋ̄_2 ⊗ Q)·c_1(Q) with Q = ℋ_1^⊣/ℋ_2 = ℋ̄_1^⊣/ℋ̄_2; then apply (2). For r = 1 the integral is deg(ℋ̄_1^⊣) = −p = d•_{1,p} (checked). Used in the proof of Proposition 5.8.6 (published p. 228). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proposition A.2.4(2) — intersection number on DL• for dim V = 2r, V non-degenerate
items.statement: Suppose κ is algebraically closed, (V, { , }) is admissible over κ, and (ℋ_1, ℋ_2) is the universal object over DL•(V, { , }). If dim_κ V = 2r for some integer r ≥ 1 and dim_κ V^⊣ = 0, then ∫_{DL•(V,{ , })} c_{r−1}((σ*ℋ_2) ⊗_{O_{DL•(V,{ , })}} (ℋ_1^⊣/ℋ_2)) · c_1(ℋ_1^⊣/ℋ_2) = d•_{r,p} (Notation 1.3.1).
items.note: Proof via the correspondence DL(V♯) ← DL~(V) → DL•(V) (items constr-a-2-4-correspondence … formula-a-2-4-chern) and Proposition A.1.5. All Chern-class algebra re-derived and correct; the identification of π with a blow-up is asserted without proof (Source issue, gap). r = 1: DL• = P(V), integrand c_1(ℋ_1^⊣) of degree −p = d•_{1,p}. The value d•_{r,p} is corroborated by Proposition B.3.5(3), whose clean factorisation requires exactly these numbers. Used in the proof of Proposition 5.8.9 (published p. 231), eq. (5.20). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proof of Proposition A.2.4(2) — the correspondence DL(V♯) ← DL~(V) → DL•(V)
items.statement: Let κ = κ̄, dim V = 2r, V^⊣ = 0. Put V♯ := V ⊕ κ1 with {1,1}♯ = 1 (orthogonal sum) and DL(V♯) := DL(V♯, { , }♯, r + 1); write (⊢,⊣) for left/right orthogonal complements in V and (⊨,⫤) for those in V♯. For a κ-scheme S, DL~(V)(S) is the set of pairs (H, H_2) with H ∈ DL(V♯)(S) and H_2 ⊆ H^⊨ a subbundle of rank r − 1 contained in V_S; π(H, H_2) := H; π•(H, H_2) := (H_1, H_2) with H_1 := (H ∩ V_S)^⊢. Then π• is well defined, i.e. H_1 is a rank-r subbundle of V_S, H_2 ⊆ H_1, H_1 ⊆ H_2^⊢ and H_1 ⊆ H_2^⊣, so (H_1,H_2) ∈ DL•(V)(S). Universal objects: ℋ over DL(V♯), (ℋ~, ℋ~_2) over DL~(V) with ℋ~ = π*ℋ, ℋ~_2 = π•*ℋ_2.
items.locator: §A.2, proof of Proposition A.2.4(2), published p. 327
items.note: The rank-r claim uses that H → V♯_S → O_S1 is surjective (else H_s ⊆ V_s at a geometric point, contradicting 1 ∈ H_s^⫤ ⊆ H_s). V♯ is admissible (rescale 1 by a with a^{p+1} = c, c^{p−1} = −1). All four bullet checks re-derived. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proof of Proposition A.2.4(2) — special points, the blow-up π and the divisor E, (A.1)
items.statement: A point s ∈ DL(V♯)(κ) represented by H_s is special if H_s^⊨ is a maximal isotropic subspace of V with H_s^⫤ = H_s^⊨. There are exactly (p+1)(p³+1)⋯(p^{2r−1}+1) special points; DL(V♯)' denotes their locus. For every S → DL(V♯) \ DL(V♯)', π^{-1}(S) is a singleton; for s special, π^{-1}(s) = P(H_s^⊨) ≃ P^{r−1}_κ; π is the blow-up of DL(V♯) along DL(V♯)' with exceptional divisor E ⊆ DL~(V) (so π is projective), E is exactly the zero locus of the projection ℋ~^⊨/ℋ~_2 → O_{DL~(V)}1 ⊆ O_{DL~(V)} ⊗_κ V♯, and (A.1) ℋ~^⊨/ℋ~_2 ≃ O_{DL~(V)}(−E).
items.locator: §A.2, proof of Proposition A.2.4(2), published pp. 327–328, eq. (A.1)
items.note: Special ⟺ 1 ∈ H ⟺ H^⊨ ⊆ V (checked); special points ↔ F_{p²}-rational Lagrangians of V_0, counted by ∏_{i=1}^r (p^{2i−1}+1). 'In particular, π is a blow-up' is not justified beyond the fibre description (Source issue, gap). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proof of Proposition A.2.4(2) — π• is generically finite of degree p+1
items.statement: For s ∈ DL•(V)(κ) represented by (H_{1s}, H_{2s}), the fibre {s} ×_{DL•(V)} DL~(V) classifies subbundles H ⊆ V♯ ⊗ O_S with H_{2s} ⊗ O_S ⊆ H^⊨ ⊆ H_{1s} ⊗ O_S ⊕ O_S1 and H^⊨ ⊆ H. With the induced pairing { , }_s on (H_{1s} ⊕ κ1)/H_{2s} (σ-linear in the first, linear in the second variable), the fibre is a disjoint union of p + 1 copies of Spec κ when { , }_s is perfect; { , }_s fails to be perfect iff H_1^⊣ = H_1, and that locus is a finite union of P^{r−1}_κ. Hence π• is generically finite of degree p + 1.
items.locator: §A.2, proof of Proposition A.2.4(2), published p. 328
items.note: The generic fibre is the set of isotropic lines of a non-degenerate 2-dimensional σ-sesquilinear space (p+1 points). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proof of Proposition A.2.4(2) — the bundles ℰ, ℰ•, the line bundle ℒ and (A.2)
items.statement: Put ℰ := (σ*ℋ^⊨) ⊗_{O_{DL(V♯)}} (ℋ/ℋ^⊨) on DL(V♯) (rank r) and ℰ• := (σ*ℋ_2) ⊗_{O_{DL•(V)}} (ℋ_1^⊣/ℋ_2) on DL•(V) (rank r − 1). Then ℒ := π•*(ℋ_1^⊣/ℋ_2) = (ℋ~ ∩ V_{DL~(V)})/ℋ~_2 and (A.2) ℒ ≃ O_{DL~(V)}(−E) ⊗ (ℋ~/ℋ~^⊨). Moreover ℒ|_E ≃ O_E(−E) = O_E(1); ℋ~_2|_E is the tautological rank-(r−1) subbundle, 0 → ℋ~_2|_E → O_E^{⊕r} → O_E(1) → 0; and ℱ := π•*ℰ•|_E = (σ*ℋ~_2|_E) ⊗ ℒ|_E fits into 0 → ℱ → O_E(1)^{⊕r} → O_E(p+1) → 0.
items.locator: §A.2, proof of Proposition A.2.4(2), published pp. 328–330, eq. (A.2)
items.note: (A.2) follows from the map of short exact sequences 0→ℋ~_2→ℋ~^⊨→O(−E)→0 into 0→ℋ~∩V→ℋ~→O·1→0 and the snake lemma (checked). O_E(−E) = O_E(1) uses the blow-up structure of π. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: Proof of Proposition A.2.4(2) — Chern class computation (A.3)–(A.5)
items.locator: §A.2, proof of Proposition A.2.4(2), published pp. 329–330, eqs. (A.3)–(A.5)
items.note: Uses π*c_r(ℰ) = c_{r−1}(π•*ℰ• ⊗ O(E))·c_1(ℒ((1−p)E)) (filtration σ*ℋ~_2 ⊂ σ*ℋ~^⊨ with quotient O(−pE)), deg π = 1, deg π• = p+1, c(ℱ(−1)) = (1+pη)^{-1}, c(ℱ) = (1+η)^r/(1+(p+1)η), so c_{r−1}(ℱ) = (1−(−p)^r)/(p+1)·η^{r−1}; each step re-derived and correct. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 13).

items.name: §B.1 setup — X*_N, the elements 𝛍_i, 𝔰_δ and Z[X*_N]^sym
items.statement: Let N ≥ 1, r := ⌊N/2⌋. GL_N is the group scheme over Z of automorphisms of Z^{⊕N}, T_N ⊆ GL_N the diagonal torus, X*_N := Hom(T_N, G_m) = ⊕_{i=1}^N Zμ_i with μ_i the i-th projection; for μ ∈ X*_N, [μ] ∈ Z[X*_N] is the corresponding element. For 1 ≤ i ≤ r put 𝛍_i := [μ_i − μ_{N+1−i}] + [μ_{N+1−i} − μ_i] ∈ Z[X*_N]; for 0 ≤ δ ≤ r let 𝔰_δ ∈ Z[X*_N] be the elementary symmetric polynomial of degree δ in 𝛍_1, …, 𝛍_r. Z[X*_N]^sym is the subring of Z[X*_N] generated by 𝔰_1, …, 𝔰_r over Z.
items.note: Z[X*_N]^sym is the ring of hyperoctahedral invariants of Z[x_1^{±1}, …, x_r^{±1}] with x_i := [μ_i − μ_{N+1−i}]; it is a polynomial ring in 𝔰_1, …, 𝔰_r. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: §B.1 — the group GL_N^ext and twisted characters χ(ρ)
items.statement: GL_N^ext := GL_N ⋊ {1, σ}, where the involution σ sends A ∈ GL_N to Φ_N ᵗA^{−1} Φ_N^{−1}, Φ_N being the antidiagonal matrix with entries 1, −1, …, (−1)^{N−1} from the top-right to the bottom-left corner ((Φ_N)_{i,N+1−i} = (−1)^{i−1}). For every algebraic representation ρ of GL_N^ext over Z, χ(ρ) ∈ Z[X*_N] denotes the restriction of the character of ρ to T_Nσ, i.e. the function t ↦ tr ρ(tσ) on T_N.
items.note: Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: §B.1 — the representations ρ_{N;δ} = ∧^δ std ⊗ ∧^δ std^∨ of GL_N^ext
items.statement: Let ρ_{N,std} be the standard representation of GL_N with basis ε_1, …, ε_N and ρ^∨_{N,std} its dual with dual basis ε_1^∨, …, ε_N^∨. For I ⊆ {1, …, N} put ⟨I⟩ := Σ_{i∈I} i, I^∨ := {N + 1 − i | i ∈ I}, ε_I := ∧_{i∈I} ε_i and ε_I^∨ := ∧_{i∈I} ε_i^∨ (in increasing order of the indices). For 0 ≤ δ ≤ r, ρ_{N;δ} := (∧^δ ρ_{N,std}) ⊗ (∧^δ ρ^∨_{N,std}) extends uniquely to a representation of GL_N^ext such that σ sends ε_I ⊗ ε^∨_{J^∨} to (−1)^{⟨I⟩+⟨J⟩} ε_J ⊗ ε^∨_{I^∨} (|I| = |J| = δ).
items.locator: §B.1, running text before Remark B.1.1, published p. 332
items.note: An earlier version of this extraction labelled this 'Construction B.1.1'; B.1.1 is a Remark and the construction is unnumbered. Verified by computer (exact arithmetic, random integer matrices, N = 2,…,5, all 1 ≤ δ ≤ r): the operator S so defined satisfies S² = 1 and S∘ρ(A)∘S^{−1} = ρ(σ(A)). Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.statement: For the unramified unitary group U(V_N) over a nonarchimedean local field (§B.2), GL_N^ext(C) is the Langlands dual group of U(V_N), and Z[X*_N]^sym ≃ Z[X*(\widehat{U(V_N)})^σ]^{W_N}.
items.note: Interpretive remark; not used in proofs. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Lemma B.1.2 — χ(ρ_{N;δ}) in terms of 𝔰
items.statement: For 0 ≤ δ ≤ r = ⌊N/2⌋: χ(ρ_{N;δ}) = Σ_{i=0}^{δ} C(r−δ+i, ⌊i/2⌋) · 𝔰_{δ−i} if N is odd, and χ(ρ_{N;δ}) = Σ_{j=0}^{⌊δ/2⌋} C(r−δ+2j, j) · 𝔰_{δ−2j} if N is even (C = binomial coefficient). In particular χ(ρ_{N;δ}) ∈ Z[X*_N]^sym.
items.note: Proof: tσ sends ε_I ⊗ ε^∨_{J^∨} to (−1)^{⟨I⟩+⟨J⟩}∏_{i∈I^∨}μ_i(t)^{−1}∏_{j∈J}μ_j(t)·ε_J ⊗ ε^∨_{I^∨}, so χ(ρ_{N;δ})(tσ) = Σ_{|I|=δ}∏_{i∈I} μ_i(t)μ_{N+1−i}(t)^{−1}; group by |I ∩ I^∨| (even if N even). Verified by computer (sympy) for N = 1, …, 7 and all δ. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Lemma B.1.3(1) — even-rank product formula
items.statement: Suppose N = 2r is even. Then ∏_{i=1}^{r} (λ + λ^{−1} + 𝛍_i) = χ(ρ_{N;r}) + Σ_{δ=1}^{r} χ(ρ_{N;r−δ}) (λ^δ + λ^{−δ}) in Z[X*_N]^sym ⊗ Z[λ, λ^{−1}].
items.note: Proof: compare coefficients of powers of λ using Lemma B.1.2. Verified by computer for N = 2, 4, 6. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Lemma B.1.3(2) — even-rank derivative formula
items.statement: Suppose N = 2r is even. Then Σ_{j=1}^{r} ∏_{1≤i≤r, i≠j} (λ + λ^{−1} + 𝛍_i) = Σ_{δ=1}^{r} δ · χ(ρ_{N;r−δ}) (λ^δ − λ^{−δ})/(λ − λ^{−1}) in Z[X*_N]^sym ⊗ Z[λ, λ^{−1}].
items.note: Proof: differentiate (1) in λ and divide by 1 − λ^{−2}; (λ^δ − λ^{−δ})/(λ − λ^{−1}) is a Laurent polynomial. Verified by computer for N = 2, 4, 6. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Lemma B.1.4 — odd-rank product formula
items.statement: Suppose N = 2r + 1 is odd. Then ∏_{i=1}^{r} (λ + λ^{−1} + 𝛍_i) = Σ_{δ=0}^{r} χ(ρ_{N;r−δ}) (λ^{δ+1} + λ^{−δ})/(λ + 1) in Z[X*_N]^sym ⊗ Z[λ, λ^{−1}].
items.note: (λ^{δ+1} + λ^{−δ})/(λ + 1) = λ^{−δ}(λ^{2δ+1}+1)/(λ+1) is a Laurent polynomial (value (−1)^δ(2δ+1) at λ = −1, used in Lemma B.4.2). Proof: by Lemma B.1.2 reduce to Σ_{δ=0}^{k} ((λ^{δ+1}+λ^{−δ})/(λ+1)) C(k, ⌊(k−δ)/2⌋) = (λ + λ^{−1})^k for 0 ≤ k ≤ r (telescoping in pairs). Verified by computer for N = 1, 3, 5, 7. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: §B.2 setup — hermitian space V_N, lattices Λ°_N, Λ•_N, groups K°_N, K•_N and Hecke algebras 𝕋°_N, 𝕋•_N
items.statement: Fix an unramified quadratic extension F/F^+ of nonarchimedean local fields; q := residue cardinality of F^+, 𝔭 := maximal ideal of O_F. Let N ≥ 1, r := ⌊N/2⌋, V_N a hermitian space over F (w.r.t. F/F^+) of rank N with a basis {e_{−r}, …, e_r} (e_0 omitted if N is even) such that (e_{−i}, e_j)_{V_N} = δ_{ij} for 0 ≤ i, j ≤ r; this identifies U(V_N) with a closed subgroup of Res_{F/F^+}GL_N. (B.1): Λ°_N := O_Fe_{−r} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ O_Fe_r and Λ•_N := 𝔭^{−1}e_{−r} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ 𝔭^{−1}e_{−1} ⊕ O_Fe_0 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ O_Fe_r. Then (Λ°_N)^∨ = Λ°_N, 𝔭Λ•_N ⊆ (Λ•_N)^∨, and (Λ•_N)^∨/𝔭Λ•_N has length N − 2r. K°_N, K•_N ⊆ U(V_N)(F^+) are the stabilizers of Λ°_N, Λ•_N; K°_N is hyperspecial maximal, K•_N is special maximal and is hyperspecial iff N is even. 𝕋°_N := Z[K°_N\U(V_N)(F^+)/K°_N] and 𝕋•_N := Z[K•_N\U(V_N)(F^+)/K•_N] are commutative, with units 1_{K°_N}, 1_{K•_N}. A_N(F^+) (resp. A_N(O_{F^+})) is the subgroup of U(V_N)(F^+) acting on each e_i (−r ≤ i ≤ r) by a scalar in F^+ (resp. O_{F^+}).
items.note: Duality statements checked on (B.1). L^∨ := {x : (x, L) ⊆ O_F}. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Notation B.2.1 — the elements a^t, t_δ and the Hecke operators T°_{N;t}, T•_{N;t}, T°_{N;δ}, T•_{N;δ}
items.statement: For t = (t_1, …, t_N) ∈ Z^N with t_i + t_{N+1−i} = 0 and a ∈ F^× (read: a ∈ (F^+)^×), a^t ∈ A_N(F^+) is the element with a^t · e_{−i} = a^{t_{r+1−i}} e_{−i} for 0 ≤ i ≤ r (hence a^t · e_i = a^{−t_{r+1−i}} e_i). For 0 ≤ δ ≤ r put t_δ := (1^δ, 0^{N−2δ}, (−1)^δ). T°_{N;t} ∈ 𝕋°_N (resp. T•_{N;t} ∈ 𝕋•_N) is the element corresponding to the double coset K°_Nϖ^tK°_N (resp. K•_Nϖ^tK•_N) for a uniformizer ϖ; T°_{N;δ} := T°_{N;t_δ}, T•_{N;δ} := T•_{N;t_δ}.
items.note: The paper takes a ∈ F^× and 'some uniformizer ϖ of F'; for a^t to lie in A_N(F^+) one needs a ∈ F^+ (Source issue, misprint; harmless since the double cosets do not depend on the uniformizer). T°_{N;0} = 1_{K°_N}. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Remark B.2.2 — independence of the basis
items.statement: The elements T°_{N;t} ∈ 𝕋°_N and T•_{N;t} ∈ 𝕋•_N do not depend on the choice of the basis {e_{−r}, …, e_r} satisfying (B.1).
items.note: Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Definition B.2.3 — Lat°_N, Lat•_N and the mixed operators T•°_N, T°•_N
items.statement: Lat°_N is the set of all self-dual lattices in V_N; Lat•_N is the set of all lattices L in V_N with 𝔭L ⊆ L^∨ and L^∨/𝔭L of length N − 2⌊N/2⌋; T•°_N ∈ Z[K•_N\U(V_N)(F^+)/K°_N] is the characteristic function of K•_NK°_N; T°•_N ∈ Z[K°_N\U(V_N)(F^+)/K•_N] is the characteristic function of K°_NK•_N.
items.note: On functions on lattices (as used in the proof of Lemma B.2.4): (T•°f)(L•) = Σ_{L°∈Lat°, L° ⊆ L• ⊆ 𝔭^{−1}L°} f(L°) and (T°•f)(L°) = Σ_{L•∈Lat•, L° ⊆ L• ⊆ 𝔭^{−1}L°} f(L•). The K°-orbit of Λ• is {L• : Λ° ⊆ L• ⊆ 𝔭^{−1}Λ°} ↔ Lagrangians of Λ°/𝔭Λ°. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Definition B.2.3 — the intertwining Hecke operator I°_N
items.statement: I°_N := T°•_N ∘ T•°_N ∈ 𝕋°_N, the composition taken as composition of cosets.
items.note: Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: §B.2 — action of 𝕋°_N, 𝕋•_N on functions on lattices
items.statement: There are canonical injective ring homomorphisms 𝕋°_N → End_Z(Z[Lat°_N]) and 𝕋•_N → End_Z(Z[Lat•_N]) sending T^?_{N;t} to the endomorphism f ↦ T^?_{N;t}f with (T^?_{N;t}f)(L) = Σ f(L'), the sum over all L' ∈ Lat^?_N such that L' and L have relative position ϖ^t (? = °, •).
items.note: For ? = •, relative position t_δ between L•, Λ• ∈ Lat• is equivalent to (L• + Λ•)/Λ• ≃ (O_F/𝔭)^{⊕δ} (used in the proof of Lemma B.4.4). Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Lemma B.2.4 — expansion of the intertwining operator I°_N
items.note: Proof by lattice counting (item claim-b-2-4-counting). Verified independently by brute-force lattice enumeration over F = F_{q²}((t)) (equal-characteristic model) for (q,N) = (2,1),(2,2),(2,3),(2,4),(2,5),(3,2),(3,3). Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Proof of Lemma B.2.4 — the counts c_{N,δ}
items.statement: For (L_1°, L_2°) ∈ (Lat°_N)² with 𝔭L_2° ⊆ L_1° ⊆ 𝔭^{−1}L_2°, let Disc(L_1°, L_2°) be the sum of the lengths of L_1°/(L_1° ∩ L_2°) and L_2°/(L_1° ∩ L_2°) (∈ {0, 2, …, 2r}) and Lat•_N(L_1°, L_2°) := {L• ∈ Lat•_N | L_1° ⊆ L• ⊆ 𝔭^{−1}L_1°, L_2° ⊆ L• ⊆ 𝔭^{−1}L_2°}. Its cardinality c_{N,δ} depends only on Disc = 2δ; c_{N,r} = 1 (Lat•(Λ°, L_2°) = {Λ•}), c_{N,δ} = c_{N−2δ,0} for 0 ≤ δ < r, and c_{N,0} equals the number of maximal isotropic subspaces of the N-dimensional hermitian space Λ°_N ⊗_{O_F} O_F/𝔭 over O_F/𝔭, namely ∏_{i=1}^{r}(q^{2i−1}+1) if N = 2r and ∏_{i=1}^{r}(q^{2i+1}+1) if N = 2r + 1.
items.locator: §B.2, proof of Lemma B.2.4, published pp. 336–337
items.note: The count of maximal isotropic subspaces of a finite hermitian space is used as known (it is Lemma B.4.5 summed over s). Brute-force verified (see lemma-b-2-4). Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: §B.2 — Satake transforms Sat°_N, Sat•_N and their common target
items.statement: Let W_N be the Weyl group of A_N(F^+) in U(V_N)(F^+) (it preserves A_N(O_{F^+})). There are Satake transforms Sat°_N: 𝕋°_N → Z[q^{−1}][A_N(F^+)/A_N(O_{F^+})]^{W_N} and Sat•_N: 𝕋•_N → Z[q^{−1}][A_N(F^+)/A_N(O_{F^+})]^{W_N}, and an isomorphism of Z[q^{−1}]-rings Z[q^{−1}][A_N(F^+)/A_N(O_{F^+})]^{W_N} ≃ Z[q^{−1}][X*_N]^sym under which 𝔰_δ corresponds to the sum of the elements of the W_N-orbit of ϖ^{t_δ}A_N(O_{F^+}) (0 ≤ δ ≤ r); both Satake transforms are regarded as valued in Z[q^{−1}][X*_N]^sym.
items.note: Normalisation (implicit, standard unitary Satake with δ_B^{1/2}) is pinned down by Lemma B.2.6: the leading coefficient of Sat°(T°_{N;δ}) is q^{δ(N−δ)} = q^{⟨ρ,t_δ⟩}. Consistency check (computer, sympy): at the trivial parameter α_i = q^{N+1−2i}, Sat°(T°_{N;δ}) as determined by Lemma B.2.6 equals the degree |K°ϖ^{t_δ}K°/K°| = q^{δ²}·#{totally isotropic δ-subspaces of F_{q²}^N} for all N ≤ 8 and 0 ≤ δ ≤ r. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Notation B.2.5 — the homomorphisms φ'_α, φ°_α, φ•_α
items.statement: Let Z[q^{−1}][X*_N]' be the Z[q^{−1}]-subring of Z[q^{−1}][X*_N] generated by 𝛍_1, …, 𝛍_r. For a Z[q^{−1}]-ring L and α = (α_1, …, α_N) ∈ L^N with α_iα_{N+1−i} = 1, φ'_α: Z[q^{−1}][X*_N]' → L is the homomorphism with 𝛍_i ↦ α_i + α_i^{−1} (1 ≤ i ≤ r) (similar to Construction 3.1.8); φ°_α := φ'_α ∘ Sat°_N: 𝕋°_N → L and φ•_α := φ'_α ∘ Sat•_N: 𝕋•_N → L (through Z[q^{−1}][X*_N]^sym ⊆ Z[q^{−1}][X*_N]').
items.note: Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Lemma B.2.6 — Satake transform of the T°_{N;i} via χ(ρ_{N,δ}) (cited)
items.note: Cited, not proved: 'This is [75, Lemma 9.2.4]' (Xiao–Zhu). Printed as 'Lemma' (earlier version of this extraction: 'Proposition'). The system is unitriangular, so it determines Sat°_N(T°_{N;i}); e.g. Sat°(T°_{2;1}) = q𝛍_1 + q − 1, Sat°(T°_{3;1}) = q²𝛍_1 + q − 1. Consistency checks: leading coefficient q^{δ(N−δ)} = q^{⟨ρ,t_δ⟩}; value at the trivial parameter equals the degree of T°_{N;δ} for all N ≤ 8, δ ≤ r (computer). Lemmas B.3.1–B.4.2 were checked by computer taking this lemma as input. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Gaussian binomial coefficients [n, m]_x and the convention used in Appendix B
items.statement: [0]_q = 1, [n]_q = (q^n − 1)/(q − 1), [n]_q! = [n]_q[n−1]_q⋯[1]_q, and [n, m]_q := [n]_q!/([n−m]_q! [m]_q!) for integers 0 ≤ m ≤ n (Notation 1.3.1); regarded as polynomials, so that [n, m]_{−q}, [n, m]_{q²} and [n, m]_λ are defined. Appendix B uses [n, m]_x = 0 for m < 0 or m > n (implicitly, e.g. [2k, −1]_{−q} in the proofs of Lemmas B.2.8, B.3.3, B.4.1).
items.locator: §1.3, Notation 1.3.1, published p. 119; used throughout §§B.2–B.4, pp. 337–350
items.note: The zero convention outside 0 ≤ m ≤ n is never stated but is forced by the proofs ('the term with δ = k vanishes'). Pascal rules used: [n, m]_x = [n−1, m]_x + x^{n−m}[n−1, m−1]_x = [n−1, m−1]_x + x^m[n−1, m]_x and (x^m − 1)[n, m]_x = (x^n − 1)[n−1, m−1]_x. Missing: routed to a source of QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.0 (route 9).

items.name: Gauss polynomial identity (cited)
items.statement: For every integer k ≥ 1, Σ_{δ=0}^{2k} (−1)^δ [2k, δ]_λ = (1 − λ)(1 − λ³)⋯(1 − λ^{2k−1}) in Z[λ].
items.locator: §B.2, proof of Lemma B.2.7, published p. 338, footnote 35
items.note: Cited, not proved: 'A proof can be found at http://mathworld.wolfram.com/GausssPolynomialIdentity.html'. Verified by computer for k ≤ 5. Missing: routed to a source of QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.0 (route 9).

items.name: Lemma B.2.7 — Σ q^{δ²}[2k, k−δ]_{−q} = ∏(q^{2i−1}+1)
items.statement: For every integer k ≥ 1, Σ_{δ=−k}^{k} q^{δ²} [2k, k−δ]_{−q} = (q+1)(q³+1)⋯(q^{2k−1}+1).
items.note: Proof: specialise the Gauss identity at λ = −q^{−1} ([2k,δ]_{−q^{−1}} = (−q)^{−δ(2k−δ)}[2k,δ]_{−q}), multiply by q^{k²}, substitute δ ↦ k − δ. Also true for k = 0. Verified by computer for 0 ≤ k ≤ 7. Missing: routed to a source of QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.0 (route 9).

items.name: Lemma B.2.8 — weighted difference identity
items.note: Proof: Pascal [2k+1, k−δ] = [2k, k−δ] + (−q)^{k+δ+1}[2k, k−δ−1], shift δ, reduce to (−1)^{k+1}q^kΣ(δ−1)q^{δ²}[2k,k−δ]_{−q}, use Lemma B.2.7 and Σ δq^{δ²}[2k,k−δ]_{−q} = 0 (δ ↔ −δ). Also true for k = 0. Verified by computer for 0 ≤ k ≤ 7. Missing: routed to a source of QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.0 (route 9).

items.name: Lemma B.3.1 — Satake expansion of q^{r²}∏(𝛍_i + 2) (N = 2r)
items.note: Proof: Lemma B.1.3(1) at λ = 1, Lemma B.2.6, Lemma B.2.7. Verified by computer (given Lemma B.2.6) for N = 2, 4, 6, 8. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Lemma B.3.2 — Satake expansion of q^{r²}∏(𝛍_i − q − q^{−1}) (N = 2r)
items.note: Proof: Lemma B.1.3(1) at λ = −q, Lemma B.2.6 (q^{r²}χ(ρ_{N;r−δ}) = q^{δ²}Σ_i[2r−2i, r−δ−i]_{−q}Sat°(T°_{N;i})), then Lemma B.3.3 with k = r − i. Verified by computer for N = 2, 4, 6, 8. (An earlier version of this extraction's 'Proposition B.3.2(1,2)' items are in fact Proposition B.3.5.) Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Lemma B.3.3 — signed Gaussian identity
items.statement: For every integer k ≥ 1, Σ_{δ=−k}^{k} (−1)^δ q^{δ²+δ} [2k, k−δ]_{−q} = (−q)^k (q+1)(q³+1)⋯(q^{2k−1}+1).
items.note: Proof: by Lemma B.2.7 it is equivalent to (−q)^kΣq^{δ²}[2k,k−δ]_{−q} = Σ(−1)^δq^{δ²+δ}[2k,k−δ]_{−q}; the difference equals ((−q)^{2k} − 1)Σ(−1)^δq^{δ²+δ}[2k−1, k−δ−1]_{−q}, whose terms δ and −δ−1 cancel. Also true for k = 0. Proof of a combinatorial lemma credited to Zipei Nie and Jun Su (Acknowledgements, p. 320). Verified by computer for 0 ≤ k ≤ 7. Missing: routed to a source of QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.0 (route 9).

items.name: Lemma B.3.4 — Satake expansion of the derivative (N = 2r)
items.note: The inner sum is d_{δ,q} (Notation 1.3.1). Proof: Lemma B.1.3(2) at λ = −q and Lemma B.2.6 reduce it to Σ_{δ=0}^{k}(−1)^δ(2δ+1)q^{δ²+δ}[2k+1,k−δ]_{−q} − Σ_{δ=1}^{k}(−1)^δq^{δ²}(δq^δ − δq^{−δ})[2k,k−δ]_{−q} = (−q)^k(q+1)⋯(q^{2k−1}+1) for k ≥ 1, which is Lemma B.2.8 after symmetrising. Both the reduction identity (k ≤ 7) and the full lemma (N = 2, …, 8, given B.2.6) verified by computer. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Proposition B.3.5(1) — φ°_α(I°_N) for N = 2r
items.statement: Let N = 2r, L a Z[q^{−1}]-ring, α = (α_1, …, α_N) ∈ L^N with α_iα_{N+1−i} = 1, and φ°_α: 𝕋°_N → L as in Notation B.2.5. Then φ°_α(I°_N) = q^{r²} ∏_{i=1}^{r} (α_i + 1/α_i + 2).
items.note: Follows from Lemmas B.2.4 and B.3.1 (checked by computer for N ≤ 8). An earlier version of this extraction labelled this 'Proposition B.3.2(1)'. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Proposition B.3.5(2) — φ°_α((q+1)R°_N − I°_N) for N = 2r
items.statement: Let N = 2r, L, α, φ°_α as in Proposition B.3.5(1). Then φ°_α((q+1)R°_N − I°_N) = −q^{r²} ∏_{i=1}^{r} (α_i + 1/α_i − q − 1/q), where R°_N := Σ_{δ=0}^{r−1} ((1 − (−q)^{r−δ})/(q+1)) (q+1)(q³+1)⋯(q^{2(r−δ)−1}+1) · T°_{N;δ} (printed with '(q+1)(q+3)⋯', a misprint for (q+1)(q³+1)⋯).
items.note: Follows from Lemmas B.2.4 and B.3.2: (q+1)R°_N − I°_N = −(T°_{N;r} + Σ_{δ≥1}(−q)^δ∏_{i≤δ}(q^{2i−1}+1)T°_{N;r−δ}). Verified by computer for N = 2, 4, 6, 8 with the corrected product; with the literal factor (q+3) the identity fails for every N ≥ 4. (1 − (−q)^m)/(q+1) ∈ Z[q]. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Proposition B.3.5(3) — φ°_α(R°_N + (q+1)T°_N) for N = 2r
items.note: Follows from Lemma B.3.4: the coefficient of T°_{N;δ} in R°_N + (q+1)T°_N is d_{k,q} − (−q)^k∏_{i≤k}(q^{2i−1}+1), k = r − δ. Verified by computer for N = 2, …, 8 (with corrected R°_N). d•_{k,q} ∈ Z[q] (checked k ≤ 7). An earlier version of this extraction labelled this 'Proposition B.3.2(3)'. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Lemma B.3.6 — T•°_N intertwines R°_N, T°_N with R•_N, T•_N (N = 2r)
items.note: Proof: 'by the same lattice counting argument as for Lemma B.2.4', T•°_N ∘ T°_{N;δ} = T•_{N;δ} ∘ T•°_N for every 0 ≤ δ ≤ r (item claim-b-3-6-commutation). Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Proof of Lemma B.3.6 — T•°_N ∘ T°_{N;δ} = T•_{N;δ} ∘ T•°_N (N even)
items.statement: Let N = 2r. For every 0 ≤ δ ≤ r, T•°_N ∘ T°_{N;δ} = T•_{N;δ} ∘ T•°_N in Z[K•_N\U(V_N)(F^+)/K°_N].
items.locator: §B.3, proof of Lemma B.3.6, published p. 343
items.note: Justified in one sentence. Checks: brute-force lattice counts for N = 2 (q = 2: 63 test lattices; q = 3: 364) agree; conceptually, the similitude g = diag(ϖ on e_{−i}, 1 on e_i) normalises U(V_N), centralises A_N, maps Lat° bijectively to Lat• and conjugates K°ϖ^{t_δ}K° to K•ϖ^{t_δ}K•, so Sat•(T•_{N;δ}) = Sat°(T°_{N;δ}). Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Lemma B.4.1 — Satake expansion of q^{r²+r}∏(𝛍_i + q + q^{−1}) (N = 2r+1)
items.note: Proof: Lemma B.1.4 at λ = q and Lemma B.2.6 reduce it to Σ_{δ=−k−1}^{k} q^{δ²}[2k+1, k−δ]_{−q} = (q+1)(q³+1)⋯(q^{2k+1}+1) for k ≥ 0, which follows from Lemma B.2.7 (for k+1) and the Pascal rule (terms δ and 1−δ cancel). Reduction identity (k ≤ 7) and full lemma (N = 1, …, 9, given B.2.6) verified by computer. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Lemma B.4.2 — Satake expansion of q^{r²+r}∏(𝛍_i − 2) (N = 2r+1)
items.note: Proof: Lemma B.1.4 at λ = −1 ((λ^{δ+1}+λ^{−δ})/(λ+1) ↦ (−1)^δ(2δ+1)) and Lemma B.2.6; the coefficient of Sat°(T°_{N;i}) is literally d_{r−i,q}. Verified by computer for N = 1, …, 9. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Proposition B.4.3(1) — φ°_α(I°_N) for N = 2r+1
items.statement: Let N = 2r + 1, L a Z[q^{−1}]-ring, α ∈ L^N with α_iα_{N+1−i} = 1, φ°_α: 𝕋°_N → L as in Notation B.2.5. Then φ°_α(I°_N) = q^{r²+r} ∏_{i=1}^{r} (α_i + 1/α_i + q + 1/q).
items.note: Follows from Lemmas B.2.4 and B.4.1 (checked by computer for N ≤ 9). Degree check at the trivial parameter: (q+1)(q³+1) for N = 3. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Proposition B.4.3(2) — φ°_α(T°_N) for N = 2r+1
items.statement: Let N = 2r + 1, L, α, φ°_α as in Proposition B.4.3(1). Then φ°_α(T°_N) = q^{r²+r} ∏_{i=1}^{r} (α_i + 1/α_i − 2), where T°_N := Σ_{δ=0}^{r} d_{r−δ,q} · T°_{N;δ} (d_{k,q} as in Notation 1.3.1).
items.note: Follows from Lemma B.4.2 (checked by computer for N ≤ 9). Note T°_N here (N odd) sums δ = 0, …, r with d, whereas T°_N in Proposition B.3.5(3) (N even) sums δ = 0, …, r−1 with d•. Missing: routed to a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (route 6).

items.name: Lemma B.4.4 — intertwining relation T•°_N ∘ T°_N = ((q+1)²T•_N + T•°_N ∘ T°•_N) ∘ T•°_N (N = 2r+1)
items.statement: Let N = 2r + 1. In Z[K•_N\U(V_N)(F^+)/K°_N]: T•°_N ∘ T°_N = ((q+1)² T•_N + T•°_N ∘ T°•_N) ∘ T•°_N, where T°_N := Σ_{δ=0}^{r} d_{r−δ,q} T°_{N;δ} is as in Proposition B.4.3(2) and T•_N := Σ_{δ=0}^{r−1} d•_{r−δ,q} · T•_{N;δ}.
items.note: 'A hard exercise in combinatorics … proof by brute force.' Proof: evaluate both sides at Λ• on f ∈ Z[Lat°_N] (B.2), using the counts (B.3), (B.4), the expansion of T•°_N ∘ T°•_N (items claim-b-4-4-counts, claim-b-4-4-i-bullet) and (B.5)–(B.7) (claim-b-4-4-reduction). Every ingredient verified (counts by lattice brute force for N = 3, 5 at q = 2 and N = 3 at q = 3; identity (B.6) for 0 ≤ k ≤ 7). An earlier version of this extraction's 'Proposition B.4.4 / V T°=((q+1)²T•+VU)V' is this lemma. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Proof of Lemma B.4.4 — the counts c•_δ(L), c°_δ(L), (B.3) and (B.4)
items.statement: Let N = 2r + 1. For L ∈ Lat°_N and 0 ≤ δ ≤ r let c•_δ(L) be the number of L• ∈ Lat•_N with L ⊆ L• and (L• + Λ•_N)/Λ•_N ≃ (O_F/𝔭)^{⊕δ}, and c°_δ(L) the number of L° ∈ Lat°_N with L° ⊆ Λ•_N and L/(L ∩ L°) ≃ (O_F/𝔭)^{⊕δ}; then (T•_{N;δ}(T•°_N f))(Λ•_N) = Σ_{L∈Lat°} c•_δ(L)f(L) and (T•°_N(T°_{N;δ}f))(Λ•_N) = Σ_{L∈Lat°} c°_δ(L)f(L). If (L + Λ•_N)/Λ•_N ≃ (O_F/𝔭)^{⊕γ} for some 0 ≤ γ ≤ δ, then (B.3) c•_δ(L) = q^{(δ−γ)(δ−γ+2)} [r−γ, δ−γ]_{q²} and (B.4) c°_δ(L) = q^{(δ−γ)²} [r−γ, δ−γ]_{q²}; otherwise c•_δ(L) = c°_δ(L) = 0.
items.locator: §B.4, proof of Lemma B.4.4, published pp. 346–347, eqs. (B.3), (B.4)
items.note: Proof via Lemma B.4.5 applied to a (2r+1−2γ)- resp. (2r−2γ)-dimensional hermitian space; the description of the ambient spaces in the sketch for (B.4) ('isotropic subspace of 𝔭^{−1}Λ•/Λ•') is loose, but (B.3) and (B.4) were verified by brute-force lattice enumeration for (q,N) = (2,3), (2,5), (3,3), all γ, δ (the K•-orbit of L is determined by γ). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Proof of Lemma B.4.4 — expansion of T•°_N ∘ T°•_N for N odd
items.locator: §B.4, proof of Lemma B.4.4, published p. 348
items.note: 'By a similar proof of Lemma B.2.4': the relevant hermitian space Λ•/(Λ•)^∨ has even dimension 2r. Verified by brute-force lattice counts for (q,N) = (2,3), (2,5), (3,3). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Proof of Lemma B.4.4 — the reduction identities (B.5)–(B.7)
items.locator: §B.4, proof of Lemma B.4.4, published pp. 348–350, eqs. (B.5)–(B.7)
items.note: Uses Lemma B.2.8 in the form (−q)^{δ+1}∏_{i≤δ}(q^{2i−1}+1) = −q d_{δ,q} + qΣ_{j=−δ}^{δ}(−1)^j j q^{j²+j}[2δ, δ−j]_{−q}. (B.6) and (B.7) verified by computer (sympy) for 0 ≤ k ≤ 7; the chain of equalities on p. 349 re-derived step by step. The first displayed (unnumbered) form on p. 348 drops a '+1' in the last factor (Source issue, misprint). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Lemma B.4.5 — counting maximal isotropic subspaces by their intersection with a fixed one
items.statement: Let V be a (non-degenerate) hermitian space over O_F/𝔭 (≅ F_{q²}, relative to F_q) of dimension m ≥ 1, r := ⌊m/2⌋, and Y_0 ⊆ V a maximal isotropic subspace. For 0 ≤ s ≤ r, the number of maximal isotropic subspaces Y ⊆ V with dim_{O_F/𝔭}(Y ∩ Y_0) = r − s is q^{s(s+2)} [r, s]_{q²} if m = 2r + 1, and q^{s²} [r, s]_{q²} if m = 2r.
items.note: Proof (m odd; m even 'left to the readers'): [r, s]_{q²} choices of Y ∩ Y_0; for fixed Y ∩ Y_0 = ⟨e_{−r}, …, e_{−s−1}⟩, Y has a unique basis completion f with (f_1…f_s) = (e_1…e_s) + (e_{−s}…e_{−1}, e_0)(A; v), subject to one hermitian matrix equation; (q^{2s} choices of v) × (q^{s²} solutions A) = q^{s(s+2)}. The printed equation ᵗA^c + A + ᵗv^c·v = 0 holds for the ordering (e_{−1}, …, e_{−s}) (Source issue, misprint). Valid in characteristic 2 (trace F_{q²} → F_q surjective). Verified by brute force for q = 2 (m = 1…5) and q = 3 (m = 1…4). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: §C.1 notation — unramified characters α̲, normalized induction, St_N
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be an unramified quadratic extension of nonarchimedean local fields. For α ∈ ℂ^×, α̲ : F^× → ℂ^× denotes the unramified character sending every uniformizer to α (for a positive real |α|, |α|̲ is the unramified character with value |α| on uniformizers). Let V be a hermitian space over F (with respect to F/F⁺) of rank N and G := U(V). For a parabolic subgroup P of G and an admissible representation σ of P(F⁺), I_P^G(σ) denotes the normalized parabolic induction (an admissible representation of G(F⁺)). A minimal parabolic subgroup P_min of G is fixed. St_N denotes the Steinberg representation of GL_N(F).
items.note: All representations have coefficients in ℂ unless stated otherwise. Since F/F⁺ is unramified, a uniformizer of F⁺ is a uniformizer of F. Convention (checked against §C.2): P_min is the stabilizer of the isotropic flag Fe_{−r} ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ Fe_{−r} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ Fe_{−1}, and a character of GL(Fe_i) is evaluated on the action on e_i; with this convention a 'strictly positive' Langlands exponent corresponds to |α| > 1, the trivial representation of U(1,1) is a quotient of I(q̲) and the Steinberg representation a subrepresentation of I(q̲). Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Langlands classification for U(V)(F⁺) (recalled)
items.statement: For every irreducible admissible representation π of G(F⁺) = U(V)(F⁺) there are a unique parabolic subgroup P ⊇ P_min of G with Levi quotient M_P, a unique tempered representation τ of M_P(F⁺) and a unique strictly positive unramified character χ of P(F⁺) such that π is isomorphic to the unique irreducible quotient J_P^G(τχ) of I_P^G(τχ) (the Langlands quotient). Writing M_P = G_0 × Res_{F/F⁺}GL_{r_1} × ⋯ × Res_{F/F⁺}GL_{r_t} with G_0 the unitary factor, one has χ = 𝟏 ⊠ (α̲_1∘det_{r_1}) ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ (α̲_t∘det_{r_t}) for unique real numbers 1 < α_1 < ⋯ < α_t, where det_r is the determinant on GL_r(F).
items.note: Recalled with reference to Konno [39]; not proved. The paper writes 'χ of P_π(F⁺)'; P_π is the parabolic P just introduced. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Local base change BC(π) for unitary groups (cited)
items.statement: For an irreducible admissible representation π of G(F⁺) = U(V)(F⁺), BC(π) denotes its local base change, an irreducible admissible representation of GL_N(F). It is defined by Rogawski [63] for N ≤ 3 and by Kaletha–Minguez–Shin–White [33] and Mok [53] for general N. In §C.3 the same notation BC is used for the local base change at every place v of F⁺ (split, inert, ramified, archimedean).
items.note: Black box: defined through the local Langlands correspondence of the endoscopic classification (quasi-split: Mok; inner forms: KMSW). Not proved here. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Base change of a Langlands quotient (recalled)
items.statement: Let π ≅ J_P^G(τχ) with M_P = G_0 × Res_{F/F⁺}GL_{r_1} × ⋯ × Res_{F/F⁺}GL_{r_t}, χ = 𝟏 ⊠ (α̲_1∘det_{r_1}) ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ (α̲_t∘det_{r_t}) (1 < α_1 < ⋯ < α_t) and τ = τ_0 ⊠ τ_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ τ_t. Let P′ be the standard parabolic subgroup of GL_N whose Levi is GL_{r_t} × ⋯ × GL_{r_1} × GL_{N_0} × GL_{r_1} × ⋯ × GL_{r_t} (N_0 = N − 2(r_1+⋯+r_t)). Then BC(π) ≅ J_{P′}^{GL_N}( τ_t^{∨c}(α̲_t^{−1}∘det_{r_t}) ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ τ_1^{∨c}(α̲_1^{−1}∘det_{r_1}) ⊠ BC(τ_0) ⊠ τ_1(α̲_1∘det_{r_1}) ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ τ_t(α̲_t∘det_{r_t}) ), which is a Langlands quotient of GL_N(F). Here τ^c := τ∘c.
items.note: Recalled property of the local base change of [33,53] (compatibility with the Langlands classification); no proof or reference given. Exponents are decreasing along P′ (|α_t^{−1}| < ⋯ < |α_1^{−1}| < 1 < |α_1| < ⋯), so this is the standard Langlands quotient on GL_N. N_0 is not named in the paper. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Tempered representations as summands of induced discrete series (recalled)
items.statement: Let τ be an irreducible admissible tempered representation of G(F⁺). Then there are a unique parabolic subgroup P ⊇ P_min of G and a discrete series representation σ of M_P(F⁺) such that τ is a direct summand of I_P^G(σ). Moreover I_P^G(σ) is a direct sum of finitely many tempered representations, each of multiplicity one.
items.note: Cited from Jantzen [32] ('see, for example'); not proved. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Base change of a tempered representation (recalled)
items.statement: In the situation of tempered-from-discrete-series, write σ = σ_0 ⊠ σ_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ σ_t along M_P = G_0 × Res_{F/F⁺}GL_{r_1} × ⋯ × Res_{F/F⁺}GL_{r_t}. Then BC(τ) ≅ I_{P′}^{GL_N}(σ_t^{∨c} ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ σ_1^{∨c} ⊠ BC(σ_0) ⊠ σ_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ σ_t), which is an irreducible admissible representation of GL_N(F).
items.note: Recalled property of BC [33,53]; irreducibility is that of unitary induction of tempered representations of GL_N. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Satake parameter α(BC(π)) of an unramified-principal-series constituent
items.statement: If π is an irreducible admissible representation of G(F⁺) that is a constituent of an unramified principal series, then BC(π) is a constituent of an unramified principal series of GL_N(F); its Satake parameter (a multiset of N elements of ℂ^×) is denoted α(BC(π)). The parabolic P′ of GL_N is suppressed from the notation when clear.
items.note: For π a constituent of I_{P_min}^G(α̲_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_r) with G quasi-split of rank N = 2r, α(BC(π)) = {α_1^{±1}, …, α_r^{±1}}. 'Contains {q, q^{−1}}' / '{−1, −1}' are used in the sense of Remark 3.1.6. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: §C.2 setup — U_N, K_N, Λ̄_N, Ū_N
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be an unramified quadratic extension of nonarchimedean local fields with residue field extension κ/κ⁺; q := #κ⁺ and 𝔭 the maximal ideal of O_F. Let N ≥ 2 and r := ⌊N/2⌋. Let V_N be a hermitian space over F of rank N with a self-dual lattice Λ_N; U_N := U(V_N); K_N ⊆ U_N(F⁺) the stabilizer of Λ_N, a hyperspecial maximal subgroup. Put Λ̄_N := Λ_N ⊗_{O_{F⁺}} κ⁺ and Ū_N := U(Λ̄_N) (a unitary group over κ⁺); there is the reduction homomorphism K_N → Ū_N(κ⁺).
items.note: Ū_N(κ⁺) is the finite unitary group U_N(𝔽_q). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Fermat hypersurface Iso(Λ̄_N)
items.statement: Iso(Λ̄_N) ⊆ ℙ(Λ̄_N) is the isotropic locus: it parametrizes hyperplanes H of Λ̄_N satisfying H^⊥ ⊆ H, where ⊥ is the left orthogonal complement for the hermitian pairing on Λ̄_N (κ-linear in the first variable and (κ,σ)-linear in the second; footnote 36, cf. Definition A.1.2). Iso(Λ̄_N) is a smooth hypersurface in ℙ(Λ̄_N), the Fermat hypersurface; it has dimension N − 2 and a natural action of Ū_N(κ⁺).
items.note: Concretely the hermitian (Fermat) hypersurface of degree q+1 in ℙ^{N−1}_κ. For N = 2 it is a set of q+1 points; for N = 3 the Hermitian curve of genus q(q−1)/2. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Primitive cohomology of Iso(Λ̄_N) and the Tate–Thompson representation Ω_N
items.statement: For a rational prime ℓ invertible in κ, put H^prim(Iso(Λ̄_N)_κ̄, Q̄_ℓ) := ker( ∪c_1(O_{ℙ(Λ̄_N)}(1)) : H^{N−2}_ét(Iso(Λ̄_N)_κ̄, Q̄_ℓ) → H^N_ét(Iso(Λ̄_N)_κ̄, Q̄_ℓ(1)) ). By Tate–Thompson (see [31]) there is a unique irreducible representation Ω_N of Ū_N(κ⁺) such that Ω_N ≅ ι_ℓ^{−1}H^prim(Iso(Λ̄_N)_κ̄, Q̄_ℓ) as representations of Ū_N(κ⁺) for every isomorphism ι_ℓ : ℂ ≅ Q̄_ℓ. Ω_N is called the Tate–Thompson representation; it is often regarded as a representation of K_N by inflation.
items.note: Existence and irreducibility are cited (Tate–Thompson lemma, Hotta–Matsui [31]). Correct for N ≥ 3. For N = 2 (allowed by 'N ≥ 2') the printed kernel is all of H^0 of q+1 points, i.e. 𝟏 ⊕ St, which is not irreducible; the intended object is the reduced H^0 (kernel of the degree map), of dimension q, which is the Steinberg representation of Ū_2(κ⁺) = U_2(𝔽_q) — see issue E10. Used in §5.6 (Definition 5.6.3, Proposition 5.6.4) and §6. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

api.name: RankinSelberg.ReducedPrimitiveTateThompsonRepresentation.characterisation

items.name: Parabolics P_N^{(r_1,…,r_t)} of Ū_N and Harish-Chandra induction
items.statement: For every N fix a Borel subgroup P_N of Ū_N. For positive integers r_1,…,r_t with r_1+⋯+r_t ≤ r, P_N^{(r_1,…,r_t)} is the parabolic subgroup of Ū_N containing P_N whose Levi quotient M_N^{(r_1,…,r_t)} is isomorphic to Ū_{N−2(r_1+⋯+r_t)} × Res_{κ/κ⁺}GL_{r_1} × ⋯ × Res_{κ/κ⁺}GL_{r_t}; for example P_N^{(1^r)} = P_N. For a representation σ of M_N^{(r_1,…,r_t)}(κ⁺), Ind_{P_N^{(r_1,…,r_t)}}^{Ū_N} σ denotes the parabolic induction, a representation of Ū_N(κ⁺).
items.note: P_{2r}^{(r)} is the Siegel parabolic (Levi Res GL_r), the stabilizer of a maximal isotropic subspace. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Principal-series constituents PS(ϵ) and the character ϵ_N^TT
items.statement: Let N = 2r. The irreducible constituents of Ind_{P_N}^{Ū_N} 𝟏 are parametrized by the irreducible representations of the Weyl group W_N ≃ {±1}^r ⋊ 𝔖_r; for an irreducible representation ϵ of W_N, PS(ϵ) denotes the corresponding irreducible representation of Ū_N(κ⁺). ϵ_N^TT : W_N → {±1} is the character extending the product homomorphism {±1}^r → {±1} (which is 𝔖_r-invariant) to W_N and trivial on {+1}^r ⋊ 𝔖_r.
items.note: Parametrization through the Iwahori–Hecke algebra of Ū_N (parameters q^2 for the 𝔖_r-generators, q for the sign-change generator), normalized so that dim PS(ϵ)^{P_J(κ⁺)} = ⟨ϵ|_{W_J}, 𝟏⟩ for standard parabolics (Curtis [22]). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Proposition C.2.1(1) — Ω_{2r} ≅ PS(ϵ^TT)
items.statement: When N = 2r is even, the Tate–Thompson representation Ω_N is isomorphic to PS(ϵ_N^TT).
items.locator: §C.2, Proposition C.2.1(1), published p. 353; proof p. 354
items.note: Proof: ϵ_N^TT is the unique nontrivial character of W_N trivial on {+1}^r ⋊ 𝔖_r, so (1) follows from (2) by [22, Theorem 4.4.5]. Published label is Proposition C.2.1 (all arXiv versions too), not 'Lemma C.2.1'. At N = 2 this holds only for the reduced H^0 (issue E10); then Ω_2 = St. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Proposition C.2.1(2) — characterization of Ω_{2r} by parabolic invariants
items.statement: When N = 2r is even, Ω_N is the unique nontrivial irreducible representation of Ū_N(κ⁺) satisfying dim Ω_N^{P_N(κ⁺)} = dim Ω_N^{P_N^{(r)}(κ⁺)} = 1.
items.locator: §C.2, Proposition C.2.1(2), published p. 353; proof p. 354–355
items.note: Proof: uniqueness — dim Ω^{P_N} = 1 forces Ω to be a constituent PS(ϵ) of Ind_{P_N}𝟏 with ϵ a character; among the characters of W_N only 𝟏 and ϵ_N^TT give nonzero P_N^{(r)}-invariants (the paper says W_N has 'four' characters, true for r ≥ 2; two for r = 1). Existence — ⟨R_{2r}, R′_{2r}⟩ = 1 from (C.1), (C.2) and R′_{2r} = R_{(2^r)} gives dim Ω^{P_N} = 1; the primitive part of the class of ℙ(Y_N) ⊆ Iso(Λ̄_N) (Y_N the maximal isotropic subspace stabilized by P_N^{(r)}) is a nonzero P_N^{(r)}(κ⁺)-fixed vector in H^prim(r−1). The printed normalization of that class is wrong (issue E12): it should be [ℙ(Y_N)] − (q+1)^{−1}c_1(O(1))^{r−1}. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Proposition C.2.1(3) — Ω_3 is the cuspidal unipotent representation
items.statement: The representation Ω_3 is the (unique) cuspidal unipotent representation of Ū_3(κ⁺).
items.locator: §C.2, Proposition C.2.1(3), published p. 353; proof p. 355
items.note: Proof: by (C.1), R_3 = (1/3)(R_{(1^3)} − R_{(3)}), identified with the cuspidal unipotent character in Prasad [61, Example 6.2]. Degree q(q−1) = dim H^1 of the Hermitian curve. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Proposition C.2.1(4) — odd N: Ω_N inside the induction of Ω_3
items.statement: When N = 2r+1 is odd with r ≥ 1, the representation Ω_N is a multiplicity-free constituent (it occurs with multiplicity one) of Ind_{P_N^{(1^{r−1})}}^{Ū_N} (Ω_3 ⊠ 𝟏^{⊠ r−1}).
items.locator: §C.2, Proposition C.2.1(4), published p. 354; proof p. 355
items.note: Proof: R′_{2r+1} = (1/3)(R_{(2^{r−1},1^3)} − R_{(2^{r−1},3)}) by [24, Prop. 8.2], and ⟨R_{2r+1}, R′_{2r+1}⟩ = (1/3)(χ_{2r+1}((2^{r−1},1^3)) − χ_{2r+1}((2^{r−1},3))) = (1/3)(2 − (−1)) = 1 (checked). Used in Proposition 5.6.4(2) with Moy–Prasad [55]. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: (C.1) Character of Ω_N in terms of Deligne–Lusztig characters (cited)
items.statement: Let 𝔖_N be the symmetric group and 𝔓_N its set of conjugacy classes, identified with the partitions of N. For π ∈ 𝔓_N let R_π be the Deligne–Lusztig character of Ū_N(κ⁺) [24, Corollary 4.3] attached to the trivial representation of the maximal torus corresponding to π; let χ_N be the character of the unique nontrivial subrepresentation of the standard representation of 𝔖_N (so χ_N(σ) = #{fixed points of σ} − 1); and let N!/z_π be the cardinality of the class π. Then the character R_N of Ω_N is R_N = (−1)^{N+1} Σ_{π∈𝔓_N} (χ_N(π)/z_π)·R_π.
items.note: Cited from Hotta–Matsui [31, Theorem 1]; not proved. Torus convention implicit in R′_{2r} = R_{(2^r)}: the maximally split torus corresponds to (2^r) (resp. (2^r,1)). For N = 2 the formula gives R_2 = (R_{(2)} − R_{(1^2)})/2 = St (degree q), consistent with E10's correction, not with the printed q+1-dimensional H^prim. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: (C.2) Orthogonality of Deligne–Lusztig characters (cited)
items.statement: For π, π′ ∈ 𝔓_N: ⟨R_π, R_{π′}⟩ = 0 if π ≠ π′, and ⟨R_π, R_π⟩ = z_π.
items.note: Cited from Deligne–Lusztig [24, Theorem 6.8]. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Characters of the induced representations R′_{2r}, R′_{2r+1} (cited)
items.locator: §C.2, proof of Proposition C.2.1, published p. 354–355
items.note: From Deligne–Lusztig [24, Proposition 8.2] (Harish-Chandra induction of R_T^L θ is R_T^G θ), together with R_3 = (1/3)(R_{(1^3)} − R_{(3)}). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Inner-product computations in the proof of Proposition C.2.1
items.locator: §C.2, proof of Proposition C.2.1, published p. 354–355
items.note: Checked: χ_N(σ) = #fix(σ) − 1; (2^r) has no fixed points; (2^{r−1},1^3) has three; (2^{r−1},3) none. By Frobenius reciprocity these give dim Ω_{2r}^{P_{2r}(κ⁺)} = 1 and the multiplicity one in (4). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Parabolic invariants of PS(ϵ) (cited, Curtis)
items.statement: (As used) For N = 2r and an irreducible representation ϵ of W_N, and a standard parabolic subgroup of Ū_N containing P_N with Weyl group W_J ⊆ W_N, dim PS(ϵ)^{P_J(κ⁺)} equals the multiplicity of the trivial representation of W_J in ϵ|_{W_J}. In particular dim PS(ϵ)^{P_N(κ⁺)} = dim ϵ, and for P_N^{(r)} (W_J = 𝔖_r) the invariants of PS(ϵ_N^TT) are one-dimensional.
items.locator: §C.2, proof of Proposition C.2.1(1), published p. 354
items.note: Cited as [22, Theorem 4.4.5] (Curtis, Bull. AMS 1979); the paper only says '(1) follows from (2) by [22, Theorem 4.4.5]'. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Cuspidal unipotent representation of U_3(𝔽_q) (cited)
items.statement: The virtual character (1/3)(R_{(1^3)} − R_{(3)}) of Ū_3(κ⁺) is the character of the unique cuspidal unipotent representation of Ū_3(κ⁺).
items.locator: §C.2, proof of Proposition C.2.1(3), published p. 355
items.note: Cited from Prasad [61, Example 6.2]. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Lemma C.2.2(1) — Ω_{2r}-types without {q,q^{−1}} and {−1,−1} are spherical
items.statement: Let N = 2r and let π be an irreducible admissible representation of U_{2r}(F⁺) such that π|_{K_{2r}} contains Ω_{2r} (hence π is a constituent of an unramified principal series). If the Satake parameter of BC(π) contains neither {q, q^{−1}} nor {−1, −1}, then π|_{K_{2r}} contains the trivial representation.
items.locator: §C.2, Lemma C.2.2(1), published p. 355; proof p. 355–358
items.note: Published label Lemma C.2.2 (arXiv v3 same; v1 Lemma C.2.3). Proof: π is a constituent of I_{P_min}^G(α̲_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_r) with 1 ≤ |α_1| ≤ ⋯ ≤ |α_r| and α_i ∉ {−1, q}; the Langlands data are r_0 (number of unimodular α_i), τ_i := I^{GL_{r_i}}(α̲_{r_0+⋯+r_{i−1}+1} ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_{r_0+⋯+r_i}) ⊗ (|α_{r_0+⋯+r_i}^{−1}|̲∘det_{r_i}) (irreducible tempered) and τ_0 := I_{P_{0min}}^{G_0}(α̲_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_{r_0}) (irreducible by Goldberg [27] since no α_i = −1). Claim (C.3): φ_α ≠ 0 in J_P^G(τ_0 ⊠ ⊠_i τ_i(|α_{r_0+⋯+r_i}|̲∘det_{r_i})), equivalent by Konno [39, Cor. 3.2] to T_wφ_α ≠ 0 (C.4), which holds since C(α) ≠ 0. Then π ≅ this Langlands quotient = the unique irreducible quotient of I(α̲), which is K_{2r}-spherical. Hypothesis 'tempered' of the previous-pass paraphrase is not in the paper. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Lemma C.2.2(2) — base change of Ω_{2r}-types with {q, q^{−1}}
items.statement: Let π be an irreducible admissible representation of U_{2r}(F⁺) such that π|_{K_{2r}} contains Ω_{2r}. If the Satake parameter of BC(π) contains {q, q^{−1}}, then there exists (α_2,…,α_r) ∈ (ℂ^×)^{r−1} with 1 ≤ |α_2| ≤ ⋯ ≤ |α_r|, unique up to permutation (correctly: up to permutation and inversion of the entries of absolute value 1), such that BC(π) is isomorphic to the unique irreducible quotient of I^{GL_{2r}}(α̲_r^{−1} ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_2^{−1} ⊠ St_2 ⊠ α̲_2 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_r).
items.locator: §C.2, Lemma C.2.2(2), published p. 355; proof p. 358–360
items.note: Proof: π is a constituent of I_{P_min}^G(q̲ ⊠ α̲_2 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_r); with Q the parabolic stabilizing Fe_{−r} ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ Fe_{−r} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ Fe_{−2} (Levi U(V_2) × ∏_{i≥2} Res GL(Fe_i)) there is a canonical inclusion I_Q^G(Sp_2 ⊠ α̲_2 ⊠ ⋯) ⊆ I_{P_min}^G(q̲ ⊠ α̲_2 ⊠ ⋯) (Sp_2 the Steinberg of U(V_2)(F⁺)) and φ_α lies in it because 𝟙_{Iw_1I} acts by −1. τ_0 is the direct summand of I_{Q_0}^{G_0}(Sp_2 ⊠ α̲_2 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_{r_0}) containing φ_α; φ_α ≠ 0 in the Langlands quotient by the case-(2) C(α). Finally BC(τ_0) ≅ I^{GL_{2r_0}}(α̲_{r_0}^{−1} ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_2^{−1} ⊠ BC(Sp_2) ⊠ α̲_2 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_{r_0}) ≅ I(⋯ ⊠ St_2 ⊠ ⋯), irreducible. Uniqueness clause as printed is inexact (issue). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Iwahori I, Siegel parahoric J, embedded Weyl group and Bruhat decompositions (proof of Lemma C.2.2)
items.statement: Fix Λ_{2r} = O_Fe_{−r} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ O_Fe_{−1} ⊕ O_Fe_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ O_Fe_r with (e_{−i}, e_j) = δ_{ij} (1 ≤ i, j ≤ r); for 0 ≤ i ≤ r, V_{2i} := Fe_{−i} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ Fe_{−1} ⊕ Fe_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ Fe_i (a hermitian subspace of V_{2r}). G := U_{2r}; P_min is the stabilizer of the flag Fe_{−r} ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ Fe_{−r} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ Fe_{−1}, with Levi Res_{F/F⁺}GL(Fe_1) × ⋯ × Res_{F/F⁺}GL(Fe_r). K := K_{2r}; I ⊆ K is the Iwahori subgroup of elements whose reduction mod 𝔭 stabilizes the flag κe_{−r} ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ κe_{−r} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ κe_{−1}; J ⊆ K is the parahoric subgroup of elements whose reduction stabilizes κe_{−r} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ κe_{−1}; I ⊆ J ⊆ K. W_{2r} ≃ {±1}^r ⋊ 𝔖_r is realized in K: the i-th −1 is the element w_i switching e_{−i} and e_i only; for σ ∈ 𝔖_r, (1^r, σ) is the element w′_σ ∈ J sending e_{±i} to e_{±σ(i)}. {w_1, w′_{(1,2)}, …, w′_{(r−1,r)}} is a set of distinguished generators of W_{2r}. Bruhat decompositions: K = ⨆_{w∈W_{2r}} IwI and K = ⨆_{i=0}^{r} J w_1⋯w_i J. For w ∈ W_{2r}, 0 ≤ i(w) ≤ r is the unique integer with w ∈ J w_1⋯w_{i(w)} J.
items.locator: §C.2, proof of Lemma C.2.2, published p. 355–356
items.note: i(w) is the number of sign changes of w (equivalently the number of occurrences of w_1 in a reduced word). [Iw_1I : I] = q, [Iw′_{(i,i+1)}I : I] = q^2. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: The Iwahori-fixed line of Ω_{2r} is spanned by f = Σ(−q)^{−i(w)}𝟙_{IwI}
items.statement: By Proposition C.2.1(2) there is a K-equivariant embedding Ω_{2r} ↪ ℂ[I\K], unique up to scalar, giving a distinguished one-dimensional subspace Ω_{2r}^I ⊆ ℂ[I\K/I]. Ω_{2r}^I is contained in ℂ[J\K/J]; the element 𝟙_{Iw_1I} acts on Ω_{2r}^I by q or −1, the former case corresponding to the K-spherical vector (excluded by Proposition C.2.1(1)); hence Ω_{2r}^I is spanned by f := Σ_{w∈W_{2r}} (−q)^{−i(w)}·𝟙_{IwI} ∈ ℂ[I\K/I].
items.locator: §C.2, proof of Lemma C.2.2, published p. 356
items.note: Checked: for r = 1, with vol(I) = 1, 𝟙_{Iw_1I} * (𝟙_I − q^{−1}𝟙_{Iw_1I}) = −(𝟙_I − q^{−1}𝟙_{Iw_1I}); in general the formula is the standard eigenvector for the Hecke character T_{w_1} ↦ −1, T_{w′} ↦ q^2. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Projection 𝒫_α and the vector φ_α
items.statement: For α = (α_1,…,α_r) ∈ (ℂ^×)^r, 𝒫_α : ℂ[I\K/I] → I_{P_min}^G(α̲_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_r)^I is the ℂ[I\K/I]-equivariant projection defined at the beginning of [15, §2]; put φ_α := 𝒫_α(f).
items.locator: §C.2, proof of Lemma C.2.2, published p. 356–357
items.note: Casselman [15]. φ_α spans the Ω_{2r}-type Iwahori line of I(α̲); since Ω_{2r} occurs exactly once in I(α̲)|_K, exactly one constituent of I(α̲) contains Ω_{2r}. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Irreducibility of unitary unramified principal series of U(V_{2r_0}) away from −1 (cited)
items.statement: (As used) Let G_0 := U(V_{2r_0}) (quasi-split, F/F⁺ unramified) and P_{0min} := G_0 ∩ P_min. If α_1,…,α_{r_0} ∈ ℂ^× have absolute value 1 and none of them equals −1, then I_{P_{0min}}^{G_0}(α̲_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_{r_0}) (a finite direct sum of irreducible tempered representations) is irreducible.
items.locator: §C.2, proof of Lemma C.2.2, published p. 357
items.note: Cited from Goldberg [27, Theorem 1.4 & Theorem 3.4] (R-groups for unitary groups). α̲ = −1̲ restricted to F⁺^× is η_{F/F⁺}, the reducibility point for U(1,1). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Nonvanishing in a Langlands quotient via the long intertwining operator (cited)
items.statement: (As used) Let P ⊇ P_min have Levi G_0 × Res_{F/F⁺}GL_{r_1} × ⋯ × Res_{F/F⁺}GL_{r_t}, let w ∈ W_{2r} be the element acting trivially on V_{2r_0} and switching e_{−(r_0+⋯+r_{i−1}+j)} with e_{r_0+⋯+r_i+1−j} for every 1 ≤ j ≤ r_i and 1 ≤ i ≤ t, and let N be the unipotent radical of P. For φ in I_P^G(τ_0 ⊠ ⊠_{i=1}^t τ_i(|α_{r_0+⋯+r_i}|̲∘det_{r_i})) (Langlands data), the image of φ in the Langlands quotient J_P^G(⋯) is nonzero if and only if T_wφ ≠ 0, where (T_wφ)(g) = ∫_{N(F⁺)} φ(w^{−1}ng) dn is absolutely convergent.
items.note: Cited from Konno [39, Corollary 3.2] and the discussion after [39, Proposition 2.2] (absolute convergence). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Intertwining constant C(α) on φ_α — case (1) of Lemma C.2.2
items.statement: In the situation of Lemma C.2.2(1) (1 ≤ |α_1| ≤ ⋯ ≤ |α_r|, α_i ∉ {−1, q}, |α_i| = 1 exactly for i ≤ r_0), T_wφ_α = C(α)φ_{wα} with C(α) = ∏_{i=r_0+1}^{r} ( (q − α_i)/(q(α_i − 1)) · ∏_{|α_j|<|α_i|} (α_i − q^{−2}α_j)/(α_i − α_j) · ∏_{j=1}^{i−1} (α_iα_j − q^{−2})/(α_iα_j − 1) ), and C(α) ≠ 0 in this situation.
items.locator: §C.2, proof of Lemma C.2.2(1), published p. 358
items.note: From Casselman [15, Theorem 3.4] 'and the continuity'; uses that the Ω_{2r}^I-eigenspace is one-dimensional. The first factor is the sign-type factor for the long root 2e_i (𝟙_{Iw_1I} ↦ −1), the others spherical-type for e_i − e_j (|α_j| < |α_i|) and e_i + e_j (j < i). Checked: c′(α)c′(α^{−1}) = c(α)c(α^{−1}) for U(1,1); the zero at α_i = q matches the Steinberg being a subrepresentation of I(q̲); all factors finite and nonzero when |α_i| > 1, α_i ≠ q. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Intertwining constant C(α) on φ_α — case (2) of Lemma C.2.2
items.locator: §C.2, proof of Lemma C.2.2(2), published p. 359
items.note: 'By the same proof of (C.3)'. The first two factors combine to −(α_i − q^{−1})/(q(α_i − 1)), finite and nonzero even when α_i = q; all remaining factors are nonzero for |α_i| > 1, so C(α) ≠ 0 unconditionally. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Remark C.2.3 — the case {−1,−1}
items.statement: In the situation of Lemma C.2.2, if the Satake parameter of BC(π) does not contain {q, q^{−1}} but possibly contains {−1, −1}, then π is unramified with respect to either K_{2r} or the other (conjugacy class of) hyperspecial maximal subgroup of U_{2r}(F⁺) that is not conjugate to K_{2r}.
items.note: Asserted as what 'the proof actually shows'; no further argument. Not used later in the paper. (When some α_i = −1, τ_0 is reducible and the Ω-line lies in the summand spherical for the non-conjugate hyperspecial; checked for U(1,1).) Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Non-split even hermitian space V′_{2r}, lattice Λ′_{2r}, special maximal K′_{2r}
items.statement: V′_{2r} is a hermitian space over F (F/F⁺ unramified) together with a lattice Λ′_{2r} satisfying Λ′_{2r} ⊆ (Λ′_{2r})^∨ and (Λ′_{2r})^∨/Λ′_{2r} ≃ κ. Put U′_{2r} := U(V′_{2r}) and let K′_{2r} be the stabilizer of Λ′_{2r}, a special maximal subgroup of U′_{2r}(F⁺).
items.note: V′_{2r} is the non-split hermitian space of rank 2r (odd discriminant valuation), U′_{2r} is not quasi-split; the reductive quotient of K′_{2r} is U_1 × U_{2r−1} over κ⁺. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Lemma C.2.4 — base change of K′_{2r}-spherical representations of the non-split U′_{2r}
items.statement: Let π′ be an irreducible admissible representation of U′_{2r}(F⁺) such that (π′)^{K′_{2r}} ≠ {0}. Then there exists (α_2,…,α_r) ∈ (ℂ^×)^{r−1} with 1 ≤ |α_2| ≤ ⋯ ≤ |α_r|, unique up to permutation (correctly: up to permutation and inversion of the entries of absolute value 1), such that BC(π′) is isomorphic to the unique irreducible quotient of I^{GL_{2r}}(α̲_r^{−1} ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_2^{−1} ⊠ St_2 ⊠ α̲_2 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_r).
items.locator: §C.2, Lemma C.2.4, published p. 360; proof p. 360–362
items.note: Published label Lemma C.2.4 (earlier version of this extraction: 'Proposition C.2.4'). Proof: π′ is a constituent of I_{P_min}^G(𝟏′_2 ⊠ α̲_2 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_r); τ_0 := the unique summand of I_{P_{0min}}^{G_0}(𝟏′_2 ⊠ α̲_2 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_{r_0}) with nonzero K′_{2r} ∩ G_0(F⁺)-invariants; claim (C.5) J_P^G(τ_0 ⊠ ⋯)^{K′_{2r}} ≠ 0, reduced by [39, Cor. 3.2] to T_wφ′_α ≠ 0 (C.6), which follows from the nonvanishing of the spherical c-function C(α) (issue: the printed C(α) is not right, conclusion unaffected). Then BC(π′) is the unique irreducible quotient of I^{GL_{2r}}((⊠_{i=t}^1 τ_i^{∨c}(|α_{r_0+⋯+r_i}^{−1}|̲∘det)) ⊠ BC(τ_0) ⊠ (⊠_{i=1}^t τ_i(|α_{r_0+⋯+r_i}|̲∘det))) with BC(τ_0) ≅ I^{GL_{2r_0}}(α̲_{r_0}^{−1} ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ BC(𝟏′) ⊠ ⋯) ≅ I(⋯ ⊠ St_2 ⊠ ⋯) irreducible. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Parabolic, Levi and spherical vector φ′_α for U′_{2r} (proof of Lemma C.2.4)
items.statement: Fix a decomposition Λ′_{2r} = O_Fe_{−r} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ O_Fe_{−2} ⊕ Λ′_2 ⊕ O_Fe_2 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ O_Fe_r with (e_{−i}, e_j) = δ_{ij} for 2 ≤ i, j ≤ r (Λ′_2 a lattice of an anisotropic hermitian plane with Λ′_2^∨/Λ′_2 ≃ κ). For 1 ≤ i ≤ r put V′_{2i} := Fe_{−i} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ Fe_{−2} ⊕ Λ′_2 ⊗_{O_F} F ⊕ Fe_2 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ Fe_i. P_min ⊆ G := U′_{2r} is the stabilizer of the flag Fe_{−r} ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ Fe_{−r} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ Fe_{−2}, with Levi U(V′_2) × Res_{F/F⁺}GL(Fe_2) × ⋯ × Res_{F/F⁺}GL(Fe_r); the Weyl group W′_{2r} ≃ W_{2r−2} embeds in K′_{2r}. For α = (α_2,…,α_r) ∈ (ℂ^×)^{r−1}, φ′_α is the element of I_{P_min}^G(𝟏′_2 ⊠ α̲_2 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_r) taking value 1 on K′_{2r}, where 𝟏′_2 is the trivial representation of U(V′_2)(F⁺).
items.locator: §C.2, proof of Lemma C.2.4, published p. 360
items.note: Well defined by the Iwasawa decomposition G = P_min K′_{2r}; I(𝟏′_2 ⊠ α̲)^{K′_{2r}} is one-dimensional, so exactly one constituent is K′_{2r}-spherical. Relative root system of type BC_{r−1}. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Spherical intertwining constant C(α) for U′_{2r} (proof of Lemma C.2.4)
items.locator: §C.2, proof of Lemma C.2.4, published p. 362
items.note: From Casselman [15, Theorem 3.1] (Macdonald's formula) 'and the continuity'. The printed formula uses α_1, which is undefined here (α = (α_2,…,α_r)); see issue. By Macdonald's formula (both maximal parahorics of the rank-one non-quasi-split U(V′_4) have reductive quotient U_1 × U_3, parameter q^3) the correct expression is C(α) = ∏_{i=r_0+1}^{r} ( (α_i − q^{−3})/(α_i − 1) · ∏_{j≥2, |α_j|<|α_i|} (α_i − q^{−2}α_j)/(α_i − α_j) · ∏_{j=2}^{i−1} (α_iα_j − q^{−2})/(α_iα_j − 1) ), which equals the printed product with α_1 := q and j ≥ 2 in the middle product. Nonvanishing (all that is used) holds in every reading since |α_i| > 1. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: BC(Sp_2) ≅ St_2 and BC(𝟏′) ≅ St_2 (used without reference)
items.statement: Let Sp_2 be the Steinberg representation of the quasi-split U(V_2)(F⁺) and 𝟏′ the trivial representation of the anisotropic U(V′_2)(F⁺) (F/F⁺ unramified). Then BC(Sp_2) ≅ St_2 and BC(𝟏′) ≅ St_2. Consequently, for α_2,…,α_{r_0} unimodular, BC of the relevant summand τ_0 is I^{GL_{2r_0}}(α̲_{r_0}^{−1} ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_2^{−1} ⊠ St_2 ⊠ α̲_2 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_{r_0}), which is irreducible.
items.locator: §C.2, proofs of Lemma C.2.2(2) (p. 360) and Lemma C.2.4 (p. 362)
items.note: Used without citation; follows from the local Langlands correspondence of [33,53] (the discrete parameter S_2 of U(2) has Vogan packet {Sp_2, 𝟏′}) or from Rogawski [63]. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Proposition C.2.5 — local Jacquet–Langlands bijection 𝒮 ↔ 𝒮′
items.statement: Let 𝒮 be the set of isomorphism classes of irreducible admissible representations π of U_{2r}(F⁺) such that π|_{K_{2r}} contains Ω_{2r} and the Satake parameter of BC(π) contains {q, q^{−1}} (Remark 3.1.6); let 𝒮′ be the set of isomorphism classes of irreducible admissible representations π′ of U′_{2r}(F⁺) such that π′|_{K′_{2r}} contains the trivial representation. Then there is a unique bijection between 𝒮 and 𝒮′ such that π and π′ correspond if and only if BC(π) ≃ BC(π′).
items.locator: §C.2, Proposition C.2.5, published p. 362; proof p. 363
items.note: Proof: BC(π), BC(π′) are constituents of unramified principal series; define the correspondence by α(BC(π)) = α(BC(π′)); Lemmas C.2.2 and C.2.4 give that it is a bijection and that corresponding representations have isomorphic BC. (Both sets are in bijection with (α_2,…,α_r) modulo the Weyl group of type BC_{r−1}.) Published label Proposition C.2.5 (v1: Proposition C.2.2, with extra conditions 'multiplicity one' and 'not {−1,−1}' dropped later). Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Remark C.2.6 — compatibility with the local theta correspondence
items.statement: For π ∈ 𝒮 and π′ ∈ 𝒮′ corresponding under Proposition C.2.5, they should also correspond under the local theta correspondence with respect to the trivial splitting character; when q is odd this has been verified in [49].
items.note: Expectation plus citation of Liu [49]; not used later. Missing: routed to the Part II UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators (route 14).

items.name: Proposition C.3.1(1) — multiplicity one for the global packet of a relevant Π
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be a totally imaginary quadratic extension of a totally real number field, Π a relevant representation of GL_N(𝔸_F) (Definition 1.1.3: cuspidal automorphic, Π∘c ≃ Π^∨, and Π_w for archimedean w the principal series induced from (arg^{1−N}, arg^{3−N}, …, arg^{N−1})), V a standard definite or indefinite hermitian space over F of rank N, and π = ⊗_vπ_v an irreducible admissible representation of U(V)(𝔸_{F⁺}). If BC(π_v) ≃ Π_v for every place v of F⁺, then the discrete automorphic multiplicity of π is 1.
items.note: Proof: consequence of Kaletha–Minguez–Shin–White [33, Theorem 1.7.1] for generic packets (Π cuspidal gives a simple generic parameter, for which the multiplicity formula gives 1 for every member of the global packet on every pure inner form). Cited black box. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Proposition C.3.1(2) — local–global compatibility of automorphic base change
items.statement: In the setting of Proposition C.3.1: if π is automorphic and Π is its automorphic base change (Definition 3.2.3), then BC(π_v) ≃ Π_v holds for every place v of F⁺. In particular, the discrete automorphic multiplicity of π is 1 by (1).
items.note: Consequence of [33, Theorem 1.7.1]; used repeatedly in §6 (e.g. BC(π_p) ≃ BC(π)_p). Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Proposition C.3.1(3) — archimedean places other than τ̲_∞
items.statement: In the setting of Proposition C.3.1: if v is archimedean but not τ̲_∞, then BC(π_v) ≃ Π_v if and only if π_v is the trivial representation.
items.note: The paper says (3), (4) follow from (1), (2) and the definition of relevant representations; in substance this is archimedean local base change (V_v is definite at v ≠ τ̲_∞, and the L-packet of the parameter of Π_v on the compact U(N) is the trivial representation). Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Proposition C.3.1(4) — the default archimedean place τ̲_∞
items.statement: In the setting of Proposition C.3.1: if v = τ̲_∞, then BC(π_v) ≃ Π_v if and only if π_v is the trivial representation (resp. is one of the N discrete series representations with Harish-Chandra parameter {(1−N)/2, (3−N)/2, …, (N−3)/2, (N−1)/2}) when V is definite (resp. indefinite).
items.note: As for (3): archimedean local Langlands/base change for U(N,0) and U(N−1,1); the discrete series L-packet of U(N−1,1) with the Harish-Chandra parameter of the trivial representation has N members. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Corollary C.3.2 — even-rank global Jacquet–Langlands transfer (definite → indefinite)
items.statement: Take a prime 𝔭 of F⁺ inert in F. Let V and V′ be a standard definite and a standard indefinite hermitian space over F, respectively, of even rank N = 2r, with fixed isomorphisms V_v ≃ V′_v for every place v of F⁺ other than τ̲_∞ and 𝔭. Let π be an automorphic representation of U(V)(𝔸_{F⁺}) such that π_∞ is trivial, BC(π) (Definition 3.2.3; it exists by Proposition 3.2.8) is cuspidal, and π_𝔭 belongs to the set 𝒮 of Proposition C.2.5 (in particular V ⊗_{F⁺} F⁺_𝔭 admits a self-dual lattice). Consider π′ := π′_{τ̲_∞} ⊗ π′_𝔭 ⊗ π^{τ̲_∞,𝔭} of U(V′)(𝔸_{F⁺}) where π′_{τ̲_∞} is a discrete series representation of U(V′)(F⁺_{τ̲_∞}) with Harish-Chandra parameter {1/2 − r, 3/2 − r, …, r − 3/2, r − 1/2}, and π′_𝔭 ∈ 𝒮′ is the representation of U(V′)(F⁺_𝔭) corresponding to π_𝔭 in Proposition C.2.5. Then the discrete automorphic multiplicity of π′ is 1.
items.note: Proof: with Π := BC(π) (relevant), Propositions C.3.1 and C.2.5 give BC(π′_v) ≃ Π_v at every place; conclude by C.3.1(1). Published label Corollary C.3.2 (earlier version of this extraction: 'Proposition C.3.2'). Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Corollary C.3.3 — odd-rank transfer (indefinite → definite)
items.statement: Take a prime 𝔭 of F⁺ inert in F. Let V and V′ be a standard definite and a standard indefinite hermitian space over F, respectively, of odd rank N = 2r+1, with fixed isomorphisms V_v ≃ V′_v for every place v of F⁺ other than τ̲_∞ and 𝔭. Let π′ be an automorphic representation of U(V′)(𝔸_{F⁺}) such that BC(π′) exists and is cuspidal, π′_{τ̲_∞} is a discrete series representation of U(V′)(F⁺_{τ̲_∞}) with Harish-Chandra parameter {−r, 1−r, …, r−1, r}, π′_τ is trivial for every archimedean place τ ≠ τ̲_∞, and π′_𝔭 is unramified. Consider π := π_{τ̲_∞} ⊗ π_𝔭 ⊗ (π′)^{τ̲_∞,𝔭} of U(V)(𝔸_{F⁺}) where π_{τ̲_∞} is trivial and π_𝔭 is unramified with BC(π_𝔭) ≃ BC(π′_𝔭). Then the discrete automorphic multiplicity of π is 1.
items.note: Proof: with Π′ := BC(π′), BC(π_v) ≃ Π′_v at every place (at 𝔭 by the hypothesis and C.3.1(2), at τ̲_∞ by C.3.1(4)); conclude by C.3.1(1). The proof also cites Proposition C.2.5, which concerns even rank and plays no role (issue). Published label Corollary C.3.3. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Definition D.1.1 — cohomologically generic homomorphism
items.statement: Let N ≥ 1 and let Σ⁺ be a finite set of nonarchimedean places of F⁺ containing Σ⁺_bad (the places above rational primes ramified in F). A homomorphism φ : 𝕋_N^{Σ⁺} → κ, κ a field, is cohomologically generic if H^i_ét(Sh(V,K)_{F̄}, κ)_{𝕋_N^{Σ⁺′} ∩ ker φ} = 0 for every finite set Σ⁺′ ⊇ Σ⁺ of nonarchimedean places of F⁺, every integer i ≠ N − 1, every standard indefinite hermitian space V over F of dimension N, and every object K ∈ 𝔎(V) of the form K_{Σ⁺′} × ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺′} U(Λ)(O_{F⁺_v}) for a self-dual ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺′} O_{F_v}-lattice Λ in V ⊗_F 𝔸_F^{Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺′}.
items.note: Localization is at the prime ideal 𝕋_N^{Σ⁺′} ∩ ker φ of the subalgebra 𝕋_N^{Σ⁺′} ⊆ 𝕋_N^{Σ⁺} (Definition 3.1.9). Setup of §3 is kept. Used in Remark 6.1.5 (implies Assumption 6.1.4 via Lemma 5.2.7 and universal coefficients) and conditions (L7). Missing: routed to a source of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 (route 8).

items.name: Definition D.1.2 — decomposed generic at a split place
items.statement: Let φ : 𝕋_N^{Σ⁺} → κ be a homomorphism, κ a field. For a place w of F⁺ not in Σ⁺ that splits in F, φ is decomposed generic at w if φ(H_w) ∈ κ[T] has distinct (nonzero) roots, among which there is no pair with ratio equal to ‖w‖. Here H_w ∈ 𝕋_{N,w}[T] is 'the Hecke polynomial'. (Footnote 37: as pointed out in [13, Remark 1.4], there is no need to assume that the roots are distinct.)
items.locator: §D.1, Definition D.1.2 and footnote 37, published p. 365
items.note: 'Essentially [12, Definition 1.9]'. H_w is not defined anywhere in the paper (issue). Intended: the monic degree-N polynomial over 𝕋_{N,w} whose roots under any character of 𝕋_{N,w} are, up to a common scalar, the Satake parameters at one of the two places of F above w; the condition is independent of that choice because the parameters at the conjugate place are the inverses (Definition 3.1.3(2)). Planned: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.7 plans integral and residual exports.
