items.name: Proposition D.1.3 — vanishing off the middle degree (Caraiani–Scholze without the similitude restrictions)
items.statement: Let N ≥ 1, let Σ⁺ be a finite set of nonarchimedean places of F⁺ containing Σ⁺_bad, let V be a standard indefinite hermitian space over F of dimension N such that V_v is split for v ∉ Σ⁺_∞ ∪ Σ⁺, and let φ : 𝕋_N^{Σ⁺} → F̄_ℓ be a homomorphism. Suppose that F⁺ ≠ ℚ and that there exists a place w of F⁺ not in Σ⁺ ∪ Σ⁺_ℓ that splits in F such that φ is decomposed generic at w. Then H^i_ét(Sh(V,K)_{F̄}, F̄_ℓ)_{ker φ} = 0 for every integer i ≠ N − 1 and every object K ∈ 𝔎(V) of the form K_{Σ⁺} × ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺} U(Λ)(O_{F⁺_v}) for a self-dual ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺} O_{F_v}-lattice Λ in V ⊗_F 𝔸_F^{Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺}.
items.locator: §D.1, Proposition D.1.3, published p. 365; proof p. 366–368
items.note: Published label Proposition D.1.3 (arXiv v1/v2: Theorem D.1.3). When F contains an imaginary quadratic field and every place of Σ⁺ splits in F, it follows from Case 2 of [12, Theorem 6.3.1(2)] for the unitary similitude group. In general the proof is a sketch: pass to the Hodge-type datum (G × T, h × h_Φ), modify [12, Theorem 5.2.3/Corollary 5.2.5] for the honest unitary group, use [71, Corollary 4.7] and the association claim of [72, Proposition 1.4] with test functions φ_Σ ⊗ φ^Σ, and conclude that the argument towards [12, Theorem 6.3.1(2)] only uses [12, Theorem 5.5.7]. The proof as written assumes that K_{w_0,0} = ∏_{v|w_0}U(Λ)(O_{F⁺_v}) is hyperspecial, i.e. that no place of F⁺ above the rational prime w_0 below w lies in Σ⁺ — not a hypothesis of the statement (issue). Intro (p. 110) refers to it as 'Proposition D.1.3'. Missing: routed to a source of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 (route 8).

items.name: Caraiani–Scholze [12]: generic part of cohomology of compact unitary Shimura varieties (cited)
items.statement: (As used) For a compact unitary (similitude) Shimura variety attached to a CM field F containing an imaginary quadratic field, with the relevant places split, and a maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra that is decomposed generic, the localized F̄_ℓ-cohomology vanishes outside the middle degree (Case 2 of [12, Theorem 6.3.1(2)]); the argument towards [12, Theorem 6.3.1(2)] only uses [12, Theorem 5.5.7], and the discussion of [12] outside §5 is valid for all proper Shimura varieties of Hodge type.
items.locator: §D.1, proof of Proposition D.1.3, published p. 366–368
items.note: Black box from Caraiani–Scholze, Ann. of Math. 186 (2017). The paper's use: reduction of Proposition D.1.3 to [12, Theorem 5.5.7] after modifying [12, §5] (Mantovan formula and trace formula for Igusa varieties). Missing: routed to a source of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 (route 8).

items.name: Auxiliary Hodge-type Shimura datum (G̃, h̃) = (G × T, h × h_Φ) and its integral model
items.statement: In the proof of Proposition D.1.3: let w_0 be the rational prime under w and fix ℂ ≃ Q̄_{w_0} inducing w. G := Res_{F⁺/ℚ}U(V) with Deligne homomorphism h (§3.2); K_{w_0,0} := ∏_{v|w_0} U(Λ)(O_{F⁺_v}) (asserted hyperspecial in G(ℚ_{w_0})). Fix a character ϖ : F^×\𝔸_F^× → ℂ^× unramified outside Σ⁺ with ϖ|_{𝔸_{F⁺}^×} = η_{F/F⁺}; Σ := {p | Σ⁺_p ∩ Σ⁺ ≠ ∅}. T ⊆ Res_{F/ℚ}𝔾_m is the torus with T(R) = {a ∈ F ⊗_ℚ R | Nm_{F/F⁺}a ∈ R^×}. Fix a CM type Φ containing τ_∞ such that all elements of Φ inducing the place w of F⁺ induce the same place of F, and a sufficiently small K_T ⊆ T(𝔸^∞) with (K_T)_p maximal for p ∉ Σ; Φ gives h_Φ : Res_{ℂ/ℝ}𝔾_m → T ⊗_ℚ ℝ; 𝔗 := T(𝔸^{∞,w_0})/T(ℤ_{(w_0)})K_T^{w_0} (cf. Definition 3.5.5). Then (G̃, h̃) := (G × T, h × h_Φ) is a Shimura datum of Hodge type with reflex field F.F_Φ ⊆ ℂ; for sufficiently small K ⊆ G(𝔸^∞), Sh(G̃, h̃)_{K×K_T} is smooth projective over F.F_Φ (as F⁺ ≠ ℚ) of dimension N − 1; for K = K^{w_0}K_{w_0,0} it has a canonical smooth projective model 𝒮(G̃, h̃)_{K^{w_0}} over W(F̄_{w_0}) with a moduli interpretation similar to §4.2, and F.F_Φ ⊆ W(F̄_{w_0})_ℚ.
items.locator: §D.1, proof of Proposition D.1.3, published p. 366
items.note: B(G̃, μ̃) → B(G, μ) is a bijection of Kottwitz sets and J̃_b ≃ J_b × T. For K^{w_0} ⊆ G(𝔸^{∞,w_0}) and m ≥ 1 there are Igusa varieties 𝒥^b_{Mant,K^{w_0},m} (𝔗-schemes over F̄_{w_0}) and [H_{𝔗,c}(𝒥^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)] := ⊕_i (−1)^i lim_{K^{w_0},m} H^i_{𝔗,c}(𝒥^b_{Mant,K^{w_0},m}, Q̄_ℓ), a virtual representation of G(𝔸^{∞,w_0}) × J_b(ℚ_{w_0}). The hyperspecial claim needs Σ⁺_{w_0} ∩ Σ⁺ = ∅ (issue). Missing: routed to a source of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 (route 8).

items.name: Stable trace formula for Igusa varieties of the honest unitary group (modified [12, Theorem 5.2.3])
items.statement: tr(φ | H_{𝔗,c}(𝒥^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)) = Σ_{(H,s,η)} ι(G, H)·ST_e^H(φ^H), the sum over equivalence classes of elliptic endoscopic triples (H, s, η) of G, using ϖ for the Langlands–Shelstad transfer; with representatives as in [12, p. 734] without the similitude factor this becomes tr(φ | H_{𝔗,c}(𝒥^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)) = Σ_{G_n} ι(G, G_n)·ST_e^{G_n}(φ^n) (modified [12, Corollary 5.2.5]).
items.locator: §D.1, proof of Proposition D.1.3, published p. 367
items.note: 'Can be proved in the same way as for [70, Theorem 7.2]' (Shin's stable trace formula for Igusa varieties), since the Shimura variety has a moduli interpretation as in §4.2 although (G̃, h̃) is not of PEL type. Asserted, not proved in detail. Missing: routed to a source of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 (route 8).

items.name: Stable/twisted comparison I_geom^{𝔾_nθ}(f^nθ) = τ(G_n)^{−1}ST_e^{G_n}(φ^n) (cited)
items.statement: With 𝔾_n := Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n ⋊ {1, θ}: I_geom^{𝔾_nθ}(f^nθ) = τ(G_n)^{−1}·ST_e^{G_n}(φ^n) holds as long as f^n and φ^n are associated in the sense of [41, 3.2].
items.locator: §D.1, proof of Proposition D.1.3, published p. 367
items.note: Cited as [12, Proposition 5.3.1] 'or rather' Shin [71, Corollary 4.7]. The paper notes that at rational primes in Σ there is no explicit local base change transfer. Missing: routed to a source of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 (route 8).

items.name: Associated functions for characteristic functions at Σ (cited from the proof of [72, Proposition 1.4])
items.statement: For the test function φ ∈ C_c^∞(G(𝔸^{∞,w_0}) × J_b(ℚ_{w_0})) of [12, Theorem 5.3.2], if φ = φ_Σ ⊗ φ^Σ with φ_Σ the characteristic function of some open compact subgroup K_Σ ⊆ G(ℚ_Σ), then for every G_n the function φ^n is associated to some f^n; for such φ, tr(φ | H_{𝔗,c}(𝒥^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)) = Σ_{G_n} ι(G, G_n)·I_spec^{𝔾_nθ}(f^nθ).
items.locator: §D.1, proof of Proposition D.1.3, published p. 367
items.note: Association 'shown in the claim in the proof of [72, Proposition 1.4]' (Shin, cohomological base change for unitary similitude groups), following an idea in [72]; the spectral identity uses [12, (5.3.2)]. The remaining argument toward [12, Theorem 5.5.7] is 'the same as on the GL-side' with these test functions. Missing: routed to a source of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 (route 8).

items.name: Corollary D.1.4 — cohomological genericity for almost all λ
items.statement: Let the situation be as in §6.1 (Π a relevant representation of GL_N(𝔸_F), E ⊆ ℂ a strong coefficient field of Π, finite sets Σ⁺_min ⊇ Σ⁺_Π, Σ⁺_lr, Σ⁺ ⊇ Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_lr, and φ_Π : 𝕋_N^{Σ⁺} → O_E from Construction 3.1.10). Suppose F⁺ ≠ ℚ. Then for all but finitely many primes λ of E, the composite homomorphism 𝕋_N^{Σ⁺} → O_E → O_E/λ (D.1) is cohomologically generic (Definition D.1.1).
items.note: Published label Corollary D.1.4 (earlier version of this extraction: 'Proposition D.1.4'). Proof: choose a place w of F with Π_w unramified with distinct nonzero algebraic Satake parameters α_1,…,α_N ([16, proof of Prop. 3.2.5]); genericity of Π_w gives α_i/α_j ∉ {1, ‖w‖} (i ≠ j), which persists in F̄_ℓ for ℓ large; Chebotarev then yields infinitely many places of F⁺ outside Σ⁺ ∪ Σ⁺_ℓ, split in F, at which (D.1) is decomposed generic; conclude by Proposition D.1.3. Chebotarev must be applied to ρ̄_{Π,λ} together with the mod-ℓ cyclotomic character (issue). Used for (L7) in §8. Missing: routed to a source of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 (route 8).

items.name: A place with regular unramified Satake parameter (cited, Chenevier–Harris)
items.statement: For Π relevant, there is a nonarchimedean place w of F such that Π_w is unramified and its Satake parameter consists of N distinct elements α_1,…,α_N, which are nonzero algebraic numbers. Since Π_w is generic, α_i/α_j ∉ {1, ‖w‖} for i ≠ j.
items.locator: §D.1, proof of Corollary D.1.4, published p. 368
items.note: 'As pointed out in the proof of [16, Proposition 3.2.5]'. The ratio condition α_i/α_j ≠ ‖w‖ is irreducibility of the generic unramified principal series. Missing: routed to a source of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII (route 5).

items.name: §D.2 setup — Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_lr, V, Λ, K, φ_Π
items.statement: Let N = 2r be an even positive integer. Consider: a relevant representation Π of GL_N(𝔸_F); two disjoint finite sets Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_lr of nonarchimedean places of F⁺ such that Σ⁺_min ⊇ Σ⁺_bad, Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_lr ⊇ Σ⁺_Π (Notation 3.1.4) and every place in Σ⁺_lr is inert in F; a finite set Σ⁺ ⊇ Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_lr of nonarchimedean places; a standard definite or indefinite hermitian space V over F of rank N with V_v not split for v ∈ Σ⁺_lr; a self-dual ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_lr} O_{F_v}-lattice Λ in V ⊗_F 𝔸_F^{Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_lr}; and K ∈ 𝔎(V) of the form K = ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_lr} K_v × ∏_{v∉Σ⁺_∞∪Σ⁺_min∪Σ⁺_lr} U(Λ)(O_{F⁺_v}) with K_v special maximal for v ∈ Σ⁺_lr. φ_Π : 𝕋_N^{Σ⁺} → Q̄_ℓ is the homomorphism given by Π, and ι_ℓ : ℂ ≃ Q̄_ℓ is fixed.
items.note: φ_Π is really the ℂ-valued (O_{ℚ(Π)}-valued) homomorphism of Construction 3.1.10; the paper then uses ι_ℓφ_Π, so the printed codomain Q̄_ℓ is a slip (issue). [ι_ℓφ_Π] denotes the ι_ℓφ_Π-eigenspace. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Definition D.2.1 — transferable open compact subgroup
items.statement: Let v be a nonarchimedean place of F⁺. An open compact subgroup K_v of U(V)(F⁺_v) is transferable if: (1) for every endoscopic group H of U(V_v) there exist an endoscopic transfer f^H_{K_v} of 𝟙_{K_v} to H and a compactly supported smooth function φ^H_{K_v} on H(F_v) such that f^H_{K_v} and φ^H_{K_v} are associated in the sense of [41, §3.2]; and (2) when H is the quasi-split unitary group of rank N, φ^H_{K_v} can be taken to be supported on a maximal open compact subgroup of H(F_v) (which is isomorphic to GL_N(F_v)).
items.note: H(F_v) means the points over F_v = F ⊗_{F⁺} F⁺_v of H, i.e. the group on which twisted base change functions live (GL_N(F_v) for the quasi-split U_N). Footnote 38: condition (2) is not needed for Proposition D.2.3, only for its application Proposition 6.4.1. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Inertial transfer φ_{K_v}
items.statement: If K_v is transferable, the function φ^H_{K_v} of Definition D.2.1(2) (H the quasi-split unitary group of rank N, φ^H_{K_v} supported on a maximal open compact subgroup of H(F_v) ≅ GL_N(F_v) and associated to an endoscopic transfer of 𝟙_{K_v}) is called an inertial transfer of K_v; the superscript H is dropped: φ_{K_v}.
items.note: Appears in Proposition D.2.3 as tr(Π_v(φ_{K_v}) ∘ A_{Π_v}). Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Lemma D.2.2(1) — split places: every level transferable
items.statement: Let v be a nonarchimedean place of F⁺. If v splits in F, then every open compact subgroup K_v of U(V)(F⁺_v) is transferable.
items.note: 'Part (1) is trivial' (U(V)(F⁺_v) ≅ GL_N(F⁺_v); endoscopic groups are Levi-type, transfer by constant terms). Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Lemma D.2.2(2) — hyperspecial levels: fundamental lemmas
items.statement: If v ∉ Σ⁺_∞ ∪ Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_lr, then (the characteristic function of) the hyperspecial maximal subgroup U(Λ)(O_{F⁺_v}) is transferable and admits 𝟙_{GL_N(O_{F_v})} as an inertial transfer.
items.note: Combination of the endoscopic fundamental lemma (Laumon–Ngô [45]) and the base change fundamental lemma ([41], Labesse). Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Lemma D.2.2(3) — small levels are transferable
items.statement: If v ∈ Σ⁺_min ∪ Σ⁺_lr, then every sufficiently small open compact subgroup K_v of U(V)(F⁺_v) is transferable.
items.note: Condition (1) of Definition D.2.1 for sufficiently small K_v is [54, Lemma 8.4.1(1)] (Morel); condition (2) by [41, Proposition 3.1.7(2)] (see the proof of [41, Proposition 3.3.2]). Used in §6 (footnote 24) and §8. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Fundamental lemma for unitary groups (cited)
items.statement: (As used) For an unramified unitary group U(V_v) over F⁺_v with hyperspecial K_v and an unramified endoscopic group H, the characteristic function 𝟙_{K_v} admits as endoscopic transfer the characteristic function of a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup of H(F⁺_v) (suitably normalized).
items.locator: §D.2, proof of Lemma D.2.2(2), published p. 369
items.note: Laumon–Ngô [45]. Black box. Planned: EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.3 plans the fundamental lemma and local transfer, including Labesse's base change.

items.name: Base change fundamental lemma and local transfer (cited, Labesse)
items.statement: (As used) The characteristic function of a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup of an unramified unitary group H over F⁺_v is associated (in the sense of [41, §3.2]) to the characteristic function of the corresponding maximal compact subgroup of H(F_v) (for H = U_N: 𝟙_{GL_N(O_{F_v})}); and (Proposition 3.1.7(2)) for sufficiently small levels the associated function can be chosen supported on a maximal open compact subgroup.
items.locator: §D.2, proof of Lemma D.2.2(2),(3), published p. 369; also §D.1 p. 367
items.note: Labesse [41] (Astérisque 257). Black box. Planned: EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.3 plans the fundamental lemma and local transfer, including Labesse's base change.

items.name: Existence of endoscopic transfers for small levels (cited, Morel)
items.statement: (As used) For every sufficiently small open compact subgroup K_v of U(V)(F⁺_v) and every endoscopic group H, 𝟙_{K_v} has an endoscopic transfer f^H_{K_v} that is associated to a compactly supported smooth function on H(F_v).
items.locator: §D.2, proof of Lemma D.2.2(3), published p. 369
items.note: Morel [54, Lemma 8.4.1(1)]. Black box. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Indicator c_v for v ∈ Σ⁺_lr
items.statement: For v ∈ Σ⁺_lr, c_v := 1 if there are complex numbers α_2,…,α_r of norm one such that Π_v ≅ I^{GL_{2r}}(α̲_r^{−1} ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_2^{−1} ⊠ St_2 ⊠ α̲_2 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α̲_r) (notation of §C.1), and c_v := 0 otherwise.
items.note: c_v = 1 exactly when Π_v (tempered, by Proposition 3.2.4(1)) is the base change of a K_v-spherical representation of the non-split U(V_v) (Lemma C.2.4). Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Normalized intertwining operator A_{Π_v} (cited)
items.statement: For v ∈ Σ⁺_min, A_{Π_v} denotes a normalized intertwining operator for Π_v in the sense of [71, §4.1]: an isomorphism between Π_v and its twist by the automorphism θ defining twisted (unitary) base change on GL_N(F_v) (possible since Π_v^{∨c} ≃ Π_v), normalized as in [71, §4.1]; tr(Π_v(φ) ∘ A_{Π_v}) is the corresponding twisted trace of a test function φ on GL_N(F_v).
items.note: Shin [71, §4.1]; cited, not re-defined in the paper. Proposition D.2.3 allows any normalized choice; the absolute values make the formula independent of the choice. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Proposition D.2.3 — dimension of old forms in the L-packet (indefinite case)
items.statement: In the setup of §D.2, suppose that K_v is transferable for v ∈ Σ⁺_min. If V is standard indefinite, then dim H^{N−1}_ét(Sh(V,K)_{F̄}, Q̄_ℓ)[ι_ℓφ_Π] = N·| ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min} tr(Π_v(φ_{K_v}) ∘ A_{Π_v}) · ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_lr} c_v | for any inertial transfer φ_{K_v} of K_v and any normalized intertwining operator A_{Π_v} for Π_v [71, §4.1], v ∈ Σ⁺_min.
items.locator: §D.2, Proposition D.2.3, published p. 369–370; proof p. 370–372
items.note: Proof (indefinite case only): Π is tempered everywhere (Prop. 3.2.4(1)), so every discrete π with automorphic base change Π is cuspidal and H^i[ι_ℓφ_Π] = 0 for i ≠ N−1; if some c_v = 0 then H^{N−1}[ι_ℓφ_Π] = 0 by Lemma C.2.4; otherwise Proposition C.3.1 and Lemma C.2.4 give dim = N∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min} Σ_{BC(π_v)≃Π_v} dim(π_v)^{K_v}, and (D.2) ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min} Σ_{BC(π_v)≃Π_v} dim(π_v)^{K_v} = |∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min} tr(Π_v(φ_{K_v}) ∘ A_{Π_v})| is proved by a quadratic base change F̆⁺/F⁺ to a definite unitary group and Shin's trace identity [72, (1.8) & (1.9)], taking square roots. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Proposition D.2.3 — dimension of old forms (definite case)
items.statement: In the setup of §D.2, suppose that K_v is transferable for v ∈ Σ⁺_min. If V is standard definite, then dim Q̄_ℓ[Sh(V,K)][ι_ℓφ_Π] = | ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min} tr(Π_v(φ_{K_v}) ∘ A_{Π_v}) · ∏_{v∈Σ⁺_lr} c_v | for any inertial transfer φ_{K_v} and any normalized intertwining operator A_{Π_v} (v ∈ Σ⁺_min).
items.note: Proof 'left to the readers' (slightly easier than the indefinite case): same argument without the archimedean factor N (π_{τ̲_∞} trivial by C.3.1(4)). Used with Lemma 6.4.2 to get d_unr = d_ram. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Vanishing of H^i[ι_ℓφ_Π] off the middle degree (proof of D.2.3)
items.statement: In the setup of §D.2 with V standard indefinite: every discrete automorphic representation of U(V)(𝔸_{F⁺}) whose automorphic base change is isomorphic to Π is cuspidal, and H^i_ét(Sh(V,K)_{F̄}, Q̄_ℓ)[ι_ℓφ_Π] = 0 for i ≠ N − 1. If moreover c_v = 1 for all v ∈ Σ⁺_lr, then dim H^{N−1}_ét(Sh(V,K)_{F̄}, Q̄_ℓ)[ι_ℓφ_Π] = N·∏_{v∈Σ⁺_min} Σ_{BC(π_v)≃Π_v} dim(π_v)^{K_v}, the sum over isomorphism classes of irreducible admissible π_v of U(V)(F⁺_v) with BC(π_v) ≃ Π_v; if some c_v = 0 the left side is 0.
items.locator: §D.2, proof of Proposition D.2.3, published p. 370
items.note: Uses Proposition 3.2.4(1) (Π tempered everywhere), Proposition C.3.1 (multiplicity one; the N discrete series at τ̲_∞) and Lemma C.2.4 (at v ∈ Σ⁺_lr exactly one K_v-spherical π_v, with one-dimensional invariants, iff c_v = 1). Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.name: Auxiliary totally real quadratic extension F̆⁺/F⁺ and definite V̆ (proof of D.2.3)
items.statement: Choose a quadratic totally real extension F̆⁺/F⁺ in ℂ such that every prime in Σ⁺_min splits in F̆⁺, every prime in Σ⁺_lr is inert in F̆⁺, and the quadratic base change Π̆ of Π to F̆ := F.F̆⁺ remains cuspidal (hence relevant); such F̆⁺ exists by the same proof as [71, Proposition 7.4]. Let V̆ be the standard definite hermitian space over F̆ of rank N that is split at all primes not above Σ⁺_min and satisfies V̆_{v̆} ≃ V_v for every v ∈ Σ⁺_min and every prime v̆ of F̆⁺ above v (it exists since [F̆⁺ : F⁺] = 2). Let Σ̆⁺_min be the set of primes of F̆⁺ above Σ⁺_min and Σ̆⁺ ⊇ Σ̆⁺_min a finite set of primes of F̆⁺ such that Π̆_{v̆} is unramified for v̆ ∉ Σ̆⁺ and every prime in Σ̆⁺ \ Σ̆⁺_min splits in F̆. Take K̆ = ∏K̆_{v̆} ∈ 𝔎(V̆) with K̆_{v̆} hyperspecial maximal for v̆ ∉ Σ̆⁺, K̆_{v̆} = K_v (under V̆_{v̆} ≃ V_v) for v̆ above v ∈ Σ⁺_min, and Π̆_{v̆} having nonzero K̆_{v̆} × K̆_{v̆}-invariants for v̆ ∈ Σ̆⁺ \ Σ̆⁺_min.
items.locator: §D.2, proof of Proposition D.2.3, published p. 370–371
items.note: Existence of V̆: the product of local Hasse invariants is 1 because each v ∈ Σ⁺_min splits into two places with the same local space and the archimedean places come in pairs. Primes above Σ⁺_lr become split in F̆ (F_v and F̆⁺_{v̆} are the same unramified quadratic extension of F⁺_v), so they lie in Σ̆⁺ \ Σ̆⁺_min. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.locator: §D.2, proof of Proposition D.2.3, (D.3)–(D.5), published p. 371–372

The last step uses that each v ∈ Σ⁺_min splits into two primes of F̆⁺ with identical local data. Missing: routed to a source of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7a (route 12).

items.statement: With E,L,N,K,q,alpha,d,delta,g,e as in S23-closure and gamma of prime-to-ell order, G_(S,gamma)=q(N^alpha)⊂K^h. Therefore the equality printed in Lemma 2.6.4 holds if and only if q:N^alpha→K^h is surjective. The formula still holds when excluding any prescribed finite set of primes. It does not assert that the main GI(T²−1), j=1 hypothesis implies this surjectivity.

items.name: One-sided rank-two localization with a distinguished class
items.statement: Let O be a DVR, π a uniformizer, Rn=O/π^n with n≥1, S a free Rn-module of rank two, v∈S primitive (v∉πS), and f1,f2:S→Rn linear. Suppose π^c Rn²⊆image(f1,f2) for 0≤c<n. After possibly interchanging f1 and f2, there exists a primitive t∈S such that f1(t)=0, expπ(f1(v))≥n−c and expπ(f2(t))≥n−c. A basis diagonalizing both maps is not asserted. For an actual abundant pair of Frobenius evaluations with targets π^m0(O/π^m), apply this after n=m−m0,c=4rR and use S25-norm for local cohomology.

items.name: Bounded-image matrix has an integral scaled inverse
items.statement: Let O be a DVR with uniformizer π, fraction field K, n≥1 and 0≤c<n. If a square d×d matrix A over O has reduction Abar whose image contains π^c(O/π^n)^d, then A is invertible over K and C=π^c A^−1 has entries in O, with AC=CA=π^c I. This holds for every integral lift A of Abar.

items.name: Primitive kernel vector preserves the second error bound
items.statement: Let O,π,n,c be as in S25-lift and A a 2×2 integral lift of a bounded-image matrix. Write its first row as π^a(u1,u2), where a is the minimum entry valuation and at least one ui is a unit. Then a≤c, t=(-u2,u1) reduces to a primitive vector in (O/π^n)^2, the first row kills t exactly, and the second row evaluated at t has valuation v(det A)−a≤c. In particular its reduction has exponent at least n−c.
items.locator: Supplied by an earlier version of this extraction (not in the paper): elementary proof for Proposition 2.6.7, p.135 and Theorem 8.3.2, pp.317–320
items.note: Only one row is killed. Neither a basis diagonalization nor freeness of the full kernel is claimed. Missing: routed to a source of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1/ES.4 (route 2).

items.name: Prime-to-ell unramified restriction preserves exponents
items.statement: Let M be a finite Oλ-module and h an automorphism with h^g=1, where g≥1 is prime to ell. The norm N=1+h+⋯+h^(g−1) induces an Oλ-linear isomorphism M/(h−1)M→M^h. For an unramified local representation with arithmetic Frobenius h and the unramified degree-g extension killing its action, restriction on H1_ns is this norm map under Frobenius evaluation. Thus evaluation after restriction vanishes exactly when the original nonsingular class vanishes and preserves its λ-exponent.
items.locator: Not in the paper: supplied by an earlier version of this extraction; Proposition 2.6.7 second paragraph, p.135; Definition 2.2.2, p.124; explicit normalization supplied in report
items.note: A source refinement of SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L0/L2. The degree is g=ord(hγ), not the order of an independently chosen lift in a larger Galois closure. This local statement does not settle E1. Missing: routed to a source of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L4 (route 1).

items.name: One-sided localization retains the rank-one error budget
items.statement: In the setup of the proof of Theorem 8.3.2, suppose the actual (S,γ)-abundant pair has been obtained, with m>mper+mlat+mΣ+8rR+mdif. Put n=m−mΣ,c=4rR and choose the primitive v=π^mΣ s0 in S where π^mper s0=s as in footnote 33. After possibly interchanging the two evaluations, there is a primitive t∈S with loc_w1(t)=0, expλ loc_w2(t)≥m−mΣ−4rR and expλ loc_w1(s)≥m−mper−4rR. Consequently, conditional on the source's geometric reciprocity outputs, level comparison and perfect local pairing, the distinguished local pairing with its constructed c2 has exponent at least m−mper−mlat−mΣ−8rR. The error bound is unchanged; no basis containing s or v is required.

items.name: Normal closure and the actual restriction map
items.statement: In the setup of §§2.3,2.6 let E=F(m)+, K=Gal(FS/F(m)), and L the normal closure over F+ of FS E. Set N=Gal(L/E) and let q:N→K be restriction. N is a finite abelian ell-group; q is additive and need not be surjective. For gamma∈Gal(E/F+) of prime-to-ell order d and in the specified c-coset, choose an order-d lift sigma in Gal(L/F+); put alpha=conj(sigma)|N. Write delta=[F:F+], h=h_gamma on K through theta_S, g=ord(h_gamma on Rbar(m)), and e=delta*g. Then e divides d, q alpha^delta=h q, and q alpha^e=q. The fixed image q(N^alpha) uses additive groups, not an assumed O_lambda-module structure on K.

items.name: A prime-to-ell cyclic quotient admits a lift of the same order
items.statement: For a finite group B with normal abelian ell-subgroup N and cyclic quotient B/N generated by gamma of order d prime to ell, gamma has a lift sigma of order exactly d. If tau is any lift, a=tau^d∈N is fixed by conjugation by tau, and sigma=(-d^(-1)a) tau is such a lift, writing N additively.

items.name: Projected partial norm has the full fixed-point image
items.statement: Let N,K be finite abelian ell-groups, alpha an automorphism of N with alpha^d=1, gcd(d,ell)=1, q:N→K additive, and e a positive divisor of d such that q alpha^e=q. Put N_e=Σ_(i=0)^(e-1)alpha^i. Then im(q N_e)=q(N^alpha). More precisely q N_e=e q A_d, where A_d=d^(-1)Σ_(i=0)^(d-1)alpha^i is the averaging projection on N.
items.locator: Supplied by an earlier version of this extraction (not in the paper): refinement of Lemma 2.6.4, published pp.133–134; original setup §§2.3,2.5–2.6

items.name: Two conjugate evaluations give a sufficient lifting criterion
items.statement: In S23-closure with delta=2, put P_h=g^(-1)Σ_(j=0)^(g-1)h^j on K. Then q(N^alpha)=im(P_h(q+q alpha)). In particular, if n↦(P_h q(n),P_h q alpha(n)) maps N onto K^h×K^h, the printed equality G_(S,gamma)=K^h holds. This is a sufficient joint-image hypothesis, not a consequence established here from GI(T²−1).

items.name: Schur–Zassenhaus complement for a normal Hall subgroup
items.statement: For a subgroup N of a group B, with N normal and Nat.card N coprime to N.index, there exists H with Subgroup.IsComplement′ N H. In the finite cyclic preimage used here, restriction identifies H with the quotient, so its chosen generator lifts gamma with the same order.

items.name: Finite-group norm and averaging projection onto invariants
items.statement: For a representation rho of a finite group G on a module over a commutative ring k with #G invertible in k, LinearMap.range(rho.norm)=rho.invariants and rho.averageMap=(#G)^(-1) rho.norm. For a cyclic group, invariants equal the kernel of generator action minus identity.

items.name: Additive Goursat quotient graph
items.statement: For an additive subgroup H of G×K whose two coordinate projections are surjective, its coordinate kernels D_G and D_K admit an additive quotient equivalence G/D_G≃+K/D_K whose graph is the image of H in the quotient product. No coefficient-module structure or finiteness is needed.

items.statement: For a submodule M of a finite free module V over a PID with finrank M=finrank V, there are bases (b_i) of V and (m_i) of M and scalars a_i with m_i=a_i b_i in V.

items.name: Paired-evaluation obstruction data
items.statement: In S23-closure with delta=2 and ell odd, set A=K^h, P_h=g^(-1)Σ_(j<g)h^j, q0=P_h q and q1=q0 alpha. Let J=im(q0)=im(q1)≤A and H=im(q0,q1)≤J×J. H is swap-stable and subdirect. Its Goursat kernels coincide: D={x∈J:(x,0)∈H}={x∈J:(0,x)∈H}. Put C=J/D and let tau:C≃+C be the induced quotient-graph automorphism; tau²=1. Define C^-={c∈C:tau(c)=-c}. All are additive groups; K and J are not assumed O_lambda-modules.

items.name: Exact anti-invariant defect of actual Frobenius evaluations
items.statement: Under S23-obstruction put G=G_(S,gamma)=im(q0+q1). Then D≤G≤J, G/D=C^+ where C^+=ker(tau−id), and x↦(xbar−tau xbar)/2 induces J/G≃+C^-. Consequently there is an exact sequence 0→C^-→A/G→A/J→0, and G=A iff J=A and C^-=0.

items.name: A bounded additive obstruction gives a bounded evaluation loss
items.statement: Under S23-defect suppose a,b≥0 satisfy ell^a(A/J)=0 and ell^b C^-=0. Then ell^(a+b) A≤G. For e_lambda=ord_lambda(ell) and kappa=e_lambda(a+b), span_O(theta_S(G)) contains lambda^kappa span_O(theta_S(A)). Thus an input inclusion lambda^c0 Hom_O(S,Rbar(m)^h)≤span_O(theta_S(A)) gives lambda^(c0+kappa) Hom_O(S,Rbar(m)^h)≤span_O(theta_S(G)).

items.name: Choose actual evaluation rows without enlarging the loss
items.statement: Let O be a DVR with uniformizer π, n>c≥0, r≥1 and R_n=O/π^n. If a set T⊆R_n^r has R_n-span M containing π^c R_n^r, there are r elements t1,…,tr of T such that the square matrix W with these rows has image containing π^c R_n^r. These rows belong to T; they are not arbitrary linear combinations replacing actual Frobenius elements.

items.name: Abundant tuples with an explicit Frobenius-defect loss
items.statement: Retain S24's injection, absolute irreducibility and free rank-one invariant hypotheses, with ell odd and delta=2. Let S be free of rank r≥1 over O/π^n, n=m−mSigma, and set c0=f(r)rR, f(0)=f(1)=1 and f(r+1)=2(f(r)+1) for r≥1. Suppose S23-error holds with kappa=e_lambda(a+b) and c=c0+kappa<n. There are r actual elements of G_(S,gamma) whose evaluation map, after identifying the π^n-torsion of Rbar(m)^h with O/π^n, has image containing π^c(O/π^n)^r. S23 realizes them at associated primes avoiding any prescribed finite set.

items.name: Rank-zero pairing threshold with bounded Frobenius defect
items.statement: In the rank-zero application of Theorem 8.2.2 retain all source hypotheses and conditional geometric reciprocity, integral comparison and perfect-pairing gates. Suppose S24-bounded applies with r=1 and kappa uniformly bounded in m. The distinguished local pairing then has exponent at least m−mper−mlat−mSigma−rR−kappa, and the global contradiction requires m>mper+mlat+mSigma+rR+kappa+mdif.
